mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on 22 october 2008 the european president and the council declared 2010 the year of combating poverty and social exclusion. at that time, the european union had 78 million people at risk of poverty, of whom 19 million were children. today, given the effects of the economic crisis, such as the growth of unemployment, the priority of combating poverty must be reinforced. people and human dignity must be the primary objective of our political action and we cannot accept that there are people in europe who are starving. i therefore believe that the european union must assess its current social situation and, if necessary, increase the financial resources to implement the necessary measures to combat poverty. to do this, we need to have a budget.

in writing. i express my solidarity with the people of haiti affected by the earthquake that struck the country on 12 january and welcome the eu's commitments to help. the european union is the world's leading donor of humanitarian and development aid. within hours of the disaster, the eu made €3 million available for initial relief operations. eur 134 million was released for the first rehabilitation and reconstruction measures. a further €200 million will be allocated for longer-term rehabilitation, in addition to the €92 million granted by different eu countries. these amounts, totalling eur 429 million, may be further increased depending on the needs assessment. i congratulate the european commission for coordinating the aid, but i regret that the face of the european union has not been sufficiently visible on the ground, damaging the image of the eu in international public opinion, as opposed to the image of the united states which contributed eur 91.6 million. during this crisis, the need for medical care was evident and calls were made for the reinforcement of the medical and healthcare staff and for increased logistical support.
the iranian issue is one of the most important in contemporary international politics. everything must be done to prevent the iranian regime, which has been so harmful to peace and security in the middle east, from gaining access to nuclear weapons. but the role of the european union in relations with iran cannot be limited to the nuclear issue. we have seen, since the rigged elections in june, a popular movement against the repressive, obscurantist and anti-democratic nature of the iranian regime. europe must be consistent in promoting the universal values of human rights because so many are risking their lives on the streets of tehran. without ever calling into question the sovereign right of the people to decide their own destiny, it is imperative that the european union take initiatives that strengthen those fighting for freedom and democracy in iran. and nothing is more decisive than free and alternative media against censorship that all oppressive regimes rely on. in this connection, we look forward to the rapid launch of the farsi television channel, which the european commission has awarded to euronews. in this regard too, we hope that baroness ashton, as the new high representative, will advance creative initiatives that contribute to political openness in iran, taking into account the recommendations of all those who have fought for a free iran, including iranian exiles. it is this concern for the political future of iran which should guide any new sanctions that may be decided in the context of the nuclear issue. as the iranian intellectual akbar ganji has explained here in the european parliament, it is imperative to avoid economic sanctions that weaken the people and in particular the iranian middle class, which is the hard core of the opposition movement. this must be an objective for the european union to take on.
the vast area covering the middle and near east, central asia and north africa, including the red sea and the gulf of aden area - where yemen has a strategic location (alongside somalia) - has long seen powerful geo-strategic interests converge on it. these interests are increasingly defended militarily and with increasing aggressiveness. it is in the light of this reality that the current situation in yemen and the terrible martyrdom to which its people are subjected must be analysed. it is in the light of this reality that the growing military involvement of the us and the eu in the region should be understood and denounced. the cruise missile attack carried out by the united states late last year on a base allegedly belonging to the al-qaeda terrorist network, which resulted in dozens of civilian casualties, is a brutal and shocking expression of this, which we strongly condemn. the real solution to the complex problems and dangers facing the peoples of the region must be found in demilitarisation, respect for the national rights and sovereignty of these peoples and genuine cooperation to solve the profound social problems affecting them.

in writing. − the european ombudsman, on his own initiative or following a complaint, acts to combat instances of maladministration by the community institutions and bodies. in this way, the ombudsman contributes to the construction of a people's europe at a time when the treaty of lisbon has entered into force and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union has acquired binding legal force. it should be noted that the right to good administration is a fundamental right of european citizens, safeguarded by article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. in 2001, the european parliament adopted a resolution on a code of good administrative behaviour to be respected by the institutions and bodies of the european union and by their administrations. i would like to see this code become a european law, which would bring legislative coherence to the eu and would guarantee that the same basic principles are applied by its institutions in their relations with citizens. it is important that european citizens know their rights and how to protect and restore them in the event of a breach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the temporary suspension of the autonomous common customs tariff duties on imports of a number of industrial products into the autonomous regions of the azores and madeira, as it aims to strengthen the competitiveness of the economic operators in the azores (manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers and retailers) and thus to ensure more stable employment in the azores and thus overcome the economic disadvantages which are felt as a result of their geographical situation. this temporary suspension of duties, allowing local economic operators in the azores and madeira to import a certain number of raw materials, parts, components and finished products duty-free, and covering sectors such as fisheries, agriculture, industry and services, provides a favourable environment for long-term investment by investors. these measures will also help to help smes and local farmers to invest and create jobs in the outermost regions, and in the context of the current economic crisis, the need for specific measures to stimulate economic activity and stabilise employment is paramount.
in writing. - the development of the outermost regions is seriously hampered by factors such as their structural social and economic situation, remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult topography and climate and their economic dependence. it is therefore essential that the european union continue to look at these regions, identifying problems and potential, studying their differences and fragility, with a view to implementing policies and measures appropriate to their economic and social development. i welcome the proposal for a council regulation because of the incentive it represents for sustainable development and the integration of the outermost regions into the world economy. the temporary suspension of common customs tariff duties allows the autonomous regions of madeira and the azores to overcome the economic disadvantages arising from their geographical situation and at the same time to respond to the specific effects they are experiencing due to the economic crisis. i welcome the initiative of the regional authorities of madeira and the azores and their commitment to contribute to the development strategy of these regions, while contributing to a competitive european union capable of sustainable economic development.

in writing. - in order to strengthen the competitiveness of economic operators in the portuguese autonomous regions of madeira and the azores and thus to ensure more stable employment in those islands, i consider it essential to introduce temporary suspensions of autonomous customs duties. that suspension will allow local economic operators in madeira and the azores to import raw materials, parts, components and finished products duty-free, provided that such products are used locally for their production or processing activities. the approval of this derogation is essential for the development of these portuguese autonomous regions, both of which are highly dependent on the tourism industry and therefore highly subject to the volatility of this sector of activity and, as such, limited in their full economic development by the characteristics of their local economy and their geographical location. in this sense, any incentive for local industries is certainly a necessary support for the improvement of the living conditions of the local population and a way of enabling the creation of employment on the islands, which is essential to fixing the populations and creating conditions for development.
in writing. the temporary suspension of common customs tariff duties will allow local economic operators in the autonomous regions of madeira and the azores to import a certain number of raw materials, parts, components and finished products duty-free. the raw materials will have to be used for agricultural purposes and for processing and industrial maintenance in the autonomous regions. this suspension will be in force until 31 december 2019 and mechanisms are in place to prevent unfair competition from arising. this will strengthen the competitiveness of smes and farmers in our autonomous regions of madeira and the azores. this measure takes account of the specific characteristics of these outermost regions and stimulates economic activity, contributing to the stabilisation of employment. the local economies of madeira and the azores depend to a large extent on national and international tourism, which has been affected by the current economic crisis. the suspension is therefore fully justified and is expected to have a positive impact on the economic development of these regions. i call for a more rapid analysis and decision-making in such cases, so that a more effective and timely response can be made. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - this resolution advocates a strategy for the danube region with a territorial logic structured by this important river and promotes the sustained and integrated development of a region covering 14 european countries. the strategy envisaged will enable a coordinated and integrated policy to achieve synergies, promote cohesion, foster economic growth and competitiveness, while protecting the environment. the modernisation of ports, the improvement of the navigability of the river with freight corridors and interconnection and intermodality with the north sea, the improvement of its water quality, the protection of the whole danube basin and, in particular, of the ecosystems that make up the natura 2000 network are objectives to be achieved and made compatible. the commission should therefore quickly launch a broad consultation process with all the countries along the danube so that the strategy can be defined by the end of the year and be compatible with the next multiannual financial framework.

madam president, commissioner, in monetary union there are no attacks on greece, spain, ireland or portugal, there are attacks on the union and there are attacks on the euro, taking advantage of signs of fragility or of the gaps that are opening up in the solidity of the bloc. and in this context, i have to tell you, commissioner, that your statements were both inopportune and dangerous, but coming from someone with your experience and background, they can only reflect a disdain for the persistence and inaction of the commission which you have made part of, because a monetary union is much more than, as you know, a single currency, a stability pact or a single central bank. monetary union, if it is to be sustainable in the long term, cannot be limited to nominal short-term indicators, cannot leave the real economy, economic growth and employment behind, and cannot ignore the brutal internal regional and social divergences that accompany it and that the commission has rightly identified in its work on emu@10. each member state has its own obligations. but anyone who considers monetary union to be a finished project is making an unforgivable mistake. we must stop using words and move on to action. the lisbon strategy did not work because it lacked the means and instruments. today, if we want monetary union to persist and be solid, we need to replace terms such as 'solidarity' and 'coordination of economic policies' with concrete means and instruments that have not been there until now. the commission has just been sworn in, not to maintain what it has done so far, but to learn the lessons and start a new phase. that's what i expect and you have my trust.
madam president, in this debate it was essential to ensure that the european union would break with its monetary policies and the blind criteria of the stability pact. it was essential to focus on social progress in order to give priority to tackling the problem of unemployment and poverty, to support production and the creation of jobs with rights, to ensure economic and social cohesion, to provide budgetary support measures for the countries in the most difficult situation, in particular by advancing funds without the need for national counterparts. but unfortunately, that's not what we heard here. commissioner almunia has insisted on the same policies, he has insisted on the same neoliberal recipes, trying to make the consequences of the bad policies of the european union, including his own responsibilities, fall on the same people as always, commissioner, especially with the sad and regrettable statements he made about greece, spain and portugal, which in my country, for example portugal, triggered a rush of speculative capital. they did win with their statements. but my country and the others lost to them and to the policies that are here. so we tell them, it's time to change policies.

in writing. european commissioners are expected to be a factor of stability and to make rigorous and reasoned statements, unlike recent statements by commissioner joaquín almunia, who has shown a lack of prudence and contributed to losses on the stock exchanges and distrust of international investors towards portugal and spain. to cope with the crisis, eu member states have launched recovery plans, stimulus and incentives for the economy, and have consequently increased their deficits. however, we also know of member states which, either through incompetence or deliberately, have misrepresented their deficits. recent developments have forced the european union to give new impetus to its proposals for supervision and to implement a strategy of enhanced economic coordination. the commission also proposes to set up a system for monitoring the deficit in each member state so that corrective measures can be taken quickly and that any irreversible situations can be avoided. this system should work in near real time. it is also important to clarify the formula for calculating the deficit so as to avoid situations of government accounting fraud and to avoid recurrent budgetary discouragement techniques with the aim of concealing the deficit.

mr. president, the un says that biodiversity is facing the worst crisis since the dinosaurs went extinct 65 million years ago. the destruction of coral reefs in the tropics, increasing desertification in africa and deforestation threaten biodiversity and have negative impacts on many sectors of the economy, such as food production, tourism, the pharmaceutical industry or energy production. the un also acknowledges that it has failed to meet the 2002 target of significantly reducing the current rate of biodiversity loss by 2010. cites is the main global agreement on the conservation of wildlife with the aim of preventing the over-exploitation of wild fauna and flora species by international trade. human consumption of natural resources, destruction of habitats, climate change, overexploitation of wild species and illicit trade are the main causes of the depletion of biodiversity. it is therefore important to ensure that, in the international year of biodiversity, the key strategic objectives of the european union in the framework of the next conference of the parties to cites are aligned with the objective of protecting biological diversity, which is fundamental to the well-being and survival of humanity. we must be ambitious and demand the protection of all endangered species.
last november, iccat adopted strong restrictive measures on catches of bluefin tuna: reduction of the catch in 2010 from 22 to 13 500 tonnes, restriction of fishing from 15 may to 15 june for purse seiners with a retainer. ambitious and unprecedented measures, in the words of then commissioner joe borg. these decisions have been taken in line with the latest scientific advice on the species and their impact should be assessed further in 2010. it is therefore pointless to anticipate further economic and social restrictions on the sector, especially in the period of severe crisis it is going through, such as those which amount to the inclusion of bluefin tuna in annex i. the fisheries sector requires a dynamic balance between its three pillars: environmental, economic and social. in the case of environmental requirements, these must be scientifically justified, as was also the case at the iccat meeting with the active participation of the european union. the inclusion of bluefin tuna in annex i would therefore set a serious precedent for disregarding the requirement of a scientific basis for the restriction and a balance between the environmental, economic and social pillars, thus opening the door to other hasty and factious decision-making and distorting the rules of responsible management.
this report on the erdf is intended to broaden the eligibility of housing assistance for marginalised communities in our member states. until now, this support has only been available to marginalised communities living in urban areas in the new member states. in other words, since the vast majority of these communities live in rural areas and shelters, these communities could not benefit from support to replace poor quality housing. the aim is to fill a gap and to give the member states and their regions greater policy options to mitigate the specific difficulties of these communities. i also welcome equal treatment for all member states, because marginalised communities with support and integration needs deserve our concern, regardless of the member state to which they belong. the conclusion of this important report on the fight against poverty and human dignity at first reading also means that it can be quickly implemented as part of the economic recovery plan, thus responding quickly to the crisis that affects us.
mr president, commissioner, let me begin by highlighting the role of the rapporteur, mr van nistelrooij, for his work in seeking consensus on this matter and also for the willingness he has always shown to incorporate other contributions into his report. tomorrow we shall vote on amendments to the erdf regulation which are of particular importance for the so-called old member states and also for portugal. these amendments will make it possible to extend the use of the erdf in the housing sector to marginalised communities, as at present this fund can only be allocated to urban development operations. the amendments which i proposed with other colleagues and which were adopted by a large majority in the committee on regional development will allow the old member states, and not just the new ones, as envisaged in the original proposal, to benefit from this possibility of funding. i have tried to avoid setting a dangerous precedent which would exclude all the former member states from this and probably other additional uses of community aid. this would make no sense, since housing problems, especially among marginalised communities, exist in both the new and the old member states. i would like to take this opportunity to reiterate that the length of time since accession to the european union should not be a criterion for allocating structural funds and that this criterion should be abandoned. the negotiation of cohesion policy post-2013 should be based on solidarity towards territorial cohesion and should be geared towards rewarding, rather than punishing, regions that have been exemplary in the use of community aid.
this report acknowledges some positive steps towards eu membership by turkey, a candidate country since 2005, but also urges it to accelerate the pace of reforms. i would remind you that in december 2006 the negotiations were partially suspended because of your refusal to apply the eu customs union agreement to cyprus. the conflict with cyprus must be resolved and the country must continue to increase its progress in the functioning of democracy and the protection of human rights, the fight against corruption, the improvement of press freedom, the need for political transparency and faster and more effective justice, the improvement of anti-discrimination laws on gender, sexual orientation and ethnic and religious minorities, and the reform of the public administration. the turkish government continues to demonstrate political will to continue reforms and has substantially increased fundamental freedoms and democratic development in the country. we must therefore continue to make progress in the negotiations with a view to securing the accession of this key country as a mediator in conflicts between israel and palestine and as a platform for understanding between iraq and iran.

in writing. − the adoption of directive 2006/112/ec had already been an important step in the fight against tax evasion. however, despite its merits, it was no longer effective enough to deal with so-called 'carrousel' vat fraud. this tax fraud accounts for a large percentage of the loss of tax revenue that occurs in the member states and has been one of the most widely used. at this time of economic crisis, when the fight against tax evasion is all the more important given the seriousness of the leakage of revenue, all efforts to combat tax evasion are essential and have an important impact not only on the response to the current international crisis situation, but also on the possibility of pursuing relevant social policies.
in writing. - i am pleased to vote in favour of this amendment to the erdf to extend its scope to housing interventions for marginalised communities in all member states. until now, housing assistance could only be provided as part of urban development operations in the form of housing renovation. i think that this is an unwarranted and discriminatory criterion, since, as in portugal, most of these families live in rural areas in shelters. these are the ones who need it most and cannot be excluded on geographical grounds. i welcome the amendment by the ep which thus strengthens territorial cohesion. moreover, instead of the commission's initial proposal restricting access to this proposal to the new member states only, this new regulation extends the scope to all member states, thus avoiding meaningless discrimination between european marginalised families. this is a global problem affecting thousands of families all over europe! in portugal, the situation is particularly serious in view of the economic crisis the country is going through and the poverty situation in many of these families.
in writing. − the european commission intends to amend the rules of the erdf (european regional development fund) regulation to allow new member states to use these funds for housing interventions for marginalised communities living in rural areas. this amendment applies only to the new member states, which, we must not forget, have large marginalised migrant communities living in rural areas, thus justifying the adoption of an exceptional scheme in the erdf regulation.
in writing. - in the fight against poverty and the improvement of the living conditions of the most deprived sections of the population, whose situation of weakness has been greatly aggravated by the deep crisis of recent years, the european union has an obligation to ensure and encourage continued policies for social inclusion. in addition to the health problem, the deterioration of living conditions aggravates and often causes risks of segregation and marginalisation. the living conditions are decisive for the self-esteem and social value of any citizen, and therefore, along with education, health and employment, play a decisive role in the construction, development and consolidation of a sustainable life project, whether at individual or family level. the committee calls for the european union to maintain intervention strategies that do not discriminate on grounds of gender, race or ethnicity. a more balanced social europe also requires that the creation and expansion of ghettos or areas easily associated with a certain disadvantaged or marginalised community be avoided. it also calls for inclusion policies to target those who need it most, without making any distinction between european citizens.

in writing. - the report we have adopted today amends the regional development fund regulation, extending its use in the housing sector for the benefit of marginalised communities, as currently this fund can only be allocated in the context of urban development initiatives. the amendments which i and other members have proposed and which have been confirmed today in the house will allow the old member states, and not just the new ones as envisaged in the commission's original proposal, to also benefit from the erdf for this new financing option. i have therefore tried to avoid setting a precedent, which i consider dangerous, and which would exclude the former member states, particularly portugal, from this and possibly other additional uses of community aid. i reiterate that the length of time since accession to the european union should not be a criterion for the allocation of structural funds and that cohesion policy after 2013 should continue to be based on the principle of solidarity with a view to territorial cohesion, which is crucial for the outermost regions such as madeira. it should also aim at greater flexibility, simplicity and transparency and a result-orientation that rewards, rather than punishes, those regions which have shown themselves to be exemplary in the use of community aid.
in writing. - tax fraud and evasion are an attack on the building of a fairer, stronger and more equitable europe in terms of social and economic development. the consequences have become even more evident and serious in this period of severe economic and financial crisis, when member states' budgets have been particularly weakened and put under greater pressure by the need for public investment and social spending. it should be noted that tax fraud in the european union amounts to more than 200 billion euros a year, or more than 2% of gdp. in the context of the open market and the free movement of goods and persons, control and supervision mechanisms have become more complex, due to the inalienable sovereign rights of each member state. to make matters worse, unscrupulous economic operators, largely encouraged by the opportunities for easy profit arising from the economic crisis, are resorting to increasingly sophisticated and ingenious tax evasion mechanisms. the proposal strengthens administrative cooperation between the member states of the european union in the field of taxation, where the process of european integration has shown a clear imbalance between the legislation produced and the mechanisms for control and supervision.

in writing. - since the previous legislature, the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion has been a priority for the european union, with a number of legislative proposals having been adopted in this area. administrative cooperation in the field of taxation is a key element of the common strategy to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. effective action to combat tax evasion and fraud has important consequences at three levels: in national budgets, the loss of important revenue for public expenditure in the general interest, especially health, education and research. tax evasion and tax fraud infringe the principle of equal tax treatment to the detriment of citizens and companies that comply with their tax obligations and, finally, distorts competition which in turn affects the proper functioning of markets. in this context of crisis, all measures to combat tax evasion and fraud are increasingly important in order to cope with the exceptional expenditure needed to avoid the effects of the crisis and to reduce, as far as possible, the high budget deficits.

in writing. - the increase in the number of requests for assistance between member states in the recovery of claims relating to certain fees, and the lack of effectiveness of recovery, at only 5%, make it necessary to amend council directive 1976/308/eec. to address the problems of slow progress, disparity, lack of coordination and lack of transparency, this resolution is justified.
in writing. - i welcome once again the eu's commitments to help the people of haiti following the earthquake last january. in haiti, before the earthquake, more than 70% of the people lived below the poverty line and their foreign debt reached 890 million usd. at this point, it is the duty of the international community to contribute to the definition of a strategy for the reconstruction of the country that is sustainable in the short, medium and long term. this is a key moment for the coordination of reconstruction efforts between international aid donors, the haitian authorities and civil society, and i welcome the recent g7 decision to forgive haiti's debts, including those owed to multilateral credit institutions. it is crucial to help this country recover from the earthquake, but it is important that the international community take advantage of this opportunity to help solve the problem of economic, social and political imbalances in haiti.
in writing. - the earthquake on 12 january 2010 on the island of haiti, which killed thousands of people and caused a situation of devastation and deep calamity, calls for our firm solidarity with the haitian people. i had the pleasure and honour of contributing to the drafting of this european parliament resolution. i think it is essential, first of all, to thank the professionals whose work, carried out immediately (through the jrc), has helped to save lives and alleviate urgent needs on the ground (health, water, hygiene, clothing, etc.), thus proving that the investment required by the ep over the years has had its positive practical effects. on the other hand, as in the asian post-tsunami, lessons must be learned from the experience. the european commission should present as soon as possible, following the 2006 barnier report, legislative measures to create a single, independent and permanent eu civil protection force capable of carrying out rescue missions and ensuring an integrated approach to assistance, rehabilitation and development. i also congratulate the member states, ngos and civil society for all the humanitarian aid that has been made available.
in writing. the european parliament has voted in favour of the resolution on the earthquake in haiti, which killed 200,000 people and injured 250,000. i express my sympathy and solidarity with the people of haiti and other nations, the staff of international organizations, including the un and the european commission, and the families of the victims of this tragedy. i would like to highlight the work carried out by some member states of the european union through the eu civil protection mechanism and under the coordination of the information and surveillance centre and welcome the proposal to carry out an assessment of the european response to the humanitarian crisis in haiti so that the european commission can make proposals to improve the eu's rapid response capacity in the future.
in writing. − january 12, 2010 will surely go down in haiti's history as one of its most terrible days. a people and a state already plagued by poverty and underdevelopment were suddenly devastated by a natural disaster of colossal, merciless and murderous proportions. the tens of thousands of dead in ever outdated statistics and the anguish and despair in the eyes of those who have lost everything have amply justified the mobilization of the international community and of so many civil societies around the world, to which i cannot but join. despite this solidarity drive, which only ennobles those who have been at the forefront of it, we must try to continue this aid, even when the focus of global attention shifts to another country. despite all international efforts, the reconstruction of the country will only take place if the rulers and the ruled are able to lead the process and assume their respective responsibilities.
in writing. - the calamitous situation in haiti following the violent earthquake on 12 january is a new challenge to solidarity between peoples and nations. the european union, by virtue of its history and cultural identity, and its importance in the context of the world economy, must play an exemplary and stimulating role in helping haitians and in the reconstruction of one of the poorest countries in the world. financial and logistical instruments must be put in place as a matter of urgency to minimise the suffering of the population affected by the tragedy and to ensure the speedy restoration of the minimum living conditions for the people. however, conditions must be assessed and ensured for the promotion of sustainable development in the country in order to counteract the situation of extreme poverty affecting a large part of the population of that country. in addition to the incentives for agricultural profitability, industrialisation and the development of sustainable product marketing channels, i consider it essential to support the implementation of a strong strategy for environmental recovery, since haiti is a striking and dramatic example of the devastating impacts that climate change represents for humanity. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - in the face of the dramatic scenario of complete destruction that has befallen haiti, there is an urgent need for effective and genuine solidarity to help alleviate the suffering of its people. the rejection and condemnation of any attempt to exploit the tragedy of the haitian people to occupy the country militarily and the unequivocal defence of the sovereignty and independence of haiti - something which the text under discussion does not do - are also imperative. it is regrettable that the resolution is more backward than the statements of some heads of state and un leaders on the deployment of tens of thousands of us troops in the country. haiti and its people lack firefighters, doctors, hospitals and basic necessities. the eu's response, which the resolution welcomes, was 'the council's decision to send 350 military police officers'. it is appropriate to recall here the rapid aid given to haiti by countries such as cuba, which promptly sent 400 doctors, saving lives and preventing epidemics, setting up medical infrastructure and distributing basic necessities, or venezuela, through debt forgiveness and fuel supply.
in writing. - we believe that this is a time for all the humanitarian aid, cooperation and reconstruction aid that the nobility and courage of the haitian people deserve. unfortunately, too much time was wasted on the supports and not everything worked out for the best. as we have pointed out, some, particularly the united states, were more concerned with strengthening their military presence with their troops than with the people of haiti. we regret that the resolution adopted did not go further in defending the state of haiti and its people, starting with the rejection of any attempt by any country or person to take advantage of this catastrophe to resume neocolonialism, forgetting the poverty in which the majority of the population lives, which remains the victim of the exploitation of multinationals and of external interference, particularly by the united states. we will continue to express our full solidarity with the people of haiti.
in writing. - the earthquake that struck haiti on 12 january 2010, in addition to all the deaths it caused, continues to affect some 3 million people every day for whom humanitarian aid is crucial. the eu's role in foreign policy has been becoming clearer, and the values the eu intends to promote are aimed at contributing, among other things, to world peace and security and the protection of human rights. the efforts of the member states to help haiti emerge from this catastrophe as a fully functioning democracy with an economy capable of supporting its people are therefore to be commended, bearing in mind that the haitian people must always be an integral part of the whole process of reconstruction, as well as their government.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document with a great sense of responsibility and with the hope that this resolution will bear fruit. i would like to commend the efforts of the various political groups in this parliament to come together to give a united voice to the house of european democracy and to stress the strong pragmatic tone of the resolution, which points to concrete ways, solutions and measures for the eu to deal with the iranian regime. in this connection, i stress the need for: a) strong condemnation of companies supplying equipment and technology to the iranian authorities for the purposes of censorship and surveillance, which should be followed by a ban on european companies doing so; b) the demand (i would even say the demand) of the absolute necessity of respecting the vienna convention/the rules of diplomacy; c) the introduction of more sanctions on iranian organizations/individuals operating abroad, which are responsible for the repression and restriction of freedoms in the country, as well as those linked to the violation of iran's international commitments with regard to the nuclear issue; (d) nevertheless to promote the continuation and deepening of the dialogue with iran, in particular with civil society.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the situation in iran, as i consider the continuing violations of human rights in iran, particularly with regard to freedom of association, expression and information, to be a matter of concern and as i support the democratic aspirations of the iranian people.
in writing. - two types of news have been coming out of iran in recent months, both of which are unfortunately not encouraging in nature: the progress in the process of enriching uranium for nuclear purposes and the crackdown on the moderate faction led by moussavi which has been contesting the result of the last presidential elections. if separately they are a cause for concern, collectively they are the subject of the deepest concern. what about a troubled country where the increasingly radicalized government kills, tortures and imprisons opponents who demonstrate against it in the streets and at the same time is tenaciously pursuing a program of uranium enrichment for nuclear energy? the fundamentalist regime of the ayatollahs may proclaim the benignity of its intentions and the peaceful destiny of nuclear energy, but these statements do not convince the international community, which rightly sees iran as a growing threat. the european union must not only firmly condemn the brutal repression of moderate iranian groups, but also join its allies and other international actors in strengthening and tightening sanctions against tehran and not renouncing any concerted action to deal with this threat.
in writing. - we support freedom of expression and democracy and agree with the need to express concern at developments in iran over the past few months, particularly those related to the repressive actions of the iranian security forces against the popular masses. but the proposed text does not do it in the best way. in our view, the necessary expression of concern about the development of the situation cannot ignore the serious threats to iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, including the agenda of diplomatic and military escalation led by the us administration, among which the concentration of american military resources in the region stands out. it must not be forgotten that these elements are also threats to the rights of the iranian people and to the very forces in iran which are continuing the struggle for democracy, progress and social justice and which the adopted text does not even mention. the right to determine the future course of iran belongs exclusively to the iranian people and their political and social forces. we express our solidarity with the democratic organisations and the people of iran who are fighting for social justice and progress in their country.
in writing. - the social upheavals in iran, the systematic repression of opponents of the regime and the people, the restrictions on freedom of the press and of expression, the failure to abolish the death penalty and the persistence of a nuclear programme against the international community are reasons for tremendous concern. the european union is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners and for the immediate release of all political prisoners. the recent cancellation of the scheduled visit of the european parliament delegation is another clear sign of the non-cooperation of this country, which leads us to condemn the policy implemented by this iranian regime.
in writing. - yemen threatens to become a new afghanistan, a privileged recruitment and training ground for al-qaeda and a breeding ground for fundamentalists and terrorists to spread throughout the islamic world. its degraded, if not disintegrated, social, political and economic situation, in which civil war rages and the absence of a government effectively controlling the whole of its territory, makes it a place without law and order capable of stopping, on its own, the establishment and growth of those hotbeds of violence and radicalism. the international community must therefore pay greater attention to the situation in yemen and be more firm in its monitoring of it, and aid to yemen must be directed with particular care to the effective improvement of the living conditions of its people.
in writing. − the overall situation in yemen is a matter of grave concern worldwide and the eu must maintain its increasingly active role in the face of the recent terrorist threats, so that yemen does not become another failed state in the international community.
in writing. - this modern form of slavery has grown alarmingly in recent years, becoming the third most lucrative activity for organised crime. in 2009, the un estimated the number of victims at 270000 and europol recorded no decrease in trafficking of women for sexual exploitation, noting an increase in forced labour. it is unacceptable and cannot be facilitated by the fact that there are legislative gaps. a rapid, comprehensive and coordinated response is needed at both legislative and operational levels. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, i urge the commission to put forward a new proposal as soon as possible, making it one of its main priorities to create a coherent european policy to combat effectively trafficking in human beings in all its aspects, from issues relating to countries of origin, transit and destination, to recruiters, transporters, operators and other intermediaries, as well as customers and beneficiaries. in parallel, adequate protection for victims and witnesses should be ensured, which can protect them through immediate assistance. an effort should also be made to take advantage of the action of instruments which, unfortunately, are still underused in this field, such as europol, eurojust and frontex.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the prevention of trafficking in human beings, arguing that the commission and the council must ensure that the fight against this scourge remains a high priority, even in times of economic and financial crisis. member states that have not yet done so should fully implement all eu policies on trafficking in human beings at national level and ratify other legal instruments in this area as soon as possible to ensure better protection and assistance to victims of trafficking.
in writing. - trafficking in human beings is today, for its victims, an inhuman and modern form of slavery and, for those responsible, criminal organisations operating in the areas of prostitution and sexual exploitation, illegal adoption, forced labour, illegal immigration and illegal trade in organs, a highly profitable activity. unfortunately, this perverse reality also exists in the european union. it is therefore urgent that the european commission take strong and decisive action to combat trafficking in human beings, which should be based on three essential pillars: (i) adequate protection of the victims, mostly women and children, ensuring them the most fundamental rights such as life, liberty, physical and moral integrity and sexual self-determination; (ii) preventive action in investigating and dismantling the networks that promote and profit from trafficking in human beings; and (iii) severe punishment, with penalties proportionate to the crimes committed, of trafficking in human beings and its exploitation for all its evil purposes.
in writing. as stated in the adopted resolution, 'urgent action against trafficking in human beings is needed on the basis of a holistic approach, focused on human rights and aimed at combating trafficking, preventing it and protecting the victims. combating trafficking in human beings requires a victim-centred approach, which means that all categories of potential victims, especially children and women, must be identified, targeted and protected.' but we regret that our amendments to this resolution, which focused on the causes and ways of combating trafficking in human beings, were rejected, namely the following: - combating unemployment, marginalisation and poverty as the root causes of trafficking in human beings, stressing that a change in economic and social policies is urgently needed to give priority to strengthening social and labour rights, employment with rights, quality public services and economic and social progress. - strengthening cooperation and solidarity with the countries of origin of migrants, in particular by contributing to the development of their economies, improving access to knowledge, cancelling their debts and taxing financial transactions.
in writing. - trafficking in human beings is a violation of the most basic human rights and a form of slavery based on the logic of sexual and labour exploitation. international estimates place human trafficking as the third most lucrative illegal trade. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european union's action in the field of judicial and police cooperation has been clearly strengthened. the fight against trafficking in human beings must be one of the central objectives of the european union, which, on the basis of the co-legislatory role played by the european parliament, should be of vital importance in this field. the fight against trafficking in human beings must therefore remain at the top of the eu's priorities, even in times of economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the eu must create a new development paradigm to deal with climate change. the next budget review should provide sufficient resources for measures to overcome this important challenge. we cannot lose sight of our commitment to combating climate change, we must as europeans commit ourselves to a co2 reduction target of more than 20% by 2020. it would be important to have the collaboration of other global partners in order to reach an ambitious and legally binding global agreement in line with the objective of warming not exceeding 2°c. i also believe that the initiatives taken within the eu to promote and encourage the green economy, energy security and dependency reduction must continue to be a priority. the eu could draw inspiration from the policy in my region, the azores, which already has about 30% of its energy from renewable sources.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the motion for a resolution on the outcome of cop 15, which i co-authored, and the outcome of the negotiations between the various political groups, as it is representative of the general interest in this matter with a view to a sustainable future. i express once again my disappointment at the results achieved in copenhagen and urge the eu to regain international leadership in the fight against climate change and to contribute to a legally binding agreement with measurable, reportable and verifiable reduction targets at cop 16 in mexico this year. for european industries to be more competitive and create more jobs, it is essential to invest in a sustainable future that will involve climate protection, energy security, reducing energy independence and resource efficiency. to this end, i call on the industrialized countries to invest more in research into new technologies, with a view not only to reducing co2 emissions but also to using natural resources more efficiently and sustainably.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint resolution on the outcome of the copenhagen conference, as i agree in general with the content of the measures proposed, of which i would like to highlight two. firstly, the absolute need for the eu to speak with one voice in international negotiations, as only in this way will we be able to ensure global leadership in the management of this important issue, which has intergenerational consequences and therefore calls for firm, leading, immediate and sensible action, similar to others already taken by the eu (e.g. the fight against the financial crisis). this design calls for a new 'climate diplomacy' in which the efforts of not only the eu but also china and the us are essential, as explained in paragraphs 5 and 15 of the document. secondly, the imperative for developing countries/emerging economies to adopt the climate change rules applied by eu member states. in this connection, i have advocated, together with some of my colleagues in my political group, the introduction of a carbon tax on imports from third countries, so that this idea can take its first steps as an element for future reflection, which in itself i consider to be quite relevant.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the outcome of the copenhagen summit on climate change. the outcome of cop15 was disappointing. it is therefore important to ensure that the european union makes every effort in its external diplomacy to speak with one voice to secure a binding international agreement on climate change that will limit the global temperature increase to 2°c.
in writing. - after the impasse of the copenhagen climate change conference, it is important that the european union continues along the lines it has followed so far, towards a serious commitment to sustainable development, seeking to reduce its carbon emissions without jeopardising european industries. the new climate policies, especially in the face of a widespread crisis, cannot lose sight of economic efficiency and cannot in any way jeopardise the economic sustainability of european nations. that is why a new approach to energy policy, focusing on clean energy, a more efficient use of the natural resources at our disposal and a strong investment in research and more environmentally friendly technologies is urgently needed if european competitiveness is to be maintained and job creation enabled in a sustainable development framework.
in writing. − the eu has always been a leader in international climate change negotiations. yet despite the ambition, the last climate conference in copenhagen was a failure for all the people who were determined to reach a binding agreement. the result is far from the eu's position, and also far from the position needed for climate protection. in the face of the disappointing outcome of the copenhagen conference, parliament's resolution is intended to send a clear signal to the citizens of europe and the world that it remains committed to combating climate change. we are already preparing the way for the next conference in mexico, where the commitment of the parties must increase. we cannot repeat the mistakes made in copenhagen, we must ask ourselves what went wrong during the negotiations and how to proceed in the future to involve the united states, china and india.
in writing. the resolution under discussion does not make the critical assessment of the causes of the failure of copenhagen that is required. instead of seriously analysing the eu's own responsibilities for this failure, the majority of this parliament persists in making scapegoats such as china (a country whose per capita atmospheric emissions of carbon dioxide equivalent are less than half the eu average), now joined by the 'alba countries', a position justified only by the most basic political blindness and factionalism, which distorts and subverts what actually happened in copenhagen. significantly, the virtuousness of market instruments such as emission trading is emphasized, ignoring their already demonstrated ineffectiveness and perversity. once again, the necessary discussion on the so-called flexibility mechanisms, such as the clean development mechanism, is ignored. at the same time, the need to respect the sovereignty of developing countries in the definition and implementation of so-called adaptation strategies is rejected. no just and sustainable solution to the problem of climate change, as well as other environmental problems, will be achieved within the framework of the irrational system that generated them. what is required is another economic and social model, one that is opposed to capitalism.
in writing. the european council welcomed the progress made in the implementation of the lisbon strategy and the commission's commitment to the lisbon strategy. the countries with the greatest responsibility in this area have not reached a consensus on reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. this is a problem that requires a short-term solution and is of concern to the whole world. it is imperative that there is more transparency and greater engagement from civil society at cop16 in mexico. the eu must be able to show its leadership in the fight against climate change. and all countries, from the united states to the so-called emerging countries, including china, which is a major polluter, must also shoulder all the responsibilities in a struggle which leaves less and less room for new opportunities. the sustaining future of mankind is increasingly at stake in a process that, if nothing is done in due time, may reach the point of no return.
in writing. - we welcome the report's express mention that: 'strongly condemns the role played by tax havens in encouraging and exploiting tax fraud, tax evasion and capital flight; calls, therefore, on the member states to make the fight against tax havens, tax evasion and illicit capital flight a priority.' we also support the view that 'in the context of oecd-led initiatives', 'results remain insufficient to respond to the challenges posed by tax havens and offshore centres and must be followed by decisive, effective and coherent action' and that 'the commitments made by the g20 so far are not sufficient to address the challenges posed by tax evasion, tax havens and offshore centres'. but the most important thing was that they were not limited to good intentions and that they were actually fighting and eliminating tax havens and offshore centres, especially when we see, in certain cases, a dramatization of the public accounts deficit with the aim of continuing and even accentuating the same neoliberal policies so that once again the workers and the people pay the bill for the crisis.
in writing. - good tax governance is essential to guarantee such key aspects as the principles of transparency, exchange of information and fair tax competition. the financial crisis has made all efforts to combat tax evasion and tax fraud, as well as the fight against tax havens, all the more urgent. at a time when millions of people around the world are suffering the effects of the crisis, it would be pointless not to fight those who are not fulfilling their obligations. this initiative is an important signal to third countries that the eu is effectively fighting everything that has to do with tax havens. the fight against tax havens worldwide is not only a matter of tax justice but also and above all social justice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr tarabella's report because i consider that equality between men and women in the european union, as recognised in the treaty on european union and in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, is a fundamental principle which is still not applied uniformly. despite the pay gap between men and women, occupational segregation and sexist stereotypes, the report aims to focus on the principle of equal pay for equal work, as laid down in the community treaties since 1957, and stresses that the economic, financial and social crisis that is shaking the european union and the world is having a real impact on women, their working conditions, their place in society and equality between women and men in the european union.
in writing. − in its report on equality between men and women in the eu - 2009, the european commission points out that the reconciliation of family and working life, occupational and sectoral segregation, wage differences and the low female employment rate are the main disparities between the sexes. these disparities between men and women are particularly exacerbated in the context of the current economic, financial and social crisis. i voted against the report because i think it has been distorted by introducing issues such as access to abortion and free access to abortion consultations, which are very sensitive issues and which, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, are a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states.
in writing. − i voted against the report on equality between men and women in the eu - 2009 because i considered that it was distorted by introducing issues such as access to voluntary termination of pregnancy (ivg) and free access to consultations on ivg, which are very sensitive issues and which, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, are a matter of exclusive competence of the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the tarabella report on equality between men and women in the european union in 2009 because it contains concrete actions and innovative policies on gender equality. the creation of a directive to prevent and combat all forms of violence against women and the introduction of paternity leave into european legislation are some of the proposals i consider to be fundamental to the promotion of gender equality and to ensure a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities between women and men.
in writing. - the situation is not good for a parliament which demands respect but does not give it. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the work of the european parliament. nevertheless, it has been a regrettable practice to sneak and bluntly introduce divisive issues under these very topics. once again, the camera has lent itself to being a mere sounding board for the most extreme agendas. i can only strongly condemn the attempt to promote the liberalization of abortion and the consequent disregard for human life and dignity under the pretext of defending equality between men and women and, illegitimately, to try to link the two causes and to condition the competences of the member states in this matter in an unacceptable way. the obsession with broadening the concept of sexual and reproductive health to include abortion - and the enforcement of its widespread adoption - highlights the kind of insidious methods used by those who try to make up reality. but it will not be euphemisms designed to numb consciences that will make it less brutal, violence against women less cruel and this initiative less deplorable.
in writing. - "violence against women is perhaps the most shameful violation of human rights. it knows no geographical, cultural or wealth boundaries. as long as it remains, we cannot claim to have made real progress towards equality, development and peace". the words are those of former un secretary-general kofi annan and, unfortunately, they remain unalterably valid. gender discrimination persists in the developed world and in europe today because it is a structural problem with serious consequences in terms of inequality of opportunity. there are still differences between men and women in the education of affections, language, the assignment of domestic duties, access to employment and the performance of professional functions. i believe that access, advancement and performance in the private sector, in public service and even in politics must be based on the merit and quality of each individual, regardless of gender. i voted against the resolution, however, because it introduces sensitive issues such as access to abortion, which are a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states.
in writing. - it was important that this resolution, which enshrines significant women's rights that the conservative right wanted to call into question, was passed in the european parliament. despite some weaknesses, the report managed to highlight important points such as the need for paternity leave to be combined with maternity leave, the issue of sexual and reproductive rights and the need to intensify the fight against inequalities and discrimination at work, against violence and trafficking of women and girls, denouncing poverty and precarious and low-paid work to which many women are subject. it was important that once again it was agreed that 'women should have control over their sexual and reproductive rights, in particular through access to contraception and abortion'. on the eve of the commemorations of the centenary of international women's day and the 15th anniversary of the beijing platform, this resolution is of particular importance. let us hope that its application becomes a reality.
in writing. - inequalities between men and women at various levels, whether occupational, sectoral or stereotypically varied, have been eroding over the years. equality between men and women in the eu is increasingly a reality and, although there are still situations of discrimination, we note the very positive developments we have seen.
in writing. - the european union is currently experiencing a major economic, financial and social crisis, which has serious consequences for women's professional and private lives. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. despite developments in employment and increasing participation in positions of responsibility, greater awareness of equal treatment is still needed. this report is welcome as an opportunity to redefine guidelines for the elimination of gender gaps in the labour market. only then will the eu's goals for growth, jobs and social cohesion be met. it is regrettable, however, that provisions on women's 'sexual and reproductive rights' were included in a report which arose in the context of an economic crisis and whose main concerns were the impact of the crisis on women's working conditions and on women's place in society. for the reasons stated above, and despite this, since the proposed amendments to paragraph 38, which i endorsed and considered essential for the economy of the document, were not adopted, i voted against the report on equality between men and women in the european union.
in writing. − i voted in general in favour of the motion for a resolution on the eu's strategic objectives for the 15th meeting of the conference of the parties to cites, i supported the amendments to include bluefin tuna in 'cites annex ii' in line with the recent recommendations of the ad hoc scientific council of the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations (fao) which in december 2009 supported the announcement of the inclusion of bluefin tuna in 'cites annex ii', with the results of the iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas) plenary assembly which set a considerable reduction in the bluefin tuna fishery to 13500 tonnes, and with the european commission's position reaffirming its concern for the reduction of bluefin tuna, committing itself to more reliable scientific studies. recognising that biodiversity loss is a serious global problem, i believe that other animals should also be the subject of conservation proposals. i see this conference as crucial to the survival and sustainability of many species. in conclusion, i consider it premature to ban international trade in tuna altogether (including this in 'annex i'), which would therefore cause a crisis in the sector, without relying on concrete data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on 'key objectives for the conference of the parties to cites' because the protection of biodiversity must be strengthened at the next conference of the parties to cites. biodiversity is fundamental to the well-being and survival of humanity. we must be ambitious and demand the protection of all endangered species.
in writing. - the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is the main global agreement on the conservation of wild species, with the aim of preventing the over-exploitation of these species by international trade, and it is therefore very important that the european union participate constructively in the 15th conference of the parties in march next year. recognising the importance of the conservation of endangered species for the safeguarding of biodiversity and the ecological balance of the planet, i would point out that sustainable development presupposes the rational use of natural resources, without this impeding the maintenance of activities necessary for development. that is why, at a time when the amendment of the cites annexes is being discussed, i would like to recall the importance of ensuring at the same time adequate protection for wild species at risk without, however, calling into question or condemning to extinction activities which ensure the economic and social viability of various communities.
in writing. - the cites convention is an important instrument for the conservation of endangered species of flora and fauna, particularly those of commercial interest, which as such should be defended and enhanced. we believe that decisions on amendments to this convention, including its annexes - which are important because they allow us to take account of changes in the conservation status of species - should be based on sound scientific data and opinions. as regards the proposal to include bluefin tuna (thunnus thynnus) in cites annex i, we consider that, in the light of the available data, it is not justified. we recall that at the last meeting of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) in november 2009, the experts considered that the species was overexploited, but did not call for a total ban on fishing. the recommendations pointed to a significant decrease in catches, which should be between 8 and 15 thousand tonnes, with a limit of 13500 tonnes. in these circumstances, we consider that we should wait for the assessment and recommendations of the experts following the development of the spring situation in 2010.

the second sub-question: there are indicators that some of the emerging countries that have been less affected by the crisis are becoming drivers of growth in international trade. in this case eu industry needs to retarget its export markets and possibly the future of its products. what strategy does the commission intend to pursue to enable eu industry to become more competitive? third sub-question: the global crisis and subsequent fall in world trade are having multiple effects on developing countries where the most unemployment is concentrated. what adjustment measures does the commission plan to take in its trade relations in particular for the poorest countries in the world? fourth point: while on the one hand large trade deficits are driven by excessive spending and indebtedness in some member states, including the united states of america, on the other hand large export-driven economies in certain emerging countries are experiencing trade surpluses. these trade deficits have contributed to global imbalances that are at the root of the global economic crisis. what strategy does the commission intend to pursue to mitigate such global imbalances in its trade policy? fifth and last point: the social impact of the economic crisis and the subsequent fall in world trade are set to outlast economic recovery. for example, we are seeing signs of economic recovery now, but levels of unemployment remain very high. when does the commission plan to conduct an impact assessment on the impact of the crisis on jobs in europe and in the developing countries? what strategy does it intend to pursue to incorporate the social and environmental dimension of trade into international wto rules? these are the five points that the committee on international trade would like to address to the new trade commissioner mr de gucht, whom i welcome to the floor for the first public exchange of views with parliament and the members of the inta committee, in particular. thank you in advance for the answers that i am sure you will be able to give to the questions that we are putting to you.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are faced with a wall of conflict between two policies which are costly for the european union, consumer protection and public order on the one hand, and freedom of movement and the provision of services on the other. in line with the case law of the court of justice on this matter, member states should retain the autonomy and legitimacy to regulate the activities of operators of games of chance and gambling on the internet. this is a sensitive area which interferes with societal values on deviant behaviour associated with gambling and also with national traditions of channelling the proceeds from this market to finance social works. the case law which has emerged from luxembourg has built up over the last few years a coherent and consistent stream of legal thought which should lead the european institutions and the commission in particular to take a more explicit position. the aim is to create a regulatory framework that is consistent with the cross-cutting concerns of all member states in preventing cross-border organised crime, which uses these types of online gambling to expand, and to provide real protection for consumers vulnerable to these types of online gambling. we expect the new commission, commissioner barnier, which is now taking office, to make this a priority on its agenda.
madam president, commissioner, we are dealing here with a matter of the utmost importance for the protection of the interests of the people and against the risks of fraud which are common in cases of games of chance, including internet games. the member states must retain their autonomy and full legitimacy to legislate in this area of gambling control, following the traditions of their countries and ensuring a more adequate level of protection of consumers and the interests of the population itself, including investments in social areas, as is the case in portugal. the rules of competition and freedom to provide services are therefore not applicable here. we are not dealing with a normal service, we are dealing with a game which has serious implications for the lives of citizens. we therefore hope that the commissioner will take this position into account in the actions he will take, recognising that the member states have every right to continue to legislate in the meantime.
in writing. − the 2007 convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance is of great political and practical importance, as it allows for more effective recovery of child support and helps to resolve often very complicated situations. since the vast majority of maintenance obligations relate to minors, it can be said that the convention is above all a measure for the protection of minors, laying down precise rules as regards the recognition and enforcement of these obligations. this proposal seeks to approve this convention on behalf of the union, which will then exercise exclusive competence over the whole convention. given the importance of this convention, i cannot but support this proposal, although i believe that, while it is the union's responsibility to communicate any declarations and reservations to the convention, member states should nevertheless be able to decide internally what meaning to give to these reservations and declarations, so as to be able to adapt them to their national reality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion by the european community of the convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance. the adoption of this convention will make it possible to introduce a set of harmonised rules at community level applicable to relations with third countries which will become contracting parties to the convention. these measures are the most protective of children, since the vast majority of maintenance claims are made against minors.
in writing. the european commission intends to approve the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance, which is binding on the member states because it was concluded by the community. the commission has external competence to approve the convention. since the practical questions raised by the international recovery of maintenance are not precisely answered, the adoption of this convention could ensure greater effectiveness in the international recovery of maintenance obligations for the benefit of children and other family members, thereby protecting the youngest beneficiaries of such obligations. for this reason, and also for the legal certainty that this gives, i consider it important that this convention be adopted.
