in writing. the 'swift' agreement allows the us treasury department to access financial payment data in order to prevent and combat terrorism and its financing. however, due to technical issues in the swift system, it cannot limit searches to specific data of specific individuals suspected of committing criminal offences. so you have to transfer, in raw form, the information about all transactions in a given country on a given date. this situation does not affect the protection of data of european citizens and businesses, as it respects the principles of proportionality and necessity. the fight against terrorism necessarily involves international judicial cooperation and, in many cases, the transfer of personal data, such as bank details.
in writing. - in accordance with the interim agreement, i support the need for transatlantic cooperation in the fight against international crime and terrorism. i would stress that this cooperation must be based on mutual loyalty and respect for the principles of reciprocity, proportionality and respect for the rights of citizens. but security cannot be superimposed on other rights, freedoms and guarantees, but must be compatible with them. it is not acceptable that the police in portugal can only access the banking data of one person with a court warrant while millions of data can be sent to be known and analysed by the american police without judicial control. i condemn the way the council has behaved towards the european parliament, withholding information and putting it in front of an established fact. it is essential that this should not happen again in the future and that the treaty of lisbon be strictly observed. in view of the above, i am voting in favour of the resolution against the agreement.
in writing. - we welcome the fact that the majority of the ep, to which we contributed, rejected the so-called eu-us 'swift agreement'. the existence of these databases and the exchange or access to them, whether by us authorities or by eu agencies or member state authorities, is proving to be highly uncertain, entailing uncontrollable dangers arising from effective 'control' of citizens by the 'powers that be'. criminals and innocents, suspects and unsuspecting, all enter a process that does not, as has been demonstrated, ensure its effectiveness. the implementation of this agreement would mean the continuation of the wrong measures being taken in the so-called 'fight against terrorism' and its not very innocent mediation for the suppression of rights. we support the need to combat all forms of crime, but this must be done primarily by preventing and preventing such phenomena, and not by increasing the security gap that undermines public freedoms and the fundamental rights and guarantees of citizens, further impoverishing the democracy we have. we will not trade freedom for more security, because in the end we will lose both. we are rather in favour of a more secure society with broad democratic rights and freedoms.
in writing. the vote was on the re-issuing of an agreement which, by detecting banking movements, has been of great importance in combating terrorism, which in recent years has targeted western societies. if the resolution is adopted and the agreement is rejected, terrorist organisations will be able to operate without effective control, with the gravity that this entails. interestingly, many of those on the far left who reject the agreement, claiming it violates the confidentiality of personal data, are the same people who, in their home countries, advocate the end of banking secrecy and the freezing of all banking data. for them, the issue is not the transfer of data but the fact that the transfer is made to the usa, a country with which they cannot conceal their obvious hostility. consequently, the vote against the resolution and in favour of the agreement i have expressed has only considered the very particular circumstances of the need to combat terrorism by all means and the recognition of the fundamental role of the united states in that fight.
in writing. − the fight against international crime, in particular through transatlantic cooperation in the fight against terrorism, is one of the european union's major priorities. but this cooperation must be based on reciprocity and mutual loyalty. the interim agreement between the european union and the united states on the processing and transfer of payment message data does not guarantee european citizens or businesses under us law the same rights and guarantees as they would enjoy in the territory of the european union. the information transfer system does not respect the fundamental principles of european data protection law, in particular the principles of proportionality and necessity. the agreement does not expressly provide for requests to be subject to judicial authorisation or to be limited in time, nor does it define the conditions for sharing data with third countries. i also regret that during the negotiations the council shared virtually no information with the european parliament and that the agreement was voted on after it had entered into force. for these reasons, and because the rights and guarantees of european citizens deserve to be respected, i am voting in favour of the motion for a resolution condemning the conclusion of the swift agreement.

in writing. − a framework agreement on the prevention of injuries caused by sharp objects and piercing in the hospital and health sector has been concluded between hospeem (european hospital and health employers' association) and epsu (federation of european public service unions). the aim of this agreement is to create standards and rules to protect healthcare workers from injuries caused by syringes and other sharp objects, which can cause the transmission of more than 20 deadly viruses and therefore constitute a serious and serious public health problem. the commission is aware of the importance of this framework agreement for the protection of the health of hospital workers and should monitor its implementation and adopt the directive implementing it shortly.
in writing. − injuries caused by syringes and other cutting medical instruments represent one of the most common and serious risks for healthcare professionals across europe, whereas hospital staff and healthcare professionals are often at risk of infections caused by injuries resulting from the use of syringes and other cutting medical instruments, as referred to in the adopted resolution. it is therefore necessary to ensure the highest possible level of safety in the work environment of hospitals and wherever healthcare is provided. we therefore adopted the resolution on the framework agreement, which contains a clause on 'minimum standards', without prejudice to existing and future community and national provisions which are more favourable to workers. member states and/or the social partners should be given the possibility and encouragement to adopt additional measures which are more favourable to workers in the sector concerned.
in writing. − the health of workers at the workplace is not only an occupational matter but also a matter of social responsibility, which means that all the bodies responsible for this area, including the european parliament, must be involved. the framework agreement concluded today between the european social partners in the hospital and health system is an important contribution to the protection of the health and safety of workers in the hospital sectors.

i would point out that in island regions air transport is sometimes the only way of access and that the operating conditions are conditioned by the size of their passenger and cargo flows. while there are island regions where the abundance of these flows is attractive to many air operators - attracting competition and low transport prices, thus improving accessibility - there are others, such as the azores, where these flows are still small and not attractive to the interest of operators. as a result, air fares are higher, constituting an obstacle to the mobility of the population and a constraint on the attraction of tourists who allow this enormous potential for development and diversification of their economic base to flourish and consolidate. this is particularly damaging in times of crisis such as the one we are going through. it is therefore essential to provide temporary support to encourage increased flows so that the market can start to function, and to make these regions, which have a high tourist potential, share the objectives of the transeuropean networks in bringing the peripheries of europe closer together.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. the commission is concerned and saddened by the terrible events in madeira, especially the high number of victims. i would like to express my personal sympathy to all the people of madeira affected by the disaster. the commission extends its condolences to the families of the victims. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the situation is therefore still serious. it is, however, under the control of regional and national forces. support from the european disaster risk reduction mechanism is not required at present. however, the damage is so severe that madeira is hoping to receive financial support from the eu solidarity fund. the commission is currently examining all possibilities for eu financial assistance to madeira. already after the terrible fire disaster in 2003, solidarity aid of over eur 48 million was approved for portugal. the solidarity fund was set up in 2002 to provide financial assistance at eu level to member states affected by major natural disasters. however, the mobilisation of the solidarity fund is subject to certain criteria. the main condition is that the portuguese national government submits a request for assistance. i would remind you that the regulation on the solidarity fund normally allows the mobilisation of the fund only for disasters of a major scale where the sum of the damage exceeds the threshold of 0.6% of the gross national income of the state concerned. for portugal, this currently means that the damage must amount to more than eur 958 million. however, in exceptional circumstances and if specific criteria are met, aid may also be granted for smaller disasters, so-called regional disasters, particularly when they affect outermost regions such as madeira. since the commission has only limited knowledge of the extent of the damage, it is too early to say whether these conditions are met. the portuguese authorities should now undertake a rapid and thorough assessment of the damage and submit a request to the commission within 10 weeks. this friday my colleague mr hahn will meet mr pereira, the portuguese minister of the interior, to discuss the way forward. mr hahn will visit madeira on 6 and 7 march to get a firsthand impression of the situation. the services of dg regional policy are ready to provide all possible assistance to the portuguese authorities in preparing the application. i want to remind you that our solidarity fund grants are not paid out immediately. the fund is an instrument to help member states in the financial management of disasters, but it is not an emergency instrument. the solidarity fund is financed by an additional contribution from the member states over and above the normal budget. that is why they must be approved by the european parliament, that is to say by you, and by the council by means of an amendment. the procedure takes several months from the time the application is submitted to the time the payment is received. however, we in the commission will make every effort to keep the procedure as short as possible. the structural funds are not available for direct emergency aid. you may be able to contribute to help with longer-term reconstruction. the commission will discuss options and possible useful and necessary programme changes with the portuguese administrative authorities at short notice. i can assure you that the commission will do everything in its power to help the people and authorities of madeira to cope with this terrible natural disaster!

the rapporteur. - i would also like to address a group of 50 fishermen who are probably entering the chamber now and who have come to watch this debate and the vote on the report. i think i can speak here on behalf of all the members of the committee on fisheries who have worked hard on this report to say that it is with great satisfaction that we have seen this day arrive, this day when the report is presented to the house and put to the vote. why would you do that? because the common fisheries policy is one of the emblematic features of the european union, which had a rather difficult beginning, having formally started in the 1980s, having undergone its first reform in 2002 and, knowing today some of the main problems that were diagnosed then (i am referring to overcapacity, overfishing, overinvestment which is not the same throughout the european union, it occurs), because these problems still remain in large part. this is the starting point for reform, for a reform which must be broad, profound and which the sector has been waiting for for a long time. what direction should this reform take, according to what we have presented in the report? first, at the level of principles, in a requirement for a balance between its environmental, social and economic aspects: environmental, to ensure the conservation of stocks; social, to ensure the appreciation and dignity of the profession; and economic to ensure the income of the activity. without these three aspects we will not have fisheries in the european union, at least not sustainable and capable of development, which is what we all want. how can these general principles, which aim to fish less, earn more and preserve stocks better, be put into practice? the report points out some fundamental aspects: investing in decentralization; strengthening the power of intervention of fishermen and the whole fishing industry in power, in decision-making; greater investment in management, which will also allow a policy of compliance and responsibility; the need to distinguish between a small-scale and industrial fleet, with specific regimes for each of them; the need to reflect on management models that are better adapted to different fishing areas and different types of fisheries; it is important to strengthen the market by targeting fishing for value-added products and by increasing the price of the first sale; to link subsidies to the requirements of good practice; to make the modernisation of the fleet conditional on safety and hygiene; to decisively develop aquaculture, an ecologically sustainable aquaculture in the european union; to develop other sectors related to catching such as processing. and let us not forget the call for attention to the growing role of women in fisheries, the need to require that fishery products from third countries, which are imported into our european union, be subject to the same requirements as our producers: certification, labelling, traceability and, finally, the integration of fisheries into the european maritime policy as a broad context for enhancing their capacities. let me conclude by saying that the work we are presenting here today is the result of the joint efforts of all my colleagues in the committee on fisheries, and in particular of the shadow rapporteurs with whom we have worked very closely, as well as with the commission, the secretariat of the european parliament, the epp adviser and other advisers from other political families and also, of course, my own office and my assistant for fisheries. it is indeed a joint work that we are presenting here and that we hope will be adopted here as well.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, in its green paper, the commission is making progress in its attempt to establish, in stages or not, a community system of transferable fishing rights, that is, private property rights for access to exploitation of a public good: fishery resources. this proposal was rejected at the time of the last reform, but ten years later the commission is back in charge, and it is the commission itself that anticipates the inevitable consequences of this privatisation of resources: the concentration of activity by entities with greater economic and financial power and the destruction of a significant part of small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing. it is telling that countries that have chosen this path, as iceland is, are now looking to retreat, faced with the nefarious and perverse consequences of this system. this parliament should take a clear position in rejecting this proposal. it should be said that this solution does not guarantee the sustainability of fish stocks, since the reduction and concentration of rights in a handful of operators does not necessarily mean a reduction in fishing effort, but only the concentration of exploitation of resources. the defence of resource sustainability requires other measures such as the guarantee of a fair return in the sector. this in turn requires market intervention and improved marketing in the sector, improving the first sale price, increasing the remuneration of fishermen's work, reducing intermediation margins and promoting a fair distribution of added value along the value chain of this sector. the reality of fisheries in the european union is complex and diverse. in these circumstances, the consensus on the importance of local management is in sharp contradiction with the institutional framework established by the lisbon treaty, which establishes the conservation of marine biological resources as an exclusive competence of the european union. we need management based on scientific knowledge, taking account of the realities and specificities of each country, each fishing zone, each fleet and each resource, and involving fishermen in the solutions and their implementation. this is very different from the mere decentralized implementation of a centrally defined policy.
as has been said by several speakers, environmentally sustainable, economically viable and socially decent fishing is the objective which we have so far unsuccessfully sought to achieve in the common fisheries policy. the commission's green paper makes a good diagnosis of the situation in the sector, raises many questions, but is very hesitant about solutions. this report also sets out a broad set of principles and consensus-based guidelines which will now need to be translated into concrete action if that objective is to be achieved in the shortest possible time. the rapporteur's effort in seeking them out and, above all, her capacity to accept compromises which removed the most controversial issues from her initial report, are to be commended. the commission now has the enormous responsibility of presenting us with its legislative proposal with the concrete measures that will make it possible to put into practice the principles contained in this report, which i am sure we will adopt by a large majority.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the azorean fishermen here. i also welcome the fact that this report presents a major development compared with the current cfp and includes measures of particular relevance to the outermost regions, such as the distinction between artisanal and industrial fleets and the creation of biogeographical regions. i also welcome the introduction of the amendments by the socialist group, which moderate the rapporteur's initial position in defending individually transferable quotas, as defended by the azorean fisheries organisations. in the same vein, we note the amendments tabled by the socialist group in defence of the principle of relative stability. we believe that the creation of biogeographical regions should be extended to the outermost regions, using them as a model of privileged management appropriate to existing resources. in addition, in order to maintain the good environmental status of marine areas and to respect the precautionary principle, the limit of 100 nautical miles islands should be reassessed, and the recovery of 200 miles is urgent, so that ... the rapporteur. - i would like to thank everyone who was here today in the plenary and who has continued to make such a valuable contribution to this long process, which, as the commissioner has just said, must continue in order to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves. the truth is that we know that it is impossible to please everyone in a report. many will say that we have not gone far enough in some respects, others will say that we have gone too far in other respects or even in those respects. i think that what is important at this stage is to stress that we have succeeded in establishing a good balance between the main issues with this report, a broad consensus, and that, taken as a whole, it has the capacity, the potential to respond in a satisfactory way to the needs, i would even say the requirements, of the sector. as we have done in the committee on fisheries, under the chairmanship of mrs fraga, i hope that we will now continue this work within the committee and, more broadly, with the council and the european commission, in moving forward with what is an equally hard job, that of legislative proposals. i believe that if we continue to work in this direction, in a team spirit and understanding that we need to consider all the issues that are important in different parts of our large european union, and if we actually try to respond to all the needs of the fisheries sector in our large exclusive economic zone, we will indeed be working for the sector. that is what we are committed to: to create the conditions for the fisheries sector to be truly sustainable and developed in the long term.
in writing. i would like to congratulate mrs maria do céu patrão neves on her work and on the report which is now being voted on. the fisheries issue is certainly a sensitive one for the portuguese, since we have several fishing communities, and it is absolutely crucial for the cds-pp. i believe that a new regulation of the cfp is needed, one which is more efficient and adapted to the various territorial realities. i therefore welcome the intention to rely on the principles of regionalization and subsidiarity, giving greater autonomy to the states and greater flexibility to the cfp. at the same time, aware that environmental challenges pose serious problems for fisheries resources, i consider it essential that the new cfp should allow for ecologically sustainable and economically viable fisheries. we are not unaware of the problems facing fishermen, and we want the new cfp to adequately protect the fishing capacity of communities that live off fishing. i also believe that it is essential that the new cfp ensures fish of sufficient quality and quantity to maintain a diet rich in fish, which we now know is more balanced and contributes to a healthy life. i shall be following with interest and particular attention the future reform of the cfp, and i shall always defend portuguese interests in this strategic sector.
the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy embodies the opportunity to review this european policy and does so in its various dimensions (economic, social and environmental), redefining new guidelines with a view to solving the remaining problems in this sector. the reform of the common fisheries policy is particularly important for the outermost regions, where fisheries are of great importance for local development and the lives of the population. the green paper report insists on reforms which i believe are necessary for a better implementation of this policy at regional level, in particular a decentralisation of fisheries management which covers the specificities of the regions and which links the sustainability of the sector with the preservation of species. in madeira, it is imperative to modernise vessels and promote measures to ensure the economic viability of fishing activities. improving the efficiency of fisheries management and a strategy for financial support for fishermen are priorities which i reiterate as essential in this reform and which must be implemented at regional level. the reform of the common fisheries policy marks the beginning of a new phase in the evolution of the sector, with more active participation of the various actors at national, regional and fisheries level.
i would like to say that the amending budget we have just adopted, amounting to eur 13.4 million, with effect from 1 may, i.e. for six months, is very unwise. there is a part of it, which concerns the reinforcement of the human resources of parliamentary committees and parliamentary groups, worth eur 4.5 million, which can be supported because, in fact, the treaty of lisbon places new legislative requirements on this parliament, but increasing by eur 8 million the resources of members for the recruitment of assistants, which will not be 8 but 16 next year, is clearly excessive, even because next year there is a further increase of eur 1500 per month for members, which amounts not to eur 16 but to eur 32 million. at a time when we are faced with a huge situation of unemployment and social crisis in all our countries, it is not sustainable to increase the resources of members without at the same time having the courage to cut the expenditure and the cost-sharing aid to which we as members are entitled, and which are not all, far from it, entirely justified. i cannot understand how a member of the european parliament, on the day he travels, can receive 300 euros in cost-sharing aid, plus the distance allowance and the time allowance, which are entirely tax-free. we can cut unnecessary expenses and then discuss how we can improve our means for legislative production. not to do this at the same time is simply to disregard the difficulties our constituents are going through. we have an obligation to set an example, today we set a bad example.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty has given the european union more competence in the field of energy policy. it is essential that the member states work together to ensure that their citizens have a more efficient, safer and cheaper energy policy. it is important to ensure the stability needed to reduce the risk of another gas-related crisis between ukraine and russia and thus provide the security of supply that eu member states and their consumers expect. the eu has made energy one of its top priorities. the energy and climate package aims to increase the competitiveness of eu industry in a world with increasingly restrictive carbon emissions. this regulation on investment projects relating to energy infrastructure in the european union will help to make the market more transparent and more predictable, supporting our companies and creating a positive environment for competitiveness.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on the notification to the commission of investment projects in energy infrastructure in the european community and repealing council regulation (ec) no 736/96, as it will enable the commission to monitor the situation of this infrastructure and anticipate potential problems, particularly of an environmental nature. the importance of environmental impact assessment of energy infrastructure projects should therefore be emphasised, so that their construction and closure can be carried out in a sustainable manner.
in writing. − given the importance of an integrated energy policy, not only to combat climate change and reduce co2 emissions, but also to ensure efficiency and reduce europe's energy dependence, the communication and transmission of data on energy infrastructure investments and projects is essential. it is important for european energy policy that the commission has a current view of the evolution of energy investments in the member states, so that it can develop integrated policies that promote greater energy efficiency and investment in cleaner technologies, ensuring progressive energy independence from external suppliers and fossil fuels. i therefore support this proposal for a regulation, with particular regard to its necessary application, which was not the case with the previous regulation which it is intended to replace.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation contributes to the implementation of a european energy policy aimed at efficiency, reliability and security. energy efficiency is a priority policy of the european union in view of the need to conserve and make the most of resources and the commitments made in the context of combating climate change. i would remind you that before moving on to new projects, the eu's target of 20% energy efficiency should be taken into account. therefore, investment projects in energy infrastructure should be compatible with the objective of achieving, by 2020, the minimum level of 20% for energy from sustainable renewable sources. the energy policy advocated must ensure low carbon production and be based on the principles of solidarity and sustainability. the reliability of the system is important as it must be operated without interruption and the deterioration of the energy supply situation inside and outside the union must be taken into account. the commission also stresses the crucial investment in infrastructure to avoid security problems in energy supply.
in writing. the rapporteur believes that this is indeed an important part of eu energy policy, based on the principle that without adequate information on our energy infrastructures, it is not possible to effectively promote a 'european energy policy at eu level'. but beyond our fundamental disagreement on european energy policy, there is also the legal basis on which this report is based, namely the framework of the internal market. however, there are positive aspects which are also considered here, in particular when it says that it is essential that the confidentiality of the information is guaranteed and that the resulting proposals are neutral and not equivalent to market intervention at political level. in addition, compliance with the reporting obligations should be easy to implement, in order to avoid any unnecessary administrative burden for undertakings and the administration of the member states or the commission. hence our final abstention vote.
in writing. − the eu's energy policy is very relevant to the near future of the use of renewable energy. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, decisions on matters related to energy policy are taken in co-decision, so it is necessary to readjust the regulations on the basis of the new eu legal reality. therefore, in order to enable all member states to communicate in an appropriate and useful way the planned developments in energy infrastructure, a new regulation is needed to make this easier and more agile.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution which stresses the importance of strengthening cooperation between the eu and ukraine. the political and economic stabilisation of ukraine and the strengthening of cooperation between ukraine and the eu in the energy field are essential conditions for the recognition of ukraine's european aspirations. the stability of the eu also depends on the stability of its neighbours.
in writing. - i recall the hope brought by the orange revolution and the break with the past of soviet influence it brought to the ukrainian people. i remember the promises of success, progress, democracy and cooperation that were then made to the ukrainians, both internally and externally. the european union then emerged as the probable destiny of a people who were clearly taking a turn towards the west. after the euphoria, it seems clear today that the protagonists of the orange revolution have failed the challenge, and the popular disillusionment with the country's destiny is equally evident. the election of the candidate defeated by yushchenko in december 2004 demonstrates both a major split in the country and a change in popular sentiment, now more favorable to russian influence. i think it is important that the european union should be able to maintain the attractiveness of ukraine to its sphere and to use the various means at its disposal to this end. i hope that ukraine will persevere and persevere in its drive towards internal democratisation and that, while respecting its past and its history, it will embark on a journey of convergence with the eu, culminating in its accession as a full member.
in writing. − following the break-up of the eastern bloc and the union of soviet republics, the ukrainian people and institutions have been strongly committed to the democratization of the country and the construction of a modern society through the development of a social, economic and political system that allows for the strengthening of the rule of law and respect for human rights, despite the difficulties normally inherent in a state in the process of regenerating its structural organization and political identity. as a reference and promoting area for peace and the economic, social and cultural development of the peoples, the european union has a duty to play a decisive role in the development of the democratic regime in ukraine, in particular by strengthening the mechanisms of european integration. this will also help to pacify regional conflicts within the country, which are of great geostrategic importance for the eu, given relations with russia and central asia, especially at the energy level. in this process, i would also like to stress the contribution of this motion for a resolution to the integration of the strong ukrainian immigrant community into the eu, as well as the value of the role of young people and education in the social, economic and cultural progress of ukraine.
in writing. − the recent elections in ukraine and, in the light of the statements by the osce/odhir election observation mission, which considered that international standards were largely met, are a sign that this country continues to move positively towards future integration into the eu area. it is important, however, that ukrainian politicians and authorities work to ensure that political and economic stabilisation is a reality in the near future. this requires the implementation of the necessary constitutional reforms, consolidation of the rule of law, establishment of a social market economy and renewed efforts to combat corruption and improve the business and investment climate.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the 13th session of the united nations human rights council. the new eu institutional structure offers a unique opportunity to increase the eu's coherence, visibility and credibility in the un human rights council. the action of the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy will also increase the eu's capacity to cooperate with countries in other regional blocs to end human rights violations, including violence directed at women and children.
in writing. − the politicization of the human rights council and the constant blockade of stronger positions condemning human rights violations in various parts of the world justify a change in its structure and mode of action. the announced candidacy of iran is yet another sign that the path taken by this body may be unreliable and unsafe and that states with a history of repeated human rights violations may use membership of this council to seek to whitewash these same violations. the european union must actively participate in the council's work, aware of its limitations and problems, and seek to impose a balanced but rigorous and demanding view of what respect for human rights should be. if you do, you will be living up to your particular responsibilities in this matter.
in writing. − the human rights council (unhrc) is a platform devoted to universal human rights and is a specific forum dedicated to human rights in the united nations system. the promotion and safeguarding of the universality of human rights are part of the legal, ethical and cultural heritage of the european union and constitute a foundation of its unity and integrity. i am sure that the eu member states will actively oppose any attempt to weaken the concepts of universality, indivisibility and interdependence of human rights. i hope that the member states will actively participate in the annual interactive debate on the rights of persons with disabilities and in the annual meeting on the rights of the child. i stress the importance of the 13th session of the unhrc, which will be attended by ministers and other high-level representatives, and which has on its agenda the economic and financial crisis and the united nations declaration on human rights education and training. finally, i welcome the renewed commitment of the united states to the united nations bodies and its subsequent election as a member of the unhrc, as well as the constructive work in the field of freedom of expression carried out at the 64th un general assembly.
in writing. - we strongly agree with the concept set out in the report on the universality, indivisibility and interdependence of human rights. however, starting from these same assumptions, it is necessary to underline the irreconcilable contradiction between this perspective and the profound attack on the rights of workers and peoples that the crisis of the capitalist system is generating, namely: high unemployment rates, increasing poverty, increasingly difficult access to quality public services at affordable prices. unfortunately, the majority of the ep did not take this contradiction into account. we regret the rejection of proposals from our group, in particular the following: - stresses that un member states should promote food sovereignty and food security as a means of reducing poverty and unemployment; - welcomes the fact that a report by the united nations high commissioner for human rights on human rights violations in honduras since the coup d'état is on the agenda for its 13th session; calls on the eu member states to make efforts to support a strong condemnation of the coup and the restoration of democracy and the rule of law in that country; - expresses its concern at the situation in colombia, in particular the discovery of thousands of unidentified dead;
in writing. - the human rights council is an intergovernmental body whose main purpose is to respond to situations of human rights violations, and given that one of the foundations of european unity and integrity is respect for and safeguarding the universality of human rights, i would just like to leave a vote of encouragement to the unhrc to continue to oppose all forms of discrimination.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on beijing + 15 un platform for action on gender equality, taking into account that the strategic objectives of the beijing platform have not yet been achieved and that gender inequality and stereotypes persist, with women continuing to occupy a subordinate position to men in the areas covered by the platform. we regret the lack of up-to-date, reliable and comparable data at both national and eu level for the indicators approved for the follow-up of the beijing platform, including women and poverty, violence against women, institutional mechanisms, women and armed conflict and female children. the commission should continue to develop the annual evaluation of the implementation of the beijing platform for action and make effective use of the indicators and analytical reports as a contribution to different policy areas and as a basis for further initiatives towards the achievement of gender equality. we reiterate the need to systematically implement and monitor the integration of the gender perspective in legislative and budgetary processes as well as in other relevant processes, strategies, programmes and projects in different policy areas.
in writing. − gender equality is a fundamental principle in our day, but inequalities between men and women persist and the strategic objectives of the beijing platform are still far from being achieved. i welcome the motion for a resolution voted on today in this house as an incentive to strengthen the institutional mechanisms for promoting equality between men and women. the mainstreaming of gender in development cooperation is essential to promote a more prosperous, fairer and richer society. i would like to stress the importance of the role of women in science and technology. women are increasingly present in areas of scientific research, yet they remain far from the top of careers and decision-making centres. harnessing this potential is essential to promote a fair balance and to support growth and jobs. it is essential to consider gender mainstreaming in different policy areas as one of the pillars for a richer, more prosperous and fairer society.
in writing. - as a strong supporter of human rights and the principle of equality, i could not question initiatives aimed at protecting the rights of women and girls, who are often severely violated, in a world where women are still the main victims of crimes against their physical integrity and sexual self-determination. however, equality between men and women must not, at any time, forget the natural, social and cultural differences between the sexes: equal rights is not the same as equal treatment. it is necessary to treat men and women equally, giving them the same rights but taking into account their special needs, which in the case of women is evident in areas such as maternity protection, reconciliation of work and family life and very special protection against crimes which are essentially committed against women and children, such as sexual exploitation, trafficking in human beings or ill-treatment. finally, i would stress that any initiative by the union in this area cannot be intended to confer on women, in the name of their sexual and reproductive health, a right to voluntary termination of pregnancy, a matter which must remain the exclusive sphere of decision of the states.
in writing. − gender equality is a fundamental principle of the european union, enshrined in the ec treaty. it is thus a specific mission of the union to promote and mainstream equality between women and men. it is unquestionable that today, in both the underdeveloped and the developed countries - and specifically in the european union - the deplorable reality of gender discrimination persists at the most diverse social, economic and cultural levels. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the environmentally sensitive products. this structural problem is a barrier to the progress and development of communities in particular and of humanity in general. i believe that eradicating domestic violence is an absolute priority, and for this it will be important to ensure cultural, social and economic equality between men and women. the economic and financial crisis, the impact of climate change and the ageing of society are variables that the european commission and the member states should take into account in their actions and policies aimed at promoting gender equality.
in writing. - inequalities between men and women at various levels, whether occupational, sectoral or stereotypically varied, have been eroding over the years. equality between men and women in the eu is increasingly a reality and, although there are still situations of discrimination, we note the very positive developments we have seen.
in writing. - the treaty of lisbon gives the european parliament increased powers. on the other hand, in a globalised world, matters are becoming increasingly complex and decisions need to be based on technical and scientific knowledge. it is essential that policy-makers are aware of recent scientific developments to enable them to make the best choices. this budget takes the decisions with cuts in the building section and increases in technical support to members provides the means for this parliament to perform its duties with excellence and with the scientific and technical foundations so necessary in the 21st century.
in writing. − in view of the new role of the european parliament in the context of the lisbon treaty and the new tasks conferred on it, and in view of the commitment made when the 2010 budget was adopted, it makes sense to increase the funds available to parliament for its functioning, ensuring all the material and human conditions so that this body can fulfil its tasks in the new institutional framework with rigor and excellence. this increase in funding should not, however, jeopardise the budgetary sustainability and the strictness of accounts which are necessary in any institution. in addition, the management of the funds made available under this budget should be rigorous and transparent.
in writing. − this amending budget for the financial year 2010, relating to the budget of the european parliament (section i of the general budget of the union), now amounts to eur 1 616 760 399, which represents 19.99% of the initial heading 5, adopted at first reading. we have reduced the reserve for buildings from eur 15 million to eur 11 million in this amendment. the need for this budget arises from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. parliament is taking on new powers, new responsibilities. our priority is legislative excellence, and to achieve this we must give members, committees and political groups the means to do so. the legal, budgetary and financial discipline rules are respected in this amending budget. as rapporteur for this budget for the epp, i believe that budgetary rigor and the desire to save must be present, more than ever, during its implementation. i therefore reiterate the importance of drawing up a 'zero-base' budget which ensures greater rigor and transparency and i ask for urgent information on the ep's fixed expenditure. i would stress the need for long-term planning of housing policy to ensure fiscal sustainability.
in writing. - the adoption and subsequent entry into force of the treaty of lisbon brings increased responsibility for the european parliament, with the corresponding administrative burden. since legislative excellence is a priority for the european parliament, it is necessary to provide members with the necessary material and human resources to make this a reality. this new budgetary allocation must, however, respect the utilization ratios of the amounts of heading 5 (administrative appropriations) of the mff, which have been set at 20% of the value of that heading, in order to maintain budgetary sustainability.
in writing. − the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon led to the adoption of a proposal to amend the budget for the financial year 2010 to cover the additional budgetary needs of the european parliament. considering that legislative excellence is the priority of the european parliament, i stress the importance of giving members, committees and political groups the means to achieve it and the means to accommodate their overall needs in terms of long-term real estate policy. the amending budget for the financial year 2010 thus amounts to eur 1 616 760 399, which represents 19.99% of the initial heading 5, approved at first reading, and the reserve for buildings, which was eur 15 million, has been reduced to eur 11 million. i would stress the importance of including in the report the achievement of a zero-based budget which ensures greater budgetary sustainability and the need for it to be in line with the annual legislative programme. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the document which will enable the european parliament to be provided with adequate means to meet the expenses associated with its new role after the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − the fisheries sector is of strategic importance for the socioeconomic well-being of coastal communities, local development, employment, preservation and creation of economic activities. it is essential to ensure the sustainable development of this sector, both economically and socially, but it is also necessary to ensure the maintenance of good environmental status in all marine waters of the european union. the implementation of the cfp is directly linked to issues such as environmental protection, climate change, security, public health, consumer protection and regional development, internal and international trade, relations with third countries and development cooperation, and it is therefore essential to ensure fair and careful harmonisation between all these areas. i stress the need to use a coherent framework within the european research area to support the sustainable use of oceans and seas. it is also essential to take account of the nature of the constraints affecting the outermost regions (ors), the permanence, intensity and combination of which differentiate them from other eu regions with geographical disadvantages and/or demographic problems.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs patrão neves on her excellent report on the reform of the common fisheries policy. the numerous problems and challenges of the cfp were identified in 2002 and have now been compounded by the economic and energy crises and the adverse effects of climate change. the cfp must introduce a set of far-reaching changes to serve the interests of today's fisheries, ensuring a fair balance between conservation of resources and the profitability of the sector, and opening the door to new management systems for the different fisheries in the eu. i welcome the concern to decentralise and de-bureaucratise the cfp and to regionalise fisheries management within the limits imposed by the lisbon treaty, as well as the need to ensure differentiated treatment for small-scale coastal fishing and industrial fishing, while respecting environmental, economic and social requirements. i would also stress the defence of the interests of community fisheries, but the national governments must be given the necessary support, since they must make fishing a strategic priority for the economic and social viability of coastal communities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy because essential commitments were made which made it possible to clearly improve the initial proposal. i would like to stress the importance of introducing an environmental and social approach in the search for new fisheries management systems which are complementary to the current system, based on the principle of relative stability.
in writing. - i would first like to stress the excellence of the report drawn up by mrs patrão neves. fisheries communities are currently facing a period of difficulty characterised by a sharp deterioration in fishery resources: this activity has an impact on the food supply of the general population and on the cohesion of the peripheral regions of the european union. an integrated and comprehensive approach to the reform of the common fisheries policy is therefore needed. i consider it urgent and essential that the european union should make an effective effort to ensure better conditions for economic sustainability for fishermen, within a framework which safeguards the specificities of each region and which recognises the differentiated attention to be given to small-scale fishing. i would stress the need for concrete measures, such as reducing the number of intermediaries in the chain between producer and consumer. the reform cannot be dissociated from the sustainable exploitation of marine resources, in a process of scientific and technical evaluation, which will contribute to the pacification of the sector and, at the same time, will have an impact on the quality and food safety of consumers. in the context of the adjustment of fishing capacity, i would stress the impact of the modernisation of equipment on the professional dignity and safety of fishermen in a sector where human losses are recurrent.
in writing. - the rejection by the majority of this parliament of the proposals we have put forward, rejecting the privatisation of fisheries resources, is indicative of the path that the next reform of the cfp is intended to take. the parliament not only does not reject the commission's proposal to create (private) property rights for access to the exploitation of a public good - it was necessary - but it paves the way for the enshrinement of this desired right. this is an option which does not safeguard the sustainability of resources and which will inevitably lead to a concentration of activity in the entities with the greatest economic and financial power at eu level, seriously threatening small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing which, in the case of portugal, represents more than 90% of the fleet. we note some positive aspects of the report, which in some cases correspond to the proposals we have put forward, but we cannot fail to note that, overall, the report does not depart from a very liberal framework and a strong limitation of the sovereignty of the states over their marine resources. the commission has also failed to give a full answer to one of the core problems facing the sector: the problem of earnings from activity. we cannot but note the rejection of the proposals we have put forward to improve the marketing of the sector by increasing the remuneration of fishermen's work.
in writing. − the common fisheries policy, last revised in 2002, is no longer the most appropriate policy to deal with the vicissitudes of this sensitive sector. it is therefore necessary to analyse the new factors influencing it and to find new solutions to make it more viable at all levels, including economic, social and environmental. it is therefore urgent to take further measures to help the fisheries sector to overcome the precarious situation in which it finds itself. fishing is very important in the eu. it is therefore essential that the new cfp takes account of the rational and responsible management of resources, that it is concerned with the protection of marine resources and with the maintenance of the livelihoods of those who have always lived from fishing. the new cfp must be able to solve the productivity problems of the sector, stabilise markets and ensure a good standard of living for the families who depend on it. however, this sector must be analysed in a global rather than a segmented way so that we can integrate all the problems and vicissitudes of the sector, so that the problems can be solved in a way that satisfies everyone and thus overcome the major problems affecting it: over-fishing, overcapacity, over-investment and waste.
in writing. - the report on the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy, which we adopted today, sets out a review of the policy in its economic, social and environmental dimensions, with the aim of redefining the guidelines for solving the remaining problems in the sector. improving the efficiency of fisheries management and a strategy for financial support for fishermen, as well as ensuring the sustainability of the sector through the preservation of species, are priorities which i reiterate as essential in this reform and which must be implemented at regional level. this document stresses the need for reforms in the fisheries sector, which is of great importance in the outermost regions, particularly in madeira, where this activity plays a major role in local development and the lives of the population. i repeat the ideas expressed in the report on the need for more active involvement of the various actors at national, regional and local level in implementing and technical measures to be taken in the fisheries sector. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which will be the beginning of a new phase in the european common fisheries policy.
mr president, on this occasion marking the centenary of the proclamation of international women's day, which has become a symbol of revolutionary struggle, a world day of action by women for their rights and against all forms of discrimination, i greet all women, but in a very special way all those who continue to be victims of discrimination, inequalities and various forms of violence. and at this point it is important to highlight the timeliness of this struggle for equality in law and in life, bearing in mind that the crisis of capitalism has particular consequences for the lives of women, the main victims of precarious and low-paid work. and from poverty! women make up the majority of the 85 million people living in poverty in the european union. therefore, while we mark this day and urge all women not to give up on their dreams, we insist on the priority of fighting injustice and discrimination, tearing new horizons for a better life and equality.
mr president, when the euro was strong a year or two ago, the wall street journal bet on its fall and explained how it could happen. the economies of the euro are very diverse, he said. just let the most vulnerable fall. that's what happened, and nowadays everyone complains about foreign speculators. but it would be better if they complained about themselves than about the european leaders. no one has forced us to make a monetary union without political union and without social cohesion. and no one has forced us to hesitate and falter when the economies, the so-called "peripheral" economies, are under attack. one thing must be made very clear: there are no peripheral economies. when a euro economy is under attack, it is the euro that is under attack, it is the union that is under attack and it must respond in solidarity. the same solidarity that was for eastern europe, that was for germany in its reunification. if it wasn't for solidarity today, it will be for self-interest later, given the size of these markets and the size of their debt and the exposure that the central european banks have to them. it better be out of solidarity.
in the last three months, six very serious maritime accidents have occurred in portugal, in which thirteen fishermen have lost their lives, eight of whom have not yet been recovered, and there has also been a total loss of vessels, the livelihood of many others. the fishing communities of castelo de neive, matosinhos, setúbal, areosa, peniche and caminha are in mourning, and i want to join them in this witness today. in a very harsh winter, with few days of work and little support for fishermen on land, we are forced to go to sea in adverse conditions. the ageing of some vessels, the lack of safety on board and good training at this level further increase the potential for accidents. this is an unacceptable reality which must be eradicated. in this context, the establishment of conditions guaranteeing the safety of fishermen should be one of the priority objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy through investment in the modernisation of vessels, the strengthening of safety measures, training of fishermen in basic safety and decent living conditions when the state of the sea advises to stay ashore.
for the gue/ngl group i believe that the technical discussion we have to have is undoubtedly very important, but it cannot hide the fact that the choice before us is a political one. and so to conduct and build the whole argument on a technical basis to avoid having to make the political choice is not very legitimate. mr haglund, for example, explained that if we had a tobin tax, we would not have avoided the financial crisis. and i might agree with him, but we would certainly have much more resources to be able to combat the effects of the financial crisis on our economies and on the most disadvantaged sectors of the european population. and that is, therefore, the question at stake here. and the second aspect concerns... and that is why i was not convinced by commissioner šemeta's mr president, the european parliament is right to raise a number of questions on this subject and not to take a definitive position on the new financial transaction tax. there are, in fact, several reasons for this. we have heard from the advocates of the tax. that it is a political problem, that technical solutions are of little interest. first, you go through the rate, then you see how it's going to be applied. it's a mistake. i know. it is not ideology that will solve the problem of the financial crisis. secondly, that this would be a tax which could help the most disadvantaged, a sort of robin hood tax, because the most advantaged outgrow their situation with economic growth. the problem of european or global scale is of little importance. it's also an escape from the issue. what would happen if only europe had this kind of tax? there are a few elements that have to be taken into account. in a time of crisis, a new tax is not going to solve anything. it is not with a new tax that we are going to solve the problem of public finances. it is not a new tax, which acts as a kind of sanction tax, a punishment tax. a tax that's meant to punish those responsible for the crisis. the final consumers are the ones who suffer from a new tax. the people who are going to suffer from a new tax are the people who need credit. secondly, there are a number of technical problems to be solved. the ones who don't care. is there a european administrative system that can apply such a tax? does anyone know what the cost of this same application is? can anyone tell me what effect it has on liquidity and credit? how will a global tax be applied to time differences and transactions made by the second? how do you control all this? all these questions are unanswered. it seems to me that in a crisis, lessons must be learned, actions must be taken. i doubt it's a new tax.

in writing. the prosperity of the eu will depend on the success of smes. the eu and the member states must therefore create a favourable environment for these companies. the biggest obstacle cited by smes is the completion of administrative formalities. in fact, smes bear a disproportionate regulatory and administrative burden compared to large companies. it is estimated that for every euro a large company spends on a worker due to regulatory obligations, a small company may have to spend up to ten euros. the commission proposal extends the concept of micro-enterprises to include enterprises which, at the balance sheet date, do not exceed the limits of two of the following criteria: balance sheet total of eur 500 000, net turnover of eur 1 000 000 and/or an average number of employees during the financial year of 10 persons. member states may choose to exempt such micro-enterprises from the application of the community directive on annual accounts. in any case, micro-enterprises will continue to keep their sales and transaction records for the purposes of their management and tax information. in portugal, 356 140 portuguese companies can be covered by this exemption.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we are talking today about absurd situations, such as a student who obtains a visa to come to belgium to study. since he is not covered by directive 2004/114/ec, he cannot go to the netherlands to collect information in a specialist library in order to write his thesis or to take advantage of a weekend to visit barcelona because he is detained in the country that issued the visa. the schengen convention provides that holders of a long-stay visa may only reside in the territory of the member state which issued the visa. they shall not travel to other member states or transit through other member states on their return to their country of origin. schengen means freedom of movement. anyone who is legally resident in a member state should be able to move freely within that area where there are no internal borders. the ideal solution would be for member states to comply with their obligation to grant a residence permit to third-country nationals holding such a visa. but that is not the case in the vast majority of member states. member states have temporarily reversed this situation by issuing d+c visas, allowing long-stay visa holders to move freely within the schengen area during the first three months. these visas will be abolished as from april 2010 with the entry into force of the community visa code, which makes it more urgent to find a solution to this problem. the amendments i have proposed, which have the support of the majority of the members of the libe committee, help to solve this problem without reducing the level of security in the schengen area. the obligation to consult the schengen information service when processing long-stay visa applications is a procedure identical to that already in place for third-country nationals holding residence permits. we are thus responding to fears of increased insecurity. it is true that several member states have issued long-stay visas and, subsequently, residence permits without consulting the sis, in particular the article 96 alerts for refusal of admission. this practice undermines the security of the schengen area and creates problems at the external borders when persons with a valid visa are flagged in sis. this creates unnecessary and complicated situations for people and border guards who will have to try to find out whether the visas are forged or whether the entry in the sis is incorrect and should be deleted or whether these visas should never have been issued. the initiative we are going to vote on will allow long-stay visa holders to move freely for a period of three months every six months, the same as for holders of residence permits, while binding member states to the obligation to issue residence permits if they allow a stay of more than one year. the need to strengthen the existing level of data protection in the schengen convention is also recognised and the european commission is recommended to present the necessary initiatives if sis ii does not start to be applied by 2012. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the two initial proposals were merged and given a new legal basis. the text we are voting on in this house is the result of negotiations with the swedish and spanish presidencies. it translates into an agreement at first reading, thus allowing this regulation to be adopted before the entry into force of the visa code. mr president, i would have liked to have asked the spanish presidency, which is absent from this debate, to give parliament the assurance that the regulation can enter into force by 5 april 2010. it is essential that this objective can be achieved in such a way as to avoid a legal vacuum. i congratulate the european commission on the timely initiative. i am grateful for the loyal cooperation of the council, in particular the swedish and spanish presidencies, and the cooperation of the shadow rapporteurs, which have enabled a broad consensus to be reached in the libe committee. with this measure we have solved a delicate problem for thousands of third country nationals and we are doing it well, by strengthening freedom and security.

in writing. the commission proposal concerns the procedures for allocating the sifim for the purpose of determining the gni of the member states used for the purposes of the union budget and its own resources. sifim indirectly measured financial intermediation services represents a part of the output of financial institutions that is not realised in the form of direct sales of services at a fixed price, but rather by charging an interest rate (higher than that applied to deposits) on loans. the commission proposes to carry out the allocation of sifim for the determination of gni and considers that this allocation should be carried out retroactively from 1 january 2005, the date of entry into force of regulation (ec) no 1889/2002. however, the proposed retroactive application from 1 january 2005 raises questions as to the exact extent of the retroactivity of the decision. it therefore agrees with the rapporteur's position that the allocation of sifim for the determination of gni does not start until 1 january 2010. this ensures that the allocation of sifim is properly carried out from 2010 onwards, thus resulting in a more accurate calculation of gni.
