in writing. − consumer protection has always been one of the eu's priorities and has been reinforced following the adoption of the lisbon treaty. consumers who are well informed of their rights and obligations contribute to a more transparent and competitive market. with the current economic crisis, it is crucial to protect the most vulnerable and low-income consumers. the increasing complexity of retail markets, particularly in services, makes it increasingly difficult for consumers to make the best choice. to assess markets effectively and adopt policies that produce the best possible outcomes for consumers, market observation tools are needed and the consumer markets scoreboard is therefore of great importance.
in writing. − solvit, which has been operating since 2002, is an online problem-solving network involving the member states of the european union, with the aim of providing a pragmatic response to the difficulties arising from the incorrect application of community law by public authorities. although the internal market is currently functioning relatively well, it is also not true that sometimes errors or problems of interpretation arise with regard to the rights of citizens and businesses who wish to take advantage of the advantages offered by the internal market. i voted in favour of this report because the solvit network has proved to be of the utmost importance in solving a wide variety of problems, from the citizen seeking another member state to study, work, join his partner, etc., to companies that may have to face administrative problems, vat refund problems, or other problems. the solvit network aims to provide citizens and businesses with a high level of service, with high standards of quality and performance.
in writing. - i welcome the busoi report on solvit. this informal network for solving internal market problems has been instrumental in providing free assistance to citizens and businesses alike in solving concrete problems in public administration. this importance is reflected in the increasing number of cases lodged over the past year. however, in view of the cross-cutting problems identified at national level, it is essential to consider a series of measures to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these centres. i therefore believe that member states should step up their efforts to provide information to citizens and businesses about their rights in the internal market, by increasing financial and human resources and by training solvit staff in internal market rules. it is equally important that staff have a sound knowledge of english in addition to their mother tongue. i call on the member states and the commission to promote the closeness of citizens and businesses to the solvit network, with a view to effective application of the internal market rules.
in writing. the internal market is not and should not be a mere bureaucratic construction. to truly reap its full benefits, european businesses and citizens need to be able to exercise their rights in practice through fast, agile and efficient means. the solvit network is a key element in this respect. given the increasing number of cases that have been lodged in solvit centres over the last year, i consider it vital, in the interests of consumers, to carry out a set of reforms and improvements which the ep proposes, namely: - strengthening the european commission's control over the effective application of the internal market rules; - a clear increase in the resources allocated to solvit centres (recruitment of experts in the fields of the internal market, increase in funds for the national centres, specialised and current training of existing technicians, coordinated online access between local centres and commission services); - strong investment in the promotion and publicity of the solvit network by the member states and the european commission through all the media, promoting a high level of proximity to citizens and businesses. for all these reasons i support the busoi report on solvit.
in writing. - the solvit network was set up by the commission and the member states with the aim of solving, without recourse to the courts, the problems encountered by citizens and businesses as a result of the incorrect application of internal market legislation. this network has proven to be effective in solving problems, but is still little used by the general public. the commission therefore intends to promote the rapid and full implementation of the solvit network, increasing transparency to overcome obstacles to free movement and informing citizens about their rights to enhance the internal market. to this end, the commission calls on the member states to promote the solvit network to citizens and businesses, taking account of its potential and the added value it represents. given that many of the issues that can be dealt with by the solvit network are now settled by judicial means, increasing the time and money spent by citizens and businesses, and given that the solvit network can provide a faster and more effective alternative solution for dispute resolution, i believe that the full functioning of the solvit network is beneficial for the functioning of the internal market, as well as for the protection of the interests and rights of citizens and businesses.
in writing. − the solvit network was launched in july 2002 and was set up by the commission and the member states with the aim of solving problems encountered by citizens and businesses as a result of incorrect application of internal market legislation, thus enabling them to find a quick, free and effective solution without having to go to court. all eu member states, together with norway, iceland and liechtenstein, have established solvit centres at national level, in most cases integrated into their ministries of economy or foreign affairs. these centres cooperate directly through an electronic database in order to find quick and pragmatic solutions to problems raised by citizens and businesses. member states should step up their efforts to provide citizens and businesses with information on the rights they enjoy in the internal market, thus enabling them to exercise those rights in practice. the services provided by solvit should be communicated to citizens and businesses in the most effective way.
in writing. - 'effective problem solving in the internal market', the solvit network, has been a successful tool in solving internal market problems. the solvit network was set up in 2002 to respond to the problems that the incorrect application of european legislation to the internal market brings to citizens and businesses. solvit effectively and less bureaucratically replaces the courts, finding solutions within 10 weeks. however, the increasing flow of solvit cases that has been occurring has resulted in several deficiencies in its response. it is therefore very important that efforts are made to increase the human and financial resources and adequate training of solvit staff so that the network can be more effective in responding to the increasing number of cases that are referred to it.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 998/2003, which the commission proposes to amend, lays down harmonised rules for the non-commercial movement of pet animals within and entry into the community. it also provides for a transitional regime allowing some member states to impose more restrictive conditions for certain diseases such as rabies, equinococcus and tick-borne diseases. given the importance of the free movement of pet animals within the european union, i reiterate, however, my conviction that it is essential that they meet all the health conditions so that they do not pose risks to human or animal health.
in writing. - this report regulates the movement of domestic animals within the european area and how this movement should be processed in accordance with the objectives of preventing the spread of diseases, especially rabies. free movement is one of the fundamental pillars of the european single market. this is a matter of particular concern to our citizens in a europe without frontiers, where we have seen an increase in the movement of pets between member states. we all agree that it should be possible to travel with our pets, but we all also agree that this should be done in accordance with certain health criteria to ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health. i therefore welcome the general passport system, which will harmonize the health measures and controls that facilitate the free movement of pets. the report also provides for a transitional arrangement until the end of 2011 so that some countries can prepare to put the necessary infrastructure in place.
in writing. - the animal health conditions under which non-commercial cross-border movements of domestic animals must be carried out are designed to ensure both a high degree of protection of human and animal health and the ease of movement of companion animals accompanied by their owners. the non-commercial movement of pet animals should therefore be facilitated, provided that they comply with the applicable rules and are accompanied during their travel within the community by a certificate of vaccination against rabies and an analysis of the immune reaction to that vaccine carried out by an authorised veterinarian.
in writing. the schengen agreement is a convention between european countries on a policy of free movement of persons within the schengen area. anyone in possession of a document proving that he is legally resident in a member state should be able to move freely within that area where there are no internal borders. however, not all countries fulfil their obligation to grant a residence permit to third-country nationals holding such a long-stay visa. it is therefore contradictory that a student who obtains a visa to take a course in portugal should not be able to go to belgium, for example, to collect information in a specialist library to write his thesis. in this respect, i voted in favour of this report, taking into account the need to facilitate the movement within the schengen area of third-country nationals legally resident in one of the member states on the basis of a long-stay visa of the type 'd' issued by that member state. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr carlos coelho, on having once again succeeded in reaching an agreement at first reading, which makes it possible to resolve this situation before the visa code enters into force next april.
in writing. − the creation, with the schengen agreement, of a european area without border controls was an important step in building an open internal market with free movement of people and goods. the crucial issue underlying the agreement is therefore to allow the free movement of persons in an area where there are no internal borders. it therefore seems absurd that citizens from outside the community, but holding long-stay visas issued by one of the states party to the schengen agreement, should not be able to move freely within this area. the examples given by the rapporteur seem to us to be evidence of the absurdity of this system in practice. i therefore support the commission's proposal, as formulated by parliament, to equate long-term visas with residence permits, thus ensuring freedom of movement for their holders.
in writing. - first of all, i welcome the excellent quality of this report. under current community legislation, third-country nationals holding a long-stay visa (for stays of more than three months) are not allowed to travel to the other member states during their stay, nor to transit through the other member states when returning to their country of origin, as this is not provided for in the schengen convention. the proposed new rules provide that a long-stay visa has the same effects as a residence permit with regard to free movement within the schengen area without internal borders, i.e. a person holding a long-stay visa issued by one member state will be allowed to travel to the other member states for three months in a six-month period and under the same conditions as the holder of a residence permit. for that system to work, controls equivalent to those in place in other areas should be put in place to ensure good communication between member states and consistency between the issuing of long-stay visas, residence permits and entries in the schengen information system (sis).
in writing. - it is positive that a foreigner who holds a long-stay visa issued by a member state can travel to the other member states for at least three months in a six-month period and under the same conditions as the holder of a residence permit. as this is the main content of the regulation to which this report refers, we voted in favour. as is known, under current community legislation, third-country nationals holding long-stay visas - which may be, for example, students who wish to make a study trip to another member state, scientists, academics, certain family members of third-country nationals and eu citizens - are not allowed to travel to the other member states during their stay, nor to transit through the other member states when returning to their country of origin, as this is not provided for in the schengen convention. the new rules now adopted provide that a person holding a long-stay visa (a visa for a stay of more than three months, or a d visa) has the same rights as a holder of a residence permit as regards free movement within the schengen area.
in writing. − the previous legislation, which did not allow a third-country national with a long-stay visa issued by a member state to travel to other member states, did not meet the mobility needs of most of these citizens. we are talking about students, scientists, academics and others who, as a result of their professional and/or academic activities, find themselves in need of travelling between several member states and could not do so in the face of existing legislation. these amendments thus correct this anomalous situation without thereby failing to continue to safeguard all the safety rules for the movement of third country nationals within the community.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental principles of the european union and the creation of the schengen area is intended to contribute to the effective achievement of this objective. the epp group, to which i belong, has always defended the principle of free movement of persons, in the sense that the schengen acquis should include common rules and procedures on visas, residence permits and border controls. in this context, and taking into account that the free movement of third-country nationals residing in a member state on the basis of a long-stay visa type d to other schengen member states is sometimes hindered by delays in their conversion into a residence permit, i support the new measures adopted. the document states that the principle of equivalence between residence permits and short-stay visas will be extended to long-stay visas. for these reasons, and because the measures adopted not only do not call into question the conditions for issuing visas, particularly those relating to security issues, but also embody a natural and necessary development of the schengen acquis, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − effective competition in the supply of goods and services reduces prices, increases quality and allows for greater choice for consumers. it also allows technological innovation to progress. research in the energy sector and investment in infrastructure, particularly in the interconnection of gas and electricity networks, are essential to promote competition. security of supply and effective competition in the energy market depend on the interconnection and the proper functioning of energy infrastructures. strong competition in the telecommunications sector with measures favouring competition for preferential tariffs is also important, and for this it is important to make a relevant market analysis. i would also stress the importance of monitoring the competitive behaviour of the fuel markets in the union. i stress that support mechanisms such as state aid should not be used to protect national industries to the detriment of the internal market and european consumers and that these mechanisms should be used with a view to the recovery of a sustainable knowledge economy.
in writing. - greater competition means more choice for european citizens and a more competitive environment for businesses. as such, eu competition and consumer policies should not be dissociated. the commission's actions to ensure an effective competitive environment within the internal market are therefore essential to safeguarding those objectives, even if the fact that the commission has been given absolute powers may be called into question. in the crisis situation of recent months, the authorisation of state aid justified by the events has been essential for the recovery of the economy. the fight against cartels and the abuse of a dominant position by undertakings is also essential to ensure that the internal market is a place of fair competition in which the various economic operators enjoy good conditions for carrying on their activities.
in writing. - the economic crisis, the effects of which are still being felt, requires exceptional measures, such as state aid. however, they must not unduly distort competition and increase budget deficits and public debt. the allocation of this money should therefore be the subject of careful consideration. rapidly rising public debt levels will be a burden on future generations and an obstacle to economic recovery and growth. excessive debt and budget deficits not only jeopardise the stability of the euro, but also impose severe constraints on public spending in priority sectors such as education, health, innovation and the environment. in this context, a rigorous assessment of the rescue and recovery package and the effectiveness of the state aid measures is necessary. protectionism and the fragmentation of the single market must be avoided, as they weaken europe's position in the world economy. a well-functioning single market is the key to a healthy economy and, most certainly, to economic recovery. economic policies must gain more legitimacy through greater involvement of the european parliament, which is the ultimate decision-making body.
in writing. − competition policy and good competition rules have always been of crucial importance for the existence of a healthy coexistence between all economic players in the euro area. although the eu has been badly affected by the recent global economic crisis, the truth is that a strong currency, a strong single market, sound public finances and a good social protection system have all helped to sustain the effects of the crisis. however, the various state aids granted by member states without a common concern may lead to significant distortions of competition. it is therefore crucial that an assessment be made of all the measures taken by each state to combat the crisis so that in the future the eu is able to react jointly and harmoniously to avoid situations of protectionism and fragmentation of the single market. such situations only harm a europe which wants to be strong in the world economy.
in writing. − in 1997, the commission published the first internal market scoreboard, focusing on the transposition of internal market rules by member states, given that substantial delays prevented citizens and businesses from exploiting the full potential of the internal market. through this measurement and publication of the transposition performance, the evaluation panel has contributed to reducing the deficit in the transposition of directives by member states. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it imperative that the member states transpose legislation on the internal market into national law in a timely manner, since the internal market can only function properly if the community rules on its operation are correctly transposed and applied and enforced.
in writing. − although member states have achieved the best results in respecting the deadlines for transposing internal market rules into national law, the data from the latest internal market assessment panel do not seem satisfactory to me. the creation of a stable, innovative internal market which meets consumers' needs and in which businesses can create new jobs is not compatible with the systematic delays in transposing community legislation and the failure to apply directives. it is the people and businesses who suffer most from the delay in implementing internal market measures in terms of the costs of less choice, less competition and more closed markets. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules of the internal market are applied. it was the member states who set the deadlines for implementing these directives. the minimum required is that they respect the objectives they have set themselves. this is a fundamental requirement for a sound internal market in the context of economic crisis.
in writing. − following the most recent publication of the internal market assessment panel results (march 2010), the percentage of internal market directives not transposed into national law was found to be 0.7%, which is lower than the result presented in july 2009, which was, as stated by the rapporteur, 1.0%. the timely and proper transposition of community rules is essential for further integration of the internal market because of its direct impact on legal certainty and the confidence of european citizens. the member states should therefore adopt a responsible approach in the application of those rules so that in the future there is no lack of transposition, but rather greater legal certainty and citizens can benefit from a level playing field in the internal market.
in writing. − the internal market cannot function properly if the community rules on its functioning are not correctly transposed and applied and enforced. it is therefore imperative that member states transpose internal market legislation into national law in a timely manner. there are 22 directives whose transposition deadline has expired more than two years ago. in addition, 6% of the directives have not been transposed in all member states, which means that 100 internal market directives do not produce all the possible effects in the eu. member states and the commission must act jointly to deal with this situation. i agree with the view that the commission should provide on its website the directives which have not been implemented in each member state, so that this situation is public knowledge. it is found that the number of infringement cases remains too high, with some member states having cases well above the eu average of 47. the member states are also called upon to ensure the operability of the crossborder networks of electronic information systems set up by the commission.
in writing. - contrary to what is said in the report, it is now clear that the process of liberalising markets and privatising public services, which is still under way, has not brought any visible gains in terms of prices, quality of service or reduction of public expenditure. on the contrary, consumer and public service user associations report price increases, a deterioration in the quality of the service and an increase in the cost of providing it. liberalisation has contributed to the closure of jobs and the creation of private monopolies, which have undermined the rights of workers, users of public services and consumers, particularly in the postal, telecommunications, transport and electricity sectors. this in turn contributes to the worsening of the economic and social crisis. so to insist on such a policy is to insist on the continuing worsening of the socioeconomic situation of millions of people. it is to insist on the squandering of that public heritage which is public services and their handing over to private groups. it is to insist on precariousness, unemployment, poverty. it is to insist on widening the gap between the richest and the poorest. it's to insist on a more unjust society. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. − a healthy internal market is crucial for healthy competition and economic development. but for this to be a reality, it is necessary that, without exception, community directives be adopted by all member states in the same way. the internal market assessment panel and the consumer panel have a crucial role to play in improving the functioning of the internal market. although we are on the right track, we are still far from achieving all the objectives set out in the report with regard to a more efficient internal market. the effort of all is therefore needed, including here the national parliaments, which have a very important and decisive role to play.

in writing. while it is true that the preservation of the earth's atmosphere should be a shared responsibility of the various countries, it is also clear that the influence that each of these countries has exerted on the atmosphere throughout history and that which they still exert today is very different, which means that this responsibility, for reasons of elementary justice, must be differentiated. on the other hand, the definition of each country's responsibility for the overall effort to reduce emissions will have to take into account its population base for the same reasons of fairness. china's per capita emissions are now four times lower than the us and about half the eu average. india has about one tenth of the eu average emissions and twenty times less than the us. at the moment, in india, there are about 500 million people (approximately the population of the eu) without access to electricity. that is why attempts to blame these countries for the failure of copenhagen are unjustified and unnecessary. the european parliament has been very active in this area, and i am sure that the european parliament will be very active in this area.
mr president, the real objective of the so-called railway package, launched with the announced - praiseworthy - objective of laying the foundations for modal transfer, interoperability, is now clear. the real intention, as we pointed out at the time, was to open up rail transport, particularly freight, to competition and private interests as a first step towards the complete liberalisation of the sector at european union level. as in other liberalisations, it starts by using what is wrong at a given moment, by dismissing the real causes of such situations, namely years of persistent policies of dismantling and atrophying the public sector, to justify liberalising measures and point to said competition, without understanding how or why, as the solution to all ills. experience, as we have heard here today, shows us the opposite: liberalization is the cause, not the solution, of the main problems in the sector, notably the quality and accessibility of services and workers' rights. public investment in the railway sector is undoubtedly strategic - for energy and environmental reasons - but not to be handed over to the profit-making logic of large private interests, which aim to dominate this key public sector in each country by liberalising it at the level of the european union's internal market.

i am pleased to hear commissioner de gucht's assurance that the commission will soon send parliament the legislative initiative to revise the system of generalised preferences so that the legislative process can be completed in time to avoid the expiry of the current system of generalised preferences, which expires at the end of next year. that system must be renewed. firstly, because it is an instrument of development aid, giving countries access to the european market on preferential terms without any reciprocity. secondly, because this scheme is also an instrument for improving the human rights situation and good governance in those same countries, since its granting is subject to conditions to be fulfilled by those beneficiary countries. for these two reasons, the union must renew its use of this instrument, which puts trade at the service of development and human rights. however, the renewal should benefit from an evaluation of the results in the preceding period. the new regulation should also comply with the following requirements which have been drawn from practice up to now. firstly, to maintain the temporary nature of the granting of the generalized system of preferences so as to allow its withdrawal as soon as it is no longer necessary. secondly, to deepen and refine the differentiation and selectivity of the beneficiary countries, according to the level of development of each and their external competitiveness. thirdly, and finally, to improve the mechanisms for monitoring compliance with the conditions attached to the generalized system of preferences, especially with regard to respect for human rights. finally, commissioner, it was desirable that parliament's opinion be taken into account at the outset of the legislative procedure.

in writing. − on 3 march, the european commission presented the 2020 strategy: 'a strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth'. it is a proposal based on five quantifiable objectives for the european union (eu) by 2020, which will frame the process and which should be translated into national objectives: employment, research and innovation, climate change and energy, education and the fight against poverty. it is a strategy that focuses on concrete, realistic and properly quantified objectives: raising the employment rate from 69% to at least 75%; increasing investment in research and development (r&d) to 3% of gdp; reducing poverty by 25%; reducing the school drop-out rate from the current 15% to 10%; and increasing the percentage of 30-year-olds with a tertiary education qualification from 31% to 40%. i voted in favour of the resolution on strategy 2020 because i believe that the objectives set out therein set the course for europe, that they provide a clear and objective response to the problems created by the economic and financial crisis in terms of unemployment, financial regulation and the fight against poverty, and that they constitute the benchmark which will enable us to assess the progress achieved.

in writing. − the european commission has published strategy 2020, which replaces the unsuccessful lisbon strategy and presents important and ambitious challenges for europe. these challenges are mainly in five areas considered strategic by the commission: (i) employment; (ii) innovation and research; (iii) climate change and energy; (iv) education and (v) the fight against poverty. these are indeed key areas for europe to overcome the crisis and to reassert itself as a major player in the global market, with a high level of development and a competitive economy capable of generating wealth, jobs and innovation. the european union needs ambition to overcome the challenges posed by the crisis, without compromising the effort of budgetary consolidation required of the member states, given the fragility of their public accounts and excessive deficits. that is why i consider it essential to strengthen the objectives of strategy 2020.
in writing. − the principle of solidarity should be the basis of the eu 2020 strategy. solidarity between citizens, generations, regions and states. in this way we can combat poverty and ensure economic, social and territorial cohesion through sustainable economic growth. this principle of solidarity must be the guarantor of the european social model. we must think about restructuring social security systems and guaranteeing minimum social rights at european level to facilitate the free movement of workers, managers, entrepreneurs, researchers, students and pensioners. efficient use of resources is a requirement of this principle and follows from the need for sustainability. employment creation must be the result of this strategy. we cannot accept that the eu has some 23 million unemployed men and women. to this end, support for entrepreneurship and bureaucratic and tax relief for small and medium-sized enterprises are essential. this cannot mean that industry or agriculture is forgotten. we have to re-industrialize europe. sustainable agriculture, with quality products, should be another objective. to do this, we need to strengthen the sustainable development of our primary sector and take the lead in scientific research, knowledge and innovation.
in writing. − strategy 2020, which is intended to continue the lisbon strategy, should begin by taking due account of the implementation of its predecessor. if it did, it would find in the guidelines it has covered - i.e. the liberalisation of important economic sectors and the deregulation and flexibilization of labour laws - the causes of their practical results: the growth of unemployment, precariousness, poverty and social exclusion; economic stagnation and recession. the commission and parliament now intend to follow the same lines. the path we are on is clear and the social and environmental rhetoric that is being used is not enough to disguise it: the emphasis on the single market, the continuation of liberalization, the commodification of increasing aspects of social life, precarious employment, structural unemployment. the consensus between the right and the social democrats on these lines is revealing. after all, they have been, collectively, its faithful protagonists in recent years. this strategy is, in fact, nothing more than the response of these two currents of the same system to its structural crisis. if it is pursued, it will itself be the seed of new and deeper crises. if it is continued, it will inevitably face the resistance and struggle of the workers and the peoples.
in writing. - we regret that they have rejected our motion for a resolution in which we advocated not only a broad consultation on the proposals now being put forward by the european commission and a full assessment of the results of the lisbon strategy in order to draw conclusions for a new strategy 2020, but also a set of new proposals, giving priority to increasing output and creating jobs with rights, tackling unemployment and poverty, and ensuring equality in social progress. this implied a new macroeconomic framework favouring sustainable development, the strengthening of domestic demand, respectful of the environment, based on wage growth, full employment with rights and economic and social cohesion. we voted against the joint resolution which was adopted because it does not go to the heart of the problem, does not propose alternative measures to the stability pact, and does not propose an end to the liberalizations or the flexibility of employment which have led to the increase in precarious and low-paid work. they therefore accept that the european commission is continuing to insist on more of the same, which has already led to the unemployment of over 23 million people and over 85 million people in poverty.
in writing. − strategy 2020 is the eu's last chance to assert itself as the world's leading economic power, after the failure of the lisbon strategy. in this context of global economic crisis, strategy 2020 must be the model that all member states must follow to start a new phase, with new paradigms that lead to sustainable development based on good practices. after the loss of many millions of jobs across the eu, the fight against unemployment has to be the eu's 'keystone'. we must be able to create jobs and to make our workforce more skilled and better trained. this will only be possible with the unambiguous support of smes, which are responsible for creating the largest number of jobs. but for strategy 2020 to be a success, we cannot make the same mistakes that were made with the lisbon strategy, namely the lack of commitment and accountability of member states.
in writing. − strategy 2020 aims to outline the future roadmap for achieving economic growth and promoting employment in the european union. its approach should be objective, with references to a sustainable social market economy, sustainable knowledge-based knowledge and the role of smes in promoting employment. a strong, modern and flexible cohesion policy must be a central element of this strategy. enshrined in the new lisbon treaty, cohesion policy, through its horizontal approach, plays an essential role in responding to the union's new challenges. the objective of european territorial cohesion is of fundamental importance in this context. the priorities of european cohesion must not only aim at promoting competitiveness at european level through the efficient allocation of funds, but also at supporting disadvantaged regions in order to overcome their social and economic difficulties and to reduce existing disparities. the active role of the european regions in promoting this strategy is also worth noting. the importance of multi-level governance is worth highlighting. a concerted sharing of the objectives, tasks and responsibilities of the 2020 strategy between the european union, the member states and local and regional authorities is desirable. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - those who have been following the israeli-palestinian conflict for many years, as i have, cannot help but conclude with sadness that many of the sincere efforts for a lasting peace are still not enough to persuade and motivate those who have chosen violence to abandon it for good. hamas's electoral victory and the partition of the palestinian territory into two, each under its authority, have greatly worsened an already bleak scenario. until hamas accepts the legitimate existence of the state of israel, the dialogue will be nothing more than a show. israel, for its part, will have to be careful about the appropriateness and proportionality of its positions, lest it jeopardize its international legitimacy. like yitzhak rabin, i too believe that a diplomatic peace is not yet a true peace, but it is an essential step towards it. we must work to that end and remove the obstacles to the steps towards true peace. judge goldstone's report points to choices made by both sides in this case: serious failures and crimes that must be investigated, tried and punished.
in writing. − it should be noted that the armed conflict in gaza, which began on 27 december 2008 and ended on 18 january 2009, resulted in the deaths of more than 1 400 palestinians and 13 israelis. in addition to the loss of human life, it is noted that much of the civilian infrastructure has been destroyed. the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and the member states should work towards a common eu position on the follow-up to the report of the fact-finding mission on the conflict in gaza and southern israel. i would stress that respect for international human rights law and international humanitarian law is an essential condition for achieving a just and lasting peace in the middle east. i support the call for the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and the member states to monitor the implementation of the recommendations contained in the goldstone report by consulting eu external missions and ngos working in this field.
in writing. - the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution on the war in gaza, recognising israel's violations of international law, was a positive step. this is proof of the impact of the goldstone report on the middle east peace process, as the european parliament has recognised israel's continued violations of international law. the truth is that the goldstone report contains clear evidence of the violations of international humanitarian rights committed by israeli forces in the palestinian territories throughout their military operations in 2008. we therefore want the conclusions of this report to be adopted immediately and its recommendations to be put into practice. at the same time, we urge the european union's leaders not to strengthen the eu-israel association agreement until the violations of international law and fundamental human rights that israel continues to commit in the occupied palestinian territories are brought to an end.
in writing. - the eu must have a fundamental concern in resolving the israeli-palestinian conflict, which, in addition to the victims it causes, has for decades been a source of great instability in the region and the world. however, i believe that there are differences between the actions of israel, as a democratic and sovereign state which shares and promotes the values that are the benchmarks of western societies, and radical movements such as hamas, which in most cases refuses to recognize the very existence of the state of israel and thus acts as an obstacle to a good resolution of the conflict. this does not prevent us from condemning, in all circumstances, the acts of violence on both sides of the conflict, which are shocking the world and can only motivate us and make us more and more committed to seeking platforms for understanding.
in writing. - i reminded the house not long ago that elections in belarus are not free, there is no freedom of expression, association or demonstration, and that the repressive activities carried out by the authorities are increasing. in addition, political prisoners have not yet been released, the death penalty has not been abolished, and the separation of powers, in particular the independence of the judiciary and respect for human rights, are not guaranteed. the recent use of police forces against upb militants and the deprivation of their rights are two more episodes that contribute to reinforcing european distrust of the belarusian dictatorship and call on all european democrats, in particular the european institutions and the governments of the member states, to be vigilant and to react firmly and coordinatedly against the authorities in minsk, who remain faithful to the worst legacy of communism. the european union cannot be a partner of belarus which does not respect its own citizens or international law. as the saying goes in my country: "once you were only badly accompanied!"
in writing. - as long as free elections are not held, the european union must not recognise the legitimacy of the belarusian parliament. the belarusian authorities are therefore called upon to carry out a thorough reform of the country's electoral legislation in line with osce/odihr recommendations. the actions of the belarusian authorities against members of the organisation representing the polish national minority are absolutely reprehensible, as are the politically biased trials and the apparent dependence of the judiciary on the executive. the eu cannot agree with the decision of the belarusian authorities to restrict access to the internet and the failure to guarantee freedom of the press, freedom of association and assembly, and freedom of worship for churches other than the belarusian orthodox church, alongside other political rights and freedoms. i believe that the level of community cooperation with the belarusian authorities should be directly proportional to the level of respect for human rights in that country. i also share the concern about the lax and belated statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the repression of the polish national minority.
in writing. - since the end of the cold war, belarus' relations with the west have reached a new level of understanding, and the european union has been developing a positive dialogue to encourage belarus to make progress on democracy and human rights. however, the eu cannot accept actions which conflict with international principles and standards on the rights of national minorities. the eu cannot make any comparative judgments on human rights.
in writing. the financial sector must take its share of responsibility for the economic crisis which still plagues us. the real economy, taxpayers, consumers, public services and society in general have so far borne a substantial share of the costs and consequences of the financial crisis. several member states have called for the adoption of a financial transaction tax. the policy and regulatory environment in this area is different today, with new regulatory initiatives such as the fight against tax havens, the removal of legal loopholes in management accounts, requirements for exchange transactions and the use of transaction repositories for the registration of derivative instruments. the european union should adopt a common position in the international framework of the g20 meetings. to this end, the commission should assess the impact of a global financial transaction tax before the next g20 summit. this assessment shall, in particular, assess the effects of the introduction of a financial transaction tax only in the european union as opposed to its introduction worldwide. the costs should be quantified and it should be determined whether this tax contributes to the stabilisation of financial markets.
in writing. − several statements in the recitals of the resolution now adopted by the majority of the european parliament are positive, in particular when it states that the financial sector should bear a fair share of the burden of economic recovery and development, given that so far it has been the real economy, taxpayers, consumers, public services and society in general that have borne a substantial share of the costs and consequences of the financial crisis. but then he almost regrets his support for the possible application of a financial transaction tax, by raising many conditions for its application. that is why we abstained. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. we must move decisively and not continue in these murky waters which only serve financial speculators and big business.
in writing. - the cds is, as a rule, contrary to the creation of european taxes. in addition, tax matters are important instruments at the service of the states, which can use them, especially in difficult times, as the present crisis is an example. finally, the different tax options, whether in the form of taxes or charges, applied in the various member states would necessarily give the rate in question a more or less punitive character, allowing for injustices on a european scale which would make no sense.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic money, the exchange of information and the exchange of information on the use of electronic money. the sepa is still operating at a deficit and does not correspond to the real needs of users. the european commission should set an appropriate and binding deadline for the use of sepa instruments, after which all payments in euro should be made using the rules of the sepa system. it is equally important to ensure that the adoption of this system does not entail additional costs for the european citizen.
in writing. − the creation of the single euro payments area (sepa) is key to further integrating the market for financial payment services, will increase competition by treating crossborder and national payments in euro equally, and can have a direct positive impact on the lives of eu citizens. as such, there appears to be an urgent need for the migration of sepa services by national public administrations and the necessary adaptation of the rules governing this initiative so that there is in fact a simplification of the current context in financial payment services and a reduction of costs for the benefit of consumers.
in writing. − the single euro payments area (sepa) will become an integrated market for payment services, subject to effective competition and in which there is no distinction between cross-border and national payments denominated in euro. a legally binding deadline should have been set for completing the migration to sepa instruments. this migration by public administrations is below expectations. it is therefore important that all stakeholders - legislators, the banking sector and payment service users - are involved in the sepa. the continuity of legal validity of existing direct debit authorisations should be ensured in all member states, as the obligation to sign new authorisations when switching from national direct debit schemes to the sepa direct debit scheme would be very burdensome. therefore, the commission should set a clear, appropriate and binding deadline for the migration to sepa instruments, which should not be later than 31 december 2012, after which all payments denominated in euro should be made using sepa standards. the commission should assist the public administration in the migration process by developing integrated and synchronised national migration plans.
in writing. − the single euro payments area (sepa) must rapidly become an integrated market for payment services. however, this is far from being achieved. and although there are directives stipulating the start of the sepa card framework and the sepa direct debit system, the truth is that they are not yet operational. it is therefore necessary to speed up all the obstacles to the implementation of the sepa system so that it can become fully operational as soon as possible. it is important that the transitional period does not exceed 21 october 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on transparency and the current state of the acta negotiations because i am in favour of a transparent process in the conduct of the negotiations. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament will have to give its consent to the text of the acta agreement before its entry into force in the european union. the ep's contribution is essential to ensure that measures to enforce intellectual property rights do not impede innovation, competition, the protection of personal data and the free flow of information.
in writing. - counterfeiting is one of the main scourges of the global economy and, despite efforts to combat it, the obvious inability of individual states to carry out this fight to a successful conclusion is evident. the risks to the health and safety of consumers which the purchase of certain products may entail are now clear. from a commercial and industrial point of view, this parallel industry, which illegitimately feeds on the creativity and notoriety of others, weakens the value of brands and makes their distinctive vocation less effective. the establishment of an open, free and fair market is important, but it will only prevail if counterfeiting is condemned and combated by the major producers. the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement may be a path worth taking, but to do so it must first be known and discussed in a transparent way, unlike what has been happening so far.
in writing. − in 2008, the european union and other oecd countries started negotiations on a new plurilateral agreement to strengthen the enforcement of intellectual property rights (ipr) and to combat counterfeiting and piracy (anti-counterfeiting trade agreement - acta), and jointly decided to adopt a confidentiality clause. any agreement on acta concluded by the european union should respect the legal obligations imposed on the eu in the field of privacy and data protection legislation as defined in directive 95/46/ec, directive 2002/58/ec and the case law of the european court of human rights and the court of justice of the european union (cjeu), following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament will have to give its consent to the text of the acta agreement before its entry into force in the european union. the commission has also undertaken to provide the european parliament with prompt and complete information at all stages of the negotiation of international agreements. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods are respected. the commission should submit proposals before the next round of negotiations.
in writing. - parliament's general condemnation of the commission's failure to provide information on the ongoing negotiations on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) and the limitations it sought to impose on its democratic scrutiny and control was clear. we therefore consider it important that the resolution should defend the commission's 'legal obligation' 'to inform parliament immediately and fully at all stages of the negotiation process of international agreements'. we are calling for democratic and transparent procedures in the conduct of the negotiations and for a public debate on their content, which we consider to be a positive development. we also stress the need to respect 'fundamental rights such as freedom of expression and the right to privacy, while fully respecting subsidiarity' and the protection of personal data. that is why we are voting in favour.
in writing. - the lack of transparency in the negotiations on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) is contrary to the spirit of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. it is essential that the council and the commission make available immediately all the documentation that has been the subject of negotiations. failure by the commission and the council to fulfil this basic duty could lead the european parliament to use legal mechanisms to access these elements, which would not in any way give the european institutions involved any credit.
in writing. the european union is the largest donor of humanitarian aid and development support. we know that every year millions are given by the european union and the member states under cooperation and development programmes and that this aid is needed and in many cases will make a difference. it is, however, my conviction as a market economy advocate that development aid can (and should) be provided through trade policies which are beneficial to developing countries. it is in this context, in my view, that the system of generalised preferences (gsp) is appropriate, which allows developed countries to offer non-reciprocal preferential treatment to products from developing countries.
in writing. - it is not safe to say, as the resolution does, that the current gsp is an instrument to help developing countries. this instrument has had the effect of increasing the economic dependence of these countries on export production to the detriment of their internal market. to a large extent, it is the large transnational corporations, some of them from eu countries, who benefit from this system, and not the people of developing countries. thus, some of the purported purposes of the gsp are contradictory to its practical results. on the other hand, in the context of growing pressure for the liberalization of international trade, it is clear that the eu is using the end of this regulation as a form of blackmail for the acceptance of the so-called free trade agreements, through unacceptable diplomatic and economic pressure on these countries. for the gsp to become a development aid instrument, it would require, as we propose, its extension and renegotiation, together with other development support policies, giving shape to effective solidarity, combating economic dependence and the exploitation of peoples and their natural resources by the eu economic groups.
in writing. - what the european community has been doing since 1971 with regard to developing countries in the area of trade preferences under the generalised system of preferences is a way of making world trade fairer and at the same time helping these countries to grow and develop economically. this regulation expires in 2011, and we need to start working immediately on a new instrument that maintains and, if possible, further enhances the benefits that this system has provided to developing states, which is even more important in this context of the international crisis. it is, however, crucial that the new list of countries benefiting from this system reflects their economic situation in a very realistic way to avoid injustices.
in writing. - like many (if not all) of the member states, the european union is faced with a budget far below its ambitions and far below what it could achieve. the list of multiple values and european expectations in this area reinforces the observation of this asymmetry. the fact that politics is, par excellence, an activity in which we have to foresee and provide becomes particularly relevant when what is at stake are aspects as essential to our common life as foreign and security policy. the treaty of lisbon and the consequent creation of the post of high representative reflect the conviction of the member states that there is a real need for readiness, coordination and convergence in european action in the fields of the cfsp. only practice will tell whether the provisions of the treaty are sufficient and whether what has been written in the treaty will be successful. i hope that the union will be able to respond positively to this important challenge.
in writing. − the report on the implementation of the european security strategy is an annual document of the european parliament which takes stock of european security and defence policy and makes proposals to improve the efficiency and visibility of this policy. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the eu's external action takes on a new dimension and importance. the european parliament has a key role to play in this respect as the guarantor of the democratic legitimacy of external action. the creation of a european action service will provide a body and a diplomatic apparatus of the union, which until now could only be provided by national representation. however, to achieve the external representation targets, it is crucial that the eu has the necessary budgetary resources.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty has brought new responsibilities to the ep with regard to the common foreign and security policy and we are ready to take on these responsibilities and to contribute to the choice of policies, but also of the faces that will represent them around the world, scrutinizing the choices of appointees to the european external action service (eeas), including here, too, the eu special representatives. the eu must demonstrate to the international community that it has a foreign policy which is increasingly representative, coherent, systematic and effective. the eu must increasingly be the main driver in building world peace.
in writing. - the european union has been described on several occasions as an economic giant and a political dwarf, meaning that it does not have the means to pursue some of its objectives, particularly in its external action. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. i doubt that this situation is likely to change any time soon. on the contrary, i think it is to be expected, given the number of states that make up the union, their histories and their particular interests. the question of common defence, which goes to the heart of sovereign powers, has always been the subject of suspicion on the part of the european countries and still today deserves particular caution, which is fully justified. this should not dissuade us from seeking closer cooperation and coordination to improve our common security and defence. despite its soft power nature, the european union should consider taking on the role of a true second pillar of an atlantic alliance which cannot continue to demand all the sacrifices of the united states of america.
in writing. - this report, which has brought together the conservative right and social democracy, is a dangerous symptom of what we have long been denouncing about the lisbon treaty: its contribution to the deepening of neoliberalism, based on federalism and the militarisation of the european union as the european pillar of nato. following the lead of the major powers, the eu seeks to resolve its own contradictions and to reposition itself in the face of a process of international power-sharing, a competitive view among powers over natural resources and markets, and a greater assertion of the european union as an economic, political and military bloc with ambitions for global interventionism. the majority of the ep here prescribes the recipe it has long advocated: - the militarization of international relations and internal security as a result of the so-called fight against terrorism; - the strengthening of budgets in these areas and the creation of new military capabilities that will contribute to the relaunch of the arms race; - the adaptation to the us and nato concepts of preventive wars and the extension of their intervention on a world scale. the result of these developments may be more war, exploitation and poverty as responses to the crisis that capitalism has plunged the world into. the road to peace requires a break with these policies.
in writing. − the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the common defence and security policy (cfsp) are two key pillars for the eu to become the leading actor in the international community in tackling the challenges and threats identified in the european security strategy (ess). although the eu considers the un security council to be primarily responsible for the maintenance and preservation of peace and security in the world, the eu must have effective policies common to all member states in order to be able to respond effectively to global challenges and threats.
in writing. - the principles which guided the signing of the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons and which date back to the cold war period are still relevant today and even more urgent. the collapse of the soviet bloc has led to the proliferation of nuclear material by several states, and the end of unified control over its use and maintenance raises fears of its irresponsible use or even its deterioration with unforeseeable consequences for the health and safety of the region. the growing number of members of the "nuclear club", the threat of terrorism, and the relative ease with which weapons of mass destruction are now being built all contribute to the climate of unrest in which we live today. the european union must be able to take a common and coherent position on these issues with a view to a safer and increasingly weapons-free world.
in writing. − changes in the international order provide new opportunities for the non-proliferation issue. at the beginning of his term, president obama stated his ambition for a world without nuclear weapons and his commitment to actively seek ratification of the complete ban on nuclear testing by the united states. the union must rise to the challenges of nuclear non-proliferation, especially in the face of iran and north korea, which remain the main threats to international security. as regards the reduction of nuclear arsenals, the priority is to continue to reduce the two main arsenals, that is to say, those of russia and the united states, which possess 95% of all nuclear weapons in the world. the european parliament expects the european union to adopt a common and ambitious position at the forthcoming conference on the review of the non-proliferation treaty.
in writing. - international nuclear disarmament is of vital importance. hence the need to defend and strengthen the npt and its ratification by all states. in the present international context, the danger of a new nuclear arms race is a matter of great concern. in accordance with the spirit and the letter of the npt, disarmament and an end to the development, production and stockpiling of new nuclear weapons are necessary. the dispute over iran's nuclear programmes requires a peaceful solution on the basis of negotiations which must be resumed. any military action, or threat of use of force, will be counterproductive and could have potentially dangerous consequences in the region. in this connection, we cannot but express our clear opposition to formulations which could in any way constitute an open door to justifying military interventions, as is the case in recital g of the joint resolution adopted.
in writing. - the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction is a serious threat to humanity, to international peace and security. extreme, unlimited and often fundamentalist terrorism leads the world to fear and to seek to prevent groups or states with unscrupulous leaders from acquiring this technological capacity. it is therefore important that the states which possess such weapons show, in a progressive manner, that they intend to reduce their arsenals by setting a good example. the next summit, scheduled for april this year, can make a very important contribution in this area, and we hope that there will be greater rigour and control over the unauthorized trade in nuclear materials. the us and china are also expected to play an important role in the denuclearisation of the korean peninsula. it is also important that all the states should not be excluded from the npt, because this is a matter which concerns all of them, not just a few.
mr president, this debate is once again demonstrating the double standards of the majority in the european parliament, the same majority which refused to condemn the military coup in honduras, ignoring that it led to the arrest and death of countless people, and which is now preparing to negotiate association agreements with a government that emerged from elections prepared by the coup plotters. of course, we all deplore the death of cuban citizen zapata tamaya in a cuban hospital after a hunger strike, but we cannot but deplore the terms of this debate and its unacceptable position against cuba, forgetting the serious consequences of the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the united states on cuba and the detention in american prisons of five cuban citizens who only wanted to defend their country. we cannot continue with an unacceptable common position which prevents the european union from maintaining comprehensive and open relations with the cuban government on the basis of bilateral interests. it is time to withdraw the common position to begin the normalisation of relations between the european union and cuba. we expect that from the spanish presidency.
madam president, we regret the death of orlando zapata, we regret that we have carried out his protest to its ultimate consequences, whatever the reasons behind it. but we cannot accept that, on the pretext of this sad and regrettable event, unacceptable political and ideological campaigns against cuba and its people are being renewed. whatever one may think of the cuban people's choices, those choices must be respected, their sovereign right to decide their own destiny and the political organization of their state must be respected. we therefore condemn any form of interference or attack, including the criminal blockade which has been imposed on it for almost half a century. we therefore also believe that the european union's logical position and the way forward should be to fully normalize relations with cuba, with the withdrawal of the common position against cuba, which represents an unacceptable discrimination against cuba and its people. above all, we do not accept the immense hypocrisy that runs through many of the seats in this parliament and we strongly condemn the double standards of the european union.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, madam president, commissioner, council, we are talking here about reinventing the energy system for europe through investment in low-carbon technologies. i think it's one of the very important challenges - as it's referred to, by the way, in the communication that's done. and it is one of the challenges that we have to face in a central way, but there is no clarification here, and that is why it is important to ask these questions and to ask for clarification. it seems that not only is there a lack of clarity on financing, but also a lack of political clarity. they talk about energy efficiency, carbon capture, nuclear, biofuels, solar energy, and they even talk about energy efficiency as the cheapest way to reduce emissions. i am surprised that there are other, much cheaper ways of reducing carbon emissions that are not even mentioned in this communication, such as, for example, reducing energy consumption, microgeneration, distribution and the different forms of distribution and different projects, which do not have to go through large structures, and access to energy. i think we would certainly be contributing to more financial clarification to make the plan cheaper. so, within this political clarification and within this financial clarification, there is still the matter of what i think is an absolutely important point, which is the emphasis that is constantly placed on public-private partnerships, as if they were the solution to everything. when you ask where the money comes from, the commission tells us that it comes from where it is. i confess i am no more enlightened by being told that the money will come from where it is, without being told exactly where it is. and so, with this bet on public-private partnerships that is systematically made when we talk about low-carbon technologies, we can safely be certain of one thing: the problem is, because you don't know where the money is coming from, and you know that it's a public-private partnership, you know in advance who's going to pay. it is the taxpayers who will pay in the beginning, it is the consumers who will also pay in the end. and we know that the ones who pay the least are, at the beginning, the institutions and the private organizations - who are the ones who make the investment, are paid for it, but in the end they monopolize the profits. without this clarification, it seems to me that we are once again systematically passing on to future generations the bill for the change in the european energy model.
research and technology play a key role in development in the low-carbon society. it is essential to bet on a radical change in society, based on the sustainability of cities, decentralized energy production and the competitiveness of industry. it is a policy that is essential for a prosperous, sustainable society, one that is prepared for the challenges of climate change, security of supply and globalisation, and a world leader in clean technologies. the set plan aims to contribute to this very objective. i welcome the basic guidelines that the communication presents on how to organise the logic of intervention between the public and private sectors, between community, national and regional funding. however, it is essential to increase public funding for scientific research in the area of clean technologies. europe must also create the conditions for more private investment in this area. it is urgent to move from words to deeds. the next eu financial perspective and the 8th framework programme for research and technological development will have to prioritise energy security, the fight against climate change and the environment. only in this way will we be able to maintain the competitiveness of our industry, promote economic growth and create jobs.
