on behalf of the gue/ngl group, we are starting today the debate on the broad guidelines for the 2011 budget and the priority that is suggested is that of youth, in particular at the time or period of life that marks the transition between studies and the labour market. in itself, this choice is to be welcomed. for example, the creation of an erasmus first job is proposed, and the problem in politics is that the devil is in the details. what do we mean when we talk about an erasmus first job? how are we gonna do that? by diverting erasmus funds to students or creating a new programme with fresh money? it is not a detail, just as it is not a detail whether this erasmus is for precarious jobs or whether, on the contrary, it is for decent jobs, which can be a gamble with a horizon for young people. is it a youth unemployment programme, as it should be? or could it turn out to be a program to hide unemployment? and it is with this example that i enter into the substance of the debate: the urgent issue for 2011 will be the widespread unemployment in the union. it is unemployment that confronts us with our responsibilities. it should challenge the european budget, but the 2011 budget is held hostage to a financial framework decided for seven years and which has not been touched despite the crisis. without a thorough and demanding review of this financial framework, the budget we will adopt at the end of the year will be doomed to continuity and mediocrity even if we adopt the best priorities in the world. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
youth, science and innovation are at the heart of the priorities of the next eu budget. investing in youth is investing in the future. education, vocational training and the transition from education to the labour market are at the heart of this budget. young graduates are increasingly being hit by unemployment. i therefore consider the erasmus first employment mobility programme to be a strategic bet for the future, by establishing a clear link between the education system and the labour market. the proposal for the creation of the erasmus first employment programme, which i have tabled together with mr josé manuel fernandes, is based on the following principles: first, additional funding to existing programmes in the field of education, science, training and innovation; secondly, each action will have a training component and a component where the trainee will have a contract with an innovative european company and will be co-financed by the european budget. i would also like to stress, as one of the other priorities in this budget, the areas of scientific research, innovation and the digital agenda. this budget also concentrates efforts on supporting the development of clean and innovative technologies, making an essential contribution to economic recovery and the dynamism of smes. the focus on youth, innovation and science is the key to re-establishing europe's global leadership.
the economic and social situation in the eu requires a substantial change in the priorities for 2011 that have guided previous budgets, including the current one for 2010. it demands that the budget be put at the service of policies which are quite different from those which have led to the unemployment of over 23 million people and have put over 85 million at risk of poverty. the objectives of a multiannual financial framework which reduced the structural funds to 0.37% of the eu's gross national income, which implied cuts in programmes of a social and environmental nature and in the fields of research, education and culture, need to be revised. the future budgets should be instruments for economic and social cohesion, understood as more than a dead letter in the treaties, for full employment with rights, investment and public services, environmental protection, cooperation and peace. it is not an instrument for the commodification of growing aspects of social life, liberalization, precarious employment, structural unemployment, foreign intervention and war. that is the point of the amendments we have tabled to the report: to show that there is an alternative and that it is not only possible but necessary.
certification mechanisms can contribute to the necessary enhancement of farmers' work by improving their income and to the promotion of food quality and safety. but the current certification procedures are complex, time-consuming and, above all, expensive, so their results have been perverse, particularly for small and mediumsized farmers. an increase in production costs and a distribution of income along the value chain, even more unfavourable to the producer, with the insertion of another agent in the chain doing business. for this reason, and also as an effective guarantee of transparency, quality and safety for consumers, certification should be carried out by public bodies and should not represent an additional cost for producers. but above all, a quality policy requires another agricultural policy: a thorough reform of the cap, which defends local production, the right to produce and the right to food sovereignty, which defends farmers and consumers from the consequences of deregulation of world trade and unbridled liberalisation of markets, by stopping them both in the framework of bilateral agreements and in the framework of the wto.
it is time for the leaders of the european union to recognise their responsibilities in the serious social crisis that is being experienced at european and world level as a result of the financial and economic crisis which they have facilitated by deregulating financial and commercial markets and by pressing for free trade agreements with third countries, without taking into account the interests of workers and peoples. the increase in unemployment and increasingly precarious and low-paid work are increasing poverty and are a direct consequence of neo-liberal policies and the crisis of capitalism. the ilo and the oecd believe that the peak of unemployment in the industrialized countries has not yet been reached and that in the near future more than 200 million workers may be pushed into extreme poverty, which means that the number of working poor may reach 1.5 billion, mainly women and young people. it is time to put an end to the backwardness we are experiencing in terms of social and labour rights. priority must be given to quality employment with rights, while at the same time respecting at least the ilo conventions. without the creation of new jobs with entitlements there is no way out of the crisis.
the world day against tuberculosis, which is being marked today, is an occasion to call for the strengthening of political dialogue and the involvement of governments and civil society in this cause. in the european union, the number of tuberculosis cases has been declining. in portugal, there is also a marked reduction, but with an incidence rate still above the eu average. this reduction is associated with the good performance of the national plan for the fight against tuberculosis. however, in some countries there has been a resurgence of the disease. the various action plans promoted by the european commission are moving in the right direction. i would like to emphasize the partnership between europe and the developing countries in the conduct of clinical trials. support from the framework programme for research and technological development for the life sciences is also important. it is essential to strengthen the role of clinical and scientific research in the fight against tuberculosis. it is therefore essential to continue to work towards discovering new and better tools to combat tb and to promote innovative technologies in diagnostics, medicines and vaccines. i therefore call on the commission and governments to join forces and step up the fight against tuberculosis so that we can successfully control and eradicate this disease.
the crises mentioned in the report (food, energy, climate, financial, economic and social) are but differentiated expressions of the same structural crisis that has been dragging on for decades. in some regions, such as sub-saharan africa, per capita wealth relative to other regions of the world has been diverging from decade to decade in a continuous way. despite the disparities, developing countries generally share some common characteristics: dependence on exports of a small number of raw materials, lack of economic diversification, a high concentration in agriculture, the extractive or energy sector, or tourism, and a strong dominance of foreign capital. the promotion of an export model and the gradual liberalisation of trade which has been imposed on these countries, if necessary by means of blackmail, as the process of negotiating economic partnership agreements shows, lead to an increase in the dependence of these countries, compromising endogenous development potential. but it is external debt that continues to be the main drain on the resources of developing countries. the debt has reached a colossal size and is self-sustaining, while maintaining the nature of its relations with the northern countries. its cancellation is first and foremost a matter of justice.
in writing. - article 3 (1) of council directive 72/462/eec of 12 december 1972 on health and veterinary inspection problems upon importation of bovine, ovine and caprine animals and fresh meat or meat products from third countries led the council, on a proposal from the commission, to adopt a list of third countries from which member states are to authorise imports of bovine, ovine and caprine animals and fresh meat. although this directive has been repealed, the procedure has remained and the list has been amended over the years, and the commission now proposes to create a regulation which will codify all the relevant amendments made over the years and which should be amended frequently so that it is constantly updated. i believe that this procedure brings clarity and transparency, not only for the member states in the event of changes, but also for third countries exporting the products concerned to the eu.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report on health problems in the importation of bovine, porcine, ovine and caprine animals and fresh meat or meat products from third countries. this report is based on council directive 72/462/eec of 12 december 1972, which led the council to adopt a list of third countries from which member states are to authorise imports of bovine animals, swine and fresh meat. despite the repeal of this directive, the procedure has been maintained and the list has been amended over the years, and it is now proposed that the commission should present a regulation codifying all the relevant amendments made over the years, which should be amended frequently so that it is constantly updated. i believe that this procedure not only enhances food security for eu citizens, but also brings greater clarity to member states and third countries exporting meat products to the eu.
in writing. - the food security of eu citizens is a fundamental issue that should concern us all. the definition of health policy criteria for the importation of certain live animals and their fresh meat from third countries must be very strict and these products must be systematically controlled so that we can verify that they are being complied with. it is therefore crucial that a list of third countries that meet the animal and public health criteria and veterinary certification to export live animals (bovine, porcine, ovine and caprine) and their fresh meat to eu countries is drawn up.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. since 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf has been extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic and financial crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious economic and financial crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to respond to the consequences of this crisis, particularly in terms of the support to be given to people who have been confronted, overnight, with the reality of unemployment. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal concerning the mobilisation of the egf for lithuania to support workers made redundant in the 49 companies operating in the furniture manufacturing sector.
in writing. - like the building sector in lithuania, which we have discussed earlier, the furniture industry has also been affected by globalisation and is now exposed to the products of fierce competition and production on a different scale. the conditions for applying for and mobilising the fund having been met, i think we should support this mobilisation.
in writing. - just two weeks after parliament approved the mobilisation of this fund to deal with redundancies in lithuania and germany, we are again approving its mobilisation, this time to deal with redundancies in 49 furniture manufacturing companies in lithuania. as we said then, the number of workers made redundant has long since exceeded the commission's initial estimates of the number of workers who could benefit from the fund. we would remind you that this is a sector which has been experiencing serious difficulties in portugal too, particularly in the municipalities where it has a significant presence, such as paredes and paços de ferreira, which has also led to redundancies and to the worsening of the social situation in the region. each new request for action makes it clearer that, far from the palliative measures - which are certainly necessary - what is required are urgent measures to protect the productive sectors and employment, particularly those most vulnerable to the crisis and those which are part of the exploitation of the development potential of each country, by promoting public projects and supporting micro, small and mediumsized enterprises, the cooperative sector... in writing. the lithuanian construction and furniture industries are joined by the clothing industry, which has been hit hard by globalisation and has thrown significant numbers of workers into unemployment. the massive vote in favour in the parliamentary committee responsible confirms the apparent goodness of the measure. i therefore see no reason to vote against the mobilisation of the fund in this case.
in writing. - just two weeks after parliament approved the mobilisation of this fund to deal with redundancies in lithuania and germany, we are again approving its mobilisation, this time also to deal with redundancies in 45 companies active in the clothing manufacturing sector in lithuania. it is worth remembering that this is a sector which is also in serious crisis in portugal, suffering particularly severely from the effects of the liberalization of world trade, without the necessary safeguard measures having been taken. each new request for the fund to be mobilised gives renewed urgency to the measures we have been advocating, namely the effective fight against unemployment and the creation and promotion of jobs with rights based on the development of economic activity, the dynamism of public employment, the eradication of precariousness and the reduction of working hours without reduction of wages. the commission has also taken measures to combat the relocation of firms, by making public aid, particularly community aid, conditional on compliance with obligations such as the protection of employment and local development. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission.
in writing. - the eu is a space of solidarity, and the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to this end. these supports are essential for helping the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who have had their businesses relocated and is therefore essential to ensure that they can return to work in the future. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries, notably portugal and spain, and it is now up to lithuania to provide this aid.

in writing. - the second european roma summit represents a commitment to dialogue on cultural diversity and what it represents in terms of human wealth. education is the key to the integration process. by providing education and training, we are fighting against exclusion, unemployment and discrimination. we are also ensuring a more just, more creative and more dynamic society. it is important to integrate ethnic minorities not only into the labour market but also into all spheres of society. protecting fundamental rights and creating a common area of freedom, security and justice are objectives of european integration. i applaud all those who promote integration at the local level, including politicians, teachers and associations, as they are often responsible for access to housing, health care, education, culture and an increased quality of life. i call on the european union and the member states to make concerted efforts and to focus on political strategies with clear legislative commitments and credible budgetary allocations. it is important to adopt a common position on the financing policy through the structural funds and the pre-accession funds.
in writing. - it is estimated that between 10 and 12 million roma live in the eu, making them one of the largest ethnic minorities in europe. most of these people live in conditions of extreme poverty and on the margins of society, with limited access to employment, education and health care. this ethnic minority continues to be the victim of discrimination and social exclusion, despite efforts to integrate it. the eu has been supporting member states' efforts to implement effective policies, including by supporting specific projects and by trying to ensure the correct and effective application of anti-discrimination laws. a conference was held in brussels this month to present the various eu projects under development. the results are expected to be discussed at the 2nd roma summit in cordoba in april. i hope that the outcome of this summit will contribute to a strong european political commitment to the future strategy for promoting the inclusion of roma people in the economic, social and cultural life of europe and ensuring equal opportunities for all in the eu, including roma.
in writing. - gypsy communities have existed throughout europe for many centuries and until recently were the target of persecution by many of the member states. their traditional nomadism, the activities they engaged in, the high rate of inbreeding and the exclusion to which they were voted contributed to the labelling of members of these communities as undesirable, dangerous and anti-social. not only do these prejudices persist today, but the consequences historically inherent in them persist, and today the roma are still one of the communities with the lowest rates of schooling and the highest crime rates. it will be for sociologists and historians to assess the causes and consequences of the problems affecting the roma. politicians are asked to be able to do something for the communities they serve. it is therefore particularly important that, on the basis of serious and in-depth studies on this subject, concrete ways and measures be identified to combat the exclusion of roma and to promote their genuine integration into the societies in which they live.
in writing. - the resolution on the second european roma summit to be held in cordoba on 8 and 9 april expresses concern at the discrimination suffered by the roma community in the fields of education, housing, employment and equal access to health systems and other public services, as well as the surprisingly low level of their participation in political life. the european parliament has, however, called on the european commission to draw up new proposals on the social inclusion of roma and urges the member states to make more visible efforts to address their just rights, taking into account that anti-discrimination measures are insufficient to facilitate the social inclusion of roma and that concerted efforts are needed at eu level, including in financial terms. the resolution recommends that the council adopt a common position on the financing policies under the structural funds and the pre-accession funds in order to reflect the european political commitment to promote the inclusion of the roma community. we hope that this second european roma summit will focus on strategic political commitments that reflect a political will to bridge the gap between roma communities and majority populations in various countries.
in writing. − the eu is a place of solidarity and inclusion, and it should do what is necessary to ensure that roma are no longer discriminated against and have the same rights to education, employment, health and housing in all member states, as well as in those that in the future wish to join. decisive steps must be taken to end discrimination, but this will require that roma do not exclude themselves and help them to integrate into a european area of inclusion.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report entitled 'the quality policy for agricultural products: what strategy to adopt?' because quality is a decisive factor for the competitiveness of european products on international markets. in this context, i welcome the introduction of mandatory labelling of the origin of products, which allows consumers to be informed about quality standards, but also about environmental protection and animal welfare.
in writing. - the common agricultural policy will necessarily have to rely on the high quality of its agricultural products, an undeniable added value for european competitiveness in a global market environment. quality policy cannot be separated from the rest of the common agricultural policy, nor can it ignore new challenges such as the fight against climate change, the conservation of biodiversity, energy supply and the development of bioenergy, animal welfare and water management in agriculture. the future policy on the quality of agricultural products must also take due account of the increasing demands of consumers, bearing in mind that, at the time of decision, quality matters to an informed consumer. i would remind you, however, that the quality policy for agricultural products cannot be so demanding that it puts small and mediumsized farmers at risk or the existence of traditional products from certain regions which cannot see their manufacture dependent on uniform and blind rules. the aim of quality policy should be to promote the member states' agriculture on the world market and to defend european products, serving both producers and consumers.
in writing. - the report under discussion contains some positive aspects, such as the defence of the application of instruments which allow the valorization and promotion of small-scale local production, as well as traditional and artisanal productions linked to certain regions of origin and associated with a geographical designation, while at the same time recognizing the delays, complexity and excessive cost faced by small producers in accessing quality certificates. however, it ignores issues that are essential to safeguarding the quality of agricultural production and the sustainability of agricultural activity in the eu countries, such as: the consequences of the deregulation of world trade and the unbridled liberalisation of markets, whether in the framework of bilateral agreements or in the framework of the wto; the various dangers inherent in the introduction of genetically modified organisms into the environment, in the ways in which this has been conducted; the need for a thorough reform of the cap, which defends local production, the right to produce and the right to food sovereignty.
in writing. - the quality of european agricultural products is a world-recognised heritage, and there is a need to protect and distinguish them from products of lower quality, food safety and sometimes even counterfeit. to prevent this from happening, it is imperative that these products be labelled, so that consumers can obtain reliable information about them. it is also important to have a clear understanding that imported agricultural products meet the same requirements as those imposed on agricultural products produced in the eu, so that there are no distortions of competition. so i vote in favour.
in writing. - i vote in favour of this report, which introduces fundamental questions for sustainable development and the progressive integration of the acp countries into the world economy. developing countries are the most affected by global warming, and it is therefore essential to step up all measures to combat climate change, such as the transfer of appropriate technologies. it is also important to agree on the eu's emissions trading scheme, whereby at least 25% of the revenues generated from the auctioning of carbon dioxide emission allowances will be devoted to aid to developing countries. issues such as sustainable development and green growth should be eu strategic priorities. i call for additional funds to be allocated to developing countries and for these to be sustainable in the medium and long term, from the private sector, the carbon market and the public sector in industrialized countries and the most economically advanced developing countries.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis that is afflicting us has had disastrous effects on developing countries, which have already been victims of successive crises (food, energy, climate and financial). it is urgent to help those who did not cause this crisis, but who are the most affected. the european union and the developed countries must respond swiftly, firmly and effectively. i believe it is crucial that member states meet their official development assistance commitments and strengthen their commitments to achieve the millennium development goals. the commission and the council must also reform international development cooperation, which is one of the main causes of ineffective development aid. i also think that the improvement in the credit facilities granted by financial institutions to the poorest countries is commendable. but it is not enough. i support the calls in this report for more sustained support for development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the effects of the global financial and economic crisis on developing countries and on development cooperation. it should be stressed that the developing countries, although not at the origin of the international crisis, are disproportionately affected by it. as the main donor of aid to developing countries, the european union has a key role to play in providing the necessary leadership to adopt measures at international level to achieve the millennium development goals.
in writing. - when we speak of the financial, economic and social crisis we are currently experiencing, we are referring to a global crisis in which special attention must be paid to the developing countries which have been directly and indirectly affected by this crisis. existing mechanisms for aid to the least-favoured countries and their populations facing conditions of extreme poverty and misery should be applied in a more efficient and targeted manner, without leading to dependency which could have negative effects on growth, wages and employment. the instruments and policies of development cooperation should therefore be ensured to enable effective development, which requires more coordinated action at both bilateral and multilateral levels. humanitarian aid, cooperation and development actions should be implemented and in this field the member states, the european union and international organisations have a key role to play. however, i am opposed to the adoption of an international financial transaction tax (tobin tax) to help finance these countries, because of the impact this would have on society at large.
in writing. - the report under discussion deals with very important issues, defending correct positions, such as the end of tax havens, the cancellation of the external debt of some countries, the need to increase efforts in the field of official development aid and the taxation of financial transactions. we cannot, however, fail to point out some negative and even contradictory aspects of the report, such as the defence of trade liberalisation, as it has been conducted by the eu, in particular through the so-called economic partnership agreements, which it has sought to impose on the acp countries, despite the resistance and denunciations of its negative consequences on the part of many of them, as well as the absence of a more comprehensive approach to the problem of external debt.

in writing. − in the context of the current economic, financial and social crisis, the ecb's role has been crucial in the way it has presented measures to respond to it, notably through measures that have enabled member states to maintain their liquidity, grant credit to businesses and reduce interest rates, amongst others. i believe, however, that exit strategies should take account of real financial market stability, otherwise the effects felt so far, and which have been mitigated by these measures, will become even more pronounced. i also think that some reflection is needed on the adaptation of the stability and growth pact, with the aim of making it more flexible and adapted to exceptional situations such as the one we are experiencing.
in writing. - as we know, the ecb's decisions are also partly responsible for the crisis we are experiencing. it is interesting to note that the report itself does not fail to make some criticisms of the ecb's actions. the ecb's economic projections, like those of the imf and other international institutions, failed to predict the severity of the 2008 recession. it also does so when it 'notes that the interest rate cuts by the ecb were less drastic than those by other central banks, such as the us federal reserve and the bank of england in the uk, and than many economic observers expected at the time'. but the report continues to defend the ecb and its guidelines, even going into major contradictions, which is why we voted against it. however, there are some other aspects that deserve reflection, in particular when it expresses its disappointment that the additional liquidity injected by the ecb has not sufficiently mitigated the credit crunch faced by industry, in particular by small and medium-sized enterprises, and that some banks have used this liquidity to improve their margins and cover their losses.
in writing. - the serious economic crisis affecting the whole world has been felt most acutely within the eu. the ecb's response to the crisis was effective, although it sometimes failed by being late or unasserted, notably the policy of reducing interest rates, which was more radical and effective in the united kingdom and the us federal reserve. we must learn from our mistakes so that they will not be repeated in the future. it should be noted that the treaty of lisbon makes the ecb an eu institution, thus increasing the responsibility of the european parliament, since it is the institution through which the ecb is accountable to european citizens.

in writing. − administrative cooperation between member states in the fight against fraud and economic crime is of paramount importance for reasons of fairness and justice, and because of the enormous impact on the economic situation of the countries. in the field of vat, where there are numerous cases of fraud, it is essential that there is a legal framework with strong measures that lead to a further reduction of such cases. greater cooperation between central administrations is desirable, through the sharing of information, provided that individual privacy is respected, of complete databases, and of well-trained staff for the detection and treatment of such cases. member states should implement the instruments provided for by the european union as quickly as possible in order to create a more transparent and effective system for combating tax fraud.
in writing. − the distortions caused by vat fraud affect the overall balance of the own resources system, which must be fair and transparent to ensure the proper functioning of the union. since public authorities are obliged to make up the corresponding revenue shortfall, the increase in fraud translates into a higher tax burden on companies that comply with tax rules. although investigations into the extent of vat evasion and fraud have not been carried out in all member states, the international vat association estimates that vat losses range from eur 60 to eur 100 billion per year across the european union. greater cooperation between central administrations through information sharing, with respect for individual privacy, is desirable. member states should implement the instruments provided for by the european union as quickly as possible in order to create a more transparent and effective system for combating tax fraud.
