in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on transportable pressure equipment which will repeal the current directive in force as well as a number of other related directives. given that the current directive contains technical provisions which are contrary to international standards on the transport of dangerous goods, it is essential to eliminate inconsistencies and bring the technical requirements into line with international rules.
in writing. − the transport of pressure equipment, in particular tanks, containers and bottles, is currently governed by directive 1999/36/ec, which lays down safety requirements for road and rail transport and sets common standards for the design, construction and subsequent inspection of such equipment. these rules, however, are in breach of international standards for the transport of dangerous goods, which is why the commission has put forward its proposal for a revision of the above-mentioned directive. this proposal does not represent any substantial change to the current regulatory framework either in terms of scope or in terms of the main provisions, but is intended only to eliminate these inconsistencies by bringing the technical requirements for the transport of dangerous goods into line with the international rules in force. i therefore support the rapporteur's view that, in the absence of a horizontal solution between the institutions on the content of the new provisions on comitology, this procedure should be concluded as soon as possible with an agreement at first reading.
in writing. − the transport of pressure equipment, including tanks, containers and bottles, is currently governed by directive 1999/36/ec. the directive ensures the free movement of such equipment within the community, including its placing on the market, by establishing common standards for the design, construction and subsequent inspection of such equipment. but some of the technical provisions of the current directive are contrary to international standards for the transport of dangerous goods. the commission has therefore put forward a proposal for a revision of the directive, which will repeal the current directive on transportable pressure equipment, as well as a number of other related directives. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of this resolution, which asks the committee to approve the report without further amendments and to instruct the rapporteur to enter into negotiations with the council.
in writing. - increasing concern for ecological and environmental protection issues leads us to take extra care with safety rules for the transport of pressure equipment. the directive aims to enhance safety and ensure the free movement of pressure equipment in the eu by defining in a clear and transparent way the rules that must be complied with to ensure the safety of the transport of pressure equipment in all member states, by harmonising procedures across the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on safety charges in the aviation sector. this proposal is of great importance in defending and protecting the rights of consumers and passengers, since it lays down a series of basic principles which must be respected by airport operators in determining their security rates. these are: non-discrimination, consultation and redress, transparency of costs and cost-relatedness of security fees, and the creation of a supervisory authority.
in writing. the european commission has put forward a proposal setting out the basic principles to be followed by airport operators in determining their security charges: (i) non-discrimination; (ii) consultation and redress; (iii) transparency of costs and the relationship with security charges; and (iv) the creation of a supervisory authority. the main question arising in this connection is the financing of the more restrictive security measures which must be implemented. the european parliament has repeatedly called for the financing of security charges to be regulated, but without success. the rapporteur rightly argues that the financing of these more restrictive measures cannot be borne solely by passengers (by outsourcing the costs) but must be financed by the states, which are ultimately responsible for the security of their airports. finally, i would remind you that it is never too late to invest in the safety of airports and passengers, as the recent attempts, fortunately foiled, to carry out terrorist attacks against civil aviation have shown.
in writing. - the european parliament has repeatedly called for the financing of security charges to be regulated in order to increase transparency and to ensure that taxes and security charges are used for their real purposes, but in vain. it has also considered that member states should bear the costs of applying more restrictive measures. the terrorist incident of a few weeks ago has once again demonstrated that airport security is the responsibility of the states and that the existing security measures, as well as those recently planned, are aimed at preventing acts of terrorism. however, what has so far been omitted in the context of the debate is the fact that the measures in question are ultimately paid for by the passengers. i agree with the amendments introduced by this resolution which will avoid parallel procedures and unnecessary administrative costs in this area.
in writing. − increasing security at airports has brought additional costs which have been borne by passengers. the additional costs of the more restrictive security measures have to be borne by the states, because they exist to prevent terrorist acts. however, it has been found that the costs of these measures are being borne by passengers. it is against this background that the vote in favour of this report is justified.
in writing. - the european parliament has already called on the commission on several occasions to regulate the financing of safety fees in the aviation sector. the commission has always advocated greater transparency and the allocation of taxes and security charges to their real purposes, considering that member states should bear the costs of applying more restrictive measures. although the commission in its proposal did not address this issue, seeking only a new economic impact assessment with a view to reducing costs, based on the principles of non-discrimination, consultation and redress and transparency of costs, this document aims to finance more restrictive measures, when they cause additional costs, by the state. i stress the importance of airport security measures and i vote in favour of this parliament's initiative. the proposal, which will apply to all commercial airports in the european union, is intrinsically linked to concerns about the right to information, non-discrimination of passengers and consumer protection. i believe that only by harmonizing legislation and clarifying the responsibility of airlines and member states for the adoption of safety measures will the objectives of greater transparency and avoidance of unnecessary costs be achieved.
in writing. - the proposal is a proposal from the european commission which is nothing more than the codification of previous rules and regulations. detailed amendments are also made. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the council's proposal is implemented.
in writing. - the proposal is, from a technical point of view, a proposal for the codification of the legal text. however, the commission was forced to reword the text, as it contains minor amendments to the annex. i voted in favour of adopting the amendments.
in writing. the development of the transeuropean transport network has been changing and redefining over the last few years. an effective trans-european transport network is essential for a healthy internal market and contributes to strengthening economic and social cohesion. the icelandic volcano phenomenon has unequivocally demonstrated the need for an effective transeuropean transport network which can respond in a coordinated manner to the problems arising in these situations. this decision is important because it provides guidance on the objectives, priorities and broad lines of action in the field of the transeuropean transport network.
in writing. - as regards national priorities in the context of the trans-european transport network, i believe it is important to focus not only on rail but also on motorways and on the interoperability and co-operability of the various modes of transport. only a genuine combined transport network, backed up by effective management, can make the maritime alternative, which is essential for our country, which benefits from privileged access to waterways, and is truly crucial for island and outermost regions such as madeira, competitive. it is also a key tool for the further completion of the internal market and for territorial cohesion. the adoption of this report by the plenary, which was unanimously adopted by parliament, the commission and the council, and which is very technical, follows the virtually unanimous indication of the committee on transport and tourism. in short, this proposal, which i myself supported, does not change the content of the text of the transeuropean transport network, adding only the maps of the 12 member states which joined the european union in 2004 and 2007. the revision of the community guidelines for the development of the trans-european transport network is in preparation and should not be known before the end of 2010.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that in the face of the current crisis it is necessary to find mechanisms for speeding up the implementation of aid programmes, thus allowing greater use of community funding, particularly for citizens, in particular the unemployed. the proposal aims at some regulatory changes to simplify the rules for implementing cohesion policy and to increase pre-financing (advance payments) for erdf and esf programmes. economic forecasts foresee a sharp decline in growth in the european union - 1.1% in 2010; in this context, this report is presented as a contribution to the response to the financial crisis and its socioeconomic repercussions. in this sense i consider it very important for greater transparency and simplification of the rules governing cohesion policy. this contribution will have a positive impact on the pace of programme implementation, particularly as it will give national, regional and local authorities the possibility of using clearer and less bureaucratic rules, which will allow more flexibility in adapting programmes to new challenges.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 laying down general provisions on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund as regards the simplification of certain requirements and certain provisions relating to financial management. the unprecedented and severe impact of the current economic and financial crisis on member states' budgets requires simplification of the management of cohesion policy and an increase in advance payments. despite the difficult economic situation, these measures will allow a regular cash flow to be maintained to guarantee payments to beneficiaries during the implementation of these programmes.
in writing. - i consider community cohesion policy to be a central issue for the development and implementation of the principle of solidarity between member states advocated by the european union. as such, and particularly in times of crisis - when these funds can help to reduce, in particular, the impact on the regions most in need - it is essential to improve the current structure of cohesion policy so that funds can be delivered more efficiently, with more effective results and in a timely manner. on the other hand, more flexibility is needed in the instruments, since rigid instruments, unable to adapt to unforeseeable circumstances such as a crisis, are detrimental to the eu's economic development. it must also be ensured that the funds made available under cohesion policy are being properly used by the member states and that the available resources are spent efficiently. to this end, i believe it is essential to rethink not only the structure of the union's cohesion policy, but also the available control mechanisms and the existence of coercive means available in the event of non-compliance by the member states.
in writing. the aim of this proposal is to provide an additional economic incentive to certain member states which have been hard hit by the economic crisis. it was submitted following the european economic recovery plan, in the context of which the provisions implementing the basic regulation, as mentioned above, had already been amended in 2009 to allow for more flexibility in advance payments. the main element of the commission proposal is to deal with the consequences of the financial crisis, so the proposed solution was to introduce a temporary option so that member states experiencing severe cash flow difficulties could request a 100% reimbursement of the funding of labour market measures under the esf, i.e. a derogation from the co-financing principle. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has entailed a change in the legislative procedure. instead of the 'yes' or 'no' vote, parliament now has full powers to decide on the content of the text under the ordinary legislative procedure. i voted in favour of this and it is now expected that the commission will present the corresponding amending budget proposal for consideration and approval by the budgetary authority.
in writing. − the commission proposal introduces a temporary option, which member states in severe cash-flow difficulties could use to finance the necessary measures to promote growth and employment to combat the crisis and which are eligible under the european social fund, which would allow them to request 100% reimbursement from the commission for 2009 and 2010, thus eliminating the need for national co-financing during this period. this is a measure we have been advocating, in order to enable the full use of community funds at a time when they are most needed. the council's position is not coincidental, however, and only points to the need for 'an additional prefinancing fraction for the member states most affected by the crisis'. the document to be voted on in the european parliament is alongside the council's position, which seems to us to be more ambiguous and less favourable to the member states most affected by the crisis. however, we consider that 'extending the deadline for calculating the automatic cancellation of annual budget commitments for the 2007 total annual contribution in order to improve the absorption of funds committed to certain operational programmes' is a positive aspect.
in writing. − simplifying access to the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund is essential to supporting the member states most affected by the economic crisis. as the real impact of the financial crisis on the real economy and the labour market becomes clear, measures are needed to improve access to union funding instruments. there needs to be a regular cash flow to facilitate payment to beneficiaries during the implementation of the programmes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal because i consider that this is a matter of great importance for portugal, and particularly for its outermost regions, which are more vulnerable to the crisis we are going through, as they feel its effects more intensely and take longer to overcome it. although i agree with the content of the report in general, i cannot help but point out the difficulties faced by regional and local authorities in securing the resources needed to meet their share of the funding for projects subsidized by community funds. it is with discouragement that i have seen the council block the possibility of increasing the community co-financing rate to 100%, even if only temporarily and as an advance which would be compensated in the last years of the programmes. the compromise solution, although not optimal, allows, exceptionally, for community funds for 2007, which have not been absorbed into slower-starting projects, to benefit from an extended period before being cancelled. we are all aware of the difficult choices facing families and businesses today and of the importance that measures such as those envisaged here can have in a desired rapid and sustained economic recovery.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty clearly assigns new responsibilities and powers to the ep. with its entry into force on 1 december 2009, many proposals which had been submitted by the commission on the basis of the treaties but were still pending on that date (at different stages of the legislative or non-legislative process) will be subject to changes. in some cases there will be differences in the decision-making process due to a significant extension of the application of the ordinary legislative procedure or the application of a new approval procedure with regard to the conclusion of international agreements; in other cases, there is only a change in the legal basis, and the commission intends to make a formal change in its 'omnibus' proposal. however, there are proposals (under the old third pillar) whose legal framework has been substantially amended and has therefore become obsolete and which should be replaced by new ones. as rapporteur for the initiative to create an evaluation mechanism to monitor the application of the schengen acquis, i would ask that a new proposal be submitted as soon as possible. i therefore support the ep's resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the consequences of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon for interinstitutional decision-making procedures. the entry into force of the new treaty requires a redefinition of the legal bases for a number of pending cases. the commission and the council must urgently promote the necessary changes in the light of the new regulatory framework.
in writing. - the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon not only required a new institutional arrangement and a new hierarchy of rules, but also a special caution about the decision-making processes under way at that time. these amendments have altered the legal basis and the procedures for the review, which fully justify their re-examination.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty gives the ep new responsibilities and powers. with its entry into force on 1 december 2009, many proposals which had been submitted by the commission on the basis of the treaties but which were still pending at that date will be subject to transformation. in some cases there will be differences in the decision-making process due to a significant extension of the application of the ordinary legislative procedure or the application of a new approval procedure with regard to the conclusion of international agreements; in other cases, there is only a change in the legal basis, and the commission intends to make a formal change in its 'omnibus' proposal. however, there are proposals (under the old third pillar) whose legal framework has been substantially amended and has therefore become obsolete and which should be replaced by new ones. i therefore vote in favour of the ep resolution.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty tackles the democratic deficit by strengthening the powers of the european and national parliaments. this is the new instrument which allows the legislator to delegate part of his powers to the european commission (article 290 tfeu), provided that it is an act of general scope which allows the supplementing or amending of parts of a legislative act which are not considered to be essential. it will thus allow for more rapid and simple filling of gaps or regulation or updating of more detailed aspects of a legislative act, avoiding overly complicated and lengthy legislative procedures which would have had negative consequences for citizens. the possibility of withdrawing the delegation at any time and the requirement for prior consent of the ep (and the council) before the entry into force of acts adopted by the commission under a delegation are both safeguarded. i support this innovation which should replace the so-called 'infamous' 'comitology' system, but it is now urgent to define how these delegations can be made, their scope, their purpose, the working methods to be used and the conditions under which control can be exercised by the legislator.
in writing. - the implementation of the lisbon treaty requires clarification of some of its rules, in particular those of a legal and procedural nature such as those relating to the legislative process, the hierarchies of rules and the powers of the institutions. article 290 (1) of the treaty provides that a legislative act may delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of the legislative act. it does so with special care and by imposing strong restrictions on its scope. nevertheless, it is important to densify the law as it is embodied in the treaty in order to avoid too disparate interpretations which would jeopardize the coherence of community law. if these acts are commonplace in the member states, the same cannot be said of the present ones. the legitimacy of the commission and the legitimacy of governments are not the same, and therefore the legislative delegation to the former should be used with greater care and diligence and with greater parsimony. i support the view that the use of delegation should make it possible to adopt simple and accessible legislation, thus contributing to legal certainty, the effectiveness of delegation and the control of the delegator.
in writing. - the treaty of lisbon amended the old comitology system by referring to new legal instruments such as delegated and implementing acts. the new treaty gives the european parliament the role of co-legislator alongside the council. the possibility of delegating to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts supplementing legislative acts is a step towards placing the two institutions on an equal footing. this report aims to clarify the conditions under which the institution of the delegation of powers of the parliament and the council to the european commission, as provided for in article 290 tfeu, can take place. the document stresses the importance of the principle of the freedom of the legislator to delegate powers to the commission as a means of 'better lawmaking'. the report safeguards the need to avoid imposing on the legislator obligations other than those already enshrined in the treaty, and the legislator should enable the commission to exercise the delegated power effectively and to monitor its use properly. for the reasons mentioned above, and considering that the first priority must be to adapt the acquis in areas which, before the treaty of lisbon, were not subject to the codecision procedure, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the european commission has presented a communication on the strategic objectives and recommendations for community maritime transport policy up to 2018. the commission proposal covers a wide range of issues relating to community maritime transport policy, allowing the maritime transport sector's stakeholders a wide margin of manoeuvre and initiative to implement the strategic objectives and recommendations now set out. the main issues addressed by the commission proposal are (i) the value and competitive position of european shipping in a global market; (ii) employment opportunities in the maritime sector; (iii) the quality of european shipping; (iv) international cooperation; (v) european shipping as a component of the european economy and a driving force for economic integration; and (vi) europe's position as a world leader in maritime research and innovation. this matter, which is linked to portugal's geographical position and the strategic importance of the sea, is of fundamental interest to our country, and all efforts to build a 'maritime economy' deserve our support and commitment.
in writing. − the european maritime sector makes an unequivocal and vital contribution to the internal economy of the community and to the european transport system. the interests of the european maritime transport sector should therefore be given priority in the development of a general european transport policy. it should be understood that the european maritime sector operates and competes mainly in a global market. the shipping sector faces major environmental challenges. it is essential to substantially improve the environmental performance of seagoing vessels and the emissions of sox, nox, fine particulate matter and co2. in this connection i would stress the need to reach agreements at world level to combat the risk of flag changes for countries which are not entitled to participate. in the field of security, i would stress that member states are invited to implement the proposed security package quickly and correctly, in particular in relation to the paris memorandum (on risk-based inspections). this will prevent unnecessary inspections, increase the effectiveness of monitoring and reduce red tape for those subject to inspections.
in writing. - the adoption of this resolution sets out the objectives necessary for a community policy on maritime transport. this means of transport is gaining prominence, not least because it is environmentally friendly and has the potential to become even more efficient in this respect. the shipping sector is essential to the european economy, not only as a transport of passengers, raw materials, goods and energy products, but also as the core of a wide range of maritime activities, such as shipping, logistics, research, tourism, fisheries and aquaculture, to name just a few.
in writing. − maritime transport is undoubtedly a european competitive advantage, but there is still much to be done to promote intermodal and co-modality, including the repositioning of the sea route as a truly competitive alternative. the maritime industry faces a number of challenges which can be turned into real opportunities if we know how to take advantage of them by focusing on training young technicians who can fill the gap in the sector. technological development and the reduction of unnecessary red tape to attract investment in the port sector are also priorities. safer and cleaner shipping should be pursued, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and responding effectively to acts of piracy. the pressures threatening the positioning of the european maritime fleet, which mainly originate from state aid to the sector in third countries, must be managed within a framework to be developed within the wto. european infrastructure and port capacity deserve further development, as do the maritime motorways, which are so important for southern and peripheral countries such as portugal and for outermost regions such as madeira. the report we have adopted today broadly covers these guidelines and has therefore earned my support.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on europeana next steps - which calls for greater involvement of all eu member states in making available contributions from their national libraries and cultural institutions, in order to enable all europeans to have full access to their own cultural heritage. the aim of storing more than 15 million works on the site in the short term could help to protect europe's cultural heritage, in order to offer future generations the possibility of building a european collective memory.
in writing. - even in the periods when the division and even hostility between the states of the continent was most pronounced, european culture and science have always been able to overcome these limits and to spread throughout the area which today comprises the union and even beyond. in this connection, it is only right to highlight the role of the universities which, having their origins in religion, made a decisive contribution to reconnecting the disadvantaged parts of what became the christian republic, and to remember all those who were able to bridge the divisions and assert their thought throughout the continent and, hence, the world. as a portuguese, heir to a language and culture that have spread throughout the world, i cannot but support the efforts being made to make european culture and science more visible and accessible to all who want to enjoy them. europeana is thus the heir to the best european tradition. i hope that the project will continue in a sustained manner and that my country, in respect of its universalist vocation, will contribute to it with new commitment.
in writing. − europeana was launched in november 2008 and aims to provide universal access to europe's cultural and scientific heritage via the internet. it currently offers 6 million digitized works and aims to reach 10 million objects by june 2010. the second phase of the project will be marked by the launch in 2011 of a more multilingual europeana.eu with more semantic web pages. only 5% of all digitised books are available on europeana, and of these, about half come from france, followed by germany (16%), the netherlands (8%) and the united kingdom (8%). the other states have a contribution of 5% or less. greater contribution by member states is desirable i support the call for europeana's holdings to reach a minimum of 15 million different digitized objects by 2015. i agree that special attention should be paid to works which are in danger of disappearing in the near future, and among these, audiovisual material. it is also necessary to agree on ways of including copyrighted material so that current and recent works can be found.
in writing. − the creation of a digital library, museum and archive, covering europe's cultural heritage, from literary works to other material of cultural and scientific importance, could bring significant benefits in the fields of education, research and culture. in order to achieve the objective of benefiting the general public - by making the material available to everyone, not only in europe but also in the rest of the world - it is essential that europeana ensures free access to the material by the public, not forgetting the importance of making it available in formats and media that also ensure accessibility for people with disabilities. the resolution adopted contains, however, some aspects which are less clear and others which are not sufficiently developed. it is not clear how and by whom the cultural and scientific content of europeana will be defined, how it will be managed - important questions to assess to what extent it will ensure effective representation of the diversity of europe's cultural heritage. there are still doubts about how the public-private partnerships proposed in the report will work, and about the overall funding of the cultural institutions associated with europeana. we believe that cultural and scientific goods are universal goods, should be freely accessible to the whole population, and should not be treated as tradable goods.
in writing. − the dissemination of europe's cultural heritage benefits various sectors, including education, science, research, tourism, and others. however, there is a major deficiency in the dissemination of cultural heritage and a large discrepancy between member states in the digitisation of their cultural heritage so that it is easily accessible. a common effort is needed to rapidly adopt new technologies that will allow the rapid compilation of all european cultural heritage in high-quality digital format, so that it can be disseminated worldwide, thereby helping other peoples to have access to europe's cultural wealth.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it calls on the european commission to evaluate the implementation of the current animal welfare action plan (2006-2010) and to draw up a new action plan for 2011-2015. the report also calls for a tighter control system and more effective penalties for owners of animals who do not comply with the welfare requirements laid down by law, for european farmers to be compensated for the additional production costs associated with higher welfare standards, and for the financing of these measures to be incorporated into the new cap aid schemes from 2013. the next action plan should focus on: general european legislation on animal protection, a european centre for the protection and welfare of animals, better control of the applicable legislation, the relationship between animal and public health and new technologies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the analysis and evaluation of the community action plan on animal welfare 2006-2010, which proposes to introduce a tighter control system and more effective sanctions for animal owners who do not comply with the welfare requirements laid down by law. it is essential to ensure that european farmers are compensated for the higher production costs associated with higher animal welfare standards in the new cap schemes.
in writing. - i agree with the epp shadow rapporteur elisabeth jeggle that a more coherent approach to animal welfare protection is needed, but that does not mean that more laws and regulations are needed. i can also say, without diminishing the importance of the protection of animal welfare, that too much regulation and too many rules to be followed can ultimately lead to harmful effects on the market. it should not be forgotten that the more standards there are, the more difficult it is for producers to comply with them and the less competitive european livestock farming becomes. in addition, excessive protection of animals must not lead to the neglect of other equally important values which must be preserved, such as economic competitiveness, the sustainability of agriculture and livestock farming and also some national traditions. on the other hand, however, human health must be protected against diseases transmitted by animals (whether wild, pet or used for human food), and for this scientific research must give us the indications for better regulation and protection of public health.
in writing. − a high level of animal welfare from rearing to slaughter promotes the safety and quality of products. european standards are among the most advanced in the world. however, european producers must not be put at a disadvantage on the european market by complying with these standards. in fact, these rules bring operating costs and financial and administrative burdens to eu farmers. in order to ensure fair competition, there must be reciprocity of standards with non-community producers. european farmers should therefore be compensated for the production costs associated with higher animal welfare standards. the financing of these compensations should be included in the new aid schemes of the common agricultural policy from 2013. it should be noted that european animal welfare policy must be accompanied by a coherent trade policy. it is noted that animal welfare issues were not addressed in the july 2004 framework agreement or in any other key wto doha round documents. therefore, no further animal welfare standards should be introduced which have negative effects on the competitiveness of producers as long as wto trading partners do not subscribe to these standards.
in writing. − the report adopted contains important positive aspects, such as: the need to regulate imports and ensure that all animals and meat imported from third countries meet the same welfare requirements as those applicable in the eu; the need to adequately cover the additional costs generated by promoting animal welfare; the recognition of the limited investment capacities of many small and medium-sized producers, hampered by an unfair functioning of the food supply chain; and the advocacy of incentives to breed, market and slaughter animals at regional level in order to avoid long-distance transport of animals, both from breeding and for slaughter. unfortunately, the report fails to recognise that the current cap promotes and favours intensive production models, often incompatible with animal welfare and health. it could and should have gone further, criticizing and rejecting the productivism of the present cap and advocating a different agricultural policy. it also makes proposals that are unrealistic and difficult to implement, such as the development of a satellite system for monitoring the transport of animals.
in writing. - we welcome the fact that europe has reached one of the highest levels in the world in this field. the creation of a tighter control system and more effective sanctions for owners of animals who do not comply with the welfare requirements laid down by law is essential, but as such measures imply additional costs for farmers, we are in favour of the compensatory aid provided for in this plan and which will be part of the new cap aid schemes from 2013. it should be noted that alongside this plan, the eu imposes strict and well-defined rules on other countries which do not comply with these rules and which therefore constitute unfair competition vis-à-vis eu farmers.
in writing. − the report voted on today objectively and critically assesses the results of the action plan for the protection of animal welfare 2006-2010 and sets out realistic and necessary priorities for growth, in the direction of progress, of food production and consumption in the european union. one point to be noted is the recognition that higher quality products imply higher costs for producers, especially primary producers, which do not usually translate into increased commercial demand, as only a minority of consumers will opt for more expensive products. the report thus emphasizes the need to compensate these same producers for the effort expended. the intention to impose on products from third countries the rules applicable to community products, ensuring fair and balanced commercial competitiveness, is also noteworthy. finally, i think it is important to support the idea of creating a european coordination centre and of adopting general and common legislation in order to harmonize good practice and establish control mechanisms.
in writing. − european agriculture contributes to the achievement of the union's climate change mitigation targets by 2020. ghg emissions have been declining as a result of more efficient eu agriculture, constant innovation and the use of new techniques such as soil storage of co2 and the development of sustainable renewable energy production. innovation therefore has an important role to play in reducing the impact of agriculture on climate change and in moderating its environmental consequences. i call for european money from the agricultural sector to be used to develop technologies for adapting the sector to combat climate change. the role of agriculture in the process of combating climate change must take into account the competitive position of the eu agri-food sector on the world market, and solutions must therefore be found to enable conventional agriculture to contribute to sustainable environmental management while protecting it from food speculation in the 'commodities' market and from international trade protectionism.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on eu agriculture and climate change because it presents concrete measures that can contribute to more sustainable agriculture. agriculture is one of the activities most affected by climate change, but it is also one of the most important contributors to co2 emissions. in the context of the future cap reform, the development of practices that allow european agriculture to better adapt to the consequences of climate change and, on the other hand, that can contribute to its mitigation should be encouraged.
in writing. - agriculture accounts for 9.3% of the european union's total co2 emissions, up from 11% in 1990. there has been a steady and progressive reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, with agriculture making a positive contribution to meeting the eu's emission reduction targets. i would also like to point out that although the environmental concerns in the agricultural sector are legitimate and necessary, they must be weighed against the impact of the proposals in terms of sustainability and agricultural productivity. the relationship between agriculture and environmental protection should therefore be carefully considered in the context of the reform of the cap, bearing in mind that, in addition to its negative impact on the environment (through, inter alia, co2 emissions), agriculture makes a decisive contribution to the conservation and management of natural resources, green growth and the management of the landscape and biodiversity. these are added values created by agriculture, which should be taken into account when it is proposed to study the relationship between agriculture and the environment.
in writing. − agriculture is directly involved in the issue of climate change as it contributes in part to the production of greenhouse gases while being affected by these changes. the negative impacts of these changes are already being felt, with drought and soil erosion being a major problem, especially in the southern member states. but agriculture can also contribute to combating climate change and has important potential for sustainable development. the cap should therefore encourage agricultural practices that limit emissions and/or improve carbon sequestration, as agriculture and forestry are the main economic sectors that are able to capture co2 from human activities by preserving and storing carbon in the soil. we need to move towards more sustainable agriculture, which requires greater efficiency, and we will have to increase world food production by 70 percent by 2050, according to fao, to cope with the increase in the world population. we will have to produce more but in a sustainable way, which requires greater efficiency, the adoption of the best techniques and practices and increased investment in scientific research in this area.
in writing. − consideration of the implications of climate change on agriculture is a relevant concern. the compatibility of agricultural activity with the preservation of a set of natural and cultural values such as soils, landscapes and biodiversity is also relevant, fully justified and necessary. however, these concerns should not make us forget that the main function of agriculture is food production, nor should they serve as a pretext for changes to the common agricultural policy which exacerbate the worrying and unacceptable food dependence of several countries, the eu - as is the case with portugal - and not only, threatening the food sovereignty and security of the peoples, in the name of an allegedly untouchable 'competitive position of the eu agri-food sector on the world market'. it would be important if this report devoted a few lines, if any, to the need to break with the productivist model which has shaped successive reforms of the cap and its disastrous social and environmental consequences. unfortunately, not a word about this. it would have been equally important to avoid any ambiguity at a time when we are faced with attempts by the european commission to impose the interests of multinational agribusiness companies on the spread of gmos.
in writing. - adaptation to climate change is becoming a reality that everyone will have to see as a priority in eu policy. the phenomenon of climate change is damaging agriculture, which according to recent reports points to a very unpromising scenario for this sector. it seems that the countries of southern europe will be the most affected by climate change. it is essential that the cap, through such changes, acts accordingly, encouraging better management of resources. optimising water resources, selecting varieties selected for their resistance to climate change and disease, protecting soils from erosion, preserving pastures, increasing reforestation, restoring degraded areas, improving forest management to limit fire risks and new disease surveillance and control measures are all very important measures to adapt european agriculture to the effects of warming. agriculture will increasingly depend on the state of the climate, and we therefore approve all measures to mitigate this serious problem.
in writing. − support for less-favoured rural areas is an essential element of the second pillar of the common agricultural policy (rural development policy), and it is natural that territories with natural or other handicaps should be the subject of specific instruments and policies. the commission proposes in this communication that, in accordance with article 50 (3) of regulation (ec) no 1698/2005, 'other less-favoured areas' be defined in accordance with objective criteria, proposing eight soil and climate criteria which, starting from a certain threshold value, indicate the existence of severe constraints for european agriculture: climatic criteria (long periods of low temperatures or heat), biophysical criteria (soils with poor drainage, stony, sandy or clay soils; shallow root depth; salt soils) and geographical criteria (areas with an unfavourable water balance or a high slope of the ground). this definition of objective criteria is positive, but these must be tested in the field to verify their reliability and adaptability to the specific cases and characteristics of each natural area. the possibility of a transitional period with a specific scheme for regions which lose their classification as less-favoured areas should also be considered.
in writing. − support for disadvantaged rural areas is an essential element of rural development policy. i am in favour of the allocation of adequate compensatory payments to less-favoured areas so that farmers can help to preserve the countryside and adopt sustainable agriculture that provides public goods such as landscapes, water and air quality, as well as the preservation of biodiversity. this support enables social and territorial cohesion by preserving rural areas and giving them a status of vital economic and natural area. the criteria for this report are 'other less-favoured areas affected by natural handicaps' under article 50 (3) (a) of regulation (ec) no 1698/2005. a committee of experts identified eight soil and climate criteria which, starting from a certain threshold value, indicate the existence of severe limitations for european agriculture. i agree that the geographical criterion, called 'isolation', must also be taken into account as it is a natural disadvantage. i hope that the member states will be able to apply objective biophysical criteria adapted to the conditions of their natural environment in order to designate areas with natural handicaps.
in writing. - it is positive that it is considered that zd payments should be linked to agricultural activity and that the application of solely biophysical criteria may not prove appropriate. we also value the inclusion of the geographical criterion isolation and cumulative use of the criteria adopted. however, these aspects are in contradiction with others included in the report, namely the definition of a 'transitional period' for adaptation to the new criteria, i.e. the tacit acceptance of the new criteria proposed by the commission. we strongly disagree with the idea that the new criteria should be reflected in the future development of the cap, as is also advocated there, by keeping this policy within the framework of rural development, with co-financing, that is to say, by maintaining another factor of discrimination between countries. the commission proposal, if implemented, will be highly detrimental to the interests of the southern countries, particularly portugal. we therefore stress the need to correct this proposal and to highlight and promote the use of socioeconomic criteria in conjunction with the group of biophysical criteria in the definition of the cap, such as gdp per capita, income per unit of family labour and desertification indicators.
in writing. − considering that more than half of the eu's agricultural area (54%) has the status of a lessfavoured area, either because of its orography, climatic conditions or less fertile land, and that such a measure is fundamental for rural development, we conclude that support for lessfavoured areas should be a priority for member states. in this way, the development of a global strategy for lessfavoured areas, adapted to the local needs of the different regions, will reduce the disparities between member states in the support they provide. the specific definition of areas with natural handicaps will thus enable adequate funds to be obtained for the exploitation of land and the improvement of agricultural production yields.
in writing. in this communication, the commission sought greater rigour and uniformity in the criteria for granting aid to farmers in areas with natural handicaps. the aim was to correct the heterogeneous application of compensatory allowances between member states due to differences in the classification of the so-called 'intermediate less-favoured areas'. such aid is crucial to preserve rural employment and communities, the continued use of agricultural land, as well as biodiversity and the cultural landscape. i am generally pleased with the report and especially with the opinion of the committee on regional development, which is trying to safeguard the interests of the outermost regions, since islands are excluded from the commission's communication. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, it seems logical that, in identifying the intermediate less-favoured areas, member states should be able to take account not only of biophysical criteria but also of other criteria such as insularity and the outermost regions. it is also important to me that regions which lose their status as 'naturally disadvantaged areas' should be given a transitional period to allow them to absorb the impact of the loss of aid. it is now up to us to ensure that, in the overall reform of the cap, the new aid schemes for farmers are designed in a coherent way and that there is better coordination between agricultural policy and cohesion policy.
in writing. - one of the areas which has developed most in recent decades has been information and communication technologies, which are present in all areas of human life. in an environment of constant change and increasing competitiveness, icts can be a powerful tool in helping to achieve sustainable development and combat poverty and social and economic inequalities. each person must be provided with the necessary skills and high-speed, permanent access, and a clear legal framework is needed to protect the rights and provide the necessary confidence and security. o the report 'on a new digital agenda for europe:2015.eu', which i voted for, intends to cooperate with the commission in the preparation of the overall strategic proposal and action plan for 2015. to this end: all eu households should have access to competitive broadband internet by 2013; pay particular attention to rural areas affected by industrial transition, which suffer from severe and permanent natural or demographic handicaps, in particular the outermost regions; finally, it stresses the importance of guaranteeing disabled end-users access at a level equivalent to that available to other end-users.
in writing. - i support the excellent report by mrs pilar del castillo on the new digital agenda. i agree that europe must play a leading role in the creation and application of icts, generating added value for its citizens and businesses, and that it will only reap the benefits of this digital revolution if all eu citizens are mobilised and equipped to participate fully in the new digital society. i welcome the aim of having broadband to cover all eu citizens and the whole of the territory, including the outermost regions. i welcome the recommendation that the concept of digital literacy be introduced into education systems from preprimary education onwards, alongside foreign languages, with the aim of producing skilled users as early as possible. i stress the impact that the digitalisation of public services (e-government) can have for citizens and businesses to enable a more efficient and personalised delivery of public services; furthermore, significant gains in transparency and competition can be made through e-procurement systems (public procurement) with more supply, higher quality and lower prices.
in writing. - a 'digital agenda' is becoming increasingly important and more inescapable in our society. technological developments, especially in terms of the availability of information, content and knowledge on the net, have been extremely rapid and in just over a decade have dramatically changed the digital landscape with the massification of the internet and mobile communications. it is therefore important to look to the future and define a strategy for the digital agenda, setting concrete objectives, with particular attention to issues relating to consumer rights, privacy and personal data, as well as copyright and the fight against piracy on the internet.
in writing. − information and communication technologies (ict) contribute to a prosperous and competitive economy and help to achieve a more environmentally friendly, democratic, open and inclusive society. they enable efficiency by helping sustainable growth. in this way, icts contribute to the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. there are currently large disparities between and within member states in terms of the availability of broadband to citizens. it is urgent to build a digital single market for services in the eu that avoids regulatory fragmentation and contributes to the free movement of digital services and e-commerce . an ambitious digital agenda must therefore be adopted, accompanied by a comprehensive action plan providing economic, social and cultural opportunities for all european citizens, with special attention to rural areas. i stress the importance of providing all citizens with ubiquitous, high-speed access to fixed and mobile broadband. all eu citizens should have access to broadband internet at a competitive price by 2013 using national and european funds to do so.
in writing. - there are a number of positive aspects to this report, although it is developed within the framework of the internal market which the european union defends. we recognise the underlying benefits of a digital agenda for europe, as presented in the report, namely in ensuring 'access to cultural products for all citizens', in guaranteeing 'equivalent access for end-users with disabilities', in the availability of 'greater investment in the use of open source software in the eu' and in 'particular attention to rural areas, those affected by industrial transition and those suffering from severe and permanent natural or demographic disadvantages, in particular the outermost regions'. we have contributed to these proposals. however, we believe that a digital agenda of the vanguard rejects any commercialisation of knowledge, education and research. we therefore do not accept that the positive objectives should be disguised by the ambiguities and variations of the european single market. the 'strengthening', 'promotion' and 'good functioning' of the 'internal market' is no longer 'consumer-friendly' and 'results in lower prices' as it is being made to believe. the opposite has been proven on several occasions in the most diverse sectors of activity in the european union. that is why we abstained.
in writing. − a new digital agenda for europe is essential if there is to be a digital revolution from which all european citizens benefit. however, this requires the involvement of all citizens in the process, so that they become actors in the new digital society. but for this to be possible, a major investment effort is needed to close the digital divide that currently exists in the eu. we must not forget that informed and enlightened citizens contribute to increasing europe's potential.
in writing. - article 317 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the commission is responsible for the implementation of the community budget in cooperation with the member states and that the court of auditors is to send the european parliament and the council a statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. i think it is essential, in the interests of transparency, that the european parliament should have this capacity to audit the accounts and to be able to analyse in detail the implementation of the community budget. i support the rapporteur and the resolutions on discharge, when he draws attention to the urgency of introducing a national declaration, at an appropriate political level, covering all community funds under shared management, so that each member state takes responsibility for the management of the community funds received. this is all the more important since we know that 80% of community expenditure is managed by the member states. finally, i note the positive assessment of the accounts by the court of auditors, which gives european citizens the assurance that the community budget is being managed properly and rigorously, despite some problems that persist and which are analysed in detail in this report.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as can be seen from the audits that have been carried out, the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds available and are meeting the objectives set. it is in this sense that the vote in favour of the report by the commission and the implementing agencies is appropriate.
in writing. − i believe that accountability of public officials to citizens is fundamental, which is why they must give an account of how public funds have been used, in an objective and rigorous way. although the court of auditors considers that the revenue and commitments do not contain significant errors, it is nevertheless concerned about the high level of non-quantifiable errors affecting budget support commitments and the significant level of estimated error in payments. like the rapporteur, i also regret that the court of auditors was unable to obtain all the necessary information and documentation on 10 payments made to international organisations and consequently was unable to give an opinion on the regularity of expenditure amounting to eur 190 million, or 6.7% of annual expenditure. i therefore urge the edf to regularize all these issues in the next financial year (2009).

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for relations with latin america which advocates the full realisation of a bi-regional strategic partnership. i would like to stress the importance of the recommendation for the coordination of the positions of the two regional blocs in the negotiations on the united nations framework convention on environment and climate change.
in writing. - i share the rapporteur's view of the need to deepen and strengthen the bonds of bi-regional cooperation between the european union and latin america. i believe, however, that the union cannot fail to pay particular attention to one of the latin american countries whose population size, economic potential and regional leadership are already calling for it. i am, of course, talking about the largest portuguese-speaking country in the world: brazil. the european commission communication com (2007) 281 of 30 may explicitly recognised that the eu-brazil dialogue was not sufficiently exploited, being processed mainly within the framework of the eu-mercosur dialogue. brazil will be the last of the brics countries to meet the eu at a summit. the time has come to look to brazil as a strategic partner, a leading economic actor in latin america and a regional leader. while the other european institutions are doing their job, the european parliament is resisting the idea of leaving this great country to mercosur alone, with brazil being the only bric country with which the european parliament does not have an autonomous parliamentary delegation. an anachronistic and regrettable circumstance that needs to be corrected.
in writing. − the biregional strategic partnership contributes to further strengthening eu-latin america coordination in the international fora and institutions. in addition to the establishment of a proposed common agenda, coordination of positions on issues of global importance should be pursued, taking into account the interests and concerns of both sides. i therefore voted in favour of the commission communication 'the european union and latin america: a partnership between global players' which aims to identify and formulate operational proposals aimed at the full realisation of the bi-regional strategic partnership.
in writing. - this report does not take account of the real problems facing latin america and does not set out the essential points which should be contained in the eu strategy for relations with latin america. for example, it ignores all the economic and social problems that will result from the signing of the free trade agreements, it accepts as an indisputable fact the normalization of relations with honduras, ignoring the coup d'état and the still recent murders of members of the resistance front against the coup. it ignores the situation in colombia, the crimes of the paramilitaries, the persecution of trade unionists and politicians, which are not a problem worth mentioning. on the other hand, it criticises, although it never explicitly mentions, bolivia and venezuela. but it says nothing about the reactivation of the us fourth fleet in the region, the us plan to use seven colombian military bases, or the interference operations carried out from military bases in the territories of eu and nato countries. unfortunately, they rejected most of the proposals we made on the above-mentioned subjects, and so in the end we voted against the resolution.
in writing. - as the eu is the largest investor and second largest trading partner in latin america, and also the largest provider of development aid, we believe that this data is sufficient to have a clear and well-defined strategy for eu-latin america relations. we call for clear guidelines on how best to work together to promote political stability, combat climate change, manage migration flows and prevent natural disasters. as we witnessed in the haitian tragedy, the eu was clearly put in the background in relation to other actors. that is why we argue that the eu should correct its international behaviour. it should therefore intervene more consistently and effectively in international politics. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. − the european union and latin america have developed a strong strategic partnership over the years. the union is the largest investor in latin america, its second largest trading partner and its largest provider of development aid. the ultimate objective is to create a euro-latin american area of comprehensive interregional partnership by 2015 at political, economic, commercial, social and cultural levels, with a view to ensuring sustainable development in both regions. in this context, i would stress the importance of resuming negotiations on the eu-mercosur association agreement as a first step, which should be the most ambitious bi-regional agreement ever. i also welcome the initiatives for a trade partnership between the european union and central america and the andean community, as well as the deepening of the existing association agreements with mexico and chile. i regret, however, that such trade agreements may affect internal community production in these same sectors, especially in the outermost regions, which are experiencing permanent difficulties, and that adequate compensation has not been found at community level for these regions. i believe that a partnership between the two regions of the world, which will bring mutual benefits in the political, economic and social spheres, is essential and i therefore voted in favour of this document.
in writing. − for historical and cultural reasons, because of its ethnic and political affinities and because of the shared values and civilizational references, canada is a reliable and important partner of the european union. a comprehensive economic and trade agreement with canada can contribute positively to the deepening of the already excellent eu-canada relations. while obstacles to this relationship arise, particularly in the areas of fisheries, security and immigration, the truth is that, compared to other countries, the us-canada relationship is stable and fruitful for both partners. i hope that this relationship of trust will endure and that the north atlantic will continue to be peaceful and prosperous on both sides.
in writing. - i note that the partnership between canada and the european union is one of the oldest and closest, dating back to 1959, and that the current negotiations for a comprehensive economic and trade agreement aim to intensify relations between the eu and canada. i would point out that in 2010 canada holds the presidency of the g8 group of countries and will host the next g20 summit. i therefore welcome the commission's statement that progress in negotiations on a comprehensive economic and trade agreement is a key factor in economic relations between the eu and canada. in this context, i believe that the eu-canada summit of 5 may 2010 in brussels creates a good opportunity to move these negotiations forward. i particularly welcome the intention to carry out a major reform of canada's fisheries management system, which will also involve the northwest atlantic fisheries organisation (nafo).
in writing. - canada is a long-standing partner of the eu. it is therefore natural that over the years this relationship has been deepened and improved. the european union is also committed to the development of a comprehensive and effective system of customs and trade facilitation. there are also other relevant issues that link the eu and canada, such as community aid, particularly to haiti, fisheries issues, and environmental concerns. we must not forget that the treaty of lisbon has given the european parliament new responsibilities in the negotiation of international agreements and that it must be involved at all stages of the negotiations.
in writing. - i voted against the interim agreement between the eu and the us on the transfer of european citizens' financial data, not only because it was manifestly wrong, calling into question the principles of necessity and proportionality and the integrity and security of european financial data, but also because it denied the ep the possibility of exercising its prerogatives properly. i believe that there is a need to strengthen transatlantic cooperation in all relevant areas, particularly in the area of freedom, security and justice. but this can only happen if there is absolute respect for fundamental principles such as proportionality, necessity and reciprocity. in this new chapter, i cannot but congratulate both the commission and the council on their new approach to cooperation with the ep. i hope that together we will be able to establish the basic principles which should guide and facilitate future cooperation between the eu and the us in the fight against terrorism. i look forward to the conclusions of the ep delegation's visit to washington, and hope that we can also see a 'turning of the page' here.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that any agreement between the eu and the us in this area should also include strict enforcement and monitoring guarantees, by a competent authority designated by the eu for this purpose. only in this way can it be ensured that these data transfers do not constitute a departure from the principles which guide eu law and practice.
in writing. − international judicial cooperation and transatlantic cooperation are essential in the fight against terrorism. the long-term agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the prevention of the financing of terrorism is therefore welcome. such an agreement, however, must not jeopardise the privacy of transactions by natural and legal persons. the european legal requirements for the fair, necessary, proportionate and lawful processing of personal data are therefore of paramount importance and should therefore continue to apply in all circumstances. the eu should establish the basic principles governing the modalities of general cooperation with the us to combat terrorism and the mechanisms for reporting information on suspicious or irregular transactions by its citizens. an eu-us judicial cooperation agreement on the prevention of terrorist financing should be concluded, ensuring that the transfer of personal data respects the rights and freedoms of european citizens and businesses and protects their security without unnecessarily compromising the privacy of their transactions.
in writing. − in accordance with the eu-us interim agreement, i subscribed to the need for transatlantic cooperation in the fight against international crime and terrorism. i stressed that this cooperation must be based on mutual loyalty and respect for the principles of reciprocity, proportionality and respect for the rights of citizens. but security cannot be superimposed on other rights, freedoms and guarantees. it is not acceptable that the police in portugal can only access the banking data of one person with a court warrant while millions of data can be sent to be known and analysed by the american police without judicial control. that's why i voted against the interim agreement. the new motion for a resolution under consideration, however, demonstrates a new approach by the commission and the council in terms of cooperation with the ep. i hope that future cooperation between the eu and the us in the fight against terrorism will be based on respect for the principles of proportionality, necessity and reciprocity.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism, and for the eu to take action to combat terrorism. many experts have stated that the protection of rights, freedoms and guarantees is not guaranteed under such an agreement. the so-called swift agreement and the framework agreement on data protection and sharing, rather than being a security guarantee, constitute a threat. within eu-us relations there is a different understanding of data protection, competences, legislation and privacy. these matters need to be clarified before the commission is given a new mandate. but the majority of the ep has given the commission a blank check, through ambiguous limitations such as 'proportionality' or 'reciprocity', opening a real pandora's box against freedom and promoting the subtraction of functions from the states, such as the decision on the transfer of data of their citizens, which is attributed to a european 'judicial public authority'. there is no possible 'proportionality' or 'reciprocity' on the mass storage and transfer of data, as it involves a set of uncontrollable dangers, namely on who accesses it, the use and the purpose.
in writing. - the fight against terrorism is a concern of the eu as well as of the whole democratic world. all the mechanisms that help to detect possible attacks are paramount to the success of this fight. the swift agreement is a very powerful instrument in the fight against terrorism, as it allows access to inside financial information regarding transfers of funds between countries. the renegotiation of this agreement with the us is a unique opportunity for the eu to contribute effectively to the detection of new terrorists and potential attacks. there is now a great desire on the part of the united states to cooperate, which is what makes for an agreement which effectively protects the data transmitted and where there is the greatest possible reciprocity.
in writing. - the fight against terrorism and its financing is an unavoidable reality and deserves our utmost attention, which is why transatlantic cooperation is imperative. the previous attempt at an agreement between the european union and the united states of america on data processing and transfer lacked proportionality, reciprocity and transparency. the resolution calls for a common definition of 'terrorist activity' and a clarification of the concept of 'data not extracted', while reiterating the need to limit the exchange of information to the principle of necessity and to limit its use to the time strictly necessary for this purpose. a set of guarantees is now being proposed which are based on european legislative practice and which therefore offer citizens greater protection in the field of fundamental rights. the aim is not only to safeguard the principle of non-discrimination throughout the data processing process, but also to designate a european authority capable of receiving and supervising us requests. i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the basis has now been laid for the opening of negotiations to reach a balanced agreement between the european union and the united states.
in writing. − the need to reach a balanced agreement with the us on the transfer of pnr data has been a constant concern in recent years. the current state of negotiations does not yet reflect the existence of any real legal protection of data in the us, as such data can be retained for years after security checks have been carried out and there is no legal protection for non-us citizens. the agreements concluded with both australia and canada are more acceptable, since the principle of proportionality is better respected, with limited access in terms of scope, time and number of data, all subject to judicial control. only with a coherent approach and the establishment of general principles and rules for the use of pnr data can we break this deadlock and proceed to conclude any international agreements in this area, whether with these three countries or with the avalanche of similar requests that is coming. i support the joint motion to postpone the vote on parliament's consent, hoping that with a little more time the negotiations can meet the concerns that the ep has always expressed.
in writing. - the debate on the transmission of passengers' personal data by airlines on transatlantic flights has been a major embarrassment in the european union's relations with the united states, australia and canada and is one of the dilemmas of our time. on the one hand, there is no doubt that the particular need to protect the privacy, intimacy and data of each citizen is a matter of great importance. on the other hand, few would deny that we are living in a time when threats to people's security require not only better information exchange between law enforcement authorities in the fight against crime, but also proper handling of that information in order to make them better able to combat organised crime and, in particular, terrorism. i hope that the pause in the procedure imposed by the european parliament will allow a fair balance to be struck between these values.
in writing. - the current state of negotiations on data transfer does not yet ensure effective legal protection of data in the us, as such data can be retained for years after security checks have been carried out and there is no legal protection for non-us citizens. i therefore support the joint proposal to postpone the vote on parliament's consent, hoping that with a little more time the negotiations can meet the concerns that the ep has expressed in this area.
in writing. the passenger name record (pnr) is another instrument in the fight against terrorism. the european parliament, under the lisbon treaty, is once again called upon to take part in the negotiations for a new pnr agreement between the eu, the us, australia and canada. the eu, as a strong supporter of the fight against terrorism and transnational and organised crime, is willing to negotiate agreements that are effective in this fight, while safeguarding and protecting civil liberties and fundamental rights.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which proposes a general ban on the use of mining technologies in the eu that use cyanide until the end of 2011, as i believe that the proposed ban is at this moment the only reliable way to protect our water resources and ecosystems from pollution caused by cyanide used in mining. i would stress the need to oblige companies operating mining installations to take out insurance to cover the compensation for any damage and the costs incurred in repairing and restoring the original ecological and chemical state in the event of an accident or malfunction.

in writing. - the increase in the total number of meps from 736 to 751 was approved, with 18 additional seats distributed among 12 member states. germany would lose three seats, due to the maximum threshold set by the eu treaty. the treaty of lisbon did not enter into force before the 2009 european elections, and the provisions of the treaty of nice therefore apply, so that the european parliament now has 736 meps instead of 751. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament. it is not possible to suspend the mandate of a member during the parliamentary term and therefore the number of members of the german delegation cannot be reduced by three. i therefore believe that the amendment to protocol no 36 requested by the european council is a direct consequence of the new provisions of the treaty of lisbon and constitutes a valid solution which will allow the member states with additional seats to appoint their own members. these 18 members must be sworn in simultaneously so as not to distort national representativeness.
