in writing. − the eu must maintain its leadership and ambition in the fight against climate change. in this area, scientific study is essential both for combating and adapting to climate change so that we can take the right and safe path. the issue of adaptation is cross-cutting across a number of sectoral policies. there must therefore be greater political coordination in these areas by the member states. i am in favour of the obligation to have national adaptation plans based on a common european framework. in areas such as water, energy and forests, i believe we should have common european policies. i would like to reiterate the need for a european hazard map for the coastline. the risks posed by climate change to the most vulnerable regions of europe need to be addressed urgently. i also believe that there should be european targets for the efficiency of public water supply systems. i would also stress that natural ecosystems are the most important carbon sinks on earth, sequestering 50% of the world's annual greenhouse gas emissions and contributing to mitigation and adaptation.

in writing. − the 2008 annual report on the protection of the community's financial interests shows that the financial impact of irregularities as far as they were identified decreased from eur 1024 million to eur 783.2 million in 2008, with reductions in all spending sectors except direct expenditure and pre-accession funds. i would particularly stress the need to introduce information on irregularities which clarifies the proportion of the total resources that have been affected by errors and cases of suspected fraud. the fight against fraud and corruption is an important obligation of the european institutions and of all member states, which must provide all the resources necessary to combat these phenomena effectively, with a view to protecting the financial interests of the union and its taxpayers.
in writing. - in this time of economic and financial crisis, not a single euro in the eu budget can be wasted, let alone if it was caused by fraud, which leads to the improper payment of eu funds. over the years we have seen the amounts of irregularities decrease significantly. however, we can only be satisfied when these amounts are marginal or close to zero. the eu must adopt budgetary control mechanisms that are effective in preventing and detecting fraud in a timely manner so that funds are only made available when it is actually a question of the correct use of funds. this is without prejudice to any effective sanction against those who, by not complying with the rules, seek to misappropriate common resources which are scarce in nature.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by recalling that this parliament has already criticised the enormous delays in the development of the sis ii project. on 22 october 2009, we adopted a resolution on the schengen ii information system and the visa information system. parliament reiterated its deep concern at the delays in the start of operations and asked the commission and the council to provide information on the results of the technical tests, calling for full transparency in the sis ii implementation process. sis ii was supposed to have started operations in 2007. it's 2010 and no one can guarantee when it will be completed. the package of proposals we are considering raises four fundamental questions. first, when should this migration take place? before sis ii can become operational, it should be personally tested in order to assess whether the system is able to function in accordance with the technical and functional requirements laid down in the respective legal instruments. only after successful completion of all tests will it be possible to migrate from sis i to sis ii. are the tests complete? question number two. no, in view of the enormous delay in the project and all the problems and difficulties encountered, the council decided to carry out two 'milestones' tests. the first in the fourth quarter of 2009 and the second in the summer of 2010. however, the first test had to be postponed until the end of january as the necessary requirements had not been met. the test took place between 21 and 24 january 2010. apparently the system worked for the first 25 hours, but for the rest of the test, the system was markedly unstable. this test was again carried out between 2 and 5 march. the final evaluation and validation of the repeat tests took place on 6 april. although the conditions of the tests were not fully met by either the member states or the contractor and although the limited number of transfers did not meet the required response times, the vast majority of member states concluded that these were insignificant deviations and that the broad objectives of the tests had been achieved. the new overall timetable and budgetary plan are expected to be adopted by the next council in june or by october 2010 at the latest. it was also considered essential that the following conditions be met before the system starts operations. the milestone ii test shall have been successfully conducted in full compliance with the conditions of operation. the overall test provided for in article 55 of the regulation must also have been successfully completed and the safety of the network must finally be fully guaranteed. thirdly, why is there such urgency in approving these initiatives? although the necessary conditions for migration are not met and there is no indication of when this will happen, the mandate given to the commission for the development of sis ii will once again expire on 30 june 2010. we therefore have to amend the expiry clauses of the migration instruments adopted in 2008 in order to avoid their expiry. fourth and final question. what aspects of the proposals have i tried to change? first, the existence of a time-bar. the commission had not proposed it. we propose that it be fixed at 31 december 2013. in addition, given the considerable delays, it is essential to establish in the legal basis that whatever technical solution is chosen, it must be based on the best available technology, respect a reasonable timetable and be acceptable in terms of cost-effectiveness. the creation of the global programme management board and its formal integration into its management of sis ii. i am deeply convinced that if this body had existed from the beginning, we would have been able to achieve better coordination, more knowledge and more efficiency. finally, i think it is essential that the migration process be subject to parliamentary scrutiny. parliament is not only responsible for the legal basis, but as budgetary authority it ensures the supervision of actions financed by the union budget. i therefore tabled an amendment with my colleague alexander alvaro to put the funds in reserve and with mr alexander alvaro, mrs sarah ludford, mr ioan encieu and mrs monika hohlmeir, a request for an audit to the european court of auditors. thank you all for your excellent cooperation.
the rapporteur. - ladies and gentlemen, there are refugees in the world who cannot return to their country because the situation is too unstable, or who cannot stay in a transit country because it has not signed the geneva conventions and cannot, for example, work in that country. the numbers are relatively limited: 200,000 a year, and some of these refugees, who have no other option but to be given the possibility of a new life in a third country, some of them have already had their problem solved through international actors who are resettling, the united states who are doing 80,000 a year, canada, australia, brazil and chile. what's missing from this painting? europe is missing. and in good time the council, under its swedish presidency, admitted that the numbers of refugees to be resettled in europe had to be greatly increased, going so far as to speak of the figure of 100 000 and in good time the commission revised some of the european refugee fund's statements to make possible a more vigorous and robust policy for the resettlement of refugees. i have two reports at the moment on behalf of the committee on civil liberties and human rights, one on codecision and one on own initiative. in the area of codecision we have, to correct the policies that are currently in place, four new features, two are of content, two are procedural. the first innovation is a dual approach. the commission proposal we are working on is mainly about regional priorities and then, within the regional priorities, what i would call humanitarian priorities. we thought it right to maintain these priorities, but to give them autonomy, that is to say, we think that europe should have intervention strategies in terms of the resettlement of refugees, which are very important from the point of view of foreign policy, which sometimes allow intervention in certain areas of the world, opening the doors of a certain country or establishing relations of trust in certain areas of the world, but at the same time giving member states the freedom to go to situations in the rest of the world which are priority in humanitarian terms. and what are those? victims of torture, or women and children who are victims of sexual violence, or people who need resettlement for serious health reasons, for example. secondly, the modulation. this is to go from the 10 member states which are currently resettling at european level to the 27 member states which are trying to do so. to this end, we have proposed that the amount to be allocated per refugee to the new member states be increased in the first year, slightly reduced in the second year and equal to all other member states making resettlement from the third year onwards, on the condition that this increased amount in the first years - which are the years when it costs the most to set up the new resettlement programme - be used for the development of a sustainable resettlement programme. the other two new features are procedural: the commission has a very good idea of what it is doing, and i think it is important that we should be able to do that, because it is a very important matter, and i think that the commission has a very good idea of what it is doing, because it is a very important matter, and i think that the commission has a very good idea of what it is doing. what we cannot accept is that the commission, as guardian of the treaties, tells us that delegated acts to which it has no legal objection should not be adopted in the framework of this important foreign and humanitarian policy decision, just because it seems to them that they are bureaucratic when we say that they are not. the fact is that this decision is part of our view and the view of the legal service of delegated acts and therefore as such we believe that it is incumbent on the commission to defend the adoption of delegated acts here as guardian of the treaties and not to raise objections to them which are at this moment merely procedural, and above all we believe that none of these issues should prevent us from reaching what is our common objective, which is to resettle more refugees in the european union.

the rapporteur. - madam president, i thank the members who took part in this debate, and i thank the commissioner. i think that if there is some convergence of will here on the issue of resettling refugees, it's because we understand that we have, which is rare, in the immigration debate -- which we all know how difficult it is in europe -- and in the asylum and refugee debate, we have a problem that we can solve. we can do it for ourselves and we can do it for the refugees, because anyone who has visited refugee camps and knows that there are children who are losing a year and another year and another year of study that they could be doing in europe, i think gives us the right dimension of the urgency of this debate. and i also hope that the procedural issues will be quickly overcome, in accordance with what is written in the treaties, because we all know that what we have is not enough and we all know that a budget line alone is not yet a real refugee resettlement programme. this is the kind of subject we are dealing with in the owninitiative report which we are also discussing here today and which has to do with quality - on behalf of the epp group. the outermost regions, because of their permanent natural handicaps, lack a specific approach from the european union to the best conditions for the development of their socioeconomic activities. when it comes to regions heavily dependent on agriculture, as is the case with the azores, particular attention is required in this sector. it is in this context that we welcome the present report on specific measures for agriculture in the outermost regions, which is quite satisfactory in the version voted by the committee on agriculture and rural development and now, after the trilogue, inexorably penalizes the working conditions of the sugar industry, whose export permitting touches the merely symbolic. at a time when diversification of agriculture is gaining expression as one of the ways of minimizing recurrent crises in the sector, i regret that this report does not express the confidence and encouragement that sugar beet production and the associated industry in são miguel lacked.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this suppression, against which we have fought and will continue to fight, supporting the struggle of the dairy farmers, will have very serious consequences for a key productive sector of the azores economy. consequences which the measures now proposed for the sugar processing industry are unlikely to mitigate, contrary to what is suggested, all the more so when it is already proposed that they should also be phased out. after these five years, what will be left? it is also important to take into account that the process of converting vineyards is significantly delayed, particularly in the case of madeira, and may even be compromised if incentives are not strengthened. the constraints and constraints affecting the outermost regions are permanent. in this respect, recognition of the specific nature of these regions must be translated into a set of permanent support measures rather than into a set of casual and time-limited questions. in the present socioeconomic context, it is quite right that community support for the agricultural sector in favour of the outermost regions should be maintained and strengthened.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. in this last speech i would like to stress the importance of updating regulation (ec) no 247/2006. however, the developments since its adoption in 2006, both in the legislative field and in the field of its application, as well as in the development of the actual situation, have made it necessary to introduce amendments in order to ensure that, in an up-to-date form, it continues to be an important instrument for adapting certain community policies in the agricultural field to the specificities of the outermost regions, as provided for in articles 349 and 107 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. let me briefly list the improvements achieved: in the canary islands, milk-based preparations considered as traditional products for local consumption are no longer subject to a time limit; the commission has also decided to extend the scope of the directive to include the processing of milk powder. in madeira, this same exception is renewed in these new forms and wine produced from hybrid varieties of direct producers can be consumed in the region. the azores will see the sugar re-dispatching derogation reintroduced and extended, both in quantity and in time, and will also benefit from the aforementioned provisions for wood in wine. these measures, which apply retroactively from 1 january 2010 and do not impede free competition in our single market, make a major contribution to the economies of these regions, whose natural fragility makes them even more vulnerable in a time of deep crisis. finally, i should like to say that with the adoption of this report, and in addition to the opportunity given to agricultural diversification, the possibilities of re-dispatching that were forbidden have been restored. it is also important to remember that, thanks to its adoption, we will be able, in a period of very severe economic crisis, to make a decisive contribution to restructuring and maintaining in the azores not only several dozen jobs but also the technical know-how linked to the activity of the agro-industrial sugar industry.

in writing. - this proposal is part of the union's legislative efforts to create a european asylum system. this european support office should thus provide specialised assistance to the member states and contribute to the implementation of a coherent and high-quality common european asylum policy. the creation of this new office will undoubtedly add value to the strengthening of mutual trust and the sharing of responsibilities between the member states. it should facilitate the exchange of information, analysis and experience between them, organise training and develop practical cooperation between the administrations responsible for examining asylum applications. it is important to address the significant differences in the decision-making process of the 27 member states with regard to applications for international protection and to achieve a degree of convergence in the way member states analyse and respond to such applications. i support the rapporteur's proposal to include the provision of resettlement support. i agree that the financing of this new agency in its early stages should be ensured by the necessary budgetary changes to the european refugee fund.
in writing. - the issues surrounding immigration and, in particular, the right of asylum are particularly sensitive. the granting or not of this right to non-eu citizens can have dramatic implications for their lives and therefore requires seriousness, attention and particular humanity. i think it is common sense that neither an open door policy, without any criteria restricting access to the union's space, is acceptable, nor is a policy of absolute entry bans tolerable. a fair balance is needed which seeks to reconcile the legitimate interests and concerns of nationals of the member states with the needs of those who seek them. in this regard, the establishment of a european asylum support office can be an important step towards the adoption of best practices, the strengthening of trust between states and the consequent improvement in the exchange of information. however, i cannot help stressing that the member states must continue to have a margin of discretion as to whether or not they will accept those who wish to enter their borders, and that the eu must not hide the fact that the member states do not have absolutely convergent interests in this matter.
in writing. − the european asylum support office aims to provide specialist assistance contributing to the implementation of a coherent and high-quality common european asylum policy. this office will develop mutual trust and responsibility-sharing and will be responsible for coordinating the exchange of information and other resettlement actions developed by the member states. as a promoter of the values of human dignity, which are fundamental elements of freedom, democracy and socioeconomic development, the european union must, in the context of the current world situation, also take a pioneering and exemplary approach to asylum. the creation of a european office to support the member states in this area of intervention with third country nationals will be crucial for the implementation of a common european asylum policy, reinforcing the co-responsibility and solidarity of the member states in a coherent action and in accordance with the values and principles of the european construction project. i call for the necessary mechanisms and resources to be provided quickly for the establishment of the support office.
in writing. − in such a sensitive area of human rights, the creation of a european asylum support office is important because it allows for specialised assistance at eu level to help define a coherent and high-quality common european asylum policy. hence my vote.
in writing. − the construction sector accounts for 40% of energy consumption and 35% of emissions in the eu. this legislation provides that by 2020 new buildings must have a near-zero energy consumption and that existing renovated buildings must meet minimum energy performance requirements. this legislation will thus contribute to reducing europe's energy dependence, to reducing co2 emissions, to improving indoor and outdoor air quality and to increasing well-being in cities. encouraging better energy performance in buildings is also an opportunity to re-skill our cities, contributing to tourism, job creation and sustainable economic growth in the eu. however, the requalification requires increased public and private investment. we are dealing with local public investment with a direct effect on job creation and the involvement of smes, a programme for the requalification of cities will be a suitable programme for the relaunch of the economy. i therefore call on the commission and the member states to use the structural funds to requalify buildings for environmental and energy purposes, to act as a catalyst for private finance and to work together to find the right financing model for the refurbishment of existing buildings.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation on the energy performance of buildings because it presents ambitious and feasible proposals for a 20% reduction in energy consumption and co2 emissions in sectors not covered by the emissions trading system by 2020. this directive will have a direct impact on the lives of european citizens, as it will help consumers to reduce their energy costs and, at the same time, can contribute to the creation of millions of jobs across the eu through planned investments in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy.
in writing. − in 2008, europe committed itself to achieving a 20% reduction in energy consumption by 2020 at the latest and to ensuring that 20% of its energy consumption comes from renewable sources. improving the energy efficiency of buildings is the most effective way to reduce energy consumption and emissions by 20% in sectors not covered by the emissions trading system. in addition, efficient buildings provide an average energy saving of 30% compared to conventional buildings. on 13 november 2008, the commission presented its proposal to amend directive 2002/91/ec on the energy performance of buildings. these changes will have significant impacts on the lives of european citizens, as they will have immediate consequences on the buildings in which they live and will create the need for research and development of more efficient technologies in the construction sector. in addition, this strategy will create jobs and contribute to sustainable growth. as the current wording is based on the agreement reached between the european parliament and the council in november 2009, i support the rapporteur's proposal.
in writing. − the adoption of this directive on the energy performance of buildings is an important step towards reducing co2 emissions and europe's energy dependence. they are increasingly decisive for the quality of life of european citizens and for the competitiveness of our economy and our social organisation. considering that the construction sector accounts for 40% of energy consumption and 35% of total co2 emissions, energy self-sufficiency of new buildings and improvement of the energy performance of renovated buildings are of decisive importance for the european union to achieve its 2020 target of a 20% reduction in energy consumption and a 20% increase in the use of renewable energy sources and energy efficiency. in addition to helping private consumers and public services to reduce energy costs, the implementation of this new legislation is expected to help combat the crisis in the construction sector and contribute to the development of urban redevelopment policies, which will have a positive impact on the improvement of the quality of life and well-being of citizens.
in writing. − improving the energy performance of buildings is of particular importance in increasing overall energy efficiency in the eu and reducing ghg emissions. if the european union is to meet its proposed targets of reducing energy consumption by 20%, ensuring that 20% of energy consumption comes from renewable sources and increasing energy efficiency by 20% by 2020, it will have to invest heavily in the best energy performance of buildings. the political agreement reached between parliament and the council results in clarification of technical aspects, minimum requirements for energy performance according to the age of the building with or without renovation, enhancing the role of local and regional authorities and supporting public authorities in implementing recommendations. but we still have some concerns about the commission's increased role in the evaluation of national inspection plans and reports, and the adaptations to the lisbon treaty which centralize more power in the commission through so-called delegated acts.
in writing. − the issue of energy efficiency is a key issue in the context of the 'strategy 2020'. this approval is a very important step towards reducing energy consumption over the next few years, towards nearly zero energy buildings by 2020. efforts must be made not only when new buildings are constructed but also when major renovations are made to existing buildings. it will also be decisive that a good example can be set in public building. hence my vote.
in writing. - only through a common asylum policy and a joint resettlement programme can we pursue a genuine human rights policy in the eu. resettlement is undoubtedly one of the lasting solutions for refugees whose protection cannot be guaranteed in the countries of first asylum. it is important that adequate funds are made available, although a single budget line cannot be considered a genuine resettlement policy. i have no doubt that this amendment to the refugee fund will be important, as it will help to fill a gap that exists in several member states and improve their reception capacity. i am pleased to see that the number of member states participating in this programme has increased in recent years and it is important that we can encourage the others to participate. this resettlement instrument must be further developed and extended by the eu in order to provide the most effective protection possible. the commission will thus have the capacity to set common eu priorities for resettlement on an annual basis, which may be based on specific geographical regions, nationalities or categories of refugees to be hosted, although it agrees that flexibility should be guaranteed to respond to emergency situations.
in writing. − the need to resettle refugees is becoming increasingly important in a europe that does not want to be closed to the outside world or blind to what is happening outside it. the capacity to welcome and to show solidarity with those who suffer the most are two european characteristics of christian inspiration which should be fully restored, without however neglecting the legitimate limits defined by the member states. indeed, the eu's common annual priorities in terms of geographical regions, but also of specific categories of refugees to be hosted, cannot fail to take account of the needs of states and their particular circumstances and their participation in resettlement actions should be encouraged.
in writing. − one of the 'actions eligible' for the european refugee fund (erf) is resettlement. the stockholm programme advocates that the eu should act in partnership and cooperate with third countries that receive large numbers of refugees. the european commission shall annually define common eu priorities for persons to be resettled, and this definition should allow for sufficient flexibility to respond to emergency situations. attention should be paid in particular to the victims of the most repressive and discriminatory cultural, social and political systems. the number of member states participating in eu resettlement programmes has been growing continuously and should be extended to as many member states as possible. i stress the positive impact of the scale of financial amounts to be made available in resettlement support, with a higher amount in the first and second years of the process, in the face of the higher costs that naturally accompany the creation of mechanisms and structures, as well as the importance of ensuring conditions to ensure the best sustainability and quality of the refugee resettlement process.
in writing. - currently only 10 eu member states, including portugal, accept the resettlement of refugees. refugee resettlement is a procedure whereby member states take in third-country nationals or stateless persons who are transferred from a third country to an eu state, following a request from the unhcr, on the basis of the need for international protection of such persons. the aim of this approval is to increase the number of ms taking refugees on board. to this end, member states applying for the first time will receive an increase in the amount of financial assistance for the first two years. priority should be given to the resettlement of children and women at risk of violence or psychological, physical or sexual exploitation, unaccompanied minors, persons with special medical needs, survivors of violence and torture and persons in need of emergency resettlement for legal and protection reasons, irrespective of the geographical priorities that the eu has set for a given period.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the proposed amendments to this regulation. the data migration phase is the last task to be carried out under the sis ii development mandate. this justifies the need to give the european commission a valid mandate for the development of the system until it starts operations. in view of the considerable delays already experienced and the high costs associated with the sis ii project, i believe that the expiry clause should be maintained. the new mandate given to the commission should be defined in relation to the date foreseen for the start of operations of sis ii, which is the end of 2011. the commission should, however, be allowed some flexibility to extend the dates through the comitology process in order to adapt the legal framework to an alternative scenario in case sis ii is not successful. the commission's failure to set a likely date for the sis ii to become operational is unacceptable as it depends on it to guarantee greater security, freedom and justice in the european area and raises questions about the lack of transparency in the way the process has been managed.

in writing. − investing in youth policies is essential for the future of european societies, particularly at a time when the number of young people in the global population continues to decline. i was pleased to receive the 'european youth report' which for the first time collects data on the situation of young people in europe as well as the three priorities set by the commission for youth. creating more opportunities for young people in education and employment, increasing access to and encouraging young people's participation in society, and promoting social inclusion and solidarity among young people are key drivers of an effective european youth policy that can contribute to the development of a european mindset. however, the existence of different definitions of 'youth' in the different member states, together with the fact that youth policy is covered by the principle of subsidiarity, highlights the weaknesses in the effective implementation of youth policy instruments. to produce concrete results, a renewed european cooperation for youth requires, alongside the urgent need to strengthen the open method of coordination, a strong will and a great political commitment on the part of the governments of the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'an eu strategy for youth: investing and mobilising'. the economic crisis is jeopardising, at least for the time being, the professional future of millions of young people across the european union, mainly because of the increased difficulties in entering the labour market. to avoid the risk of wasting young people's talents, it is urgent to ensure that training measures ensure a better match between skills and labour market requirements, thus promoting the autonomy and economic independence of young people.
in writing. - at a time when europe is experiencing the biggest and most serious economic and financial crisis in recent decades, it is essential that the european union youth strategy now under discussion focuses on the problems brought about by the crisis and which particularly affect young people. among these, we highlight the high rate of unemployment among young people, the difficulty of entering the labour market, low wages, the inadequacy of the formal skills acquired in school and university to the requirements of working life, and the difficulty of reconciling the always demanding start of working life with family life. these are concerns that should be present in any european youth strategy. the aim should therefore be to find policies and strategies that enable young europeans to adapt better and more quickly to the challenges of the 21st century, especially in a context of crisis. i would particularly stress the importance of measures which give due weight to education, aimed at the acquisition of new skills and the stimulation of creativity and entrepreneurship. finally, i believe that in order to achieve the objectives proposed, it is necessary to strengthen coordination between the various actors involved in the implementation of the youth strategy.
in writing. − the focus on youth is on a good education system, which gives top priority to the problems of early school leaving and illiteracy, and which supports equal access for all young people to high quality education and training at all levels. the promotion of lifelong learning opportunities is also advocated. given the high unemployment rates among europe's young people and the fact that young people with low skills are more easily affected by unemployment, it is essential to ensure that young people receive the best possible training, which will enable them to gain early access to and long-term permanence in the labour market. the first job is very important. we therefore proposed an 'erasmus first employment' which was approved. the european commission is expected to follow up on this proposal. the eu should better inform, develop and implement the instruments it already has at its disposal. the young people must be called upon to take a greater part, in particular, in building the recycling society, in the fight against climate change which has already been achieved with the cooperation and generosity of young people.
in writing. - we believe that this report takes a correct approach to the problems of young people, as something that is cross-cutting across various sectors of society. in doing so, it identifies specific problems in a number of areas - education and training; employment; health; welfare and the environment; participation; culture and others - such as school drop-out, unemployment, job insecurity and precariousness, unpaid internships, brain drain, environmental degradation, drug addiction, social exclusion and others. the rapporteur has put forward some proposals to solve these problems which we think are fair and deserve our agreement, but there are others which we think are clearly insufficient, others which are still ambiguous and some which are even contradictory. we cannot accept, for example, that an eu2020 strategy 'more geared to young people' could mean adopting flexibility and job insecurity, or intermittent work - concepts present in the strategy - as a 'strategic' solution for young people, with the argument of competitiveness and a possible way out of the crisis. as in other areas, harmonization is required here too, in the interests of social progress and not by lowering the living and working conditions of young people. some countries, such as portugal, have constitutionally enshrined a wide range of youth rights, which should be enforced and not restricted.
in writing. − the eu youth strategy is becoming increasingly important and, given that young people now make up 20% of the total population, it should be seen as a political priority. the objectives are clear and defined and relate to such important areas as creating more employment opportunities or encouraging more active participation by young people in society. in the current context of financial and economic crisis, combined with the problem of ageing, young people are also one of the most vulnerable groups. i therefore support an increasing focus on youth policies at european union level. hence my vote.
in writing. - in view of the need to repeal directive 86/613/eec on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women engaged in an activity in a selfemployed capacity, this proposed amendment represents a significant step forward, as does the situation of the spouses of selfemployed persons. as regards social protection, it is proposed that where a social protection system for selfemployed persons exists in a member state, that member state should take the necessary measures to enable spouses to benefit from social protection in accordance with national law. although social protection for spouses is not compulsory, this proposal is an important step, as in many member states spouses still do not enjoy any form of social protection, either compulsory or voluntary. finally, this proposal provides for the protection of maternity. there is no provision for selfemployed women or the assistant spouses of selfemployed men to have the same period of maternity leave as that provided for employed women. however, they may be entitled to appropriate compensation to enable them to interrupt their activities for at least 14 weeks and/or to request temporary replacement service. for these reasons i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this directive which establishes a framework for the application in the member states of the principle of equal treatment between men and women engaged in an activity in a selfemployed capacity or contributing to the pursuit of such an activity. the low participation of women in self-employment constitutes an inequality, as family responsibilities appear to have a negative impact on women's entrepreneurship compared to men's. as regards the spouses who work together, the lack of social security coverage and the non-recognition of their contribution to the activity of family businesses gives some companies unfair competitive advantages, so this initiative would ensure a level playing field in europe. measures to close the gender gap in entrepreneurship and to improve work-life balance are essential. i call on the member states to ensure in practice full equality between men and women in working life, with a view to promoting entrepreneurship initiatives among women.
in writing. - the december 1986 directive has proved ineffective and has had very unsatisfactory practical results, according to its implementation reports. for this reason, it is urgent to strengthen maternity protection for selfemployed women and to ensure equal treatment for men and women in selfemployment, including their assisting spouses. in europe, 16% of the working population is selfemployed, of which only one third are women. this number is undoubtedly due to the numerous obstacles faced by women entrepreneurs, particularly in the area of reconciling their family and professional lives. however, if the 1986 directive did not achieve its objectives, the present proposal is also not very ambitious. i regret that in order to achieve a political compromise at council level, the potential of this directive has been reduced. it can, however, be seen as a first step towards improving the current situation with regard to social protection for selfemployed women and assisting spouses, with the creation of minimum rules and the recognition for the first time at union level of a right to maternity benefit allowing a break from work for a minimum of 14 weeks.
in writing. - as a firm supporter of the principle of equality, i could not call into question initiatives aimed at protecting women's rights at work, such as the present report by my dear colleague. as i have already said, "men and women must be treated equally, with equal rights but with special needs, which is particularly evident in the case of women in areas such as maternity protection and work-life balance". i am therefore pleased to see that the protection of the maternity rights of selfemployed women is one of the concerns raised here. however, as a staunch supporter of the principle of subsidiarity, i believe that many of the matters under consideration should remain within the sphere of the autonomy of the states.
in writing. - the efforts made by the european parliament to strengthen the mechanisms of social justice and gender equality in the european union are to be commended. in addition to being an unquestionable principle in the civilized world, and particularly in a europe which considers itself culturally and socially advanced, ensuring equal treatment for men and women in selfemployment, particularly in access to social protection mechanisms - particularly in the field of maternity - is even more urgent and flagrant in this long period of deep economic and social crisis. i would stress the concern for eliminating differences in treatment between sectors of activity, in view of the recognised changes in the organisation and in the equipment and mechanisms of work or production. there should be equal criteria for all workers in accessing public social protection schemes, in particular in regard to contributions and allowances. i would also point out that this recommendation will certainly strengthen the incentives for female entrepreneurship. the european economy still has much to gain and to develop with a stronger and more comprehensive participation of women.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to ensure equal treatment for men and women in self-employment. so, since the fundamental rights of equality and social protection are already safeguarded, and the proposed amendments to the original text are aimed at a general improvement in the protection of the spouses of selfemployed workers, in particular with regard to the maternity allowance granted to selfemployed women and to spouses or persons living in a de facto union, i see the adoption of this text as an important and very positive step towards approximation with the current european legislation for employed women. hence my vote.
in writing. - i welcome this proposal for a regulation which aims to simplify and improve the existing regulatory framework with a view to encouraging innovation in the textile and clothing sector, allowing fibre users and consumers to benefit more quickly from innovative products. the issue of simplification is key to fostering innovation in european industry and to increasing the level of information provided to consumers. it is also important to find a less burdensome legislative alternative with less onerous procedures and costs for transposing directives. the industry will benefit from the reduction in the time between the submission of an application and the ability to place the product on the market, resulting in savings in administrative costs and the possibility to market earlier, increasing the benefits of the sale.
in writing. − on 30 january 2009, the commission adopted a proposal for a new regulation on textile names and related product labelling. the proposal brings together all existing legislation on textile product names and labelling into a single regulation. the rapporteur said that the proposed revision was 'essentially a technical exercise with no major political implications'. however, we know that the competition to which european textiles are subject, especially with products from china, requires that more profound measures be taken in the future in the field of labelling. that should be the task of the commission from now on. the challenges facing the european union today also require the internal market to be improved and strengthened. to this end, efforts must be made to reduce the barriers to their full implementation. the harmonization and simplification of the rules on textile names meet this objective, since they clarify the information provided to the consumer and thus contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the sector.
in writing. − the correct identification of the place and manner of manufacture and of the essential characteristics of the product's composition is a fundamental prerogative to ensure consumer confidence and the protection of their rights, while introducing an important factor to promote fair competition in the global textile market. in this context, the standardisation of the methodology for the labelling of textile products will benefit the competitiveness of the european textile and clothing industry, and in particular of the portuguese industry. i stress the need for harmonised rules on the indication of the origin of textile products imported from third countries and precise criteria for the use of the 'made in' mark of origin for products manufactured in the eu, as well as social labelling so that the consumer is informed of the respect of health and safety standards and human rights. i also think that eco-labelling, which relates to the environmental performance of textile products, is important. the introduction of these more transparent and clearer rules on the labelling where information on non-textile and animal components is included will also make it possible to strengthen the consumer's ability to differentiate products and their quality.
in writing. we have voted in favour of this report, taking account of its general line, in defence of designation of origin and with concern for the protection of the rights of consumers, workers and the production of the textile and clothing industry in our countries. but we have some differences of opinion on the details of labelling, particularly on the content of fibres which is too detailed, especially where small and mediumsized enterprises are concerned, given the costs that this may entail. so, although we voted in favour of it in general, there are some detailed proposals with which we disagree and we insist on the need to revise them or at least to provide for support measures, taking account of the problems of small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. - the designation of origin of products is very important for consumers to have an accurate idea of the origin of what they consume. it is not correct to designate a product as eu originating when it is only packaged in an eu country and the other production steps are carried out in non-eu countries. the new rules adopted will contribute to greater transparency in international trade and better information for consumers. hence my vote.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the legislative resolution granting macrofinancial assistance to ukraine, as it will enable it to cope with the consequences of the global financial crisis through the sustainability of the budgetary situation and external accounts. this response to ukraine's request is essential for economic stabilisation, in conjunction with the current imf programme, but it is necessary that ukraine take appropriate measures to prevent and combat fraud, corruption and any other irregularities related to this assistance, and that provision is made for controls to be carried out by the commission and audits by the court of auditors. in this context, i refer to the memorandum of understanding and the loan agreement to be concluded with the ukrainian authorities which provide for the adoption of specific measures to be implemented by ukraine in the field of preventing and combating fraud, corruption and any other irregularities affecting assistance.
in writing. - i was pleased to vote in favour of parliament's proposal for macrofinancial assistance to ukraine. ukraine, as a potential candidate country for accession to the european union, is a privileged partner and should be the target of specific policies aimed at solving its concrete problems. but the european union's macrofinancial assistance to ukraine will only contribute to the economic stabilisation of the country if the serene political-party landscape and the political forces which have been too consumed over the past few years by internal power and influence guerrilla warfare establish a broad consensus on a scrupulous implementation of the structural reforms necessary for the country's future. it is also essential that the ukrainian government act to put an end to the lack of independence of the judiciary, which is subject to too much influence not only from political power but also from economic agents. without a free and independent judiciary there is no rule of law, there are no guarantees of human rights, there is no foreign investment, there is no progress. the mechanisms which the loan agreement will define should take account of these factors in order to allow a strict control of their applicability by the community institutions.
in writing. - the recent news of violence between ukrainian parliamentarians has worried the whole of europe and clearly reflected the split in that society, the crossroads it is at today and russia's inescapable role in that region. i believe that the european union cannot fail to point the european way to ukraine and, in this sense, the macrofinancial assistance it is now providing should be another sign of rapprochement and solidarity at a time of particular social, economic and financial weakness. i hope that ukraine will unreservedly embark on a process of convergence with the european union, that the proposed association agreement will enter into force and strengthen bilateral relations and trade, and that this process may lead to ukraine's accession to our common space. i also hope that the need for such aid will diminish and that ukraine will regain political stability and achieve social balance and renew its business fabric and persist in the option of democracy, human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. − ukraine's economy has been severely affected by the international financial crisis, with a huge decline in its industrial production, a deterioration in the budgetary situation and an increase in external financing needs. the community financial support reflects the country's strategic importance as a potential candidate for eu membership. i therefore vote in favour of providing macrofinancial assistance to ukraine of up to eur 500 million in the form of a loan to support the process of economic stabilisation in the country and to reduce the balance of payments and budgetary needs identified in the current imf programme. i believe it is important to help ukraine to return to the minimum socioeconomic levels required and to enable its public accounts to stabilise, thus creating prospects for growth and political confidence. i also agree that control mechanisms should be ensured to increase clarity, transparency and accountability and that the european parliament should be regularly informed about the work of the economic and financial committee.
in writing. - the macrofinancial assistance to ukraine now proposed does not constitute genuine and disinterested aid. on the contrary, i did. conditioning this assistance on imf requirements and the 'key principles and objectives of economic reform set out in the eu-ukraine association agenda' means, inter alia: - the establishment of 'a comprehensive eu-ukraine free trade area'; - compliance with the 'eu common foreign and security policy (cfsp) objectives'; - 'intensification of coordination through military channels to address issues of common interest'; - ukraine's possible participation in the eu naval operation atalanta; - establishment in ukraine of 'a fully functioning market economy' and the eu-defined principles of macroeconomic stability; - exchange of 'best practices' between the eu and ukraine on reform of the social security system with the aim of 'improving the sustainability of ukraine's pension system'. it is clear from all that is explicitly assumed and from much that can be read between the lines, given the known meaning of much of the community vocabulary mentioned above, that our vote could not be otherwise than against. we are also expressing our solidarity with the ukrainian people.
in writing. the process of stabilising and relaunching the ukrainian economy is supported by the international monetary fund (imf). in view of the worsening economic situation and prospects, ukraine has requested union macro-financial assistance. the macrofinancial assistance programme is very important in helping the financial balance of european nations that have been through the recent world crisis and that have been hurt by the consequences of that crisis in their main trading partners. the financial imbalances are budgetary and balance of payments imbalances. this aid is important for ukraine to face the crisis in a more consistent way. the eu must therefore be a space of solidarity. hence my vote.
in writing. − the outermost regions face increased challenges due to their geography, which places them far from the centre of the union. i therefore welcome the adoption of specific measures in the agricultural field for these regions in the context of the current economic crisis. in particular, i would stress the specific nature of the regions of the azores and madeira and welcome the main measures taken in connection with the introduction, extension or adaptation of certain derogations in the sugar, milk and wine sectors. it is important to stress that it is essential to have an integrated strategy for the outermost regions, without forgetting that each of them has its own specificity, and it is important to find the best responses for each of the regions. i would stress the various instruments that exist in the eu, such as regional strategies and neighbourhood policy, and the importance of continuing to discuss the strategic guidelines for the outermost regions in order to raise awareness among decision-makers of the specificities and potential of these regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation laying down specific measures in the agricultural field for the outermost regions of the european union. the adoption of this report not only represents an opportunity for agricultural diversification but also restores more possibilities for the re-dispatch of products. in a period of economic crisis this is a decisive contribution to restructuring and maintaining in regions such as the azores not only many dozens of jobs but also maintaining the activity of the agro-industrial sugar industry.
in writing. the commission proposal provides for amendments to regulation (ec) no 247/2006 laying down specific measures for agriculture in favour of the outermost regions of the union. these amendments relate to the sugar, milk and wine sectors. i welcome the quality of the work of the rapporteurs who have spoken. the current multiannual financial framework and the next financial perspective must have the principle of solidarity as one of its basic principles. social and territorial cohesion must be ensured in this way. we all know the natural difficulties faced by the outermost regions of the european union, given their geographical situation and conditions, which have a negative impact on their economic activity and their productive fabric. the amendments go against this principle of solidarity and i therefore support them.
in writing. - the assumption underlying the report, and made explicit in the first recital of the compromise proposal, of accepting the end of milk quotas is unacceptable to us, justifying our vote against. if it comes to fruition (as the report adopted admits, taking it for granted), the end of the milk quotas will have extremely serious effects on the azorean milk sector and the entire local dairy industry. the consequences for the regional economy of the abolition of milk quotas - which we are fighting against and will continue to fight against - would not be mitigated by the measures now proposed for the sugar processing industry, with a view to extending the period of re-dispatching. this is a fair objective, but it is weakened at the outset when it is accepted - here too! - that this measure should be phased out within five years. as regards madeira, the process of converting vineyards is significantly delayed and may even be compromised if incentives are not reinforced - a need which is ignored in the report. the negative consequences for the region of the so-called 'geneva agreement' on banana trade are also being ignored. another aspect that would be worth considering is the possibility of supporting the development of an inter-island market for the marketing of local agricultural products.
in writing. − the economic and social development of the outermost regions of the european union is conditioned by their peripheral location, insularity, small surface area, adverse climate and geographical situation and economic dependence on a small number of products. these factors, taken together, severely restrict their development. as enshrined in article 349 of the treaty of lisbon, provision is made for the possibility of specific measures in favour of the outermost regions, which should be implemented through appropriate initiatives designed to meet their specific needs, particularly in the agricultural and fisheries sectors. the main amendments relate to the introduction, extension or adaptation of certain derogations in the sugar, milk and wine sectors. in view of all these conditions and the international crisis we are facing, we shall vote in favour of these measures. hence my vote.
in writing. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on regional development on the report by mr luís paulo alves, i am pleased with the way we have started to move towards a more rapid and effective adjustment of the maximum quantities for the export of products covered by the supply arrangements from the outermost regions. this dossier falls within the scope of article 349 of the treaty of lisbon, which provides for aid to the outermost regions in view of the permanent difficulties they face as a result of their geographical situation, topography and climate. the provisions of this regulation should meet the specific needs of these regions and the realities of the local market. this was the objective i had in mind when drafting my proposals, which the european commission has committed itself to revising in the overall review of this regulation to be carried out in 2010. i have also been concerned to safeguard the income of madeiran and azorean producers of wine of hybrid varieties prohibited by the common organization of the european wine market by enabling them to continue to grow it for family consumption and not be obliged to grub it up. as i expected, the compromise reached in the trilogue between parliament, the commission and the council was confirmed today by a large majority in the plenary.
in writing. - as i said earlier, the treaty of lisbon points to an increase in the volume of matters to be dealt with by the european parliament in co-decision. the appropriate technical and logistical means are needed to carry out the work quickly and effectively. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (aema) is based on the principle of equal treatment for all medicinal products.
in writing. - in line with the policies i have been advocating, i consider it important to adopt a zero-based budget policy at the beginning of each parliamentary term. parliament's budget will thus reflect real needs and increase transparency, budgetary rigor and efficiency. i am also in favour of the separation of fixed and variable costs, the latter being justified by a cost-benefit analysis. this cost-benefit analysis is important for better results and resource management. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, new powers have been conferred and with the entry of 18 new members, it is necessary to create the conditions for them to be able to exercise their mandate in a dignified and effective manner. i would stress that legislative excellence must be the parliament's top priority and that it must be given the resources it needs to function properly, especially at a time of great demands, when the european institutions have a key role to play for europeans and for society in general.
in writing. - with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european parliament's powers have been extended, which naturally entails new measures to meet the increased needs. this estimate of the 2011 budget therefore represents an increase of 5,8% compared to the 2010 financial year in an attempt to ensure that parliament can fully use and develop its prerogatives. the budget for 2011 will be €1,710 547 354, of which 20.32% will be allocated to heading 5 (administration), which will allow the reconciliation of policy objectives with their financing. this budget proposal includes provisions on the representation of croatia, the reinforcement of the secretariat for members, the increase in posts, the increase in the annual number of visitors invited by members, the reduction of parliament's carbon footprint and the financing of the house of european history and the visitor centre. this report reflects a sensible budget, geared towards a european parliament sustainability policy, but which nevertheless has a rigorous approach to the effective use of available resources.
in writing. - i voted overall in favour of the effort to simplify the cap which should benefit farmers by allowing them to focus on producing safe, quality food, but also national and union authorities by reducing the bureaucratic burden associated with the implementation of the cap. the cap is of vital importance to the eu, both because it ensures safe food production and because of concerns for the preservation of the environment or rural areas, with a view to effective sustainable development. simplifying has to mean greater responsibility for all the agents involved. i therefore welcome the need to make the cap a simpler, more transparent and fairer instrument, and i would like to stress, as a first step, the proposal to establish a uniform system for the identification of animals with the possibility of self-certification, the reduction of inspection quotas to levels below those currently defined and the question of traceability of sheepmeat and goatmeat: i am referring specifically to the proposal to identify herds by herd. and the necessary reform of the cap will finally have to distinguish between support for individual farmers or their associative movement and the return of large agri-food companies to the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that simplification of the cap is essential for the competitiveness of european agriculture, for the preservation of jobs and for the sustainable development of european rural areas. the control rules need to be streamlined and made more accessible to farmers, with the help and advice of national bodies, to ensure that the quality of european agricultural products does not impose unnecessary burdens and additional difficulties on those involved in agricultural activity.
in writing. - simplification of legislation is a key objective in bringing europe closer to citizens. we need simple policies that are easily understood by those who do not know the community vocabulary and do not speak european. to that extent, a policy as fundamental and structural as the cap must be understood by its main target groups, in this case european farmers. i therefore agree with the rapporteur when he rightly says that 'the new cap must enable farmers to concentrate on the central objective of providing safe, quality food of known origin, while helping them to provide non-marketable public goods'. i hope that the new cap can be simpler, more transparent and fairer, more geared to farmers' needs and to the market, with quicker and less bureaucratic procedures (although safe and effective). legal certainty does not require complexity or lengthy procedures. it requires simplicity and efficiency. that is exactly what we want for the new cap.
in writing. the common agricultural policy must ensure an adequate supply of safe food and must also respond to challenges such as the preservation of rural areas, mountain regions, disadvantaged regions and the multifunctionality of european agriculture. the harmonization of legislation must be accompanied by the elimination of redundancy. the 25% reduction in administrative burdens is expected to be achieved by 2012. the common agricultural policy must be simplified, which will make our agricultural economy more competitive. in this way, jobs are preserved and created and a contribution is made to the sustainable development of our rural areas. the simplification of the cap should benefit farmers first and foremost, not just the national authorities and the paying agencies of the member states. farmers should have access to functional systems that allow them to submit applications for direct payments at their place of residence easily and without red tape. this simplification should be accompanied by a simplification of its implementation, and member states should minimise the bureaucratic formalities required of beneficiaries, in particular in the field of rural development. more flexibility is required. the commission is therefore in favour of allowing more flexible payment arrangements before all checks are finally completed.
in writing. - the need to change the penalties, particularly as regards non-compliance not attributable to the producer; the simplification of the application procedures; the very positive changes in the identification of animals, particularly sheep and goats. however, the approach proposed by the rapporteur is significantly market-oriented, competitiveness-oriented, and 'reducing excessive protectionism', deepening a sense of liberalization, with the well-known disastrous consequences. the document also continues to support the current aid distribution model. it states that 'the distribution of the single payment should be equitable', but does not propose concrete measures to achieve this objective. it is convinced that the current definition of agricultural activity for the purposes of the single payment should be revised, but it does not propose any changes to the current model of paying for not producing. in short, the report lacks proposals and measures to change the current cap model, particularly (but not only) as regards the distribution of aid.
in writing. − simplifying the cap is essential to meet the objective of reducing the administrative burden in the agricultural sector by 25% by 2010. bureaucracy is a serious obstacle for farmers, who, by wasting too much time on paperwork, neglect their daily activities in their fields. the new amendments will also reduce the administrative burden on farmers by hundreds of millions of euros, with tangible benefits, especially in view of the difficult economic situation in which we live. simplification of rules and control mechanisms is essential for farmers, who must ensure that 500 million citizens are provided with food at a reasonable price. hence my vote.
in writing. - the report on the simplification of the cap reflects on a subject which has been of great concern to farmers, the main target of the cap, but also to european citizens in general who find the cap difficult to understand because of the complexity of its mechanisms. the need for simplification measures is therefore recognised by all as urgent and it is crucial that they have a direct impact on farmers as a whole and not just on the administrations of each member state, as has often been the case. the elimination of market management mechanisms cannot be considered as one of the ways of simplification. one of the problems to be corrected by simplification should be the need to eliminate discrimination at the level of the single payment scheme in the various member states, problems arising from the inefficiency of national administrations, such as checks, deadlines, payments, etc., preventing us from having a multi-speed cap, which promotes inequalities between farmers in the various member states.
in writing. − simplifying the common agricultural policy (cap) legislation is crucial to making europe's agricultural economy more competitive, preserving and boosting jobs and contributing to the development of rural areas. it seems to me essential that whenever the commission proposes new regulations in this field, it should simultaneously seek to remove unnecessary administrative barriers. the simpler the legislation, the more comprehensible it will be for all concerned, whether farmers, national and regional authorities or bodies monitoring the application of funds. this will reduce the support and time required by these agents in preparing applications, the number of errors and the costs associated with monitoring funding. simplification is also needed in the control of the use of funds and random audits seem to me the most efficient way of doing this. the application of penalties must be transparent and proportionate, taking into account the size of the holdings and the local realities, particularly in the outermost regions, such as madeira. it is because this report goes against the above points that i have voted in favour of it today in the house. it is now up to us to ensure that, in the overall reform of the cap, there is better coordination between agricultural policy and cohesion policy.
in writing. - i welcome this resolution which aims to improve the simplification rules in the field of contract award, while contributing to the creation of greater legal certainty. european initiatives in the field of public procurement require coordination at european level to avoid inconsistencies and legal problems. it is also important to clarify the legal conditions under which public procurement legislation applies to institutionalised public-private partnerships. i call on the commission to simplify procedures so that both local authorities and businesses can reduce costs and time spent on red tape. on the other hand, simplified procedures will facilitate access for smes and allow them to participate on more balanced and fairer terms. public administrations should be encouraged to use ecological, social and other criteria in the award of public contracts. i urge the commission to explore the possibility of using public procurement compatible with environmental protection as a tool to promote sustainable development.
in writing. − in 2004, the commission carried out a review of the directives on public procurement procedures, aiming at simplifying procedures towards more transparent, efficient, flexible and less bureaucratic public procurement. the rapporteur says that 'the main task of public procurement services is to purchase goods and services in economically and cost-effective ways in order to fulfil the public service mission. however, public authorities are not economic operators like others and have a special responsibility in that they administer public money.' once again i am forced to point out that a complex law is not the law that best serves the interests of the parties. in the case of public procurement, the opposite is true. the more complex, opaque and time-consuming the procedures, the more the law is evaded and, ultimately, the more corruption is encouraged. it is therefore imperative that in the process of revising the current directives on public procurement, a search be made for simpler and more effective rules to regulate a sector which represents some 16% of the gross domestic product of the european union.
in writing. the annual turnover of public procurement in the european union amounts to over 16% of gross domestic product, i.e. over eur 1 500 billion. at a time of economic crisis, public procurement directives should neither make procurement procedures more difficult nor delay them. contracting entities, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, require legal certainty and certainty and fast procedures. i believe that the commission and the member states, in cooperation with regional and local authorities, should review the various sets of rules applicable to public procurement in order to unify them and to simplify the whole legal framework for public procurement in order to reduce the risk of errors and to increase efficiency in the use of the structural funds. it is noted that a large part of the irregularities in the implementation of european projects co-financed by the structural funds and the cohesion fund result from the improper transposition of eu rules. i believe that the commission should consider the possibility of using accelerated variants of procedures in the framework of the structural funds even after 2010, so that these resources are not wasted by the member states.
in writing. - the award of public contracts is a very delicate matter which deserves to be treated very seriously, as public funds are involved. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the award of public contracts must therefore be transparent and fair to all interested parties, with the main criterion being the best price-performance ratio, so that the best overall bid is considered, not just the one with the lowest price. hence my vote.

in writing. − over the past five decades, organ transplantation has become a globally effective practice that contributes to improving the quality of life and increasing the life expectancy of patients. this directive lays down rules aimed at ensuring high standards of quality and safety for organs of human origin intended for transplantation into the human body, in order to ensure a high level of protection of human health. it introduces national quality programmes which set out standards and practices for the transplantation process in the member states. it also sets out more precisely the harvesting process and related issues such as the information system. traceability and protection of donors and recipients also deserve special attention. in view of the three main objectives of this proposal, namely to ensure quality and patient safety at community level, to ensure the protection of donors and to facilitate cooperation between member states, i voted in favour of this report. however, i would like to stress that organ transplant programmes must be based on the principle of voluntary and free donation, which has already been enshrined in previous legislation on substances of human origin, and must be careful about any form of marketing.
in writing. the report also calls for the establishment of a european network of national experts in the field of health and safety at work. it is unacceptable that on average 12 people die every day waiting for a transplant. this directive will facilitate organ donation and transplantation and exchange between eu member states, to the benefit of thousands of european patients.
