in writing. − i welcome this proposal and welcome its three main objectives: to ensure quality and safety for patients at community level, to ensure the protection of donors and to facilitate cooperation between member states. in the european union there is generally a broad social consensus on organ donation for transplantation. however, due to differences in culture, tradition and organisation, there are different approaches to this issue in the member states. i would stress that, although the directive should maintain or seek to achieve harmonisation of quality and safety measures, it should not create an additional administrative burden for the member states and should provide for a sufficient margin of flexibility which does not jeopardise existing good practice. in order to ensure a high level of health protection throughout the eu, the proposed directive sets out common binding standards on the quality and safety of human organs intended for transplantation. i support the commission's view that, in principle, organ transplant programmes should be based on the principle of voluntary and unpaid donation. organ donation must always be free of charge and protected against any possible commercialisation.
in writing. − organ transplantation is an important form of rehabilitation for patients suffering from a multitude of diseases that cause fatal organ failure. the number of transplants in the european union has been increasing, saving and prolonging many lives. however, there are still large waiting lists for transplants. our vote in favour expresses our agreement with the improvements which the report seeks to make in the face of the present situation, not only in terms of quality and safety, with the establishment of the necessary procedures for harvesting and transport, but also in terms of the protection of the donor and the recipient, with due regard to ethical principles and non-compensation. the report also addresses, in a way that seems to us to be correct, the worrying issue of trafficking in human beings and organs.
in writing. - the aim of this directive is quite clear, we need more organs for patients, more cooperation between member states in this area and the fight against organ trafficking. one of the main reasons for this new legislation is that it provides for the designation of an authority responsible in each member state for ensuring that the quality and safety standards of organs are met. these authorities will be responsible for ensuring the quality and safety of organs ' throughout the whole chain from donation to transplantation, as well as in the assessment of their quality and safety during patient recovery and subsequent follow-up'. the new directive also requires that healthcare professionals involved in all stages of the chain, from donation to transplantation or organ disposal, be appropriately qualified and specific training programmes should be developed for these professionals. for all these reasons we vote in favour. hence my vote.
in writing. − transplantation is one of the medical specialties which has developed the most in the last few decades and has achieved remarkable success, decisive in saving human lives. paradoxically, it was the success of transplantation that, among other factors, contributed to an increasing number of organ transplant candidates, thus giving rise to long waiting lists, as well as the human drama associated with the death of about 12 patients a day in the eu because they do not receive the organ they need to survive. one way of minimising this problem is through exchange between eu member states, ensuring better match between donor and recipient, a shorter time frame and a higher number of organs used. however, such exchanges require uniform high standards of quality and safety, which are laid down in this directive of the european parliament and of the council. the mikolášik report on the quality and safety standards of organs for transplantation is thus an important contribution to minimizing the shortage of organs, along with the fundamental protection of the health of the recipient and the living donor, for which we warmly welcome it.
in writing. the european parliament has approved the calendar of plenary sessions for 2011. i regret that 200 million euro per year is still being spent by the european taxpayer to hold 12 annual sessions in strasbourg. the hypocrisy goes so far as to disregard the precept of the treaties, which would mean holding a monthly session, also in august. the legitimate aspirations of the city of strasbourg could be met by the permanent establishment of one or two european union agencies in the city. as for the circus, it should obviously end! it is also pointless for the european parliament to meet 48 days a year in a city which has no direct air links with almost all the capitals of the member states. and the ones that do exist have business hours that are incompatible with parliamentary activity. it is easy to see that the heads of state and government who take these decisions travel by private plane and do not waste tens or hundreds of hours a year to get to strasbourg.
in writing. the motion for a resolution contains some pertinent reservations concerning the use of the enzyme preparation based on thrombin with fibrinogen as a food additive for the reconstitution of foods which we consider relevant. reservations which the commission's proposals do not entirely remove. there are still doubts about the possibility of using unpackaged reconstituted products, compromising the necessary consumer information, and about the effectiveness of the ban on the use of these products in restaurants and other public establishments serving food. the commission itself recognises that the use of this food additive may mislead the consumer as to the state of the final food. the proposed labelling solution, in view of the above, may not be sufficient in itself to remove this problem. there are also concerns about the food binding process (e.g. cold mixing without the addition of salt and without any subsequent heating process) and the safety of the final product. we therefore support this resolution.
in writing. the proposal that proposed that bovine and/or porcine thrombin be included in the list of food additives authorised in the eu. and it gave us no assurance that this substance would confer a clear advantage, that it would benefit consumers, and that in the end its use might even mislead consumers. in addition, the whole process of binding several pieces of meat significantly increases the surface area that can be infected by pathogenic bacteria. hence my vote.
in writing. − organ transplantation is essential in the treatment of certain diseases, has positive results in terms of years of life gained, improves the quality of life of patients and allows for a better cost-benefit ratio when compared to other replacement therapies. however, there are several factors to be aware of with this therapy, including the risk of disease transmission, limited organ supply and organ trafficking. there is currently no common european database on organs intended for donation and transplantation or on living or deceased donors, nor a pan-european certification system to attest to the legal procurement of organs and tissues from the human body. i voted in favour of this report, welcoming the action plan on donation and transplantation (2009-2015) adopted by the commission in december 2008, which sets out a cooperation approach between member states in the form of a set of priority actions, based on the identification and development of common objectives and the evaluation of donation and transplantation activities through defined indicators that can help identify benchmarks and good practices.
in writing. − the discrepancy in the percentage of organ donors in the various european countries seems to indicate that some of the member states' systems will be more effective than others and should therefore be studied and possibly adopted by those with lower success rates. in addition to the adoption of best practices, it is clear that, in a matter which is closely linked to the health and life of citizens, there is a need to optimise resources and to take collective advantage of the european scale of organ supply. it makes no sense for someone to die because they don't have an organ available in their country when, next door, it can exist and be available. i agree with the idea that those who encourage or promote so-called transplant tourism and the use of organ trafficking networks should be punished, particularly severely if they are health professionals or insurance companies. i would stress the need to provide effective support for both transplant recipients and the altruistic and voluntary donors, to whom our societies owe a debt of gratitude.
in writing. − currently, there are 56,000 patients in the eu waiting for a suitable organ donor and 12 people die every day waiting for a solid organ transplant. organ transplantation is virtually the only therapeutic option for patients with end-stage liver, heart and lung failure. however, there is a significant discrepancy between the number of patients waiting for a transplant and the number of patients who actually get a transplant. this discrepancy results from the shortage of organs for transplantation in relation to needs. the inclusion of more patients on waiting lists coupled with the minimal increase in the number of transplant patients is reflected in a longer waiting time. this time is costly and can have a negative impact on patient survival and transplant success rates. the commission proposal to draw up a european action plan on donation and transplantation for the period 2009-2015 sets out a cooperation approach between member states, based on a set of priority actions, and based on the identification and development of common objectives, the establishment of consensus quantitative and qualitative indicators and benchmarks, the submission of regular reports and the identification of good practice.
in writing. − organ transplantation can ensure a full and healthy life for many years for people who would otherwise often need intensive care or simply not survive. the number of transplants in the european union has been increasing, saving and prolonging many lives. however, there are still large waiting lists for transplants. 56 000 patients in the european union are waiting for a suitable organ donor and, according to estimates, 12 people die every day waiting for a solid organ transplant. the number of post-mortem donations is insufficient in itself and the number of living donors does not meet the needs. furthermore, there are wide discrepancies between member states as regards post-mortem organ donation rates, and there is currently no common eu-wide database on organs for donation and transplantation or living or deceased donors, nor a certification system to attest to the legal procurement of organs and tissues from the human body. it is in this context that the report under discussion proposes steps which we consider important for strengthening cooperation between member states in this field, from which all can benefit.
in writing. - we support this new directive for a variety of reasons, but above all because we believe that this is a decisive plan to save many lives in the eu. every day, 12 patients die and 60,000 are waiting for a compatible donor for organ transplantation in the u.s. transplantation has steadily increased over the past two decades and is the only treatment available for cases of terminal organ failure such as liver, lungs and heart. the death rates among people awaiting a coronary, liver or lung transplant are between 15% and 30%, so patients needing an organ transplant should have to wait less for this operation thanks to this new directive. hence my vote.
in writing. − this report sets out a series of actions aimed at promoting cooperation between member states in the field of transplantation in order to contribute to an increase in transplants, a reduction in waiting lists and, consequently, a reduction in the number of deaths of patients waiting for an organ. at the same time, the action plan also sets quality and safety standards common to the member states, which not only contributes to the protection of patients but also facilitates cooperation between states. the creation of national and eu-wide registries of transplantation procedures (avoiding discrimination, monitoring results, etc.) will allow for a broader and more accurate knowledge of the european reality, as well as reducing opportunities for organ trafficking. the report supports the action plan and stresses the need and urgency of the action lines outlined, while also developing a firm stance against all forms of organ trafficking in different parts of the world. i consider this report to be an important complement to the commission's communication and a valuable contribution to a pressing human cause in the context of health care for european citizens.
in writing. - human rights and fundamental freedoms are the set of values and principles that distinguish us as human beings and on which our coexistence is based. they are universal, indivisible and interdependent. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty is an important step in terms of human rights, not only because it gives the charter of fundamental rights a binding character, but also because by conferring legal personality on the eu, it allows the eu to accede to the echr. this accession is of the utmost importance both at political and legal level in creating a genuine area of human rights. as regards union action, to which member states have transferred important powers, it will ensure that citizens are afforded protection similar to that which they already enjoy vis-à-vis the member states. the european institutions are obliged to act accordingly, in particular during the process of drafting and adopting legislative proposals. on the other hand, the harmonisation of legislation and case law in the field of human rights between the eu and the echr should contribute to the creation of an integrated system in which the european courts for human rights (ecthr and ecthr) should operate in harmony, without a hierarchical link, but rather in terms of specialisation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the accession of the european union to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms is a strong message that increases the union's credibility in the eyes of third countries which it regularly requires to respect the convention.
in writing. - the european union's accession to the convention follows the process initiated in maastricht to give the european community legal personality, which culminated in the treaty of lisbon. the adoption of the charter of fundamental rights, first with a narrow scope of application and then with its extension by incorporation into the treaty, was an important step in this process. the european union now participates more closely in a continental human rights area. i welcome this development. i hope that the various legal, technical and institutional questions which are now being raised can be solved on the basis of the principle of subsidiarity and voluntary cooperation between states and respect for their sovereignty and for national legal systems and the rule of law.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report in favour of the union's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights (echr). this is because accession is a step forward in the process of european integration and another step towards political union. furthermore, the union's system of protection of fundamental rights being completed and intensified by the incorporation of the charter of fundamental rights into its primary law, the accession of the union to the echr will constitute a strong message in terms of coherence between the union and the countries belonging to the council of europe and its pan-european human rights regime; this accession will further enhance the union's credibility vis-à-vis third countries, which it regularly requires, in the context of its bilateral relations, to respect the echr. this accession also guarantees citizens, as regards the union's action, protection similar to that which they already enjoy vis-à-vis all the member states.
in writing. − the eu's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms was already envisaged by the treaty on european union and, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it now becomes mandatory. accession will strengthen the protection of human rights in europe and subject the union's legal system to external judicial review, ensuring a harmonisation of case law between the court of justice of the european union and the european court of human rights and allowing european citizens to enjoy protection in relation to the action of the european institutions on terms analogous to those which already exist in relation to the member states. it should be noted that this accession does not make the eu a member of the council of europe nor does it call into question the principle of the autonomy of community law, since the court of justice remains the sole authority with jurisdiction over the validity and interpretation of union law. i would also stress the importance attached to the possibility for the union to nominate candidates and to choose a judge to represent it, the need mentioned to keep parliament duly informed about the accession negotiations and to establish in future a mechanism for exchanging information between the parliamentary assemblies of both institutions.
in writing. − the european union has been a strong advocate of the international criminal court and all its member states share its membership of this important court. i hope that the states parties will live up to their responsibilities and that the kampala conference will produce an international criminal court better equipped to meet the challenges of the present time, with appropriate cooperation from national legal systems and with sufficient means to exercise its powers effectively. the enormous gravity of the crimes on which your activity will preferentially focus thus demands it.
in writing. − the eu is a strong supporter of the icc (international criminal court), which promotes the universality and upholds the integrity of the rome statute, with a view to protecting and enhancing the independence, legitimacy and effectiveness of the international judicial process. this is demonstrated by the fact that the eu systematically promotes the inclusion of a clause on the icc in negotiating mandates and agreements with third countries. the eu has already made available over €40 million over ten years under the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr) for projects to support the icc and international criminal justice. the review conference of the rome statute of the international criminal court in kampala, uganda, represents a unique opportunity for states parties, as well as non-state parties, civil society and other stakeholders, to strongly reiterate their commitment to justice and accountability. there are 111 states parties to the icc, with some regions, such as the middle east, north africa and asia, underrepresented. i hope that the member states will participate in this conference by making themselves represented at the highest level and by publicly reaffirming their commitment to the icc.

has refused to analyse the causes of the current situation or to draw the consequences in relation to the main policy areas it has pursued in implementing the lisbon strategy: the liberalisation of economic sectors, including financial services, and labour flexibility, which it has called flexicurity. what they now want to do is to continue to pave the way for greater concentration of wealth through a series of directives which facilitate the privatisation of strategic sectors of the economy and attacks on public services of interest to economic groups in the areas of health, social security, education, anything that can make a profit. they prefer to think that only a break with these policies can lead to a change of direction and that only this can bring social progress, but it mr president, we are facing an acceleration of global change which has devastating consequences for our economic, political and social systems and, therefore, for all our citizens. we are witnessing today an unprecedented weakening of the states' capacity to respond. the european union must therefore identify common causes and allies and act clearly and unitedly on the world stage. extraordinary situations require lucidity of joint action. if we do not take the necessary measures of rigour and collective responsibility, europe will be condemned to marginalization and impoverishment, and only a strong europe, respecting its common rules, will be able to respond adequately to the new times. weak and indebted states are not able to protect their citizens. we must therefore be able to win back the confidence of the citizens, to win the battles of stability, budgetary austerity, job creation, the stability of monetary union, globalisation and strategic choices. this is on the off chance that we have our future compromised. and the future is won by betting on social cohesion, ensuring peace, building a new model based on the values of freedom, social justice and responsibility. the 2020 strategy and the europe 2020 integrated guidelines are thus essential instruments for a new cycle of growth and jobs in europe. for proper implementation and achievement, clear and quantifiable targets need to be set in employment, education and poverty reduction. it is also crucial for the success of the strategy that everything is done to facilitate the transposition of the national objectives by the member states and to ensure the proper implementation of the strategy.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the single market is not a purely economic reality. it is essential to ensure that the revitalization of the single market takes a holistic approach that integrates consumer objectives, economic, social and environmental concerns, for a renewed single market.
in writing. − the internal market and related policies have enabled european citizens to have greater access to goods and services, greater variety and at lower cost. the principles of the internal market have given european consumers greater access to information and greater protection of their rights, but they have also become more aware of their duties. the internal market is therefore not a static reality but a dynamic, changing reality in a globalised world, and one in which its development and further implementation must continue to be considered. i agree with the rapporteur and stress the importance of the internal market of the european union for european integration itself, for greater social cohesion, sustainable development, competitiveness and economic growth which will enable us to face future developments and compete in a globalised world.
in writing. − the construction of a fully functioning integrated european single market is a fundamental process for the deepening of european integration, social cohesion, economic growth and sustainable development of the union. but the economic crisis has undoubtedly affected citizens' and consumers' confidence in the single market. it is important that the european citizen understands the importance of the single market, how it works and, most importantly, the benefits it can bring to citizens, consumers and smes. revitalising the single market requires a common holistic approach by its various players to integrate the objectives of consumers and citizens, particularly those linked to economic, social, health and environmental concerns, in a renewed single market. this new programme for the completion of the single market must be designed in such a way as to promote social justice, ensure market integrity, encourage innovation and promote the transition to the new digital age. these are imperatives which could give the single market competitive advantages over other major world economies. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the internal market is not a one-way street.
in writing. − the construction of a single market has always been and remains one of the eu's main objectives. a fully functioning single market is a fundamental process for deepening european integration, social cohesion, economic growth and sustainable development in the eu. the recent financial crisis has raised some doubts about the timing of the single market, with some arguing that it is in a fragile state, which is very damaging to the process of integration of the single market and the history of the union itself. it is very important at this stage to find a tool that informs eu citizens in a clear and unambiguous way about how the single market works and the great benefits it can bring to consumers and smes. hence my vote.
in writing. - the priority given to knowledge is more important than ever. more needs to be done in the area of the knowledge triangle, by adopting a framework of reforms necessary to make knowledge a social value, by strengthening the links between enterprises and universities, as in the case of the knowledge and innovation communities (kics) of the european institute of technology (eit). it is essential that universities integrate the economic and social environment into their main sphere of action, within the framework of their research and innovation programmes. it is urgent to develop a strategy of investing in new sources of growth, fostering research, development, innovation and education to strengthen our industrial base, a service sector of excellence and a modern rural economy. the role of higher education institutions, universities and polytechnics, both public and private, will be of enormous value in a context of state confidence in these institutions, which should enjoy autonomy so that they can make their indispensable contribution to the development of europe. it is necessary to strengthen both the interdisciplinarity and transdisciplinarity of education and research programmes and cooperation between universities, and that in this respect icts are a key instrument.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the dialogue between universities and enterprises: a new partnership for the modernisation of european universities, because it presents measures which contribute to the increase of the employability of european students. cooperation between the education sector and enterprises is essential to closing the gap between the supply of education and the demand for employment.
in writing. − i believe that partnerships which enable the modernisation of universities, especially those which promote better education and qualifications for individuals, are essential to increasing european competitiveness. this qualification will be reflected in the level of innovation, research and development which are indispensable for sustained economic and social growth. partnerships between universities and enterprises should be established to facilitate the entry of these workers into the labour market, thus contributing to the reduction of the high unemployment rates that are particularly evident today. in this context, i would also like to stress the importance of the european union's cohesion policy, whose funds will be extremely useful for this purpose.
in writing. − the lisbon european council in march 2000 and the barcelona european council in march 2002 endorsed the strategic objective of making the eu the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world and its education and training systems a world reference in terms of quality by 2010 and of creating the european research and innovation area. member states are responsible for education and training policy and the eu's role is to support the improvement of national systems through new eu-wide instruments, mutual learning and the exchange of information and good practice. the knowledge-based economy and the accelerated pace of technological development pose challenges to higher education and research in europe, but they also open up new opportunities which must be effectively exploited. in this context, it is of the utmost importance to create quality partnerships in higher education and in business. i believe that cooperation between the education sector and enterprises at local, regional, national and transnational level is crucial to closing the gap between the supply logic of the education sector and the demand logic of the world of work.
in writing. - the report on the dialogue between universities and enterprises takes a position which we do not understand as the path to the modernisation of education. we must take very seriously the risks that impede free, public and democratic access to education. we believe that it is urgent to acknowledge the mistakes made in the bologna process and, contrary to what the rapporteur says about bologna, to demystify the question of mobility as a means of bringing the member states closer together and of achieving equality. in addition, it should be borne in mind that the bologna process is not neutral, it involved an initial investment, which followed in parallel a policy of discharge of the state in respect of the financing of universities. the issue of university autonomy is mentioned several times in the report, and the idea of 'partnership' between universities and enterprises is added as a way of securing funding for institutions. this university-enterprise concept distorts the real meaning and value of education as a universal right, and shapes education according to a mercantilist vision, taking away its content and quality. it's a neoliberal view that we oppose.
in writing. − university-enterprise dialogue is essential for the quality training that is intended for young people in the eu. cooperation between the education sector and enterprises at all levels is essential to bring the supply logic of the education sector and the demand logic of the world of work closer together. partnerships between education and training institutions and enterprises are essential to increase students' employability, improve entrepreneurial potential and facilitate familiarity with the world of work. hence my vote.
in writing. − the rules in force in the central and eastern european countries before accession were less stringent than the rules applied in the eu at the time. this has necessitated eu intervention and financial assistance to improve the level of protection of human health and the environment. it is in this context that we are voting on this proposal. the commission proposal for a regulation provides for financial assistance for the dismantling of units 1 to 4 of the kozloduy nuclear power station in bulgaria and also for the treatment of the radioactive substances resulting from this operation. the rapporteur believes that the lack of eu assistance could compromise safety, as wwer 440/230 reactors (as is the case) have serious design deficiencies that could not be overcome.
in writing. − the protection and enhancement of human health and the environment are priority objectives in european development policies. in this connection, i consider it absolutely necessary that the european union should safeguard the appropriate financial and technical resources for the dismantling of units 1 to 4 of the kozloduy nuclear power plant in bulgaria, as the european parliament is advocating in this resolution. europe is thus avoiding a pole of high radioactive emissions and the risk of serious accidents. in addition to the safety conditions of decommissioning operations, it is urgent that the european community should play an active role in supporting bulgaria to overcome the negative effects of decommissioning on the competitiveness of the economy, energy sustainability and the dynamisation of the labour market. in this context, the eu intervention strategy should ensure support for the creation of new jobs and sustainable industries in the areas affected by decommissioning.
in writing. − with the accession of the countries of central and eastern europe to the eu and the use of nuclear energy by these countries, the eu has found it necessary to provide financial assistance to these countries to deal effectively with radioactive waste in order to improve the level of protection of human health and the environment. the financial support approved here fits into the above framework. hence my vote.
in writing. − innovation is most effectively addressed at regional level through proximity of actors such as universities, public research organisations or industry, promoting partnerships in the field of knowledge transfer and the exchange of good practice between regions. cohesion policy is a key pillar of the european integration process and one of the eu's most successful policies, bringing increasingly heterogeneous regions together and stimulating economic growth and job creation. it is essential to promote and implement successful models in the knowledge triangle and to ensure the sustainable development of regional strategic research frameworks for innovation, in collaboration with companies, research centres, universities and public authorities; unlock the potential of cutting-edge regional clusters based on knowledge to mobilise regional competitiveness and the inclusion of cluster development in both the cip and fp7. i would like to draw attention to the importance of the knowledge and innovation communities set up within the eit, which bring together the main european regional knowledge-based clusters; i would also like to see the structural funds promoting the exchange of knowledge in regional clusters, since these clusters represent a great opportunity, especially for the less-favoured regions.
in writing. − i think it is relevant to look at how the indicative framework of the community strategic guidelines on cohesion for 2007-2013, and in particular guideline 1.2, improving knowledge and innovation for growth, has been followed by the member states and regions in their respective national strategic reference frameworks (nsrfs) and operational programmes. this analysis provides a more concrete view of what has been achieved and of the challenges that remain to be overcome in a subject that is increasingly on the agenda. in a time of crisis, when it is not only healthy but also urgent to avoid waste and duplication, i believe it is important to make a thorough assessment of the way in which cohesion, research and innovation policies and their instruments (structural funds, seventh framework programme for r & d and the competitiveness and innovation framework programme) are articulated in order to make them more efficient and productive.
in writing. − research and innovation are priority areas and absolutely crucial for the competitiveness and success of the european economy in the current global context of crisis, strong competition and increased effort to face new challenges such as climate change and territorial cohesion. this crisis intensifies the risks of regional imbalances and worsening economic and social conditions in the most disadvantaged regions. in this respect, i support this resolution, which stresses the urgency of making access to the structural funds more effective, flexible and simplified, in order to ensure rapid access to support and financing mechanisms for new business projects and the revitalisation of small and mediumsized enterprises. this is a strategy of great relevance and importance for the territorial cohesion of the european union, while ensuring that this crisis becomes an opportunity to capitalise on potential and improve efficiency in the return on resources.
in writing. − cohesion policy is a key pillar of the european integration process and one of the union's most successful policies, fostering convergence between regions and stimulating economic growth and job creation through structural fund funding. in the current 2007-2013 period, all member states allocate a significant share of their total financial allocations to innovation and development activities. i believe that cohesion policy is well placed to create synergies with research and innovation policies in terms of funds and capacity building, networking and knowledge transfer. better use of funds will lead to greater development of research, knowledge and innovation capacity in the various regions, and the territorial dimension will be strengthened in partnerships for the design and implementation of public policies. this report is an initiative which i support because i consider it essential to implement synergies between the structural funds for research and innovation and the funding of the seventh framework programme for research and technological development activities with a view to achieving the goal of the knowledge society more efficiently.
in writing. - in the present situation, where many states are facing serious difficulties in their public finances, it is essential to adopt policy measures that lead to economic and social stability, but above all that stimulate growth. in addition to the deficit, the level of public debt needs to be analysed, and best practices on this issue adopted, in order to allow for a more stable situation so that the mistakes of the past are not repeated in the future. i also believe that it is essential to adopt reasonable criteria for the concept of a recovered economy, since the situations differ from one country to another. finally, i would stress the need for a competitive tax policy, not only for the eu but also for investments in third countries.
in writing. − as the current crisis demonstrates with its profound impacts on economic development, citizens' quality of life and social stability, the sustainability of public finances is a decisive condition for economic recovery and development reliability. the insufficiency of the revision of the stability and growth pact has also become apparent. i therefore reiterate the need to strengthen the mechanisms of the european union institutions, always in the interests of greater integration and territorial cohesion, to ensure greater capacity for intervention and defence to counter risks and deviations from common policies. i would also like to stress the social concerns raised in this report, which points to the profound disparities between citizens' incomes, a situation which is detrimental to the productivity and competitiveness of the economy. i therefore support the need to encourage member states to introduce the appropriate reforms to reduce these imbalances. tax justice and the efficiency of public administration expenditure are fundamental to the process of economic recovery and social cohesion. reducing poverty, ensuring social cohesion and promoting growth and productivity in the economy are unquestionable priorities in the european union, to which a gradual reduction in the tax burden on labour and smes will certainly contribute.
in writing. − the main objective of this report was to analyse the long-term sustainability of public finances in the european union with a view to its economic recovery. the plenary debate could not have come at a more opportune time in view of the unprecedented economic and financial understanding reached last week between european leaders. the measures taken, including the unblocking of aid to greece, the acceleration of the consolidation of public finances in the member states and the creation of a financial stabilisation mechanism, demonstrate strong solidarity but also point to a period of sacrifice that will affect all europeans. these sacrifices must be distributed in a fair and balanced way. this is a time for courageous decisions at national level with a long-term perspective and without any easy-going approaches. balance of public accounts is achieved by a cut in expenditure, an increase in revenue or both simultaneously. in a period of economic contraction, we have nothing left but to reduce public expenditure substantially by cutting waste and optimising the way the state functions. after several amendments, the final content of this proposal addresses some of these challenges and for that reason i gave my vote in favour of it.
in writing. − i vote overall in favour of the proposals in this report which seek to include cohesion policy in the pursuit of the objectives set out in strategy 2020. the new treaty of lisbon reinforces the principle of economic, social and territorial cohesion, and without this solidarity clause the european union itself is meaningless! the ultimate objective of cohesion policy is to reduce disparities in the levels of development of the various european regions and to make up for the structural backwardness of the less-favoured regions and the outermost regions. in the approach to strategy 2020 - which is committed to promoting growth, competitiveness and employment - it is important to bear in mind that cohesion policy can be an important instrument for the success of the objectives it sets.
in writing. - the ultimate objective of cohesion policy is to reduce disparities in the levels of development of the various regions by directing resources, in particular, towards growth and employment. the 2020 strategy presents important and ambitious challenges for europe in five strategic areas: (i) employment; (ii) innovation and research; (iii) climate and energy changes; (iv) education and (v) the fight against poverty. this is an ambitious and daring strategy, as i have had the opportunity to refer to. the rapporteur also stressed the need to design the strategy in line with a future cohesion policy, ensuring that the 2020 strategy is also implemented at regional and local level, something which was missing from the lisbon strategy and which is essential for the development and economic growth of the various regions. as i have had the opportunity to state publicly, i consider that a regional implementation of the objectives of strategy 2020 can be most beneficial for a more balanced regional development.
in writing. - in the european development project, much progress is needed in terms of territorial cohesion, which is crucial in the fight against poverty and social exclusion, the promotion of employment and sustainable development, and social cohesion. i have no doubt that smes have a decisive role to play in the success of the construction of europe. i therefore welcome the recommendations in this report, such as the need to simplify the rules for access to and management of the allocation of funds made available, in order to encourage their use and the effectiveness of their application, covering the whole of the eu. regions implement more than one third of public investment in the eu and increasingly focus structural fund spending on growth and employment-related objectives. i consider it essential that the eu swiftly adopt specific provisions and measures to 'meet the specific needs of regions suffering from severe and permanent natural or demographic handicaps, in particular coastal, island, mountain, cross-border and outermost regions'. i also reiterate that 'vocational education and training are indispensable for the development of the eu and can make it more competitive in the face of global challenges'.
in writing. - the rapporteur regrets that strategy 2020 has not properly incorporated a review of the results of the lisbon strategy, an opinion which we share. if the declared objectives of the lisbon strategy - economic growth, employment and social cohesion - have not been achieved, but have been set back, it is because of the instruments of the lisbon strategy - which were also its objectives! i am very much in favour of liberalization and privatization and the deregulation and flexibilization of labour legislation. options, instruments and objectives now taken up by strategy 2020. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment. it is precisely this 'free, open and functioning market' that has led to more poverty, social exclusion and undermined territorial cohesion in the eu. that is why we do not accept alignment of cohesion policy with this strategy. the real objective of the community is to reduce disparities in the levels of development of the various regions and to establish genuine economic, social and territorial cohesion.
in writing. − this resolution is an important document, as it sets out the best ways of the necessary link between cohesion policy and the eu 2020 strategy. in a period of renewed reflection on european cohesion policy, with a post-2013 horizon, it is indeed important to present it as an indispensable instrument for the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy, in the reiterated assertion that cohesion policies are essential to delivering on the eu's overriding design of integration. cohesion policy has been decisive for a better balance of european regions and is now being pointed out as a key factor in overcoming the current financial crisis in the european union by strengthening competitiveness with endogenous potential. in a present without any increase in the eu budget and with pressures on the cohesion policy budget (around 45% of the eu budget), we believe that a good articulation between the objectives of cohesion policy and the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy is essential in order to simultaneously strengthen cohesion and contribute to a positive response from all regions and all citizens to the challenges facing the eu.
in writing. − cohesion policy is a key policy for achieving the objectives of the 2020 strategy: promoting education, training and research, job creation and economic growth. following the shortcomings of the lisbon strategy in achieving the cohesion objective, namely the lack of adequate consultation of the european parliament and the involvement of regional and local authorities, the report stresses the importance of the contribution of cohesion policy to future strategic objectives. it is therefore important to move towards greater ownership of the objectives of the strategy by local and regional authorities and bodies. the regions have a crucial role to play as a vehicle for economic and social actors, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises. only a strong cohesion policy, given its horizontal approach and adequately funded, will be able to foster development in the european union and make it more competitive in the face of global challenges. the regional dimension of europe must be strengthened by a strategy which takes account of the specificities of the various regions or groups of regions, such as the outermost regions. for the reasons i have outlined, i consider cohesion policy to be an essential instrument for achieving the objectives of strategy 2020 and i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − following the paris declaration of 13 july 2008 establishing the new union for the mediterranean, the previous barcelona process should have been given a new impetus, as expressed in the declaration: 'revitalisation of efforts to transform the mediterranean region into an area of peace, democracy, cooperation and prosperity'. however, 2009 was a year of major changes for the european union (european elections, the president of the commission, the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the fight against the economic and financial crisis, etc.) which delayed the implementation of the union for the mediterranean. i believe that this report correctly identifies the next steps to be taken to achieve the objectives set out in the establishment of the union for the mediterranean and i look forward to the outcome of the second summit of heads of state or government, scheduled for 7 june in barcelona. the strengthening of the union's mediterranean relations is fundamental and i believe that only political dialogue and closer cooperation between the union and the other mediterranean countries will help to create an area of freedom, justice, peace and sustainable and lasting prosperity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the union for the mediterranean (upm) in advocating greater involvement of the european parliament in the development of this regional initiative. it is essential that the european parliament can make its contribution to the success of the summit to be held in barcelona next june, the outcome of which, after two years of difficult start, will be of enormous importance for the future of the upm.
in writing. - any dispassionate observer will say that the euro-mediterranean partnership has not progressed as much as it should and that much remains to be done before it can take on a real form and a concrete and productive content. historically, the mediterranean has united more than it has separated. the cultures that grew up around it formed the core of what was western civilization, and both shores contributed to forging identities with obvious affinities. the religious wars have dug a hole where there used to be a bridge. this bridge, which, in a way, still stands today. i hope that the european union, together with its partners, will take concrete steps to promote and structure a euro-mediterranean partnership capable of overcoming fears, differences and mistrust and of projecting itself decisively into the future. both shores of what was once the inland sea of a thriving civilization would have everything to gain from this evolution.
in writing. - the deepening of relations with the mediterranean countries is particularly important at this time, given the increasingly precarious economic and social situation in the southern countries. in this respect, i consider it urgent that concrete and effective progress be made in consolidating the union for the mediterranean. the deepening of euro-mediterranean relations is all the more urgent because of the impact it will certainly have on the consolidation of an area of peace and cultural, economic, political and social development. i would, however, stress the worries that are warranted in the situations concerning women's rights, gender equality and discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation - areas where the strengthening of european influence could be a factor in more positive developments. the enormous potential of renewable energy sources in the mediterranean region is an example of the added value that the european union can exploit and leverage for the implementation of energy efficiency policies, as well as extending the eu's trading space to 800 million people.
in writing. - we strongly disagree with the guidelines set out in this report, which essentially point to the attempt to extend the economic dominance of large eu companies over the southern part of the mediterranean, access to and control over natural resources, particularly energy, the exploitation of the labour force and the repression of immigrants. it is remarkable how the majority of meps seem to live on a glass roof, totally insensitive to the consequences of so-called free trade, insisting on these policies and thus contributing to the worsening of the situation. for example, in portugal, more than 100 000 jobs in the textile sector have disappeared, due to the closure of thousands of companies, also due to increasing external competition. the european parliament has been a great help to the people of europe in the last few years, and it is a great help to the people of europe in the future. we demand the establishment of fair and just economic relations, at the service of the peoples and countries of both regions.
in writing. - i agree with this report overall, as i believe that after the prague summit joint declaration on the eastern partnership, the eu should strengthen its partnerships to the east and specifically with the 3 countries of the south caucasus, through a clear and well-defined strategy. maintaining peace, stabilising borders and resolving border disputes, making progress towards democratization, the rule of law and promoting regional cooperation are essential for the development of this region of the world. i therefore believe that the eu should guide its action by encouraging sustainable development, based on the principles of good governance, absolute respect for human rights and good neighbourly policies, which should have peaceful coexistence between these countries and their neighbours as their main objective. in this connection, i would like to highlight the important role that the eu-eastern neighbourhood parliamentary assembly (euronest) can play. the geostrategic importance of the region, particularly in terms of the supply or transport of raw materials between east and west, should be an important element to be taken into account in the establishment of future agreements between the eu and these countries.
in writing. - the recent conflict between russia and georgia, a country which has been proclaiming its desire to join the european union and its adherence to its values, makes clear the urgency of defining a strategy for the south caucasus region. historically plagued by bloody conflicts and largely placed in the orbit of russian influence, the south caucasus has been rehearsing timid steps towards stabilisation, but remains hotbeds of potential conflict that must be treated with the utmost attention and seriousness. the tense relationship between armenia and azerbaijan is a good example of this. i hope that the european union will deepen its knowledge of this region and contribute to peace and progress among the peoples of the south caucasus, as well as to the general acceptance and respect in the region of freedom, democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law.
in writing. in the enlargement policy and in the strengthening of the european union's commercial, political and cultural relations with third countries, the strategic importance of the south caucasus countries, armenia, azerbaijan and georgia is underlined. given the geostrategic situation of these countries, which are neighbours of the powerful russia, turkey and iran, the european union can and must play a decisive role in influencing and promoting peace and security in this region, which will be decisive in ensuring the best conditions for economic, cultural and social development and the democratisation of this region, which is also surrounded by the black and caspian seas. the process of deepening relations aimed at integrating these countries into the european union will certainly contribute to strengthening the levels of justice, freedom and human progress. i also support the report's call for a strategy for the development of energy markets in the european union.
in writing. − this report on the eu strategy for the caucasus is another element of the dissemination of a narrow and very focused view of the 2008 conflict between russia and georgia and the territorial and sovereignty issues of the latter over south ossetia and abkhazia, in order to camouflage its economic and geopolitical interests in this region. what is at stake, as the report itself says, is that the three caucasus countries are essential for the transit of energy resources and the supply of the eu, on which the eu is very much dependent, free trade agreements to make the economies more attractive to foreign investors. it is on the basis of these interests that one must understand the implicit support for the relaunch of the arms race and the militaristic escalation in the region, in which the eu takes sides in the arms race between the usa, nato and russia. it is in this same vein that we can understand the hypocrisy of the majority of the ep, which is proud to defend the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states when it comes to georgia, and has promoted, supported and supports the process of kosovo's secession from serbia.

the failure of the governments of the member states to reach agreement has rendered unviable the first attempt at a community legal instrument to ensure greater uniformity in procedural safeguards throughout the union. this new gradual approach starts with the right to translation and interpretation in criminal proceedings and is the first of six measures in the roadmap. at present, the right to a written translation of important documents in the case does not exist in all member states. and even when it does exist, that right can vary considerably. for example, the right to interpretation between the suspect and his lawyer is not always guaranteed. this directive allows these rights to be conferred on any person suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the end of the proceedings. i support the agreement reached in the trilogue. the commitments made make it possible to respond to most of the concerns, both those expressed by parliament and those resulting from the commission's proposal. i congratulate commissioner reding on having put forward a good proposal in good time and i congratulate our rapporteur, baroness ludford, on the commitments she has been able to secure on most of the points. i would particularly stress the written translation of the essential documents in the case and the guarantee that the level of protection should never be lower than that provided for in the european convention on human rights and the european charter of fundamental rights. i hope that the member states will implement what has been agreed quickly and not leave the transposition of this important directive to the last minute. i was very pleased to hear commissioner reding assure me that she will immediately put forward further proposals under the road map, and i would encourage her to do so. we must make it clear that we are building a europe of justice in a coherent way and not just a europe of security and a europe of freedom. finally, i am pleased to note that all member states, with the exception of denmark, will be covered by these rules, since both the united kingdom and ireland have exercised their opt-in rights.
a free trade agreement is being concluded between the european union, colombia and peru, which further opens our market to agricultural products which are absolutely key to the outermost regions. i'm talking about the banana, the rum and the sugar. the agreement guarantees european companies easy access to the manufacturing market in these two countries and will benefit member states that export high technology and import agricultural goods. but this agreement objectively harms the outermost regions as a whole, whose vulnerability is well known. the canary islands alone lost about 20% of the market share in banana sales in the first four months of the year. but let it be clear that we are not against the agreement. the only requirement is that the impact of this agreement on the regions most affected by it - see the example of banana producers in madeira and the canary islands - be assessed and that compensatory measures be defined to minimise the damage caused.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, madam president, we are once again in a fundamental debate for the defence of the rights of road transport workers and road safety. it is unacceptable that the european commission has been insisting since october 2008 on amending the 2002 directive and now wants to exclude so-called independent drivers from its application and to worsen the working conditions of everyone, in particular by extending working hours to unbearable levels, just to facilitate greater profits for the large employers in the sector. for example, so-called self-employed drivers could be working up to 86 hours a week, all year round, which would not only jeopardise their health and safety, but would also be a danger to the road safety of all road users, and encourage social dumping and labour deregulation by multiplying the number of so-called self-employed drivers. the committee on employment and social affairs has already rejected the proposal twice, but unfortunately the rapporteur, with the support of the european commission and the council, insisted on continuing negotiations on the proposal for a directive on her own, as if the decision of the committee on employment and social affairs did not exist. so we are here in a very serious situation which must merit the clear opposition of the majority of this european parliament - which has just been called into question by the commissioner. the proposal for a rejection which we support is therefore aimed at preventing this serious threat to workers' rights and the safety of all those who travel on the roads of the european union from continuing. we therefore call for the rejection of the european commission's proposal and for compliance with the 2002 directive, which should have been applied to self-employed drivers since 2009 to combat social dumping, defend the right to health and rest for workers in the sector and improve road safety conditions.
mr president, food labelling is crucial to ensuring food safety. i am in favour of clear information for the consumer, but at the same time less red tape, simplification of regulations, greater legal certainty and increased competitiveness of the food industry, without ever forgetting small businesses. direct marketing by farmers and local and artisanal products cannot be subject to the rules of this regulation. it's products like these that ensure our diversity, that ensure our deepest roots. we must inform the consumer, but without pressuring him to make a choice, or stigmatising our regional products. the commission proposal is excessively paternalistic because it seeks to guide the consumer rather than inform him. some people want to make us the menu, some people want to tell us the dishes we can or cannot eat. i can assure you that the portuguese, and in particular the people of minho, will never stop eating the pica on the ground, the cabidela rice, they will never stop eating the green broth, the portuguese-style stew, accompanied by some good regional sweets and a red green malga. i therefore welcome the amendments, the adjustments and the work done by the rapporteur, agreeing with her position and her report and arguing that the consumer must be aware and well informed, but it is he who must decide and who has this responsibility.
mr president, good food labelling is essential. the indication of the place of origin is important, as is the indication of the fat, sugar and salt content. the information must therefore be clear, accessible to be effective and contain only the essentials, but this does not imply that certain traditional products which are, in some cases, manifestations of the culture of certain european regions cannot or should not be exempted. as regards wine, i think it should also be exempted for two reasons: the commission has already adopted a regulation on this subject. the wine contains no fat or sugar, it contains alcohol, the grading of which is already indicated on the current labelling and is even recommended as red wine by the world health organization. on the other hand, the new labels would only harm an economic sector already in serious difficulties.
in writing. the sommer report is important not only for creating informed consumers but also for avoiding market distortions and catalysing the european economy through mechanisms for transparency and uniform application of rules in the eu. i am surprised to see attempts to integrate wine into this labelling system with information on energy value and sugar content resurfacing in the form of amendments to the plenary. the wine already contains a number of mandatory labelling requirements, so adding new requirements will make it cumbersome, difficult to read and of little practical value. the special labelling requirements for wine are historically explained by the fact that wine is a highly regulated product with specific characteristics, which should benefit from this proposed derogation so that the five years of exemption allow for a prudent analysis of the references that should be on the label. the financial crisis affecting europe today calls for caution in a context where the wine sector is composed mainly of smes; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quality of the products is not compromised. in this context, i consider it inappropriate and wrong to label wine in the light of this regulation under consideration.
