in writing. − transparency on how structural funds are spent, in particular through ex post publicity of the beneficiaries, the names of operations and the amount of public funding allocated to operations, is key to the underlying debate on how to spend european public money. however, the definition of 'beneficiaries' and the amount of public funding paid to the beneficiary to be published (amounts allocated or amounts actually paid) is not clear. i welcome the recommendations in this report that they contribute to a culture of mutual trust involving all stakeholders which will contribute to a better use of european funds.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the measures proposed in this report because i believe that transparency must be a key condition for achieving the general objectives of all policies, and even more so of cohesion policies. the variability in the presentation and conditions of access to data resulting from the apparent differences between member states and managing authorities in the interpretation of the minimum requirements of the european transparency initiative does not allow for a full comparison at eu level, and i therefore welcome the introduction of clearer rules regarding the disclosure of information on beneficiaries of funds under shared management. reduced red tape, simplified procedures for obtaining funds and greater control over financial management are positive steps. i also welcome the proposal for bilingualism as regards the official dissemination by the member states of public information on the programming process for the funds. finally, i believe that the commission should set an example by adopting practices which promote transparency. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the financial interests of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the transparency of regional policy and its financing to ensure greater control over the way public funds are used. in addition to the current minimum requirements, it is urgent to ensure that the lists of beneficiaries of the structural funds published on the commission's website include more detailed information for greater transparency, such as location information, summaries of approved projects, types of support and a description of the project partners.
in writing. − regional policy and the european union's cohesion funds are fundamental to the principle of solidarity between member states. it is essential that the money allocated to them is used efficiently and in a targeted manner, contributing to the development of the areas for which it is intended. greater responsibility on the part of the member states, transparency in the use of these funds and penalties for mismanagement will lead to a further reduction of imbalances in the european union.
in writing. - given the size and regional diversity of europe and the importance of the credibility of the european institutions, i voted in favour because i believe that the sharing of public information and the homogeneity of procedures are crucial to ensure the necessary transparency in the implementation and financing of regional policies, with a view to economic and social cohesion and the strengthening of a fairer and more equitable europe. i would also stress that ensuring compliance with common rules and the publication of objective information on public investments should not entail an increase in bureaucracy. i believe that it is important to reduce it in order to improve the transparency and effectiveness of european policies.
in writing. − transparency in the use of eu funds, as well as public information of beneficiaries of eu funds, is essential for the european transparency initiative (eiti). such disclosure allows us to gauge how public money is used, which is essential for the good health of democracy and for the good management of ever-limited resources. however, at this time of crisis, other mechanisms are needed to allow for even greater transparency, in particular the prior information by the commission of decisions concerning the financing of major projects. it is therefore essential to continue to develop all available mechanisms leading to ever greater transparency with regard to all beneficiaries of european union funds. hence my vote.
in writing. − this report calls into question the transparency of the transversal guiding principle in the programming and decision-making process of cohesion policy and makes a number of technical and administrative proposals which are useful for greater effectiveness in the development of regional policy. the document, which i voted in favour of, addresses not only the issues of the wide dissemination of data on beneficiaries and the necessary reduction of administrative burdens and the speeding up of procedures, but also the issue of transparency in the partnership between the regions, the member states and the european union. on the basis of this concern, a reference is made, on the basis of an amendment which i have signed, to the need for more targeted, regular and timely information to be provided to the partner organisations, in particular through more technical assistance and training measures, which is undoubtedly useful for partners in the outermost regions of the union, such as the outermost regions.
in writing. - the peace process in northern ireland is a successful example which has earned, and should continue to earn, the support of the european institutions. as in european integration, so in post-conflict situations such as this, the path to stability will be made by establishing de facto solidarities that facilitate and increase cross-border and inter-community relations. i hope that other parts of the european union, which are plagued by the phenomena of secessionist terrorism, will be able to analyse the irish experience and learn from it lessons that will enable them to eradicate violence and build societies that everyone can call their own, with respect for the law, traditions and human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of extending the international fund for ireland, as i believe it is important to stress the european union's mission of peace between peoples and communities as a determining factor for economic and social development, as well as for the enhancement of human dignity and the quality of life of citizens. this can be seen in the case of ireland. the european union must continue to play a decisive role in maintaining peace and in eliminating regional, ethnic and cultural tensions, thus promoting conditions for social and economic progress.
in writing. - since its inception in 1986, the international fund for ireland has been helping to promote economic and social progress and to encourage contacts, dialogue and reconciliation between nationalists and unionists throughout ireland. the continuation of the peace process developing in ireland needs to continue to be supported by the eu through contributions to the international fund for ireland, support which has been available since 1989. the strengthening of this support will serve to strengthen solidarity between member states and their peoples. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it contributes to the creation of a more competitive european rail freight network. the change in the transport sector over the last decades and the increasing opening up of national rail markets (creating serious non-compliance problems) make it necessary to implement these measures which will contribute to the creation of an efficient distribution network between eu member states.
in writing. − in recent decades the railway market share in freight transport has been steadily declining, accounting for only 10% of freight transport in 2005. in an attempt to meet this challenge, the commission promoted the idea of working better on the issue by proposing in december 2008 a regulation on a european rail network for competitive freight transport. in april 2009, the european parliament adopted its first reading on the proposal, giving its support to the commission. the council also reached political agreement on this regulation, although it made some amendments. without questioning the importance of rail freight transport and the need for european coordination of this transport by supporting the creation of so-called freight corridors, the truth is that, in the current economic and financial context of the eu countries, the creation of an integrated freight transport system necessarily implies a very high level of investment by the states, which we cannot guarantee that they will be able to promote and/or ensure. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − a european rail network for competitive freight transport is essential for the eu to achieve the objectives set out in the european union strategy for jobs and growth. the creation of rail corridors that allow a rapid and efficient connection from one national network to another will therefore improve the conditions for using the infrastructure. the adoption of this regulation is essential to make rail freight transport more competitive than currently used, thus bringing not only economic but also environmental benefits, as rail transport is environmentally friendly. hence my vote.
in writing. - although freight transport has been in decline for several years, it remains the safest and most efficient alternative to road transport, among others. this report proposes to try to increase the market share of rail by creating corridors between at least two member states so that goods can move quickly. i have read it and i do not believe that the creation of these corridors will give priority to goods rather than passenger transport, and i do not therefore believe that there is any difference in treatment between the two types of rail traffic. the one-stop-shop may be of strategic coordination importance, since it will be the place where the management of the track orders will take place. the council's position has reduced it to an information desk, but my view is contrary to that of the rapporteur, who considers it to be essential to achieving the desired flow of goods. this network of corridors will allow for better synchronisation of european rail services, create interfaces between the different modes of transport and provide a new impetus for sectoral investment, and therefore deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of this proposal to adapt the rules of procedure of the european parliament to the treaty of lisbon. more powers for the european parliament must also mean more responsibility! the lisbon treaty is essential, since the european union needs to combine enlargement with deepening. and with this treaty it has done so in a balanced, credible and fair way, improving the coherence, legitimacy, democratic nature, effectiveness and transparency of the decision-making process, clarifying the division of powers between the union and the member states, and contributing to a more efficient inter- and intra-institutional relations within the union. the compromise amendments reached with this adaptation of the rules of procedure to the treaty of lisbon are largely the result of the epp's efforts to clarify and simplify the decision-making process of this parliament and its relationship with national parliaments.
in writing. − the large production of legislation by the european institutions and the participatory method in which this production takes place, the profusion of documentation which they repeatedly incur and the fact that the hierarchies between sources and legal rules are not always clear make it essential for the european parliament to mitigate these risks by making an effort to bring its statute into line with the recent treaty of lisbon. i believe that this was necessary in the interests of clarity of procedure and legal certainty.
in writing. - the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon requires the european parliament to adapt to the new conditions of functioning and sharing of responsibilities in decision-making processes. i would stress the impact of the strengthening of the european parliament's powers, the new composition of the national representations and the introduction of a closer relationship with the national parliaments. i support the amendments to the rules of procedure now proposed, considering also the simplification and clear definition of the regulatory procedures to improve the capacity to respond to the needs of citizens, institutions and member states, while ensuring conditions for the efficient implementation of european policies.
in writing. - the adoption of the treaty of lisbon has brought new responsibilities to the european parliament, which requires the adaptation of its rules of procedure to the new rules. this regulation thus adapts the rules of procedure of the european parliament to the new challenges posed by the treaty of lisbon. hence my vote.
in writing. the european parliament has already adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, which calls for the immediate release of all political prisoners. this is a necessary adaptation of the rules of procedure of the european parliament after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. after a first vote at the november part-session, which secured the necessary amendments directly related to the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the other amendments were postponed for an extended period of reflection. the ppe, the group to which the psd belongs, signed several compromise amendments, notably concerning the question period to the president of the commission and the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and the president of the eurogroup, the implementation of the statute for members, the revision of the treaties and delegated acts. i would like to stress, however, the amendments concerning interparliamentary cooperation, the european parliament's relationship with national parliaments in the course of the legislative process and the composition of the european parliament's delegation to cosac, three subjects to which i had to devote special attention as vice-president of the european people's party with responsibility for relations with national parliaments.
in writing. the european parliament voted today on the necessary adjustment of its rules of procedure following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. after the vote at the november partsession, the vote on the other amendments not directly related to the entry into force of the treaty was postponed until this part-session. twelve compromise amendments were signed with the group of the european people's party, to which i belong, on a number of subjects: the question period to the president of the commission and the high representative of the union, written questions to the council and the commission, regular interparliamentary cooperation, the implementation of the statute for members, the delegation to cosac, the revision of the treaties and the delegation of legislative power. i am voting in favour of the other amendments to the document, including the introduction of a provision on subsidiarity and proportionality in the examination of legislative acts and on the relationship between the european parliament and national parliaments in the course of the legislative process.
in writing. − one of the key objectives for 2011 will be to maintain, promote and achieve funding for research and technological development in the union by adequately funding the framework programme, thus contributing to the europe 2020 strategy. the increase in the number of applications for funding has increased in proportion to the increase in the control mechanisms in an attempt to ensure the correct use of community funds. internal bureaucracy and the creation of more administrative rules and procedures reduce trust in the process. it is particularly difficult for smaller organisations - such as smes, high-tech start-ups, smaller institutes, universities and research centres - to cope with such complexity. i call for a simplification of access to research funding. a culture of mutual trust involving all stakeholders needs to be developed. this will boost research and innovation, making europe a more attractive place to live and work.
in writing. - the role of the european parliament in the negotiation of the community budget is strengthened by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. in the current economic, financial and social crisis, it is essential to allocate funds to stimulate growth and competitiveness in the union. in this context, it is important that the union's solidarity funds be strengthened, assuming effective use by governments, in order to mitigate the impact of this crisis in the most disadvantaged regions.
in writing. − i would remind you that the 2011 budgetary procedure is the first of its kind since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and that its single reading requires greater cooperation and coordination with the other branch of the budgetary authority. i would stress the concern and the effort to ensure adequate funding for the european union's strategic development priorities, particularly in the areas of youth and innovation, alongside energy efficiency, combating climate change, promoting employment and gender equality. i also believe that it is essential to ensure the viability of mechanisms which guarantee the sustainability of the agricultural sector. i would like to make a special reference to the dairy sector. in the current context of crisis and of severe pressure on the public finances of the member states, i stress the need to ensure the budgetary sustainability of the european union with a view to pursuing the central objective of social and economic cohesion. however, i consider it important that the draft budget for 2011 already reflects the financial implications of the flagship initiatives of the eu 2020 strategy, such as 'innovation union', 'youth on the move', 'a resource efficient europe', 'new skills and jobs' and 'an industrial policy for the age of globalisation'.
in writing. - we voted against this report on the draft budget for the financial year 2011 because it does not correspond in the least to the needs of the european union's financing today, where the creation of the eurozone has exacerbated social and territorial inequalities, without taking due account of the principle of economic and social cohesion. in a situation of crisis, the need is even more acute for another community budget which would at least double the amount of money to allocate at least half of this budget (calculated on the basis of 2% of community gnp) to investments in the productive sector and to support the social functions of the states, in order to create more jobs with rights, to combat poverty and to reduce territorial inequalities in order to promote economic and social cohesion. on the other hand, it is also essential to increase the rates of community co-financing for the countries with weaker economies, in particular for programmes in the social field and productive investment. finally, the amounts allocated to the military area must be substantially reduced and the central objectives of the budget must be changed in order to achieve balanced development and social progress.
in writing. − the draft budget for 2011 will be the first since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and its preparation requires greater cooperation and coordination between all parties involved in its negotiation in order to reach an agreement on all expenditure during the merger process. the trialogue to be held in july should be unequivocal in paving the way, so that points where there should be greater consensus are identified in advance. the main points to be considered will be the budgetary implications of the european stabilisation mechanism, the eu 2020 strategy and youth-related programmes.
in writing. − in this parliament's response to the 2011 draft budget proposed by the european commission, i support my group's view that it is impossible to clearly define the implications of the draft budget for the flagship initiatives of the strategy and that more and better information is needed. i also welcome the inclusion of the youth programme as one of the priorities for next year in the commission's draft, but i regret that the increase in appropriations for this area was symbolic, when more of these initiatives should be expected. since i consider it unacceptable that the 2011 budget for posei should be less than in 2010, especially at a time when the conclusion of the agreement between the eu and colombia and peru will have serious repercussions on the production of bananas, sugar and rum in the outermost regions, i supported an amendment with the members of the outermost regions, which also calls on the commission to promote, as soon as possible, a study of the impact of this situation in these regions.
in writing. - stronger regulation of derivatives markets should take account of the special situation of firms which must continue to hedge their financial and operational risks on favourable terms and in an appropriate way with the help of derivatives. non-financial corporations use these instruments to hedge currency, interest and commodity risks. this non-speculative protection contributes to the creation of stability and growth in employment and investment. however, the proposed regulatory measures should not lead to a manifest deterioration in the risk coverage of companies. i call for derogations and lower capital requirements to be allowed, especially for smes, in the case of bilateral derivatives.
in writing. - the derivatives market, as the economic, financial and social crisis has shown, needs effective regulation to make the trading of these financial instruments more transparent. these products should be subject to more effective supervision so that their transaction does not have adverse effects on the market. on the other hand, because of the variety of derivatives and the necessary protection of investors, i support stricter information rules.
in writing. − i welcome the mobilisation of the european institutions to ensure the best efficiency, security and soundness of derivatives markets, recognising their importance for the sustainability of economic development and the need to ensure the regulation and verification of the procedures and transactions linked to the transaction or trading of these financial instruments. in view of the size of the derivatives market and its impact on the global economy as evidenced by the current economic and financial crisis and the exponential increase in the risk component in the global market, i consider it essential to ensure transparency, for which not only the effectiveness of market supervision is essential, but also clear, concise and complete information standards. credit default swaps of sovereign issuers used by financial speculators have led to unjustified levels of various national spreads. this highlights the need for market transparency and stronger european regulation in relation to the trading of credit default swaps, particularly those linked to sovereign debt. future legislation is expected to bring not only transparency to derivatives markets but also robust regulation. i would stress that the costs of future market infrastructures should be borne by market participants and not by taxpayers.
in writing. - instead of proposing the end of the derivatives market, the majority of the european parliament simply defended the prohibition of speculative trading in credit default swaps (cds) of sovereign debt, urging the commission to consider risk ceilings for derivatives, particularly cds, and to agree on them with international partners. the commission is expected to present its proposal on derivatives markets in september, but the ep will legislate on the subject on an equal footing with the council. all this waiting is regrettable when one sees the sharp rise in the implicit interest rates of the bonds of sovereign issuers in some euro zone countries to unsustainable levels, knowing the negative role that credit default swaps have played in the whole process. speculative bonds based on sovereign debt cannot be allowed any longer. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. we therefore support the positive proposals, but we are against the backward position and the enormous delay in the regulation of the capital market.
in writing. − derivatives have historically played an important role in the transfer of risk in the economy. however, the lack of transparency and regulation of the derivatives market had a very pernicious effect on the financial crisis. one of the instruments that has affected european economies the most and led to the rise in sovereign debt interest rates was the cds (credit default swaps). this regulation advocates the prohibition of speculative trading in this instrument, as it may lead to distortions of sovereign debt markets. it is of paramount importance to distinguish between derivative products used as a risk management tool to hedge a real underlying risk to which the entity is exposed and derivatives used solely for speculative purposes. hence my vote.
in writing. - i welcome the broad lines of the communication presented by the commission. the development of new applications and the very functioning of the 'internet of things', as well as the strong impact it will have on the daily lives and habits of european citizens, will be closely linked to the trust that european consumers place in the system. it is essential to ensure a regulatory and legal framework that protects the european consumer and promotes public and private investment in the iot sector. the 'internet of things' is a major economic opportunity, as it will allow the optimisation of production processes and energy consumption, as well as the creation of new jobs and new services for an increasing number of european citizens and businesses. if the european union is to become a true leader in this market, it must take a proactive approach in this area, stimulating research and pilot projects.
in writing. − the rapid and uninterrupted growth of the internet means that at present some 1.5 billion people are connected via computers and mobile devices. the next step is leading to a gradual transformation of a network of interconnected computers into a network of interconnected objects - the internet of things - from books to cars, from household appliances to food (e.g. a refrigerator programmed to recognise expired or nearly expired products). such technological innovations can help to meet the diverse expectations of society and citizens, and act as a catalyst for growth and innovation, bringing benefits in terms of the economy and the well-being of the population. however, it needs to be regulated in a precise and comprehensive way to enable the internet of things to meet the challenges of trust, acceptance and security. it is essential to ensure full respect for privacy and the protection of personal data and to put in place appropriate measures to protect data against possible misuse and other risks associated with personal data. i therefore support this proactive approach, without forgetting that the internet of things is essentially an internet of things for people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the badia i cutchet report for supporting the creation of an 'internet of things'. i believe that new information technologies have significant benefits for our society, but it is important to ensure that any potential impacts on health and the environment, as well as aspects relating to the protection of privacy, are taken into account.
in writing. − the internet has become part of the daily lives of millions of people and today plays an irreplaceable role as a means of communication and a vehicle for the transmission of information and knowledge. the exponential growth of content hosted on the internet makes it a tool of multiple and growing uses and, at the same time, the scene of a new type of crime that takes advantage of the speed and dematerialization of information flows and the massive volume of personal data made available by network users. i share the concerns expressed in the resolution about the need to address politically motivated restrictions on internet access and to allow for safer use of the internet by children and adolescents. i share the view that the day-to-day use and management of the network should be left to the private sector, but i believe that the states cannot avoid having a present and active regulatory role, aimed above all at preventing abuses and violations of citizens' rights.
in writing. − the impact of new technologies on people's safety and quality of life has become unavoidable, highlighting the simultaneous benefits and risks they bring. the internet of things is a new set of added value for human life, but this does not prevent the recognition of any risks inherent in a tool with great potential. i would stress the need to encourage research and the launching of pilot projects, and to take advantage of the opportunities that are now arising, particularly in optimising energy savings, in production processes, in creating new jobs and new challenges. however, it is crucial that the union has a common framework of reference to frame or strengthen the provisions on system governance, confidentiality, information security, ethical management, privacy, collection and storage of personal data and consumer information. the rapid evolution of the internet of things requires a government for the internet of things that is secure, transparent and multilateral. i therefore share the commission's concern with regard to the security, protection of personal data and privacy of citizens, as well as the governance of the internet of things, for reasons of respect for privacy and protection of personal data.
in writing. the internet of things is a project that started in 1999 in the united states. it is gaining increasing popularity and is expected to revolutionize person-thing-thing interaction over the next ten to fifteen years through the increasing use of rfid (radio frequency identification) technology. the development of the internet of things, with all the innovations and positives it can bring to our daily lives, still has a wide margin of uncertainty, both conceptually and technically, which is worthy of some concern. the technology behind this step is called rfid, a tag, which is an electronic component consisting of a chip and an antenna. the chip, which is only a few millimeters wide, can hold, receive and transmit information without wired connections, which raises various problems related to ownership, management, privacy, etc. the rapporteur, mr van den broek, has already made a number of suggestions for improving the quality of the information provided by the commission. however, we have serious doubts about the management of this data. we are on a somewhat unclear path, which is why we abstained from voting.
in writing. − the role of so-called information and communication technologies (ict) in promoting social development, economic growth, research and innovation and creativity in european public and private bodies has been important. the rapid evolution of the internet in recent years has led to new concerns and the need for the european union to have a common framework of reference to frame and strengthen existing provisions on governance of the system, in particular with regard to confidentiality, information security, ethics management, privacy, collection and storage of personal data and consumer information. it is therefore very important that the governance of the internet of things is concerned with respecting the security, data protection and privacy of those who use it, as this is the only way to bring benefits to eu citizens. hence my vote.
in writing. − the internet is a 'global public good' whose unilateral management and control by a single government has been the subject of numerous criticisms. the european union should develop a strategy that reflects a consensus view of the fundamental aspects of internet governance and that can be strongly defended in international forums and in its bilateral relations with the united states. i support the european commission's favourable position towards the current management model based on private sector leadership. i also call for the participation of developing countries to be improved, in particular by financing their participation.
in writing. − the internet has had a huge impact on society and citizens' lives over the last twenty years. the eu is a good example of this, as although it represents just over 7% of the world's population, it has almost 19% of the world's internet users. internet governance has been at the forefront of public policy priorities, seeking to ensure that citizens can benefit fully from the potential of the internet, while seeking to find the best solutions to tackle the problem of inappropriate or illegal content, as well as to adequately protect consumers and try to resolve issues of jurisdiction in a global online world. i fully agree that the internet is a global public good, which should always defend and respect the public interest. it is essential that the eu develops a strategy on the key aspects of internet governance and i support the spanish presidency's initiative to draft a 'european charter of the rights of internet users'. it is important to reform icann internally to give it a more representative structure, with more control from the international community, with more accountability and transparency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on internet governance, which involves sensitive issues such as the protection and guarantee of fundamental rights and freedoms, access to and use of the internet and cybercrime. the spanish presidency's proposals for a european charter of the rights of internet users and for the recognition of a fifth fundamental freedom (freedom of access to the network) could provide the eu with more effective instruments to ensure greater protection of security-related aspects and pluralistic and non-discriminatory access to the network.
in writing. - the public role of the internet and the way it influences not only everyday life but also mass movements, political initiatives and communication strategies is now undeniable. it is legitimate to say that the internet has an irreplaceable public role and that this cannot be neglected by the member states of the european union, which must demand greater access and participation in the governance of the internet without thereby calling into question the leading role of the private sector in the daily use and management of the network, which has proved essential for its vitality and growth. the role of states is becoming more relevant, as are issues relating to cybercrime and the protection of users' security and privacy, as well as citizens' freedom of access and expression via the internet.
in writing. − given the increasingly dominant role of the internet in the daily lives of citizens and institutions and even in the governance of different countries, as well as its impact on economic, cultural, social and human development, internet governance is assumed as a matter of paramount importance in the global world. it is therefore of the utmost importance that the european union should ensure that the conditions are right for active intervention in this area, in order to defend the public good and its values and principles. in this context, i voted in favour of this report, stressing the importance of widening the representation of global diversity in the entities that currently control the internet market, such as the internet corporation for assigned names and numbers (icann) and the internet assigned numbers authority (iana).
in writing. - this report takes as a starting point the important role of the internet, which has become an indispensable instrument for promoting democratic initiatives, political debate, digital literacy and the dissemination of knowledge. access to the internet simultaneously guarantees and depends on the exercise of a number of fundamental rights, including respect for privacy, data protection, freedom of expression and association, freedom of the press, political expression and participation, non-discrimination, education and cultural and linguistic diversity. it therefore stresses that the institutions and stakeholders at all levels have a general responsibility to ensure that everyone can exercise their right to participate in the information society. it also addresses the threats that cybercrime is posing to societies that use ict, noting the increase in incitement to terrorist attacks, hate crimes and child pornography, putting people, including children, at risk, and states that 'the role of public actors in shaping a global strategy needs to be strengthened'. the commission is also concerned about the unrepresentative structure of the internet corporation for assigned names and numbers (icann) and the limited scrutiny that the international community, including the eu, exercises over the functioning of icann.
in writing. - the internet is now a global instrument and its management should therefore be guided by the common interest. the internet is today one of the main means of spreading democratic values in the world, and is an indispensable instrument in promoting all kinds of initiatives, political debate and the dissemination of knowledge. the development of the internet is therefore essential if it is to be made more equitable for everyone in the eu. it is also essential that it is safe for all its users, in particular for children who are less able to defend themselves against the potential dangers of its use. we must therefore prevent the governance of the internet from being dominated by any single entity or group of entities, so that it maintains its status as a global public good. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, but i would point out that access to innovation in certain regions, particularly the outermost regions, is subject to certain conditions. in order to promote better use of the potential of these regions in areas such as research or innovation, account should be taken of the difficulties linked to the lack of critical mass. the unique geographical and climatic characteristics of the octs provide specific advantages for the development of certain actions in the fields of biodiversity, marine resources, climate change, renewable energy and water, environment, natural resources, health and new technologies. in the field of natural resources and biodiversity in particular, the outermost regions provide european research with privileged access to tropical ecosystems with unique biodiversity and agriculture, which allow research in the context of the european research area as natural laboratories. they are also places for experimentation. despite the potential of many regions and all efforts, many regions continue to have more difficulty than others in improving the factors that contribute to competition, growth and employment, as set out in the lisbon strategy, especially in the context of r & d & i.
in writing. − an innovation policy must address the major societal challenges we face, bringing together all relevant actors. investment in knowledge and reforms to promote technological progress, research, innovation, education and training is essential to promote prosperity, growth and employment in the medium to long term. the fight against new challenges requires innovative initiatives in the application of new technologies but also requires innovative initiatives in the social field, at the level of the organization. i call for efforts to be made to move from technological innovation to social innovation, public service innovation and regional innovation.
in writing. the importance of knowledge and innovation is gaining prominence in the political agenda and jargon, and few today dare to question the importance of investing in this field and the need to link knowledge, innovation, enterprises and employment. the risk of unanimity around the concept is, however, that it will be emptied, as has happened with other trends such as the environment or the sustainability of the economy or support for entrepreneurship. these themes fill pages of manifestos and election programmes and almost always end up losing their distinctive character, being mere statements of fact. in this respect, and despite the government's serious efforts in some areas, i cannot help but point out the negative aspects of the technological populism from which the prime minister of portugal seems to suffer. it would be better if he paid more attention to the content and less to the form in which he proclaims the improvement of working conditions and scientific production and if he remembered that competitive effort requires ambition but realism.
in writing. - the decisive role of innovation in the success and sustainability of economic and social development and the success of european integration is now widely accepted. the importance of innovation, which is necessarily linked to research and education and never separated from them, is becoming even more evident in the face of the increasingly rapid pace of global and human evolution. in this sense, i support this report for the review of community innovation policy, stressing the urgent need for the european union to coordinate efforts to boost resources in this area. i would also stress the importance of encouraging private initiative and of a comprehensive, cross-cutting strategy in the priority implementation of european innovation policy.
in writing. - we agree with several aspects of this report, although its wording does not always focus on the most important issues. for example, we agree that innovation is one of the elements, not the element, in overcoming the challenges that are currently being posed, both at the global social and environmental level and at other levels equally important to society. but the priority given to each of the areas in the europe 2020 strategy, such as entrepreneurship, competitiveness, climate change, employment, demographic change and an inclusive society, leaves the documentation and analysis of the needs for innovation in a changing world far behind what would be needed to promote genuine economic and social cohesion, productivity growth, job creation in the member states and their wage appreciation, which we consider to be fundamental. that is why we abstained. in its communication of 2 september 2009 entitled 'review of community innovation policy in a changing world', the european commission outlined the developments in eu innovation policy since 2005. it is now expected to take up and implement some aspects of the proposed innovation action plan which is due to be presented shortly.
in writing. − innovation, together with research and training, is one of the most important aspects of the development of knowledge in the eu. a community innovation policy is of great relevance to achieving the objectives outlined in the eu 2020 strategy. however, the capacity for innovation, particularly in enterprises, lacks financial resources which are not easily available to enterprises, especially smes, at the moment. the adoption of this regulation is thus an important step towards supporting entrepreneurs as the driving force of innovation in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the eradication of poverty to be of the utmost importance. since poverty eradication is the main objective set by the lisbon treaty for eu cooperation and development policy and since it is a moral duty whose long-term usefulness to the eu's interests is vital, i consider it crucial that this objective be a priority in our foreign policy. it is also important to stress that, despite the deep economic crisis in europe and the world, we cannot and must not neglect external aid, which is essential for the creation of a more just and united world. considering that the objectives set out at the 2000 millennium summit, where we committed to improve our action on poverty reduction, are still far from being achieved, and that the year 2015 - the target for achieving those objectives - is approaching by leaps and bounds, it is of the utmost urgency to examine distinct factors aimed at maximising the outcomes of the millennium development goals. i would like to take this opportunity to express my support for this project.
in writing. - i welcome the role that europe has played as the world's largest contributor to development aid. development aid has helped to alleviate poverty for millions of people in the developing world. extreme poverty has fallen from 1.8 billion to 1.4 billion people. nearly 90 percent of poor children are in school today. great strides have been made in the fight against malaria and tuberculosis, and child mortality is falling by the rocks. however, the recent food and fuel crises and the global economic downturn have reversed much of the progress made over the past decade. rich countries are responsible for the current financial, economic and climate crises, but developing countries are the most affected by global warming, and it is therefore essential to step up all measures to combat climate change, such as the transfer of appropriate technologies. i call for additional funds to be allocated to developing countries and for these to be sustainable in the medium and long term, from the private sector, the carbon market and the public sector of industrialised countries and economically more advanced developing countries.
in writing. − the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) plays a key role in development policy. with only a few months to go until the un summit, despite significant progress on some of the mdgs, the truth is that we are still far from where we want to be. it takes more: member states must meet their commitments on oda, new financing mechanisms need to be explored (which do not translate into more taxes in this time of crisis), and above all, policy coherence for development is essential (following the resolution adopted in may this year on the coherence of eu policies in a development perspective and 'the concept of public aid for more development'). i welcome the fact that the ep has set as priority mdg targets health, education, the most vulnerable groups and poverty eradication through concrete measures in trade, agriculture and fisheries policies; and also with the demand for a new global governance that gives more voice to developing countries and promotes democracy, peace, the rule of law in developing countries. i am, however, against abortion being considered as a means of contraception.
in writing. - "if you're going to san francisco, be sure to wear some flowers in your hair, if you're going to san francisco, you're gonna meet some gentle people there" proclaimed scott mackenzie! but that is not the world, nor can this message be applied to the complex economic and social reality of today's world! that is why i voted against this report, without, of course, calling into question the goodness of its aims! "imagine there's no countries, it isn't hard to do, nothing to kill or die for, and no religion too. imagine all the people living life in peace". but it was the same john lennon who added "you may say i'm a dreamer"... unfortunately, this is not the reality! but it is up to us to make the world a fairer and safer place, where everyone can live with at least a modicum of dignity. the proposals in this report are intended to pursue multiple objectives, without focusing on or defining effective priorities, 'firing' in all directions, which does not make them feasible. finally, they seem to me to be too state-centred and too centralised in the central public administrations. i disagree with this philosophy. on the contrary, i believe that the mdgs should be based on community-based projects (e.g. millennium villages), with strong involvement of all community actors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the cashman report because we still have a long way to go to achieve the millennium development goals. it is necessary to strengthen existing measures in order to achieve them by 2015, in particular by fulfilling the responsibilities assumed by member states in relation to aid to developing countries. i welcome the adoption of paragraph 42 which calls on the member states and the commission to reverse the worrying decline in funding for sexual and reproductive health and rights in developing countries and to support policies on voluntary family planning, safe abortion, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and the provision of reproductive health facilities such as life-saving medicines and contraceptives, including condoms.
in writing. − the eradication of poverty and the reduction of the gap between rich and poor are important objectives to which all governments should devote attention and resources. the un adopted them at the 2000 millennium summit, and the european union, as the largest donor, has an important stake in the outcome of this collective effort. despite all the efforts of developed countries, many of which are facing crises that could undermine their commitment, the responsibility lies with recipient states who must be able to meet their responsibilities for good governance, the rule of law and essential civil liberties. i cannot but regret that the rapporteur, in the face of his good intentions, is trying to get the house to adopt a resolution which, in flagrant violation of the powers of the member states and third countries in these matters, advocates the promotion of abortion as a means of achieving the millennium goals. the tactic employed is not new, but the stealthy method is no less reprehensible.
in writing. − the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) has been a key commitment of the international community. europe is the leading international donor. this funding to developing countries has helped alleviate poverty, reduce mortality and improve the skills of millions of people. in fact, extreme poverty has declined, almost 90 percent of poor children are in school, and infant mortality is dropping exponentially. there is still much to be done, much support to be given so that the least developed countries achieve the mdgs of poverty eradication or access to education and health. europe, as a defender of fundamental rights, human rights, and with solidarity as a principle and as the world's largest contributor of development aid, must take a leading role in this matter and, in particular, in the next un review meeting to be held in september. i regret that this report has mixed noble aims with sensitive issues of individual conscience, such as abortion. the promotion of policies in support of abortion does not serve the achievement of the mdgs. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − the initial objective of the millennium declaration in 2000 was, inter alia, to 'reduce by half the percentage of people living in extreme poverty, provide safe drinking water and education for all, reverse the trend of the spread of hiv/aids'. we are far from achieving these objectives - which were already limited in themselves - a situation which the report acknowledges. the eu as a whole has been cutting its aid budgets, while its countries have recently spent billions of dollars to bail out their banks, passing the bill on to the people, leaving the economic and financial groups holding them untouched. the text contains, however, some contradictions which we consider important to point out, in particular when it criticises the liberalisation of trade and at the same time supports opening up to trade through the conclusion of the doha round in the wto and accepts the economic partnership agreements (epas) and free trade areas (ftas). trade liberalisation accentuates inequalities, creating greater exploitation of workers and natural resources, more poverty and social exclusion, and increases relations of dependency between countries. sacrificing development aid to these goals, as the eu and the us have done, means that the mdgs will not be achieved in 2015.
in writing. − the eu remains the main driver of the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) and the largest donor in the world, so it has to assume its responsibilities and play a leading role at the un high level meeting in september 2010. the achievement of the mdgs, including poverty eradication, will be very important in ending the suffering of millions of people around the world. it is important, however, to point out that, once again, covertly and under the pretext of fighting poverty, there is a desire to insert subtle references to the background of fracturing matters which are not taken up with the justified visibility, in particular in the abortion policy in developing countries.

inequalities that persist in real life, such as the problem of difficulty in accessing employment with decent rights and wages, poverty, the maintenance of discrimination and stereotypes that wages, pensions and pensions below the minimum subsistence income and difficulties in accessing quality public services. the current economic and social crisis has particularly serious consequences for women, exacerbating inequalities and discrimination. this is the case of the gender pay gap, which averages more than 17%, and of indirect discrimination, which tends to intensify when unemployment rises and affects women and young girls. even the jobs created in recent years, especially those for young people and women, have been mostly precarious and poorly paid, with no respect for fundamental rights, particularly in the area of maternity, which has also contributed to the low birth rate. the multiple discrimination against specific sectors of women, including older women, the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner malmström, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to make four points of importance. first, the evaluation procedure. since their accession to the european union in 2007, romania and bulgaria have started working towards their full integration into the schengen area. in order for the council to take a decision to abolish internal borders, it is necessary that the evaluation procedures certify all the necessary conditions for the application of the relevant parts of the community acquis, namely data protection, the schengen information system, air, land and sea borders, police cooperation and visa policy. the evaluation procedures started with the data protection part. the aim is to verify that each of these member states is sufficiently prepared to implement all the data protection provisions. the results obtained are therefore a precondition for the evaluation process concerning the schengen information system, which implies the transfer of x data to these countries. the adoption of this decision is thus a first step towards the abolition of checks at the internal borders with bulgaria and romania. secondly, access to documents. the council forwarded this draft decision to the european parliament. however, no evaluation reports and follow-up reports were sent which would have allowed parliament to have access to all the information necessary to draw up a reasoned and reasoned opinion. it was only after parliament's insistence that the documents were handed over by the council. i am grateful to the romanian ambassador for his efforts in finding a solution to this situation by asking for the classified documents to be declassified and the term 'limited' to be adopted. this solution has made it possible to meet the timetable, but we will have the same problem when the european parliament is asked for its opinion on the other aspects of the schengen acquis. it is therefore necessary to conclude the agreement between the european parliament and the council on the transfer of confidential documents as soon as possible. thirdly, the evaluation of romania and bulgaria. in relation to bulgaria, shortcomings were identified in the adoption, implementation and application of council of europe recommendation 85/15 on the use of personal data in the police sector and weaknesses were found in the activity of the national data protection board. bulgaria has duly followed up these recommendations and the council concluded on 26 april that the necessary conditions in terms of data recovery had been met. in relation to romania, weaknesses were identified in relation to the adoption of two laws regulating the processing of personal data, as well as in relation to the facilities and resources of the national data protection authority, and the introduction of periodic assessments in relation to schengen data. romania has generally followed up the recommendations adequately and the recommendations still pending do not prevent romania from properly implementing all the necessary requirements with regard to data protection. the conditions are thus being fulfilled for us to give the green light to romania and bulgaria in the field of data protection. finally, mr president, there is the review of the schengen evaluation mechanism. i would like to take this opportunity to recall the need to establish as soon as possible a european evaluation mechanism that is simple and effective, efficient and transparent in the schengen evaluation area. parliament rejected the proposals put to it last october. i ask the commission to exercise its right of initiative as soon as possible.

in writing. the baltic sea has experienced periods of great prosperity and activity, such as the heyday of the hanseatic league, which allowed for the fruitful exchange of people, goods and knowledge between different territories belonging to different nations. these exchanges helped to strengthen the links between the league's cities and fostered the emergence of de facto solidarities such as those that, centuries later, schuman would advocate as the best method of making europe. the particular semi-enclosed shape of the baltic sea and the flow of vessels that ply it have led to the accumulation of large quantities of pollutants from various sources, which must be removed urgently or else the entire ecosystem of the region will be threatened. the european union should contribute to the implementation of projects aimed at promoting maritime research and development and the baltic sea. given the particularly serious circumstances affecting him, it should be a priority.
in writing. − the baltic sea and its coast have been plagued by problems of pollution, acidification and loss of natural resources and biodiversity. in order to reduce pollution in the baltic sea, eight eu member states, denmark, estonia, finland, germany, latvia, lithuania, poland and sweden, will implement a baltic sea development programme called 'bonus'. this programme aims to support scientific development and innovation by providing the necessary legal and organisational framework for transnational cooperation between the baltic states in the field of environmental research in the baltic sea region, which is in line with the eu2020 objectives for research and knowledge. the eu contribution shall be up to eur 50 million for the entire implementation period, equivalent to the contribution of the participating states, in order to promote their interest in the joint implementation of the programme. i welcome the financial support of the european commission for this programme and especially the fact that the participating member states will ensure the sustainability of this programme even after eu funding. for these reasons i voted in favour.

in writing. − the gnss agency (european global navigation satellite system) (the agency) is hereby established, which replaces the european gnss supervisory authority (the authority) established by council regulation (ec) no 1321/2004 (the regulation) on the management structures for european satellite radio navigation programmes. this change is due to the fact that several of the authority's functions are now carried out by the european commission. it is therefore necessary to revise the regulation to take account of the fact that the agency is no longer responsible for the management of the public interest relating to the european global navigation satellite system (gnss) and for the regulation of those programmes.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 683/2008 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 july 2008 on the further implementation of the european satellite navigation programmes (egnos and galileo) sets out the new framework for the public governance and funding of the galileo and egnos programmes. it provides for the principle of a strict division of powers between the european community, represented by the commission, the authority and the european space agency, and makes the commission responsible for the management of the programmes. furthermore, the regulation provides that the authority shall carry out the tasks assigned to it in respect of the management role played by the commission and shall act in accordance with the guidelines developed by the commission, which has the obligation to inform the european parliament and the council of the consequences of the adoption of accreditation decisions for the harmonious development of the programmes. i think it is important that the member states and the commission are represented on the management board, which has the powers to draw up the budget, monitor its implementation, adopt the appropriate financial rules, establish a transparent procedure for decision-making by the agency, approve the work programme and appoint the executive director.
, in writing. − amendments to regulation (ec) no 683/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on the further implementation of the european satellite navigation programmes (egnos and galileo) were adopted, which sets out the new framework for public governance and funding of these programmes. it provides for the principle of the division of competences between the european community, represented by the commission, the authority and the european space agency, and makes the commission responsible for the management of the programmes. in order to ensure that the agency carries out its tasks in respect of the role of programme manager of the commission and in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the commission, it has been expressly provided that the agency is managed by its executive director, under the direction of the management board, in accordance with the guidelines laid down for the agency by the commission, and that the representative of the commission on the management board of the agency has 30% of the voting rights. given that the management board must adopt its decisions by a two-thirds majority, the commission, with one-third of the votes, may, with the support of at least one member state, block any decision of the management board which is not in accordance with the commission's guidelines. since we have doubts about what is proposed, we have opted to abstain in the final vote.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, considering its implications for the future commission budget and the contribution that space activities can make to the 2020 strategy for innovative high-tech growth, skilled employment and european cohesion. the potential of a programme like gmes - as is the case with the excellent work being carried out in the azores - to support biodiversity, ecosystem management, adaptation to climate change, the provision of rapid emergency response services, land and marine monitoring or even support for transport policy, not to mention the security aspect it provides, particularly in border control and marine surveillance, must be recognised. it should be noted that these services are crucial for a 'new economy' in a number of remote, island and outermost regions which, by relying on these types of technologies, which are likely to be 'exported', are contributing not only to the creation of added value for these nereus regions, but also to the creation of skilled employment and the increase in the attractiveness of these same regions through science and technology, while waiting for the establishment of cadres and new companies.
in writing. − i welcome the eu's strategic decision to develop a european earth observation facility dedicated to environmental and security areas, led by the eu in partnership with member states and the european space agency, with the aim of promoting better exploitation of the industrial potential of policies for innovation, research and technological development in the field of earth observation. gmes can bring tangible benefits to europeans in terms of jobs, competence, safety and environmental protection. it is also fully compatible with the eu2020 strategy and the post-copenhagen strategies. gmes is a key tool in support of biodiversity, ecosystem management and climate change mitigation. it will contribute to greater security, for example by providing information on natural disasters such as forest fires or floods. it will also help to improve the management of natural resources, to monitor the quality of water and air, to plan cities, to facilitate the flow of transport, to optimise our agricultural activities and to promote renewable energy. i believe that i have the potential to significantly improve the living conditions of our generation and our children's generation.
in writing. - space policy has been elevated by the present commission to the status of a key sector in the future of the european union. the european earth observation programme, in this context, could be a challenge for the european union by fostering the development of its industrial strategy (in particular the space industry), by creating benefits for citizens in terms of job creation and the development of research for innovation, by improving environmental research and the safety of citizens and, finally, by creating synergies with other sectors, which could create interesting opportunities for smes. the development of this programme, which is the responsibility of the commission, requires additional budgetary resources, which is why we believe that this should be carefully assessed when the multiannual financial framework is revised.
in writing. − the regulation on the european earth observation programme (gmes) and its initial operations is designed to provide europe with its own earth observation capability in the fields of environment and security. gmes, like the galileo satellite navigation programme, is a union infrastructure which makes it possible to manage the environment better and at the same time to increase the safety of citizens. in the face of climate change and in order to strengthen civil protection this is a very important programme. in fact, this regulation will provide the means to gather accurate data on land, sea and atmospheric changes. this increases our capacity to prevent and manage large-scale disasters, such as oil spills, forest fires, floods and landslides. this regulation covers only the financial needs for the period 2011-2013, which is a cause for concern. it is noted that esa's commitments for the launch of the sentinel satellites require timely and precise preparation and imply huge costs for the actual launch, planned for the period 2014-2017. the commission and the council are thus expected to find a suitable solution to this problem.
in writing. the gmes initiative, earth observation, is a project of considerable importance for the future of the european union. this is a union infrastructure which makes it possible to manage the environment better and to increase the safety of citizens. this programme can serve as an example of the will to create a genuine european industrial strategy in the space industry and will create more benefits for society. it will lead to more jobs, more security and environmental protection. it will open up a significant market niche for smes.

in writing. - i welcome the approval of the conclusion of the statute of the international renewable energy agency (irena). renewable energy is one of the key solutions for the future. different countries have different political and economic approaches to encouraging the production and use of renewable energy. however, despite its enormous potential, the current use of renewable energy is still limited. the obstacles are varied and include lengthy import tariff licensing processes and technical barriers, uncertainty about financing renewable energy projects, and insufficient awareness of renewable energy opportunities. it is therefore essential that the international renewable energy agency fulfils its objective of becoming a centre of excellence for renewable energy, advises public authorities on the preparation of national programmes for the introduction of renewable energy, disseminates information on renewable energy and offers training and advice on best practices and financing options.

in writing. − irena, of which portugal is a founding member, was officially established on 26 january 2009. the use of renewable energy is one of the main objectives of eu climate change policies. irena will therefore contribute to the implementation of these objectives, in particular with regard to increasing the share of renewable energy in total energy production by 20% by 2020. i therefore voted in favour of adopting its statute.
in writing. − as resources such as oil become less available and more expensive, we will increasingly have to opt for alternative and renewable energy sources such as water, wind, sea waves, solar energy, which are inexhaustible resources. this is why these resources have become more and more important in the world context, and the creation of the international renewable resources agency (irena) is of extreme importance. hence my vote.
in writing. - i regret once again that the rome iii regulation, adopted in october 2008 by the european parliament, has ended up being blocked at council level. i am glad that several member states, not accepting this situation, have decided to use enhanced cooperation to move forward with this proposal which should allow couples with partners of different nationalities or residing in a country other than their own, at an already difficult time in their lives, to have the possibility of choosing the law that should apply to their divorce. the need for common rules is clear, given that some 350 000 marriages between people of different nationalities take place in the european union every year and that some 20% of all divorces in the eu have crossborder implications. i therefore support the authorization of enhanced cooperation between these 14 member states, including portugal. i hope that others will take the decision to join this initiative, which helps to facilitate the proper functioning of the internal market by removing possible obstacles to the free movement of persons. i look forward to the concrete legislative proposal being presented to us as soon as possible.
in writing. − because of their sensitivity and particular nature, family law issues are the exclusive competence of the member states. however, there have been many attempts to 'communitise' these matters. the initiative to allow enhanced cooperation in the area of the law applicable to divorce and legal separation is another one in this regard. i am sensitive to the legal issues and practical problems raised by the dissolution of marriages between nationals of different states, and i believe that this is a matter which deserves to be treated with the utmost caution.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report which should allow couples from different member states or residing in a country other than their own to choose the law that should apply to their divorce. in 2007, 140 000 divorces were entered into in the eu between couples from different member states. in these cases, european citizens are confronted with problems of the legal order applicable to their separation. i would also like to stress the activation of the enhanced cooperation procedure to which portugal is a party, which has enabled progress to be made on this report, which was blocked in the council by disputes over family law (e.g. in malta, marriage cannot be dissolved by divorce).
in writing. − in the absence of complete harmonisation of the laws of the member states on divorce and legal separation, enhanced cooperation in this area has made significant progress, leading to greater harmonisation of private international law and strengthening the process of integration.
in writing. − the so-called convergence reports of the commission and the ecb allow an assessment of the progress made in the member states with a derogation and whether they are already in a position to fulfil their obligations relating to the achievement of economic and monetary union. the 2010 convergence report covers the nine member states still benefiting from a derogation (bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, latvia, lithuania, hungary, poland, romania and sweden), as the united kingdom and denmark have not so far expressed a willingness to adopt the euro. according to the report, of all the member states assessed, only estonia fulfils the necessary criteria for adopting the euro. the purpose of this proposal for a decision is therefore to abolish the derogation for estonia with effect from 1 january 2011. i voted in favour and congratulate estonia on having achieved all the necessary conditions, especially at this time of global economic crisis.
in writing. − it is with a sense of responsibility that i vote in favour of this report and the proposal for estonia to adopt the euro as from 1 january 2011. in a difficult context of the global economic, financial and social crisis which has affected nominal convergence in other member states, estonia has been successful in implementing a broad set of major structural reforms which have enabled it to meet the convergence criteria. the credible and sustained efforts of the estonian government and people are particularly visible in the public debt, the lowest in the eu, and the deficit, which in 2009 was below the 3% target set by the maastricht criteria. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the accession of estonia to the eurogroup. estonia's accession to the euro once again highlights the vision, attraction and confidence of the member states not yet in the euro area in the single currency and its future.
in writing. − at a time when the euro's detractors are questioning the viability of the single currency, the union is once again showing that this is a project that maintains its strength and persists in its objectives, while retaining all the capacity and attraction for new states. since estonia has fulfilled all the maastricht criteria, in accordance with article 140 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union ('tfeu') and the protocol (no 13) on the convergence criteria annexed to the tfeu, there is no reason to delay the adoption of the euro by this baltic state. the commission has also taken note of the fact that the estonian authorities have not yet adopted a decision on the compatibility of the aid with the internal market. the integration of the single currency, as this crisis has shown, is not an end in itself. the effort to consolidate the budget and balance the public accounts should be continuous, active and effective. i congratulate estonia, despite the difficult time for its adoption, and its people and government, on joining the euro, and i hope that they will continue the efforts for convergence undertaken so far.
in writing. − given estonia's economic indicators and the sustainability of its public accounts, i am in favour of its adoption of the euro on 1 january 2011. in the current context of global crisis and continuing financial market pressure on the euro, estonia's entry into the euro area is a positive sign that reinforces the importance and viability of the european process of economic and monetary integration. i would like to highlight the example of estonia, which has managed to combine progress with the rigorous and sustainable management of public accounts. despite the negative economic environment, it posted a deficit of 1,7% of gdp in 2009, while the overall government debt-to-gdp ratio was 7,2% of gdp, well below the 60% reference value in the european union. in this context, i reaffirm the urgent need to set up effective mechanisms to monitor the economic and budgetary performance of all member states on a permanent basis and in real time, in order to ensure that the convergence criteria are met.
in writing. - monetary union, despite the financial crisis and the attacks on the euro, is an undeniable reality and must be strengthened by the gradual entry of all member states not yet members. the conclusion that estonia, despite the international crisis, has met the maastricht criteria and can thus become a full member of the euro area as of 1 january 2011 is good news for those who advocate an ever-stronger economic and monetary union.
in writing. − the total amounts (included in amending budgets drawn up after the provisional annual accounts were closed at the end of march and) returned to the member states since 2007 are as follows: the commission has also decided to extend the deadline for the submission of comments to the council on the draft amending budget for the financial year 2007 to 31 december 2007 (see recital 13 above). the total value of surpluses is the result of a combination of three factors: the implementation of expenditure, the implementation of revenue and the change in exchange rates. the surpluses are not returned directly to the member states but are entered as revenue in the next budget in accordance with the financial regulation. the immediate consequence is a reduction in the own resources to be charged to the member states. i believe that these surpluses should be reinforced in the budget for the following year by increasing commitment expenditure, or reverted to a european fund that would finance eu priorities. it is important, however, that there is the flexibility to avoid these surpluses. the annual surpluses are the result of the fact that the policies and measures proposed and planned for the development of the european union have not been fully implemented. i therefore believe that the final adoption of amending budget no 4/2010 must be an opportunity to reflect on the budgetary situation in the european union.
