in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the draft directive of the european parliament and of the council on the rights of interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings because it strengthens the rights of citizens who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. i consider it important that member states ensure that suspects or accused persons who do not understand or speak the language of the criminal proceedings in question are provided with interpretation services without delay.
in writing. - we all know that criminal justice, in order to function effectively, must specifically provide for the rights of suspects and/or accused persons, in order to guarantee them an adequate possibility of defence through appropriate legal and judicial means. in this context, it is essential that suspects and/or accused persons are guaranteed the right to be informed, in a language they know, of their rights and duties and the content of the charge against them, as well as of everything that is decisive for the proceedings in which they are involved. this is the only way to ensure an effective defence, the cornerstone of the rule of law and modern criminal procedure. i also welcome the council's decision to progressively adopt measures of judicial cooperation in this and other areas, since the safeguarding of procedural rights is the key to quicker, more effective and fairer proceedings.
in writing. − the creation of a free area within the multiplicity of realities that make up the european union cannot be achieved without guaranteeing equal conditions for every european citizen throughout the european area, in particular in access to justice, as a basic value of democracy and of any rule of law. i therefore support the introduction of a directive which will ensure that all member states have common standards for interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings in the european union, allowing any citizen outside his country of origin to have the right to express himself and to be heard in his mother tongue, or in another language he accepts as valid, in police interrogations or court hearings. given the importance of ensuring a fairer europe for the consolidation of european integration, i call for these new measures to be implemented as quickly as possible in all member states and for the european union to be able to pursue the process of further harmonisation in the area of guarantees of rights and judicial procedures.
in writing. − the search for an eu as an area of freedom, security and justice is reinforced by the adoption of this regulation. it is very important that a citizen of any member state should have the right to interpretation and translation of all parts of his criminal proceedings, so that mutual trust and cooperation between member states can be strengthened and the rights of individuals can be safeguarded in a fully informed manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of rejecting the european commission's proposal on the organisation of working time for persons performing mobile road transport activities. the commission should accept the wishes expressed by the european parliament and amend the present proposal. all workers, not just employees, engaged in this activity should have a weekly workload limitation to ensure greater safety for european road users and to avoid unfair competition in the road transport sector.
in writing. − legal certainty is an essential value for the correct application of the law, which is why any amendment of a legal text which creates additional difficulties in defining its scope of application should be rejected as a bad legal technique. as there are still many doubts about the scope of the proposed directive, particularly as regards the distinction between self-employed drivers and mobile workers, we agree with the rapporteur that it should be recast.
in writing. − the competitiveness and viability of enterprises cannot be sustained by rules which are distorted and disproportionate to the general values and principles of labour law, since they only serve to promote situations of unfair competition and precariousness of the labour market. in the case of transport, the possibility of granting exceptional treatment to selfemployed drivers, by releasing them from a set of rights and obligations laid down in the legislation for the sector, especially as regards working time, would create an unacceptable situation of inequality and unfair competition in relation to salaried drivers, in addition to the aggravation of road safety and the risks to life. i therefore voted against the commission proposal, because i considered that it did not contribute to dignity, safety, health, welfare and fair competition at work.
in writing. - it was very important that the european parliament voted today to reject the proposal, which we support, to reject the european commission's proposal to exclude selfemployed bus and lorry drivers from the legislation regulating working time in this profession. the committee on employment and social affairs of the european parliament, whose position was confirmed in plenary, believes that self-employed drivers should be subject to the same standards as employees, for health and safety reasons and to ensure fair competition in the sector. the commission proposal, which was rejected by 368 votes to 301, with 8 abstentions, was intended to amend the 2002 directive on the organisation of working time for persons performing mobile road transport activities. the rejection of this proposal means that the 2002 directive (directive 2002/15/ec) which provides that self-employed drivers are to be covered by the same rules as employees from 23 march 2009 remains in force. we therefore consider this vote to be of great importance in order to combat social dumping, to defend the right to health and rest of workers in the sector and to improve road safety conditions.
in writing. - we voted today on a dossier on the protection of the health and safety of workers which has generated a relevant debate. the european commission's proposal to parliament proposed that the directive should not cover selfemployed road transport workers, i.e. drivers who are selfemployed and not employed. however, the report adopted by the parliamentary committee on employment and social affairs proposed that the commission's proposal be rejected. i believe that the two fundamental issues underlying this dossier relate, on the one hand, to the need for a european definition of the concept of selfemployed and, on the other, to the need for each member state to make an additional effort to ensure that workers who are not free to organise their professional activities and who therefore should not be employed as selfemployed are properly covered by contracts. while i believe that the phenomenon of 'fake' selfemployed should be tackled at national level through appropriate regulation, monitoring and sanctions, it seems to me that the discussion that has begun can help to pave the way in this direction. that is why, after having followed this dossier closely, i thought it right to vote against the european commission's proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation on food labelling because it aims to help consumers make more informed choices - by extending mandatory labelling to other nutrients and introducing new rules on the country of origin - and because it simplifies, updates and merges, in a single document, seven directives and a regulation currently in force on food labelling, thus simplifying legislation. i also argued that artisanal foodstuffs and wines were not covered by this regulation because of their particular nature, which in the case of wine has already been translated into a regulation of its own. as regards country of origin labelling, which is already mandatory for certain foods such as beef, honey, fruit, vegetables and olive oil, it should be extended to all types of meat, poultry and dairy products. the country of origin shall also be indicated for meat, poultry and fish used as ingredients in processed foods. as regards meat and meat-containing foodstuffs, origin should be defined as the country where the animal was born, raised and slaughtered, and not where the meat is processed, as is currently the case.
in writing. - consumers have the right to know what is in the food they eat. for this reason, information on the composition and nutritional value of food is indispensable, as it is the first factor enabling the consumer to make specific choices. the commission proposal for a recast of the community rules on food labelling is designed to simplify the existing framework for this purpose. the proposal also aims to provide greater legal certainty for those involved in the food chain, to increase the competitiveness of the european food industry, to ensure food safety, to provide consumers with complete information on food products and to promote healthy eating as part of the european union's strategy to combat obesity. i welcome the following basic proposals contained in the regulation: · all mandatory entries must be in characters of a minimum size of 3 mm. · inscription of a comprehensive nutrition declaration in the 'main field of view' of the packaging. · mandatory information on the energy value of the food and the fat content, saturated fatty acids, glycides, with a specific reference to sugars and salt, listed in the respective order on the front of the packaging. i call on the member states to adopt these standards in ... (summary statement pursuant to rule 170 (1) of the rules of procedure)
in writing. − the existence of a uniform food labelling system within the internal market is not only vital and necessary to ensure high levels of food safety for the european consumer, but also an important instrument for the competitiveness of companies in the sector in intra-community trade. i therefore vote in favour of the amendments tabled by the rapporteur, in which i support the rejection of the traffic light system as a system for reporting the levels of fat, carbohydrates and proteins, and in favour of the adoption of a simple, transparent and easily understandable community labelling system. providing consumers with information on the composition and nutritional value of foods, as well as on the main nutritional ingredients and their energy value, is essential to guide them in making informed and informed choices and purchases. i therefore believe that the commission has adopted a paternalistic position in this matter by seeking to guide the consumer in his choices rather than inform him. however, i believe that direct marketing by farmers and local and regional products should not be subject to the rules of this regulation, since it is these products that contribute to the diversity of european gastronomic culture.
in writing. − we now know that poor nutrition and the abuse of certain nutrients (such as salt or fats) can be responsible for a number of diseases which not only represent serious public health problems but also a very high cost for health systems. in many cases these are diseases (such as hypertension) that could be prevented with better nutrition and proper information. i therefore consider it essential that there should be adequate regulation of food labelling. we cannot legislate a healthy diet; but we can give consumers the information they need to know exactly what they're consuming, and then make an informed choice. these are not measures against food producers (the proposal is reasonable to the extent of excluding traditional products and small and medium-sized restaurants serving unpackaged meals) but in favour of public health.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report on food information for consumers, which combines and replaces seven directives and one regulation. food labelling is crucial to ensuring food safety. i am in favour of clear information for the consumer, less red tape, simplification of regulations, greater legal certainty and increased competitiveness of the food industry, without ever forgetting small businesses. i am glad that direct marketing by farmers and local and artisanal products are not subject to the rules of this regulation, as the commission had intended. it is products like these that guarantee our roots, our cultural and gastronomic diversity. i am also pleased that prepackaged products served in small restaurants, hotels and cafes are not covered by this regulation. the same is true of wine. the commission has already adopted a number of proposals for the introduction of a european label for wines. the consumer must be informed, but without being pressured or directed to make a choice. the consumer must have the freedom and responsibility of his decision.
in writing. - the right to know the composition of food as fully as possible and as reasonably justified is a fundamental right of consumers. it is also a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for informed and conscious food choices and, as such, a factor in promoting the health and well-being of populations. we recognize and support the fact that the structure of the proposal applies primarily to prepackaged food and that the specificities of the catering sector and the heavy weight of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in it should be safeguarded, since prepared meals cannot be considered as standardised products. however, we regret that many relevant amendments have been rejected, significantly impoverishing the content of the report - which we cannot but consider a concession by the majority of this parliament to the interests of some powerful sectors of the food industry. as an example, note the rejection of the amendment that provided for consumer information if the product intended for consumption is a genetically modified product and/or contains derivatives and substances classifiable as gmos.
in writing. − the labelling of foodstuffs is intended to ensure that consumers have complete information on the content and composition of these products in order to protect their health and interests. we therefore believe that labelling of foodstuffs is essential to increase market transparency, as it allows producers to inform consumers in a regulated and credible manner about the quality and/or regional specificity of their products. we also welcome the fact that traditionally or artisanally produced food and wine deserve special treatment, which takes account of their particularities.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report which, in general, responds in a balanced way to the initial proposal of the european commission, advocating exemption from the scope of the regulation for non-pre-packaged products and regional products; exemption from the labelling obligation for wines and wine products; rejection of the 'traffic light' system (red, yellow or green to illustrate carbohydrate, protein and fat levels); and mandatory indication of the place of origin of meat, subject to the results of an impact analysis to be carried out by the european commission. the derogations provided for, in respect of the general arrangements applicable, for regional products, wine and, to a certain extent, meat are positive. the initial proposal of the european commission would severely penalise portugal, which, recognised for its historic gastronomic traditions, would face increased competitiveness problems in relation to the northern eu member states, with a highly industrialised gastronomy and with little use of traditional techniques and/or instruments. in addition, the report makes a very positive provision that direct marketing by farmers will not be subject to the rules of the general regulation.
in writing. − a uniform food labelling system at community level is needed to ensure greater transparency through simplified information for consumers, more legal certainty for food businesses and greater clarity of the community acquis. in my view, the commission has gone too far in its proposal in trying to educate consumers about their preferences. the information on labels should be limited to the essential. i therefore supported the rapporteur in her amendments rejecting the traffic light system to illustrate carbohydrate, protein and fat levels and her proposals to include, in a visible way, information on the energy value and nutritional value on the packaging. i believe, however, that community legislation should exclude local and artisanal products and products marketed directly by farmers. regional products ensure the continuity of local specialities and the diversity of the offer. in view of their specific nature and the fact that they are themselves a guarantee of european diversity, the regulation should not apply to those products. i also hope that the rules adopted today will not harm small and mediumsized enterprises in the sector and that the five-year transitional period provided for in the document adopted will allow them to adapt more effectively.
in writing. − the adoption of the new eu 2020 strategy must take account of the growing effects of the economic and financial crisis affecting the eu as a whole. a forward-looking, ambitious and coherent strategy is therefore needed. in this new eu 2020 strategy, it is essential to put people and environmental protection at the heart of governance. the member states must be concerned to reduce their public expenditure by means of major structural reforms. efforts need to be focused on citizens by strengthening their participation and autonomy, encouraging their entrepreneurship and innovation, and on smes by making the legislation more favourable to them. a strategy to accelerate sustainable economic growth, together with reforms to boost and improve competitiveness, is needed.

in writing. − the eu 2020 strategy should, at this stage, focus on concrete, real measures within the reach of the member states, so that it produces the intended effects. innovation, research and development and a focus on the skills of workers are key to enhancing europe's competitiveness in a globalised world. this path will make it possible to cope with the current crisis by reducing unemployment levels and encouraging investment. a more consolidated cohesion policy is also important in order to reduce the differences between regions and thus to put the principle of union solidarity into practice. i strongly support the various flagship initiatives and believe that these initiatives will lead to an improvement in living conditions in the union and to greater competitiveness vis-à-vis third countries.

the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union, which is to be adopted by the council on the basis of article j.3 of the treaty on european union. in 2001, in response to concerns raised by governments and non-governmental organisations about the use of police and security equipment for torture, the european parliament adopted a resolution urging the commission to come forward with a proposal for european legislation to regulate the trade in such items. the commission submitted its proposal the following year, which was adopted in 2005, constituting regulation (ec) no 1236 of 27 june 2005. the regulation introduces, for the first time, a binding control on a number of equipment commonly used in serious human rights violations, but which has not been included in the dual-use or strategic export lists of member states. it prohibits the export and import of products intended for that purpose which may be used only for that purpose and makes the export and import of products which may be used for that purpose subject to authorization. the regulation imposes information and reporting obligations on member states on the application of its rules. the 2005 regulation represents, as already mentioned, a remarkable step forward in the defence of the most essential human rights, namely human life and personal integrity, which are at the heart of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union as well as of international human rights instruments and conventions, both of the united nations and of the council of europe. the entry into force of the regulation was welcomed by human rights organisations and, as mentioned above, the un special rapporteur on torture welcomed the regulation as an important milestone in the fight against torture and as a model which could be followed by countries in other regions. but, ladies and gentlemen, what good is a regulation of this kind if it is not properly applied? and how can we even know whether it is being properly implemented if the member states, who are responsible for its implementation, do not report on its results, as required by the regulation? in fact, it is deeply frustrating to know that only seven countries have provided information on the licensing decisions of the covered articles. and even some of the reports contain insufficient information to allow a responsible analysis of the situation. we cannot continue to accept that member states of the european union continue to allow or turn a blind eye to the manufacture and international trade of products prohibited or subject to the regulation. first, member states should be explicitly urged to comply fully with their obligations as set out in the regulation and to submit in a timely manner annual public reports on their activity, providing detailed information allowing appropriate public scrutiny, including in those reports as a minimum the following: the number of export or import applications received, the items included and the countries of destination for each application, as well as the decisions taken in each case, the report on non-activity, where applicable. it would also be interesting to know more about what measures have been taken or are planned for cases of infringement of the regulation by commercial operators. because without the proper punishment there is obviously no compliance with the rules. finally, there are reasons for updating and introducing more regular procedures for the revision of the regulation itself and in particular of its annexes. this regulation, ladies and gentlemen, is proof that the protection of human rights may require the prohibition or restriction of trade in certain products. free trade cannot be applied to instruments of death or torture. let us therefore put it into practice seriously so that it can be the model it was intended to be for the union and also for other countries outside the european union.
human rights violations are unfortunately a global constant and as such it is crucial that the level of protection that human rights defenders should enjoy is increased and that the level of their working conditions is improved in order to achieve the desired results. these international actors i am talking about are the driving force behind the protection of human beings against any form of abuse to which they may be subjected on a daily basis; it is they who risk their lives and shape the initiatives and legislation that we produce here. and because the work they do is not confined to the territorial and geographical limits of the union but extends throughout the world, it is worth noting the decisive role that the creation of the european external action service and its 'central contact point' can play in strengthening the protection of these citizens. i therefore believe that by introducing incisive measures such as those proposed here, we can promote a current and positive link between transnational and cross-cutting dialogues and policies, and effectively contribute to the pioneering and always realistic vision that has guided eu action in the field of human rights.
in writing. the community has an obligation to protect biodiversity and species conservation by defending animal welfare and taking action against cruel cetacean killing. it is therefore essential that the eu should speak out in agadir against the abuse of hunting, particularly in the field of marketing, and especially hunting for scientific purposes. we know that quotas are being continually missed. we cannot therefore make compromises which allow countries to continue to have room to abuse the law. it is important that the eu maximises its presence in the iwc by speaking with one voice. whales are migratory species, which makes it all the more important to control the abuses committed by some which seriously compromise the interests of all. the preservation of whales and their habitats is now of enormous economic and social importance to many coastal communities in the development of activities around them, such as whale watching, with real impacts on the sustainability of these communities, such as in the azores, my home region, where the transition from the historical practice of commercial whaling to this new activity has taken place. in agadir, therefore, courageous positions are required.

madam president, commissioner, minister, ladies and gentlemen, as we all know, europe has a huge shortage of aquaculture products, is subject to increasing competition from third countries and has a huge untapped production potential. with this report, which i am sure will have broad support from the various groups, the european parliament is sending a clear message to the commission on the key issues for aquaculture which should be given special attention in the future common fisheries policy. i therefore congratulate my colleague, mr guido milana, on the important contribution his report has made to putting the subject of aquaculture on the european political agenda at a timely time. i therefore wholeheartedly support your report and urge the commission to take due account of its main recommendations, in particular the need to provide the future fisheries policy with a single and harmonised regulatory framework, to establish clear environmental criteria and requirements, to reduce the bureaucratic obstacles to the licensing of new fisheries, to step up monitoring to ensure compliance with environmental standards and product quality and to provide the appropriate financial incentives under the european fisheries fund to meet the high investment required by innovation and the high technology used by the sector.
i welcome the theme and timing of this report and warmly congratulate your rapporteur on the comprehensive work he has done. aquaculture must be taken as a european priority, given that: first, many fish stocks are overexploited and aquaculture is a significant complement to overcome the shortage of fish on the european market. secondly, the agri-food industry has grown by 7.6% over the last few decades worldwide, while in europe it has grown by only 0.5%. thirdly, the european union imports two thirds of what it consumes, but its aquaculture production accounts for only 2% of world production. fourth, aquaculture is a business worth over eur 3.5 billion, employing over 65 000 people. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the future of the aquaculture sector. when the reform of the common fisheries policy is being discussed, it is important to rethink the future of aquaculture by giving it greater support and focusing on specific training of professionals, raising awareness among producers of a higher quality policy and production standards.

in writing. − human rights defenders are committed to the realisation of one or another of the rights enshrined in the 1948 universal declaration of human rights and other international human rights instruments. in other words, its work aims at the protection of civil and political rights as well as the promotion, protection and realization of economic, social and cultural rights. the declaration recalls that it is primarily the responsibility of states to create an environment favourable to the activities of human rights defenders, allowing individuals, groups and associations to pursue political activities aimed at promoting and protecting human rights without restrictions other than those authorised under the european convention on human rights. only a holistic approach to human rights defenders can give greater effectiveness and credibility to european union policy. this approach should therefore include preventive and protective measures to enable them to act in a timely manner. the short and long-term needs of human rights defenders should be duly taken into account.

in writing. - portugal is the third country with the largest quota for bluefin tuna, with some 80 portuguese vessels fishing for tuna, a fish which is also a staple in the portuguese diet. it is therefore essential for our country that this species be preserved, not only because the economic livelihood of countless households depends on it, but also because it is an essential fish for the food of the populations. therefore, when the rapporteur recalls the possibility of including bluefin tuna in the annex to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), which would prevent trade in it, i cannot fail to stress again, as i have done in the past, the importance of ensuring at the same time adequate protection for wild species at risk without, however, calling into question or condemning to extinction activities that ensure the economic and social viability of various communities.
in writing. - i welcome the approval of the bluefin tuna catch documentation programme which prohibits the landing, transhipment, caging, harvesting, internal trade, import, export or re-export of bluefin tuna which is not accompanied by a duly completed and validated catch document. the new regulation establishes a european bluefin tuna catch documentation programme to support the implementation of conservation and management measures approved by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). the document incorporates the provisions of the iccat programme to identify the origin of all specimens of this species. the programme also aims to reduce illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing for bluefin tuna, which has contributed to the near-extinction of bluefin tuna stocks.
in writing. − the eu must be very active, demanding and exemplary in relation to the state of fish stocks. this is because the figures currently presented for various species are worrying. countries like japan continue to show a lack of interest in the decline of some marine species, making it very difficult to conserve them. i therefore consider it essential that this catch documentation programme for bluefin tuna be approved in order to reduce illegal fishing and to prohibit landing, transhipment, caging, harvesting, internal trade, import, export or re-export of bluefin tuna which is not accompanied by a properly completed and validated catch document. the sustainability of the planet is at stake, through the preservation of its resources, fauna and flora, which should deserve increasing attention from the eu legislator.
in writing. - this report concerns the transposition into community law of an iccat catch document programme. on the basis of the iccat meetings held in recife, a number of measures were adopted, which are the subject of this report, namely: - general obligation to harvest caged fish in the year of capture or before the start of the fishing season with trawl nets with retention of the following year (exceptions are allowed); - prohibition on the use of chartered fishing vessels; - addition of a new annex with detailed instructions on the issuing, completion and validation of the documentation programme. good quality bluefin tuna has a high commercial value, which is why operators have made little effort to evade controls, often in breach of the law. this report is intended to avoid this kind of situation as much as possible and therefore deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. the conservation of bluefin tuna stocks is an issue which the epp group, to which i belong, has always defended, given the alarming threat of depletion of this species of fish. the aim of the parliament's report, which i support today, is to find a balance between the growing environmental concerns about the near disappearance of bluefin tuna and the economic and social importance of the european union's fishing industry by incorporating into community rules the conservation and management measures adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. these measures include a new complex documentation programme which must accompany the tuna consignment throughout the chain of control and the impossibility of using chartered fishing vessels. it would be desirable that such measures be applied in an effective manner and proportionate to the objective of preserving the species in question, so as not to compromise the economic and social viability of the various coastal communities in the union, especially those where the degree of dependence on fishing activity is much higher, as is the case in portugal and its outermost regions - the azores and madeira.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because i consider that equal treatment between women and men is one of the objectives of the european union and therefore one of the fundamental principles of any political response to the economic and financial crisis and the transition to the post-crisis period; because i consider it essential that the commission, the council and the member states take the necessary measures to mainstream the gender perspective in all eu policies and that they review existing legislation to ensure that equality between men and women is properly implemented and to allow for positive discrimination measures to be adopted wherever necessary; and because i agree with the call on the european institutions, the member states and local and regional authorities to take concrete measures, including through legislation, to promote the balance between men and women in positions of responsibility in local administrations and in business and political life, including in the boards of public and regional institutions, and european and national administrations, which should set the example; calls, therefore, for binding targets to be set to ensure equal representation of men and women.
in writing. − while i am a supporter of the principle of equality and the need to close the gender gap, particularly in employment, i cannot fail to stress that the current financial crisis affects men and women equally and that measures to combat the crisis must be taken globally, ensuring that states, businesses and families can best cope with this period of austerity. i do not, however, fail to recognise that states must endeavour, not only in legislation but in practice, to eliminate the differences which still exist between men and women in the labour market by establishing equal pay for equal work, equal conditions for access to management positions and by legislating to enable women to reconcile family life with their occupation in an appropriate way so that the option of starting a family does not become an excessive burden on their career.
in writing. - in the current context of the global economic crisis, which has aggravated social problems, the risk of gender discrimination is a real threat to the consolidation of a developed, fair and equitable europe. gender discrimination is a structural problem that persists in the developed world and in europe, with serious consequences for equal opportunities and economic and social stability. i understand that the irreplaceable and indispensable role of women in the family and social context is not properly recognised, valued or protected. the situation of women's greater vulnerability is even more evident in the unacceptable discrimination in pay and in access to and advancement in employment, whether in the private sector, in the public service or even in politics. the european union must take a firm stand for equal opportunities based on the promotion of professional ability and merit, irrespective of gender or colour. however, i regret that this noble cause is being used to promote various issues which are fundamentally divergent, because of their ethical and moral contextualisation, as is the case with abortion and the incentives given by the state and the regional authorities in this area. so i abstained.
in writing. − the policy of equality, aiming at equal treatment regardless of gender, is an increasingly welcomed priority in legislation. however, this should not invalidate a fundamental principle which allows the choice of persons to be based on competence and this, nor should it be allowed that under strictly administrative imposition more qualified persons, also regardless of gender, are overlooked in relation to less qualified persons. it should also be rejected whenever, under a disguised pretext, be it the crisis or any other, they intend to surreptitiously introduce changes of substance in fracturing matters which are not assumed with the justified visibility, in particular in the field of abortion policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because:- i consider it essential that a committee be set up to start discussing the financial perspective after 2013, in particular the political priorities for the mff after 2013, in order to calculate the financial resources that the union needs to achieve its objectives and pursue its policies for the period starting on 1 january 2014. to define the duration of the next mff. to propose, in accordance with the objectives and priorities defined, a framework for the future mff, indicating the main areas of union activity. to specify the relationship between the reform of the system of financing the eu budget and a review of expenditure in order to provide the committee on budgets with a sound basis for the negotiations on the new mff.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider equality between men and women to be an essential requirement for the full enjoyment of fundamental human rights. it is also worth noting that this is a basic principle of the european union and it is high time that real efforts were made to end the existing discrimination between the sexes. moreover, gender equality is a key instrument for economic development and social cohesion, with an unquestionable impact on productivity and economic growth, bringing numerous social and economic benefits. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include women in the workforce. thus, actions of this scale are extremely useful as they have a positive impact on the full inclusion of women in the labour market and in society in general. it is in this sense that i consider this report to be an indispensable contribution to the fight against discrimination against women and to overcoming the serious obstacles to gender equality. i believe this will have a major impact in breaking down age-old gender barriers, creating a more just and equal society.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the sharing of family and domestic responsibilities between men and women is an indispensable condition for the promotion and achievement of equality between women and men. it is time to move from intentions to concrete policies and actions that can contribute to the eradication of violence against women and to the promotion of women's rights by combating gender stereotypes and all forms of discrimination in society and in the family.

in writing. - the concern of policymakers with the clarity of business involving sport is not new, nor is the suspicion that many sports agents will allegedly engage in reprehensible or even unlawful conduct that calls into question the truth of sport, the health and safety of their representatives and the truth in commercial transactions. the links of some of these agents to organised crime networks have also been noted. this worrying situation deserves all the attention the european union can give it, urging a separation of the wheat from the chaff which reinforces the demand, transparency and rigour required for the exercise of such an activity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on players' agents in sport for supporting the call for the regulation of the activity of sports agents, if necessary in the form of a directive. i am particularly concerned about the findings of the study on sports agents in the european union, commissioned by the commission, with regard to criminal activities associated with sports activities, where these are affected by organised crime linked to the activities of sports agents. i believe that this situation is harmful to the image of sport, its integrity and, ultimately, its role in society. i would particularly stress the specific vulnerability of young sportsmen and the risk of becoming victims of human trafficking and the specific responsibility of sportsmen's and club agents in this situation. i therefore support the idea of rules on the activities of sports agents which bring about harmonization and transparency. i think it would be useful to introduce a licensing system for agents throughout the eu and a register of agents.
in writing. − the football industry is booming and increasingly involving significant amounts of money. the players' agents are one of the main players in this industry and are of capital importance, as they are the ones responsible for negotiating with the clubs when the players' transactions are made. on the other hand, football players and other players in more media-oriented sports are being recruited at an increasingly young age and, if they are not well advised, their careers may be at risk. this is why we need to have well-defined rules so that the activities of agents do not lead to less correct practices which may harm players, especially the youngest ones.
in writing. i am voting in favour of this joint motion for a resolution. good neighbourly relations between the eu and russia are fundamental to the stability, security and prosperity of the whole of europe. aware of their shared responsibilities in promoting stability, the eu and russia have been intensifying negotiations and seeking new cooperation partnerships that go beyond mere economic cooperation, also integrating the areas of rule of law or respect for human rights. a good example of this enhanced cooperation, which i would like to highlight, is the signing of the joint declaration on gaza by the vice-president of the commission and high representative of the eu for foreign affairs and security policy, catherine ashton, and the russian foreign minister, sergei lavrov. i also regard as very positive the progress that russia has made in order to be able to meet the objective of wto accession, in particular the abandonment of protectionist measures, which is an indispensable requirement and must continue. finally, i would like to stress the need to involve russia in the eu baltic strategy, specifically in improving maritime safety and ensuring a high level of environmental protection.
in writing. − russia is still far from being a country in which human rights, civil liberties and the rule of law are fully guaranteed. it is therefore unrealistic to try to circumvent this by claiming that there is a full understanding between the two blocs on the issues of rights, freedoms and guarantees. that said, i cannot but welcome the eu-russia summit and hope that russia will develop into the credible, reliable, democratic and secure partner that the european union so badly needs. i therefore believe that the union will have every advantage in supporting russia's efforts to democratize and in strengthening the concrete partnerships with that state which will bring it closer to the other europeans with whom it shares its history and culture. if the european institutions and the member states contribute to making possible peter the great's dream of a russia fully integrated into the concert of nations and, in particular, into europe of which it is also a part, they will have done a great service to world stability.
in writing. − the eu is committed to negotiating with russia a new framework agreement to further develop eu-russia relations. russia is an important partner of the eu. i advocate cooperation to address common challenges through a balanced and results-oriented approach based on democracy and the rule of law. they must share not only economic and commercial interests but also the objective of close cooperation at world level and at the level of the common neighbours on the basis of international law. the eu and russia should therefore intensify their negotiations on a new partnership and cooperation agreement which is broad, comprehensive and legally binding. this agreement must go beyond economic cooperation and also include the areas of democracy, the rule of law, respect for human and fundamental rights. i support the objective of russia's accession to the wto, to help russia attract more foreign investment and diversify its economy. the establishment of the customs union with belarus and kazakhstan by russia is likely to create additional obstacles to the accession of the russian federation to the wto.
in writing. − eu-russia relations are very important for both sides, but need to be broadened and intensified beyond economic cooperation to include the areas of democracy, the rule of law and respect for fundamental human rights. the conclusion of a strategic partnership agreement between the eu and russia is therefore of the utmost importance for the future development and intensification of cooperation between the two parties. the current economic and trade relations between the eu and russia are proof of the results of a common effort and commitment.

in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the motion for a joint resolution as a whole. i think it is time for the european union to play a much more active and autonomous role in the search for a solution to the arab-israeli conflict. bearing in mind the centuries-old relations of some eu member states with the arab world, the unparalleled and committed support of europe in equipping the palestinian national authority with the means to become a viable and self-sustaining state, the unparalleled scale of humanitarian aid for the reconstruction of the palestinian areas affected and the traditional relations of friendship and partnership with israel, the eu is a credible partner and an irreplaceable agent. we are living through weeks of dangerous escalation of tension and violence in the middle east. each tragic event fosters more hatred and misunderstanding, fuels radicalism and inspires fundamentalism. with the lisbon treaty, the eu finally has the institutional basis to design an external relations and security and defence policy commensurate with its demographic size and economic importance. without arrogance, aware of the scale of the problem, without being naïve or masochistic, it is time for europe to take up this challenge!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the israeli military operation against the humanitarian fleet and the blockade of gaza by condemning the attack on the humanitarian fleet, which took place in international waters and constituted a violation of international law. i believe that israel must end the blockade of the gaza strip, which has resulted in a humanitarian crisis and growing radicalisation, increasing insecurity in the region.
in writing. - just as the deaths of human beings are always to be deplored, so too must the use of adjectives such as peaceful or humanitarian by supporters of terrorist organisations who refuse to accept peaceful coexistence in the region be condemned. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is also necessary to consider the attempt to break through a naval blockade, motivated by the violent seizure of power in gaza by hamas, as a hostile act, whatever name is given to it. apart from the need to support the weakest and most vulnerable among the palestinians, it must be acknowledged that hamas, which exploits and mobilizes them, continues not to recognize the state of israel, and that several of its most prominent militants have repeatedly called for its destruction. all of this reinforces the understanding that a conflict like the one in the middle east lacks smoothness of purpose, perseverance in action and generosity in forgiveness.
in writing. − the israeli military operation in international waters on 31 may 2010 against the humanitarian aid flotilla bound for gaza resulted in the death of nine civilians and the injury of 38 civilians and seven israeli soldiers. i offer my deepest sympathy to the families of the victims. for the full truth to be known, i call for an immediate and impartial international investigation into this attack. i believe that israel should immediately end the blockade of the gaza strip, which has resulted in a humanitarian catastrophe and a growing radicalization that is a source of insecurity for israel and the whole region. the eu's policy towards the middle east must have a decisive and coherent political role, alongside effective diplomatic instruments, in the pursuit of peace and security in this border region of strategic interest to the eu.
in writing. - we consider that this resolution has a clear message of condemnation of the attack on the humanitarian fleet carried out in international waters, in clear violation of international law. it is a step in the right direction with regard to the urgent need to end the blockade of the gaza strip, which is resulting in a humanitarian catastrophe for the palestinian people. we are still far from what is necessary in condemning and protesting against the criminal massacre perpetrated, at the behest of the israeli government, against the six vessels of the freedom fleet, which were carrying some 10 000 tonnes of basic necessities, humanitarian aid for a population imprisoned for years on end in its own territory, men, women and children who face a dramatic and calamitous humanitarian situation as a result of the brutality unleashed against them, which has turned gaza into a gigantic concentration camp. we must say enough once and for all. we must impose on israel respect for international law. the us and the eu must end their collusion with israel. we must put an end to the apartheid imposed by israel on the palestinian people and defend the right of the palestinian people to their own state within the 1967 borders.
in writing. the israeli-palestinian conflict is extremely complex and therefore requires careful analysis. while it is true that the loss of human life in this particular incident is unacceptable and worrisome, on the other hand the state of israel has the right to exist and its people to live in safety. israel has been the target of several terrorist attacks by radical movements, including hamas, and it is its right to act pre-emptively to prevent the supply of weapons and materials used in such terrorist attacks. of course, we cannot accept the way in which the vessel approached, completely unable to prevent the loss of human life, thereby exacerbating all the antagonistic impulses. and in this assessment my vote is justified.
in writing. − as well as publicly defending human rights, the european union must seek to prevent their violation by creating barriers to trade in goods which could be used to impose the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. this effort must be accompanied by the same commitment by the member states and the active attention of their respective civil societies in combating the multiple forms of torture and violence that threaten the freedom, health and dignity of every person. more attention to this market and more regulation of trade in these materials and more monitoring of their actual use are fully justified and deserve my support.
in writing. - unfortunately, torture is still practised in many countries. the convention against torture imposes on states a number of obligations, ranging from prevention of torture, investigation of incidents, prosecution of perpetrators and compensation for victims. notwithstanding the above, torture continues to be practiced worldwide, with the use of a wide range of police and security equipment. this is why measures must be taken to prevent such equipment from being freely distributed and to allow it to be sold and acquired by individuals who may then use it for torture and ill-treatment.

in writing. - i deeply regret the tragic loss of life aboard the south korean corvette cheonan and express my condolences to the government of the republic of korea, the bereaved families and the korean people. i note that the investigation by the international joint civilian-military investigation team has produced clear and indisputable evidence that the cheonan was sunk as a result of an external underwater explosion caused by a torpedo manufactured in the democratic people's republic of korea (dprk), in line with the findings of an independent evaluation by the neutral nations oversight committee. i reiterate the condemnation of the attack expressed by the high representative/vice-president and commend the restraint shown by the republic of korea. i urge the commission to maintain the current humanitarian aid programmes and to keep the channels of communication with the dprk open, as these aid programmes have a direct influence on the living conditions of the people of north korea.
in writing. the incident with the south korean corvette cheonan is in every way reprehensible. this situation is causing great instability on the korean peninsula and measures must be taken to ensure that a new incident of this nature with loss of human life does not happen again. although denying involvement, the dprk is the prime suspect in setting off this situation in the face of evidence, including the wreckage found at sea of a north korean-made torpedo. there must be a condemnation of this incident by the entire international community, in particular china and russia, which have not yet condemned this situation in a clear and unequivocal way. it is only right that the problem be referred to the united nations security council so that it can take steps to prevent similar incidents in the future.
in writing. - although it has not been broadcast on our television news, the situation in bosnia-herzegovina is far from completely stabilised, with a worsening of ethnic political tensions that is not expected to lead to a new armed conflict. this deep and latent antagonism has a negative impact on the country's poor governance and poor articulation of priority government policies and it is now clear that bosnia and herzegovina has a long and difficult road ahead if it is to join the eu. unfortunately, the term 'balkanization' still means division, struggle for the same space and conflict of difficult resolution, and the european union should be more attentive to the possibility of a new outbreak of disputes between the communities that make up the country and seek to prevent them by effective intervention with the main political and social actors.
in writing. the eu has reiterated its pledge of accession for the western balkan countries, including bosnia and herzegovina. however, the primary responsibility for accession lies with these countries and depends on their ability and determination to meet the copenhagen criteria. the political climate in bosnia and herzegovina is unstable and there is no common vision shared by all political forces. there has been no progress in the process of inter-ethnic reconciliation and in the functioning of state structures. i would remind you that joining the eu means accepting the values and rules on which the eu is founded, namely respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to national minorities, solidarity, tolerance, democracy, the rule of law and, in particular, respect for the independence of the judiciary. freedom and independence of the media, both public and private, are fundamental democratic requirements. i therefore urge the authorities in bosnia and herzegovina to promote the development of independent media. i also condemn the attacks on journalists and urge the competent authorities to take appropriate measures to avoid similar situations in the future.
in writing. − the eu enlargement process must always be considered and any new accession must always respect common reference factors of the eu countries. the countries of the western balkans are in the forefront of future accessions, among them bosnia and herzegovina. however, the primary responsibility for accession lies with these countries, in particular in their capacity and determination to meet the copenhagen criteria. in this respect, bosnia and herzegovina has not made much progress towards stabilisation and development. the climate of political instability and the lack of a common vision shared by all political forces should be emphasized in particular, and there is now an increasing use of incendiary language, which undermines the process of inter-ethnic reconciliation and the functioning of state structures. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - in view of the physical reality of airspace (which is global and shared), i believe that greater cooperation between the european union and the united states on air transport regulation is both appropriate and necessary. issues such as passenger safety are cross-cutting and i therefore support the creation of joint eu-us air traffic management programmes such as sesar and next gen, as well as the need for the us to share information with the eu in the context of the airline blacklist. finally, as i said, since airspace is global and shared, and since the ultimate objective of the eu-us air transport agreement is the full opening up of the market, i support parliament's position in calling for greater liberalisation of the air transport market by eliminating unbalanced discrimination and restrictions.
in writing. − the opening of eu-us aviation markets which together account for some 60% of world air traffic will benefit consumers on both sides of the atlantic, provide substantial economic advantages and create jobs. i welcome the cooperation between the eu and us authorities responsible for aviation safety, and reiterate the importance of the european blacklist of airlines that do not comply with the rules in force and the us system of monitoring airline standards. it is important that both sides share information on this issue. it is noted that the privacy of european and us citizens should be respected when passenger personal data is exchanged between the eu and the us, in accordance with the criteria required by the european parliament in its resolution of 5 may 2010. it therefore stresses the urgency of adopting international standards on data protection and privacy. i welcome the agreement to reduce noise and emissions from aircraft and the intention to increase technical cooperation between the eu and the us in the fields of climatology, research and technological development.
in writing. the eu-us air transport agreement is based on the liberalisation of this sector. the document states that the ultimate objective of the eu-us air transport agreement is the full opening of the market without any restrictions on either side. by establishing such agreements and by highlighting the interest of large economic groups in the liberalisation of the single market, the eu is overriding the existing bilateral agreements defined by each member state and is taking the sector out of the public sphere and putting it into the private domain. as regards safety, and while we always advocate that a high level of safety should be provided in air transport services, we are seriously concerned when safety, cost-minimisation and liberalisation are combined, where profit and the concentration of wealth are the main considerations. we therefore believe that air transport, as an important sector in mobility within and outside the member states, should be a public service provided by public undertakings in each country, guaranteeing the quality and safety of the services provided to citizens. we voted against all of this.
in writing. the eu and the us have signed a new agreement on the use of the eu's financial instruments. to this end, and following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it is necessary that the european parliament be fully informed and consulted on the work carried out by the joint committee, as well as by all the entities concerned. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment.
in writing. - at the same session as the vote on the european parliament and council regulation on a european rail network for competitive freight transport, the question of the implementation of the directives of the first railway package, which fell far short of the initial objectives, arose. as rail is a priority, it is urgent to take appropriate measures to ensure the proper implementation of the first railway package, in particular with regard to the progressive opening and liberalisation of markets, while respecting competition rules.
in writing. - i note that the vast majority of the 22 member states have not correctly implemented the three directives of the first railway package, which has prevented the share of rail transport in transport in general from increasing. i consider that the independence of the infrastructure manager is a precondition for fair, transparent and non-discriminatory treatment of all operators. rules are needed to ensure the independence of infrastructure managers, especially when they are part of a railway holding company that is also engaged in rail transport activities. the level of investment in maintaining railway infrastructure is insufficient in a large number of member states, leading in several cases to a deterioration in the quality of existing infrastructure. it is proposed that the commission should review the first railway package by september 2010, addressing as a priority issues such as the independence of infrastructure managers and the lack of resources and powers of regulatory bodies. it is also expected to propose appropriate pricing principles for access to infrastructure to stimulate public and private investment in the railway sector. the liberalisation of the railway market should not undermine the quality of the rail transport service while safeguarding public service obligations.
in writing. the resolution deplores the delay in implementing the three directives which make up the so-called first railway package by several member states, considering that this delay prevents fair competition in the railway market. the real aim of this package is thus once again demonstrated: to open up rail transport, including freight, to competition and private interests as a first step towards full liberalisation of the sector at eu level. it is up to the states to decide in which areas they are to exercise their social functions through public services, as well as to decide on the way in which these public services are to be organised. this is a sovereign choice of the people, which must be respected. we therefore reject any form of undemocratic imposition of measures contrary to the interests of the people - such as that which this resolution clearly embodies. liberalisation is the cause and not the solution of the main problems in the railway sector, notably the quality and accessibility of the service and workers' rights. the persisting policies of dismantling and atrophying the public transport sector must be stopped and reversed, with a view to its surrender to the profit-making logic of large private interests. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the current crisis.
in writing. − the effective implementation of the first railway package is essential for the future creation of a european rail network. addressing problems such as the independence of infrastructure managers and the lack of resources and powers of regulatory bodies needs to be a priority, as well as proposing appropriate principles for charging for access to infrastructure. the creation of rail corridors that allow a rapid and efficient connection from one national network to another will therefore improve the conditions for using the infrastructure. a more competitive rail transport system than the current one brings not only economic but also environmental benefits hence my vote.
in writing. − the first railway package adopted in 2001 contained elements which, in my view, can contribute to the integration of european rail, both passenger and freight, and thus to exploiting synergies and deepening the completion of the internal market and territorial cohesion. however, the three directives in this package, which concerned the development of rail, the licensing of railway transport undertakings and the allocation of capacity and the application of infrastructure charges and which aimed to revitalize this means of transport, have not yet been transposed in most member states, notably in portugal. i therefore agree that a review of this first package by the european commission makes sense, particularly as regards the more problematic issues such as the independence of infrastructure managers, the legal framework for regulatory bodies and the way in which access to infrastructure is charged. any development in the rail transport sector should safeguard the main aspects underlying the provision of the public service, namely its quality and safety and its access by citizens and businesses at affordable prices. good management of these infrastructures and their interoperability will be key to the creation of a truly integrated european rail network.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the floods in central europe, in particular in poland, the czech republic, slovakia and hungary. as one of the signatories of the proposal, i would like to reiterate the need for the european council to resume work on the revision of the european union solidarity fund with a view to creating a more robust and flexible instrument to respond effectively to the new challenges posed by climate change.
in writing. − the floods in central europe have re-established the agency's focus on the adequacy of the european union solidarity fund to the specific needs of member states affected by natural or man-made disasters, dramatic circumstances that are occurring at a worryingly increasing rate and that call for increased attention from governments to water and soil policies. as i have said before, i believe that the structure and availability of the fund should be improved and its mobilisation evaluated frequently in order to make this mechanism more suitable to help mitigate the effects felt by the member states and to promote the reconstruction of the most affected areas in a flexible, prompt and appropriate manner.
in writing. - i express my solidarity with the regions affected by the disaster, my deepest condolences to the families of the victims and note the serious economic impact on the region. in these situations the european union solidarity fund should be fast and flexible. i therefore regret that the council has blocked a proposal to this effect, which parliament had approved by an overwhelming majority at first reading in may 2006. i also support the need for member states to comply with the requirements of the flood directive and to review planning, land use policies and best practices in the light of the increased flood risks caused by the way soils, habitats and drainage are managed and to strengthen flood control capacity and drainage infrastructure in order to limit damage caused by heavy rainfall. member states and regions affected by the natural disaster should pay particular attention to the sustainability of their reconstruction plans.
in writing. - the need to provide support as soon as possible to the areas affected by the economic and social consequences of this natural disaster; - the need to revise the solidarity fund regulation, adapting the eligibility criteria to needs not currently covered and allowing for more flexible and timely mobilisation; - the need to pay greater attention to disaster prevention. in the latter area, cooperation should be strengthened, both at regional and eu level, based on complementarity of actions and the principle of solidarity between member states. in particular, priority eu support to member states should cover, inter alia, preventive measures relating to the correction of risk-inducing situations: riverbed renaturalisation; recovery and protection of watersheds, wetlands and associated ecosystems; increasing the flow capacity of bridges and waterways; protection/remodelling of inhabited areas, including urban areas, particularly vulnerable to certain types of disasters; and maintenance and safety monitoring of existing major infrastructure.
in writing. - the eu, as a space of solidarity between its member states, could not remain indifferent to the catastrophes that struck several countries in the form of floods, notably poland, the czech republic, slovakia and hungary. the rapid mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund (eusf) is therefore very important in order to enable the countries affected by this disaster to use the aid they need quickly to restore the infrastructure to working order, thereby minimising the suffering of the flood-affected populations.
in writing. the document adopted by the european parliament today expresses the european parliament's solidarity with the people of the member states who have been hit by the floods and who have been severely affected by these natural disasters. i support the initiative to include in a joint document of the various political families represented in the european parliament the need to help the communities affected by this catastrophe. i am aware of the reality of the destruction caused by the effects of a natural disaster and i am aware of the various risks and the serious economic, social and human difficulties which result for the population. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance to call for more rapid support at european level, which can only be achieved by making the conditions for allocating the solidarity fund more flexible. as the document states, an urgent debate on this matter is needed. only then can we really speak of european solidarity. for the reasons i have mentioned, the resolution adopted has my clear and unequivocal vote in favour.

in writing. − adequate training of magistrates and the creation of a european judicial culture accelerate judicial proceedings, particularly in cross-border cases. we will thus make a significant contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market, both for businesses and for citizens. although member states have the primary responsibility for training magistrates, it is essential to have eu funding for these training courses for magistrates to promote a european judicial culture. i believe that the proposed pilot projects should not be restricted to erasmus-style exchange programmes for members of the judiciary. the commission, in cooperation with the member states, should make proposals for the establishment of a union-wide network of accredited legal training bodies to provide familiarization courses in national, comparative and european law for judges on a stable and continuous basis.
in writing. − judicial training, which aims to train the judicial magistrates of all member states, is very important in order to achieve a european judicial culture based on mutual understanding. the training of judges is also an obligation of each member state, which must, despite the current crisis, make an effort to continue to invest in the training of these legal professionals.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it urgently necessary to adopt a strategy for aquaculture in the eu, since the current situation, characterised by a series of community standards of different origins and sources which vary in all the member states, makes it impossible to achieve objectives which contribute to the creation of an innovative economic sector with a high technological potential, capable of promoting regional development in a number of maritime, coastal and island regions, as well as in the eu as a whole. i would like to recall the potential of research and the use of advanced technologies to promote employment and retraining for traditional fishermen and as a catalyst for related economic activities. i would also remind you that the development of such a strategy requires a single regulatory framework and, at the same time, appropriate certification and labelling. it is also necessary to strengthen this sector through the necessary investments - without prejudicing other sectors and taking into account the various environmental impacts - because this, as a complementary activity for our coastal communities, can also contribute to combating the fisheries deficit that normally exists in our food balance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the milana report for advocating the need for sustainability in the development of an efficient, economically viable and environmentally friendly european aquaculture in the medium and long term.
in writing. - according to the report, the european aquaculture sector comprises more than 16 500 enterprises, with an overall annual turnover of over eur 3.5 billion and directly and indirectly employing some 64 000 people. that is why it is an unavoidable sector which cannot continue to be the poor relation of fisheries policy without adequate, harmonized legislation to encourage investment. so when we discuss the future of the common fisheries policy (cfp), it is crucial to look at the potential of aquaculture to provide high quality fish with a lower environmental impact, as this can reduce the capture at sea of species at risk.
in writing. − the european aquaculture sector comprises more than 16 500 companies, with an overall annual turnover of over eur 3.5 billion and directly and indirectly employing some 64 000 people. european production in this sector, although it doubled between 1981 and 2001, when it reached 1.3 million tonnes, remained virtually unchanged (+0.5%) until 2008, while world production grew at very high rates (+7.6% per year) during the same period. there is currently no specific and harmonised regulatory framework for the aquaculture sector at community level. on the contrary, it is governed by a series of community rules of various origins (environment, public health, etc.) and by national rules which vary considerably from one member state to another, which is a source not only of disorientation for operators in the sector but also of discriminatory situations and problems of market distortion. i therefore support a proposal for a regulation which consolidates in a single text all the community provisions governing the aquaculture sector, which will result in a clear, stable legislative framework and legal certainty. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − we share the view expressed in the report that aquaculture is a sector with a strong potential to contribute to the economic and social development of numerous regions, including coastal and rural areas, as well as to promote local production and employment. we welcome the measures of simplification and de-bureaucratization which the member states are adopting at the legislative level to frame and regulate the activity. the environmental impacts of aquaculture are now one of the main constraints on the development of the activity. in particular in saltwater aquaculture, the amount of animal protein used in the feed of the farmed specimens is still disproportionately high in relation to the yield obtained. in many cases, problems persist in the discharge of effluents with high pollutant loads into the natural environment. the report recognises these and other problems, and rightly points to the importance of investment in research and development in overcoming them by improving the sustainability and environmental and economic viability of the activity. despite the fair criticism of the 'proliferation of private certification', we believe that more should have been done in this area, clearly advocating the importance of a public system of certification of the food and environmental quality of aquaculture products. as is the need for greater regulation of trade.
in writing. − the aquaculture sector has not had a harmonious development strategy across the eu. it is an important sector for the eu's economic development as well as for ensuring the food supply of quality fishery products, thus also helping to reduce the pressure on wild species, many of which are in danger of extinction. this industry is also important in terms of food security, economic activities and employment, especially in rural and coastal areas.
in writing. − although the eu is the world's largest market for aquaculture products, there is still no harmonised eu legislation on the subject, which has led to regulatory distortions and disorientation among market operators. aquaculture products are part of the diet of european citizens and this report highlights the importance and urgency of a new european strategy to cope with the expansion and potential of the sector. in madeira this is a key issue and, when the economic and social development plan for the autonomous region of madeira for 2007-2013 was drawn up, the fisheries sector, and in particular aquaculture, was identified as one of the thematic priorities, highlighting the need, among others, to promote sustainable management of resources with a view to their conservation and exploitation, while also seeking to promote greater transparency of the markets for aquaculture products. it should be noted that only with adequate funding, in particular through the european fisheries fund, and the use of new technologies and experimental research will it be possible to achieve a structured and sustainable development of the sector, which is environmentally balanced and promotes competitiveness among operators, thus giving greater quality assurance to consumers.
