in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the protocol on integrated coastal zone management in the mediterranean which contains the basic principles for better environmental protection in these zones, including the sustainable use of resources, the preservation of coastal ecosystems, as well as specific provisions relating to certain economic activities that may affect coastal zones, such as construction, tourism, fishing, aquaculture or maritime activities.
in writing. the protocol on integrated coastal zone management (gizcm protocol) aims to reverse the trend of worsening environmental conditions in the mediterranean sea over the last few decades, which have been denounced by environmentalists and men of culture such as the spanish writer arturo pérez-reverte. over-exploitation of fisheries resources, warming, pollution, the disappearance of native fauna and flora and the emergence of species from elsewhere all add to the urgency of an integrated and coordinated response among as many mediterranean coastal states as possible. the european union has a particularly important role to play in this joint effort. it is necessary to ensure that the mediterranean, the cradle of western civilization, remains balanced not only ecologically and landscapistically but also economically, and that it is able to be bequeathed to future generations in such terms that they can recognize the mark of the past in it, enjoy it in the present and preserve it for the future.
in writing. − the european union is a contracting party to the barcelona convention (convention for the protection of the marine environment and the coastal region of the mediterranean) as are all the coastal member states of the mediterranean. in accordance with article 4 (3) of the convention, the parties shall promote integrated coastal zone management, taking into account the protection of areas of ecological and landscape interest and the rational use of natural resources. the gizcm protocol sets out the general objectives and principles of integrated coastal zone management, such as the sustainable use of natural resources and the preservation of coastal ecosystems. it also contains specific provisions on economic activities in coastal zones, such as construction, tourism, fisheries, aquaculture and maritime activities, as well as on instruments for integrated coastal zone management (such as environmental assessments, national strategies and monitoring mechanisms). the iczm protocol has already been approved on behalf of the european community. the commission now proposes, by means of the abovementioned proposal for a council decision, that the council should proceed to conclude the protocol on behalf of the eu. the council must now obtain the consent of the european parliament before adopting the decision on the conclusion of the protocol.
in writing. − the protocol on integrated coastal zone management in the mediterranean (iczm protocol) represents an important effort by the european union to promote integrated coastal zone management, taking into account the protection of areas of ecological and landscape interest and the rational use of natural resources. the economic activities of the region, such as construction, tourism, fishing, aquaculture and marine activities, should be re-thought, re-evaluated and studied in depth so as not to jeopardise the sustainability of the region, which is essential for future generations. i believe, however, that for such an initiative to have short-term effects, full mutual assistance by the mediterranean coastal states is necessary.
in writing. − the 2005 prüm treaty sets out a legal framework aimed at developing cooperation between member states in the fight against terrorism, crossborder crime and illegal immigration. in 2007, it was decided to transpose it into the eu legal framework. it is in the framework of the prüm decision and its implementation that the exchange of dna data, dactyloscopic data and vehicle registration data, as well as the exchange of information on major events with a cross-border impact and the provision of information for the prevention of terrorist acts take place. the aim of this agreement is to enable iceland and norway to join the eu member states in such exchanges, thus strengthening cooperation between the authorities responsible for preventing and combating criminal offences. as iceland and norway are schengen associated countries, it is important that the eu supports their efforts to prevent and combat terrorism and all forms of cross-border crime, while ensuring full respect for fundamental rights, including the protection of personal data, and respect for the principles of proportionality and necessity.

in writing. − frontex, set up in 2005, has as its main objective to coordinate operational cooperation between member states in the management of external borders. all countries associated with the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis should participate in this agency, the modalities of which should be specified in separate agreements between the eu and those countries. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it was nevertheless decided to include liechtenstein in this agreement for reasons of effectiveness, even if it will only apply after the conclusion of this protocol. i therefore support the adoption of this agreement, which lays down the rights and obligations to ensure effective participation of switzerland and liechtenstein in frontex, in particular with regard to voting rights, their financial contribution, data protection and confidentiality issues, etc.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this proposal, which seeks the association of the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein with the frontex agency. as provided for in the frontex agency regulation, the states associated with the implementation and development of the schengen acquis participate in the activities of the frontex agency. however, the modalities of their participation should be defined by agreements with the union. the conclusion, as soon as possible, of this participation agreement between the eu and these two states will therefore be very positive for all parties involved. as a vital instrument of the european strategy to combat illegal immigration, frontex should be able to have the means and conditions to ensure effective coordination of operational cooperation between member states in the management of the external borders of the union. the conclusion of this agreement will thus enable the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein to contribute to closer cooperation on external border control and surveillance between their competent administrative services and those of the eu.
in writing. − the participation of the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein in the frontex agency increases the means at their disposal and the capacity for joint response to the phenomenon of illegal immigration involving states on the fringes of the union which suffer from similar problems to those experienced internally in combating illegal immigration. i welcome the willingness shown by the two countries to cooperate, i hope that it will be established effectively and bear fruit, and i hope that this experience of working together will be extended to other areas as well.
in writing. − the frontex agency was set up in 2004 under articles 62 (2) (a) and 66 of the ec treaty and started its work on 1 may 2005. the agency was conceived as an important instrument of the common european strategy to combat illegal immigration. the purpose of the proposal for a council decision, which is subject to the approval procedure, is to sign and conclude, on behalf of the union, the agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein, of the other part, on the modalities of the participation of those states in the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union, known as frontex. i welcome the conclusion of this agreement, which will enable these two states to contribute to closer cooperation in the field of external border control and surveillance. i hope that the member states will make every effort to complete the necessary ratification procedures as soon as possible with a view to the association of the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein with the frontex agency.
in writing. - the frontex agency was set up as an important instrument of the common european strategy to combat illegal immigration. its main role is to provide operational coordination between member states in the management of the external borders. the extension of this cooperation to other european countries is very important for the fight against illegal immigration, as it provides the agency with more material and human resources to meet its objectives.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament, and this independence cannot be called into question. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree with the european commission proposal, with the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. as regards the amendments tabled by parliament, i would like to stress that the member states should provide the commission (eurostat) with all statistical and budgetary information on the basis of a standardised and internationally accepted accounting method and that the figures for the planned budget deficit and the level of government debt should be those set for the current year by the member states. those figures shall correspond to the latest official forecasts, based on the latest budgetary decisions and on economic developments and prospects, as well as on monthly and quarterly results. such values shall be determined as far in advance as possible of the notification deadline.
in writing. - the good quality, reliability and accuracy of statistics is essential if, in a crisis context such as the one we are currently experiencing, situations such as those in greece are not to be repeated. i therefore consider it crucial that the political commitments made in this area are implemented efficiently and rigorously and that the statistical data are brought into line with existing community legislation, for example by submitting national safety declarations to the commission (eurostat). the commission (eurostat) should also be given more powers of inquiry, allowing it to carry out unannounced inspections of national statistical offices and to have access to all accounting and budgetary information, thus enabling it to assess the state of national public finances. the imposition of financial and non-financial penalties on statistics not presented in accordance with community legislation should also be considered.
in writing. - this report is another step in the attempt to monitor the internal life of countries, now through statistics. they propose, for example, that monitoring visits be made to a member state whose statistical information is under scrutiny. they want the commission, through eurostat, to have the right to access the accounts of public bodies at central and state administration, local government and social security levels, including the provision of detailed basic accounting information, relevant statistical surveys and questionnaires and other related information, including transactions of an extra-patrimonial nature, although they add that this should be done in compliance with legislation on data protection and statistical confidentiality. the commission should also consider drawing up sanctions under the stability and growth pact for the submission of distorted macroeconomic statistics by member states. in practice, if these proposals are accepted by the commission and the council, the commission (eurostat) will have access to all statistical and budgetary information required for the assessment of the quality of data in the national, regional and local accounts, inventories, excessive deficit procedure (edp) tables, accounts of extra-budgetary bodies, non-profit organisations and similar bodies, which are part of the general government sector in the national accounts.
in writing. − the quality and reliability of statistical data on the economic performance of eu countries are of paramount importance for the assessment of the real condition of member states' economies. the greek statistics, which according to various reports were distorted and did not reflect the reality of the economy, were an important warning to take measures to prevent such situations in the future. the strengthening of eurostat's powers and its technical and human resources is therefore very important if the eu is not to face in the future a situation where statistical data are misused by the member states. the strengthening of eurostat's inspections, with the possibility of carrying them out without prior notice, will be very important for the future reliability of statistical data on the economy of the member states.
in writing. − the european commission's proposal was very positive and has been improved by the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament, namely:- the acquisition by the commission (eurostat) of a staff with appropriate training and the greatest possible degree of independence;- the promotion of harmonisation of the collection of statistical data;- the standardisation of statistical and budgetary information provided by the member states;- the application of sanctions under the stability and growth pact in respect of the submission of distorted macroeconomic statistics by the member states. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the european strategy for the baltic sea region is the first attempt to create a common development strategy for a macro-region. the strategy aims to solve common problems and coordinate actions to achieve shared objectives. there are two major areas of interest for this region: the environment and scientific development. this is a complex but interesting strategy which could be developed for other regions of europe.
in writing. as i have already said, the baltic sea, because of the particularly serious environmental problems it faces, must be one of the european union's priorities. the fact that the baltic sea is today one of the main channels of communication and exchange between member states reminds us of the role the baltic sea has played in other historical periods and highlights the need for the union and its member states to recognise the existence of regions which, by virtue of their identity and the development problems and challenges they face, have the advantage of being seen by them as functionally integrated realities. the baltic sea and the regions of the states bordering it have the potential to be considered and operate as a pilot macro-region. i hope that the conclusions drawn from the practical implementation of the european union's strategy for the baltic will make it possible to assess more accurately and appropriately the future role of the macro-regions in european cohesion policy.
in writing. − the baltic sea is one of the most polluted seas in the world, and with the emergence of the concept of macro-regions, where common development objectives or problems are focused, and the geographical characteristics and conditions, it makes perfect sense to try to create a common integrated development strategy for this macro-region. common resources in the baltic sea region are shared by many countries, resulting in considerable interdependence, thus justifying a comprehensive strategy for the region. the baltic sea strategy is the first and so far only attempt to create a common integrated development strategy for a macro-region and should be considered as a pilot project and an example within the european union.
in writing. − this report advocates the importance of developing strategies for the european union's macro-regions, which are seen as a group of territories grouped around common objectives and challenges, and it focuses, as a first initiative, on the baltic sea region strategy. i support the document because i consider it essential to have an integrated territorial plan which promotes a strategy based on the common interests of the territories of the regions concerned, which should count on the contribution of all european policies in pursuing its objectives and be guided by the objectives of european regional policy, in particular the objective of cohesion. the green paper on territorial cohesion points in this direction by highlighting the importance of intervening in the various regions of the european union on the basis of their functional needs. it is hoped that this initiative will be the first of many capable of providing the various european macro-regions with an appropriate legislative and programmatic framework, based on the idea of european territorial cooperation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the contribution of the european union's regional policy to the plan for the revival of the european economy to be essential. regional policy must be seen as a long-term development policy of the european union, which advocates the recovery of competitiveness and employment in the member states. the fight against the economic and financial crisis also involves the acceleration and simplification of cohesion policy programmes, which i consider to be of the utmost importance for a greater adjustment of budgetary policy and necessary to combat the current difficult situation, and which, through this acceleration of programmes, will contribute to the strengthening of the union, its member states and its regions. it is essential to pursue the objective of greater competitiveness, sustainability and flexibility for these programmes in the context of a globalised world. i also believe it is essential to continue to give special attention to objective ii regions by supporting the economic and social conversion of these areas, highlighting all their potential and promoting the coordination of all the means and instruments to achieve the promotion of growth and employment.
in writing. - this report focuses on the contribution of eu regional policy to resolving the economic crisis. the structural funds are essential for investment in areas that contribute to improved productivity and economic growth. in a time of budgetary constraints, when there are cuts in public investment in the member states, the role of the structural funds is even more significant. these funds are also instrumental in financing actions aimed at preparing europe for the post-crisis period, such as actions to train europeans in new areas and new technologies.
in writing. − bearing in mind that the recently adopted eu 2020 strategy is structurally based on economic, social and territorial cohesion, a dynamic cohesion policy, and that the structural funds are indispensable instruments for achieving the objective of sustainable and inclusive growth in the member states, and in particular in the regions, i voted overall in favour of the proposals contained in this report. in the context of the economic and financial crisis in which the eu is currently experiencing, regional and cohesion policy and, in particular, objective 2 programmes are becoming increasingly important in the process of economic recovery, boosting competitiveness and job creation at regional and local level, providing essential support for public investment. i therefore regard the introduction of greater flexibility, which is vital, on the one hand, with the simplification of cohesion policy programmes, as very positive. on the other hand, greater flexibility in the allocation of union funds so that regions can fully benefit from support for infrastructure investment, support for their business community, which is mainly made up of smes, or stimulation of research and modernisation in the industrial or agricultural sectors.
in writing. - in view of the importance of the principle of solidarity, i consider it essential that community funds for cohesion policy be effectively implemented. as i have had the opportunity to express on other occasions, the efficient allocation of european union cohesion funds is crucial to reduce the imbalances observed in the various regions of the eu-27, to help to mitigate imbalances, and to foster european competitiveness. it is essential to help the less-favoured areas develop, to emphasise the efficient allocation of funds for innovation and technology, education and to implement measures that stimulate in particular employment and competitiveness. the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy should also be a guiding element in this respect.
in writing. − regional cohesion is a fundamental objective of european integration and is gaining particular emphasis in this phase of a severe and prolonged economic crisis, with a strong impact on the level of unemployment, especially in the most disadvantaged regions. with the 2006 reform, objective 2 now concerns the strengthening of regional competitiveness and employment in a total of 168 regions in 19 member states, representing 314 million inhabitants, with an overall funding for 2007-2013 of eur 54.7 billion (just under 16% of the total funds). some 74% of this amount is earmarked for improving knowledge and innovation (33.7%) and for more and better jobs (40%). i am in favour of investing in the real economy and supporting small and mediumsized enterprises, giving priority to innovation, competitiveness and employment. this is a guideline that is part of and reinforces the eu 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. to this end, i stress the urgency for the member states and their regions to make use of the european funds at their disposal, an issue which is gaining in importance in this economic and financial crisis, as i have stressed both here in the european parliament and in several speeches in portugal.
in writing. the report under discussion is not another attempt to disguise the real responsibility for the economic and social crisis we are going through. and with it, yet another attempt to put the sole responsibility for the supposed overcoming of this crisis on the shoulders of the workers and the populations. the document strongly supports the key priorities of the eu 2020 strategy and calls for further policy reinforcement to deepen the eu 2020 strategy by building on the european single market. we recall that these priorities are identical to those already known in the reformed lisbon strategy, the same ones that justified and promoted the processes of privatisation of public services, the liberalisation of dismissals and the degradation of working conditions, the increase in unemployment and the promotion of social regression - in other words, the structural causes of the systemic crisis of capitalism we are facing. the structural funds, or any other financial instrument of regional policy which has cohesion as its central objective, should be geared towards genuine commitment to economic development and social progress, territorial cohesion and the reduction of regional disparities. they should not be used perversely to finance policies whose consequences are clearly contrary to the stated objectives and which themselves are the seeds of new and deeper future crises.
in writing. − the good response to the financial and economic crisis has demonstrated the importance of eu regional policy. in the specific case of objective 2, which covers more than 300 million inhabitants in the most disadvantaged regions, but who are nevertheless also suffering the consequences of this serious crisis. this is the time to strengthen the instruments of objective 2 in order to achieve the key priorities of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. - this regi report takes a realistic and extremely up-to-date view of the situation facing the member states and their regions in the context of the economic and financial crisis in europe. as a native of madeira, an outermost region classified as a regional competitiveness and employment objective region, the issue here is profoundly familiar and relevant to me, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of the report presented. objective 2 of the community's cohesion policy aims to empower regions facing serious unemployment problems and structural difficulties which are further exacerbated by the crisis we are experiencing. in order to fully achieve regional policy and the objectives of strategy 2020, it is necessary to strengthen the competitiveness of the regions through the development of labour and economic policies. only then will europe be able to achieve real smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. for these reasons i support the rapporteur's view that there should be more flexibility in the allocation of community funds and aid so that the regions concerned can benefit from modernisation and support which translates into real development and which, in time, can lead to a more sustainable economy.
in writing. - this regulation aims to establish a common framework of rights for passengers travelling by bus and coach, guaranteeing a level of protection comparable to that already established for other modes of transport, such as trains and airplanes. it is important that comparable conditions be achieved in road passenger transport between carriers in the various member states and between the different modes of transport, which should include liability in the event of death or damage, compensation and immediate assistance in the event of cancellation or delay, without forgetting the possibility for the passenger to lodge a complaint if he considers that his rights have not been respected. i regret the lack of ambition in the council's proposal, not only because it considerably reduces the scope of this regulation, but also because it weakens the level of protection for road passengers travelling in the eu. i have no doubt that it is important to preserve the economic viability of enterprises and to take account of the specific nature of the industry in this sector, which is largely made up of small and mediumsized enterprises. however, it is equally important to ensure a balance between the economic aspect and the aspect relating to the protection of passenger rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on passenger rights in bus and coach transport, as it introduces a strengthening of the rights of citizens using these means of transport, in particular compensation for passengers in the event of delay, cancellation or accidents and assistance for disabled people.
in writing. − whatever the means of transport used, passengers have the right to a quality and safe service, which is why i welcome the intention to introduce harmonised standards on passenger rights in bus transport throughout the eu. i also believe that passengers' rights should be generally the same, whatever the means of transport used, except where this is incompatible with the characteristics of the transport in question. it seems reasonable to me that states should defend their right to exempt certain operators of scheduled urban, suburban and regional transport services, including services for the implementation of the regulation, provided that they are bound by rules of national law or contractual obligations to respect the rights of passengers. we must not forget that in europe there are not only large hauliers but also small and medium-sized hauliers, which we will have to look at with particular care. finally, i congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on their conciliation work with the council and hope that it will be possible to reach agreement on the final version of this regulation as soon as possible.
in writing. the european union should make it a strategic and priority line of action to create the conditions for promoting and enhancing the use of public transport. it is a key issue for the success of a europe committed to combating climate change and urban pollution, to preferring renewable energy sources and to reducing dependence on fossil energy sources. in this context, i would like to stress the contribution of this report to ensuring not only an efficient network of connections but also conditions of comfort, quality of service, safety and assistance, seeking to reconcile the rights of citizens, in particular the concerns about the rights of disabled people and people with reduced mobility, with the need to take account of the viability of transport companies, especially in this period of severe economic crisis. the preservation of the economic viability of undertakings, taking into account the specificities of the bus transport industry, must therefore be reconciled with a high level of protection for passengers, comparable to that already existing for other modes of transport.
in writing. - the amendments proposed at second reading generally guarantee an improvement in the rights of passengers in public transport by road, which we value. we note that the amendments adopted further improve the previous version by ensuring, inter alia: - that passengers should be able to benefit from liability rules comparable to those applicable to other modes of transport in the event of an accident resulting in death or bodily injury; - that carriers must be liable for loss of or damage to passengers' baggage on terms comparable to those applicable to other modes of transport; - that the member states should promote the use of public transport and introduce interoperable and intermodal information systems to provide timetables and prices by issuing multimodal tickets in order to optimise the use and interoperability of the various modes of transport; these services must be accessible to persons with disabilities; - that bus transport companies will be liable for loss or damage resulting from the death or bodily injury of passengers caused by accidents related to the provision of transport services.
in writing. - the lack of regulation on passenger rights in bus and coach transport makes it necessary to adopt this legislative resolution, as passengers' rights must always be safeguarded, regardless of the transport they use. it is also very important to adapt transport infrastructure, new vehicles and refurbishments of used vehicles to the needs of passengers with reduced mobility.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of accidents. the position outlined by the council on the proposed regulation has emptied the substance of both the commission's 2008 proposal and the position adopted by parliament at first reading, which would then have greatly limited the scope of the report and would have exempted most bus service providers from the scope of the future regulation. i would like to see a full legal framework for adequate protection against the loss of luggage, delays and cancellations of services, and above all for the liability of companies in the event of death and damage. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments tabled by mr cancian to ensure that the passengers concerned, in particular the disabled and those with reduced mobility, have access to a suitable means of transport and are provided with an adequate level of protection, always bearing in mind the difficult economic environment in which we live and the need for the companies providing this type of service to survive.
in writing. − the full liberalisation of the passenger shipping market can only be achieved when consumers (and not just companies) can make the most of its benefits. it is essential to give consumers effective rights to ensure that liberalisation allows for real choices. we must not forget that 22 of the 27 member states of the eu are coastal countries, and it is therefore urgent to ensure safety and security for the users of these means of transport, so that we can harmonise the protection measures for these passengers with those for other means of transport. it should be remembered that in some matters the regulation of seafarers' rights was scattered and differed from state to state. the new set of rules will provide european citizens with immediate solutions in the event of delays, cancellations or denied boarding, information obligations for passengers and means of complaint and redress. i particularly welcome the provisions introduced by the european parliament for disabled passengers and passengers with reduced mobility, particularly as regards accessibility, non-discrimination and assistance. by enshrining a general principle of not refusing to transport such persons, the fight against social exclusion is ensured and a union of persons without internal borders is achieved.
in writing. - following the success of the community initiatives on the regulation of passenger rights in air and rail transport, we now have a proposal for the regulation of passenger rights in maritime and inland waterway transport. as i said in connection with the recommendation we have just voted on, whatever the means of transport used, they have the right to a quality and safe service, which is why i think it is good that harmonized standards on passenger rights are being introduced. i also believe that passengers' rights should be generally the same, whatever the means of transport used, except where this is incompatible with the characteristics of the transport in question.
in writing. - in defence of equal treatment and criteria for users of different types of public transport, whether air, sea or land, i support this report, in order to ensure the protection of citizens' rights in extraordinary and exceptional situations that may arise in the use of maritime transport. the burden of proving that a vessel cannot carry out a transport operation because of exceptional circumstances or adverse weather conditions should clearly fall on the carrier. i would stress that safety conditions must not be neglected or put on the back burner. the complaints system shall be accessible and clear to passengers. i welcome the fact that the time limits for resolving complaints, delays in notification, replacement equipment and compensation have been strengthened from the passenger's point of view. combating exclusion is a priority for the eu. i therefore believe that the rights of disabled passengers and those with reduced mobility must be strongly guaranteed.
in writing. − the union must take care of the rights of passengers travelling by sea and inland waterways, so that they enjoy a high level of protection comparable to that already existing in other modes of transport. passengers with reduced mobility due to illness, age or any other factor should also be able to benefit from the same conditions as other users, which requires investment in terminals and ports.
in writing. the aim of this report is to provide passengers in maritime transport with a legal protection framework similar to that already in place for rail and air transport, with particular emphasis on the case of disabled passengers and those with reduced mobility. i am pleased to see that mention has been made again of natural disasters which, unfortunately, have become increasingly frequent in europe and which cause great damage and lead to potentially tragic situations, and which must therefore be taken into account in order to allow possible precautions to be taken and subsequent claims for assistance. i also think it is important to stress the need to ensure that information for passengers, especially foreigners, is provided in a clear way, particularly with regard to their rights in the event of delays and complaints. for these reasons i voted in favour of the amendments to the council's position.
in writing. − consumer rights must be protected. this legislation is a step in the right direction, giving more rights to passengers travelling by boat and bus. maritime passengers will have rights similar to those provided for by european legislation for air and rail passengers. for example, passengers will be entitled to compensation in the event of delay, cancellation or accidents and to assistance in the case of disabled passengers.
in writing. the effectiveness of the use of information and communication technologies in road transport is indisputable. however, it is found that intelligent transport systems (its) are used in a fragmented, inefficient way. it is urgent to define a legal framework, to harmonise the operation of the systems and to create an efficient cooperation mechanism between all the stakeholders in the tsi. i therefore support the adoption as soon as possible of the its directive in order to accelerate the implementation of these technologies in the road transport sector and at interfaces with other modes of transport. this new directive will make a significant contribution to improving environmental performance, energy efficiency, transport safety and the mobility of passengers and goods. the internal market is working properly!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on intelligent transport systems in the field of road transport and interfaces with other modes of transport, as these will make it possible to improve the safety and organisation of european transport systems, making them more efficient from an economic and environmental point of view.
in writing. - this proposal proposes a legal framework for the deployment of its in europe in the field of road transport and interfaces with other means (gps, automatic alarm system and traffic control instruments). the aim of this directive is to ensure greater interoperability of the transport system and to create an effective cooperation mechanism between all the parties concerned in the its. the four priority areas identified are: (i) better use of traffic routes and travel data; (ii) management of european transport corridors; (iii) road safety; and (iv) vehicle integration into transport infrastructure. all these objectives make road transport more efficient, safer, greener and ensure better interoperability with other means of transport, and are therefore conditions for the effective implementation of its systems. the agreement now reached with the council, and reflected in this recommendation, will, in the rapporteur's words, make it possible to make up for the delays in its applications and services and eliminate inefficiencies in transport, making it more efficient and safer and at the same time contributing to the objective of making transport cleaner.
in writing. − the establishment of a framework for the deployment of a system promoting the interconnection and coordinated sharing of information between the different intelligent land transport systems will be crucial to ensuring more efficient land mobility within the european union. the grouping and harmonization of all the service potential of the different information systems relating to land traffic, which operate in a disconnected and independent manner, will bring great advantages at economic, social and also quality of life levels for citizens, allowing safer and greener, shorter or faster journeys to be planned. it will also be important for better public infrastructure management and transport policy-making. for the better impact of this initiative, i would stress the importance of developing specifications for road transport, particularly as regards links with other means of transport. i support the european parliament's position to commit the member states to the deployment of interoperable applications and services in the field of intelligent transport systems, and to stress the need to ensure seamless access and the creation of an efficient cooperation mechanism between all stakeholders.
in writing. − the deployment of intelligent transport systems (its) in the road sector and their interfaces with other modes of transport are essential to ensure the operability of the systems, to guarantee access to all transport without interruptions and to create cooperation mechanisms between all those involved in the implementation of its. the adoption of this draft legislative resolution is an important step towards the implementation of the its.
in writing. - all measures aimed at simplifying procedures and removing unnecessary formalities for intra-community transport are welcome and deserve my support. we must not forget that more bureaucracy means higher costs for businesses and, in many cases, loss of efficiency, which we cannot allow in the present crisis. we know that administrative burdens (and the additional costs they impose) have made the transport of goods by sea less attractive and have been a major obstacle to its full development, even though it is the mode of transport which is least harmful to the environment and, therefore, the one which should be most promoted and supported in a framework of clean development. i therefore look forward to the proposal for administrative simplification (by reducing customs formalities, guidelines for plant health inspections and streamlining documents) now being put forward, and hope that it will be an impetus for a new lease of life in intra-community shipping.
in writing. - in this period of severe economic crisis and weak dynamism in the various sectors of activity, aggravated by the difficulties of public finances in the states, i consider it a priority to focus on simplifying legislation and regulations in order to make the conditions for the operation of companies and institutions more efficient. shipping is subject to complex administrative procedures, even for ships sailing between two ports in the european union and not entering third country ports, which brings unnecessary burdens and costs. i therefore support measures to reduce bureaucracy, which make it profitable to use new technologies and enhance the concept of the single european area by eliminating complex administrative procedures and also guaranteeing gains through the reduction of administrative burdens. this initiative, to remove unnecessary administrative formalities from intra-european maritime transport of goods and to harmonise procedures in the ports of the different member states, is crucial for the promotion of a european maritime transport area without barriers and for ensuring conditions for a more attractive, efficient, economic and environmentally friendly transport service.
in writing. − maritime transport is undoubtedly one of the greenest modes of transport and should therefore be encouraged in order to achieve the environmental objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. in a time of international crisis, the increase in this transport means a reduction in the administrative costs imposed on shipping companies. the formalities required by european union legislation should therefore be simplified and harmonised. it is essential to create a large european shipping area without barriers.
in writing. - the achievement of freedom of movement in the european area also requires the creation of a european maritime area without barriers, the aim of which is to abolish or simplify controls on ships and goods in intra-community space. the reporting formalities required of ships arriving in or departing from ports of the member states should therefore be simplified and an electronic data transmission system (safeseanet) introduced, with which the national systems should be interoperable, accessible and compatible. i am convinced that a maritime area with fewer formal barriers will make maritime transport more attractive and more efficient and will therefore help to boost related activities, particularly in the coastal areas concerned, such as islands, and i therefore support the measures proposed in this report.
in writing. − the transport sector is crucial in europe in terms of the service it provides to the european, in terms of jobs and in terms of environmental impact. this resolution sets out the main lines for european transport policy for the next 10 years with a particular focus on reducing the impact of transport systems on the problem of climate change. transport is responsible for 25% of co2 emissions in europe. cleaner vehicles and more efficient transport systems are essential to reduce this effect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a sustainable future for transport, because the sustainability of transport is fundamental, not only from an environmental point of view, but also for the social, economic and territorial cohesion of the eu. more efforts and innovative forms of investment are needed to complete the trans-european transport network and ensure the sustainable development of transport in the medium and long term.
in writing. − according to the report, the transport sector in the eu accounts for 10% of wealth (gdp), employs over 10 million people and is responsible for 25% of total co2 emissions. these figures make it clear that talking about the future of the eu, talking about the eu 2020 strategy or even talking about cohesion policies is also talking about transport. if transport policy is to give priority to ensuring the safety of passengers and users (and that is why we have adopted two initiatives on passenger rights today), it cannot ignore other objectives such as the coherent and harmonious development of all regions, linking the coast and the interior and the large cities to the most deprived areas, or environmental protection and the reduction of co2 emissions, giving priority to less polluting means such as maritime and rail transport, which should become a priority for the transport of goods. an adequate and efficient transport network is essential to the practical realisation of the internal market and to allow the free movement of people and goods. that is why we have voted today on a proposal on intelligent transport systems (its) which will enable more integrated, safer and more efficient european transport.
in writing. the transport sector is of great importance for the completion of the european internal market. it is this sector which effectively allows the free movement of people and goods throughout the eu. it is also an essential element in the development of the eu and its regions and has a direct influence on the social cohesion of the regions. transport policy must therefore not be dissociated from other policies: regional, environmental, economic, social and employment policies. the transport sector produces 10% of the eu's wealth in terms of gross domestic product and provides more than 10 million jobs, but it also accounts for around 25% of total co2 emissions. i would therefore stress that the decarbonisation of transport must be a priority. in this context, the possibility of internalising external costs should be emphasised. however, it can only make a decisive contribution to reducing exhaust gases and noise and to reducing transport bottlenecks if two conditions are met: on the one hand, the internalisation of external costs must cover all modes of transport and, on the other hand, revenues must be reversed to the benefit of the sustainability of the infrastructure.
in writing. - the report includes guidelines for the future of the transport sector which we consider to be indisputably necessary, such as investment in more environmentally sustainable transport and its proper articulation, the development of sustainable urban mobility plans, the promotion of public transport, the recognition of passengers' rights, in particular those of people with reduced mobility, the adoption of measures to increase road safety and respect for the rights of workers in the sector. however, this statement of guidelines to be followed is in conflict with the emphasis placed on the completion of the internal market, i.e. with the insistence on liberalization of the sector, whether in rail transport, maritime transport and cabotage transport or in air transport. the dismantling of the public transport sector and its privatisation and consequent subjection to the logic of profit - as is clearly shown by the experience in several member states (which the report omits) - removes it from the democratic control of the citizens and leads precisely to the results contrary to the intentions expressed in the report, to a marked degradation of the service and the amputation and characterisation of its social function. whether in terms of safety, quality and accessibility of the service, or in terms of workers' rights, among other aspects.
in writing. − the transport sector is fundamental to the economic development of the european union and its regions, having a direct influence on the competitiveness and social cohesion of the regions, and also contributing to the development and consolidation of the internal market. given its weight in the economy, this sector will play a key role in the eu 2020 strategy, especially in terms of reducing co2 emissions. therefore, and despite its importance for the economy, employment and the professional and private mobility of people, investment is needed in the environmentally friendly improvement of transport, including road transport, as well as in safety, as this sector was responsible for the deaths of around 39 000 people in 2008. so, despite the crisis that has hit this sector hard, now is the time to make a big transformation of the sector, making it safer, more sustainable and more efficient.
in writing. - i consider the transport sector to be an essential area for the development of the european union and its regions, given its influence on competitiveness and the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the regions and its contribution to the effective completion of the european internal market. it is important to look ahead to the future of transport in terms of sustainability and interoperability and i therefore welcome the proposals in the document which set targets to be achieved by 2020 and which aim, in particular, at a percentage reduction in co2 emissions and a reduction in the accident rate. i also welcome the aspect of efficient co-modality, which is even more relevant in the outermost regions, such as madeira, particularly as regards the link between road, sea and air transport. however, i do not support the initiative to create a specific fund for the dynamisation of the transport sector because i believe that such funding should continue to be provided by the various existing means and guided by the priorities of cohesion policy and whose coordination should be facilitated in the implementation of the various european policies.
in writing. - the ep is directly elected by the citizens. the right to petition gives european citizens the opportunity to address their representatives if they believe their rights have been infringed. it is the duty of parliament to investigate the situation and to do everything in its power to put an end to these violations by providing citizens with the most appropriate and rapid means of redress. the number of petitions received has been increasing, although not all of them have been admissible, which shows that citizens are becoming increasingly aware of this right, which allows the impact of european legislation on the daily lives of eu citizens to be assessed. the lisbon treaty reconfirmed this right as a pillar of european citizenship and created the conditions for increased citizen participation in the eu decision-making process, in order to enhance its legitimacy and accountability. i think it is essential to create incentives for greater participation. the creation of a portal with an interactive multi-step model for petitions to inform citizens about the solutions they can obtain by submitting petitions and the areas covered could help to achieve this.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the report as a whole and congratulate the committee on petitions on the work it has done in 2009. a particularly demanding year for a commission whose agenda is defined by citizens in the exercise of their right to petition the european parliament. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon reaffirms the right to petition as a pillar of european citizenship. however, statistics on the number of inadmissible petitions show that the right to petition, as a tool enabling european citizens to express their concerns to parliament about the effects of european policies and legislation on their daily lives, is still not being used properly by all those who use it. this highlights the need to continue efforts to inform and educate the european citizen about the eu mechanisms and instruments at his disposal. i therefore welcome the proposal to set up a single point of contact at european union level to provide guidance to european citizens when they seek answers and solutions to all the issues they feel are violations of their rights.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, has created the necessary conditions for increased citizen participation in the eu decision-making process with a view to enhancing its legitimacy and accountability. it is clear that european legislation has a direct impact on citizens. they should therefore be encouraged to have a strong participatory attitude in order to give their views on the effectiveness, shortcomings and gaps in the legislation. the right of petition enshrined in the lisbon treaty gives european citizens the possibility of turning to the european parliament whenever they consider that their rights have been infringed. the european parliament, through its committee on petitions, investigates and seeks to resolve any infringements. i am sure that the european parliament will be involved in the formulation of the right of citizens' initiative so that this instrument can fully achieve its objective and ensure greater transparency and accountability in the eu decision-making process, allowing citizens to propose improvements or additions to eu law.
in writing. - the annual report of the committee on petitions shows that european citizens are increasingly turning to their representatives when they feel that their rights have been violated. it is therefore important to improve access to petitions by those concerned, in particular through the internet and electronic means. the majority of petitions continue to express concern about the implementation of european legislation in the internal market and the environment, as these are the areas where member states fail most to implement community directives.
in writing. − the current economic crisis has led to a huge increase in unemployment rates, with a particularly strong impact on the younger population. some 21.4% of young people in the eu are unemployed and kept on the margins of the economy, which is all the more serious when we consider that with the ageing of the population we are putting the eu's own economic and social future at risk. it is also the young workers who are in the most precarious, temporary, low-quality jobs, with the lowest wages and the least social security. it is essential that new employment opportunities be found, which are dignified, regular and permanent, enabling these young people to become self-sufficient. it is up to the member states to invest politically and economically in job creation. they should ensure equal access to education, invest in education and training and strengthen the school guidance system in order to reduce the risk of early school leaving and failure. it is up to the eu to define common strategies and in this respect i support the rapporteur's proposal for the creation of a european youth guarantee which can ensure that any young person in the eu has the right to receive an offer of employment, a traineeship or vocational training after a maximum of 4 months of unemployment.
in writing. - youth unemployment is one of the most important and urgent problems facing europe, currently affecting 5.5 million young people under 25 across the union. a structural problem whose scale and economic and social impact have been greatly increased by the recent economic crisis. it is therefore with a sense of responsibility and the awareness that youth must be placed on the political agenda that i vote in favour of this report. the pressing problem of youth unemployment is accompanied by other risks and social and economic costs for our societies. these are reflected, for example, in the loss of opportunities for economic growth, the erosion of the tax base and its consequences for public investment, the increase in social assistance expenditure, or even the risk of long-term unemployment and social exclusion. i understand that we cannot resign ourselves to losing young europeans to social exclusion. on the contrary, europe has much to gain if it can include young people in the labour market and society through an integrated approach, common strategies and a coherent combination of educational, financial, labour and social policies that confirm the robustness of youth policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on promoting young people's access to the labour market and strengthening the status of traineeships and apprenticeships, both of which are key to ensuring that young people do not bear the costs of the current crisis. the participation of young mothers in the labour market must also be promoted by extending the networks of quality childcare facilities.
in writing. the rapporteur concludes her explanatory statement with the following exhortation: let's turn the lost generation into the generation of hope. i share the desire and the goodwill that this statement contains and i would like to be more certain that this reversal is still possible. i recognise that there is a clear separation between school and academic life and the labour market and the need to bridge this gap so that a smoother transition from school to employment is possible, and to carry out the assessment of the fit between what is taught and working life. while the status of the learner today is clearly different and better than in the past, it is also true that in many cases today's trainees are not given effective training appropriate to their needs and expectations.
in writing. - in the current economic crisis, there are now more than 5.5 million young people under 25 in the eu who are unemployed, which is twice the total unemployment rate. youth unemployment has a heavy social and economic cost for our societies, resulting in lost opportunities for economic growth, an erosion of the tax base that has hampered investment in infrastructure and public services, increased costs of social assistance and under-utilisation of investment in education and training. europe's youth is a wellspring of untapped human resources. the forecasts of the economic and social situation call for action. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report which aims to create more inclusion in the labour market through better jobs, a proper transition to the labour market and tackling precarious working conditions. i would like to highlight in this context my proposals for the 2011 eu budget to give priority to youth. i also mention the proposal to help young people to get their first job on the european labour market through erasmus 1st employment.
in writing. - while this report does highlight the serious problem of youth unemployment, which is currently at twice the rate of unemployment in general, it does not propose any substantive measures to actually solve the situation, which would require a break with the current policies of the stability pact and other monetarist, liberal and anti-social policies in force. while emphasising the fight against youth unemployment, the promotion of training and employment for young people and the need to end the abuse of traineeships and training, often unpaid, as a substitute for work rather than a complement to education and training, the report does not point to safe ways out of this situation. but even more worrying is the defence of the concept of flexicurity as a way of ending youth unemployment and a way of transitioning from the education system to the labour market. the reality is that this means the precariousness of low-paid and insecure work, which hinders any project for the lives of young people. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - youth unemployment is one of europe's most pressing problems. with the global economic recession, this problem is becoming even more worrying, since we are faced with more than 5.5 million young people under 25 unemployed. we risk losing a generation to social exclusion, putting the eu's economic and social future at risk. youth unemployment has enormous social and economic costs for our societies, and consequently seriously affects the opportunity for economic growth, a loss of taxation that delays investment in infrastructure and public services, an increase in the cost of social assistance and an under-utilisation of investment in education and training. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on atypical contracts, job security, flexicurity and new forms of social dialogue. atypical employment relationships are defined as new forms of employment contract which have one or more of the following characteristics: parttime, occasional, temporary, fixed-term, home-based and teleworking, parttime work for a period of 20 hours or less per week. the financial and economic crisis facing the european union could lead to unstable labour markets and increasing social exclusion. it is therefore urgent to help member states safeguard as many jobs and employment in europe as possible. efforts to invest in skills, training and sustainable job creation need to be intensified, as well as the promotion of the principles of flexicurity. under the eu 2020 strategy, clear guidelines and concrete measures to protect employment and create job opportunities should be proposed.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the majority of the measures proposed in this report. the economic crisis has, of course, led to a significant increase in the number of atypical contracts and precarious working conditions. and that they have a greater impact on young people and women. however, i believe that the european social model, whose objectives focus on sustainable growth, full employment, the promotion of well-being and social protection, has the necessary conditions and means to lead the eu and its member states through the crisis. in this regard, i would like to highlight two aspects which i consider vital in the face of the current economic crisis and abnormally high unemployment figures in the eu, with a view to protecting quality and decent employment and creating new job opportunities under the 2020 strategy. the first concerns the need to step up investment in skills, vocational and lifelong training. the second concerns the importance of effective implementation of flexicurity strategies, thus making it possible to combat illegal employment and reduce job insecurity.
in writing. − in recent years, following the global economic crisis, unemployment in the eu has risen exponentially (to 10% at the end of 2009). with the current model having proven to be both ineffective and not the most suitable for job protection, it is essential that we find new ways of overcoming the crisis and creating a sustainable long-term employment policy. so i think the key is to invest in training workers, in the specific skills of each person and in innovation. the rigid models of labour law have proven to fail. the example of the united states shows that flexibility is not synonymous with insecurity but with dynamism in the labour market. this is what the figures quoted in the report show when they tell us that only 10% of unemployed people in the us last more than a year, compared with 45% (!) in the eu. this is what i believe europe should be looking for in the european concept of flexicurity. atypical contracts (part-time; shift, occasional or temporary work; homework; teleworking, etc.) should not be regarded with suspicion simply because they are atypical. society has evolved, the world has changed, and industrial relations must necessarily keep pace with this change.
in writing. − atypical employment relationships are defined as new forms of contract which have one or more of the following characteristics: parttime, occasional, temporary, fixed-term, homework and telework, parttime work for a period of 20 hours or less per week. the jobs lost as a result of the current crisis were primarily those in the atypical work sector, where it is more difficult to find a new job. more than one fifth of european workers change jobs every year. in the eu, 45% of all unemployment periods last more than a year, compared with about 10% in the us. it calls on the council to take this reality into account and to adopt concrete measures to protect quality and decent employment and create sustainable work opportunities in the framework of the eu 2020 strategy. a set of essential rights should be guaranteed to all employed persons, irrespective of their employment status. i also support the urgent extension of the protection of workers in atypical forms of employment. the eu cannot lose its european social model, but must strengthen it.
in writing. - we voted against this report on atypical contracts, safe working practices, flexicurity and new forms of social dialogue, because, although it has some positive points, such as the encouragement of the transition from typical forms of work to formal forms of work, the report in general is mainly about promoting flexicurity. this is illustrated by many of the articles in the report, in particular where it refers to: it considers that an update of the thinking on flexicurity at european level is essential in the light of the current crisis, in order to contribute to increasing productivity and the quality of jobs, ensuring job security and protection of workers' rights, ... allowing companies the necessary organisational flexibility to create or reduce jobs in response to the ever-changing needs of the market. what we do know is that employers and governments at community level are not looking for a fair and balanced application of the principles of flexicurity which can help to make labour markets stronger in the event of structural changes. on the contrary, as has happened in portugal, precariousness is increasing and safety is decreasing, with increasingly weakening labour relations and the rights of those who work.
in writing. - a europe that is increasingly focused on its citizens must seek to be inclusive in the labour market. in this time of severe economic and financial crisis, it is necessary to take advantage of all the mechanisms that allow us to save jobs, especially among the most vulnerable parts of the labour market. the social partners are also called upon to take the necessary steps to ensure that the social partners are able to take part in the negotiations.
in writing. − the selective collection and recycling of bio-waste is fundamental to europe's sustainable development. i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the european commission to draw up a proposal for a specific directive on bio-waste by the end of the year. the new legislation should stipulate the mandatory selective collection and recycling of bio-waste.
in writing. - waste treatment is a problem affecting europe and humanity. tons of waste are generated every day, causing harmful environmental damage and negative impacts on the health and quality of life of citizens. i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr josé manuel fernandes, on his excellent work. the current legislation on bio-waste does not meet the needs of regulation of the matter. i welcome the initiative to propose a specific directive to achieve the objectives of effective and sustainable management of bio-waste (better legislation, simplification, clarity and legal certainty). the problem is not only the harmful environmental impact of the normal landfilling of this waste, but also the relevant role in fertilizing the soil and the entire energy potential underlying it (via biogas) which can be used to generate electricity, heating or automobile fuel. a specific directive on the management of bio-waste seems to me to be a basic corollary to the implementation of the principles contained in the framework directive on waste. it is necessary to compile scattered standards, harmonize practices and boost the internal market through environmental synergy, recycling and the creation of green jobs. a resource-efficient europe is not just a europe 2020, it is a europe of the future!
in writing. − efficient management of bio-waste not only provides environmental benefits but also makes a positive contribution to society and the economy. i therefore vote in favour of the proposals contained in this report. the importance of improving the efficiency of bio-waste management and of prioritising prevention/reduction of bio-waste will contribute to the promotion of sustainable development and sustainable management of natural resources. the positive effects of better management of bio-waste should not be overlooked, in particular the impact on the functioning of the internal market, on the future of agriculture through the preservation and restoration of soil fertility or the promotion of renewable energy. the importance of bringing together the vast body of legislation on bio-waste management into a single piece of legislation and the need to harmonise member states' policies through a specific bio-waste directive is thus underlined.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the commission's green paper on the management of bio-waste in the european union, as it will strengthen environmental protection in the eu and help combat climate change by making selective collection and recycling of bio-waste compulsory.
in writing. − the mere observation of the amount of bio-waste we throw out daily and which comes from our private consumption should alert us to the need to explore properly the best ways of using it and of reducing its impact on the environment. if we add industrial consumption to private consumption, this need quickly takes on an urgent character and should motivate both policy-makers and experts to persist in studying the most appropriate processes and methods. i believe that a directive aimed at an effective improvement in the management of this type of waste could be of great benefit to all citizens in the member states.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this resolution, for which i am rapporteur, which calls for the development of a specific directive on bio-waste by the end of 2010 and the establishment of a mandatory separate collection system for member states, except where this is not the best option from an environmental and economic point of view. the amount of bio-waste generated in the eu is estimated to be around 100 million tonnes per year. waste is the fourth largest source of greenhouse gases in the eu, especially when landfilled. the resolution aims to encourage the diversion of bio-waste from landfills, to encourage the production of high-quality compost to recover soils without chemicals and to stimulate the creation of renewable energy. the european commission has so far insisted that a directive on this waste stream is unnecessary. i hope that the commissioner responsible for the environment dg will read the report, understand the position of the large majority in parliament and stop taking an autistic view on this matter. our position is ambitious and realistic. we are calling for a specific directive that brings clarity and legal certainty, and we hope that the commissioner will live up to parliament's ambition.
in writing. - the management of bio-waste, which is absolutely necessary for the healthy existence of the human species and its harmonious balance with nature, should not be seen in the light of narrow commercial interests. the report under discussion refers to the obligation for member states to have a separate collection system and the appropriate treatment of bio-waste through anaerobic digestion and composting. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. apart from the technical difficulties inherent in the proposed treatment, which cannot be ignored, it is much more expensive. the question which the report fails to answer is: who will pay? the report is laconic in terms of measures to prevent the production of waste, with the discourse focusing almost exclusively on recycling. reduction is one of the best ways of combating waste problems. the possibility of home composting is mentioned, which allows many bio-waste to be diverted from the general treatment system - a question not addressed in the report. as for the compound, it is not enough to say that it must be produced. the conditions must be created for its use, without restrictions and without adequate technical or scientific justification, which only favours the strong competitor, the fertiliser industry.
in writing. − i consider measures to improve the management of bio-waste in the european union, taking advantage of its wide-ranging environmental and economic benefits, to be fundamental. with the economic and territorial expansion of the european union, the quantities of waste generated are increasing, with the amount of bio-waste produced annually in the eu estimated at around 100 million tonnes of food and garden waste and 37 million tonnes of waste from the food and beverage industry. many of these biodegradable garden, kitchen and food waste can and should be harnessed as a source of renewable energy and in recycled materials. in this way we will not only be contributing to the fight against climate change, but also to the promotion of healthier soils and the slowing of biodiversity loss.
in writing. - i welcome the overwhelming approval of this report, as it focuses on the pressing issue of the management of bio-waste in the eu and moves towards calling on the european commission to draw up a directive creating a mandatory separate collection system for all member states. in fact, waste management is a serious and current problem that needs urgent resolution, especially when we consider that the eu produces about 100 million tonnes of bio-waste per year. it should also be stressed that the eu's commitment to combating climate change, which it is a world leader in, requires proper waste management, as waste is the fourth largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the eu. biowaste can also be reused for bioenergy and biofuel production. the recycling industry currently creates up to 250 jobs for every 10 000 tonnes of waste recycled. the call for a specific directive on bio-waste management is an important contribution of this report, recognising that the current bio-waste standards are fragmented and that greater clarity, simplification and legal certainty are needed.
in writing. - the management of bio-waste in the eu is an extremely important issue nowadays, not only because of the massive amount of waste produced annually (estimated at 139 million tonnes), but also because of the constant climate change we are witnessing. the production of bio-waste, by definition, is inevitable, but what can be avoided is its mismanagement, particularly in the case of landfilling, which is the main source of emissions of gases to the ozone layer. this waste can be transformed into a social asset, because if we can extract benefits from it, then we can renew industries and harness resources that would otherwise be untapped. i am referring, among other things, to its capacity to be used for the production of bioenergy, which can be converted into electricity and heating, or biofuels, as an alternative to fossil resources which are practically exhausted by the incessant demand. the report is an important step towards the sustainable development of the union and i believe, in full agreement with the rapporteur, that the best way to achieve the objectives set out, both for environmental policy and for the internal market, will be through the drawing up of a directive on bio-waste.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, the european project, which has been built up with such effort over the last 50 years, has never been more threatened than it is today. the frustration of european citizens is enormous, the financial system that was supposed to serve them has destroyed their savings, their pensions, their investment projects, their jobs, in short, their future. the way forward is clear and lies in the architecture we have discussed here today. we need a strong european supervisory architecture covering all products and all actors, with effective intervention methodologies and instruments, and able to respond to the reality of a market which, especially in the european context, does not recognise national borders. risk cannot and should not be eliminated from the financial market, but we need regulation to make this risk more transparent and to prevent the accumulation of bubbles whose bursting affects the whole system and spreads to the real economy. but if, despite these defenses, new crises occur in the future, it is crucial to have mechanisms in place to limit contagion, especially in the banking system, because it is vital to the functioning of the economy and is the depository of citizens' savings. it is precisely in the powers and competences of the banking authority that lies the capacity to implement a new strategy for crossborder crisis management in the banking sector, the subject of my report. it is not in our hands to prevent banks from going bankrupt, but to ensure that their reorganisation or eventual liquidation is carried out in an orderly manner, limiting the side effects on the rest of the system and, above all, avoiding the taxpayer from paying the costs of the crises they generate. this requires a set of new provisions, the adoption of rules, definitions, methodologies, instruments and terminology common to all those involved in restructuring, reorganisation or liquidation operations. the national legal frameworks relevant to crisis management, in particular bankruptcy and liquidation laws, need to be harmonised. it is necessary to confer on supervisors extended powers of intervention. clear criteria, not only quantitative but also qualitative, must be drawn up to enable an institution in difficulty to be assisted. we need to prepare contingency plans. this whole process for 27 member states takes time. however, some 50 of the 12 000 banks operating in europe account for 70% of assets. this means a huge concentration of risk, but also an opportunity to act on them first. there are therefore grounds for proposing a special and urgent procedure for the regulation of banks which, because of their cross-border nature and their relationships with other banks, have a possible
