systemic impact on the financial system. for these banks, it is possible to anticipate special supervision by the new european banking authority, although it will operate in the college of national supervisors. it is possible and urgent that they should, in view of the risk they pose, start making contributions to a fund to finance any intervention that may be necessary; it is important that the banking authority establishes a specialised unit to coordinate the intervention in the event of a crisis in these banks. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment is based on the principle of the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment against pollution. this proposal fits perfectly into what we are discussing, especially the powers of the banking authority, which i would even say is the most obvious test of its effectiveness. the vote in the economic and monetary committee was overwhelmingly in favour of this proposal, 87% of the votes cast. we also count here in the house on the massive vote of this institution that, by massively supporting this proposal, which is visionary, which is realistic but which is pragmatic, we will take the urgent action needed to revive the hope of europeans in europe, in its financial system and, in particular, in the banking system.
the rapporteur. - i shall try to be very brief and to emphasise only four points. the first of these is that it has been an extraordinary experience to work in such solidarity with my colleagues from the other political forces. i am very grateful to you for including me in the monitoring package and in particular i am very grateful to mr garcia margallo for all the cooperation that was possible. secondly, i would like to thank my personal collaborators and also the colleagues who contributed to the specific report i am responsible for, which enabled me to incorporate 90% of their proposals. a special word to the secretariat, to susana vravova and to the committee services. finally, my thanks to the commissioner and his services, and the very clear expression of hope that, on the basis of the report, which i hope will be adopted tomorrow, it will indeed be possible to build a solid basis, a truly european basis which protects the citizens.
the new directive creates a more demanding and up-to-date regulatory framework for industrial emissions, which we consider to be an important step towards better protection of the environment and public health, in particular for people living and working in the vicinity of industrial complexes or in areas under their influence. the setting of emission limit values for a wide range of pollutants and the need for large emitters to adapt to these limit values by means of the best available technologies establish an important principle: that in order to protect the environment and public health we must implement the best available technologies in production processes, especially those with the greatest environmental impact. this is the approach we are also advocating for emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. the use of market instruments such as carbon trading, which the european union has been advocating, is countered by the need for a regulatory approach that is environmentally effective and socially fair, as opposed to the merchant approach. we therefore welcome the rejection, at this second reading, of the application of emission trading to nitrogen oxides and sulphur dioxide which some have called for, and we note the amendment which clarifies the possibility of setting limit values and therefore a regulatory approach, rather than a market approach, also for carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases subject to the european emission trading scheme. however, in pursuing this overall effort to reduce emissions, we cannot fail to take account of the differences between member states and the specificities of each. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not distorted by the effects of the crisis. the compromise reached ensures that this diverse reality is respected. the planned, appropriate and justified derogations and the transitional national plans ensure the necessary flexibility in the implementation of the best available technologies without compromising the original objectives of protecting the environment and public health. we also welcome the express possibility for member states to maintain or adopt more stringent protective measures than those laid down in this directive, in particular those relating to the greenhouse gas emissions already mentioned. in order to safeguard sustainable production in the different member states and regions, this new regulatory framework now established should be complemented by community measures to support the modernisation of production systems, in particular in the most vulnerable economies. finally, it is also essential to support public r&d investment that ensures the evolution and continuous improvement of the best available technologies.
i would also like to begin by thanking the rapporteurs for their excellent work. deforestation, as we know, is one of the major environmental and social problems on the planet, and every year we lose 13 million hectares of forest, contributing to 20% of global carbon emissions and posing a huge threat to biodiversity. the contribution of deforestation to climate change is undeniable and as such is largely responsible for the occurrence of extreme weather events and floods or even desertification of vast areas of the planet. the loss of forests puts all of humanity at risk, but that risk and that impact are not shared equally by all of us. communities with fewer resources and communities that rely more on the forest and nature for their survival are the most affected. deforestation is about our collective existence, about the scarcity of natural resources, about their distribution, about the rights of local and indigenous communities, about social justice. the main cause of deforestation is illegal logging, which accounts for 20 to 40 percent of the world's industrial timber production. so we are also talking about a transfer of wealth from the producing countries to the consuming countries of the same wood. this illegal practice puts at risk the sustainable exploitation of timber and the companies that make it. it's not enough to say nice things. this parliament must take strong and consistent action in this fight. this report takes a very significant step in that direction by defining the prohibition of trade in timber. good intentions are not enough either. effective means are needed, namely sanctions, which in this case can be of three types. first, fines which effectively take away the economic benefit of the illegal practice, increased by repeated offence. secondly, the confiscation of the timber and the products in question. and thirdly, the immediate suspension of the authorization to carry on a commercial activity. and that is why anyone who harvests or markets a natural resource must be socially responsible, and so too anyone who brings timber or timber products into the european union for the first time must be required to take steps to ensure that it is legally harvested timber. therefore, all operators below must provide basic information on such wood, in particular its origin and destination. the people must also have the right - and i end here, mr president - to have access to information about who is complying and who is not.
mr president, europe needs to renew its confidence and hope. in a crisis that has not yet been overcome, we had the fire brigade, as jacques delors said. we hope that the belgian presidency will bring in the architects. the first test, of course, will be the council's approach to parliament's proposals on the financial architecture as early as september. but today one of the greatest challenges for europe is to ensure that the european currency does not collapse, whether because of a lack of follow-up instruments, or because of a lack of growth in the eurozone, or above all because of the growing divergences and internal tensions caused by the economies that make it up. cutting structural funds today, as the commission proposes, which were created to stimulate convergence between divergent economies, seems to be fuelling a fire that has not yet been extinguished. we clearly need architects. one last question, please. i would like to know the external dimension of the european union's action, in particular to know a little more about what the belgian presidency is proposing for cancun and doha.

mr president, mr leterme, i want to say first of all that i listened to you very carefully and i also read your programme very carefully and so i will start with something you said to us here today when you presented yourself, which was that a european union with a monetary government but without economic governance does not work. i could not agree more, and that is why i am calling for the measures for this economic governance to be clear, transparent, but above all democratic, because they have not yet existed. the commission has not yet taken a decision on the budget, and the strengthening and the objectives set are in the direction of more of the stability and growth pact, more insistence on the deficit and public debt. and we know very well that these measures are measures which, once again, will strengthen that monetary governance, but not the economic governance which is necessary and urgent. and that is why wage reduction measures, such as those which have been applied in the context of the stability and growth plans, do not make for competitive growth, and therefore to insist on the same is to insist on recessionary measures which will only bring about more recession. i would also like to say that we are not yet very satisfied with the new architectures they are announcing and with the additional measures and the continuation of the important initiatives taken in the european area in recent months. so perhaps it was to apply what had been announced, rather than announce new things. because not only was it not applied, we didn't feel it, the greeks didn't feel it either. and i think it is essential that we make progress once and for all towards social and economic integration in a decent and transparent way.
in writing. belgium takes over the eu presidency at a time when many of the consequences of the systemic crisis of capitalism are becoming more acute. the crisis in the eu is also, as is becoming clear, a crisis in the very foundations of the integration process itself. more than 85 million people in the eu have fallen into poverty. the number of people who are not in the labour force is very high, and according to the criteria proposed in recent weeks, it could be much higher, over 100 million. structural imbalances within the eu are worsening. economic and social cohesion is increasingly a mere propaganda device, a dead letter in the treaties. the seriousness of the situation contrasts with the complete absence of measures to deal with it. on the contrary, in the face of the crisis, the eu's revenue - with the strengthening of the stability and growth pact and the consequent attacks on wages, social rights and the social functions of the states - will inevitably lead to an even sharper economic decline and an even more rigid social regression. in this context, the intensification of the social struggle in the various countries will certainly mark the six months of the belgian presidency. being a factor of hope and confidence in a better future!
belgium takes over the presidency of the european union at a time of economic and social challenges for a number of countries. this presidency should be used to prepare and debate the fifth report on cohesion policy which is expected to be adopted by the commission by november and to bring more emphasis to the structural funds in the europe 2020 strategy as well as to the relationship between cohesion and regional competitiveness through the continuation of governance covering the various institutional levels, namely european, national, regional and local. the october summit on the new european innovation strategy will also be an opportunity for national leaders to seek greater clarity on issues such as the funding of innovation and the indicators that will be used to measure it. i cannot but stress that the allocation of more resources to this field, the financing of which in the outermost regions of europe must be given special attention, must be accompanied by the promotion of the proximity between universities and research centres and the national business fabric. only in this way can this commitment be reflected in real business opportunities and greater competitiveness for our companies in the context of industrial conversion.
madam president, i think that, after the results of these previous votes and because we need a qualified majority, as a democratic requirement we should repeat the vote on amendment 5. (applause)
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because i consider that, in the chapter on effective governance in the area of remuneration, shareholders should have the possibility to contribute to the determination of sustainable remuneration policies and that, to this end, they could have the possibility to express their opinion on remuneration policies by means of a non-binding vote at the general meeting of the company on the remuneration report, and that members involved in risk control should be independent of the business units they control, have appropriate authority and be remunerated independently of the performance of these business units.
in writing. - aware that the lack of effective control instruments contributes significantly to excessive risk-taking by financial institutions and of the importance of the management of listed companies taking account of the stability of the financial system, i vote in favour of the general measures proposed in this report. indeed, with the current economic and financial crisis, it has become clear that the inappropriate level of remuneration practised by some companies has encouraged an excessive and reckless practice of risk taking, aimed at maximising short-term profit. such repeated practices have led to the development of risk-based business models to the detriment of the sustainable growth of companies. measures should therefore be taken to reduce the risks taken and to re-shape the incentive system. in this connection, rather than launching a european initiative on remuneration policy in the financial sector and in listed companies, coordinated european action is required in the field of the remuneration of directors of these companies.
in writing. − the remuneration of directors of listed companies has been at the forefront of discussions about the economic crisis. a remuneration policy based on principles of transparency, rewarding long-term rather than short-term results and preventing excessive risk-taking, as has sometimes been observed in the past, is essential. it should also be borne in mind that the elements of an effective remuneration policy should be approved by the general meeting of shareholders with a view to fair compensation of directors for their work.
in writing. − the recent economic and financial crisis has raised the issue of remuneration for directors of listed companies and remuneration policies in the financial services sector. the search for short-term results to achieve socalled variable remuneration can sometimes lead to less prudent management practices that protect the interests of workers, shareholders and society at large. the systemic risk arising from the fact that large financial groups operate on a global scale leads to measures to regulate these variable remunerations in order to safeguard future situations of fragility of the financial undertakings concerned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because of the set of guidelines it advocates. i consider it appropriate to ensure: 1. effective governance in the area of remuneration - whereas supervisory authorities should be able to decide whether a financial institution or a listed company should have a remuneration committee; 2. effective alignment between remuneration and prudent risk-taking - by adjusting remuneration to the types of risk that impact the overall performance and stability of the company; - by basing variable remuneration levels on predetermined and measurable performance criteria; - by stating that remuneration plans should not include guaranteed premiums; 3. a balanced structure of the remuneration package - through the dissemination by enterprises of clear, comprehensive and timely information on their remuneration practices, - through the publication of details of the pension and supplementary pension arrangements of companies, including those relating to public enterprises.
in writing. − the novel food regulation states that food produced with nanotechnologies should only be authorised after being subjected to evaluation methods. the regulation also states that food derived from cloned animals or their descendants should not be authorised in the european union. we are facing new situations and the precautionary principle should apply. it will be essential to deepen scientific knowledge in these areas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on novel foods because it introduces new rules which will strengthen the safety of these foods in the eu. i also believe that food derived from cloned animals or their descendants should not be allowed in the european union.
in writing. the aim of the regulation is to ensure food security by promoting the widest possible path from farm to table. we therefore have concerns about production processes, labelling and market monitoring. i support these concerns precisely because they allow the consumer to make an informed choice about the food he eats, with a good knowledge of its composition and how it is produced. however, in the face of the increasing trend towards eu regulation in these matters, i would like to recall what has happened to gm cereals, which were once banned in the union but are freely imported from third countries. this puts european producers at a disadvantage when their products compete on supermarket shelves with others, which are essentially the same but with faster and cheaper production methods, allowing them to become more attractive to the consumer. finally, i would point out that in the united states the fda has already approved the consumption of cloned animals as food (2008). this, like the past with gmos, poses real problems for europe in importing these products and makes it urgent to regulate this matter.
in writing. − this regulation lays down harmonised rules for the placing of novel foods on the community market in order to ensure a high level of protection of human health and life, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests, while ensuring the transparency and effective functioning of the internal market and stimulating innovation in the agri-food industry. the regulation applies to food additives, food enzymes, food flavourings and certain food ingredients with flavouring properties, the production of which has been subjected to a new process, not used before 15 may 1997, which results in significant changes in the composition or structure of food, such as artificial nanomaterials. where a novel food is likely to have an effect on the human body comparable to that of a medicinal product, the commission shall request the european medicines agency (ema) to determine whether that novel food falls within the scope of regulation (ec) no 726/2004. i am in favour of excluding food produced from cloned animals and their progeny from the scope of the regulation. i do not see any justification for the consumption of cloned animals, because i am not convinced that cloning does not jeopardize the welfare of the animal.
in writing. − the novel food regulation aims to establish harmonised rules for the placing of novel foods on the community market in order to ensure a high level of protection of human health and life, animal health and welfare, the environment and the interests of consumers. we voted in favour of this second reading because we believe that the proposed amendments are in line with these objectives. the document also calls on the commission to submit a legislative proposal to prohibit the placing on the community market of food derived from cloned animals and their descendants, as has already been done in other texts such as the resolution of 3 september 2008. this is a correct and proper application of the precautionary principle. we also welcome the indication that new foods placed on the market need to be monitored. unfortunately, the majority of parliament has again rejected the need to label food containing genetically modified organisms (gmos) or animals fed gmos, calling into question the principle of transparency, information and consumer choice.
in writing. - without rigor, products that may cause problems for society cannot be approved. this regulation is therefore of the utmost importance for the european market, as it safeguards food safety and human health. food produced using nanotechnologies should be subject to a specific risk assessment before it can be approved, labelled and placed on the european market. food produced from cloned animals or their descendants is a controversial issue, but in my view such food should not be allowed in the european union. the uncertainties about the economic, social and environmental impacts of these new technologies require an increasingly careful assessment. scientists become the main mediators of society's relationship with risk, with the power to anticipate future dangers and decide on the approval of new foods. only foods appearing on the community list may be placed on the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ippc directive, which aims to prevent and control emissions from industrial installations. this is an integrated pollution control covering emissions to air, water and soil. this legislation has a very large impact at european level, as it applies to thousands of industrial plants, thus encouraging european industry to use less polluting and more efficient technologies and processes in terms of the natural resources consumed. this directive will contribute to better air, water and soil quality in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on industrial emissions because i believe that a balanced agreement has been reached on ensuring an integrated approach to reducing emissions while at the same time ensuring the competitiveness of european industry, based on the best available technologies.
in writing. the commission's proposal for a directive aims to consolidate the seven existing directives on industrial emissions into a single instrument. this effort aims to ensure a high level of environmental protection while at the same time standardising and simplifying procedures across the various member states and reducing unnecessary administrative burdens. while recognising the need for an ambitious approach to industrial emissions control, in line with the eu's environmental and climate change objectives, i think it is important to point out that the rules and targets imposed on european industries cannot be so ambitious as to jeopardise their competitiveness in a globalised world. the concept of clean development, which i enthusiastically support, presupposes growth and competitiveness in a more environmentally friendly context. it cannot, therefore, mean more difficulties and more obstacles to european industrial activity.
in writing. − in 2005, the commission initiated a review of the pcip directive, which resulted in a proposal for a directive on industrial emissions that aims to review and merge the seven existing directives on the subject into a single directive. the pcip directive covers some 52 000 industrial installations, whose emissions account for a large proportion of all air pollution in the eu. under this directive, the competent authorities of the member states are required to take account of brefs when granting operating licences to industrial installations and when setting the emission limit values (elvs) applicable to certain installations. in addition to polluting the atmosphere, industrial activity also has negative environmental impacts on water and soil and produces waste. an integrated approach to licensing that takes into account the overall effects on the environment is therefore essential. i welcome the adoption of this report, especially the restriction of derogations by industrial operators.
in writing. - as we said during the debate in plenary, the new directive creates a more demanding regulatory framework for industrial emissions and, with it, conditions for better protection of the environment and public health, in particular for people living and working in the vicinity of industrial complexes or in areas under their influence. the important principle is enshrined that in order to protect the environment and public health, we must implement the best technologies available to us through scientific and technological development in production processes, especially those with the greatest environmental impact. but the compromise reached at second reading also ensures the necessary flexibility in the implementation of the best available technologies (bat) to take due account of the differences between member states and the specificities of each one, from the outset at the level of their production systems and production conditions, as well as at the level of the capacity to implement the necessary adaptations in production technologies and processes. the derogations provided for - appropriate and justified - and the transitional national plans make it possible for the various member states and their undertakings to adapt to the new legislation without compromising national production, while safeguarding the original objectives of protecting the environment and public health.
in writing. - this directive summarises in one text seven previous separate directives on industrial emissions. the prevention and control of emissions from industrial installations into the air, water and soil are key to achieving the objectives of a greener economy as set out in the eu 2020 strategy. it is worth noting that many of the pollutants that will now see their emission reduced are risk factors for health and the environment, contributing to the increase in diseases such as cancer and asthma. it is very important that the emission reduction deadlines set out in this directive are met.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ban on the placing on the european market of illegally harvested timber and timber products. this decision is very important for protecting the world's forests, which are an essential factor in the fight against climate change. it will also contribute to the protection and preservation of europe's forests. the illegal import of timber into europe has the effect of drastically lowering the price of timber, making it financially impossible for european forest owners to maintain the timber properly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on obligations for operators placing timber and timber products on the market because the fight against illegal logging is fundamental to halting biodiversity loss and deforestation and is also a key element in the fight against climate change.
in writing. the alarming rate at which forests are disappearing calls us all to make a serious effort to protect a natural heritage essential to the survival of the human species itself. european consumers should be able to be sure that when they buy wood and wood products, they are not contributing to deforestation or fuelling an illegal trade that takes advantage of the criminal exploitation of forest resources and puts at risk companies that behave responsibly and respectfully towards biodiversity. parliament wants to see greater demands made in combating this scourge and greater rigour in importing and selling, which i think we should support.
in writing. - deforestation continues at a rate of approximately 13 million hectares per year and is responsible for almost 20% of global carbon emissions and is a major cause of biodiversity loss. it is also the source of serious human rights violations, because in many countries forests are of great cultural and social importance to indigenous and forest-dependent peoples. illegal logging is one of the main causes of deforestation, with the volume of industrial timber from illegal logging estimated at 350-650 million m3 per year, representing 20-40% of the world's industrial timber production. it causes the price of timber to fall, deprives us of natural resources and tax revenues and exacerbates the poverty of forest-dependent peoples. as a major consumer of timber and timber products, the eu has an obligation to take effective action against deforestation and illegal logging, which should undoubtedly include a ban on the market for illegal timber and timber products. i support the exclusion of smallholders from the scope of this regulation because i believe that the duty of due diligence is too burdensome.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims to lay down the obligations of operators placing timber and timber products on the market. we understand the need to preserve forest resources, ensuring their rational and sustainable exploitation and maintaining biodiversity in our forests and woodlands. however, the report raises some concerns as regards the operationalisation of the procedures in the member states. given the diversity of countries, for example in terms of the size of the property, the regulation may in some cases prove difficult to implement and may entail high costs. on the other hand, there are still doubts about the concept of illegal logging, which is not consensual, given that there is national legislation which already deals with the appropriate regulation, as in portugal, where there are forest species protected by law, the felling of which requires a special authorization. in this way, besides not adding anything substantially new in the field of forestry protection, this regulation may create constraints on the forestry sector in countries such as portugal, which may affect many small and mediumsized enterprises. the problem of the inadequacy of controls on wood from third countries also persists and needs to be resolved.
in writing. − deforestation and forest degradation are the main factors responsible for biodiversity loss. in turn, illegal logging is the main driver of deforestation, accounting for 20 to 40% of the world's industrial timber production. in order to put an end to this illegality and to apply severe sanctions to those who extract timber illegally, this regulation was adopted. the adoption of this regulation is therefore very important in order to avoid a fall in the price of timber, the deprivation of natural resources for citizens, the loss of tax revenue and the worsening of poverty for the populations that depend economically on the forest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive because i believe that the identification of the areas to be covered by technical standards should strike a fair balance in creating a single set of harmonised rules, avoiding unnecessary complications in regulation and its application. only those areas should be selected where consistent technical standards make a significant and effective contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the relevant legislation, while ensuring that political decisions are taken, in accordance with the current procedures, by the european parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. − as is now clear, due to the consequences of the current economic and financial crisis, the continued success of the european integration process is absolutely dependent on the ability to find solutions for strengthening the competences of integrated supervisory intervention structures at european level. national sovereignty is increasingly dependent on supranational intervention through community structures with resources and powers to act and devise strategies outside the influence of national and isolated wishes and needs. i therefore reaffirm my support for the consolidation of the competences of the european structures responsible for acting and supervising the activities of the various european financial sectors, such as the european banking authority, the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has highlighted major weaknesses in financial supervision, both in individual cases and in relation to the financial system as a whole. the supervisory models were national in scope and did not keep pace with the globalisation that has occurred in the financial system, where various financial groups develop their operations across borders with the resulting systemic risks. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims at an overall improvement in the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. the establishment of a european system of financial supervisors and the definition of their responsibilities are essential to achieve an effective supervisory model in all sectors, in particular banking, insurance and supplementary pensions, and securities and markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i believe that the authority should take into account the impact of its activities on competition and innovation in the internal market, the union's overall competitiveness, financial inclusion and the new eu strategy for jobs and growth. i also agree that in order to achieve its objectives, the authority should have legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy. according to the basel committee on banking supervision, the authority should have powers to deal with the issue of compliance with legislation, in particular with regard to systemic and cross-border risks.
in writing. - for the effective regulation of financial and speculative markets, and in view of the circumstances which have given rise to this crisis with serious consequences for europe and developed countries, it is essential to ensure effective and efficient intervention in securities transactions, in line with the efforts of the european parliament and the other european institutions. the aim is to create a structural basis for monitoring, evaluation, monitoring and action which, within an efficient legal framework, will prevent the recurrence of situations such as those which led to the outbreak of the current economic, financial and social crisis. in this context, a european securities and markets authority, together with the appropriate legal personality, will need to be endowed with legal, administrative and financial autonomy in order to be able to ensure the safety and soundness of markets and the transparency of transactions in order to avoid new systemic risks.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has highlighted major shortcomings in financial supervision, both in individual cases and in relation to the financial system as a whole. the supervisory models were national in scope and did not keep pace with the globalisation that has occurred in the financial system, where various financial groups develop their operations across borders with the resulting systemic risks. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims to improve the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. the creation of the european financial markets authority is essential to achieve an effective supervisory model.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential that the community should supervise the financial system and that a european systemic risk board (esrb) should be set up. it is essential to create an effective supervisory system without impeding the financing of the economy, i.e. to create conditions that allow stable financing of the economy, so as to ensure sustainable growth and employment; to safeguard the single market where the eu must be provided with quality financial supervision to avoid fragmentation of the single market; to allow the eu to maintain its status to defend the euro and the other european currencies, while it is necessary that the eu maintains its status at the level at which decisions are taken, reaffirming its attachment to multilateral procedures, as in this way the eu will be better prepared to assert its values and defend its strategic interests. the establishment of the esrb represents an important innovation for macroeconomic analysis at european level, the main purpose of which is to assess systemic risks. establishing close cooperation between the esrb and, in particular, the national supervisory authorities and the european sectoral authorities is a priority for the creation of coherent supervision at the macro-micro-prudential level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i consider that the esrb's task should be to monitor and assess systemic risk at normal times, with the aim of mitigating the exposure of the system to the risk of failure of systemic components and increasing the resilience of the financial system to shocks. in this regard, the esrb should ensure financial stability and mitigate negative impacts on the internal market and the real economy. in order to achieve its objectives, the esrb should analyse all relevant information, in particular relevant legislation with potential impact on financial stability, such as accounting, bankruptcy and viability provisions. i also agree that the esrb should, where necessary, issue and make public risk warnings and make general recommendations to the union as a whole, to individual member states or groups of member states, with a defined timetable for the relevant measures. where such risk warnings or recommendations are addressed to individual member states or groups of member states, the esrb may propose appropriate support measures.
in writing. − the creation of structures capable of preventive intervention, supported by a permanent and duly substantiated assessment, should be a priority in the decision-making process and policy action of the european union in the current framework of the response to the current crisis, where it is imperative to ensure the efficiency of a community macroprudential supervision of the financial system. the european systemic risk board, by being able to monitor and assess the risks of the financial system during periods of normal operation, could be the guarantor of financial stability, which is absolutely necessary for the real economy to develop and provide growth, wealth and jobs. i would stress the rapporteur's concern to ensure a balanced and realistic proposal, through effective supervision that safeguards the financing of the economy, the single market and the interests and objectives of the european union.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has highlighted major shortcomings in financial supervision, both in individual cases and in relation to the financial system as a whole. the supervisory models were national in scope and did not keep pace with the globalisation that has occurred in the financial system, where various financial groups develop their operations across borders with the resulting systemic risks. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims to improve the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. i believe that the creation of the european systemic risk board is essential to achieve an effective supervisory model and to avoid systemic risks caused by the cross-border nature of large financial groups.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i believe that a new framework for financial crisis management should be established to stabilise or liquidate institutions in difficulty in order to minimise the risks of contagion in the european financial system. i also agree that the european banking stability fund should finance the orderly winding-up or financial interventions to help financial institutions in difficulty where they may threaten the financial stability of the union's single financial market. this fund should be financed by appropriate financial contributions from the financial sector. contributions to this fund should replace contributions to national funds of a similar nature.
in writing. - i believe that in the context of the crisis, in which supervisory failures have been observed, the european authorities for banking, financial markets and insurance and supplementary retirement pensions will be able to prevent the current problems from reappearing. those authorities should be empowered to exercise more effective and efficient supervision, in particular of entities and situations involving entities with cross-border activity and the effects of which could be detrimental to the entire internal market, investors and european consumers. i believe that the national authorities should, however, continue to play a key role in relation to national financial institutions, coordinating their action with their counterparts in other member states, in particular with regard to the exchange of good practice. the commission's proposal for a financial supervision package also requires that the directives already in force and affected by these new measures be amended accordingly, for reasons of consistency with the community legal order.
in writing. − a european banking supervisory authority will consolidate the effectiveness of the deep reform of the current system of financial market supervision in which the institutions of the european union are engaged today, in order to ensure a structural basis for intervention with sufficient powers to avoid a repetition of the last global financial crisis, which would be unbearable for society and the world economy. it is absolutely inappropriate to accept a system of supervision based on the action of national authorities whose jurisdiction ends at their borders, when the market players are financial institutions whose intervention is located in the european area without borders. i therefore emphasize the rapporteur's attention to the importance of small and mediumsized enterprises and the european perspective of the proposal.

in writing. − in order to ensure transparency and credibility of european markets and institutions with citizens, the strengthening of the powers, resources and autonomy of european supervision in insurance and pension markets is essential to ensure the effectiveness of the current reform that the institutions of the european union are committed to implement in the supervision of financial markets, in order to avoid new risks of a crisis such as the one currently affecting the global economy, with particular impact on european social reality.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has exposed major weaknesses in financial supervision, both in individual cases and in relation to the financial system as a whole. the supervisory models were national in scope and did not keep pace with the globalisation that has occurred in the financial system, where various financial groups develop their operations across borders with the resulting systemic risks. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims to improve the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. the creation of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority is therefore essential to achieve an effective supervisory model.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i believe that credit institutions and investment firms should require their employees to undertake not to use personal hedging or insurance strategies which would jeopardise the risk-alignment effects inherent in their remuneration arrangements and because i agree with the principle that the measures provided for in this directive are steps in the reform process in response to the financial crisis. in line with the conclusions of the g20, the financial stability board and the basel committee on banking supervision, further reforms may be necessary, including the need to create countercyclical buffers, dynamic provisions, the underlying bases for the calculation of capital requirements under directive 2006/48/ec and measures supplementing risk-based requirements for credit institutions, to help prevent leverage in the banking system. in order to ensure adequate democratic oversight of the process, the european parliament and the council should be effectively involved in the process in a timely manner.
in writing. − the increase in the capital of financial institutions is important so that consumers are not harmed and do not lose their investments in the event of difficulties in the institution. however, it must be borne in mind that this increase in own funds cannot be so disproportionate as to lead to a lack of liquidity by financial institutions. this would have serious consequences for the market as a whole and therefore this question should be seriously considered.
in writing. − the stability and financial sustainability of banking activity is absolutely crucial for the development of the real economy. the current global crisis has exposed the fragility of the banking system and its credibility with citizens and businesses, as well as the negative effects on europe's productive and industrial capacity and on the financial stability of the member states themselves. the financial crisis was caused by excessive risk exposure imposed by banking rules, based on extraordinary incentives for immediate results and increasingly unsustainable, in the face of insufficient own funds and deregulated uses of resources. in this context, sound and ethically sound remuneration and incentive practices in the banking sector are urgently needed to prevent policies that encourage excessive risk-taking, as well as the imposition of higher capital requirements for trading book and re-securitisations.
in writing. − it took time to adopt new rules on the limitation of bonuses, but these will only apply from january 2011 and the rules on banks' own funds only at the end of that year. this is regrettable, since they have already applied the austerity measures to the workers and the majority of the population, as is happening in portugal, greece and other countries. that is why we are voting against this double standard. but they only set stricter rules on bankers' bonuses and strengthen the rules on banks' own funds so that they are better prepared to deal with future crises. pension policy is also covered by the new legislation. if the employee leaves the credit institution before retirement, the discretionary pension benefits shall be retained by the credit institution for a period of five years in the form of contingent capital. however, it accepts that bonuses will continue even in the case of credit institutions benefiting from exceptional intervention by their governments, only these bonuses will be strictly limited to a percentage of net revenues, whenever it is incompatible with the maintenance of a sound capital base and the timely end of public support. this is unacceptable.
in writing. − every business sector should be concerned with delivering good results for its shareholders. however, the financial crisis that emerged in 2008 brought to light the fact that some financial institutions have management practices geared towards easy and short-term profit without measuring the risks that could arise for the financial health of the institution. in addition, many of these financial institutions were not properly capitalised to support their trading portfolios and re-securitisations, using uncoordinated leverage schemes that significantly increased the risks of the operations. i am voting in favour of this legislative resolution so that in future there will be no more situations of decapitalization of financial institutions and so that remuneration policies will be reviewed and put in the context of more responsible objectives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation, including the amendments adopted by the european parliament, because i considered that the ecb should ensure sufficient human and financial resources for the performance of secretarial tasks, ensuring a high level of staff quality, reflecting the broad scope of the esrb and the composition of its general council. the ecb shall also ensure equitable financing of the secretariat from its own resources. furthermore, i agree that all secretariat staff should be required not to disclose information subject to professional secrecy, even after their duties have ceased, in accordance with article 8 of regulation (eu) no .../2010 [esrb] in order to ensure the objective set out in article 6 of this regulation.
in writing. − the need to ensure conditions for stronger and more effective european supervision of financial markets has been the subject of a strong commitment by the european parliament, which has become more evident and valued with the development of the current economic and financial crisis. a system of supervision based on a nationalist basis, based on the individualistic logic of each member state, is proving increasingly ineffective and fallible in the face of the global dimension of financial markets, in a logic of increasingly integrated development. i therefore support this legislative resolution of the european parliament. with the appropriate technical support and drawing on the capacity and resources of the european central bank, the european systemic risk board (esrb) will undoubtedly play a decisive role in the european union in acting more rapidly and in advance by analysing information on the evolution of systems and detecting potential risks. this will be key to preventing new crises or, in the case of their inevitability, to mitigating their negative impacts and to finding ways to reverse the trend quickly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution in agreeing with the recommendation made by parliament to the commission to submit to parliament, by 31 december 2010, in accordance with articles 50 and 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, one or more legislative proposals concerning an eu crisis management framework, an eu financial stability fund (fund) and a resolution unit, in accordance with the recommendations set out in the annex, taking into account the initiatives taken by international bodies such as the g20 and the international monetary fund to ensure a global level playing field and based on a thorough analysis of all available alternatives, including an impact assessment. i believe that the existing financial sector supervisory mechanisms at eu and international level have proven ineffective in preventing or sufficiently containing the contagion effect, that the involvement of shareholders and then creditors in burden sharing is essential to minimise the costs borne by taxpayers as a result of the crises in financial institutions and markets, and that a strong internal market for financial services is fundamental to the union's overall competitiveness.
in writing. − in the context of the crisis, i consider it important that new mechanisms are provided for which avoid considerable damage to consumers and which increase transparency and security in financial markets. i therefore support the creation of a european crisis management framework as well as a common set of rules to be followed by national supervisors. the establishment of a risk assessment panel and the criteria for such an assessment will have to be well defined ex ante and with due caution. only in this way will there be no additional risk for institutions entering any difficult phase. this cannot be aggravated by information which is known to the market in an extemporaneous manner. if that were to happen, we would risk heading for failure, which is undesirable.

the european union is a strategic partner of latin america in general and the mercosur countries in particular, and they share a common history and civilizational values with us. it is also a geopolitical space where freedom, democracy and respect for human rights have made remarkable progress. it makes perfect sense, therefore, to deepen political and cultural ties and to take advantage of mutual economic advantages. i therefore welcome the european decision to reopen negotiations on the association agreement with mercosur, even though i regret and condemn the recent protectionist acts of argentina, which are in complete contrast to the spirit of openness shown by the european side. however, i cannot fail to warn the commission of the potentially negative consequences for the european agricultural sector if this negotiation is not properly conducted. we all know the scale of the imbalance in our trade balance with mercosur and the production conditions and demands placed on farmers on both sides of the atlantic. for this reason, in addition to the questions which have been formally put in writing, in particular as regards how the commission intends to approach the question of sensitive products, i would like to know how it intends to react to argentina's understandable gesture.
the first eu-brazil summit, organised by the portuguese presidency in 2007, filled an unexplained gap. brazil was the only bric country with which europe did not have a strategic partnership. strengthening the eu-brazil dialogue makes perfect sense as it allows for deeper cooperation in key sectors such as energy security and sustainable development, biodiversity and climate change, etc. brazil's demographic weight, economic development and political stability make it an unavoidable player on the international scene. as we look ahead to the 4th eu-brazil summit, it is important to take stock of the progress made and to look at how we can develop this partnership to address common challenges and to harmonise positions, for example with a view to the united nations climate change conference in mexico later this year. the summit is also an opportunity to move forward the negotiations with mercosur towards the conclusion of an association agreement and to overcome existing differences.
the resumption of negotiations in september between mercosur and the eu is a process of the utmost importance for the eu. on the one hand, in a multipolar world in which the bric countries are gaining increasing weight, it is essential for the eu to establish a privileged relationship with the countries of latin america, where it holds more investment than in russia, india and china combined, which would ensure, with a privileged trade relationship, the consolidation of a huge economic advantage on a global scale. on the other hand, we have the level of trade openness for agricultural goods and the definition of the sanitary and phytosanitary rules necessary for trade between the blocs. the competitiveness of mercosur on agricultural markets has been strengthened and increased in recent years, and an impact study on the consequences of an agreement for european agricultural activity, which is in no way in a position to suffer further shocks at the moment, is therefore essential. we must not therefore rush into a process of too rapid conclusion which does not take into account any negative impacts on european agriculture, nor into excessive protectionism which jeopardises the important position which the union can secure in this part of the world.

mr president, commissioner, europe is now the largest european market for fishery and aquaculture products, importing some 60% of the fish consumed. the community's fish production is not, and will not be in the near future, sufficient to meet the demand for this type of product, so that recourse to imports becomes a necessity. in this context, two fundamental aspects must be safeguarded. firstly, the creation of the conditions necessary to guarantee the community consumer access to imported quality fishery and aquaculture products. secondly, the establishment of a framework of fair competition, both for imported products and for those produced and caught by the european fisheries and aquaculture sectors. fishery and aquaculture products imported into the european union must therefore meet the same environmental, social, health and quality requirements as community production. the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products also needs to be reformed, in particular the mechanisms used to counter phenomena such as the gradual abolition of customs duties and increasing competition from imports. this report from the european parliament, which has been conducted in an exemplary manner by my colleague alain cadec, is timely and contains a number of important proposals for the sustainable development of fisheries and related sectors, including marketing.

in writing. − in november 2006, parliament adopted a resolution recognising the strategic importance of the european languages of universal communication - english, spanish, portuguese and french - in order of the number of speakers - as a means of communication and as a form of solidarity, cooperation and economic investment, and the european commission recognised in 2008 that these languages are an important bridge between the peoples and nations of the different regions of the world. when the organisation and functioning of the eeas is established, i believe it is essential that it makes the most of the communication capacity of these global european languages and adopts them as working languages. the linguistic regime and practice which govern this service will determine the extent to which it is used for communication with the outside world. that said, i can only rejoice at the establishment of the eeas and hope that it will produce results that meet the expectations placed in it. the european union will have much to gain from a competent and efficient eeas, able to be its voice in the world and to cooperate actively with the diplomatic services of the member states.
in writing. − the purpose of this decision is to establish the organisation and functioning of the european external action service (eeas), a functionally autonomous body of the union under the authority of the high representative, established by article 27 (3) of the treaty on european union (teu), as amended by the treaty of lisbon. the european parliament also has a role to play in the union's external action policy, in particular with regard to its political control functions (as provided for in article 14 (1) teu) and its legislative and budgetary functions as laid down in the treaties. the high representative must also regularly consult the european parliament on the main aspects and the basic options of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and must ensure that parliament's positions are duly taken into account. the eeas shall assist the high representative in this task. specific provisions should be laid down regarding access by members of the european parliament to confidential documents and information in the field of the cfsp. i have no objections to this, and i have voted in favour of this decision.
in writing. - we voted against this report, which is the result of negotiations between the council and the majority of parliament on one of the central points of the lisbon treaty and a key element in the federalism of the european union, which has now become a legal personality, as they advocated in the european constitution. it is noted that this service will involve more than five thousand people in eu embassies in various countries around the world. to make matters worse, we note that no proposals from our group were put forward, in particular those which advocated that the eu's military structures should not be part of the european external action service or even have any institutional link. the same was true of the eu's secret intelligence structures. it is also particularly worrying that the proposal we tabled calling on the council to cease development and to abolish military and civilian-military structures under its jurisdiction and to cease financing military and civilian-military activities has been rejected. the future of the european union and the paths it intends to take are therefore of great concern.
in writing. - the adoption of the treaty of lisbon led to the creation of the european external action service, thus laying the foundations for a strong european diplomatic service. the establishment of the eeas is intended to ensure the coherence of european external action and the conduct of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp).
in writing. - as a member of the committee on constitutional affairs, where the european external action service was widely discussed and where i was able to express my views, and as a member of the epp, i give my support and vote in favour of this report. the european parliament presented a united position among political groups, which had a common interest in making the most of the new powers that the treaty of lisbon conferred in particular on this house, both in terms of political control and financial control of the european external action service. i repeat my initial concern, which i have constantly expressed, including through amendments to the draft reports, and which is related to the need to ensure the geopolitical balance of the european external action service which is now being set up. i would stress the high representative's commitment to the creation of a team based on geographical balance, with representatives from all 27 member states, banning any kind of discrimination and also promoting equality.

in writing. - the european parliament expresses its deep concern at the tragic and violent clashes that have recently erupted in kyrgyzstan and conveys its condolences to the families of all the victims. i would stress the call in this resolution for every effort to be made to return the situation to normal and to create the necessary conditions for refugees and internally displaced persons to be able to return to their homes voluntarily, safely and with dignity. the commission is also asked to step up humanitarian assistance in cooperation with international organisations and to launch short and medium-term programmes to rebuild destroyed houses and replace lost property, as well as rehabilitation projects, in collaboration with the kyrgyz authorities and other donors, to create favourable conditions for the return of refugees and internally displaced persons.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on hiv/aids in view of the 18th international aids conference, because there is a need to step up efforts to address hiv/aids as a global public health priority and to facilitate universal access to health care, education and employment for people affected by this virus. it is essential to combat stigmatisation and discrimination against people living with hiv/aids and to ensure that their rights are protected.
in writing. - a matter such as this should have been the subject of broad consensus among the political groups, which should have refrained from seeking to use it in favour of this or that agenda. the fact that there is a joint motion for a resolution which has only been endorsed by the left and far-left parties in parliament makes it clear that this objective has been unfortunately called into question. it is the people, their illness and the suffering that comes with it and the impact it has on societies, particularly the less developed ones, that should be concerned. it is for them that we must work to find the best solutions to combat this scourge and to mitigate its effects.
in writing. - the scourge of aids remains a serious humanitarian problem of global dimension, which therefore requires an integrated response of global scope, involving states, institutions and societies in different regions and continents. the social stigma that persists on this issue and the continued spread of the disease, with a high mortality rate, particularly devastating effects in the underdeveloped countries and with greater humanitarian needs, must necessarily mobilize the concern and commitment of the eu institutions and the member states to provide effective resources for a comprehensive and effective response, capable of ensuring the necessary reconciliation of policies to prevent and promote the appropriate treatment of the disease. i do not agree, however, with the association between a sensitive issue such as abortion and the fight against hiv.
in writing. − the resolution takes a comprehensive approach to hiv/aids, supported by current data. the essential issues raised, which we naturally support, are, among many others, the following: - the defence of universal access to health care and the demand that governments fulfil their obligation to provide a public health service for all; - the need to promote, protect and respect the human rights, including the sexual and reproductive health rights, of people living with hiv/aids; - the need to draw attention to the economic, legal, social and technical barriers, as well as legislation and punitive measures, which prevent effective responses to hiv; - the need for fair and flexible funding for research into new preventive technologies, including vaccines and microbicides; - the call on member states and the commission to reverse the worrying decline in funding for the promotion of sexual and reproductive health and rights in developing countries.
in writing. − hiv/aids remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, killing 2 million people in 2008, and is projected to remain an unavoidable cause of premature mortality worldwide for decades to come. the number of new infections continues to outstrip the expansion of treatment, when two-thirds of the people who needed treatment in 2009 have not yet received it, meaning that 10 million people in need have not had access to the necessary effective treatment. i therefore believe that the eu should make every effort to invest more in research, treatment and education in order to improve the whole picture. the end of stigmatisation and discrimination against people living with hiv/aids should also be promoted. i also believe that the eu should be particularly sensitive to the problem in sub-saharan africa, where 22.4 million people are hiv positive and continue to be the most affected region.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the future of the cap after 2013 because it is necessary to strengthen the cap policies and ensure an adequate budget in order to respond to the challenges facing european agriculture, such as climate change, food safety and quality and the competitiveness of the sector.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of ionising radiation. the proposal also implies a greater procedural difficulty in the future distribution of community funds to farmers, although the present system itself needs greater simplification, not the other way around. it should also be stressed that the portuguese state has unfortunately been wasting hundreds of millions of euros of funds from the first pillar. with the abolition of the second pillar and the transfer of some measures from the second to the first, many of the measures currently supported would no longer be supported, particularly because of the obvious budgetary impossibility, leading to a weakening of the common agricultural policy. in fact, the advantage of any possible transfer of cap funds to other policies is not understood. on the contrary, we are in favour of measures to ensure that the only truly common policy in the eu is maintained.
in writing. - the cap has increased productivity, ensured security of supply and provided consumers with quality food at reasonable prices. the new cap will have to face new and unforeseen challenges and provide a framework for the future based on stability, predictability and flexibility in times of crisis. the cap reform must be reviewed in the context of the economic crisis and the fight against climate change, while maintaining its competitiveness in the global context. the agricultural sector is expected to be in a position to make a significant contribution to the priorities of the new europe 2020 strategy on combating climate change, innovation and job creation through green growth, while continuing to ensure food security for european consumers through the production of safe and high-quality food. however, i believe that the cap should give priority to the production of so-called first generation public goods and to food sovereignty as a guiding principle, so that the member states are self-sufficient. i also support the regulation of the milk market from production to marketing. in this context i consider it essential to maintain milk quotas.
in writing. − the fundamental change that is urgently needed in the common agricultural policy should, among other things, introduce the principle of the right to food and food sovereignty, give priority to food self-sufficiency and the ability of countries and regions to develop their production to meet national or regional food needs; support activities that promote local production and respect the local environment, protect soil and water, increase the production of non-gmo food and promote seed biodiversity for farmers and the diversity of livestock species. that is the content of one of the amendments we have tabled to the report under discussion. the rejection of this amendment and the principles contained in it by the main political groups in this parliament is indicative of the path they intend to take. the report also points to this. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the cap is not subject to the same rules as other agricultural products, and that the cap is not subject to the same rules as other agricultural products. that is unacceptable to us.
