in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the lyon report by the european parliament, which is the result of the excellent work of its rapporteur, assisted by the shadow rapporteurs, and also of the contribution of all the colleagues who tabled amendments, took part in the debate and tried to build consensus. this report does indeed reflect the consensus that can be reached between members from the 27 member states and from different political families, which is significant in itself, and even more so in the context of the ep's new co-decision powers. the report, which is the final result of several rounds of negotiations, takes a number of structural positions for the future cap, which we consider to be fundamental: not to reduce the budget, not to renationalize the cap, to maintain the two pillars of the cap, to implement a new system for the distribution of aid, to divide between first and second generation public goods, not to render unworkable the decision on the dismantling of milk quotas, which will be repealed by the council, the need for a safety net, the need for greater transparency in the food chain and the need to simplify the cap. it is now necessary to continue monitoring the internal work of the european commission until the publication of the final communication in november.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, but i am making this declaration of vote to underline that in paragraph 44, on market management, i voted against the first part of the paragraph proposed by the rapporteur and in favour of the second part of the same paragraph, thus decisively affecting the decision of the european parliament in the light of portugal's strategic interests. the version proposed by the rapporteur, although broadly interpreted, would allow the dismantling of milk quotas to be brought forward. i know and support the position of the portuguese agricultural sector, which has reiterated its conviction that the end of the milk quota system could be a major penalty for portuguese producers. in fact, 93% of milk produced in the eu is traded on the european market and represents a significant share of the revenues of eu dairy companies. milk quotas have enabled milk production to be maintained and developed in a sustained manner in the 27 member states, contributing to the matching of supply and demand (european and international) in the dairy sector and allowing price stability and sustainable incomes. the dismantling of this system without an alternative proposal will lead to the abandonment of production in the countries where it is least competitive, a category in which portugal falls.
in writing. - i supported this report because it is a strategic element for countries like portugal and for the outermost regions of europe, and it was a remarkable effort on the part of parliament to vote on it in this first year of the legislature. the common agricultural policy is a key part of the financial and budgetary framework of the european union for the period after 2013 and deserves a detailed analysis. internal agricultural production, which can make a major contribution to reducing member states' trade deficits, food security and trade with third countries are key aspects of this policy. european farmers produce foodstuffs of high safety and quality, with strict environmental and animal protection clauses, and they should be rewarded for this and not harmed. to this end, it should be ensured that conditions are imposed on third countries with which the union has trade agreements which are similar to those imposed on producers in the european internal market. i also think that we need an agricultural budget which allocates its funds fairly and with special attention to regions such as madeira and the azores, which face permanent constraints due to their peripheral location, insularity, small area, adverse climate and geographical situation and which must therefore receive permanent support.
in writing. − the report deals with imports of fishery and aquaculture products into the eu and the conditions under which they must take place. imported products must meet the same quality criteria as those produced in the eu. the report calls for the creation of an eco-label for fishery products. this would provide consumers with information on the origin of the product and the health, social and environmental conditions under which the product was fished.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the import regime for fishery and aquaculture products into the eu in the context of the future reform of the cfp, as i believe that issues relating to imports of fishery and aquaculture products into the eu should be given very particular attention in the context of the ongoing reforms of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - after having voted on the guido milana report on a new impetus for the strategy for the sustainable development of european aquaculture at the last part-session, we are now called upon to vote on another one on the import regime for fisheries and aquaculture products. according to the report, europe now imports 60% of the fish it consumes. in addition, by 2030 consumption growth is expected, which will be almost entirely covered by increased imports. while it is not intended that european production should be able to meet our demand needs (which would be impossible, both now and in the future), the truth is that the future reform of the cfp cannot fail to look at the question of imports and to try to give it the most appropriate response, either by increasing european production (not only by increasing catches but also by focusing on aquaculture), or by requiring that imported fish comply with the same standards as those caught or produced in the union, or even by providing adequate information to the consumer on the origin of the fish. this is a question which, as the rapporteur rightly argues, will have to be given serious consideration in the reform of the cfp.
in writing. − the eu market, at around 12 million tonnes and €55 billion in 2007, is the world's largest market for fishery and aquaculture products (faps), ahead of japan and the united states. this market, which has been growing strongly since 2005, is increasingly dependent on imports, to the extent that the consumption coverage rate of the community production is now below 40%, i.e. an import dependency rate of more than 60%. consumption forecasts indicate that demand could increase by approximately 1 500 000 tonnes by 2030 and that this increase would be almost entirely covered by additional imports. as i said in the june plenary session, i am in favour of a proposal for a regulation which consolidates in a single text all the community provisions governing the aquaculture sector. in this context, and given that portugal is the largest fish consumer per capita in europe, i would advocate that aquaculture be made a strategic priority for the eu. i am therefore particularly pleased that the commission is advocating a sustainable aquaculture policy to reduce import dependence in the amp sector.
in writing. - the work of data collection and systematisation made possible by the preparation of this report should be valued, as it helps us to have an up-to-date picture of a situation which is, from several points of view, worrying, as the report rightly acknowledges. the existence of economically, environmentally and socially sustainable fisheries and aquaculture sectors in eu countries is incompatible with the trade policy that the eu has been pursuing. by deregulating and liberalizing international trade, and by turning it towards a logic of competition rather than the logic of complementarity which should govern it, the interests of importers and distributors are being promoted, but at the same time thousands of producers are being condemned to ruin and abandonment, food balance deficits are being increased and basic criteria of quality, food safety and the environment are being called into question. the fisheries and aquaculture sectors (like agriculture) are strategically vital sectors which are not compatible with a mercantilist approach and trade regulation is required, including the possibility of using trade defence instruments as suggested in the report. we also stress the need for urgent reform of the common organisation of the market in fishery products, which we also support.
in writing. − as the world's largest importer of fishery products, the eu market has a political responsibility, along with other major fishery importers, to ensure that wto trade rules are in line with global standards for fisheries conservation and management. the eu must join forces to increase aquaculture fish production in a sustainable way in order to reduce fish imports in the amp sector. i am particularly concerned about the possibility of importing and marketing genetically modified fish, which i believe should be banned from being marketed in the eu. i therefore advocate a strict certification policy which can effectively control these problems. i also support the idea of putting a strong emphasis on research and development in european aquaculture, which accounts for only 2% of world production.
in writing. the community strategy for the sustainable development of aquaculture was recently adopted. of course, it is now urgent to regulate the issue of imports of fishery and aquaculture products, as the eu is currently the world's largest market for ppa, but does not have sufficient production to meet demand and is therefore dependent on these imports. it is therefore necessary to regulate the way in which they are made, in order to ensure that the quality and good practice required of community producers is also required of third countries. i agree with the rapporteur on the question of customs protection. it does not seem to me feasible, especially in the present period, that tariffs can be abolished and yet our producers can be expected to survive and be competitive with third parties. as i have already mentioned, the issue of fisheries and aquaculture is one of the priorities set by madeira in the current esdp, so the region is in the process of promoting the competitiveness of the sector through sustainable management of resources, diversification of fish production, the enhancement of products from a quality perspective and the qualification of fishing assets in order to increase productivity. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
the case of farai maguwu illustrates the brutal repression in zimbabwe, but also the need to broaden the scope of the kimberley process. diamonds must not only be certified as free from war crimes but also from human rights violations, including those committed by states and mining companies. diamond mining is relevant to the fight against poverty and the achievement of the millennium development goals. according to global witness, africa exported $393 billion worth of oil and minerals in 2008, nine times the total amount of aid the continent received. a fair exploitation of natural resources for the benefit of local populations can thus be crucial in strengthening the rule of law, promoting corporate social responsibility and thus guaranteeing human rights. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
madam president, i would propose that, where we refer to the african charter of human and people’s rights, instead of saying ‘of which zimbabwe is a full member’ we say instead ‘which zimbabwe has ratified’.
the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of life of the people of europe. if the commission communication falls far short of what is necessary in this area, as the rapporteur admits, the truth is that the report itself also falls short of what is necessary. concrete measures are needed to put an end to the manipulation of food prices and the cartels of intermediary sectors in the supply chain, such as the large-scale distribution that the liberalisation of agricultural markets has brought about. the guarantee of fair minimum prices for farmers must be restored in order to guarantee a decent income that will enable them to maintain themselves in a sector of strategic importance, countering the abandonment of production and the increase in food dependence of several countries and regions, as is the case in portugal. consideration should be given to establishing maximum marketing margins, in particular for large areas, in relation to the prices paid to producers, in order to ensure a fair distribution of value added along the supply chain of the food chain. measures and policies, including fiscal measures, are needed to stimulate and support the functioning and modernisation of local and regional markets. food security, the preservation of ecosystems and the strengthening of the economic and social fabric in the primary sector also require that international trade be guided by a logic of complementarity and not competition between producers and products. we must question and break with the system which treats food as if it were just another commodity and which allows speculation on food, leading, as has been happening, to explosive situations from the point of view of food dependence and price volatility.
this report focuses on a very important issue in the field of agriculture, which lacks coordinated action at european level, given that, on average, the price of food products has increased by 3.3% a year since 1996, the cost of producing agricultural products by 3.6% and the prices paid to farmers by only 2.1%. we are therefore faced with a situation of serious trade imbalances in the food supply chain which must be corrected. farmers and the agri-food sector, in accordance with the objectives set by the cap, produce food that meets very high quality standards and maintains prices that are affordable to consumers. however, a very small number of powerful retailers impose their prices, almost without negotiation, on 13.4 million farmers and 310 000 agribusinesses across the european union. in this context, i support the call for the european commission to come forward with legislative proposals to solve the problem, including the amendment of the european competition rules, going beyond the mere recommendations and strategies developed by the high level group on the supply chain; to organise a wide information campaign at european level to inform farmers of their rights; to prohibit abusive practices which are particularly felt in the sector of perishable agricultural products such as fruit and vegetables; to promote support for farmers' organisations so that they can have a greater critical mass and increase their bargaining power. it would be interesting to equate farmers' organisations and cooperatives with small and medium-sized enterprises so that they can benefit from special exemptions. we recognize that the balance between full respect for the rules of free competition in a market economy which we advocate and the necessary and urgent intervention which is requested of the european commission has not always been easy, but we consider that, on the whole, it has been achieved, and we therefore approve and welcome this report.
this own-initiative report which we are debating today, under the responsibility of josé bové, whom i congratulate on the way he conducted it and on the good result it produced, in which i had the privilege of being the shadow and negotiating the 17 commitments obtained, is absolutely essential at a time when agricultural policies are increasingly market-oriented, farmers in europe are faced with very low income levels and millions of consumers, as a result of the crisis which affects everyone, are in urgent need of keeping food affordable. that is why, if farmers' incomes are going to increasingly depend on the value generated in markets and the price of food on their proper functioning, then improving the functioning of the food supply chain becomes absolutely necessary for a more equitable sharing of value generated, from agricultural producers to final consumers, ensuring fair incomes for some and adequate prices for others. this requires rebalancing the relationships established along the food supply chain, making them transparent and ensuring a framework of fair and competitive good practice. we therefore call on the commission to take account of the proposals which have been widely supported in the committee on agriculture.

the rapporteur. - madam president, the report i am presenting is the result of a compromise between groups with very different views on employment policies and protection against unemployment. i would therefore like to thank the shadow rapporteurs and the committees on employment and the budget for their willingness to reach an agreement to help the victims of collective redundancies in the union. this agreement is based on two findings: the first is that the social effects of the crisis will continue to be felt even if economic recovery is achieved, which is far from a given. as a result, mass redundancies are not a thing of the past. unfortunately, they will continue to shape the social life of our countries. that's why the first choice is simple: do we want to extend the globalisation adjustment fund, the only european instrument for those who are subject to collective redundancies, until 2020? the answer from this report is clear: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the social partners are able to take part in the negotiations. the second finding is that this fund started with many shortcomings, but that the amendments to its regulations have significantly increased the number of applications to use it. it is too early to make an assessment, but we can point out and identify the main difficulty. the time between the time of the collective redundancy and the arrival of the money in the countries is between 12 and 17 months, in some cases much longer. we have a social emergency response fund that's as slow as a snail. what concerns me is the social consequence. this is why many workers end up not benefiting from the fund and, on the other hand, the delays discourage the willingness to prepare applications in the regions and countries which need them most. in fact, this is where the authorities do not put the applications in the field before they have them approved in brussels, because this forces them to go ahead with the national component of funding in a context of budgetary austerity. that is why the report proposes a chain of short-term measures to reduce delinquency by 50% and it is proposed that the fund should become permanent from 2013. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, some of the member states which have benefited most from the fund are resisting its simplification, fearing that the acceleration will end up requiring more and more money. let's face it, that risk exists whether the fund is slow or fast. the risk of a long period of mediocre growth exists because it depends on the impact that austerity policies will have on the recovery of our economies. but what we are discussing here today is something else, namely europe's attitude to collective redundancy. if we sacrifice their victims on the altar of budgetary restraint, or if we are at least able to give these people at least as much attention as we have given to the financial system that our taxes have saved. the choice of this report is a matter of ethics, of the way we look at our fellow men and the way we look at europe. i want it unambiguously social.

in writing. i support this report on the financing and operation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, as i fully support the rapporteur's idea of a more rapid mobilisation of this fund. the egf was established to alleviate the negative consequences of globalisation for workers made redundant by helping them to find employment again by supporting personalised reintegration programmes. this fund has a maximum budget of €500 million per year, never fully exploited by the member states. at present there is still a period of 12 to 17 months between the time when the collective redundancies occur and the time when egf funding is made available to the member state. the rapporteur's proposals for simplification and flexibility could reduce the time required to mobilise the egf by half. in order to respond to the increase in unemployment resulting from the economic and financial crisis, it is essential that the egf becomes a genuine flexible and targeted support instrument on a permanent basis. only in this way can the egf be used to promote new skills for new sustainable and quality jobs, contributing to the improvement of the union's competitiveness in the context of globalisation.

in writing. − counterfeiting of euro coins is a significant threat, especially for coins with higher denominations. the lack of a binding common framework for coin authentication may make it difficult to protect coins. the regulation now adopted is a legally binding instrument which makes it possible to establish a common method of authenticating euro coins. one of the main objectives of the regulation is to ensure that the institutions ensure that euro coins reintroduced into circulation are subject to authentication procedures. authentication shall be carried out by means of coin-processing machines referred to in article 5 (3) or by duly trained staff in accordance with the methods laid down by the member states. moreover, because authenticating euro coins inevitably implies costs for the institutions involved in this process (credit institutions and a number of other institutions such as cash carriers), i propose including the right of institutions to withhold a processing fee.

in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report, which is geared to the situation of the outermost regions, whose economies are fragile by nature and have very specific characteristics requiring concrete responses suitably adapted to their particularities. the measures now approved are designed to strengthen the competitiveness of local economic operators and should help to help local smes and farmers to invest and create jobs, thus promoting more stable employment in the autonomous regions of the azores and madeira. in the context of the general economic crisis, this is a specific measure to stimulate economic activity and employment in the medium term, important contributions to cohesion and convergence in the european area. the customs suspension will last for 10 years and cover a wide range of products such as finished products for industrial use, raw materials, parts and components used for agricultural purposes, industrial processing and maintenance. although it is not possible to carry out a rigorous assessment of the impact of these measures, since they are an integral part of a series of other measures adapted to the specific problems of these autonomous regions, the european commission expects these approved measures to have an impact on the union's own resources/revenue of the order of 0,12/year for the period 2010-2019.

in writing. − this agreement aims to establish more effective cooperation in the field of mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between the eu member states and japan. i consider the conclusion of this agreement to be important, not only because it allows the creation of a clear and coherent regulatory framework governing such cooperation, but also because there were no bilateral agreements between the member states and japan in this field. the current challenges of globalisation are increasingly leading to the need for transnational responses, with the fight against crime as a clear example, where cooperation and assistance between the various states of the international community play a key role. under this agreement, a formal request may be made, or only spontaneous exchanges of information may take place, such as witness statements, records, bank statements, location or identification of persons. the requested state always has the possibility of rejecting such a request on the classical grounds of refusal, but this must be preceded by a consultation phase between the states concerned. i therefore support this agreement which allows for more effective legal aid while safeguarding an adequate level of guarantees.
in writing. - organized crime has long since moved beyond the borders of individual states and is now active in many parts of the world. this is a situation which is characteristic of our times and which requires concerted responses on the part of the international organizations, the states and the peoples who are victims of criminal acts. the agreement between the union and japan on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters is another step in this direction. the rule of law states have an obligation to ensure that the borders which separate them at the international legal level are not used by criminals as a way of escaping justice, thus frustrating their conviction and the fair compensation of the victims. however effective the police and judicial authorities of individual countries may be, the exchange of information and the adoption of best practices will benefit everyone if we can all benefit from mutual legal assistance. i pray that it is.
in writing. − in february 2009, the council authorised the opening of negotiations for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and japan on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. by decision of 30 november 2009, the council authorised the signing of that agreement on the basis of articles 24 and 38 of the treaty on european union. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament was asked to approve the council decision in accordance with article 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the agreements are modelled on other judicial cooperation agreements concluded in the past and focus in particular on cooperation in the conduct of investigations or the taking of evidence, as well as on other activities such as the service of communications in the requested state. among the most important provisions, i would stress the collection of evidence and statements, the possibility of using videoconferencing, the obtaining of records, documents or extracts from bank accounts or, in particular, the location or identification of persons, as well as the provision of information held by the legislative, administrative or judicial authorities of the requested state or by their local authorities.
in writing. - the globalisation of our times is not limited to the economic sphere, but is now extending to other areas, including crime. that is why judicial cooperation in criminal matters between states is always on the agenda. in the case of japan, and despite the lack of a regulatory framework, the judicial authorities of the two countries have been cooperating with each other. it is therefore of the utmost importance that negotiations begin on the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and japan on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. hence my vote.
in writing. - this is another key step in establishing broad judicial cooperation with third countries.
in writing. according to a 2008 fidh report, japan continues to sentence criminals to death and to lock them up for decades in secret and isolated prisons. the pace of executions has accelerated in recent years, most notably in 2008. no revision of death sentences has been accepted since 1986. the agreement the eu is about to conclude does not include extradition procedures. however, it allows for the assumption of various pieces of evidence useful in carrying out possible convictions - including the temporary transfer of a detained person to be heard. article 11 allows eu member states to refuse requests for mutual assistance under certain conditions but does not prevent them from being granted when the death penalty could be the outcome of the trial. i am in favour of judicial cooperation in criminal matters where it is done in compliance with the rights of the defence, procedural guarantees and human rights. in the case of japan, this raises some puzzles, to say the least. that is why i cannot give the green light to this new treaty.
in writing. - the interconnection of the business register is essential as the current fragmentation not only harms the business world but also leads to a lack of consumer confidence. in particular, the problems this fragmentation creates for smes, which are part of the backbone of the european economy, job creation, economic growth and social cohesion in the eu and in cross-border relations, which pose clear obstacles to the eu's single market. i fully support the creation of a single window, which should be available in all eu languages and properly disseminated, in order to ensure access to quality, reliable and up-to-date information from the eu business register. in the current context, where profound measures are being taken to overcome the crisis, this instrument could be a valuable addition to strengthening the confidence of 500 million eu citizens in the single market and to improving cross-border trade relations. i therefore welcome the report voted on in this house today.
in writing. - when we talk about the internal market we have to realise that one of its consequences is an increase in cross-border trade. this is desirable and should be encouraged, but it also entails the need to make official and reliable information available to the public about companies operating in the eu. the lack of uniformity of the data contained in the different trade registers leads to legal uncertainty, which is not in the interest of union companies or consumers. it is therefore necessary to create a centralised european portal where the registration data of all member states are to be found in a uniform manner. this increases transparency, efficiency and legal certainty, and strengthens the confidence of the 500 million european consumers, which is essential in the context of the exit from the crisis. finally, and following closely the opinion of the econ committee, i stress the need for a new system (or portal) which should not represent an additional administrative burden for european companies. this system should make life easier for all market players and not be a (more) red tape to overcome.
in writing. − the increasing cross-border economic activity, in the interests of legal certainty and transparency, requires better interconnection of business registers. this reduces costs and increases efficiency. the interconnection of business registers is an appropriate measure to strengthen the further integration of the economic area within the eu and to improve legal certainty for businesses and consumers. the registers operate at national or regional level and store only information relating to companies registered in the territory (country or region) for which they are competent. there are already different mechanisms in place to interconnect business registers: the european business register initiative (ebr) and the business register interoperability throughout europe (brite) project. the ebr and brite are optional and brite is only a research project. a single point of access to business information for all european companies would save time and money. therefore, the participation of all member states should be considered mandatory.
in writing. - economic globalisation undoubtedly leads to the need for an interconnection of business registers. at present, all information on companies is recorded only at regional and national level, and it is necessary to extend it to all member states, given the growing demand for access to information on companies in a transnational context. the creation of interconnection of business registers is very important to stop the economic losses that affect all stakeholders, be they the companies themselves, their employees, consumers and the general public.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the view that the new sustainable economy should be based on the provision of skilled employment that promotes innovation in sectors strategic for europe's future, notably energy and research. the added value of these areas of knowledge, their ability to be relocated, their ability to be found in both peripheral and central regions of the european continent, offer enormous potential in terms of new technologies and the possibility of adapting to the new environmental and human situation. it will be essential to focus on sectors that promote the prevention and mitigation of the effects of climate change, where maritime regions will have a huge role to play, as well as on alternative ways of producing energy, taking advantage of the natural resources of each of europe's regions. knowledge linked to innovation in the environment is the future of the new economy, and there needs to be a strong focus on the application of knowledge to new economic uses. knowledge can produce added value, but it can only promote employment through synergies between research centres, production centres and distribution centres, providing employment in a wide range of areas from research to services and trade.
in writing. - my vote in favour of this report is based on the recognition of the importance of green jobs in a society that aims to be sustainable. green work must also be one that contributes by saving energy and natural resources, using renewable energy, preserving ecosystems and reducing the impacts of waste generation and pollution. in fact, the positive side-effect of promoting work in these sectors is considerable and should be enhanced. at the same time, adequate working conditions and basic and continuing training for workers must be ensured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'developing the employment potential of a new sustainable economy' because it argues that the creation of green jobs should not be a mere numerical assessment. it is equally important to know how to ensure good working conditions and how to ensure a transition to a sustainable economy in a socially fair way.
in writing. − the number of parliamentary committees involved in the preparation of the report six demonstrates both the importance of the employment issue today and the way in which the concept of sustainability is now an inescapable part of the lexicon and political discourse. the sustainability of the economy and its potential for job creation are problems shared by workers, businessmen and politicians, technicians and laymen, environmentalists and industrialists, among others. one of the main problems is precisely the cost of sustainability and how it is shared. we wonder to what extent this requirement, which is not always sufficiently visible or feasible, will not be adversely affecting the capacity for initiative and organisation in the markets, or will it not be introducing an additional degree of difficulty in an economy already battered by crisis and uncertainty. there is therefore a growing need today for sustainability not just to be a broad concept, and therefore difficult to achieve, but rather to be a practical and achievable presupposition for interpreting human action and interaction in the world, including at the economic level, for the benefit of all and not just a few radicals.
in writing. − development is sustainable when meeting the needs of the present generation does not threaten the needs of future generations. we must take an integrated approach to economic, social and ecological interests, intensify social dialogue, strengthen corporate responsibility and adopt the principles of prevention and the polluter pays. the thinking must be long-term, with the aim of competitiveness and social, economic, territorial and environmental cohesion, and that is why i am in favour of investments in human, social and environmental capital, technological innovation and new ecological services. this commitment is our contribution to the fight against climate change. the eu has committed itself to reducing ghg emissions by at least 20%, meeting 20% of its energy needs with renewable energy and increasing energy efficiency by 20% by 2020. according to an ipcc study, limiting global warming to 2°c will only be possible if industrialized countries reduce their ghg emissions by 80 to 90% by 2050 compared to 1990. in this way, it advocates the creation of green jobs that contribute to sustainable growth based on social justice and eco-efficiency and the promotion of employment in the rural world in order to avoid desertification.
in writing. - this own-initiative report has positive aspects in several areas and has taken up part of the opinion i was responsible for in the committee on industry, energy and research, although it does not stress, as it should, the need for greater attention to the specificities of each member state. i would like to highlight a few positive aspects: - considers that a new sustainable economy of the european union must ensure balanced economic and social development, stressing the importance of the public sector; - calls for a sustainable and ambitious industrial policy that puts the emphasis on resource efficiency and stresses that a green economy must offer prospects for decent and well-paid work, that it must focus on energy efficiency, which in turn also contributes to industrial diversification. - stresses that the transition to a new sustainable economy is a very complex process, and therefore insists on the need to pay particular attention to areas affected by deindustrialisation, either by creating appropriate financial support or by integrated sustainable development interventions, accompanied by innovative measures capable of creating quality jobs with rights and living wages, aimed at reducing regional inequalities and asymmetries, in dialogue with the social partners, and stresses the importance of supporting smes;
in writing. − the concept of employment in a new sustainable economy is creating a new paradigm in relation to the economic assumptions that have hitherto been regarded as fundamental to economic development and job creation. a sustainable economy implies major changes in employment potential, and companies in the renewable energy and energy efficiency sectors will play a key role in creating new jobs worldwide. the german example illustrates the success of firms in this sector in creating new jobs. however, it is essential that other eu countries follow germany's example if a multiplier effect of employment in a sustainable economy is to be seen across the european area.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because the full completion of the internal market and its efficient functioning are as important for the eu as they are for its trading partners, in particular the efta member states. switzerland, the eu's fourth largest trading partner by volume, has its model of economic integration without accession based on bilateral sectoral agreements. this poses additional challenges as bilateral agreements, unlike the eea agreement, do not provide for any automatic mechanisms to adapt their content to the evolution of the relevant eu acquis. despite the positive developments regarding the agreement on the free movement of persons (fmpa) between the eu member states and switzerland, there are still issues in the implementation of the fmpa that need to be addressed. i therefore believe that all possibilities for improving the implementation of the fmpa should be considered, in particular the reinforcement of the standardisation of the implementation of the fmpa and greater convergence between community and swiss legislation on the internal market.
in writing. - switzerland has a particular history and idiosyncrasy which is reflected not only in the way it governs itself internally but also in the way it has chosen to relate to other states and in the caution and reservations it places on those same relations. the swiss reluctance to join large international organizations or to sign treaties which are binding on them and affect their internal legal order is not new. nor is it particularly new that it gives preferential treatment to its own nationals and to companies based in the community to the detriment of external competition, which sometimes suffers unreasonably from legal or administrative obstacles to its action. nevertheless, switzerland has been an important partner of the european union and has concluded over a hundred bilateral agreements with the eu governing the relationship between the two. the swiss decision to remain outside the european economic area did not help to speed up and facilitate the union's economic relations with that country, but it did not prevent them from developing into an overall positive outcome. i wish them to grow stronger and expand.
in writing. − the four member states (iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland) of the european free trade association (efta) are major trading partners of the european union (eu), with switzerland and norway ranking fourth and fifth respectively among the eu's most important trading partners in terms of volume, and belong with the eu to a common cultural space in terms of sharing core values and a cultural and historical heritage. given that the new rules of the lisbon treaty may lead to a more delayed application of internal market legislation in the eea (european economic area) /efta states, i agree with the need for the commission to formalise the procedure for the notification of new community regulations and legislation falling within the scope of the eea agreement in order to narrow the gap between the adoption of new legislation and its eventual acceptance by the eea/efta states. i also agree that the parliaments of the eea/efta states should be closely involved in the eu legislative process on proposals which are relevant for eea purposes. i therefore advocate that the commission should forward to the national parliaments of the eea/efta states the legislative proposals which are sent for consultation to the national parliaments of the eu member states.
in writing. − switzerland, together with iceland, norway and liechtenstein, is part of the european free trade association (efta) and is an important trading partner of the eu. however, iceland, norway and liechtenstein have further strengthened their trade relations with the eu by adopting the agreement on the european economic area (eea). as switzerland is the eu's fourth largest trading partner in terms of volume, the adoption of the eea agreement is of paramount importance. hence my vote.
in writing. - it is absolutely essential to create a genuine european economic area as envisaged by the porto treaty.
in writing. - i hope that the eu-korea free trade agreement will be mutually beneficial and that the restrictions on free trade will be minimal for both sides. the safeguard measures are intended to address serious injury to the union industries. the bilateral safeguard clause should be tightened up in the agreement signed with south korea in october so that the modalities of its application are properly laid down and its operation is subject to a transparent process involving the counterparty. in the interests of free trade, these clauses must be limited to what is necessary to avoid greater harm and be appropriate and proportionate to the situations they are intended to prevent. i hope that european industry will be increasingly robust and creative so that the actual recourse will not happen.
in writing. - this proposal for a european parliament and council regulation constitutes the legal instrument for the application of the safeguard clause of the eu-korea fta. a free trade agreement between the eu and the republic of korea was concluded on 15 october 2009. the agreement incorporates a bilateral safeguard clause which provides for the possibility to reinstate the duty applied to parties benefiting from the most-favoured-nation (mfn) treatment whenever, as a result of trade liberalisation, imports increase under conditions which cause or threaten to cause serious injury to the union industry manufacturing like or directly competing products. in order for these measures to become operational, the safeguard clause should be incorporated into the legislation of the european union, as it is necessary to specify not only the procedural aspects of the application of safeguard measures, but also the rights of the parties concerned.
in writing. − the adoption of this safeguard clause, which is a recognition of the harmful consequences of the liberalization and deregulation of world trade, does not remove the dangers and concerns that the eu-south korea free trade agreement entails for the future of various sectors of economic activity, particularly in some member states, such as portugal, and in regions more dependent on these sectors. we recall the textile and clothing sector, which is particularly targeted by this agreement. we are reminded of the study by the directorate-general for employment and eurofund, which puts forward scenarios of a reduction in community employment in this sector of between 20 and 25% by 2020, but even goes so far as to put forward a scenario of a loss of 50% of the jobs currently existing in the european union. we also recall sectors such as the electronics industry and the automotive component industry. the neoliberal fundamentalism of the eu, in the name of the profits of its multinationals, continues to sacrifice jobs and productive capacity on the altar of free trade, continues to aggravate deficits, to promote external dependence and chronic and growing imbalances in trade balances. it continues to justify attacks on workers' rights, social dumping, the ruin of millions of small producers and many small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. − the eu-south korea free trade agreement is of great importance for the economic development of the eu member states. however, in order to avoid distortions and to ensure a balance between imports and exports from both sides, bilateral safeguard clauses are necessary. these clauses allow to safeguard possible serious injury to the eu industry in case of an excessive increase in imports of certain products. it is therefore necessary to incorporate that safeguard clause into eu legislation in order to make those measures operational.
in writing. the european union is the world's most demanding production area and the world's most permeable market. this creates very serious problems, especially for our producers who, because of the heavy and extensive set of standards they have to meet, sometimes have higher production costs than their competitors in other parts of the world. if they gain free access to our markets, this creates an unfair competition situation which is unbearable for producers, but also for processors, industry and traders and which is very damaging in the medium term for european society. in this context, i warmly welcome this report on trade between the european union and korea which, by providing for a bilateral safeguard clause to avoid significant damage to european industry in the event of a high volume of imports, recognises this chronic problem and begins to take appropriate measures to minimise it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, in which i was responsible for the european socialist group, because i considered it necessary to rebalance the relationships established along the food supply chain, to make them transparent, to ensure that there is a framework of fair and competitive good practice and a system of supervision to ensure their proper functioning. i now hope that the commission will take account of the guidelines adopted by parliament here today and translate them into its legislative proposal which it will present to us by the end of the year.
in writing. − once the problems in food supply chains have been identified at european and global level, effective solutions are urgently needed. this report sets out some ways forward, among which i would highlight the need to promote the increase in the surplus value of european agri-food production, the importance of considering measures against abusive practices, such as a system of sanctions and the drawing up of public lists of companies that are in breach of the rules, and the creation of a european observatory on agricultural prices and margins. in addition, i believe it is essential to promote the rationalisation of the food supply chain in order to reduce the environmental impact of food transport, the marketing of local food products and the sustainable development of the rural economy.
in writing. − the food crisis and the resulting volatility in food and commodity prices have exposed existing concerns about the functioning of food supply chains at european and global level. they also pointed to the gap between the annual increase in food prices, 3.3%, and the price farmers receive, 2.1%, compared to the increase in expenditure, 3.6%, reflecting the lack of price transparency along the supply chain. i am in favour of the content of this report because i believe that balanced trade relations would not only improve the functioning of the food supply but would also benefit farmers themselves. i therefore reaffirm that the fundamental objective of the cap must be to maintain the competitiveness of european agriculture and to support agricultural activity in the eu in order to ensure local food production and balanced territorial development. but without neglecting the ability to secure fair incomes in the agricultural sector. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'fair income for farmers: improving the functioning of the food supply chain in europe' as measures are needed to ensure fairer incomes for farmers, more transparent prices for consumers and a better functioning of the food supply chain in europe, including through legislative proposals to correct an unfair distribution of income along the food chain, respond to price volatility and reduce the vulnerability of farmers.
in writing. - we all agree that farmers, because of the specific nature of their activity, are particularly exposed to price volatility. some good measures for their protection are advanced in the report, but others cannot but be questioned. the compulsory reporting of market shares is therefore in danger of becoming a mere bureaucratic measure. i also express doubts about the fact that the existence of abuses of dominant positions and unfair practices in the food supply chain is highlighted, because if there are indeed abuses and unfair practices, the current competition laws must be applied and the offenders punished! that is why i do not see much need for a new relationship between competition rules and the cap. as far as private labels are concerned, we know that they give consumers greater freedom of choice and studies show that consumers end up preferring these products. that's how the market works. there are many subjects in this report which will allow for further reflection in the future.
in writing. - farmers must have a fair income. it is not acceptable that since 1996 farm costs have increased by 3.6% while prices of products produced by farmers have increased by only 2.1%. however, food prices have risen by 3.3% a year, which means that farmers have been the ones being penalized. it should be noted that the average income of farmers decreased by more than 12% in the eu-27 in 2009. all the objectives of the treaty of rome relating to agriculture (increased productivity, adequate food supplies, reasonable consumer prices, stabilization of markets) have been achieved, with the exception of the objective of ensuring fair incomes in agriculture. the commission should improve the european food price monitoring tool to meet the need for greater transparency in food price formation among consumers and farmers. i also call on the commission to implement swiftly the pilot project on the creation of a european observatory of agricultural prices and margins (complete with data on prices, margins and volumes), for which the european parliament and the council have adopted an allocation of eur 1.5 million in the 2010 budget.
in writing. - the report falls far short of the ambition that seemed to be associated with its title. the text ends up offering little or nothing concrete on how to achieve fair incomes for farmers, leaving vague and even ambiguous wording, referring to the european commission to submit proposals that would be the obligation of the ep to submit. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of certain substances and preparations is a very good one. a price policy is needed which takes account of the sensitive nature of this activity and which, among other measures, fixes fair minimum amounts to be paid to farmers. quantitative control of imports is required, by implementing community preference, giving priority to the production of each country and its food sovereignty. large-scale farms should be obliged to market a significant share of each country's national production, taking into account in particular the levels of agri-food dependence and the state of its trade and agri-food balance.
in writing. - the eu can only have a strong and self-sufficient agricultural sector if farmers have fair incomes and what they produce is sold at a fair price. however, the great pressure exerted by the main food supply chains has led to a decrease in prices paid to farmers and an increase in the cost of products to consumers. the increase in consumer prices must be reflected in the price paid to the farmer, because only then can balanced trade relations be achieved. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it contains numerous proposals to balance the balance of power between the different players in the food production and supply chain. the weak link in this chain is now small and mediumsized farmers, and without fair compensation it will be impossible to successfully combat the human desertification of rural areas and at the same time to reconvert small farming and the associated manufacturing industry in environmental terms.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the financing and operation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, because i fully support the idea that the fund should be mobilised more quickly, especially at a time when the increase in unemployment resulting from the economic and financial crisis must be addressed by making the egf a flexible and permanent support instrument.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution in agreeing with the requests made to the european commission to speed up the egf, which include, amongst others, an evaluation of the contributions granted taking into account the impact of the egf on its network of beneficiaries and the small and medium-sized enterprises potentially affected by redundancy schemes and whose workers could benefit from the fund. i also agree with the proposals to the commission which aim to reduce by half the time required to mobilise the egf, in particular that the commission should have the necessary human and technical resources, while respecting the principle of budgetary neutrality, to process applications submitted by the member states in an efficient and rapid manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the financing and operation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. the increase in the number of applications for assistance from the fund and the difficulties in applying the procedure for mobilisation and implementation require rapid amendments to its procedural and budgetary provisions. given the disparity between cases, the european commission should make a proposal for greater flexibility in the intervention criteria applicable to each member state in order to avoid inequalities in access to this instrument.
in writing. - the vicissitudes of the european globalisation adjustment fund make particularly clear both the disparity and the relatively small number of egf applications and the shortcomings of this instrument to support the reintegration of dismissed workers into the labour market. it is necessary to examine in detail the reasons for the insufficient use of the fund and to identify ways of speeding up its use by the member states, in particular those most affected by unemployment.
in writing. − the eu, in order to mitigate the negative consequences of globalisation for workers who are victims of collective redundancies, has created the european globalisation adjustment fund to financially support personalised vocational reintegration programmes. the fund has an annual allocation of €500 million. in view of the economic and social crisis, the low rate of implementation of this fund is surprising. in fact, from 2007 to the first half of 2009, only €80 million of the €1.5 billion available was used for 18 applications, in favour of 24 431 workers and 8 member states. since the changes to this fund in may 2009, the number of applications submitted has increased from 18 to 46, the total contribution requested has increased from €80 million to €197 million and the number of countries submitting applications has increased from 8 to 10. however, 9 member states have not yet made use of the egf. in addition, the eu regions with the highest gdps have benefited most from this fund. the reasons for this must be assessed and action taken to ensure that the fund is implemented more effectively and more quickly and that it is transformed into an independent fund with its own appropriations for commitments and payments.
in writing. - the implementation of this fund has shown that we were right when, at its very first stage, we criticised several aspects of its regulation, and that we partially took up this criticism in the subsequent revision which the european commission had to propose, acknowledging some of the criticisms we had made in the original version. we therefore agree that the commission should be asked to bring forward its mid-term evaluation by 30 june 2011 and to accompany it with a proposal to revise the egf regulation to 'remedy its most obvious shortcomings'. but, as i said in the plenary, it is essential not to forget the preventive measures that must be taken to stop multinationals moving, to combat unemployment and to increase employment with rights. it is also essential to ensure that the fund is not used to cover or facilitate redundancies caused by business restructuring or relocation of multinationals. finally, we insist on the need to increase the community contribution from 65% to at least 80% in order to make it possible for member states with the greatest financial difficulties to have recourse to the fund, so that the unemployed who need it most can be supported quickly and effectively.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund has been a very important instrument in helping the thousands of unemployed in the eu who have found themselves in this situation in the face of the relocation of industries to other continents. in the current crisis and in the face of the large increase in the number of collective redundancies, improvements to this instrument are necessary, as well as the search for new sources of financing. hence my vote.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution to agree with the requests made to the european commission to speed up the egf, which include an assessment of the contributions granted taking into account the success rate of reintegration and the increase in the professional qualifications of the beneficiaries, a comparative analysis of the measures financed in response to each egf application and the results obtained on the basis of reintegration and the impact of the egf on its network of beneficiaries and the small and medium-sized enterprises potentially affected by redundancy plans and whose workers could benefit from the fund. i also agree with the request to the commission to make available to the member states a series of guidelines for the design and implementation of applications for egf funding, aimed at a rapid application procedure and a broad consensus among the parties concerned as regards the strategy to be applied and the measures to be taken for the effective reintegration of workers into the labour market. finally, i agree with the call for the member states to set up a structure for the communication and administration of the egf at national level, in liaison with all the parties concerned, in particular the social partners, and to exchange good practice at european level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree with the requests made to the european commission to speed up the egf, which include an evaluation of the contributions granted taking into account the success rate of reintegration and the increase in the professional qualifications of the beneficiaries. i also agree with the proposals to the commission which aim to reduce by half the time required for mobilising the egf, in particular that all means should be made available to ensure speedy and enhanced communication with the member state concerned.
in writing. − the structural funds have proved to be invaluable tools for reducing imbalances in the european territory, in particular by supporting the most vulnerable outermost regions. the creation of the european globalisation adjustment fund reflected the european union's recognition that the phenomenon of globalisation has brought about major changes, not always positive, and has had a differentiated impact on europe, with some regions gaining from the process and others losing, and much more. however, this fund has not enjoyed the visibility it deserves, which in my view is mainly due to the enormous time lag between the request for aid by the member state and the actual receipt of the funds. this delay has serious consequences for the families concerned and is linked to the complexity of the application, mobilisation and implementation of funds, which should be simplified as a matter of urgency and as a matter of top priority. only in this way will it be possible to achieve the objective of this fund through the effective reintegration of workers who become unemployed following significant changes in international trade patterns. the report we voted on today reflects an effort to reach a compromise between the various political groups and that is why i supported it.
in writing. - the brussels i regulation provides the basis for european judicial cooperation in civil and commercial matters. this instrument is one of the most successful eu legislative acts, having laid the foundations for a european judicial area. it has proved to be very effective in facilitating the settlement of cross-border disputes through a system of judicial cooperation based on global rules of jurisdiction, as well as in relation to the coordination of parallel proceedings and the circulation of judicial decisions. i agree with the need for improvements, such as the abolition of the exequatur procedure in all matters covered by the regulation, allowing for the free movement of judicial decisions to be accelerated, but provided that all the necessary guarantees are safeguarded. i also consider it important to create a european judicial culture through training and the use of existing networks (e.g. the european judicial training network, the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters), which should improve communication between judges. it is essential to create a well-structured and easily accessible legal framework, which should involve the commission's review of the interrelationship between the different regulations dealing with jurisdiction, enforcement and applicable law.
in writing. − aware of the enormous importance of council regulation (ec) no 44/2001 in the field of private international law and the need for an appropriate legal framework to enable the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, i agree with the rapporteur that the revision of this regulation raises very important technical and legal issues. i am inclined to agree with the abolition of the exequatur as proposed in the report and i find many of the proposals contained here interesting and pragmatic. this will be a debate to watch closely.
in writing. the resolution deals with the application of council regulation (ec) no 44/2001 of 22 december 2000 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters (brussels i) in the light of the commission's green paper. this regulation, together with the brussels convention which preceded it, is one of the most successful eu legislative acts, having laid the foundations of a european judicial area, bringing good services to citizens and businesses. it has promoted legal certainty and the predictability of decisions by standardising european rules. it does, however, need to be updated. i agree with the abolition of the exequatur (execution clause) as it will speed up the free movement of judicial decisions and is a key pillar in the construction of the european judicial area. however, such deletion must be compensated by appropriate safeguards designed to protect the rights of the party against whom enforcement is sought. i believe that the commission should review the interrelationship between the different regulations dealing with jurisdiction, enforcement and the applicable law and that the overall objective should be a soundly structured and easily accessible legal framework.
in writing. − this report analyses the social integration of women in the context of european union policies. it also analyses the role of women in ethnic minorities. this knowledge base is essential to understanding the integration difficulties faced by these women, which include both traditional minorities and newly established minorities such as immigrants. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to meet the legitimate aspirations of women belonging to minority groups. specific action is needed at eu level, in particular when adopting policies and measures aimed at social inclusion. in addition, as the report advocates, it is essential to encourage the political and social participation of these women in areas such as political leadership, education and culture. this will help to combat their underrepresentation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that women belonging to ethnic minorities are subject to multiple discrimination. this calls for raising public awareness of women's rights, the need to empower women and encourage them to take on leadership roles in their communities. this is also a way of promoting human rights. although social inclusion is still the sole responsibility of the member states, the european commission should take a gender perspective into account when adopting policies and measures aimed at social inclusion.
in writing. − in an increasingly multicultural society, policies to integrate minority groups are of particular relevance as a way of combating discrimination, racism, violence and the exclusion and marginalisation of minority groups, pushing them to the fringes of society. we know that stigmatization and exclusion of minority groups only breeds discontent and revolt, which in turn breeds appetite for transgression and violence. it is up to our society to integrate without discrimination, to accept without excluding. this does not mean, however, that we accept without question all the realities which are part of the culture, tradition or creed of ethnic minorities. this is particularly relevant in customs relating to women. we must therefore firmly combat all cultural practices of discrimination on grounds of sex and all forms of violence still felt against women belonging to certain ethnic groups. integration also means protecting, and in this case protecting women, especially female children, so often the silent victims of customs and traditions that we cannot accept.
in writing. − this resolution addresses social inclusion policies in the european union for women belonging to ethnic minority groups. i would stress the need to promote the education and training of these women and to support their access to the labour market in order to avoid social exclusion and discrimination. only through inclusion can we address the stigma and prejudice that ethnic segregation creates. it should be noted that the european union does not have a legally binding policy on social inclusion, mainly because social inclusion is the responsibility of the member states. however, integration policy has been gaining in importance at eu level and integration is becoming even more important as the economic and social aspects underlying population ageing are becoming more relevant. eu rules and principles apply, in most cases, only to eu citizens who are also citizens of the member states. minorities who have settled and acquired legal status as citizens are protected by the rules and principles of the european union. however, this protection must be extended to migrants who are not yet nationals of a member state.
(gue/ngl), in writing. - the social integration of women belonging to ethnic minority groups is a relevant issue, given that these women are more vulnerable to social exclusion, as the current situation with the unacceptable collective expulsion of the roma population by france clearly demonstrates. it is essential that the fight against all forms of discrimination, whether based on sex, ethnic origin or colour, be placed at the centre of community attention and policies. it is therefore time to break with the macroeconomic policies that exacerbate unemployment, social inequalities and discrimination. as the report says, we must strive for genuine social integration by focusing on quality, universal public services that are accessible to all, including immigrant families and children, in particular in education, health, housing and social protection. no more empty statements and empty words. we need urgent measures to promote dignity and equality and to provide clear answers to social problems, and not to resort to xenophobic and discriminatory actions, which are all the more reprehensible when they come from the government itself.

in writing. - this is a report that focuses on a subject for which european public opinion has become increasingly sensitive, not only because of dramatic situations occurring outside the european union and challenging our moral conscience, but also because of the recognition that problems at this level also occur among us and require our political and civic intervention. women belonging to ethnic minority groups often face pressure from higher-ranking relatives who prefer to maintain traditions that enslave women. as a general rule, they have a low level of education, little information about the possible means of asserting themselves in relation to family authority and the societies in which they are integrated and/or host. at this level, they may still face xenophobic feelings. the development and implementation of european gender equality policy should contribute to decisively reducing the serious injustices to which these women are subjected worldwide and also in the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the role of women in an ageing society because i feel it is time to raise awareness of gender inequalities in the older population, which are mainly the result of lifelong gender disadvantages. it is now clear to everyone that older women are at greater risk of poverty because they have reduced pensions because of the gender pay gap or because they have stopped or interrupted their work to devote themselves to their family without having received any pay or having been registered with the social security system. in a time of economic recession, the risk of falling into poverty is even greater for these women. it is time for our institutions to adopt a more positive attitude towards ageing. i therefore welcome the commission's initiative to make 2012 the launch year for active ageing and solidarity between generations. the adoption of an age-gender approach should become an indispensable tool in policy-making in all relevant areas (economic, social, public health, consumer rights, digital agenda, rural and urban development, etc.).

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'the role of women in an ageing society'. the pay gap between women and men is now over 17% in the european union. this is why, and because women often stay at home during their working lives to care for children or other dependent family members, often opting for parttime work, the pay gap between women and men widen at retirement age. it is urgent for member states to adopt measures to take into account the gender dimension in the reform of pension schemes and the adjustment of the retirement age, taking into account the differences between men and women in working standards and the higher risk of discrimination of older women in the labour market.
in writing. - considering, as the report tells us, 'that gender is a significant factor in ageing, as the life expectancy of women is about six years longer than that of men', and knowing that european society is ageing, the truth is that we will have, increasingly, older women in our society who have to be assured of adequate living conditions and a role which, in many cases, may still be active. we must not forget, as the report also reminds us, that older women are more vulnerable to poverty and therefore need special attention. but more than solutions based on welfare or social status, i believe that these women must be assured of an active role in society. many are professionals with vast experience that can be used to the benefit of the younger ones. others are grandparents and great-grandparents and can, within the family, take on key caring roles, allowing young mothers to better balance family and work. they are invaluable assets and it is our task to encourage and protect them, creating a society of genuine solidarity between generations.
in writing. − this resolution addresses the vulnerability of older women in the context of the phenomenon of population ageing in the eu which is seen as a burden on national economies by ignoring the potential of older people, who are repeatedly seen as passive objects rather than active subjects. i would stress the particular risk of poverty to which older women are exposed, and i therefore support incentives to employ older people, for example through compensation for employers. i do not agree, however, with a specific scheme for older lbt women. with the entry into force of the eu charter of fundamental rights, the prohibition of discrimination on any ground has become part of the legislative competence of the european union. article 21 of the charter prohibits discrimination on grounds, inter alia, of sex, race, colour or ethnic or social origin, genetic characteristics, language, religion or belief, political or other opinion, belonging to a national minority, wealth, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation, while article 25 provides that the union recognises and respects the right of older persons to an independent and dignified life and to participate in social and cultural life. i understand that the implementation of these rights will serve to combat any kind of discrimination.

in writing. − this is a report that focuses on a theme that is becoming increasingly important in western countries, given the traditional increased work that women do in society and the fact that this may be aggravated in a context of an inverted demographic pyramid. in addition to these aspects it is also important to consider that the life expectancy of women is higher than that of men and continues to increase which, being a positive aspect in itself, often implies an increasing number of women who are left to themselves at the end of life. today, often: the adult woman takes care of the children, the parents and the in-laws; later, she takes care of her grandchildren, mother and mother-in-law; and then later on, she's still alone, a widow, and her children are far away because of the extreme mobility that characterizes contemporary societies, with no one to take care of her who took care of everyone. the attention paid to this subject, the means of monitoring the situation it points out and the interventions in this field it advocates, determined my approval.

the commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, freedom of the press and of expression is not a medal that has been won over time and can be hung in a window. it is something that must be won every day with effort, and we in europe often forget this. freedom of the press is currently under threat in europe, threatened by the crisis, by the concentration of the media and also by the opportunism of some political leaders. in italy, journalists who publish wiretaps can be fined up to €10,000. mr berlusconi, who controls five of the six television channels, wants to implement a law that would force websites to ask the government for permission to reproduce video or audio reports, expanding his control to new media. in hungary, there is a plan to create an authority over the media controlled by the prime minister. in romania, the supreme national defence council, the military, is asking the local parliament to pay attention to the phenomenon of smear campaigns organized by the media and so on. at the same time, it is not just a problem of states, it is a problem of companies as well. media concentration increases, media owners, owners, increasingly interfere with newsrooms. the commissioner said that the member states have constitutional traditions which protect fundamental rights. but we in europe are also building our own constitutional tradition and we must, for reasons which mrs in 't veld has just mentioned, also extend the defence of media freedom to the european area. some ideas: we need to create ways to support independent and freelance journalists, journalists who are now impoverished and who are easy prey to pressures from the state or from companies. we need to expand anti-trust legislation and we also need to probably create a press support fund to guarantee the independence and quality of the press until a new business model is found on the internet in this transitional phase.
