for the gue/ngl group madam president, animal protection is a value which europe has an obligation to promote, but what is at stake here goes far beyond this premise and raises difficult questions for us. no value should be regarded as an absolute value in itself. we are therefore faced with choices and contradictions, and only balanced legislation can resolve them. on a scale of values, should animal welfare be subordinated to the value of human health? what is the european research strategy when it comes to, for example, human health and basic research? how can we avoid suppressing european medical research, which could ultimately lead to its destruction? the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we must have the capacity to develop and promote alternative methods to the use of animals for scientific purposes, but there is a lot of discussion to be had and i would very much like to see it taken further.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would also like to begin by congratulating mrs jeggle on the excellent work she has done on behalf of parliament and her committee on agriculture in the commission and the council. after a year and a half of negotiations, under the swedish, spanish and now belgian presidencies, it was possible to reach a compromise between the requirements of the scientific community and what, in these circumstances, we can call animal welfare. the majority obtained to reach this result was achieved around a very emotional, very intense debate, where everyone made concessions, and with a broad citizen involvement, as you would expect in a matter as sensitive as this. but we as policy-makers have to make decisions and, although we are not without sensitivity to animal suffering, we have to make choices by hierarchising values and this position today brought forward by mrs jeggle reflects an era of hierarchising values which we feel is appropriate between the benefits to human health and the suffering of animals. the socialist group will therefore vote against this report and reject all amendments.
mr president, the report which mrs jeggle is presenting to us today should bring to a close a long and complex process which has been made possible only by hard work and a skillful capacity for dialogue, and for which we thank her. indeed, where the issues under consideration involve not only multiple interests but also moral values, they trigger not only sound rational arguments but also emotions. they do not facilitate the consensus we are seeking here, in order to serve the european citizens, to contribute to the construction of europe by drawing up and presenting common standards, while respecting the positions of the different political groups and the different member states, and it is precisely this desirable standardisation of criteria which is at issue in this report, in the context of the assumption of a higher level of protection of animal life. thus, over a period of two years, and since the decision to revise the 1986 directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes and the recognition of the disparities between the member states, efforts have been made in this context to establish more detailed rules in this area in order to reduce the disparities in procedures. the higher level of protection that should be afforded to animals used for scientific purposes had to be balanced against the imperative of safeguarding the conditions necessary for biomedical research to continue and develop in the european union. this balance has been achieved in the text we are about to vote on. for the benefit of the animals we protect, in fulfilling our human responsibilities to animals and without compromising the quality and progress of biomedical research from which we all benefit every day.
mr president, the development of techniques and methodologies which dispense with animal experimentation and which minimise the suffering inflicted on animals, where this proves necessary, must be an objective of scientific research and experimental and technological development which must be encouraged. in addition to their development, account should be taken of the need for the dissemination of these techniques and methodologies and their uptake by research and development institutions and national scientific and technological systems at different levels of development. the european union should play an important role in this area by promoting cooperation between scientific and technical institutions and systems in different countries, including third countries. in our view, of course, the establishment of common minimum levels of protection in this and other areas should not prevent each member state, if it so wishes, from adopting more advanced protection measures.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it will update the existing directive, which dates back to 1986, and because it also aims to increase the balance between the interests of the research sector and the strengthening of the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. i also consider essential in this respect the commitment to promote the progress of alternative methods to animal use and to ensure the improvement of animal welfare without compromising progress in this sector. the most important points approved by this report concern animal welfare aspects, namely the implementation of substitution, which is intended to facilitate the advancement of alternative approaches not involving the use of live animals; the introduction of a process for classifying methods used in animals on the basis of pain levels and the setting of a maximum pain limit; and the implementation of the directive through a more effective control system. the lack of oversight has sometimes led to experiments where alternatives to animal use exist still being carried out using animals, especially in basic experiments not intended to test hypotheses put forward by scientists.
in writing. − the use of animals in scientific research is associated with discoveries of great social impact, increased longevity and human well-being. the present state of science does not yet allow for the total abandonment of animal testing. it is therefore imperative to ensure the maximum possible protection and welfare of the animals still used, taking into account the objectives of the experiment. i believe that this revision of legislation sets higher standards by strengthening animal protection. with this directive, the european union will improve its standards for the welfare of animals used in scientific experiments, as it plays a significant role in reducing the number of animals used in experiments and requires the use of alternative methods wherever possible, while ensuring a level playing field for the eu industrial sector and enhancing the quality of research carried out in the eu. the result of today's vote showed a general consensus on the need to improve the situation of animals needed for scientific research and safety testing, while maintaining a high standard of research and intensifying efforts to find alternative methods to animal testing.
in writing. - a civilized society recognises animals as living beings who share our existence and whose pain and suffering must be prevented as far as possible. i do, however, recognise the need for the use of animals in scientific trials to test new medicines and therapies or to enable scientific research to be translated into discoveries that help to cure disease or limit suffering and increase the life expectancy of human beings. the wide diversity of legislation and the lack of adequate protection in some member states called for the adoption of a directive setting minimum standards without prejudice to those states which provide greater protection for the animals concerned. the negotiations between the ep, the council and the commission were not easy, but a text was reached which i believe is overall balanced and which deserves our support. it is a step forward which should be welcomed, even if it could be happier in some respects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes because i believe that the compromise reached with the council reflects the balance that can be struck between the needs of scientific research for the protection of human health and the requirements of animal welfare and rights.
in writing. - as has been said by the parties involved, the text we are adopting today is a satisfactory compromise between the various interests at stake, achieved after long negotiations between the institutions involved - parliament, commission and council. i do not think it is debatable in civilized societies that the use of animals for scientific purposes should be properly regulated, as is the case in europe. and that is what we are talking about here: proper regulation of a use which is fundamental to scientific progress and to the discovery of new procedures, treatments or medicines which in the future will be of greater civilization value and benefit to all. it seems that such regulations cannot be excessive in the protection they afford animals, otherwise they would compromise scientific study and research. in making a choice, i choose the people who will benefit tomorrow from the results of what we allow today to be studied and researched on animals. if the proposal we are adopting today allows for advances in the study of neurological diseases, autoimmune diseases or cancer, amongst others, i believe we will all have won.
in writing. - about 12 million animals are used in scientific procedures in the 27 member states each year. it is important that every effort be made to reduce the number of animals used in these experiments to the minimum necessary. the most pragmatic approach to this end is to use alternative methods, since the current state of science does not yet allow for the complete abandonment of animal testing. directive 86/609/eec on the protection of animals used for experimental and other scientific purposes was adopted to harmonise practices in the field of animal experimentation in the eu. however, some member states set ambitious targets while others limited themselves to applying minimum rules. the resolution thus seeks to correct this situation of inequality. a level playing field for industry and the scientific community in the eu should be ensured, while strengthening the protection of animals still used for scientific purposes, in accordance with the protocol on the protection and welfare of animals annexed to the ec treaty. in the field of animal testing, efforts should be made to further promote the development, validation, acceptance and application of alternative methods and to apply the principle of the 3rs of animal testing: replace, reduce and refine.
in writing. - we believe that in this, as in other areas, the establishment of common minimum levels of protection at legislative level should not prevent each member state from adopting more advanced and more stringent protection measures, if it so chooses. we therefore voted in favour of the amendment proposed in this connection. as regards the techniques and methodologies which make it possible to dispense with animal experimentation, as we said in the debate, we believe that it is important to encourage their development, but that more is needed. it is also important to disseminate them and make them assimilatable by the wider r&d institutions, including in the national science and technology systems with comparatively lower levels of development. any legislative framework in this area must take account of this need - a fact which one of the proposed amendments did not seem to us to fully safeguard. the eu should play an important role in this area by promoting cooperation between the scientific and technical institutions and systems of the different countries.
in writing. - the adoption of this report, after tough negotiations between the parties involved, is a balanced compromise, safeguarding both the protection of animals used for scientific purposes and the need for their use to achieve important discoveries and developments in technologies and therapies used later in the cure of many diseases affecting civilization. hence my vote.

in writing. − this initiative aims to examine the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, ensuring that they are respected in the union's proposals. subsidiarity is a dynamic and evolving concept, and allows the union to extend its action where necessary and to limit it where it is no longer justified. proportionality is a guiding principle for the exercise of the union's exclusive or shared competences, which should not exceed what is necessary to achieve the objectives. it highlights two major innovations in this area: the creation of the impact assessment committee and the fact that the entry into force of the lisbon treaty gives national parliaments an important role in assessing how these two principles are applied - ex ante political control, which can lead to a review or possible withdrawal of the proposal, or ex post judicial control, with recourse to the court of justice if they consider that these principles have been breached. this evaluation system enables the union to legislate better by presenting an analysis and justification of its proposals, and improves their quality, rigor and transparency. i welcome the fact that the impact assessment system is working properly and i support the strengthening of the analysis process.

in writing. − this resolution addresses the theme 'better lawmaking' which covers the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality which are indispensable to the proper functioning of the european union, through, for example, the need for impact assessment studies of the lawmaking process, the simplification and harmonisation of law and the reduction by 25% by 2010 of the administrative burden resulting from european law. i would like to highlight the european citizens' initiative introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which will allow citizens to participate actively in the process of creating european law, the fact that the european parliament is now on an equal footing with the council in the ordinary legislative procedure and the involvement of national parliaments in monitoring the application of the principle of subsidiarity. in this context, in accordance with article 225 of the lisbon treaty and because it is an example of 'best legislation', i proposed in an own-initiative report the drawing up of a specific directive on bio-waste, which was approved by a majority in the july plenary session, and to which i hope the commission will respond promptly.

in writing. - better regulation has become an essential condition for the proper functioning of the european union and for the correct application of european law based on greater transparency, effectiveness and consistency of decisions. the correct application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, now reinforced after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, should contribute to simpler legislation and better understanding by citizens and to european decisions being taken as close as possible to the citizen. the lisbon treaty provides that the european parliament must act on an equal footing with the council and provides for closer involvement of national parliaments in monitoring the application of the principle of subsidiarity. in addition, the union regulatory environment should continue to promote impact assessments and the reduction of administrative burdens. as the report which i am voting in favour of states, only by significantly reducing administrative burdens and by effectively applying european laws in the internal legal systems, as well as by efficient impact assessments taking account of economic, social and environmental aspects, can we actually legislate better.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in the last year newspaper headlines and news headlines have been occupied on several occasions by storms, floods, heat waves, fires and other disasters, with profound consequences for people, the territory, the economy and the environment. but this has not been a reality of this past year alone. during the first six years of the european union solidarity fund, the commission received 62 requests for financial support from 21 different countries. of these, about one third fall into the category of major disasters. other disasters have not led to calls for the mobilisation of the fund, although their impacts on the affected populations, the environment and the economy have been considerable and, in many cases, lasting. disasters are deeply wicked. they almost always affect those who have the least means of protecting themselves, whether states or individuals. for this reason, the report states that a community approach to disaster prevention should include, as a central concern, the reduction of disparities between regions and member states in this field, in particular by helping to improve prevention in regions and member states with high risk exposure and lower economic capacity. natural disasters and, for the most part, man-made disasters can and should be prevented. often, disasters are fueled by policies that create an inadequate relationship between man and the physical environment around him. this report recognises that some of the eu's sectoral policies - such as the cap - have contributed to an increase in the exposure of certain regions and their populations to risk, in this case by promoting the abandonment of production and the consequent desertification. it is therefore necessary to correct and reverse them. the promotion of a balanced use of land and of economic and social development in harmony with nature is a decisive factor in disaster prevention. this report is rich in guidelines and recommendations. the debate in the various committees, the discussion with the shadow rapporteurs and the rapporteurs on the opinions and the proposals they all made for the final version of the report contributed a great deal to this. i thank all of you for your commitment and interest and for your openness to a discussion which has been profound and enriching. the report also contains a number of recommendations, some of which i would like to highlight very briefly: the creation of a financial framework appropriate to disaster prevention, which would strengthen and articulate the existing financial instruments; the definition of a set of actions to be given priority support to the member states with a view to correcting risk-inducing situations; the strengthening of early warning systems in the member states and the establishment and strengthening of links between the various early warning systems; the creation of a european public agricultural insurance scheme; the creation of the european observatory on drought and desertification; the launching of a specific initiative in the field of forestry and fire prevention. finally, in the context of prevention and in the light of the experience gained in recent disasters, it is imperative to revise the solidarity fund regulation to allow for a more flexible and timely mobilisation of this instrument. mr president, mr commissioner, the problem of disasters has been the subject of several resolutions in this parliament. some of the recommendations contained in this report were already contained in these earlier resolutions. this only reinforces his urgency. follow-up to these recommendations is necessary by putting them into practice. unfortunately, very little has been done in this area, and the commission bears particular responsibility for this delay. i urge the commission to take the broad consensus which the report has gathered during its discussion and vote in committee - and which i hope will be confirmed in its vote in this house - as a clear sign that this resolution is to be taken seriously and that the measures set out in it are to be put into practice.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that e-commerce, as an important sector with a future for economic growth in europe, cannot be left out of the internal market. e-commerce can contribute to the knowledge economy, bring added value and opportunities to european businesses and consumers, and improve the competitiveness of our economy in the context of the eu 2020 strategy, including the development and promotion of new forms of entrepreneurship for small and medium-sized enterprises. last year, one in three consumers in europe bought at least one item online, but only 7% of european consumers dared to do so in another member state. this trend must be reversed and the idea of creating a european trust mark, as advocated by the rapporteur, can help to do this. the need to develop a secure and innovative online payment modality may also contribute to increased trust of european consumers in electronic services from other member states. internet access must of course be extended and democratized in the eu. the commission must ensure that the diversity of consumer protection rules does not constitute an obstacle to the development of intra-european electronic commerce.
in writing. - e-commerce is a constantly evolving reality these days. it's no longer an emerging technology, it's a reality that's becoming more and more widespread. it is an important means of promoting cross-border trade, improving access to more varied, higher quality products, and competitively reducing prices. however, 10 years after the adoption of the e-commerce directive, crossborder e-commerce is not developing as rapidly as domestic e-commerce. technical and legal reasons are the reason behind the failure of 60% of crossborder orders attempted via the internet. i voted in favour of this report because it identifies the problems affecting european e-commerce and also points the way to a genuine online single market for europe. this requires improved implementation of european legislation for the benefit of all european consumers and retailers, increased efforts to achieve a high level of protection for e-commerce users, giving those users confidence to exploit the single market to its full potential, informing them about their rights and how to secure them in the field of e-commerce.
in writing. − the internal market for e-commerce is crucial for europe, notably in achieving the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. however, there are obstacles that need to be overcome. this report proposes measures to this end, among which i find particularly interesting the fight against copyright infringement on the internet and the development of a secure and innovative online payment system that does not impose deterrent fees. this will make it easier to combat piracy, encourage entrepreneurs to market on the internet and, on the other hand, facilitate access to and trust in the internet by users.
in writing. − e-commerce is a market of key importance for the eu in the 21st century, including in pursuing the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. we face the enormous challenge of creating a true online single market for europe, which will enable the eu to compete in the global market. the confidence of european businesses and consumers in the digital environment is reduced due to unnecessary barriers to e-commerce, such as the fragmentation of the european market, consumer insecurity, transaction insecurity, lack of redress mechanisms, etc. it is essential to simplify cross-border rules and to find practical solutions to issues such as copyright, consumer protection, labelling and sector-specific rules, e-waste and recycling rates, online declaration and invoicing. it is essential that existing legislation, such as the services directive, is fully transposed and implemented. at the same time, the commission should complete its assessment of the community legislation applicable to the digital single market and present the initiatives that appear necessary to address the main obstacles. i support the 13 commission recommendations for the development of policies and practices in the field of crossborder e-commerce.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. in a single market with more than 500 million consumers, further e-commerce flexibility and the promotion of consumer trust in transactions together not only allow the economic potential of the digital single market to be exploited, but also encourage the development of new market niches for smes, with consequent potential for job creation. the discrepancies between domestic and cross-border e-commerce prevent consumers, in particular those residing in peripheral or outermost regions, as well as those with reduced mobility, from benefiting from the benefits of e-commerce (access to a wide range of goods and services). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the provision of services to consumers, in particular in the area of electronic communications. i would stress that the operation of the 'one-stop shop' is essential for the completion of the digital single market for e-commerce. but equally important are measures such as the standardisation of postal and banking costs in the eu, simplification of vat returns for distance sales or the increase in .eu domain registrations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the completion of the internal market for electronic commerce. the eu 2020 strategy aims to promote a knowledge-based economy. in order to achieve this goal fully, the european commission needs to present measures to increase the speed of broadband services and further rationalise the costs of these services across the union. it is necessary to standardise rules and practices to ensure that distance traders can reach markets other than those limited by their national borders.
in writing. − in its communication of 19 may 2010 on a digital agenda for europe, the commission expressed its desire to make online transactions simpler and more trustworthy. according to the report, one in three europeans have made a purchase online, but only 7% of consumers dare to opt for cross-border transactions and only 12% express confidence in this type of transaction. it is therefore urgent to improve consumer safety (or perception) in relation to these transactions in order to foster the development of a market with very high potential easier, more convenient and, in many cases, lower cost transactions for the consumer. for a true electronic single market, it is essential that consumers feel safe when transacting online and that businesses realise the immense potential of online commerce to increase online supply and remove barriers across borders.
in writing. − the free movement of goods in europe is seriously hampered by fragmented sets of national rules. figures on the state of e-commerce in the eu show that in 2009 one in three consumers in europe bought at least one item online, but only 7% of european consumers would dare to do so in another member state. non-public eu investigations into e-commerce practices have shown that 60% of consumers' attempts to buy cross-border items in the eu fail, with the transaction or shipment being denied by the seller, although the buyer could save at least 10% by making an electronic purchase abroad (even including shipping costs) in half of the 11,000 cases investigated. i therefore stress the need for a comprehensive legal and regulatory framework capable of overcoming border barriers, enhancing value added and regulating the risks of an activity in continuous evolution and with a high margin of progression. this requires constant attention and monitoring, with priority given to the reliability of communications and transactions. the consolidation of e-commerce requires work on security and trust for businesses and consumers, particularly in the area of payments and delivery and return services.
in writing. - the report on electronic commerce contains some contradictions and an excessive insistence on the creation of the internal market. we recognize the importance of electronic commerce, but there is much to be done to prevent it from becoming a vehicle for new and serious problems. as we have stressed in the debate, there are many issues that need to be clarified, such as the protection of copyright, the protection of children's rights, consumer rights and safety. the report does make a number of suggestions to increase the confidence of all operators in the e-commerce market, but not all of them are the most appropriate or even take due account of all the interests and rights involved in a process which can prove to be very complex. it is true that the e-commerce supply chain needs to be more transparent, so that the consumer always knows the identity of the supplier, as well as its trade name, geographical address, contact details and tax number. but the rights of children and young people and people with various dependencies must always be safeguarded.
in writing. − the single market has always been one of the eu's major objectives. in the present day, cross-border e-commerce can make a very important contribution to the further development of the single market. internally, online shopping is already widely embraced by consumers. however, this is not the case in electronic commerce between the various member states, mainly because of the lack of mutual trust between seller and buyer. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. hence my vote.
in writing. - i abstained on this report despite the fact that i consider it important to promote electronic commerce and the necessary extension of internet networks and services in good conditions to the whole population, even in the most isolated areas. i also agree that it is essential to combat the discrimination faced by many citizens who wish to make online purchases, in particular on the basis of the member state in which they are located or the e-mail address they use to make the transaction. i agree with many of the suggestions made in this report. but i do not regret that the services directive has not yet been fully transposed in some member states, i do not support the commission's policy for the postal services sector, nor do i welcome the eu 2020 strategy. these underlying choices are largely responsible for the difficult social situation the eu is facing today. the construction of future models in the communications sector and even in electronic commerce will certainly be better framed in a perspective more centred on people and their rights and not just subordinated to commercial interests.
in writing. − it is essential to ensure safety in the civil aviation sector in europe and to reduce the number of accidents and incidents through investigative and prevention procedures. i voted in favour of this regulation because i believe that it promotes an environment conducive to spontaneous reporting of occurrences, by calling for the efficiency, speed and quality of european civil aviation safety investigations. i agree that investigations should be carried out by a national authority or other authorities responsible for safety investigations. i also believe that it is important to set up a european network of authorities to improve the quality of research methods and the training of researchers. another aspect which i consider important is the establishment of standards on the timely provision of information on persons and dangerous goods on board in the event of an accident, and the improvement of assistance to victims and their families.
in writing. − the intensification of air traffic has led to an increase in the risk of air accidents. despite the improvements that have been introduced in the field of safety, there are still gaps in the current accident investigation system. the safety system in this area is essentially based on feedback and lessons learned from accidents and incidents that have occurred, and it is important to strengthen coordination between the authorities responsible for safety investigations, including through the establishment of a european network, which should ensure full independence and a high level of efficiency, diligence and quality in such investigations, in order to identify any safety deficiencies and take corrective action. it is important to ensure effective prevention and a high level of safety in the civil aviation sector in europe and to spare no effort to reduce the number of accidents and incidents in order to ensure citizens' confidence in air transport. in addition to safety investigations, particular attention should also be paid to the issue of strengthening assistance to victims of air accidents and their families, whereby all european airlines should have a crisis and assistance plan.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on the investigation and prevention of accidents and incidents in civil aviation, because it introduces new rules which will make it possible to strengthen accident prevention and the transparency and speed of accident investigations.
in writing. − given that civil aviation has experienced a significant increase in the number of flights and passengers over the years, albeit associated with a decrease in air accidents and incidents, safety must remain a key concern today and always. i also know that the directive regulating the investigation of air accidents dates from 1994 and that much has changed in civil aviation since then, so i think it is urgent to review this regulation. i agree with the rapporteur when she speaks of the need for greater coordination and integration in the investigation of air accidents. in a space of increasing integration, and given that the consequences of an air crash do not affect only one state, it makes no sense for the national authorities to remain in a situation of almost backwardness in aviation. in this context, it seems to me possible to give a new role to the european aviation safety agency (easa). finally, i believe that this is one of the areas where it is imperative for the european union to act in a coordinated and integrated manner in order to ensure the safety of all passengers in european airspace.
in writing. - air transport is now undeniably playing a decisive role in the mobility of people and the dynamics of the world economy. its importance and impact will surely continue to grow in a society increasingly determined by globalisation and the priority given to the commercialisation of time and space. in the current context of global crisis and strong pressure to reduce costs and expenditure, an efficient regulatory and supervisory framework is required, taking into account the interests of users. safety is the main concern of users and has a strong impact on the pricing of travel. i would therefore stress the contribution of this report to the quality and independence of investigations into accidents and incidents in civil aviation, by harmonising the level of investigation capabilities of the member states and at the same time ensuring the adaptation and updating of european legislation in this area, in the face of developments in the sector and the emergence of new actors such as the european aviation safety agency. i would like to stress, however, that priority must be given to accident prevention and that this is the direction in which research should be directed as a tool for identifying problems and providing solutions.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment in the event of accidents. we appreciate the active role of the member states, particularly through their respective authorities responsible for investigations, which will form part of the european network of national authorities for this area. this network is presented with specific objectives: to make suggestions to the competent national authorities, to share information on research methods, to coordinate and organise training for researchers in each member state, to develop common research methodologies in the eu, and to develop and manage a framework for sharing resources. we will be following the future of this structure, because we believe that its operation should remain within the strict framework of the objectives set out above, and within the framework of the scheme of participation of the member states, through the national authorities responsible, now defined.
in writing. - currently, the european legislation governing aviation accident investigation is from 1994. the commission has therefore decided to amend the proposal to take account of the new situation in the sector. despite the great advances in aviation safety in recent years, the constant increase in air traffic means an increased risk of accidents. it is therefore necessary to focus not only on safety but also on prevention and to require from airlines, particularly low-cost airlines, that profitability levels must not be achieved at the expense of safety. it is also very important that the need to support the victims and their families is not given priority. hence my vote.
in writing. - air traffic has increased considerably since the european directive governing the investigation of aviation accidents in 1994. although there have been significant improvements in safety, these developments have naturally led to an increased likelihood of accidents, and have been accompanied by increased technological complexity and the emergence of new actors such as the european aviation safety agency. i think it is essential that air accidents be investigated independently and transparently in order to fill in the gaps and protect passengers. the promotion of a community-wide network of national authorities responsible for research can also help to reduce imbalances in research capacities between the various member states. assistance to victims and their families should be a priority for each country, so it is essential to ensure that all airlines established in each territory have assistance plans. i am pleased with the work of the rapporteur from the committee on transport and with the agreement reached with the european council at the end of june, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this regulation contributes to the response to the problem of gas supply crises in europe. it is crucial to define rules that ensure and improve the management of gas supply in europe. for better management of community emergency situations, i consider it essential to ensure greater capacity for interconnection between member states and greater coordination of action. i also believe in the importance of the regulation in setting up preventive and emergency plans at member state and commission level. the emergency response should also allow for greater flexibility to deal with crises with different characteristics in terms of duration or intensity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on measures to ensure the security of gas supply, because i believe that more coordinated action at european level is needed to allow for better management of possible future crises.
in writing. - gas currently accounts for more than a quarter of the energy supplied to the european union and more than half of this comes from suppliers outside the eu. by 2020, more than 80% of the gas used will be imported and some states are already 100% dependent on imported gas. this raises serious questions of security of supply, as the recent crisis has shown. naturally, this situation requires european action to ensure that there is sufficient infrastructure and capacity to avoid and resolve unexpected gas supply problems. in addition, it is urgent to look at the problems posed by the security of gas supply in europe and the risks associated with transit. the current proposal is based on three fundamental points, which is why i am voting in favour of it: (i) direct applicability of the new community legislation; (ii) the establishment of preventive action plans and emergency plans in the event of a supply disruption; and (iii) the strengthening of the role of the european commission in coordinating emergency measures and declaring an emergency at community or regional level, imposing the principle of solidarity between member states.
in writing. − this regulation on the security of gas supply, which repeals directive 2004/67/ec, is a legislative document that provides a concrete response to a real problem facing the union. this was evident during the gas crisis between russia and ukraine last winter, when millions of european citizens and our own economy were severely affected. the guarantees of energy supply, particularly gas, are fundamental to economic and social well-being and stability. in the face of the crises we have seen in europe, which usually occur at times when people are most in need of coping with extreme cold temperatures, the new european legislation ensures a coordinated response capacity at european level, both in terms of the service provided to consumers and in terms of the reaction to external supply cuts. the implementation of this regulation will thus contribute to significantly reducing the eu's vulnerability to external disruptions to energy supply and will also strengthen the leading role of european gas companies in the world and the geopolitical positioning of the union as a strategic global player. i would also like to stress the positive aspects of the imposition of preventive action plans.
in writing. − we recognise the concerns expressed about the security of gas supply, in which member states should play an active role, in particular through their respective competent authorities, but we consider the question raised about gas from russia to be exaggerated. if they fear problems, the solution is negotiation and diversification of sources of supply and production and not to use this pretext to deepen european integration, concentration and centralisation of decisions and infrastructure projects supporting the integration of the internal gas market. as i said in the debate, the most important issue for the future is the announced oil crisis, and the european union should therefore actively promote the replacement of refined oil in its fleets, and the best substitute is precisely natural gas. and we should not forget that there is also natural gas of non-fossil origin, biomethane, produced from waste, which, incidentally, several european countries are producing, of which i would like to mention sweden, switzerland and spain. it is a path that should be encouraged in terms of community investment.
in writing. − the security of gas supply in the european union must ensure that all citizens have access to energy for their basic needs, such as cooking and heating, and to essential public services such as hospitals and schools. it must also ensure that jobs are preserved. these must be the priorities and public policies are needed to implement them. the security of the population cannot be left to the market and to struggles for resources. prevention is essential here, as is solidarity between member states in times of energy crisis or disaster. energy security highlights the importance of decentralisation, the variety and proximity of generation processes and the integration of energy networks. micro-generation is therefore seen as the best guarantee of security of energy supply for the needs of citizens.
in writing. - gas is an increasingly important energy source in the eu landscape. the past has shown how important security of supply is, given that the eu is heavily dependent on gas from eastern europe, particularly russia. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. achieving this objective requires a common and effective approach to the security of supply of this fuel, which must be based on rules of transparency, solidarity and policies compatible with the functioning of the internal market. hence my vote.
in writing. - it is well known that pakistan is the country of origin of many illegal immigrants. there is therefore every advantage in establishing quick and effective means of contact with your authorities. i am not unaware of the reservations that the parliamentary left has about the agreement, but i believe that it confuses illegal immigration with the right to asylum and good personal feelings with good public policy. i agree with the wording of the resolution. this agreement between the union and pakistan does not only concern what is known as readmission. it is, as you can see, a bilateral agreement aimed at the extradition or, if you like, the expulsion of illegal immigrants from their respective territories.
in writing. − the aim of the agreement is to increase cooperation between the administrations of the eu member states and pakistan in order to speed up the readmission process. to this end, the agreement lays down the obligation to readmit nationals of the country concerned and, under certain conditions, third-country nationals and stateless persons on a basis of full reciprocity, as well as the necessary technical provisions on the readmission procedure. pakistan is a major source or transit country for migrants who do not, or no longer, fulfil the conditions in force for entry, presence or residence in the territory of an eu member state. despite ten years of negotiations, i welcome the adoption of this agreement, which is preferable to previous ad hoc agreements on this matter and will have positive effects not only for the eu-pakistan relationship but for the whole region.
in writing. - our vote against signing the agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation is justified, from the outset, by the fact that it creates a situation of legal uncertainty. but the most substantial reason is our criticism of the immigration policy of the european union. the legal complexity does not guarantee respect for the rights of immigrants, criminalizing them, as has been denounced by many organizations, forcing pakistan to take in its own nationals in an illegal situation and seeking to hold pakistan accountable for accepting afghans who have been in transit through that country. secondly, this agreement is yet another flagrant example of the hypocrisy that presides over eu decisions, which wants to wash its hands of its responsibility for the degradation of the situation of both the afghans after the us invasion and the maintenance of the occupation war by nato and the pakistanis in the now widened war on pakistan. the eu considers people fleeing war, hunger and poverty to be illegal (even terrorists) and should be returned to their countries of origin in search of decent living conditions for themselves and their families. the eu considers illegal and must expel immigrants who have fled the crimes of nato, who have been lured into mafia networks, who have been exploited as cheap labour and in conditions of work that are almost slave-like. this is an unacceptable position.
in writing. - i voted against this report because the eu-pakistan readmission agreement will allow people to be sent to a country which has not signed the 1951 geneva convention, which does not respect human rights and whose internal situation does not offer the necessary security for people to return. the eu will also be failing to respect the right to asylum if it sends back to pakistan citizens of other countries (e.g. afghanistan) who have arrived in the eu from pakistan, which could lead to the same person being subject to a series of deportations from one country to another that the eu will not control. in addition, this readmission agreement contains no safeguards or control mechanisms, is full of legal loopholes and ambiguities, and does not adequately respect the protection of personal data.
in writing. − the fight against illegal immigration has always been a priority for the eu. the agreement now approved has been negotiated with pakistan for many years and it seems to me to be a balanced document, and it is intended to extradite only citizens who are illegally present in eu territory. it is not therefore citizens who are seeking asylum or who are seeking to settle in the eu and who seek the authorities of the host country to regularise their situation. we cannot confuse illegal immigrants with citizens who want to settle legally in the eu. it is nevertheless very important to continue to press pakistan to ratify the 1966 international covenant on civil and political rights and the united nations convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on trade and economic relations with turkey. the full implementation of the eu-turkey customs union, which has been in place since 1996, requires the removal of the remaining bureaucratic obstacles, tariff and non-tariff barriers. i also consider it important that turkey should put women's employment at the centre of its economic and social policies, given the low participation of women in the labour market.
in writing. - the european union and turkey have been important trading partners for several years. this mutually beneficial partnership has been hampered by turkish attempts to restrict access to its market for european products by means of administrative and bureaucratic constraints. i hope that these barriers will be removed, that turkey will fight decisively against the counterfeiting of european products and defend the legitimate rights of creators to the proceeds of their inventive processes, and that trade and economic relations between the union and turkey will grow and strengthen. as i have already said, whatever the future shape of eu-turkey relations, i hope that they will be closer and continue along the path of dialogue and effective cooperation and that turkey will continue along the path it has embarked on towards freedom and democracy of a western origin.
in writing. - in 1963 turkey and the eec concluded an association agreement, which provided for the establishment of a customs union by 1996. this act allowed for the deepening of economic relations through the creation of the au. the products covered by the ua include all industrial products and processed agricultural products. in 2009, turkey's exports to the eu amounted to eur 33.6 billion and imports from the eu to eur 40.4 billion. turkey has also become the 17th largest economy in the world according to world bank statistics, and the sixth largest economy in europe. turkey ranked 20th as a recipient of foreign direct investment (fdi). the au created in 1996 does not cover agricultural products and areas such as services and public procurement. as regards public contracts, turkey continues to grant a price advantage of 15% to turkish tenderers. turkey is urged to simplify procedures and bureaucracy and to remove the remaining tariff and non-tariff barriers to the elimination of all unnecessary obstacles to trade between the eu and turkey.
in writing. - this report seeks to consolidate an economic and commercial relationship with turkey which is in fact aimed at subjugating it to eu interests. the references are many and explicit: to remove the remaining tariff and non-tariff barriers between the eu and turkey, to maintain open trade and investment regimes, to strengthen turkey's capacity to resist internal protectionist temptations, to extend the customs union to agricultural products, services and public procurement. the development of these economic and trade relations only benefits the large monopolies in the eu and turkey, to the clear detriment of workers whose rights are being stripped away to increase competitiveness, of small and mediumsized enterprises and of small and mediumsized farmers, who face rising production costs and falling production prices and incomes. the pressure on turkey to respect the agreements reached, which imply the normalisation of relations with all eu countries, including cyprus, is positive. it is necessary that economic and trade relations should not override the interests of the peoples and that any progress in relations with turkey should be subject to the end of the turkish occupation of the northern part of cyprus.

in writing. - it is well known that turkey is one of the eu's main trading partners. this relationship is old, dating back to 1963, and was deepened with the establishment of a customs union in 1993, as provided for in the initial agreement. nevertheless, there are still many bureaucratic obstacles which have prevented trade and economic relations from being even more profitable for both sides. turkey must therefore make an additional effort to combat such obstacles to the common good.

in writing. - declaration of vote the failures to combat biodiversity that have been observed require an urgent european response. i believe that this resolution is a contribution to that end. i therefore welcome the clear position that halting biodiversity loss is the absolute minimum level of ambition to be achieved by 2020. this requires a number of measures, some of which are set out in the resolution, and of which i would stress increased crossborder cooperation and the enhancement of biodiversity, particularly from an environmental and economic point of view. in this context, i would stress, on the one hand, the importance of biodiversity and ecosystem resilience for climate change mitigation and adaptation. i also think it is important that this resolution recognises that sustainable economic development and nature conservation should not be inseparable and that the development of green infrastructure also has the potential to create jobs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of eu legislation on the protection of biodiversity, because ambitious measures are needed to halt biodiversity loss and restore ecosystems, including through a cross-cutting approach to the various sectoral eu policies, which recognises biodiversity as a key element in climate change mitigation and adaptation.
in writing. - to quote the rapporteur, the loss of biodiversity threatens our food supply, our leisure and tourism opportunities, our ability to cope with climate change and our sources of wood, medicine and energy. i therefore agree with the need for the eu as a whole, and with particular attention to all areas covered by community policies, to find a sustainable strategy for the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of ecosystems. i believe that this is particularly relevant in the area of agriculture and fisheries, which is why i am following the reforms being prepared in the cfp and the cap with particular attention, since the proper and sustainable preservation of biodiversity, while essential and desirable, cannot be a brake on the sustainability and development of agricultural and fisheries activities.
in writing. the european union is committed to the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment. unfortunately, the eu will not meet its biodiversity target for 2010. the loss of biodiversity is continuing at an alarming rate. the rate of loss is estimated to accelerate to a value ten times higher by 2050. in the eu, 42% of mammals, 43% of birds, 45% of butterflies, 30% of amphibians, 45% of reptiles and 52% of freshwater fish are threatened with extinction. in its 2008 mid-term review of the implementation of the community biodiversity action plan, the commission noted that 50% of species and up to 80% of habitats of european conservation interest are in a poor conservation status. this loss of biodiversity is unacceptable, not only from an ethical point of view but also from an ecological and economic perspective, since we are depriving future generations of enjoying the benefits of a healthy biodiversity. european policies for the protection of biodiversity need to be coordinated and integrated with other sectoral policies, such as agriculture, forestry, fisheries and natural disaster prevention policies, to ensure maximum protection of biodiversity.
in writing. − this report is clear in calling attention to important issues such as: incomplete implementation of legislation, incomplete and weak integration into sectoral policies, insufficient scientific knowledge and knowledge gaps, lack of political will, insufficient funding, lack of effective instruments geared to tackling specific problems such as invasive alien species. in general, we follow the concerns and demands expressed in the report. we welcome the inclusion of the proposals we made in the debate in the environment committee on several of its chapters, in particular those on funding and the inclusion of biodiversity in the relevant sectoral policies. but we cannot but point out and strongly reject the inclusion in the report, albeit incidental and merely as a suggestion for reflection, of the reference to possible innovative systems for payment for ecosystem services. this is an unacceptable commodification of nature. the loss of biodiversity is one of the consequences of a system - capitalism - based on the exploitation of nature and its resources (beyond their natural regenerative capacity) and their commodification. it will not be possible to find a just and effective solution to this or other environmental problems within the framework of this system.
in writing. - the rapid rate of man-made biodiversity loss is worrying. biodiversity should be seen as the most reliable barometer of the state of the environment. so, faced with alarming figures of biodiversity loss in the eu, with 42% of mammals, 43% of birds, 45% of butterflies, 30% of amphibians, 45% of reptiles and 52% of freshwater fish threatened with extinction, i consider the legislation now in place to protect biodiversity, and even to strengthen it, to be fundamental and essential. hence my vote.
in writing. − i warmly welcome this report on the application of eu legislation on the protection of biodiversity, which derives from and underlines the importance we all recognise of it in the environmental, economic and social spheres and in sectors as diverse as agriculture, fisheries and tourism. i would like to stress here today another aspect which, although not being omitted in the course of the debate, has not been sufficiently emphasized. i am talking about the intrinsic value of biodiversity and the moral duty we have to protect and defend it. it is man who, having the greatest power over biodiversity, has the greatest responsibility to preserve it, to pass on to future generations this heritage he has received, to enjoy and care for. the european union is thus doing its part by legislating for the conservation of biodiversity, and this certainly deserves my support.
