in writing. at a time when the developments in the crisis of capitalism in the european union are leading to a worsening of the living conditions of millions of europeans and a worrying deterioration of the economic and social situation in several member states, the council decides to put these issues aside and insist on the old political guidelines which have led us to the present situation. this is why we insist on liberalizing and deregulating world trade, whether in the context of the wto - with the call for the conclusion of the doha round - or in the context of new bilateral agreements. this creates the conditions for putting even more pressure on the most vulnerable production systems and on the labour force, in the direction of their devaluation. the result: more unemployment and more precariousness. the council considers that the time has come to take full advantage of the lisbon treaty and to 'promote europe's interests and values in the world'. the path is clear: closer alignment with nato and the usa, increased external interventionism and a disturbing escalation of militarism in international relations. as regards the so-called 'financial supervision package' mentioned in the conclusions, the message is clear: the main mechanisms of financial speculation remain untouched. as it is, speculation will continue to run rampant.
only about two years after the start of the serious financial crisis did the council and the european parliament agree on a package of measures which they call financial supervision, but which in fact amount to the minimum of intervention in this sector, and without the fundamental basic decisions in this area having been taken beforehand, namely the end of tax havens, the taxation of capital movements, the end of the derivatives market. the commission is also proposing to democratize the ecb and radically change its objectives to give priority to employment with rights and, at the very least, to seek a balance between social progress and public finances. this means that the main mechanisms of financial speculation remain on the market and that the measures now taken are more aimed at facilitating the control by the great powers and their financial groups over the member states with weaker economies than at facing the problem of financial speculation head on and putting a stop to it. on the other hand, we must not forget that this package is part of the measures taken by ecofin on the prior control of national budgets included in the so-called european semester, which deserves our most vehement protest.
the fragility of financial regulatory and supervisory institutions worldwide has been, in some ways, at the root of the difficulties we have been witnessing in the european union and the eurozone. the need to stimulate economic and family aid schemes was a determining factor in the marked increase in public deficits. the package we are discussing today is the creation of a new architecture for financial supervision in europe based on the creation of institutions and mechanisms that will have the task of macro-prudential supervision, that is, of the overall risks of the european financial system, and micro-prudential supervision, in the banking, insurance and securities markets in coordination with the network of national supervisors. there are also other areas where the esas are expected to contribute to financial stability, including by centralising the supervision of credit rating agencies registered in the european union under a single institution, promoting mandatory technical standards and mediating conflicts between national supervisors. the new supervisory architecture could also contribute to the smooth running of new community mechanisms for economic, budgetary and social planning, coordination and supervision within the union.
in writing. − having regard to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which provides that the union must have the resources necessary to attain its objectives and implement its policies, and that the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has introduced new areas of action, the example of which is the eeas. i believe that a mere reallocation of resources or redefinition of priorities within the framework of the multiannual financial framework (mff) will not be sufficient to meet the new needs of the union, and that a fundamental revision of the mff and of the flexibility mechanisms included in the interinstitutional agreement (iaa) is therefore necessary. the union needs greater flexibility to allow it to build up reserves and room for manoeuvre in order to be able to react quickly and effectively to unforeseen or urgent situations. i therefore vote in favour of this report and its recommendations.
in writing. - the proper planning of the european union's activities and their continuity are not compatible with simple annual budgeting, but rather justify the existence of a multiannual financial framework capable of providing its institutions with the appropriate means to fulfil their powers and duties. the interim evaluation of the implementation of the multiannual financial framework justifies the preparation of the report which underlies the resolution we voted for. it contains some of the widely felt concerns about the inadequacies of the multiannual financial framework and the union's current financial capacity to achieve its objectives, which i also share. the criticism of the european union is often based on the lack of transparency in its accounts. the clarity of community budgets and multiannual planning, their sustainability and the respect for them by all those involved in the budgetary process, including, of course, the european parliament, must be instruments to eradicate this suspicion and to motivate citizens and political actors to take a more active part in this area of action.
in writing. − between 2007 and 2009, the ceilings of the current mff were reached or exceeded. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the programme, which is to be submitted to the council by the end of the year. the remaining margins under the current financial framework are insignificant for the remainder of the period. the available margin under heading 1a (competitiveness for growth and jobs) shall be less than eur 50 million per year and the overall available margin under all headings shall be limited to eur 436 million in 2012 and eur 435 million in 2013. however, this margin will be further reduced by the existence of commitments which are not yet budgetary. the lisbon treaty brought new powers and bodies and the already adopted eu 2020 strategy, which advocates smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, must now start to be implemented with the necessary financial resources. this is a case for urgently reviewing the current mff and for flexible management of it.
in writing. - this report calls for the rapid adoption of the instruments necessary for the implementation of the budgetary provisions of the lisbon treaty. this means putting the community budget even more at the service of neoliberalism, federalism and militarism - the fundamental pillars of the process of european integration under way, which this treaty enshrines and deepens. we know our position on this, and we could not vote otherwise than against it. we have always criticised the inadequacy of the current multiannual financial framework, which has reduced the structural funds to 0.37% of eu gni, which has meant cuts in programmes of a social and environmental nature, as well as in the fields of research, education and culture. we therefore advocate strengthening it and refocusing its objectives. we are in favour of a community budget which is in the service of genuine economic and social cohesion. in the service of full employment with rights, investment and public services, environmental protection, cooperation and peace. we therefore reject the view of the community budget as an instrument for the commodification of increasing aspects of social life, liberalization, precarious employment, structural unemployment, external interventionism and war.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty has given the eu new prerogatives in a number of areas, such as external action, sport, space, climate change, and others. the eu needs to be provided with sufficient resources to achieve its objectives and to implement its policies. it is in this context that a multiannual financial framework is being established, which i agree with, in order to provide the eu with adequate financial planning for the achievement of the ambitious policy objectives set.
in writing. - in view of the current instability of the markets and the particular vulnerability of some member states in relation to financial markets, i believe that the creation of the european financial stabilisation mechanism is justified. i hope that its use will be as low as possible, which would mean that the member states would be able to respond to the crisis, but i would stress the important role that this mechanism can play in the event of serious financial difficulties. the creation of a budget line providing for the possibility of the european financial stability mechanism guarantees being provided as early as this budgetary year has the solidarity merit of providing the union with the capacity to respond more quickly to any problem that arises in the meantime, as well as giving a signal of confidence to the financial markets regarding the collective commitment of the eu to the security and stabilisation of markets and to helping resolve financial disruption situations. despite these advantages, i believe that a serious and highly rigorous assessment of their impact on the union's accounts, which should be of a large magnitude, is necessary and, if necessary, that speed should be sacrificed for the sake of soundness.
in writing. - this amending budget is the result of an initiative by the committee on budgets and its chairman to use an amending budget to introduce an amendment to create a 'pro memoria' item to finance the guarantees provided for in the european financial stabilisation mechanism (efsm). the commission has also decided to extend the scope of the financial contribution to the european investment bank (eib) for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2015. the european budget will only be called upon to intervene if the member state receiving the loan is unable to repay it. this amending budget for the financial year 2010 therefore includes the creation of a new budget line 01 04 01 03 for the european union guarantee and, consequently, a new article 802 in the revenue table. a pro memoria mention is proposed for commitment appropriations and payment appropriations as well as for revenue.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis that has hit the world, and which the eu has not escaped, has brought with it a number of challenges, including the need for the eu to respond to speculative attacks on the weakest economies that could undermine the single currency. the european financial stabilisation mechanism (efsm) was therefore needed to ensure support to member states that feel threatened by such attacks. the budgetary framework for this mechanism requires the adoption of an amending budget, which is justified in the event of exceptional, unavoidable or unforeseen circumstances.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the recommendations made in this report. the simplification of the vat refund procedure, as provided for in the vat refund directive, is contributing to the further integration of the internal market. as it has been found that delays in complying with the deadlines are sometimes the responsibility of the member states, which have postponed the opening of their web portals or for other technical reasons, i am in favour of not calling into question the right of taxable persons to deduct vat. the preservation of the taxpayer's right to deduct vat is of particular importance and relevance in the current economic climate in which the union finds itself. delays in the refund of vat to companies operating in the internal market may lead to greater difficulties for those companies, in particular in their financial needs, which will consequently have an impact on the recovery of the union economy and the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. - i consider the proposed amendments to the current directive on vat refunds and the possibility of adopting certain implementing measures which will improve the functioning of web portals to be very important. for the greater effectiveness and simplification of the current tax rules, cost reduction and integrity of the internal market, it is essential that measures on electronic vat refunds are implemented swiftly by a number of member states. i could not agree more with the rapporteur when she says that any delay in vat refunds can have very serious financial consequences for businesses in the internal market, especially in the current context where any financial increase can be catastrophic.
in writing. - i voted in favour, as i believe that this report makes a very positive contribution to improving the efficiency and transparency of tax procedures within the european union. i would stress the defence of the rights of taxpayers, particularly as regards the deduction and refund of vat. the implementation of measures to facilitate and reduce the bureaucratic burden on european companies operating in the different member states of the union, as well as the standardisation of procedures, is crucial to consolidating the internal market and contributing to the relaunch of the european economy. it regrets the delay in the implementation of the measures on electronic vat refunds by some member states. it is clear that in the current economic situation the delay in the refund of vat has serious financial consequences for companies operating in the internal market.
in writing. − directive 2008/09/ec (the 'vat refund' directive) was intended to simplify the vat refund procedure and reduce the administrative burden by introducing an electronic procedure which would allow the taxpayer to submit a single refund application. however, the delay in the implementation of this directive in most member states has led to complaints from several companies, and some amendments to it are now necessary to safeguard the interests of taxpayers, as we all know that the delay in vat refunds can have serious financial consequences for companies operating in the internal market, thus contributing to a slower economic recovery in the eu. hence my vote.
in writing. − over the past few years, the eu pharmacovigilance system has evolved towards better coordination of member states' work. however, the current legislation still contains some gaps and the commission has presented amendments to strengthen pharmacovigilance in the eu and to streamline procedures. the report, while endorsing the amendments proposed by the commission, reinforces them in a number of areas, such as: strengthening the role of the pharmacovigilance advisory committee (praac), which should have the power to recommend action to the committee for medicinal products for human use; strengthening the role of healthcare professionals in voluntarily reporting adverse reactions to medicinal products; strengthening the role of patients in direct reporting of adverse reactions; all adverse reactions to medicines, not just serious ones, should be reported in the eudravigilance database by the competent authorities and companies, i.e. for the first time, all adverse reactions will be centralised in one place in the eu; need for a clearer information leaflet on the main characteristics of medicines. i therefore voted in favour of this report. there can be no doubt that pharmacovigilance is a priority of community public health policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards pharmacovigilance of medicinal products for human use, regulation (ec) no 726/2004 laying down community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use and establishing a european medicines agency, because the agreement reached with the council will allow an effective and transparent european pharmacovigilance system to be established, in particular through the creation of a european medicines safety web portal and means for patients to report adverse reactions to the competent national authorities.
in writing. − pharmacovigilance is the system used to monitor the safety of medicines after they have been authorised for public use. every year 197 000 people die in the eu from adverse reactions to medicines. it is therefore a priority to achieve a good pharmacovigilance system based on adverse reaction reporting by healthcare professionals, companies and patients themselves. the rules governing the centralised procedure are set out in this regulation (for new medicinal products or for medicinal products against cancer, hiv or degenerative diseases), whereas the centralised system is provided for in directive 2001/83/ec. i therefore advocate increased cooperation on pharmacovigilance, which would allow a more comprehensive 'set' of adverse reactions to medicinal products to be obtained, avoiding duplication of monitoring of the same adverse reactions in other member states. i welcome the proposed measures to encourage health professionals to voluntarily report adverse reactions to medicines to their competent authorities. i would particularly like to highlight the creation of an internet portal per member state (article 106 of the directive) where all relevant information on medicinal products will be available to all citizens who wish to consult it. these national portals will be linked to the european portal which will be managed by the european medicines agency (article 26 of the regulation) and available in all official languages of the union.
in writing. the pharmaceutical industry is one of the most important sectors of today's societies in economic, social and scientific terms. the eu is no exception and finds this sector a source of economic growth as well as sustainable employment and contributes to the general well-being of european citizens. however, despite existing legislation, the number of deaths caused by adverse drug reactions in the eu is estimated at around 197 000 per year. on the basis of these assumptions, it is very important that there is consistent, well-founded and targeted legislation in this sector. the main objective of this proposal is to improve the procedures for the authorization and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use in order to avoid the side effects of medicinal products affecting both citizens and animals, as has happened in the past. i agree with the new measures adopted, which are ultimately an added value that translates into practical solutions for the consumer.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as it focuses on a topic pharmacovigilance which is becoming increasingly important in scientifically and technologically developed societies, particularly in relation to biomedical research, and reinforces the previous provision in regulation (ec) no 726/2004 laying down community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use, updating it to the extent of the needs recognised today. in this context, i would particularly stress the importance of cooperation between the member states, which, by enabling a very considerable increase in the information on adverse reactions to medicinal products, allows for a more rapid and accurate detection of any problems, i.e. allows for more effective pharmacovigilance. the new system also proposes that all adverse reactions to medicines be notified to the european medicines agency, in a broadening of criteria and centralisation of institutions that will contribute to biomedical research, with valuable social benefits.
in writing. − over the past few years, the eu pharmacovigilance system has evolved towards better coordination of member states' work. however, the current legislation still contains some gaps and the commission has presented amendments to strengthen pharmacovigilance in the eu and to streamline procedures. the report, while endorsing the amendments proposed by the commission, reinforces them in a number of areas, such as: strengthening the role of the pharmacovigilance advisory committee (praac), which should have the power to recommend action to the committee for medicinal products for human use; strengthening the role of healthcare professionals in voluntarily reporting adverse reactions to medicinal products; strengthening the role of patients in direct reporting of adverse reactions; all adverse reactions to medicines, not just serious ones, should be reported in the eudravigilance database by the competent authorities and companies, i.e. for the first time, all adverse reactions will be centralised in one place in the eu; need for a clearer information leaflet on the main characteristics of medicines. i therefore voted in favour of this report. there can be no doubt that pharmacovigilance is a priority of community public health policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending, as regards pharmacovigilance, directive 2001/83/ec establishing a community code relating to medicinal products for human use, because the agreement reached with the council will make it possible to define an effective and transparent european pharmacovigilance system, in particular through the creation of a european web portal on the safety of medicinal products and means for patients to notify adverse reactions to the competent national authorities.
in writing. - consumer safety is a matter of vital importance to me, especially when these consumers are also patients who look to the medicines used for a cure or at least a significant improvement in their health. that is why i consider the commitment made to the new pharmacovigilance rules to be important, giving the emea (european medicines agency) centralised powers in this area, in particular through the creation of a pharmacovigilance database. greater, better and more integrated access to information can be vital to reduce the severity and frequency of some adverse reactions and to facilitate and speed up the processes for the suspension or withdrawal of medicinal products with serious adverse reactions. i also think it is important to create an easily accessible online page where all european citizens can find the information leaflet for any medicine in their own language. the right of patients to safety and information is, in my view, a fundamental right, and i shall therefore remain attentive to the other proposals in the pharmaceutical package which have not yet been examined in this house.

in writing. − pharmacovigilance, which is the assessment, detection and prevention of adverse reactions to medicines, is of great importance, especially when we consider that it is the fifth leading cause of death in hospitals, with an estimated 197 000 deaths per year in the eu. the maximum transparency and the provision of means to the competent authorities should be ensured throughout the process. the functioning of these bodies should be guided solely by the protection of public interest and public health and should therefore be public bodies, independent of any commercial interests. it is important that there is a system, involving healthcare professionals and patients, through which adverse drug reactions can be reported in a safe and reliable manner. we share the rapporteur's view that the member states must continue to play a leading role in the community pharmacovigilance system. therefore, the competent authority of each member state should continue to act as the screening centre for all spontaneous reports of adverse reactions to medicinal products. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing on the market and use of biocidal products, because it strengthens the rules on the authorisation, marketing and use of biocidal products in the eu with a view to protecting human and animal health and the environment, in accordance with the precautionary principle.
in writing. − the high levels of hygiene to which our civilization has become accustomed require an increasingly constant and intensive use of biocidal products. at the same time, these products are required to be increasingly effective and aggressive, which means that their handling becomes more dangerous. therefore, the approach to regulating the placing on the market and use of biocidal products must pay particular attention to the protection of consumers/users. once again, as i have said on other occasions, the rules on this matter must be uniform and valid throughout the eu, otherwise we will not be effectively ensuring the protection of all european consumers and, not least, environmental protection.
in writing. − this regulation aims to harmonise existing legal rules at european level and to adapt them to the latest technical developments. consumers should be able to assume that the products they buy comply with uniform minimum standards in the eu internal market, regardless of the member state in which the product is purchased. clear labelling of treated materials and products is therefore essential as is the corresponding authorisation of biocidal products, whether they originate inside or outside the eu. the european market for biocidal products is estimated at around eur 890 million per year, about 27% of the world market. three large companies account for approximately 25% of the european market. a balance must therefore be struck between the interests of large enterprises and those of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). there is a need to provide more assistance to smes in an industry dominated by several large industrial producers, which is why it is appropriate to exempt smes from paying an annual fee for placing biocidal products on the market. in addition, member states should set up national helpdesks to complement the guidance documents made available by the european chemicals agency (echa).
in writing. − our abstention at first reading expresses our concern about some critical issues that the majority of this parliament has ignored in view of the real need for member states to protect their citizens against the harmful effects on health and the environment of biocidal active substances used on the market. the european chemicals agency, which will be responsible for scientifically assessing whether a biocidal product can be authorised for use on the market, now has three months to draw up its opinion on the conclusions of the assessment and submit it to the commission, compared with the previously planned nine months. we believe that this reduction will not be met with the necessary rigour to protect public health and the environment. we hope that this question will be reconsidered in future negotiations with the commission and the council. we welcome the recognition that member states may take account of regional differences and local environmental problems in their national commitments, as well as the reference to respect for the principle of subsidiarity. we also assess the proposed procedures for nanomaterials and the additional levels of protection that should be considered for more vulnerable groups such as children and pregnant women.
in writing. - every year, some 90 000 tonnes of biocidal products are placed on the market to control pests and germs. the eu's concerns are therefore natural, since it is argued that biocides should be safer and more environmentally friendly. this is intended to strengthen the protection of human health by prohibiting the most toxic chemicals, such as carcinogens or substances harmful to fertility, and to protect animals and the environment. i believe, however, that in addition to this approval, a comprehensive certification of products imported into the eu should also be required. hence my vote
in writing. - i voted in favour of the following report because i believe that europe really needs a financial supervisory body, such as a complex and effective structure, which is able to dominate the eu's financial institutions and ensure their proper functioning. it is in this context that i very much welcome the creation of a european banking authority, a european insurance and occupational pensions authority and a european securities and markets authority, as i believe that only in this way can we improve the level of regulation in the european internal market, ensuring the integrity and proper functioning of the markets, while preserving the stability of the financial system and ensuring the coordination of european and international supervision. only through more effective supervision can we identify risks to financial systems, alerting us in time to crises like the one that hit the world in 2008. this powerful crisis has brought to the fore the need to reform this sector in order to maximise competition by encouraging the existence of genuinely competent supervisory bodies that are truly able to make the much needed difference in this important sector.
in writing. - in line with previous reports on the creation of european authorities in the field of financial regulation, i also vote in favour of the proposal for the creation of a european insurance and occupational pensions authority. i would like to stress once again the importance of providing the european union, and in particular the internal market, with european supervisory authorities in order to mitigate the economic and financial impacts of future stresses on financial markets.
in writing. - if there is one lesson that we all, regardless of our political convictions or worldviews, have learnt from the recent crisis, it is that we need to reform the institutional structure of supervision by creating european bodies and, with this, to reformulate the whole concept of macro- and microeconomic supervision. the agreement we have reached and which is voted on today has many virtues. one of these will be the creation of autonomous european bodies for the supervision of banking, insurance and financial markets. these bodies will not replace national supervisory authorities but will work with them in exercising their prudential and systemic risk mandate in order to prevent a new crisis of the scale of the one we have faced from crashing down on european banking and financial markets. personally, as i have had the opportunity to say many times, i am not afraid of the existence of european supervisory authorities. i think it is essential that they can exercise their mandate independently and competently, thus strengthening the confidence of the markets and their agents, in this case in particular in the insurance and pension sectors.
in writing. − in order to ensure transparency and credibility of european markets and institutions with citizens, the strengthening of the powers, resources and autonomy of european supervision in insurance and pension markets is essential to ensure the effectiveness of the current reform that the institutions of the european union are committed to implement in the supervision of financial markets, in order to avoid new risks of a crisis such as the one currently affecting the global economy, with particular impact on european social reality. the commission has put forward a set of proposals aimed at establishing a more efficient, integrated and sustainable system of financial supervision in the eu. this approach is based on a european system of financial supervision (esfs). the commission proposes to set up three new european decentralised agencies: the european banking authority (eba), the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa) and the european securities and markets authority (esma). it should be noted that the impact of the creation of these three agencies on the european budget amounts to some eur 59.699 million for the years 2011 to 2013.
in writing. - this report is included in the so-called financial supervision package. in its vote we took account of the way in which the council, the commission and the european parliament itself have delayed action in this area and have limited themselves to decisions which do not alter the fundamental question of financial speculation, including the question of sovereign debt insurance which functions as a highly speculative derivative product. without a charge, the creation of european authorities in these areas will be of little use. so our vote against is mainly a protest against the fact that no proposals have been put forward so far on the end of tax havens, the taxation of capital movements and the end of the derivatives market. this means that the main mechanisms of financial speculation remain on the market and that the measures now taken are more aimed at facilitating the control of the great powers and their financial groups over the member states with weaker economies than at facing the problem of financial speculation head on and putting a stop to it.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has brought to light the major weaknesses in financial supervision, both in individual cases and in relation to the financial system as a whole. the supervisory models were national in scope and did not keep pace with the globalisation of the financial system, where several groups operate across borders, with the resulting systemic risks. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims to improve the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. the creation of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority is therefore essential if we are to have an effective supervisory model, along with many other control mechanisms, to be decided on and implemented with real urgency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree with the european commission proposal, with the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the following report because i consider that the current eu system has several shortcomings in relation to macro-financial surveillance and because i consider that this is a very important issue to be forgotten and i commend the initiatives taken to address this issue. the recent financial crisis that has hit the world, if anything, has undoubtedly served to draw our attention to the fragility of new economic systems, the constant economic risk we are living in and the dire need to create a body in charge of macroeconomic surveillance within the eu. that is why i am pleased that members from all political groups voted in favour of this report, and it was approved by an overwhelming majority, which illustrates quite well the general concern about fiscal sovereignty. in my view, it is of the utmost importance that this new system of financial supervision should function without repressing the financing of the economy, safeguarding the single market, allowing the eu to maintain its status and providing timely warning of risk situations. it is for all these reasons that i welcome the creation of the european systemic risk board.
in writing. - i am in favour of the generality of the proposals in this report and of the creation of a european systemic risk board (esrb). the european parliament, aware of its responsibilities and in the use of the new powers conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon, should be called upon to play a decisive role in improving the eu supervisory framework. the inability to address the weaknesses of the existing supervisory structure, highlighted by the current financial crisis, has made it all the more urgent to create macro-prudential supervisory mechanisms capable of ensuring the stability of european financial markets. the unity of the single market must also be safeguarded and the eu must be given the tools to defend the euro and other international currencies on a global scale. i would also like to underline the important contribution that the esrb is making by calling for european-level macroeconomic analysis to assess potential systemic risks. given the fragility of micro-prudential supervision at member state level, i believe that close collaboration between the esrb, central bankers, supervisors and the 'real economy' will not only legitimize the action of the esrb itself but will also be a relevant input for the effectiveness of its action.
in writing. - if there is one lesson we have all learned from the recent crisis, it is that the institutional structure of supervision needs to be reformed by creating european bodies, and thus the whole concept of macro- and microeconomic supervision needs to be reformed. personally, as i have had the opportunity to say many times, i am not frightened by the existence of european supervisory authorities, quite the contrary. i think it is essential that they exist and that they can carry out their mandates independently and competently, thus strengthening the confidence of the markets and their agents. in this particular case, the creation of a european systemic risk board aims to provide the european union with an effective supervisory system without impeding economic growth; to protect the single market from the risk of fragmentation; and finally, through the development of a european macroprudential perspective, to help solve the problem of fragmentation of individual risk analysis at national level by strengthening the effectiveness of early warning mechanisms and enabling risk assessments to be translated into concrete action. it is therefore welcome to the creation of this european systemic risk committee, and hopes that excellence in the fulfilment of its mandate will be the starting point for better supervision in the union.
in writing. − the creation of structures capable of preventive intervention, supported by a permanent and duly substantiated assessment, should be a priority in the decision-making process and policy action of the european union in the current framework of the response to the current crisis, where it is imperative to ensure the efficiency of a community macroprudential supervision of the financial system. the european systemic risk board, by being able to monitor and assess the risks of the financial system during periods of normal operation, could be the guarantor of financial stability, which is absolutely necessary for the real economy to develop and provide growth, wealth and jobs. i would stress the rapporteur's concern to ensure a balanced and realistic proposal, through effective supervision that safeguards the financing of the economy, the single market and the interests and objectives of the european union.
in writing. - in voting on this and other reports included in the so-called financial supervision package, we took account of the way in which the council, the commission and the european parliament itself have delayed action in this area and limited themselves to decisions which do not alter the fundamental issue of financial speculation, including with sovereign debt. so our vote against is above all a protest against the fact that we have not heard any proposals on the end of tax havens, the taxation of capital movements and the end of the derivatives market. this means that the main mechanisms of financial speculation remain on the market and that the measures now taken are more aimed at facilitating the control by the great powers and their financial groups over the member states with weaker economies than at facing the problem of financial speculation head on and putting a stop to it. the implementation of these measures may have some positive impact at an early stage, but their scope is too limited and if the basic measures are not adopted, time will show that speculation will continue.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has highlighted major weaknesses in financial supervision, both in terms of micro- and macroprudential supervision. supervisory models have not kept pace with the globalisation that has occurred in the financial system, where several financial groups develop their cross-border operations with systemic risk. there was therefore no cooperation, coordination or consistency in the application of union legislation. this directive thus aims to improve the functioning of the internal market by ensuring a high level of prudential supervision and regulation, the protection of depositors, investors and all beneficiaries, and in fact only fails. it is therefore essential to safeguard the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets, to maintain the stability and sustainability of public finances and to strengthen international coordination and cooperation in the field of supervision. i believe that the creation of the european systemic risk board is essential to achieve an effective supervisory model and to avoid systemic risks caused by the cross-border nature of large financial groups. but many other steps will have to be taken to ensure that the truly immoral situations which have occurred in the recent past, with damage to economies, shareholders, depositors, taxpayers and the credibility of the system, do not happen again.
in writing. - i shall abstain from voting. on the one hand, the commitment reached on macro and micro-prudential supervision is a step forward from the current lack of any assessment and regulation of financial risk at union level. but on the other hand, the solutions that have been established are not up to the problems they are intended to tackle. the proposal does not take due account of the interdependence of the myriad of actors and products that make up the financial system, as well as their relationships with the real economy. none of this can be reduced to a solution of the sum of the parts on which the supervisory architecture is based. the ecb's role in the world economy is not limited to the financial sector, but it is also a major player in the world economy. finally, the european systemic risk board ends up being the weak link in a system which concentrates effective powers in the interests of the states, extending in the financial area the intergovernmental logic which marks the present european construction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree with the european commission proposal, with the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. in view of the integration of international financial markets, it is essential that the union should make a strong commitment at world level. the esrb should draw on the technical expertise of a high-level scientific committee and assume all the responsibilities that are required at the global level in order to ensure that the union's voice is heard on financial stability, in particular by cooperating closely with the international monetary fund, the financial stability board and all g20 partners.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the financial crisis has highlighted the failings of financial markets at global level, and european markets were no exception, not avoiding contagion in an increasingly integrated world economy. in parallel with the proposals to create an integrated level of supervision at macro and micro level, this report proposes a package of revisions to the sectoral directives, mainly in the area of banking and securities, in order to adapt them to a new architecture of banking supervision. with the g20 also committing to take action to build a stronger and globally more consistent supervisory and regulatory framework for the future of the financial sector, the eu's response needs to be ambitious, addressing specific cases such as macro and micro supervision, and global regulation, focusing on harmonisation and cooperation on systemic risks at the global level. this is a unique opportunity to introduce our policy objectives from an integrated view.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the financial supervision package for the reasons set out below. the establishment of the three authorities should be accompanied by the development of a single code of rules in order to ensure consistent harmonisation and uniform application and thus contribute to a more efficient functioning of the internal market. the authorities should ensure a high, effective and consistent level of regulation and supervision, taking into account the interests of all member states and the diverse nature of financial institutions. the subject matter of technical standards must be of a genuinely technical nature and their drafting requires the expertise of supervisory experts. technical standards adopted as delegated acts should further develop, specify and determine the conditions for the consistent harmonisation of standards included in the basic acts adopted by the european parliament and the council, by supplementing or amending non-essential elements of the legislative act. this directive should identify situations where it may be necessary to resolve a procedural or substantive issue concerning compliance with union law that supervisors cannot resolve on their own. in such a situation, one of the supervisory authorities involved should be able to refer the matter to the competent european supervisory authority.
in writing. − the increasing interconnection between national markets and the multinational or at least transnational nature of many of the main players in financial markets, and especially the economic and financial crisis now felt around the world, have made it clear that the way in which supervision operates at european level needs to be rethought, re-formulated and even re-engineered. in this context of systemic adjustment to the present reality, the three european authorities to which this resolution refers are of particular importance, having been given particular responsibilities in the new structure which is intended to be better able to meet the challenges which are now being posed and which have repercussions for all european citizens. i hope that this new architecture which is now being designed will be successful in practice, that our joint efforts to reduce risks and safeguard transparency and truth in the markets will not be satisfied with the solutions which have now been found, and that we will always be available to contribute, in the light of experience and taking into account best practice, to improving what needs to be improved.
in writing. - i vote overall in favour of the measures presented in this report with a view to defining the competences of the european supervisory authorities. although it has highlighted the fragility of financial markets, the current situation in the european and global economy is a good opportunity for the eu to develop a stronger supervisory and regulatory framework consistent with the needs of a globalised economy. the union's responses to the crisis need to be bolder, both at the macro-prudential and micro-prudential level of supervision and regulation. recognising the complexity of designing the new supervisory and regulatory architecture of the union, i believe that it should be based on the precautionary principle. it is also important that the esas have effective capacity to go beyond the monitoring of systemic risks of national financial institutions and are also empowered to assess cross-border and systemic risks at european level as well as international systemic risks.
in writing. − as is now clear, due to the consequences of the current economic and financial crisis, the continued success of the european integration process is absolutely dependent on the ability to find solutions for strengthening the competences of integrated supervisory intervention structures at european level. national sovereignty is increasingly dependent on supranational intervention through community structures with resources and powers to act and devise strategies outside the influence of national and isolated wishes and needs. i therefore reaffirm my support for the consolidation of the competences of the european structures responsible for acting and supervising the activities of the various european financial sectors, such as the european banking authority, the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority.

in writing. − the financial crisis has revealed inadequate financial regulation and weak market surveillance mechanisms. we all know that mere cooperation between national supervisory authorities was not enough for a single internal market, a genuine area without frontiers. that is why i believe that with a new european supervisory authority, it will be easier to prevent future crises, because we need more agile institutions for faster responses. i believe that the european systemic risk board will have a leading role in monitoring and assessing potential threats to our financial stability. we need a set of rules that will give us a level playing field and more adequate protection for our depositors and consumers, taxpayers and small and mediumsized enterprises, as it is essential to safeguard the position of those who have suffered most from this crisis and to ensure credit facilities in future crises. we must also pay particular attention to the large financial institutions, usually called too big to fail, which can, as has been seen, cause the collapse of an entire world financial system.
in writing. - i am in general in favour of the measures proposed in this report for the creation of a european banking authority. the financial crisis has exposed the many weaknesses in financial supervision and in particular in the union banking system. in view of this, the european citizens have noted that urgent measures have been taken by the european parliament and the commission. at a later stage, where we are now, we must develop preventive mechanisms which will enable us to better adjust the european economy to possible future shocks. in this sense, the creation of this european banking authority is a key contribution to financial supervision, as it will be responsible for defining the modus operandi and governance model in crisis management, from the need for early intervention to the possible resolution of insolvency proceedings, if necessary.

in writing. - if there is one lesson we have all learned from the recent crisis, it is that the institutional structure of supervision needs to be reformed by creating european bodies, and thus the whole concept of macro- and microeconomic supervision needs to be reformed. that is how the european banking authority comes into being. as confidence in banking has been severely shaken by the global financial crisis, it is urgent that markets and europeans in general regain confidence in the soundness and robustness of their banking institutions and, in particular, regain confidence in supervisors. that is why the role of this new european banking authority is so crucial for the future. and on this matter we can have no doubt: when there are financial institutions whose failure could cause the collapse of the entire financial system, we can't keep whistling to the side. as my colleague, mr garcía-margallo, who has played a key role in all this supervision, rightly says, there are only two options in this matter: more powers for the national supervisory authorities or more europe. more protectionism or more internal market. and in this matter i have no doubt which way we should go, and that is more europe and more internal market, with careful and competent supervision.
in writing. − a european banking supervisory authority will consolidate the effectiveness of the deep reform of the current system of financial market supervision in which the institutions of the european union are engaged today, in order to ensure a structural basis for intervention with sufficient powers to avoid a repetition of the last global financial crisis, which would be unbearable for society and the world economy. it is absolutely inappropriate to accept a system of supervision based on the action of national authorities whose jurisdiction ends at their borders, when the market players are financial institutions whose intervention is located in the european area without borders. i therefore emphasize the rapporteur's attention to the importance of small and mediumsized enterprises and the european perspective of the proposal.
in writing. - it is another report included in the so-called financial supervision package and based on the proposal for a regulation establishing a european banking authority which is an integral part of a european system of financial supervision. one of its articles states that the objective of the authority is to protect the public interest by contributing to the short, medium and long-term stability and effectiveness of the financial system for the union's economy, its citizens and its businesses. again, these are decisions which do not alter the basic question of financial speculation. without putting a stop to the derivatives market and tax havens, the creation of european authorities in these areas will be of little use. so our vote against is mainly a protest against the fact that no proposals have been put forward so far on the end of tax havens, the taxation of capital movements and the end of the derivatives market. what is clear about this whole financial package is that it is intended to create the illusion that the problems of the crisis are being solved, but without touching on the underlying issues that allow the financial groups to make large profits at the expense of speculation, including on the sovereign debt of the member states with the weakest economies.

in writing. - if there is one lesson we have all learned from the recent crisis, it is that the institutional structure of supervision needs to be reformed by creating european bodies, and thus the whole concept of macro- and microeconomic supervision needs to be reformed. personally, as i have had the opportunity to say many times, i am not afraid of the existence of european supervisory authorities. i think it is essential that they exist and that they can carry out their mandates independently and competently, thus strengthening the confidence of the markets and their agents. europe urgently needs to develop specialised macro-prudential oversight capabilities to detect systemic risks, i.e. to detect risks to financial stability at the european level and, where necessary, to sound the alarm and ensure monitoring of the situation. however, the current supervisory structure that we are approving, and in particular the european systemic risk board, which will not be able to impose measures or sanctions on member states or financial institutions, relies to a large extent on the european central bank (ecb) to be able to carry out its activities and to fulfil the tasks assigned to it. i believe that the ecb's prestige and reputation will be an asset to the new european systemic risk board.
in writing. − the need to ensure conditions for stronger and more effective european supervision of financial markets has been the subject of a strong commitment by the european parliament, which has become more evident and valued with the development of the current economic and financial crisis. a system of supervision based on a nationalist basis, based on the individualistic logic of each member state, is proving increasingly ineffective and fallible in the face of the global dimension of financial markets, in a logic of increasingly integrated development. i therefore support this legislative resolution of the european parliament. with the appropriate technical support and drawing on the capacity and resources of the european central bank, the european systemic risk board (esrb) will undoubtedly play a decisive role in the european union in acting more rapidly and in advance by analysing information on the evolution of systems and detecting potential risks. this will be key to preventing new crises or, in the case of their inevitability, to mitigating their negative impacts and to finding ways to reverse the trend quickly.
in writing. − the need to respond to a future financial crisis and the new models of macro and microprudential supervision have led to the creation of the european systemic risk board (esrb) and the european system of financial supervisors (esfs). however, only the prestige of the ecb will make this new system efficient, since the new esrb will not be able to impose measures or sanctions on member states or financial institutions, and its warnings will not be binding. this new supervisory architecture, which is coordinated by and dependent on the ecb, will be tasked with anticipating future crisis scenarios in order to take preventive measures to prevent the emergence of new crises. it will also be necessary to ensure that all choices for management positions throughout the system are based on criteria of genuine competence and merit rather than on short-term tactics of the distribution of powers between states.

in writing. - artistic, scientific, industrial and cultural creation deserves protection, and that is why there are internationally recognised intellectual property rights (ipr). these ensure the integrity of the creation/invention and must protect it against counterfeiting and piracy. however, modern technologies - notably the internet - have made piracy and counterfeiting easier and more accessible. we all know how easy it is to illegally download or buy counterfeit products online and how these behaviors affect, very specifically, the creative industries. i agree with the rapporteur when she talks about the need to educate consumers to respect ipr and to reject counterfeiting and piracy, however easy and less serious they may seem to them. i also think it is very important to create a digital internal market for the legal provision of online content as a way of combating piracy on the internet. these are active and positive measures to combat piracy and counterfeiting, and they are in line with the approach i advocate that should be taken to this matter.

in writing. - there are several contradictions in this report. although, on the one hand, there are aspects which deserve our full support, particularly when it defends copyright, even stating that the encouragement of the creation and promotion of cultural industries is not against creators, on the other hand, it enters into the field of patents and acta (anti-counterfeiting trade agreement), without taking into account the specificities of various sectors. hence our abstention at the end. in this way, we want to send a signal of recognition of the existence of copyright problems and the need to defend them in various areas, including the internet. we know that counterfeiting and piracy must be combated, but we must take account of the diversity of sectors and not confuse copyright with patents, particularly in the field of software or medicines. we stress the call on the european commission to strike a balance between the various interests at stake, although we are not sure that this will be achieved. but we will continue to be attentive to the development of the situation, particularly in defending the interests of authors and cultural industries in countries such as portugal, without forgetting other interests, such as those of disadvantaged populations and peoples.
in writing. - intellectual property rights have been flouted throughout history. however, technical progress in information technology, particularly the internet, has exacerbated the problem. it is also important to stress that any infringement of intellectual property rights (ipr) is very harmful to economic growth and is the main cause of the so-called "parallel economy", with all the harm it causes. only with the uncompromising defence of intellectual property rights is it possible to develop technical and scientific innovation, to discover new patents and to develop the cultural industry, which contribute in a strong way to the growth of the eu economies. i believe that by adopting this report we are making an important contribution to achieving these objectives. hence my vote.
in writing. - i personally voted in favour of the gallo report on the protection of intellectual property rights in the internal market because i believe it takes a fair and balanced position on this important issue. intellectual property rights (ipr) deserve no less protection than other rights. the creators and researchers, as well as the companies which market them, are entitled to such protection. the european economy is also based on creativity, research and innovation. the complacency with which a certain anarchist-leftism looks at the violation of ipr, under the pretext of internet freedom, is not justified. like defamation, libel, or racial hatred, they are not illegal just because they are practiced on the internet. nor should ipr infringements be condoned. the right to private copying already adequately guarantees the individual's right to protected works. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of intellectual creators are not infringed.

in writing. - i welcome the fact that the treaty of lisbon has enshrined territorial cohesion, alongside economic and social cohesion, among the eu's fundamental objectives, which is the most visible and quantifiable manifestation of european solidarity. eu cohesion policy should cover all eu regions, with particular emphasis on regions with special geographical characteristics, such as the portuguese archipelagos of madeira and the azores. i am convinced that only a specific, flexible and integrated european policy framework with legal and financial implications, capable of adapting to the scale of intervention most appropriate for the region in question, while at the same time responding to common challenges (globalisation, climate change, demographic change), will be able to combat development inequalities between and within member states and regions. i support this resolution and call on both the commission and the member states to ensure that these regions can continue to benefit from specific provisions, particularly in the context of the new financial perspective, and to draw up specific eu measures and programmes tailored to each region, aimed at its structural adjustment, making it more competitive and capable of facing new challenges.

in writing. − within the eu, with all its asymmetries and regional differences, one situation deserves special treatment: mountainous, insular and sparsely populated regions. these regions, because of their geographical and demographic characteristics, are facing specific difficulties and therefore deserve special treatment in regional development and cohesion policy. the cohesion policies provided for in the treaties cannot be a mere political objective translated into the legislative bodies of the eu. they must be concrete and objective policies which enable the sustainable development of all regions, including those which, for natural reasons, are most difficult and are more remote (in the case of islands) or inaccessible (in the case of mountain areas). as a portuguese, this is a particularly important issue for me, and i therefore hope that the commission will welcome this resolution and follow up the proposals that are left here.
in writing. the resolution could provide guidelines and recommendations relevant to regions with structural and geographical constraints which constitute constraints on their economic and social development. however, it is a side-effect and does not touch on the really important points in the analysis of this problem. the exclusive reference to territorial cohesion overlooks the importance of a fundamental pillar of economic and social development: economic and social cohesion. the document welcomes the inclusion of territorial cohesion as a new objective of the union a guideline expressed in the lisbon treaty. as we have already said on more than one occasion, new cohesion objectives must be given new and sufficient financial resources, otherwise they will become the dead letter of the treaties or mere propaganda. that did not happen. the existing funds for the convergence objective have proved insufficient and the policies being pursued by the eu are aggravating the existing asymmetries rather than correcting them. although mountainous, island and sparsely populated regions share certain constraints and conditions, each needs to be dealt with specifically in accordance with its differences and particularities. we cannot but regret the absence of any specific reference to the outermost regions.
in writing. - with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the principle of territorial cohesion has gained greater prominence and has shown particular concern about the asymmetries existing in the various regions. the mountain, island and sparsely populated regions should be given a special status to overcome the strong constraints inherent in them. in order to make these regions better able to adapt, a european strategy is therefore essential to promote the social and economic development of the least favoured regions through specific programmes to overcome the backlog of these regions. hence my vote.
in writing. - the regions of the european union are very different in their level of development. the objective of territorial cohesion, an expression of european solidarity, is to eliminate these differences and promote harmonious development by means of financial structural adjustment and the adaptation of the various sectoral policies to the characteristics of each region. the mountain, island and sparsely populated regions are particularly disadvantaged regions whose social and economic development is affected by their natural and geographical characteristics. particular attention should therefore be paid to them, in particular by taking into account a number of indicators of their level of development, complementary to gdp, which take due account of the specificities of each region, by eliminating rigid criteria for eligibility for cross-border cooperation programmes, by coordinating the various means of financing and by establishing partnerships between the various levels of government. in this context, the outermost regions, which have some characteristics which overlap with those of these regions, by the same token, justify an analogous application of the proposals contained in this resolution, in accordance with the specificities of each region concerned.

when we talk about preserving biodiversity, we are also talking about combating climate change, food security, public health, fighting poverty, achieving the millennium development goals, sustainable development of the planet, in other words, our collective future. the european union, as has already been said, must speak with one voice in nagoya and do everything to achieve good results. political will is needed to save the most endangered species of fauna and flora. it has also been said here by several colleagues that the costs of biodiversity loss are in the order of 50 billion euros per year, or about 1% of gross domestic product, but it has also been said, and there are studies proving that by 2050 these costs may amount to 7% of gross domestic product, but the return on investment in biodiversity conservation is 100 times higher. biodiversity is fundamental to climate change mitigation and adaptation, taking into account, for example, the role of terrestrial and marine ecosystems as important carbon sinks, and so we hope that the conference will produce good results. this is what the citizens expect, and also to be made aware of the challenges we all face.
the preservation of biodiversity is an ethical imperative and an essential condition for the future of the human species itself, which is above any economic consideration. before nagoya, the european union must learn from its failure in this area and must correct its course if it is seeking practical results rather than repeated and inconsequential declarations of intent. among other things, it will have to make a major change in its sectoral policies. the reduction in the diversity of cultivated species and varieties, the erosion of the genetic base on which food depends, the promotion of the use of agricultural varieties specific to certain regions, the combating of the homogenisation of agricultural production, intensive carrier-based models and the abandonment of small and medium-scale production resulting from current agricultural and trade policies must be stopped and reversed. these are just a few examples. biodiversity and the set of environmental balances that depend on it are a heritage of our planet, a common good that cannot under any circumstances be subject to private appropriation, a priceless common good whose use and enjoyment, in justice and equity, must be ensured for all.

mr president, commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, cohesion policy, given its objectives, clearly has a european added value. it demonstrates european solidarity by reducing regional disparities and contributing to economic, social and territorial cohesion, and it must therefore have the necessary budgetary resources. cohesion policy must also be sufficiently flexible to take account of regional specificities, particularly in the less developed regions, and gdp must remain the main criterion for determining eligibility. the eafrd, which supports rural development, should be coordinated with cohesion policy funds in order to increase efficiency and achieve maximum results. i also call on the commission to evaluate the implementation of the cohesion policy funds so that the necessary measures are taken urgently to improve the implementation rates of the respective funds.
cohesion policies are no longer just an instrument of european construction, but are the effective implementation and dynamic witness of the european project itself as a community of citizens who share the values of social justice and solidarity. in this context, it is understandable that there is an insistence on all regions being included in cohesion policies and that the eligibility criteria, which have so far been concentrated on gdp per capita, be broadened in the interests of greater fairness. but we must never lose sight of the first and ultimate aim of cohesion policies: to promote equal living standards for all european citizens, which always requires increased attention to the poorest regions, such as some of the outermost regions, which are in fact lacking in specific measures.

mr president, commissioner, cohesion policy is the great pillar of european solidarity. cohesion is the means by which the aim of reducing disparities between regions is achieved and the harmonious development of the european union as a whole is encouraged. in the next period from 2014 to 2020, we must define a framework capable of enhancing the effectiveness of regional policy. governance at the various levels should be encouraged through greater involvement and participation of regional and local authorities, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity and as provided for in the new lisbon treaty. the special situation of the outermost regions should not be overlooked. this group of regions faces very important challenges and should continue to benefit in future from specific provisions in the implementation of european policies. gdp should remain the main eligibility criterion, but we should take into account other indicators which can provide a more complete picture of the regional reality.
