in writing. − in view of the irregularities detected and the inability of the academy to account to parliament for its budgetary and financial situation, i support the rapporteur in her decision to refuse to give the director of the european police academy discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2008.
in writing. − the european police college has had difficulty in meeting the standards of good administration that any regulatory agency must meet. since 2006, repeated audits have identified problems with respect to the academy's compliance with the financial regulation, the staff regulations and the accounting system, as well as shortcomings in the management of the budget, human resources, public procurement procedures and the rules applicable to expenditure for the organisation of courses. according to the resolution, improvements in the academy can only be expected in 2014, when its multiannual plan will have been fully implemented. i do not agree that the academy needs at least nine years (2006-2014) to reach the acceptable level of good administration that is expected of a regulatory agency.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as can be seen from the audits known to us, the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds available and are meeting the objectives proposed. however, according to the rapporteur, this is not the case with the european police college, since there are several irregularities and an inability to present its accounts, hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative proposal because i recognise the importance of allowing albania and bosnia and herzegovina to move within the european union through a visa-free regime, with effect from this year. this is a process which follows on from what has recently happened with serbia, montenegro and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. i believe that this vote represents an important step towards european integration and political and economic cooperation with this region, although it is still important to direct efforts to move forward with the process of visa liberalisation in kosovo, which is the only area in the western balkans where there is no plan to open negotiations.
in writing. - i am very pleased to vote in favour of the european union's recognition that the conditions for visa liberalization for new states on our continent, in this case bosnia-herzegovina and albania, have been met. but i regret that the european union is not as open to other countries, in particular ukraine and croatia, and that the countries which have emerged and acquired their sovereignty and independence from the ussr do not deserve, and for that reason alone (they are former soviet republics), the same recognition!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the fajon report, as the outcome of the missions and evaluation reports showed that progress had been made in meeting the requirements for albania and bosnia and herzegovina to be included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for access to the schengen area.
in writing. - those who remember the tensions and conflicts that have plagued the western balkans cannot help but feel that a long way has already been travelled towards their pacification and stabilisation. the union naturally wanted to help to reduce the barriers which separate it from most of the balkan states and to allow its citizens to enter the union without a visa. i am in principle in favour of the abolition of barriers to the movement of people and therefore support the removal of these barriers. i also believe that this facilitation of the movement of balkan citizens within the european territory must be accompanied by improved crossborder cooperation and a more fruitful exchange of information with their countries of origin in order to cope with the expansion of the activities of the criminal networks originating from them.
in writing. - i strongly support the objective of abolishing the visa regime for all western balkan countries. the abolition of visas for citizens of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia in december 2009 was an important step towards their european integration. the visa-free regime is of great importance in people's lives, as it strengthens relations between peoples and allows the principle of free movement to be realised as one of the fundamental rights of europe. ensuring that the european union will implement the visa-free regime for both countries, and in particular for bosnia and herzegovina, in the very near future - early autumn 2010 - will reduce the risk of further political and ethnic instability, strengthen political and economic cooperation in the region and increase popular support for the eu and the prospects for european integration, broaden the horizons of the populations and contain extremist and anti-european forces. i voted in favour of this resolution so that bosnia and herzegovina and albania benefit from the visa-free regime as soon as possible.
in writing. − we are in favour of visa-free travel as soon as possible for the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina and albania, countries which were excluded from this possibility in 2009 when the visa-free regime for all western balkan countries was abolished. this decision 'awards' the capacity of these countries to 'carry out the necessary reforms'. in this way, they say, we are opening the "doors" to those who do everything "to please us". the question is: what is the price that the people of these countries are paying for this? those who today say they are rewarding the balkan countries are the same people who yesterday did everything to destroy yugoslavia and dismantle the achievements of its peoples. the great powers of the eu and nato have their hands stained by the crimes they committed there, in an operation that succeeded in creating hatred and war between peoples who had long ago decided to unite their wills in building their state. we therefore do not support the dismantling of what is left of yugoslavia, fuelled by those who want to take over its wealth, exploit its people, exploit its geostrategic location, the old dream of the great capital of the eu. it is already being announced that the next to be included in the regime will be kosovo, the eu and nato protectorate in the region.
in writing. − the eu has always been concerned that its citizens should be able to move freely between the member states. gradually, this facility was extended to third countries, as several citizens of non-eu countries began to be able to travel to the eu area without a visa. the aim of this report is to abolish visas for citizens of albania and bosnia herzegovina, following the example of other western balkan countries, notably the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia. the progress these two countries have made in recent months is leading the eu to lift entry visas for their citizens, which will help reduce the risk of further political and ethnic instability, strengthen political and economic cooperation in the region, increase popular support for the eu and prospects for european integration, broaden the horizons of the populations and contain extremist and anti-european forces. hence my vote.
in writing. − the countries of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia have recently been included in the positive list of this regulation and their citizens are therefore exempt from the visa requirement to enter the territory of the european union. the states of albania and bosnia and herzegovina have also made progress towards, once the required criteria for exemption have been verified, becoming exempted and leaving the negative list. it is essential to decide on the fundamental right of a future community citizen to travel within the european union. the implementation of this liberalisation also requires a stronger fight against organised crime in both countries, as well as the development of a strategy to support the integration of returnees in the case of albania and the harmonisation of criminal laws in accordance with the federal criminal code in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. the possibility of visa-free travel in the near future will help to strengthen political and economic cooperation and reduce the risk of tensions in the region. in addition, the support of the european union will certainly help to broaden the horizons of citizens. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of the document.
in writing. − despite the efforts of the united nations mission in the democratic republic of congo (drc) and the extremely difficult work of humanitarian organisations, human rights violations continue to persist. the situation is alarming, with mass violations of civilians by members of armed groups, unacceptable suffering, poverty, displacement of people and the degradation of the situation in refugee camps, as well as the forced recruitment of civilians and child soldiers. the congolese army still lacks sufficient human, technical and financial resources to carry out its mission. this resolution reinforces the priority of training and adequate salaries to reform the congolese army and improve its discipline. it also stressed the need to redouble efforts to put an end to the activities of armed groups and to hold those responsible for human rights violations to account. it also stressed the urgency of developing close cooperation between the government of the drc and the international community, taking into account the participation of women in the resolution of the conflict. the dialogue with a view to the peace process must be resumed immediately, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - the growth of violence against local populations and large-scale acts of destruction, such as the burning of houses, schools, churches or even entire villages, as has happened in the democratic republic of congo, must be stopped. rape and other forms of sexual violence against women and children (about 14 rapes a day, according to unhcr data) have been used as weapons of war. we cannot allow a general feeling of impunity to develop for the commission of crimes which constitute very serious violations of fundamental rights. it is essential that the perpetrators of these crimes be brought to justice and convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity. i reiterate the call made to the united nations and the congolese government to open investigations. i hope that the un security council will take urgent action to prevent further attacks on the civilian population and to provide all the necessary assistance to the victims. i welcome the adoption of the american law on the 'ministry of conflict' and hope that the european union can take similar legislative initiatives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution condemning violence against women and children in the democratic republic of congo. it is urgent to step up the fight against impunity and to put an immediate end to the violence and human rights violations in that country.
in writing. the democratic republic of congo has experienced profound instability due to the artificiality of its borders and internal animosities. the proliferation of belligerent movements and the atrocities committed by them are the saddest pages in the history of the african continent. in fact, the list of tragedies and attacks on human rights and justice is growing too fast for even the best informed to keep up with. the international community has recently been alerted to a wave of mass rapes which deserve our disgust, condemnation and the strongest repudiation. the use of this kind of violence as a weapon of war, which is unfortunately not new, should nevertheless be condemned unreservedly and those responsible, both materially and morally, should be prosecuted. the congo lacks peace and stability, but this will not be achieved without the unequivocal identification and exemplary punishment of all the perpetrators of the most gross violations of human rights who have been enjoying scandalous impunity.
in writing. atul khare, un under-secretary-general for peacekeeping operations, informed the un security council that between 30 july and 4 august, more than 500 people were victims of collective violations in north kivu province by the democratic forces for the liberation of rwanda (fdlr), a hutu rebel group, and the mai mai militia. i strongly condemn the collective violations, as well as other human rights violations, and welcome the call on the united nations and the government of the drc to conduct a full and impartial investigation into all incidents and to ensure that those responsible for violations of human rights and international humanitarian law are held accountable for their actions and prosecuted in accordance with international law.
in writing. - we strongly condemn the violations of women and children and all human rights violations in the drc. the end of these acts will only be possible with the end of the foreign military presence and external interference, which are the factors fuelling the conflict. the un and eu missions have already proven that they are not the solution, they are part of the problem. our group has proposed 'the termination of eupol and eusec missions in the drc, in recognition of their negative contribution to the escalation of violence and the situation in the country by training security forces who commit crimes against the civilian population'. the majority of meps rejected this proposal, siding with those who want to maintain the conflict and benefit from it. peace will only be achieved through a political agreement between the various actors involved, both internal and external. the countries of the region, in particular rwanda and uganda, which are violating the sovereignty and independence of the drc and are an active party to the conflict. but above all, the us and the eu, the main beneficiaries of a war economy that is sustained by the sale of minerals important to produce the components of computers and mobile phones of american and european companies.
in writing. the eu cannot be indifferent to the various armed conflicts that exist somewhat all over the world. the violence in the democratic republic of congo is a conflict that has dragged on for several years and has already caused millions of deaths, displacement and displaced persons. it is therefore very important to call on all the parties to the conflict to cease hostilities so that the people of these regions can return to live in peace. it is very important that we continue to support the un missions on the ground in order to alleviate the suffering of the entire population, but with a primary concern for the elderly, women and children.
in writing. − in a world where 43 countries still retain the death penalty and where children are forced to watch public executions, europe must continue to call for an end to this practice, which constitutes a cruel and unacceptable violation of the right to life. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the eu should use diplomatic instruments to contribute to the abolition of the death penalty, by pressing government authorities to adopt a moratorium on executions with a view to its complete abolition. the resolution calls on the council and the commission to provide guidelines for a comprehensive european policy to be applied to the dozens of european citizens sentenced to death in third countries, as regards the provision of information and legal assistance, which i consider equally important. i also recognize the importance of the adoption of the world day against the death penalty and the european day against the death penalty.
in writing. - the value of life and the multiplication of judicial errors which history has bequeathed to us are reasons enough to oppose the death penalty. the abolition of the death penalty worldwide is a priority for the eu. the 10th of october has been designated as the european day against the death penalty. we are firmly committed to contributing to its global abolition and to the universal acceptance of this principle. according to amnesty international, there are still 58 countries in the world that have not abolished it, and about 18 carried out executions in 2009, with china alone executing more people than all other countries combined. the only country in europe that still applies the death penalty is belarus. the european parliament was the first european institution to launch this campaign in the early 1980s, and the eu is now the main institutional actor in the fight against the death penalty, as well as the main funder of efforts to do so. we are fighting for the adoption of moratoriums on its application until the death penalty is finally abolished.
in writing. - as a national of one of the first countries in the world to abolish the death penalty, portugal in 1867, i consider the death penalty an inhuman punishment and the most extreme denial of human rights. that is why i am pleased to vote in favour of this motion for a resolution. the promotion of human dignity and, consequently, the fight for the abolition of the death penalty are, and must remain, among the objectives of the european union's human rights policy. in the name of a comprehensive and effective european policy on the death penalty, the union, through its institutions and in particular through the high representative, must speak with one voice. the establishment of a worldwide moratorium on the use and imposition of the death penalty in all regions of the world is not only a fundamental step towards the abolition of the death penalty in the world, it is above all a vital step towards a more dignified humanity!
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the eu should use all the diplomatic and cooperation-supporting instruments at its disposal to contribute to the abolition of the death penalty. portugal is an example to follow in this area, as it was the first european state to provide for the abolition of the death penalty in its constitutional law, more than 140 years ago. unfortunately, this is not the reality in more than 40 countries around the world, where violations of the right to life enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights persist.
in writing. − the death penalty constitutes an unacceptable violation of the inherent dignity of every human being and the inalienable and unrepeatable value of every life. it therefore deserves our strong condemnation and the unreserved commitment of all to eradicate it. i hope that more countries will join the group of countries which have finally abandoned this practice. regardless of the seriousness of the concrete individual actions which, in the abstract, could motivate and even justify such a sentence, i consider that the abolition of the death penalty constitutes a huge civilizational advance and a distinctive feature of penal systems which, like those of the member states of the union, strive to separate justice from revenge. it is urgent to maintain this non-vengeful disposition and to ensure that even the worst of criminals should be treated with dignity even when they do not deserve it. in fact, the mere application of the death penalty would not live up to our common heritage of respect for human life, which is so often forgotten by our policy makers. at this moment my thoughts also turn to all those who are not even guaranteed a fair trial and who are killed, either randomly or deliberately, in the most barbaric ways in the most unforgiving of contexts.
in writing. − the eu has been the main institutional actor in the fight against the death penalty in the world over the past few years, and this fight has been a priority in its external human rights policy. while it is true that there are still more than 40 countries worldwide that practice the death penalty and that one of these countries, belarus, is in europe, it is necessary to continue to combine all efforts to make the abolition of the death penalty worldwide a reality, since it is the most cruel, inhuman and degrading of punishments and constitutes a violation of the right to life enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights. hence my vote.
in writing. - the days we dedicate to various social causes are always an invitation to reflect and debate on the privileged topic and, above all, a repeated call for attention to a near change in behaviour with a view to adhering to new values or a new interpretation of ancestral values, which is decisive for the construction of the society in which we want to live. the death penalty is one of the most heinous acts of legalization which i believe cannot be justified by any other form of prior action. even murder does not justify the death penalty for the murderer, which is to punish a criminal act by an identical act which, by court order, becomes legal from a legal point of view, but not legitimate from an ethical point of view. in this context, i warmly welcome the resolution for the establishment of a world day against the death penalty in the hope that this may constitute another important step towards its effective abolition throughout the world.
in writing. − it is important that the eu ensures the protection of its coasts through its prevention and response capacity to such problems. the legislation in force must also improve safety in oil exploration and extraction. the european maritime safety agency, based in lisbon, provides support and technical assistance to the european commission and the member states in the development and implementation of community legislation on maritime safety and security, as well as in the area of pollution caused by ships. in june this year i put in writing to commissioners oettinger, kallas and georgieva the suggestion that the european maritime agency's remit be extended to create mechanisms for monitoring the safety of european oil platforms in the north sea, the black sea and the mediterranean and to be responsible for preventing environmental disasters linked to oil exploration. this suggestion allows for economies of scale in terms of financial, human and technical resources. i welcome the response of the commissioners, who have shown an openness to revising the regulation of the european maritime agency, and i call on the ec to make the necessary efforts to achieve this objective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on 'eu action on oil exploration and extraction in europe', as i considered it necessary to strengthen safety and working conditions on offshore oil platforms in the european union in order to prevent environmental disasters such as those in the gulf of mexico.
in writing. - given the importance of oil extraction to the countries that extract it and the dangers involved (as can be seen from the terrible consequences of oil spill accidents), it is essential that the union creates the conditions for the safest possible oil exploitation. to this end, it is important that there is adequate legislation with the basic safety standards for offshore oil and gas production, ensuring the safety of their extraction and supply in the eu. as a portuguese, i cannot fail to recall in this connection the prestige disaster which deeply affected the galician coast, with consequences that extended beyond the portuguese and french coasts, and i would point out that the measures now proposed should not be limited to oil exploration and extraction but also to its transport and supply, knowing that oil tanker disasters are, unfortunately, more frequent than we would like and that it is also important to review safety standards in order to reduce the likelihood of such disasters occurring.
in writing. − the deepwater horizon oil spill in the gulf of mexico was a wake-up call for the eu and its member states to urgently examine all aspects of oil exploration and extraction in the european union and to take all necessary measures to ensure that such an environmental catastrophe does not occur in our waters. it is therefore necessary and urgent to adopt a common european, cross-border system for oil spill prevention and response. i would stress the request for a report from the commission assessing the level of environmental pollution and the biological state of the gulf of mexico, and for a review of the eu's ability to respond immediately to accidents involving offshore installations, and for the development of a european action plan in cooperation with the member states. i welcome the call for legislation to ensure that high safety standards are applied to all oil rigs and oil exploration operations in the eu, but i disagree with the imposition of a moratorium on any new oil drilling in deep water in the eu until such standards are ensured throughout the eu because of the disproportionate impact this measure could have on the industry.
in writing. the resolution is generally positive, warning of the need to prevent and ensure the necessary support in the event of environmental disasters caused by oil spills. ensuring the independence and quality of environmental impact assessments and accountability assessments is an important aspect of ensuring a high level of protection of human health and the environment, preventing potentially hazardous activities on the seabed from causing damage to the marine and coastal environment, ensuring the protection of biodiversity and ensuring that coastal populations can thrive in their local farming and fishing activities. we cannot, however, fail to criticize the fact that in a resolution on this subject the problem of the physical limits of oil reserves, the very high and worrying dependence of mankind on this primary source of energy, the need for a fair and careful management of existing reserves and the need to look for alternative sources of energy supply are completely forgotten.
in writing. - the various accidents in the field of oil exploration and extraction over the years have been warning of the dangers of this activity, but it was the recent and very serious accident in the gulf of mexico that forced new and different measures to be taken to avoid similar situations in the future, since they threaten the environmental balance and biodiversity of entire regions with the damage, for everyone, that ensues. the eu must therefore take the necessary measures to ensure that oil exploration and extraction in europe is carried out in the best possible safety conditions, thus avoiding future environmental and human catastrophes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, following the debate with the council and the commission, where we discussed the european union's plans and main strategic objectives to halt the loss of biodiversity, on the eve of the conference of the parties to the convention on biological diversity. i therefore hope that a strong and coherent position from the european union will be brought to this conference with ideas on the concrete measures that will be taken to ensure that the protection of biodiversity contributes to sustainable development. i remind you that conservation of biodiversity is fundamental to the quality of ecosystems, has direct effects on essential functions such as food production or water availability, prevents landslides and floods. i would also like the political responses to ensure the integration of biodiversity into activities in economic sectors such as agriculture, the forestry sector, the fisheries sector and the tourism sector to have the courage and the ambition to protect this invaluable but extremely fragile heritage, as is the case in my region, the azores, from other blind external interests that may threaten it.
in writing. − in the year 2010, proclaimed by the united nations as the international year of biodiversity, and in the face of the failure to meet the global target of significantly reducing the rate of biodiversity loss by 2010 and the european target of halting biodiversity loss, the resolution on the eu's strategic objectives for cop 10 of the convention on biological diversity in nagoya is of particular importance. the preservation of biodiversity, as well as the sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources, should continue to be advocated, which i believe is reflected in this resolution. the commission and the member states must speak with one voice at cop 10 and its internal decision-making procedures must be speeded up. in particular, it is important to strengthen diplomatic efforts with third countries. finally, i believe it is essential to integrate the environmental factor into relations between the commission and the member states with third countries, stressing the importance of pursuing an integrated approach and an ecological diplomacy.
in writing. − in a matter as sensitive as it is essential, the preservation of biological diversity, the european and world natural heritage, it is important that the member states and the commission agree on the position to be taken by the european union at cop10. i therefore welcome this motion for a resolution. the complexity of biodiversity conservation requires multiple mechanisms, solutions and efforts. i therefore believe that the promotion of synergies between the various world organizations, member states and ngos will make it possible to develop instruments for safeguarding biodiversity within the framework of environmental conservation policies, maximising this objective. finally, i would like to stress the need to signal to the market the economic benefits of its intervention in the preservation of biodiversity, as well as the inclusion of environmental issues in the agenda of the member states and the commission in its relations with third countries, also known as ecological diplomacy.
in writing. - as i have already had the opportunity to say about the report by mrs esther de lange, voted at the last plenary session, 'i agree (...) with the need for the eu as a whole, and paying particular attention to all the areas covered by community policies, to find a sustainable strategy for the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of ecosystems. i believe that this is particularly relevant in the area of agriculture and fisheries, which is why i am following the reforms being prepared in the cfp and the cap with particular attention, since the proper and sustainable preservation of biodiversity, while essential and desirable, cannot be a brake on the sustainability and development of agricultural and fisheries activities.'
in writing. the united nations has proclaimed 2010 as the international year of biodiversity. unfortunately, the eu will not meet its biodiversity target for 2010. the loss of biodiversity is continuing at an alarming rate. the rate of loss is estimated to accelerate to a value ten times higher by 2050. this loss of biodiversity is unacceptable, not only from an ethical point of view but also from an ecological and economic perspective, since we are depriving future generations of enjoying the benefits of a healthy biodiversity. the commission and the member states need to speak with one voice and to increase the speed and efficiency of their internal decision-making procedures in order to be able to reach a rapid consensus on an internal eu position at cop 10, and to devote more resources and time to their diplomatic efforts with third countries.
in writing. - this resolution contains positive and important points, others are ambiguous and unclear and others are still negative and even worrying. we support the concern expressed about the failure to meet eu and global targets for a significant reduction in the rate of biodiversity loss. we value aspects such as sharing the benefits of genetic resources, rejecting patents on life and life processes, protecting traditional knowledge and practices of indigenous peoples, linking genetic diversity to global food security, referring to the impacts of biofuels and drawing attention to the problem of exotic species. but we cannot but reject and strongly criticise the intention to move towards new forms of private appropriation of nature and its resources, such as the introduction of forms of 'payment for ecosystem services' - which is more than once advocated in the resolution. the report also mentions the ambiguous and unclear aspects, such as the call for 'the values of biodiversity and the opportunities arising from its preservation and sustainable use to be integrated into national accounts'.
in writing. - the rapid rate of man-made biodiversity loss is worrying. biodiversity should be seen as the most reliable barometer of the state of the environment. the eu is therefore faced with alarming figures of biodiversity loss, with 42% of mammals, 43% of birds, 45% of butterflies, 30% of amphibians, 45% of reptiles and 52% of freshwater fish threatened with extinction, and i consider the legislation now in place on the protection of biodiversity, and even its reinforcement, to be fundamental and essential. so, with regard to biodiversity, we have to be ambitious to achieve the strategic objectives for 2020. hence my vote.
in writing. − biodiversity is a rich heritage that we have received from past generations and that we have a duty to pass on to future generations. beyond the whole anthropological perspective, it is also important to recognise the intrinsic value of this biological diversity. today, one in five species is threatened with extinction, a frightening figure which requires us to take proportionate action to defend and protect biodiversity. in this context, i welcome this resolution which is aimed at promoting the effective and decisive implementation of the previously set target for 2010 of a significant reduction in the rate of biodiversity loss and which systematises the different aspects of urgent action to protect biodiversity by setting new targets for 2020.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree that the issue of financial institutions that are too big to fail should be taken into account, and that capital requirements and countercyclical capital buffers should be proportionate to the size, level of risk and business model of a financial institution. i call for an in-depth study of capital instruments before and after the crisis to assess the importance of specific capital instruments and their relevance in a crisis situation. the future european banking authority should play a leading role in the definition and implementation of measures relating to capital requirements and countercyclical capital buffer rules at eu level.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the majority of the measures proposed in this report. countercyclical regulation requires harmonised criteria to ensure comprehensive and scrupulous oversight of financial markets and the market environment by supervisors, including, inter alia, the exchange of all information, the synchronisation of regulatory measures and the real-time monitoring of exposures and risks, including the requirement for audit trails on all financial market transactions. the development of high-quality liquidity standards is therefore an essential element of the crisis response, but they should be sufficiently differentiated to take account of the specificities of banks' business models and their risk profile. in this regard, the future european banking authority should play a leading role in the definition and implementation of measures related to capital requirements and countercyclical capital buffer rules at eu level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that the supervision and regulation of financial market players is essential to safeguard the interests of citizens and the financial and economic stability necessary for development and progress. in addition, the crisis we are experiencing today has shown that the own funds of banks were manifestly insufficient in terms of solvency and liquidity. the capital requirements and countercyclical capital buffers shall be proportionate to the size, risk level and business model of a financial institution. i would also like to stress the call and the warning to the basle committee on the importance of ensuring the necessary adjustments in the regulatory framework so that the european economy and the european banking sector, which are characterised by strong interdependence, are not harmed and placed at a competitive disadvantage in the context of the global market.
in writing. - the global financial crisis, which continues to cause problems in the economies of all countries, has confirmed that a strong banking sector is of paramount importance to avoid similar situations in the future. the basel ii package and the revision of the capital requirements directive will help to ensure that we have a strong banking industry which will be able to withstand any future crises similar to those experienced in the recent past. the report aims to improve the quality of the capital base and to extend and strengthen the own funds requirements for covering risks (such as counterparty credit risk arising from credit derivatives, repurchase agreements, etc.). it is also intended to introduce a leverage ratio to curb excessive leverage in the banking system and other additional countercyclical measures such as the constitution of capital buffers in times of favorable economic conditions. last but not least, global standards for liquidity management are proposed. hence my vote.
in writing. - the basle committee and the commission should clarify the treatment of reciprocal participation arrangements; - there should be a thorough study of capital instruments as they stand before and after the crisis in order to assess their relevance in a future crisis situation; - high quality liquidity standards are an essential element of the crisis response; - the criteria for high-quality liquid assets should be defined; - the commission should include all euro area sovereign debt in the high-quality liquid asset category irrespective of its specific rating; - the future european banking authority should play a leading role in the definition and implementation of measures on capital requirements and countercyclical capital buffer rules; - countercyclical regulation requires harmonised criteria to ensure comprehensive and scrupulous monitoring of financial markets and the market environment by supervisory authorities.
in writing. − the adoption of the financial supervisory package for the european union last september included, inter alia, the creation of micro-prudential banking supervisory institutions and mechanisms in coordination with the network of national supervisors. the owninitiative report we voted on today focuses on a subject which i think fits into this new architecture in some way and which i consider to be crucial for any economy. the definition of the quantity and quality of own funds is a highly sensitive issue which must be analysed in terms of its impact, in particular on the european economic recovery, and its general context. given that our business fabric is financed mainly by the banking sector - which is one of the pillars of the economy - it seems to me essential that banks manage their risk and profits in a prudent long-term perspective. in addition, i believe that these concerns should be discussed from a transatlantic cooperation point of view and in a proactive manner. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with its general content, which i believe is another step towards the implementation of new community mechanisms for economic, budgetary and social planning, coordination and supervision within the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'health systems in sub-saharan africa and global health', as it reaffirms the need to fulfil the commitments made by the international community in the context of the millennium development goals and the european union's commitment to improve the support it provides to health services in sub-saharan africa. the importance of supporting the development of sustainable mutual models, based on solidarity north-south solidarity and between its members but aiming at their autonomy and self-financing in the long term, should be underlined.
in writing. - sub-saharan africa remains the region with the lowest average life expectancy at birth (of the 20 countries with the lowest average life expectancy, 19 are african countries), and the highest mortality and maternal and child mortality rates. it is also the area with the highest prevalence of deaths from hiv infection, with the prevalence rate in the adult population in several countries exceeding 15%. these figures cannot but raise a strong question and a warning signal that it is urgent that humanitarian aid to these countries be properly directed towards health and the provision of basic medical care to populations in great need. the european union and individual states have a role to play here, not because, as the report says, this situation of extreme deprivation is due to the colonial past of the african continent, but because we europeans have special ties of friendship and solidarity with africa which cannot be forgotten.
in writing. − there is unquestionable recognition of the serious health problems and extreme needs of the african population, and of the importance of effective intervention by the developed world to ensure better living conditions on a continent marked by numerous scourges, from natural disasters to wars, conflicts and oppressive dictatorships. but it is not acceptable to use this cause to force the introduction of fundamental and non-negotiable values of humanity, as is the case with the right to life. it is not by imposing new, divisive concepts that we will help to solve the problems of underdeveloped africa. i voted against it.
in writing. - the report contains aspects which we consider important, such as the consideration that health is not a commodity and the concern expressed about the 'increasing commodification of health'. we value the defence of women's right to control without constraint issues relating to their reproductive health, including in the areas of procreation, contraception, termination of pregnancy or sexually transmitted diseases. it is also important to draw attention to the problem of the shortage of qualified health personnel in a large number of african countries. instead of helping to secure these resources in their countries of origin, several european countries have contributed to the phenomenon of 'brain drain' by attracting many of these professionals to their territory. where the report could and should have gone further is in what it calls the "external determinants" that "can drastically reduce the room for manoeuvre of states . . . and profoundly affect the health of populations". we cannot ignore the structural adjustment programmes, the external debt and the cuts and privatisations that they are trying to make possible, also in the health sector, where the deficits are already enormous. nor is the way in which the eu is trying at all costs to impose epas that will further weaken the economies of these countries.
in writing. − it is urgent that we continue to join forces to ensure that the eu's investments in health systems in sub-saharan africa are effectively implemented, to reduce once and for all the major disparities between this continent and the rest, in particular as regards childbirth, life expectancy and hiv incidence. it is important, however, to leave a warning to the governments of these countries to use the funds available for what they are granted and not to be diverted to other types of activity, because often the bad governance of certain countries leads to the aggravation of problems in health systems. i should also like to stress that in these countries we must continue to preserve and encourage the birth rate, and that this should not be accompanied by the voluntary termination of pregnancy. while we must respect women's rights, the recurrent practice of abortion should not be the main driver of birth control. hence my vote.
in writing. − it is important to increase the eu budget, but it is also important to improve the flexibility and simplification of the rules on use for a better implementation of the budget. the eu must have policy priorities that contribute to economic growth and the creation of more and better jobs, as well as policies that contribute to competitiveness, such as scientific research and innovation. i call for the architecture of cohesion policy after 2013 to be a simple, fair and transparent transitional regime, taking into account past experiences and the latest trends in the social and economic situation of the regions concerned and enabling them to continue on their path to growth and development. the eu budget must be linked to the european political agenda. for example, energy is on the agenda of all european leaders, and yet we invest in scientific research in the field of energy four times less than we did in the 1980s. i think that the european union's 2020 strategy is a good starting point and a good basis for work.
in writing. − since its foundation, the union has promoted peace and prosperity as core values, an area of freedom and security, a single market and fostered social, economic and territorial cohesion through sustainable development. these values, of which we are proud, must continue to guide the process of european integration in the future and, of course, its regional development policy. and 2013 is tomorrow! it is therefore important that everyone should work towards this objective, because the european reality today is quite complex and is in the process of profound change following the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. the adverse global environment has also refocused the union's priorities on addressing specific or temporary problems which need to be solved but which cannot distract from the principles underlying the union's regional policy. the architecture of cohesion policy post-2013 should reflect unequivocally that cohesion policy is not a policy of redistribution of financial resources between member states and regions. it is, or should be, a policy geared to the social, economic and territorial development of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu cohesion policy and regional policy after 2013. the implementation of cohesion policy, which contributes to stable and sustainable economic growth and job creation in the european union, is indispensable for the success of the europe 2020 strategy. while important for achieving the objectives of this strategy, cohesion and regional policy should be independent and provide a framework for the establishment of strong synergies between all european policies.
in writing. − as i have had the opportunity to express on other occasions, the european union's cohesion policy is crucial to reduce the imbalances observed in the various regions of the eu-27, to help to mitigate imbalances, and to foster european competitiveness. it is essential to help the less-favoured areas develop, to emphasise the efficient allocation of funds for innovation and technology, education and to implement measures that stimulate in particular employment and competitiveness. the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy should be a guiding element in this respect too and i therefore welcome the recommendation to encourage greater use of the technical assistance resources available to build the capacities of smes and ngos.
in writing. − cohesion policy aims to reduce disparities between the levels of development of european regions and to mobilise growth potential to achieve economic, social and territorial cohesion. this policy has proved to be essential to the process of european integration in the quest for modernisation and sustainable growth. in accordance with the spirit of the treaties, these characteristics require that an eu-wide regional policy be implemented throughout the union territory, covering all european regions. specific provisions should continue to apply to the outermost regions, border regions, regions with specific geographical characteristics and other regions facing specific development challenges. the current accumulation of short and long-term challenges facing the european union has led to the adoption of the europe 2020 strategy in order to create a favourable framework for stable and sustainable economic growth and job creation in europe. the implementation of cohesion policy is essential to the success of this strategy. i would stress that territorial cohesion implies an approach geared to territorial development, so there must also be sufficient flexibility to adapt to regional specificities and to support the less developed regions in their efforts to overcome socioeconomic difficulties.
in writing. - this resolution has several positive aspects, particularly when it stresses the objectives of cohesion policy, which aims to reduce disparities between the levels of development of european regions and to mobilise the growth potential to achieve economic, social and territorial cohesion. this is an area that facilitates the pursuit of modernization and sustainable growth and shows some solidarity. so it was important that it be reinforced. it is essential to take account of the regional dimension in the proposal for the revision of the eu budget and in the future financial framework, without which it is difficult to achieve social, economic and territorial cohesion. cohesion policy should be adapted to the outermost regions referred to in article 349 tfeu by adopting specific measures. the commission should propose measures on a permanent basis and with adequate funding, which are able to adapt to the needs of each outermost region, helping them to cope with the permanent constraints. specific provisions should also continue to apply to border regions, regions with specific geographical characteristics and other regions facing specific development challenges. but we do not want cohesion policy to be subordinated to the priorities of the eu 2020 strategy, which puts the emphasis on 'competitiveness', 'deregulation', 'adaptability' and 'entrepreneurship', always to the detriment of cohesion and convergence.
in writing. - without an assertive cohesion policy, such as has always been practised, the eu would not have been able to reduce the disparities between the geographically most favoured regions and all the others. strengthening these policies, at a time when the crisis has caused some delay in the difficult task of reducing disparities, is essential if the objectives of the 2020 strategy are to be achieved and if the eu is to achieve one of its main pillars of solidarity, which has already enabled the development and evolution of many european regions.
in writing. - cohesion policy is the great pillar of european solidarity. it is through this policy that the aim of reducing regional disparities is achieved and the harmonious development of the european union as a whole is encouraged. in the next period from 2014 to 2020, a framework capable of enhancing the effectiveness of regional policy should be defined. multi-level governance should therefore be encouraged, with greater involvement of regional and local authorities in the legislative process, as provided for in the new lisbon treaty, and with respect for the principle of subsidiarity, with decisions being taken at the level closest to the citizens. the special situation of the outermost regions, such as madeira, where i come from, must not be forgotten. since this group of european regions faces very particular challenges to their development, they should continue to benefit in the future from specific provisions in the implementation of european policies. it would also be desirable to apply other complementary indicators of gdp, which should remain the main criterion for eligibility for regional policy aid, which take account of the specific attributes of the regions and are able to provide a more complete picture of the reality of each region.
in writing. − the european social fund plays a key role in improving professional and employment opportunities, in promoting the adaptation of workers' skills to labour market requirements and their integration into the labour market, and in strengthening social inclusion. it is important that member states use the european social fund to invest in skills, employment, training and retraining with a view to creating more and better jobs. the europe 2020 goals and objectives can be achieved by using this instrument in supporting smes and adapting the education and training system to the needs of smes. there is a need to place a strong emphasis on modernising the education and vocational training system, on decent work, including the fight against precarious and undeclared work, on gender equality, on creating conditions for reconciling work and private life, and ensuring the inclusion of people who are excluded from the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european social fund should be the main financial instrument for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. it is essential that member states use this fund to invest in training and retraining, with a view to improving the skills of their citizens and creating more and better jobs.
in writing. − given the current employment situation in europe, with the unemployment rate reaching historic highs in several states, i believe that the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy can be achieved by using the european social fund to support small and medium-sized enterprises ('smes') and by adapting the education and vocational training system to the needs of enterprises in order to improve employability. the success of the eu2020 strategy depends on the competitiveness of european businesses and industries and also on our economic dynamics in the post-crisis world. this requires a commitment to the vitality and dynamism of enterprises (especially smes and the technological and scientific industries) and to the proper training of europeans. it is in the service of these objectives that i believe the european social fund should be, and that is why i am reversing the emphasis that this resolution places on the importance of training and education as a means of combating poverty, unemployment and social exclusion, creating wealth and betting on competitiveness.
in writing. − the fight against unemployment and social exclusion has received special attention from european citizens and institutions, owing to the effects of the current economic and social crisis. in this context, the european social fund is of increased importance in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, training and vocational qualification, as well as innovation and the dynamism of smes, are now particularly important. the aim is to promote more and better jobs with a view to eradicating poverty and social exclusion. i therefore reiterate the importance and the urgent need to make the esf, like the other structural funds, more flexible, simpler and more adaptable, in order to enable it to respond more effectively to the new european reality and to the new social problems.
in writing. - we believe that the european social fund should support member states' measures to promote employment, to promote the quality of work in all its aspects (training, working conditions, contractual relations, working time and organisation), and to contribute to reducing social inequalities and disparities in income distribution. increased european social fund funding can help achieve the objectives of social inclusion, combating poverty and social exclusion and education and training, and make an important contribution to economic and social cohesion. the resolution adopted today in the european parliament highlights some of these measures. it stressed the key issues on which the fund should focus, calling for 'continued efforts to achieve social cohesion'. but much more is needed than the money from this esf. and we need to change our policies. the jep must be abolished and replaced by a genuine social progress and development programme.
in writing. − the european social fund is the instrument par excellence for creating new professional and employment opportunities, promoting the adaptation of workers' skills to the requirements of the labour market and their integration into it, and enhancing social inclusion. it is therefore essential for the eu to achieve the objectives set out in the 2020 strategy in the social and employment fields. strengthening this important instrument is therefore essential if we are to achieve the whole strategy outlined by strengthening support for smes, which are the engine of the whole economy and the main drivers of economic and technological development and job creation.
in writing. the european social fund aims to promote employment opportunities and the geographical and occupational mobility of workers in the european union and to facilitate adaptation to industrial change and the evolution of production systems. to this end, vocational training and retraining are of the utmost importance, especially in a period of economic crisis and rising unemployment such as the present one. the fund aims to improve the employment opportunities of workers and to contribute to an improvement in their standard of living. that's why it's an essential tool. job creation and the promotion of employability are a means of achieving the objective of economic, social and territorial cohesion within the union and synergies between the various european policies should be fostered in order to achieve the eu 2020 objectives of growth and jobs. however, i am not in favour of making the esf a financial instrument independent of the other structural funds, with its own rules and budget. i believe that synergies will be better achieved if we do not go for such a sectoral approach to european funds, but instead focus on better coordination between the various instruments and a more efficient use of them.
the rapporteur. - madam president, poverty and social exclusion are violations of human dignity and fundamental human rights, but in the middle of the european year against poverty we risk setting the sad record for people living in poverty. there is a scandalous backsliding in this rich europe, where profits for the financial sector and economic groups continue to grow and take refuge in tax havens. the wave of indignation is therefore growing among millions of workers, women and young people, victims of wage cuts and precarious and low-paid work, the unemployed and pensioners with poverty reforms. if at the end of 2008 eurostat said that, even after the social transfers, some 85 million people were at risk of poverty, the situation will be much worse with the deepening of the eu's neoliberal policies and the so-called austerity measures being taken in some member states, implying wage cuts and public health, education and other services, reduction of social supports and increase in taxes on essential goods, including food, as now also in portugal, after greece, ireland and others. it is unacceptable that the european commission and the council continue to put pressure on member states because of the irrational criteria of the stability pact, looking only at financial issues but not at the social issue, having given all the public support to the banks and the financial system, forgetting the people and, worse still, now forcing workers and deprived populations to urgently pay the public aid that governments have given to the banks with the approval of the european union officials and the applause of the financial groups. so we need to change policies to tackle poverty and social exclusion, as demanded by millions of demonstrators in struggles for this europe outside, including here in strasbourg. the objectives and guiding principles of the european year against poverty cannot be words gone with the wind. the european union's commitment to the un millennium development goals cannot be overlooked. policies should recognise the rights and share the responsibility, promote cohesion and participation of people at risk of or living in poverty, take and implement concrete measures to effectively prevent and eradicate poverty, including the homeless and migrants, not forgetting people with disabilities, and not compromising the future of young people and children. unfortunately, the europe 2020 strategy only aims to lift 20 million people out of poverty by 2020, which is a step back from the initial objectives of the so-called lisbon strategy. the multidimensional nature of poverty and social exclusion requires a social dimension to macroeconomic policies as an integral part of the strategy to exit the crisis, which implies a change in priorities and policies, in particular monetary policies, including the stability pact, budgetary and fiscal policies, competition policies and the internal market. priority must be given to economic and social cohesion and the defence of human rights, which implies at least a balance between economic, employment, social and environmental policies and a fair redistribution of wealth and income. it is in this context that minimum income systems are an effective instrument to ensure people's security and to reduce the consequences of exclusion and unemployment in order to support access to decent work, combating precariousness and poverty wages that increase the percentage of working poor. these minimum income systems play an important role in income redistribution and ensure solidarity and social justice, particularly in times of crisis, by acting as social stabilisers and counter-cyclical action, providing additional resources that boost demand and consumption in the internal market, combating recession. therefore, minimum income systems based on at least 60% of the median income of each country must be an integral part of a strategy aimed at social integration, involving both general policies and specific measures for the most vulnerable groups in society in terms of housing, health care, education and training, social services, helping people to get out of poverty and encouraging action towards social inclusion and access to the labour market for all those who are able to do so, in conditions of dignity and not modern slavery, as is happening with precarious and low-paid work that affects millions of workers, especially women and young people. here is the challenge to the european commission: the commission is proposing an initiative and an action plan on minimum incomes to lift children and young people, adults and the elderly out of poverty and put them on the path to social progress.
madam president, europe is going through a period of transformation as a result of the current economic, financial and social crisis. the crises that already exist in some member states have worsened, social inequalities have increased, and this has increased the number of citizens living below the poverty line. today, there are more poor people in the european union. there are more women and men who earn less than 60% of the average wage in the country in which they live. we have a serious problem which requires concrete and effective measures. eighty million europeans live at or below the poverty line. although the poverty line in the european union varies from country to country, it is certainly a growing phenomenon in our community, which has the most advanced social model in the world as its development paradigm. in portugal, about 20% of the portuguese live or are at risk of living in poverty, on less than 360 euros a month. the data on child poverty in my country is devastating. portugal is one of the eight countries with the highest levels of child poverty. we welcome the objective of lifting 20 million citizens out of poverty by 2020, as well as efforts to promote employment and social inclusion. i welcome the rapporteur's contribution and would like to emphasize that, while it is desirable that there should be a minimum income, the amount to be fixed should be a matter for each member state.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i would like to thank all the members and all the members, and also the commission and the council and the belgian presidency, for the words they have said here, but i would like to stress three points which several members have also stressed. the first is that good words are not enough, good intentions are not enough. this european year for combating poverty must be given practical substance. policies need to change. you have to put people first. we need to understand that it is the workers who create wealth and that they need a living wage, but that to create more wealth, we need more jobs. more jobs with rights and fair wages. but there is also a need for another redistribution of wealth and income, and it is in this context that the minimum income system emerges as an essential instrument to help in this struggle, maintaining different minimum incomes in each country, but a common goal... (the president cut the speaker off)
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat poverty, and it is not the commission's intention to do so. it demands to be placed at the top of our priorities and deserves a collective response guaranteeing a minimum of dignity for our fellow citizens who are in a situation of social fragility. this is a profound problem that is affecting our young people, our elderly people, but also our workers in a growing way, affected by the loss of 6 million jobs in the last two years alone and by the insufficiency and precariousness of their wages, even when they are able to stay in their jobs. we need a systemic approach to tackle and solve the causes, the problems at the root of the problems, but we cannot at the moment dispense with immediate and urgent responses to their consequences. that is why ensuring that those who are vulnerable in our society have a minimum income for their existence and providing them with urgent responses so that they can get out of this situation is not only a necessity but above all a demand that we must subscribe to and that this report very well defends.
in writing. - i welcome this proposal, as the aim is to make the collection of data by type of goods compulsory for statistics on maritime transport, which provides a useful framework for supporting and monitoring the policy of promoting co-modality, which in the case of island regions should mean greater support for a combination of maritime and air transport, as these are the only means of transport available. this statistical survey would also allow a better understanding of the costs associated with the outermost regions, both in terms of goods and passengers, which could influence decisions on other policies such as the trans-european networks and, more specifically, the motorways of the sea, which should include maritime transport between islands and between them and the european continent. i also support the rapporteur's intention to adapt the present provisions to the new rules on delegated acts introduced by the treaty of lisbon, with the aim of strengthening the european parliament's powers in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree that it is essential to have complete and homogeneous statistics by type of goods for all modes of transport. this information provides a useful framework to support and monitor the policy of promoting co-modality, i.e. the possibility of optimised combination of different modes of transport in the same transport chain and the modernisation of freight transport logistics. i call for european statistics on all modes of transport to be compiled according to common concepts and standards, in order to achieve the greatest possible comparability between modes of transport.
in writing. the proposal aims to make compulsory the collection of data by type of goods for statistics on maritime transport, by standardizing the type of information collected and processed in the 27 member states. as the rapporteur says, 'the existence of complete and homogeneous statistics by type of goods for all modes of transport would provide a useful framework to support and monitor the policy of promoting co-modality, i.e. the possibility of optimised combination of different modes of transport in the same transport chain and of modernising the logistics of freight transport'. i am aware of the importance of the safe and efficient transport of goods for international trade, and i support the commission's proposal.
in writing. − the objective of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is to amend directive 2009/42/ec in order to make the collection of data by type of goods compulsory for maritime transport statistics. currently, this data is collected on a voluntary basis by 18 member states. five member states have no coastline and do not provide data in accordance with the directive. in most cases, the collection of the relevant data will not impose any additional burden on respondents, as the member states concerned should be able to compile the data using existing data sources (e.g. customs documents). i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need for complete and homogeneous statistics by type of goods for all modes of transport to allow for a general framework of comparability in the eu.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation aims to make the collection of data by type of goods for maritime transport statistics compulsory, the rapporteur considering that in most cases the collection of the relevant data will not impose any additional burden on respondents, as the member states concerned should be able to compile the data using existing data sources (e.g. customs documents). in addition, data collection by type of goods is already mandatory for european statistics on road, rail and inland waterway transport. we share the view that the existence of statistics on all modes of transport, both goods and passengers, would provide a useful information framework for the definition of a policy of interoperability and co-modality, i.e. the possibility of optimised combination of different modes of transport in the same transport chain, contributing to a modernisation and rationalisation of the logistics of freight transport and promoting its sustainability. this possibility depends, of course, on the comparability of available statistics, which requires the harmonization of certain standards and concepts.
in writing. the proposal aims to make it compulsory to collect data by type of goods for statistics on maritime transport. at present, this collection is carried out on a purely voluntary basis by 18 member states for maritime transport and is already mandatory for european statistics on road, rail and inland waterway transport. the existence of complete and homogeneous statistics by type of goods for all modes of transport, including maritime transport, will provide a useful framework to support and monitor the policy of promoting co-modality, i.e. the possibility of optimised combination of different modes of transport in the same transport chain and the modernisation of freight transport logistics.
in writing. - the compulsory collection of data by type of goods for the statistical survey of maritime transport is, in my view, essential for the promotion of co-modality, favouring the possibility of combining different modes of transport. since this data collection is already mandatory for statistics on other modes of transport road, rail and inland waterway , i believe that a common framework including statistical surveys on maritime transport is appropriate, which can also help to ensure maximum comparability between the various modes of transport. the revision of directive 2009/42/ec should therefore, in line with the commission proposal, follow this line and be applied already to the 2011 data, in line with the voluntary practice already being developed by 18 member states of the european union.

in writing. - resolution on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, in accordance with point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management. the machinery and equipment industries in the danish region of nordjylland were caught off guard by the changes in the markets and the global credit crisis and suffered dramatic cuts in orders, which led to redundancies in more than forty companies. in regions particularly dependent on one sector such as nordjylland, market recovery and the relocation of workers to other areas of activity tends to be slower and more difficult. the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund seems justified.
in writing. − in the face of the social impact of the global economic crisis, with particular effects on employment, the proper use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is of key importance in alleviating the suffering of many european citizens and families, contributing to their social reintegration and professional development, while also providing new qualified resources for the needs of businesses and the dynamisation of the economy. this is the context in which denmark's intervention plan to help 951 people made redundant in 45 machinery and equipment manufacturing companies in the small region of nordjylland is set. in this case, 40% of the workers laid off were skilled in manual work, metalworking and mechanical construction, and 33% of the workers were unskilled. this reality clearly demonstrates the need for an effective response in the technical and professional development of the citizens affected by this global crisis. i therefore hope that the european institutions will step up their efforts to implement measures to speed up and improve the utilization rates of such an important resource as the egf, which at present has very low rates of mobilisation. this year, only 11% of the available eur 500 million has been requested.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by denmark in relation to 951 redundancies in 45 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 28 (machinery and equipment manufacturing) in the nuts ii region of nordjylland, i voted in favour of the resolution in agreeing with the european commission proposal and the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. i would stress as of particular relevance that: (1) the egf supports the reintegration of workers made redundant into the labour market, without relieving undertakings of their responsibilities; (2) the commission, in the context of the mobilisation of the egf, proposed an alternative source of payment appropriations to the unused esf resources, as the european parliament had been calling for; (3) the functioning and added value of the egf is assessed in the context of the overall evaluation of the programmes and various other instruments established by the iia of 17 may 2006, in the context of the mid-term review process of the multiannual financial framework 2007-2013; (4) the commission proposal includes information on the application, analysing the eligibility criteria and explaining the reasons for its approval, again in line with parliament's requests.

in writing. - having regard to the requests for assistance from the netherlands in relation to 512 redundancies at nxp semiconductors netherlands, which operates in the electronics sector in the nuts ii regions of gelderland and eindhoven, i voted in favour of the resolution in agreeing with the european commission proposal, with the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. i also agree that the commission, in the context of mobilising the egf, has proposed an alternative source of payment appropriations to unused esf resources, following the european parliament's frequent calls for attention to the fact that the egf was set up as a separate specific instrument with its own objectives and deadlines, and that it is therefore necessary to identify appropriate budget lines for carrying out transfers.
in writing. − aid for workers made redundant as a result of restructuring and relocation should be dynamic and flexible so that it can be activated quickly and effectively. given that the netherlands has submitted a request for assistance in relation to 512 redundancies at nxp semiconductors netherlands, which operates in the electronics sector in the regions of gelderland and eindhoven, and having regard to the reasons i gave in my explanation of vote on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in the region of catalonia (spain), i am voting in favour of this report.

in writing. - the portuguese company qimonda, part of a leading german group, was referred to in portugal as a successful example and as being at the forefront of its sector of activity. it was the largest portuguese exporter and, before the problems that led to its insolvency became known, it was preparing to invest in new technologies and had obtained public funds to support the production of solar cells. qimonda's workers were highly skilled and had high productivity rates, so it was not to be expected that the company would become unviable in such a short space of time. in 2008 the company even considered the possibility of setting up three more industrial units in portugal, all in the vila do conde area. the north region, where the traditionally industrial qimonda was located, has been particularly hit by business closures and unemployment. the ability of qimonda to attract more skilled workers, which the region so badly needed, is now compromised. i hope that the workers at qimonda will be able to benefit adequately from the mobilisation of the fund and be able to re-enter the labour market fully. here i leave my sympathy to them and their families.
