in writing. - i welcome this report which ensures that this convention and the recommendations adopted by the north-east atlantic fisheries commission are implemented, which makes it possible to adopt measures relating to the control and enforcement of all fishing vessels used or intended for use in fisheries targeting fishery resources. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. the implementation by regional fisheries organisations of measures to combat illegal fishing should be given the highest priority and therefore the control and enforcement regime adopted by this convention should be able to be rapidly transposed into eu law, with the ep being fully and timely informed at all stages of the negotiation process with the regional fisheries organisations, ensuring the presence of observers from this institution in the negotiations.
in writing. − it is important that the eu establishes a community regime to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the proposed regulation should incorporate measures fixing the fishing opportunities and associated conditions applicable in community waters and, for community fishing vessels, in waters where catch limitations are required. it is essential that it is in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and that it contributes to sustainable development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a control and enforcement regime applicable in the area of the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries, because it introduces a new control and enforcement scheme to ensure the conservation and balanced use of fisheries resources in the region. this scheme includes, inter alia, the control of vessels engaged in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and a control system to be exercised by the port state where fishery products are landed.
in writing. - given the importance of fisheries for europe (both as an economic activity creating jobs and wealth and as a source of food for the population), we must always be very cautious about any regulation that imposes new and more demanding obligations on european fishermen. the current proposal aims to update the eu regulation transposing the control and enforcement regime adopted by the neafc convention. these measures are intended mainly to promote compliance by non-contracting party vessels with the rules of the convention and to include a new system of port state control to prevent the landing in european ports of frozen fish whose legality has not been confirmed. it also lays down new measures to control vessels engaged in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i believe that these measures will ultimately serve to protect european fishermen from the introduction of fish on the european market which does not comply with community rules, which is to be welcomed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i share the need to transpose into community law the system of control and enforcement adopted by the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries. i would stress in the new rules the control of illegal and unreported fishing vessels and the new port state control system, which effectively prevents the landing and transhipment in european ports of frozen fish whose legality has not been confirmed by the flag state of fishing vessels flying the flag of another contracting party. in 2007 and 2008, the european parliament was not represented at the nafo annual meeting. i cannot therefore fail to mention that, in the light of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament must be represented in future negotiations of international conventions on this subject.
in writing. − the proposed control system contains provisions to promote compliance with conservation and enforcement measures by non-contracting party vessels and thus ensure full compliance with the conservation and management measures adopted by the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries (neafc). it is therefore a question of filling in the gaps in the control system, particularly as regards illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing activities, which deserves our agreement. the report considers that member states whose vessels are authorised to fish in the neafc regulatory area should allocate sufficient means of inspection to this regime. it should be noted that the control of fishing activities now places increased demands on the member states, both in the context of the common fisheries policy and in the context of the regional fisheries organisations. we therefore consider that the financial means for monitoring should be reconsidered, particularly as regards the maximum co-financing rates provided for in the cfp financial measures regulation for the acquisition, development and/or modernisation of monitoring equipment by the member states. we have therefore proposed raising the current rate from 50% to 75%, taking into account the ongoing review of this regulation.
in writing. − the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is essential to ensure the sustainability of fisheries resources and to ensure greater fairness and equity in the distribution of wealth. the very existence of the fishing community depends on these assumptions. the control of all fishing vessels engaged or to be engaged in fishing in the areas defined in the convention, as well as coercive measures, are of great importance in this context. this report goes in that direction. we must all be involved in this effort and deepen it. the prevention, deterrence and elimination of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing should be a priority of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a control and enforcement regime applicable in the area of the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries is of the utmost importance in view of the updating of eu rules transposing the control and enforcement regime adopted by the neafc (north-east atlantic fisheries commission). as with the other transpositions of the rfp recommendations into community fisheries law, this one also aims to introduce tighter controls in the fight against illegal fishing, to eliminate any legal loopholes and to uphold the basic principle of the cfp of sustainable fishing inside and outside community waters. in addition, the text agreed and voted on today, in my view, upholds parliament's prerogatives under the ordinary legislative procedure and includes the necessary adaptations resulting from articles 290e and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − in view of the importance of this convention in contributing to the consultation, cooperation and optimum use, rational management and conservation of fisheries resources in the north-west atlantic area, and in promoting international collaboration to improve the sustainable management of marine resources on the basis of scientific research, the amendment presented is considered essential, which completely reformulates the convention with the aim of aligning it with other regional conventions and international instruments and incorporating modern fisheries management concepts. the positive measures include the simplification of the structure of this convention, the modernisation of budget contributions in accordance with the user/payer principle for the contracting parties, new definitions of obligations and a review of the decision-making and dispute settlement process for the latter. these improvements are essential to promote the future cfp.

in writing. − the northwest atlantic fisheries organisation (nafo) has as its main objective to contribute, on the basis of cooperation between states, to the sustainable management and conservation of fishery resources in the nafo convention area. we support and value the principle of international cooperation and collaboration in this field, based on sound scientific foundations. in this respect, we consider that the amendment to the convention adopted in 2007 and 2008, in line with the objectives set out above and aiming to take up other regional conventions and international instruments and incorporate modern fisheries management concepts, should be supported. we cannot, however, fail to point out and regret the delay with which the european parliament is called upon to give its opinion. the commission's proposal for transposition into community law is dated 8 march 2010. it therefore took more than two years for the document to be drawn up and for parliament to be heard. in future it would be important to have more timely involvement and participation, preferably in the negotiating processes themselves.
in writing. − the northwest atlantic fisheries organisation (nafo) has as its main objective to ensure the rational management and conservation of fishery resources in the nafo convention area. the eu is a contracting party to this regional fisheries organisation/rfo and, like the other contracting parties to this rfo, adopted at the 2007 nafo annual meeting the amendment to the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the northwest atlantic fisheries. the amendment aims to simplify and modernise the structures of this organisation, adapting it to the current reality of fisheries, introducing new definitions of obligations for contracting parties flag and port states , clarifying the rights and obligations of nafo contracting parties. in view of the eu's best interests, particularly the fishing opportunities granted to the european union under the convention, i consider that the adoption of this amendment is essential, and i am only being late. like the rapporteur, i regret the delay in the european commission's submission of its proposal (more than two years) compared to the date on which the amendment was adopted (2007) at one of the nafo annual meetings. this report deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. - companies must be prevented from converting permanent jobs into atypical jobs which lead to job insecurity. this situation is made more serious by the increase in unregistered female workers and the fact that many women have no choice but to accept precarious work. despite this, it is found that women are underrepresented in precarious work, as paid domestic work and care work are not taken into account. the legislative framework should be adapted to existing realities which may lead to precarious working conditions, in particular involuntary parttime work, the fact that companies do not present the lack of working conditions: no job security, low wage levels, lack of social protection and career advancement opportunities or the absence of collective representation of workers. in contrast to these realities, initial and continuing training, increased information on women's rights and a real awareness of women's occupational and family situation must be promoted, since the fact that women's income is recorded as a second income is often misleading, since it is often the only income of families.
in writing. - precarious work is not a gender problem although it may be felt particularly strongly among women and any view that seeks to reduce its dimension to a gender issue is reductive. as i have had the opportunity to argue on several other occasions, the rigid models of labour law have clearly failed. the example of the united states shows that flexibility is not synonymous with insecurity but with dynamism in the labour market. increasing flexibility does not mean increasing precariousness. it's the opposite. in the post-crisis period, we will realise that the models we were used to have failed and that the labour market - if we really want to create jobs - will have to look at atypical contracts (part-time, shift work, casual or temporary work, homework or teleworking) as normal forms of work, without losing in security what will be gained in dynamics and flexibility. in this context, i believe that women can be the main beneficiaries of more flexible systems, where the combination of their working life with family life or motherhood does not represent such a high cost as in more traditional forms of work.
in writing. − the current economic and financial crisis has increased the problem of poor working women who, often having to reconcile work with family commitments, find themselves in a particularly vulnerable employment position. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to combat this problem by urging member states and the social partners to develop new and effective strategies on job insecurity, taking into account the principle of gender equality. i would stress in this resolution the request to the commission to submit a proposal on the application of the principle of equal pay for men and women.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this own-initiative report which stresses the gender dimension of precarious employment, denounces various situations and insists on a set of measures to combat discrimination against women. it is generally positive, although it contains some contradictions and statements with which we disagree. among the various positive proposals, the following stand out: calls on the commission to support the member states in developing a campaign to enable women workers in precarious situations to gradually obtain stable employment; calls on the commission and the member states to develop strategies to combat precarious work, with a focus on decent and environmentally friendly jobs and gender balance; it called on the council and the commission to identify the characteristics of precarious employment in the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states and in the new gender equality strategy.
in writing. - precariousness affects not only working conditions and relationships but also the stability and quality of life of workers themselves. precariousness in europe affects women more, which exacerbates gender disparities in employment, particularly in terms of social rights and pay. this reality is even more acute in domestic work and in the work of migrant women. in this crisis, the precarious men and women were among the first to lose their jobs. with the recession and the destruction of contract jobs, the employment structure is becoming even more precarious. we need to reverse the cycle. gender equality and social rights at work must be guaranteed. the fight against precariousness and the fight against women's double working hours must be urgent objectives of the union, and i therefore support this report, which is a step in that direction.
in writing. - precarious work is an important factor of social instability which is worsening very significantly in a time of high unemployment rates (which continue to rise in several countries, including my own, portugal). traditionally, all forms of job insecurity or job volatility have hit the female workforce first and most strongly: with lower wages (even for equal work), with higher unemployment rates and also with a marked precariousness at work, due to ancestral social factors, but also to the specificity of motherhood. the negative impact of this reality is not limited to the already very serious discrimination which women are subjected to downstream, but by making it difficult for women to have equal access to the world of work, it conditions their economic independence and their autonomy as persons. in this context, combating job insecurity, particularly for women, is a very constructive contribution to social stability and also to gender equality - one of the fundamental values that the european union embodies.

they all submit to the new brussels consensus. at national level, budgets are governed by a single slogan: austerity. at european level, the consequence is very simple: a residual budget. the crisis is not over, and i would like to say this to the european council, but in the meantime social measures at national level are being withdrawn altogether. the crisis is not over, but our national budgets all point to wage freezes or cuts, pension cuts and increases in the most unfair of all taxes, vat. this is the context in which governments refuse to give one more euro to the european budget. your proposal is, by 3 billion euros, worse than the one we are discussing here today. but the proposal we are discussing here is also a timid one, and one without any audacity. in reality, in writing. it is an old battle of the csd to make the state a good person in terms of fulfilling its obligations. in february this year, a draft law on the cds was approved in parliament, which provides that the state will start to pay interest on late payment when the delay in payment exceeds the limits set out in the contract or the law (30 or 60 days). for several years now, the cds has also advocated the possibility of offsetting claims between debts owed by the state to enterprises and debts owed by enterprises to social security or taxation, thus seeking to make life easier for enterprises which, not being paid by the state, are nevertheless faced with the obligation to pay their tax and social contributions. we are therefore fully in line with the text now being adopted, which establishes an average period of 30 days for the payment of debts owed by the state to its suppliers (this period may be extended to 60 days in specific cases) and the obligation to pay interest for late payment. these are rules of the utmost fairness which can help to alleviate the situation of many businesses, especially smes.

in writing. ethnic profiling is not a new practice in the member states, but has been on the rise in recent years (especially after the terrorist attacks in madrid and london). however, the only member state which has looked into this and legislated on this subject is the united kingdom. profiling within specific databases may be lawful and have legitimate purposes. however, when the criteria used for data collection focus exclusively on race, ethnicity or religion, they should be considered discriminatory and in that case illegal. it is legitimate for the authorities to carry out investigations and identity checks on their territory in order to safeguard public order and security, to prevent crime and to monitor illegal immigration. however, the physical and ethnic characteristics of the persons concerned should not be considered as an indication that they are criminals or are in an illegal situation in the country. each person must be treated individually and there must be a reason, other than the person's race or ethnicity, for their data to be entered in a database or for them to be treated differently from the general population.

in writing. − the european external action service is now an integral part of the european administration, open, efficient and independent in accordance with article 298 tfeu. in amending the rules applicable to officials and other servants of the european communities, i emphasise the equal status of eu officials and temporary staff from the diplomatic services of the member states, in particular as regards eligibility to take up all posts on equivalent terms and the promotion of equal opportunities for the under-represented gender.
in writing. − the european external action service works in collaboration with the diplomatic services of the member states and is composed of officials from the relevant services of the general secretariat of the council and the commission and seconded staff from the national diplomatic services of the member states. the eeas should therefore be considered an institution of the union for the purposes of the staff regulations and the conditions of employment of other servants. officials of the european union and temporary staff from the diplomatic services of the member states should therefore have the same rights and duties and be treated equally, in particular as regards eligibility to take up all posts on equivalent terms. that is why the amendment proposed in this resolution is necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution because i agree that it is crucial that the eu can use all its external instruments within a coherent framework, and that the provision of budgetary resources in 2010 to establish this framework at its initial stage is the political aim of this report.
in writing. - the budgetary instruments need to be adapted to the new reality of the european external action service. i therefore believe that the efforts made to ensure that the appropriations for its powers are adequate, that its action is efficient and effective as intended and that its expenditure is effectively controlled are fully justified. the european institutions and the member states should pay particular attention to the early days of the european external action service in order to be able to monitor its activities and identify its main problems.
in writing. - this proposal for an amending budget is necessary in the context of the implementation of the treaty of lisbon, in order to make it possible to implement and operate the european external action service. it is therefore an initiative which i support and which it is important to ensure, within the principles of efficient management of european resources, emphasizing the good balance between cost and benefit, as well as the imperatives of budgetary restraint due to the impact of the economic crisis on public finances.
in writing. - our vote against this report, which represents a further step towards the establishment and operation of the european external action service (eeas), is consistent with our opposition to the creation of this service. a central point of the lisbon treaty and a cornerstone of federalism in the european union, it will involve more than 5 000 people in the future 130 eu embassies in countries around the world. a diplomatic mega-structure which will inevitably subordinate the representations and interests of the member states, placing, here too, the interests of the powers which have determined the course of the eu above them. moreover, the eeas's non-connection with military and intelligence structures is not guaranteed. the european union is not a military power, but a political power. the question is also, in a budget as extremely small as the eu's, where will the contributions to meet this expenditure come from? all this at a time when the effects of the crisis are being exacerbated by so-called austerity policies, when enormous pressure is being put on national budgets, when wages and social benefits are being cut and taxes on labour income are being increased.
in writing. - following the amendment of the staff regulations and an amendment to the financial regulation to incorporate the creation of the european external action service into these documents, it is now necessary to adopt a budget for its proper functioning. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a step in the right direction.

in writing. - having regard to the fact that the annual allocation for financial assistance for accompanying measures in the banana sector was eur 75 million in 2010, with the largest part of this financial assistance coming from a reallocation of heading 4 of the budget, which was eur 55.8 million, and that in 2011 this heading is only eur 875 530, agrees with the ep's proposal to invite the commission to submit a new proposal to mobilise the flexibility instrument for the remaining part of eur 74 124 470. this proposal is justified by the need for financial assistance for accompanying measures in the banana sector, especially if we consider that eu financial assistance to acp banana suppliers affected by the liberalisation resulting from the most favoured nation status in the wto must be guaranteed if the eu wishes to maintain its influence as a global player. it is also worth mentioning that it makes perfect sense to make this proposal viable, given that these measures are provided for in point 27 of the interinstitutional agreement on the use of the flexibility instrument.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution for agreeing that eu financial assistance to acp banana suppliers affected by the liberalisation resulting from the most favoured nation status in the wto should not be called into question and that the budgetary effort should not be delayed. i therefore support the commission's proposal to propose an amendment to regulation (ec, euratom) no 1905/2006 to enable the financing of accompanying measures in the banana sector for the years 2010 to 2013 with an overall budget of eur 190 million, and possibly an additional eur 10 million if the margins allow.
in writing. the commission proposes an amendment to regulation (ec, euratom) no 1905/2006 to finance the banana sector follow-up measures for the years 2010 to 2013 with an overall budget of eur 190 million. the proposed annual breakdown is eur 75 million in 2010. it should be noted that the margin available under heading 4 is only eur 875 530. the largest part of this financial assistance in 2010 comes from a reallocation within budget heading 4 (eur 55.8 million out of a total of eur 75 million) which concerns instruments and actions that the eu and, in particular, the european parliament have identified as being of high interest. moreover, the need for financial assistance linked to the accompanying measures in the banana sector was not foreseen when the current multiannual financial framework was adopted. however, eu financial assistance to acp banana suppliers affected by the liberalisation resulting from the most favoured nation (mfn) status in the wto should not be called into question and the budgetary effort should not be delayed. i therefore agree with the amendment to draft amending budget no 3/2010 as proposed by the rapporteur.
in writing. the report sets out the measures needed for financial assistance to acp countries which will be affected by the liberalisation of banana trade between the eu and 11 latin american countries, in which the eu commits not to apply quantitative restrictions or measures having equivalent effect to the importation of bananas into its territory. when the geneva agreement was signed, which provides for this liberalisation, the eu committed to channelling eur 200 million to the acp countries as compensation for the impact this measure would have on their exports to the eu. we criticised this agreement at the time, which will mainly benefit the us multinationals which dominate the world market in this sector. several acp countries and several acp banana producers expressed concern at the consequences of the agreement, considering that the eur 200 million would not compensate for all the impacts of the agreement. the report now foresees an overall budget of €190 million, and possibly an additional €10 million if margins allow. in addition, the impacts on eu banana producing countries and regions, such as the autonomous region of madeira, have not been adequately addressed. for these reasons we abstained from voting on the report.
in writing. - the eu has always been concerned with helping developing countries, particularly the acp countries. in the specific case dealt with in this draft amending budget, the acp banana-producing countries. this extraordinary aid comes as part of the liberalisation of banana trade between the eu and 11 latin american banana-producing countries. this form of aid is, in our opinion, better and more effective than direct aid with funds, to be applied without criteria. by helping the banana sector in these countries, we are helping them to develop their economies, create jobs and fight poverty.
in writing. - i welcome the draft budget for 2011, which is being discussed today, because it covers exactly the priorities set out. for the first time, parliament is on an equal footing with the council in these matters. this is the first budget since the treaty of lisbon. for this reason, and because of the crisis europe is going through, it will be important for the conciliation process to be successful. it is essential that the eu has a budget for the implementation of the priority areas and the new competences conferred by the treaty. it is important that we fight for our convictions and for a budget that is visionary in times of crisis. parliament's proposal reflects this ambition. the figures proposed by the council reflect the austerity of the budgets adopted at national level in the eu. however, the eu must have the capacity to react to policy changes brought about by major challenges. the eu has a duty to present an ambitious european budget that contributes to economic recovery. only by strengthening areas such as science and innovation, which contribute to economic growth and more and better jobs, can we make europe a more attractive place to live and work.
in writing. − against the backdrop of a fragile recovery in the euro area and weak public finances in many member states, a budget used wisely can stabilise and stimulate the recovery of the economy, although it must be used wisely. as regards citizens, there was an increase in the competitiveness heading for growth and jobs and also in the cohesion heading for growth and jobs, although there was a reduction in education and training. the committee stresses the need to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented in a timely manner and that the commission's proposals are implemented in a timely manner. in the field of regional development, there is an increase of 3.2%, which is considered to be fundamental. as regards agriculture, the extreme volatility of the dairy sector should be recalled, and the need for a permanent approach to tackling this issue, in particular through a milk fund, should be emphasised. as regards fisheries, there is a reduction in the amounts allocated to the cfp, which is regrettable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on agreeing with the ep's horizontal priorities for the 2011 budget, the areas of youth, education and mobility, which require, within the various policies, specific cross-sectoral investment as a means of promoting eu growth and development. i agree with the proposed increase in appropriations for all programmes related to these priorities, namely the lifelong learning, people and erasmus mundus programmes. i also agree that the employment mobility of young people is an essential instrument for ensuring the development of a competitive and dynamic labour market in europe and as such needs to be strengthened. i am in favour of increasing the appropriations for the european employment service and to this end i strongly support the launch of the preparatory action your first eures job, which aims to help young people to enter the labour market or to access skilled jobs in another member state as a first step towards a specific non-academic youth mobility programme.
in writing. − the community budget is essential for the development of the activities of the european union and, especially in times of crisis, for the effective allocation of funds relating to cohesion policy. i believe that the council should not arbitrarily reduce, as has been noted, priorities such as the money allocated to innovation, and with the objectives of growth and competitiveness. the council cut 0.55 per cent in commitment appropriations and 2.77 per cent in payment appropriations, approving a final budget of eur 141.8 billion for commitment appropriations and eur 126.5 billion for payment appropriations, which could be particularly critical if it impacts european growth and competitiveness. i therefore support the european parliament's maintaining the initial funds allocated to those areas.
in writing. - with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the distinction between compulsory expenditure (co) and non-compulsory expenditure (nce) has been abolished, meaning that the ep and the council are now jointly responsible for all eu expenditure, on which they decide jointly. in addition, the annual budgetary procedure becomes a special legislative procedure (the budget is adopted by means of a regulation) which may be considered a special codecision procedure or, to avoid confusion, a joint decision of the ep and the council. the 2011 budget that parliament is proposing is ambitious, smart, committed, rigorous and realistic. we have given priority to policies relating to youth, education, mobility, training, research, competitiveness and innovation. i would like to highlight the preparatory action your first eures job, in which i was personally involved, which will promote the mobility of young people in the european union and make it possible to combat unemployment. this budget still amounts to about 1% of gross national income. the need for revision of the multiannual financial framework is clearly demonstrated, given the low margins of its headings, and in particular headings 1a, 3b and 4. the urgency of the debate on the need for new own resources for the community budget is also clear.
in writing. − we share the criticism of the arbitrary cuts and reductions made by the council to the draft budget, leaving it some eur 7 billion below what was agreed in the 2007-13 multiannual financial framework (mff) for 2011. this is all the more unacceptable as the mff is already an extremely meagre figure, which compromises any objective of economic and social cohesion and thus accentuates the harmful effects of the policies pursued by the eu. we therefore share the view that a substantial budgetary review is absolutely necessary, as is an immediate review of the ceilings of the current mff. but we cannot accept that, on the basis of this fair criticism, the budget should be made more lisbon-like, as the report says, and kept in the service of the basic pillars of the lisbon treaty - neoliberalism, federalism and militarism - that is, in the service of the same policies which have generated the profound crisis facing the workers and peoples of europe today. what is needed, starting from the necessary strengthening of the community budget - on the basis of contributions from the member states in proportion to their gni - is a break with these policies and a genuine commitment to cohesion, social progress and the preservation of the environment.
in writing. − the entry into force of the tfeu has strengthened eu policies and created new areas of competence, including common foreign and security policy, competitiveness and innovation, space, tourism, the fight against climate change, social policy, energy policy, justice and home affairs. these new powers imply a budget to enable them to be implemented and therefore require all branches of the budgetary authority to be coherent and consistent with regard to increased financial capacity. we must therefore provide the community budget with the necessary funds to achieve the objectives set for 2014 so that the 2020 strategy is not compromised. it is true that in this crisis scenario, member states are resistant to increased co-financing, but they must be sensitive to the eu's intentions and the need not to call into question all that has already been achieved in terms of cohesion and integration.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on agreeing to the ep's horizontal priorities for the 2011 budget, in particular in the areas of youth, education and mobility, which require specific cross-sectoral investment, across the various policies, as a means of promoting eu growth and development. i agree with the proposed increase in appropriations for all programmes related to these priorities, namely the lifelong learning, people and erasmus mundus programmes. i also believe that the employment mobility of young people is an essential instrument for ensuring the development of a competitive and dynamic labour market in europe and as such needs to be strengthened. i am therefore in favour of increasing the appropriations for the european employment service and i strongly support the launch of the preparatory action your first eures job, which aims to help young people to enter the labour market or to access skilled jobs in another member state, as a first step towards a specific non-academic youth mobility programme.
in writing. - this is the first budget of the union to be voted in accordance with the rules of the lisbon treaty, with only one reading. although there are still some sensitive points left for conciliation, and they concern matters which i consider of the utmost importance, such as the allocation for cohesion and for agriculture, i welcome the proposal put forward. the adopted document restores the commission's initial proposal for the cohesion for growth and employment section, after the council had reduced the amount allocated. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i also welcome the appropriations allocated under the competitiveness for growth and employment heading, which includes the provision for financing most of parliament's proposals, such as those relating to smes and the youth, education and mobility programmes. i am voting in favour of the document, although it does not include the ppe's proposals for intervention measures on cereals, milk and milk products and powdered milk, which were unfortunately rejected by the agri committee.
in writing. - the extension of maternity leave from 14 to 20 weeks should be considered a fundamental right. this new period should not be seen as a threat, even in view of the introduction of parental rights. the consequences for the legislative framework of the various member states are not very significant, nor are they economic, if we consider for example the possibility of creating a temporary work grant at european level, which promotes professional mobility, which can stimulate the sharing of best practices and the continuation of the professional tasks of women on maternity leave. the guarantee of 100% monthly salary on maternity leave and the extension of the period of the ban on dismissal from six months to one year should not be called into question, taking into account demographic concerns reconciled with the current economic situation. other simple but important measures include the possibility of flexible working hours after maternity leave, preventive health and safety measures and the extension of these rights to couples adopting children, which favours a fairer legal framework.
in writing. − this proposal aims to improve the safety and health conditions associated with parenting. in this respect, i believe that we must reduce the disparities between men and women and promote a balanced reconciliation of professional life with family and private life. only then will there be the fostering of a parenting with shared responsibilities. on this basis, i believe that the extension of maternity leave to 20 weeks, of which 6 weeks must be after childbirth, as proposed by the rapporteur, is an appropriate period, with the possibility of sharing it between the parents. i also welcome the proposal in the document to guarantee full payment of the monthly salary during maternity leave, with the benefit being 100% of the last salary or the average monthly salary. finally, i think it is appropriate that the same measures should also be applied in cases of adoption of a child under 12 years of age and that they should also be aimed at self-employed women. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the report in plenary.
in writing. - i generally agree with the measures proposed in this report, as i consider this issue to be one of the most important challenges that europe will have to overcome in the coming decades: the ageing of the population. for example, in portugal, which i know better. but, like other countries in the union, the birth rate does not guarantee the renewal of generations and presents a harsh reality that jeopardizes the future. i believe that more flexible policies on maternity and paternity leave could help to reverse these trends. it is therefore important to send families a consistent message of support for motherhood and fatherhood, with concrete measures for a better reconciliation of work, private and family life. meeting this challenge is essential to achieve the economic and social objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and as a way of trying to reverse the demographic ageing of our continent. in portugal too, maternity leave is already paid at 100% for 120 days. i therefore support the idea of women being paid during maternity leave, as expressed in this report.
in writing. − the csd has long regarded the issue of births as a priority for the state and recognises that it is not possible to stimulate births without protecting parentality. it is not new that our programmes have chapters devoted to the family and birth. it is also not new that we defend the rights of mothers and fathers to form a family without this representing an increased burden or difficulties in work. family and birth-friendly policies, such as those we advocate, are, however, transversal and do not limit themselves to extending maternity leave (a measure we applaud, as we advocated in our 2009 government programme an extension to 6 months of parental leave). that is why we are pleased to see the ps in the european parliament standing with us in defence of mothers and fathers, a position which is so different from that which this party has in national politics, when it cuts in family allowances, in the sharing of medicines for chronic patients, in deductions from the irs for education and health expenditure or when it dramatically increases the tax burden on citizens, especially on families with children and lower incomes.
in writing. − the eu is facing a demographic challenge, characterised by low birth rates and a growing proportion of older people. improving work-life balance provisions helps to respond to this demographic decline. in portugal, the birth rate does not ensure the renewal of generations and reveals a reality that jeopardizes the future. i therefore believe that to counteract this trend, the improvement of the safety and health of pregnant, breastfeeding and lactating workers must be promoted, which means promoting a balanced reconciliation of working life with family and private life. i agree with the rapporteur's position and with the amendments introduced, such as the extension of the minimum period of maternity leave from 14 to 20 weeks; the principle of equal pay for equal work; the establishment of health and safety requirements at the workplace; and the ban on dismissals. i also agree that in the case of adoption, the right to a period of leave, shared between both members of the couple, should also be recognised.
in writing. - the positive vote on the report on improving the safety and health of pregnant workers, women who have recently given birth or who are breastfeeding at work is the culmination of a long process of discussion in the european parliament, which had already begun in the previous legislature and in which we actively participated by contributing to its adoption. although we are still at the first reading of the proposal for a directive, it is a positive sign in the area of women's rights, especially for those countries which do not yet have 20 weeks of fully paid maternity leave or which do not yet apply two weeks of fully paid paternity leave. the adoption of this proposal for negotiation with the council recognizes the fundamental social value of motherhood and fatherhood, in respect of the rights of working women who wish to assume motherhood. the adoption of this proposal also represents a victory over the more conservative positions that persist in this european parliament, which means that the fight will continue in defence of women's rights, maternity and paternity rights, the rights of the child. we now hope that the council will accept this position of the european parliament, which increases the european commission's proposal from 18 to 20 weeks and aims to amend the current directive still in force which only provides for 14 weeks of maternity leave.
in writing. the report adopted proposes a maternity leave of 20 weeks without loss of pay. this measure alone could represent a huge social improvement in the lives of women in about two thirds of the countries in the union. this is the case in portugal, where women are entitled to only 16 weeks of full pay. the inclusion of two weeks of paternity leave is also an important step in the fight for equality between women and men. more importantly, this report is adopted against the backdrop of the measures recently adopted as a result of austerity policies, which favour cutting public spending and reducing social rights. i hope that this report will thus contribute to strengthening labour and social rights in the union and in all the member states.
in writing. − there is consensus in the eu that one of its main problems is low population growth, in the face of low birth rates. so anything that helps to change this situation is very important. the protection of pregnant and breastfeeding women at work and the reduction of the disparities between men and women are important steps in this direction. despite the crisis we are going through, the measures adopted here today are very important to reverse, in the near future, the demographic downward trend facing the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposals for implementing measures to promote the improvement of the safety and health of pregnant workers, women who have recently given birth or are breastfeeding, including a 20-week maternity leave and a two-week paternity leave, both without reduction of pay. these are social measures which correspond to the europe we want to have, aimed at supporting births, the family, the health of babies, the employment of parents. it is, however, a project which is difficult to implement and which may perversely aggravate discrimination against women in the world of employment because: (1) it places additional pressure on social security systems which, in many cases, are already on the verge of sustainability; the new system of wage-setting is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women, and (2) it introduces new constraints on the labour market, which no longer meets the needs of the current working population. i am therefore afraid that these measures to support working parents will lead to an increase in unemployment and/or precarious work among young women. the negotiations between parliament and the council must be realistic and pragmatic, and also ambitious, if the future law is to be in line with the values of the proposal voted on in plenary this week.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because there is a great disparity in many countries as regards the conditions for paying companies, when the state, smes and large companies are involved. we know that in this situation of economic crisis and increased difficulties, companies are increasingly struggling with liquidity problems and are even at increased risk of bankruptcy in many member states. the directive which sought to regulate this matter had limited effects, so the proposal we have now adopted represents an important step forward in fixing and complying with payment deadlines, not only in relations between companies and public bodies but also in the relations which companies establish among themselves. we will now have legislation that makes it more effective to meet payment deadlines, with a clear system of penalties for delays and that also brings us an effective improvement in the balance of the abuse of a dominant position that the state and large companies often exercise over smes. this directive must now be transposed rapidly by the member states so that the serious problems caused by the introduction of long payment periods and delays in payments can finally be solved.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on combating late payment in commercial transactions, as it will allow the adoption of harmonised measures which, in the current economic crisis, may be particularly important for the performance of companies, in particular smes. however, i think it is good that a derogation system for the health sector is guaranteed.
in writing. − late payment is a problem with extremely serious consequences for the health of the world economy and whose impacts are particularly devastating for small and medium-sized enterprises. this is a reality of even more pernicious effects in this current period of economic and financial crisis. the bad example of the public administration, as is particularly the case in portugal, is unacceptable. measures to curb late payments in commercial transactions are needed to safeguard the health of the european economy, avoiding financial suffocation of productive structures and overburdening the use of financing products that increase dependence on the banking sector. i would like to draw attention to the particular case of agricultural producers, who often have to pay back payments owed to them by large areas and distributors. the maximum 30 days that can be waived up to a limit of 60 days for payment after service and invoicing is quite reasonable for the balance of trade relations and will be decisive for promoting a culture of timely fulfilment of commitments.
in writing. − late payment of commercial transactions, whether between companies or between companies and public entities, is responsible for cash flow difficulties in smes and in turn often contributes to further delays in payments, thus forming a vicious circle that is difficult to reverse. with the implementation of the new rules proposed here, we are convinced that an important step has been taken to put an end to this situation and thus help businesses to cope with this period of economic and financial crisis. the proposed sanctions are balanced and necessary and are expected to act as a deterrent to less correct commercial practices which have been adopted by commercial operators.
in writing. − the document makes a significant contribution to solving the problem of late payment in commercial transactions between companies or between companies and public entities. the initiative aims to improve the liquidity of european union companies through harmonisation. the fight against late payment is particularly welcome in the current crisis period, as long delays have a negative impact on business activities. the measure is intended to contribute to the proper functioning of the internal market by urgently reforming the time limit and the penalties to be applied in the event of non-compliance. in this context, i welcome the legislative proposal which has found broad support within the epp group, to which i belong, for the stipulation of a 30-day deadline as a general deadline for payments for transactions between companies and between companies and public bodies, with the latter being able to benefit, in exceptional cases, from 60 days. i also welcome the establishment of the applicable interest rate on the basis of the ecb reference rate plus 8% in late payment situations. in my view, this measure will be a strong incentive to economic activity for small and mediumsized enterprises, which are often blocked by the bureaucratic process and whose economic performance is seriously affected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because poverty is a very serious problem affecting 85 million of our fellow europeans and should not leave anyone indifferent. it demands to be placed at the top of our priorities and deserves a collective response that guarantees a minimum of dignity for those in situations of social fragility. poverty affects our young, our old, but also our working people in an increasing way. there has been a loss of 6 million jobs in the last 2 years alone and an increase in the insufficiency and precariousness of their wages, even when they are able to stay in their jobs. we need a systemic approach to tackle and solve its causes and the problems at its origin, but we cannot at the same time dispense with immediate and urgent responses to its consequences. that is why ensuring that those who are vulnerable in our society have a minimum income for their existence and providing them with urgent responses so that they can get out of this situation is not only a necessity but above all an imperative which we must subscribe to and which must be fulfilled within a framework of responsibility and demand.
in writing. − the current economic crisis has had a huge impact on the rise in unemployment and the unbridled acceleration of the impoverishment and social exclusion of people across europe. poverty and social exclusion have reached unacceptable levels, with some 80 million european citizens living below the poverty line, of whom 19 million are children (equivalent to almost 2 in 10 children) and many others facing serious obstacles in terms of access to employment, education, housing and social and financial services. unemployment levels have also reached unprecedented levels in all member states, with a european average of 21.4%, with 1 in 5 young people unemployed. this situation is unacceptable and we must do everything in our power to help resolve the drama these people are living through. in this context, 2010 was designated the european year for combating poverty, with the aim of reinforcing the eu's political commitment to take action with a decisive impact on poverty eradication. i agree with the need for a minimum income in each member state, accompanied by a strategy for social reintegration and access to the labour market.
in writing. - not being insensitive to the very serious consequences of the current crisis for citizens, creating and/or aggravating the poverty situation of many europeans, i do not agree with the state-oriented view that seeks to solve this problem with more social benefits, in this case a minimum income, established at european level. more social benefits require more money from the state, which can only be achieved, since the state does not create wealth, by increasing its tax revenue. that means more taxes on everyone, making everyone poorer and more dependent on that same bloodsucking state. the fight against poverty must be fought on the side of employment policies and economic competitiveness. if portugal did not see several companies closing every week, it would not see so many portuguese people unemployed and in poverty. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. as i said in this plenary session a year ago, i am in favour of a new concept of sociality within the european union, capable of ensuring a minimum standard of living for every citizen. in a social, just, developed and cohesive europe, it is urgent to ensure that measures are taken to eliminate and minimise the risks of social dumping and the deterioration of the living conditions of citizens in the face of the devastating effects of the current economic crisis. for a stronger and more united europe, we must ensure that the basic rights of citizens are protected throughout the european union. i believe that minimum standards are needed in the areas of health, education, social pensions and even the level of pay, ensuring greater uniformity in terms of employment conditions. in the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion, i welcome this report as a contribution to encouraging all member states to fulfil their responsibilities for active inclusion by correcting social inequalities and marginalisation. i stress the need for a realistic balance and respect for the principle of subsidiarity. i therefore vote in favour of this report and against the proposed amendments.
in writing. - i would stress the importance of the adoption of this report, for which i was responsible in the european parliament's plenary, proposing the introduction of minimum income schemes in all eu member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament. as the report says, 'the introduction of minimum income schemes in all eu member states consisting of specific measures to support people (children, adults and the elderly) with insufficient income, through a financial contribution, and guaranteeing access to essential public services is the most effective way to combat poverty, ensure an adequate standard of living and promote social integration'. the resolution adopted calls for minimum income schemes to be set at at least 60% of the median income in the member state concerned, urges the commission to draw up an action plan to accompany the implementation of a european initiative on minimum income in the member states, draws attention to the growing poverty of workers and the need to respond to this new challenge, insisting on a fair distribution of income.
in writing. − the indication of the application of the minimum income in all countries of the european union is a key measure for the fight against poverty. i therefore vote in favour of this important report. the minimum income is, however, calculated on a country-by-country basis and does not therefore contribute to social convergence in the european area. in the context of the crisis we are living in, it maintains national inequalities. more convergent social policies are therefore needed at european level for a fairer distribution of wealth. this is an important role for the eu.
in writing. − states cannot be insensitive to situations of extreme poverty and must ensure that no one is left to their own devices in situations which are often deeply degrading. so extraordinary, exceptional support in these strict cases must be considered. however, experiments in the allocation of minimum incomes, such as the portuguese one, without any really effective monitoring, and with a huge number of people registered as beneficiaries, but who could and should work, without doing so, without even trying, are a perversion of logic that must be considered. i therefore vote against the motion because the aspects of the system's sound supervision which i have described call it into question from the point of view of both financial feasibility and moral considerations.

in writing. - poverty is one of the biggest social problems in the world, to which the eu is unfortunately not immune. the long-running financial and economic crisis in which we are living has further aggravated the poverty of europeans, creating in some countries, such as portugal, a new wave of poor people who used to belong to what is commonly known as the middle class. the allocation of a minimum income is an important social measure, with a significant impact also on the economic level and expressing what many interpret as a moral obligation. it is important that this minimum income be regulated in such a way that it constitutes a lever to guide the poor to an acceptable standard of living and that it can never constitute an incentive to passivity in the face of a difficult situation, including the possibility of lack of commitment in the search for a job.
in writing. - the economic crisis has exacerbated social inequalities within the eu. at the end of 2008, some 17% of the european population, or 85 million people, were living below the poverty line. the effects of the crisis, including the increase in unemployment and the decline in job opportunities, have left many people in a difficult situation. it is essential that europe engages in the promotion of a more inclusive society through poverty eradication measures. 2010 is the 'european year for combating poverty and social exclusion' and the eu 2020 strategy sets the target of reducing by 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty. the truth is that the level of poverty affects not only social cohesion but also the economy. so, and in view of parliament's commitment to contribute to the fight against poverty and social exclusion, i consider the minimum income scheme based on 60% of the median income of the respective state to be an important contribution to social inclusion. for these reasons, and because i consider that the document highlights the need for concrete action to achieve more effective social and economic cohesion, while respecting subsidiarity, i voted in favour.

on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, i have to say that i fully understand the situation in pakistan, but i would like to say that this decision is tragic for europe and particularly for some countries which are already experiencing great difficulties, such as portugal, spain or greece. for example, the textile and clothing industry accounts for 11% of total portuguese exports, 22% of manufacturing employment and, for some products, 80% of production is even made in portugal. and so these 80%, diluted perhaps in the 27 of europe, may mean little to the european commission, but to portugal they mean a great deal. europe cannot demand from these countries very violent measures, which are self-evident, to control public accounts and contain the deficit, and at the same time take decisions that strike at the productive heart and the capacity to create wealth and to maintain jobs in these very countries. this decision, i must say, also breaks the normal market rules in ways that are not conceivable. i do not advocate any market protectionism, but i do call for the uncompromising defence of its good rules, a healthy market and a fair market. they understand that this decision will allow products manufactured in pakistan to enter europe at a cost price below that which is possible for our companies, simply because they are not required to produce under the same conditions. and this, i'm very sorry to say, is called unfair competition. unfair competition. pakistani companies have no social costs to their workers, no environmental protection costs, no particular concerns in combating a reality of child labour, no equivalent restrictions on the use of raw materials for public health reasons. i would even ask: how is it possible to take such a radical decision without first presenting a detailed and accurate report on its negative impact in the various countries? there are, however, consequences which i can already anticipate, and those consequences are the closure and bankruptcy of companies in the european union, particularly in portugal, and the increase in the number of their unemployed. you better have the right idea, because somebody else is going to have to take responsibility for that, too. and, at the very least, if you take this proposal as inevitable - because there will be those who have it - at least, please, anticipate some things that are not contemplated at this time. for example, the setting of the quota limit, as is provided for ethanol but not for textiles. the waiver for a maximum of one year, because if aid is temporary... in three years, believe me, no european company can stand in direct competition with pakistani companies. i'm finished, madam president. and, by the way, a provision on raw materials, so that pakistan itself does not prevent european companies from accessing these raw materials in order to benefit from this production itself.
for the gue/ngl group on the one hand, we have large european importers who profit from the entry of pakistani products into europe. on the other hand, we have another small number of large pakistani textile factories, which happen to be located in territories outside the disaster areas, which also benefit greatly from this commission proposal. this is the reality. the winners are not the sick, not the homeless, not the children, not the elderly who have lost their homes. the big businessmen win. and what is being done here is the instrumentalisation of catastrophe, the instrumentalisation of extreme weather events, for the realization of big business. that is what is absolutely intolerable in the proposal that is being made by the commission. you better be scratching your way through.

mr president, the impact of a large number of sectoral activities and policies on the marine environment, from fisheries to maritime transport, tourism, energy, science and technology and others, calls for an integrated policy which promotes a beneficial interrelation of all these areas within a framework of sustainability of the marine environment and preservation of their ecosystems, because in this interrelation local and regional specificities have a decisive weight and because it is also at this level that the effects of this integrated policy will be expressed. it is also at this level that the definition of the sea, rather than its mere implementation, must be carried out, involving the coastal communities that interact with, animate and depend on the marine environment, without forgetting the necessary overall vision and the essential articulation and cooperation that arise from the fact that the oceans and seas are interconnected and interdependent. any community initiative in this area should safeguard the sovereignty and competence of the member states over their territorial waters and exclusive economic zones and, at the same time, contribute to the development of the resources therein as part of their endogenous potential and their comparative advantages. a comprehensive vision of an integrated maritime policy should include, among other things, the promotion of marine research and development and marine technology and engineering in its various aspects, including shipbuilding the promotion of environmentally more sustainable maritime transport and port infrastructure in the context of its public management, the enhancement of fisheries by ensuring the modernisation of the sector and its environmental sustainability and socioeconomic viability, adequate and autonomous financing that does not draw resources from the european fisheries fund and, finally, the role and special characteristics of the outermost regions.
mr president, commissioner, the oceans and seas cover 70% of the planet's surface, they have been the cradle of life and, throughout human history, have been a source of food through fishing and a means of communication between peoples and cultures through maritime trade. this is where the concept of traditional maritime activities, fishing and transport originated. the sea is now taking on a new role in the global context as a geostrategic and geopolitical arena that gives europe a central role. in addition, we are now living in the so-called period of new uses for the oceans, with the exploitation of their energy, mineral and genetic resources, which, along with fishing and maritime transport, require a holistic approach and concerted action, which mrs meissner has also tried to portray, and for which i warmly congratulate her. the planning of european maritime space and its uses is fundamental for the european union, especially for coastal regions and even more so for the outermost regions. in order for the pmi to be a whole greater than the sum of its parts, and in this case the fisheries sector, it is imperative that this activity be represented in the maritime clusters so that, in a synergistic way, they can combine their will and overcome difficulties arising from overlapping interests in the use of maritime space. in this context, the protection of the most ecologically sensitive marine biogeographical regions and the promotion of sustainable fishing, with the use of increasingly selective fishing gear, is an imperative for achieving the goals set at the 2002 johannesburg summit. e creation of cross-sectoral policy instruments covering the different sectors of the various maritime activities, defending their respective requirements and specificities in terms of the use of the maritime domain, should therefore be ensured. protecting the oceans is a moral obligation we have to ourselves and to future generations.
