in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide in the framework of the legislative proposal on the mid-term review of the development cooperation instrument (dci) and the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr), for which the commission proposes only a technical amendment to allow the costs of fees, charges and other charges relating to the financing of actions covered by the dci and the eidhr in the beneficiary countries to be financed by the budgets of the instruments. whereas the cdi and the edf were the only financial instruments not to provide for an exception to the principle of non-eligibility of such costs, in the case of edf projects this is of particular importance given the special conditions under which they are carried out. i therefore believe that the commission's legislative proposal for the mid-term review of the emcdda provides the ideal opportunity to ensure that this instrument meets the new requirements laid down in the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. - i vote in favour of all the proposals in this report. the emcdda, as a financial instrument aimed at promoting the development and consolidation of democracy and the rule of law and contributing to respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms in third countries, is an important vehicle for union assistance in the field of rights, freedoms and guarantees. the legislative proposal for the mid-term review of the emcdda launched by the commission provides an appropriate opportunity to review the legal basis of this instrument, ensuring that it now complies with the new requirements laid down in the treaty on the functioning of the eu. in particular, the procedure for delegated acts, provided for in article 290 tfeu, which significantly strengthens parliament's powers by granting it a right of veto, obliges the commission to submit an amended proposal for acts adopted in co-decision.
in writing. - as with the amendment to regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation and regulation (ec) no 1889/2006 establishing a financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide contained in the resolution following the report by mr gay mitchell, this resolution also takes on board the need to carry out a legislative amendment of an eminently technical nature and of the same nature. i believe that the european union should continue to give the defence and promotion of democracy and human rights a central place, not only in its discourse but above all in its political practice, and that to this end it is absolutely necessary and even urgent to do so in coordination with the united states of america.
in writing. − the financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide is another very important argument for strengthening the eu's capacity to respond to crisis situations or emerging crises. as the world's largest donor of external aid and responsible for more than half of official development assistance, the eu needs instruments to enable it to address crisis situations, taking into account the eu's horizontal and geographical objectives and priorities, while making these actions complementary to the community's geographical policies and objectives and instruments. when it comes to development, the eu's objectives must be to combat poverty and its causes. in the case of this instrument, the legislative proposal is concerned only with a technical amendment which will make it possible to make this instrument more flexible in the implementation of programmes and projects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the financing instrument for cooperation with industrialised and other high-income countries and territories (ici regulation) which aims to support economic, financial and technical cooperation as well as academic and research exchange in the areas of community competence, because i consider that the changes proposed by the commission are substantial, since all the current references to partner countries (which, so far, only covered industrialised and high-income countries and territories), including their qualitative assessment, should now also include the listed developing countries. this broadening of geographical coverage is an opportunity, as programmes currently funded under the ici regulation can now be extended to other countries. however, this is also a greater challenge. i therefore think it is important to make it quite clear to whom this funding can be granted, for what purpose and under what conditions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution because i consider it to be in the union's interest to continue to deepen its relations with developing countries, particularly in the fields of economic, commercial, academic, business and scientific exchanges. the community therefore needs a financial instrument to finance these measures. moreover, with the extension of the geographical coverage of regulation (ec) no 1934/2006, the developing countries covered are now the subject of two separate external policy financial instruments and it is important to ensure that these two financial instruments remain strictly separate.
in writing. - i believe it is essential that europe establishes strong relations with certain regional and global actors, supporting them and establishing strong political and economic links. i would like to mention in particular two countries with which portugal has strong historical and emotional ties, brazil and angola, two important global players in south america and africa respectively, which the eu should increasingly look to as partners. given that the main general objective of regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 is to eradicate poverty through the achievement of the millennium development goals, cooperation is essentially limited to the financing of measures designed to meet the criteria applicable to official development assistance (oda) as established. this often excludes other types of action which do not fall within the scope of oda but which are nevertheless essential in the context of the union's external policy. it is precisely to regulate such practices which involve economic, commercial, academic, business and scientific agreements and exchanges with developing countries that it is proposed that this regulation be adopted.
in writing. − the financing instrument for cooperation with industrialized countries and territories is a financing instrument for cooperation with industrialized and other high-income countries and territories. it aims to support economic, financial and technical cooperation as well as academic and research exchanges. the aim of this regulation is to extend the scope of this instrument substantially to include cooperation with developing countries, and the overall financial framework should be increased to this end. the geographical extension proposed here is an opportunity to take the programmes to new countries, but it also represents a great challenge, so it is very important to make it quite clear to whom this funding can be granted, for what and under what conditions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution because i consider it to be in the union's interest to continue to deepen its relations with developing countries, particularly in the fields of economic, commercial, academic, business and scientific exchanges. the community needs a financial instrument to finance these measures. moreover, with the extension of the geographical coverage of regulation (ec) no 1934/2006, the developing countries concerned are now covered by two separate external policy financial instruments and it is important to ensure that these two financial instruments remain strictly separate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution, but i consider that the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council, by drastically reducing the margin for heading 4 of the 2007-13 multiannual financial framework (mff), does not leave enough room for manoeuvre to deal with and react appropriately to a potential coming crisis.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the general proposals contained in this report. i think that the role of the european parliament is eminently political in the face of the commission's proposal to set up a monitoring programme for the acp banana-producing countries. i also believe that this programme can only be legitimated by a paradigm shift from a purely commercial perspective to a more comprehensive and integrated vision such as that of development and the fight against poverty (the number one target of the mdgs). since the conclusion of eu-acp preferential agreements is incompatible under the agreements signed between the eu and the wto and the positive results in the acp banana-producing countries of previous preferential agreements have been demonstrated, it is necessary to support the adaptation, reorganisation and competitiveness of the banana exporting sector in these countries. in a broad sense, these accompanying measures for the banana sector should have a positive impact not only on producers, the first link in the production chain, but also on the criteria for combating poverty. the whole chain will thus be able to enjoy acceptable living conditions and easier access to markets.
in writing. − economic, financial and technical cooperation, as well as academic and research exchanges between the union and third countries, is one of the priorities of european foreign policy and efforts in this direction should be supported. the amendment proposed by the commission extends the scope of the regulation to a large number of developing countries. as the rapporteur makes clear in his explanatory statement, this change is an opportunity, but it is also a major challenge to the proper use of this instrument, which may lose in coherence what it has gained in scope. this enlargement requires additional funding and, at the same time, an even more careful and rigorous allocation of resources, otherwise it would scatter resources which could be mobilised for meaningful and fruitful cooperation projects.
in writing. - the reasons for our abstention in this report are the same as those for voting on the report on the budgetary review to establish financial assistance for the acp countries, which will be affected by the liberalisation of banana trade between the eu and eleven latin american countries. this liberalization will mainly benefit the us multinationals which dominate the world market in this sector. as for the acp countries, as several of their representatives have already stated, including some local producers, the amount of eur 200 million which the eu proposes to allocate to them is not likely to offset all the impacts of these measures. the question therefore arises: what are the grounds for the impact assessment carried out by the commission following the signing of the geneva agreement? once again, the eu's proclaimed development policy objectives, particularly poverty reduction, are subordinated to the commercial interests of its economic groups. unfortunately, the claim that the aim is to improve the standard of living and the living conditions of the people in the banana growing areas and value chains, in particular small farmers and small entities, has little practical meaning.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the indication of the country of origin on certain products imported from third countries, as i considered it important to provide consumers with correct information enabling them to exercise their freedom of choice. european consumers have the right to know where the products they buy come from so that they can make informed choices.
in writing. − if there is one area in which the eu has been successful, it is in protecting consumers' rights by imposing rules that defend their rights and ensure that they are sufficiently informed to exercise their freedom of choice in conscience. this was one of the standards to which the european consumer had become accustomed and to which european producers had adapted. so, for the sake of transparency, consumer protection, but also protection for european producers, it is essential that goods imported from third countries are correctly identified as such, giving account of their origin. i'll even go further: if europe is so restrictive in the rules it imposes on its producers - for example, the rules for animal husbandry - it should only allow the import of products which comply with those same rules, otherwise it would be allowing low-cost products, made in breach of all community rules, to enter the market and thus unfairly compete with the european product, which is much more expensive to produce and/or manufacture.
in writing. - our vote in favour of the indication of the country of origin on certain products imported from third countries is based on the need to clarify the route taken by the products to reach the eu countries. further action is needed, given that this indication alone, without the accompanying measures, will have a very limited impact. but a break with the current wto guidelines is a priority to allow countries to give priority to the development of their production and their market, with controls on imported goods, imposing minimum quality and technical criteria equal to those required of companies within the eu, combating dumping, effective regulation of capital markets, penalizing business relocations, taxing financial transactions and ending tax havens. the establishment of more equitable and fairer economic relations, at the service of peoples and countries, supporting development and cooperation based on equality between states and building alliances and agreements with countries from all continents, is necessary to combat deep social injustices and inequalities, hunger, disease and poverty.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'produced in' in the labelling of foodstuffs. the community economy needs to be strengthened by improving the competitiveness of eu industry in the world economy. we can only have fair competition if it works with clear rules for producers, exporters and importers, taking account of common social and environmental considerations. this regulation is therefore an important step towards eu consumers finally having the same rights as millions of consumers worldwide. although this rule cannot yet be applied to all products imported into the eu, we must nevertheless continue to develop towards the point where all imported products must bear their indication of origin.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the indication of the country of origin on certain products imported from third countries, considering that consumers have the right to know the origin of the products they buy in order to be able to make an informed choice. this is all the more necessary as we know that in today's globalised world, external trade is increasingly borderless, and it is therefore important to ensure that the origin of products circulating in the eu and beyond is clearly identified. this can also be an important step towards more detailed labelling of various products in order not only to guarantee consumer rights more fully but also to ensure reciprocity in the production requirements imposed on community and non-community producers.
in writing. − the potential of the single market cannot be fully exploited without the support of a modern standardisation system. in this sense, the implementation of the european standardisation system (ess), which must be emancipated, has been fundamental to the completion of the single market, in particular through its ability to respond to the growing need for standards capable of guaranteeing product safety for consumers, ease of access, environmental protection or innovation. i believe that european standardisation is an important means of promoting innovation and r & d, thus contributing to the competitiveness of the union. in this particular case, the european framework programmes for innovation and r & d can be a valuable input in the standardisation process. i also believe that european standardisation contributes to creating a level playing field for all market players, especially smes and micro-enterprises, which are so important in the dynamics of the european economy. however, i believe that the union and the member states should take greater account of the interests of smes in the development of standards, since their participation in the standardisation process is often different from their weight and importance in the european economy. i therefore vote in favour of the proposals in this report.
in writing. − when the commission expresses its willingness to review the european standardisation system, it is essential to recognise the contribution it has made to the protection of european consumers and the internal market. like the rapporteur, i believe that the revision of the european standardisation system must build on the strengths of the existing system, which constitute a solid basis for improvement, while avoiding radical changes that could undermine the system's fundamental values. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take action to combat fraud. this will be a discussion to be followed with interest.
in writing. the european standardisation system has been instrumental in the achievement of the single market. it has played a key role in responding to the growing need in european policy and legislation for standards that ensure product safety, ease of access, innovation, interoperability and environmental protection. however, european standardisation to meet the future needs of businesses and consumers and to realise its full potential benefits for public and social objectives must adapt to the challenges posed by globalisation, climate change, the emergence of new economic powers and technological developments. it is therefore necessary to develop a strategic approach to european standardisation and to review the current system in order to ensure that it can continue to be successful and meet the needs of the next decade, enabling europe to maintain its leadership in the global standardisation system.
in writing. − the standardisation process plays a significant role in ensuring the quality of public or private products and services, as well as compliance with safety, environmental and social responsibility standards. this report seeks to involve smes and the various social actors in the standardisation process. it promotes the sharing of information on new regulations and encourages the dissemination of these processes on clear, simple and user-friendly information websites available in all the official languages of the european union. i have, however, some reservations about the genuine representation of all the social partners in the standardisation processes and also about the financing process of the european standardisation system. i'm voting for it.
in writing. - moldova has made a positive convergence with european standards of freedom, democracy and good governance and an apparent willingness to continue this effort, which i cannot but welcome. the forthcoming electoral period will be a major test of the strength of its institutions and its democratic culture. despite the positive indications, it must be remembered that many issues remain unresolved, including the many issues of transnistria, which threaten its stability and progress. i hope that the union can make a strong contribution towards a lasting solution to this problem.
in writing. − having regard to the outcome of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) and the eastern partnership launched in may 2009 which recognise the european aspirations of the republic of moldova and the importance of moldova as a country with deep historical, cultural and economic ties to the member states of the european union, i welcome the progress made by the republic of moldova in the past year and am confident that the electoral process can further consolidate democratic institutions and respect for the rule of law and human rights in moldova. i hope that the moldovan authorities will carry out the necessary reforms and fulfil their commitments to keep the republic of moldova on the path of firm european integration. i also highlight the start of negotiations on the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on 12 january 2010 and underline the good results that the commission is obtaining from the republic of moldova in this process.
in writing. - once again, the majority in parliament is trying to interfere in the internal affairs of a country, openly taking the side of the forces in moldova that harbour the interests of eu economic groups, undermining the independence and sovereignty of this country and the expressed will of its people. the council also welcomed the progress made by the republic of moldova in the past year and called on the authorities to carry out the necessary reforms and to honour the commitments made to keep the country on the path towards european integration. what is not said is that power in moldova is the result of a coalition formed following a genuine constitutional coup, which used a series of provocative and destabilising manoeuvres to bring the communist party, which had won the elections, to power. and that this same coalition, once in power, has initiated a disturbing anti-communist and anti-democratic escalation, in a clear move to discredit the communist party. the majority of the ep's position shows its deep anti-communist character and its hypocrisy when it comes to defending democracy, the rule of law and human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint resolution because, in the face of the elections scheduled for 28 november 2010, and in view of the sectarian attempts by the right-wing forces to promote the banning of the names and symbols of their main left-wing opponents, it is important to stress the need for the elections to be held in strict compliance with international standards, giving equal opportunities to all political forces. i also think it is important to reiterate support for the territorial integrity of the republic of moldova and to underline the role that the eu can and must play in helping to build a solution to the transnistrian problem.
in writing. − moldova has been making efforts over the past few years to increasingly converge with european benchmarks of freedom, democracy and good governance. the efforts outlined here have been consistent and have demonstrated that moldova is concerned about continuing its path towards possible enlargement. moldova will soon face an election period which will be a good test of the degree of consolidation of its democratic culture as well as its institutions. despite all the positive aspects already mentioned, there are still some issues which must be dealt with positively, in particular the transnistria issue, which may in some way cause some instability. the eu must continue to make every effort to ensure that the reforms that have been implemented in moldova continue on track.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the integrated maritime policy (imp) as regards the assessment of progress made and the new challenges because i believe that the eu needs concrete measures to mobilise the maritime economy by encouraging and promoting the economic potential of maritime clusters, in particular in the member states and in regions with a large exclusive economic zone, such as portugal and the azores. i believe that smart growth, as envisaged in strategy 2020, can only be achieved if the different potentials contained in european diversity are mobilised in an intelligent way. i therefore consider the strengthening of the integrated maritime policy to be very important in order to promote economic growth and the creation of new sustainable jobs in maritime regions, to protect marine ecosystems and, in particular, to encourage the exchange of best practices.
in writing. - it is important that the eu ensures the protection of its coasts. the legislation in force must also improve safety in oil exploration and extraction. the european maritime safety agency, based in lisbon, provides support and technical assistance in the development and implementation of community legislation on maritime safety and security and in the area of pollution caused by ships. in june this year i put in writing to commissioners oettinger, kallas and georgieva the suggestion that the european maritime agency's powers should be extended to create mechanisms for monitoring the safety of european oil platforms in the north sea, the black sea and the mediterranean and to be responsible for preventing environmental disasters linked to oil exploration. this suggestion allows for economies of scale in terms of financial, human and technical resources. i welcome the commissioners' response, which has shown an openness to revising the regulation of the european maritime agency, extending its powers to deal with incidents of marine pollution. i would like to ask the commission to extend the powers of the european maritime safety agency to ensure the protection of our coasts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on an integrated maritime policy because i believe that it should promote greater coherence between the various policy sectors, so that the potential of the seas and the maritime sector can be used in an ecological, economically sustainable and effective way.
in writing. - the eu has 320 000 km of coastline, with one third of its citizens upward trending living on the coastline. our economic activities at sea and on the coast produce 40% of the eu's gdp, and according to all forecasts, there is still a great deal of untapped development potential. in fact, 40% of intra-european trade and 95% of extra-european exports take place by sea. the rapporteur sums up in one sentence the importance of the sea for europe. as a portuguese, i know it well. it is also as a portuguese, a people who have always turned to the sea and found prosperity and wealth in it, that i consider it essential that europe has a maritime policy that allows it to take advantage of all the potential that the sea has, as an economic and energy resource, as a creator of jobs and wealth and as a driver of competitiveness and innovation. i would particularly like to stress the concern about environmental disasters at sea - i am reminded of the prestige case which occurred just off the northern coast of portugal - and the need for stricter rules to prevent them in european seas.
in writing. − the sea provides important trade routes, acts as a climate regulator and is a source of food, energy and resources. in the 21st century, the sea has assumed a new identity and has assumed a geostrategic and geopolitical importance unparalleled in human history. today, more than ever, it is a key factor for europe. europe must take advantage of this centrality. member states such as portugal have to take advantage of their relationship with the sea and the size of their exclusive economic zone, which in the case of portugal is one of the largest in the world. the european union concentrates around 40% of its gdp and 40% of its population in maritime regions. the direct turnover of the maritime tourism sector in europe was estimated at eur 72 billion in 2004. some 90% of europe's external trade and almost 40% of its internal trade pass through its ports. i therefore advocate an ambitious blue growth strategy, and for this the commission should present a global and cross-sectoral strategy, based on a broad research of policy options and potential and a broad consultation of stakeholders, for sustainable growth in coastal regions and maritime sectors by 2012.
in writing. − the report presents an overview of the imp linked to the eu's external policy objectives. we disagree with this approach and with several other aspects of the report, such as the insistence on the creation of a european coastguard, in a federalist line which disrespects the sovereignty and powers of the member states over their territorial waters and exclusive economic zones. we reject the proposal to introduce market economy instruments such as emissions trading schemes in the maritime sector - mechanisms which, even without applying to the maritime sector, have already proven ineffective in achieving the environmental objectives they claim to pursue. but we recognize the positive aspects it contains, such as: the proposal to include in international forums and agreements the improvement of working conditions at sea, the safety and environmental performance of ships; the proposal to implement the ilo maritime labour convention in community law; the enhancement of maritime freight transport; the preservation of small and secondary ports; the expansion of the short sea transport network; the importance attached to improving links to the outermost regions. it also proposes that marine sciences be given greater importance in the 8th framework programme for research.
in writing. - an integrated maritime policy is essential to make the most of the immense wealth that the sea provides us with, as well as all the economic potential that exists there. we must not forget that our economic activities at sea and on the coast produce 40% of the eu's gdp, and yet, according to various studies, there is still a great deal of untapped development potential. in fact, 40% of intra-european trade and 95% of extra-european exports take place by sea. despite these figures and the enormous potential that still remains to be exploited, there is no integrated european maritime policy which would allow us to avoid treating separately the policies pursued in the fields of maritime transport, the maritime economy, new technologies, coastal regions, offshore energy, fisheries, surveillance and maintenance of law and order at sea, tourism, protection of the marine environment and marine research. this motion for a resolution is intended to help to change the present situation.
in writing. - to date, policies in the fields of maritime transport, the maritime economy, new technologies, coastal regions, offshore energy, fisheries, maritime surveillance, tourism, protection of the marine environment and marine research have evolved separately. an individual approach often leads to contradictory measures and to situations of conflict and mismatch. an integrated approach is therefore desirable, including a governance framework with all decision-making levels on the one hand and all cross-sectoral sectors and instruments on the other. in the context of coordinated planning of activities, i support the request to the commission to draw up strategies for sea basins which take account of the specificities of the regions and exploit their strengths. this would be a good proposal for the case of the outermost regions, such as madeira, as it would allow the region to take advantage of its activities linked to the sea and create synergies with the activities of the other regions of the sea basin in which it is integrated. the outermost regions also give the european union, through its maritime territory, the largest exclusive economic zone in the world, which highlights the importance of maritime and sea-related activities in these regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on eu trade relations with latin america because they must be a priority for the eu. the eu is currently latin america's second most important trading partner and the main trading partner of mercosur and chile. european trade policy must also play an important role in achieving the millennium development goals, as well as international commitments related to human rights, food security and environmental sustainability.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty defines the eu's trade policy as an integral part of the union's overall external action. recently, there has been a decline in eu-lac trade due to the increasing share of asian countries in the external trade of lac, despite the fact that the eu remains latin america's second largest trading partner. although the association agreements between the european union on the one hand and mexico and chile on the other have led to a substantial increase in the volume of trade, mexico's trade with europe remains modest compared with that with the united states. i therefore support the need for both sides to develop a wider range of economic activities in trade. the bulk of lac imports from the eu are now industrial products (over 85%). in turn, more than 40% of the region's exports to the eu are commodities. it is therefore necessary to mobilise resources and technical assistance to identify and finance programmes that provide local and regional production opportunities and sustainable access to global markets for excluded communities and small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - we did not vote in favour of this report because of its contradictions. although it does have some positive aspects in relation to the new realities in latin america, several of its paragraphs are unacceptable. for example, we highlight, on the positive side, the recognition that all countries have the right to create the necessary mechanisms to defend their food security and to ensure the survival and development of small and medium-sized producers. but, however, at another point it says exactly the opposite when it says: regrets the protectionist measures taken during the financial crisis by some latin american countries, in particular argentina; calls on the commission to address the issue of market access with latin american countries on a regular basis. or when it says deeply concerned about the restrictive measures recently adopted by the argentine authorities on food products imported from third countries, including the european union. the support for the liberalization of international trade, which is apparent in some of its proposals, is also unacceptable, although there are still differences of opinion on other points.
in writing. − as the eu is latin america's largest investor and second largest trading partner, and also the largest provider of development aid, we believe that these data are sufficient to have a clear and well-defined strategy for eu-latin america trade relations. we call for clear guidelines on how best to work together to promote political stability, combat climate change, manage migration flows and prevent natural disasters. a good way to provide the aid that latin america needs is to boost trade relations between the two blocs, which, if they are established, will be among the most important in the world. however, we must not forget the outermost regions of europe which may be affected by the import of certain agricultural products, in particular the portuguese region of madeira in respect of banana imports. we must find a balanced agreement which will enable the latin american countries to develop, but which at the same time will not be detrimental to the various economic sectors of some member states, especially the agricultural and livestock sectors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 21 october 2010 on eu trade relations with latin america, as i believe that the free market stimulates the world economy and can be an important factor for development in latin american countries. i do, however, believe that the mandate given to the european commission to conduct the negotiation process should be reviewed because it is already too old and inappropriate to the present circumstances in which the negotiations will take place. in this review there would certainly be an opportunity to stress the need to carry out studies prior to the conclusion of agreements on their impact on the european productive fabric and in particular on agriculture, and a strong position should also be taken to ensure that agricultural products are no longer allowed to continue to serve as a bargaining chip for commercial advantages at other levels.
in writing. − the european common commercial policy is an integral and relevant part of the union's overall external action and can play a very positive role in the objectives of wealth creation and in economic and political relations between the peoples and countries of the european and latin american areas. i have no doubt that deeper integration in economic areas can bring benefits to both sides, particularly in terms of creating more and better jobs. however, i am aware of the effects that the bilateral trade agreements that have been concluded between the european union and the countries of latin america may have on the economies of the outermost regions. in my own region, madeira, the consequences are particularly visible in the banana production sector. i therefore advocate that this production sector and the other strategic and traditional sectors in the outermost regions be preserved. to this end, and in accordance with the european union's commitment to its outermost regions, they should be adequately compensated and their vulnerable economies given special attention. the protection of these regions is covered by this document and i am voting in favour of it.

in writing. it is essential and urgent to conclude a general and comprehensive agreement with the us on data protection, avoiding that these issues are dealt with individually by the member states in the framework of bilateral agreements. i am fully aware of the difficulties involved in negotiating this agreement, as there is a very different approach to data protection on both sides of the atlantic. in the eu, the right to data protection is a right explicitly enshrined in both the charter of fundamental rights (article 8) and the treaty of lisbon (article 16). in the united states, there is no general law on privacy protection, nor even an explicit reference to a fundamental right to privacy in the constitution. in matters relating to access to data, rectification, reciprocity, judicial protection and independent supervision, much remains to be done. i therefore ask the council to approve the negotiating mandate for this agreement as soon as possible, so that the negotiations can move forward and achieve the urgently needed progress and the respective transposition of these results into their respective legislation as soon as possible.

the european commission has put forward a set of proposals for the exchange of passenger name record (pnr) data with third countries and the opening of negotiations on agreements with australia, canada and the usa. the establishment of general principles on pnr is one of the tools for preventing transnational crime and terrorism. however, it raises problems with regard to the protection of civil liberties and fundamental rights. the pnr database is provided by passengers in the booking and check-in process, enabling the authorities responsible to investigate past crimes, prevent new crimes and carry out risk analyses. this security instrument is now used with third countries, leading to the need to establish legal security of data. these proposals focus in particular on the modalities of transfers of pnr data, on the rules for monitoring the correct application of the pnr agreements and on their reciprocity. parliament supports the commission's recommendations and the opinion of the european data protection supervisor, stressing that the privacy of passengers should not be violated and that the data should be used only and exclusively for the purposes for which they are intended.

in writing. if the current demographic trend is maintained, there will be a profound change in the structure of the population and the age pyramid within a few years. the number of young people aged 0-14 is estimated to increase from 100 million (1975 index) to 66 million in 2050, and the working age population will increase from 331 million today to 268 million in 2050. in addition, the number of people aged over 80 will increase from 4.1% in 2005 to 11.4% in 2050. the ageing of the population is one of the biggest policy challenges facing the eu. the eu and the member states must act urgently and in concert, not least because we are already facing a high rate of youth unemployment and the difficulty of financing pension schemes. the promotion of equity and solidarity between generations, a fundamental value, will therefore have to be worked on in conjunction with pension systems, the budget, debt, health care and rehabilitation, the promotion of births and the defence of the family and anti-discrimination policies. this should be achieved by implementing smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in line with the eu 2020 strategy.

in writing. − given that alternative investment managers represent around usd 1 trillion in assets and thus play an important role in financing the european union economy, and at the same time taking into account the financial crisis that has emerged in the investment market, although these funds are not directly related to the origin of the crisis, it is considered necessary to regulate all financial services actors and for the most part to regulate these high-risk funds, protecting investors while promoting market stability. this regulation plays a key role, because it replaces national regulations with european regulations and provides for conditions to take account of the specificities of the different funds involved in accordance with their systemic risk. it is considered a time of crisis to establish rules of conduct for all financial services and at the same time to promote a genuine single market by making it possible to frame common rules at european level. the rules proposed by this regulation provide for greater transparency in the management of own funds and in marketing within the european union (in different member states through a simple authorization) and with third countries.
in writing. − whereas the recent financial market difficulties have shown that many of the strategies applied by alternative investment fund managers are vulnerable to some or even many risks affecting investors, other market participants and the markets themselves; i voted in favour of this parliament's position because i agree that it is necessary to ensure that the operation of alternative investment fund managers is subject to strict governance controls. alternative investment fund managers shall be managed and organised in such a way as to minimise conflicts of interest. i agree that the organisational requirements established in accordance with this directive should not prejudice the systems and controls established by national law relating to the registration of natural persons working in or for investment firms. it is necessary to specify the powers and duties of the competent authorities responsible for the application of this directive and to strengthen the mechanisms necessary to ensure effective cross-border cooperation in the field of supervision.
in writing. - this is the first european directive to regulate hedge funds, culminating a negotiation process that has lasted over a year. the new rules, the document says, are intended to 'control the activity of managers and ensure greater transparency in the management of these funds, to protect investors and promote the stability of financial markets'. but, in fact, it did not go to the bottom of the matter. we're not done with these hedge funds. the derivatives market continues. and so the mechanisms that allow speculation will continue. a great opportunity to really regulate the financial markets has been lost. the council and the majority of the european parliament have caved in to the enormous pressure of the financial lobby. the financial crisis has shown that the dysfunctions of the global financial system stem, on the one hand, from excessive exposure to risk, of which these funds are an example, and, on the other, from the weakness of the systems for managing such risks. the new european regulation sets common requirements for the authorisation and supervision of hedge funds, but does little to ensure that serious systemic risks do not persist. we cannot therefore vote in favour of this proposal. in the meantime, new directives are being discussed and negotiated, and it is still possible to get to the bottom of the matter, namely to put an end to these speculative funds. we'll see about that.
in writing. − the financial crisis of 2007 was dominated by large investment banks, which had in their product portfolio a number of alternative investment funds (hedge funds) which were not supervised at all and which often consisted of assets of dubious value. the crisis reflected this reality and now concrete measures must be taken to prevent future crises caused by financial mechanisms that no one controls and that often cannot be quantified. this directive sets out a series of rules which will make these financial mechanisms more transparent and controllable, so that they are one of the funders of the european economy and not the ones responsible for its collapse.
in writing. - there should be an explicit obligation to establish and maintain, for the categories of staff whose professional activities have a significant impact on the risk profile of the alternative investment funds they manage, remuneration policies and practices consistent with sound and effective risk management, the information and disclosure requirements and the specific safeguards against asset dismantling should be subject to a general exception as regards the supervision of small and medium-sized enterprises; - it is necessary to specify the powers and duties of the competent authorities responsible for the application of this directive and to strengthen the mechanisms necessary to ensure effective crossborder cooperation in the field of supervision.
in writing. - i am voting against this report because it is content to regulate only the behaviour of companies managing alternative funds, without touching on the nature and composition of the financial products in question. this commitment to "financial industry creativity" overlooks the inherently destabilizing and voracious speculative dimension that is decisive for this type of fund. on the other hand, the proposed regulation is extremely weak. its european dimension has so many exceptions and derogations that it does not break with the differentiated national regulatory model in force. the report also does not clearly distinguish between those who are engaged in this type of fund and those who are engaged in traditional banking, nor does it prevent the action of hedge funds located in tax havens. on the other hand, by setting 'thresholds' on the value of 'systemically important' assets, it opens the door to formal fragmentation processes which will put a large number of investment companies that want to be covered outside the directive. the security of the monetary assets of european citizens is too important a public good to be exposed to the timidity of the proposed directive.
in writing. − the financial crisis has made it clear that the activities of the various players in the financial markets, in particular those involved in the management and administration of alternative investment funds, need to be closely monitored. indeed, the impact of aifms on the markets in which they operate is largely beneficial, but recent financial market difficulties have shown that their activities are vulnerable to a whole range of risks, the proper management of which requires a coherent framework across the european union. the establishment at community level of a harmonised regulatory and supervisory framework is appropriate to the cross-border nature of the risks inherent in the activities of alternative investment fund managers and contributes further to the strengthening of the internal market. that is why i voted in favour of this position of the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of considering that taiwan should be moved to the positive list as regards the granting of visa exemption. in view of the existing trade relations between the eu and taiwan, i believe that this decision will have a positive impact. most countries in the region with a similar level of development have already been granted visa-free travel and this decision reinforces the eu's decision to prioritise policies that contribute to economic growth and the creation of more and better jobs, as well as policies that contribute to competitiveness.
in writing. - i support the granting of visa-free travel to taiwanese nationals, thereby moving the country onto the so-called positive list. this decision will have a favourable economic impact on eu-taiwan relations, which is already an important eu trading partner (19th). the eu is also the largest foreign investor in taiwan. it should encourage tourism (the eu is already one of the most important destinations for taiwanese nationals). on the other hand, it does not increase the risks of illegal immigration, since the level recorded has been very low (average of 45 persons in 2006-2008), nor in terms of public security. it will strengthen regional coherence, as the vast majority of countries and entities in the region with a similar level of economic development already benefit from this visa-free regime: hong kong, macao, japan, south korea and singapore. i welcome the adoption by taiwan of the necessary measures to ensure a high level of security for identity cards and passports, with the introduction of biometric passports, as well as the announced measures to prevent the differential treatment of the various eu member states.
in writing. - i am very pleased to vote in favour of the european union's recognition that the conditions for visa liberalization for taiwan have been met. taiwan has witnessed over the past decades a manifest process of democratization and significant economic growth, ranking 25th in the world today. the european union and taiwan maintain economic and trade relations and cooperate in the fields of research, science, technology, education and the environment. in this sense, visa liberalisation with taiwan is strengthening eu-taiwan bilateral relations, strengthening partnerships in various fields and encouraging a reciprocal increase in tourism.
in writing. - anyone who has travelled outside the european union can only conclude that the freedom of movement within the union has been a factor which has substantially improved our lives. the abolition of internal borders is an important incentive for the mobility of people and goods. the fact that people can move within the union with relative ease makes the role of the external borders even more important and the need to adopt without complications a policy of entry into the european area that is suited to serving, first of all, the citizens of the member states. without neglecting humanity in the treatment of those seeking to enter our countries and respect for their rights, i believe that the union would do well to examine carefully which countries can be part of the so-called 'positive list'. in this respect, the inclusion of taiwan in the list seems reasonable to me in view of its levels of human and economic development and the effective existence and functioning of the rule of law on that island.
in writing. - the inclusion of taiwan in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from visas is a clear provocation to the people's republic of china, violating the sovereignty of its institutions over its territory, and constituting a blatant attempt to foment divisions and violate its territorial integrity. if this decision is confirmed, it will be an implicit recognition of taiwan and a violation of international law and the un charter by the eu, because taiwan has never been a sovereign state, as it has been successively recognized by the un general assembly, which has never accepted its participation in the un. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. this is yet another position aligned with the us which has been violating china's sovereignty, as happened even recently when it sold arms to the supposed "authorities" of taiwan. it is unacceptable that the majority of the ep continues to support the violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states, as happened in the case of kosovo with regard to serbia and is happening in the case of south sudan with regard to sudan.
in writing. − the criteria for third countries whose nationals are subject to the visa requirement are established by means of a case-by-case assessment of the country's situation with regard to issues such as illegal immigration, public order and security, as well as the union's external relations, regional coherence and the principle of reciprocity. during the process of reviewing the lists, the european commission shall be assisted by the member states. it is your responsibility to decide whether a third country should be included in the positive list or, on the contrary, in the negative list. the information provided to the commission by the member states, together with the valuable data provided by the centre for information, reflection and exchange on border crossing and immigration (cirefi), helps the commission to adopt its conclusions. the inclusion of taiwan on the positive list is entirely justified and rewards its economic and democratic progress.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the inclusion of taiwan on the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement (the so-called 'positive list') as justified by the level of development achieved in terms of democratic governance, economic growth and education, and as a contribution to strengthening trade relations between the european union and taiwan. it should also be noted that this measure does not represent an increased risk to illegal immigration and public security, and the commitment of the government of taiwan to extend the visa waiver to all 27 member states by the end of 2010.
in writing. − it is considered essential that this support be applied to energy projects, especially in a time of crisis, stimulating the european economy by creating new jobs. the ep's request to include support for projects in the field of energy efficiency and renewable energy is relevant, as it has to some extent forced a shift from a logic of essentially cross-border projects to a logic at regional level, which will have a wider impact throughout europe. it should be remembered that one of the main problems for regional smes to invest in renewable energy projects is due to the costs of the initial investments required, which is mentioned in this same regulation, and the introduction of technical support in the implementation of projects is commendable. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented in a way that is consistent with the objectives of the treaty. as regards scope, the support provided for decentralised renewable energy projects in local environments and their integration into electricity grids is also considered necessary.

in writing. the european union's energy dependence is well known and the way in which the member states are trying to cope with it is known, through the diversification of energy production methods and the focus on renewable energies. this effort has been abruptly slowed down by the economic and financial crisis in which we find ourselves. a programme of community financial support for energy to stimulate the economy could be a way of reversing the recent trend and resuming initiatives aimed at greater energy self-sufficiency in the member states. it is well known that the initial costs of projects of this nature are particularly high and that there is a collective advantage in supporting those who risk investing in this area. this sector has the potential not only to protect the environment but also to create more jobs in a europe that is less dependent on the outside world. i hope that the programme will bear good fruit and that it will serve what it was created for and avoid red tape and waste.
in writing. − this is an amendment to the regulation establishing the european energy programme for economic recovery (eepr), which provided for the allocation of eur 3.98 billion for 2009 and 2010. it is noted that this amount has not been used and the instrument of the sustainable energy financing initiative, proposed by the commission to use the remaining funds, is now being set up. the unused money (eur 146 million) will be channelled into this new financial instrument, which will go towards sustainable energy projects, especially in urban areas, covering, inter alia: - public and private buildings incorporating renewable energy and/or energy efficiency solutions; - investments in combined heat and power generation, including micro-generation, and in energy-efficient district heating/cooling networks, in particular from renewable energy sources; - decentralised renewable energy sources integrated into local environments and their integration into electricity networks; - micro-generation from renewable energy sources; - clean urban transport to support greater energy efficiency and the integration of renewable energy sources, with particular emphasis on public transport, electric vehicles and hydrogen and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions; - local infrastructure, including efficient outdoor lighting of public infrastructure.

in writing. − personal data, their protection and the individual's right to such protection are matters which have received increasing interest from policy-makers and civil society itself. the technological means available pose a major challenge to respect for individual privacy. this concept too is being called into question by the increasing voluntary and involuntary exposure to which citizens are subject today. they also face the growing tension between the individual right to privacy and the collective right to security. all these issues have taken on worrying proportions after september 11, 2001, and remain on the agenda. more than with conventional police forces, terrorism and other forms of organised crime are today combated by the rapid and effective exchange of information between security agencies. without it, we would be exposed to concerted, transnational criminal action without the possibility of giving it adequate answers. for all these reasons, i believe it is essential to open negotiations with our partners so that we can face collective dangers together and that the data exchanged between the parties respects the principles of appropriateness and proportionality for the purposes for which they are intended.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on demographic challenges and solidarity between generations, because in the current context, where demographic challenges are facing an unprecedented reality with increasing life expectancy and falling birth rates, they constitute one of the most urgent challenges for social policy in the coming years. urgent decisions are needed, especially at a time when the supply of jobs for the youngest and the sustainability of pension systems for the oldest are being called into question. intergenerational solidarity is needed to enhance the optimisation of the contributions of both generations. the only way this can be achieved is by ensuring free and equal access to employment and lifelong learning and career progression in all age groups, ensuring on the one hand that the youngest are in employment and on the other that the contribution that older people can still make to society is exploited, in particular through voluntary work and the possibilities for them to continue working beyond the established retirement age.
in writing. - we are faced today with a high rate of youth unemployment and underfunding of pension schemes. we must find a joint solution, because, especially in an ageing society, youth must be regarded as a precious and essential resource which must necessarily be mobilised for the pursuit of social and economic objectives. if the current trend cannot be reversed, it is estimated that by 2030, as a result of demographic change, the ratio between the active and inactive population will be 2 to 1. while the main instruments for promoting equality between generations are the responsibility of the member states, the eu has a key role to play in terms of monitoring, monitoring the correct and effective implementation of eu anti-discrimination legislation, as well as promoting the exchange of best practices and action programmes. it is essential that the eu and the member states promote new initiatives for active, healthy and dignified ageing. at the same time, it is necessary to establish long-term prospects for young people, as well as to take measures to encourage their mobility during their studies, to ensure quality vocational training and to create more jobs, ensuring their full participation in society.
in writing. − equity and solidarity between generations within the european union are set to be one of the most important challenges for european social policy in the coming decades. i therefore vote in favour of the measures and initiatives proposed in this report. societies and economies must begin a paradigm shift in how they equate population ageing. instead of viewing them as a burden and synonymous with increased costs, older people, thanks to their experience and knowledge, should be seen as an asset in the company culture. companies should be encouraged to develop age management strategies that increase their competitiveness by taking advantage of the experience and specific qualities of their older workers. i also believe that the ageing population provides an important opportunity to improve competitiveness and to encourage innovation potential and thus boost growth and employment. finally, i would like to express my concern about the high rate of youth unemployment in the eu and the need to create more jobs and establish long-term prospects that will enable them to participate fully in society.
in writing. - as i said earlier, european society is ageing, which is often seen as a negative factor in economic analysis. of course, the reversal of the demographic pyramid in states that are still heavily welfare states means that there are fewer and fewer people contributing to the system and more people dependent on that same welfare system. more aging population means, in very gross terms, more pension spending and more health care costs. however, a caring society cannot look at aging in this way. it is essential to create active ageing solutions and ways to harness the immense human potential of older people, which, even in a competitive market like the european one, still means added value (either in terms of experience or knowledge). at the other extreme, we cannot talk about population ageing without talking about birth rate policies that encourage the birth of children in the european union. the average birth rate in the eu is 1.5 children, one of the lowest in the world, and this can only be reversed by strong policies that support families and do not penalise (economically, fiscally and professionally) those who decide to have children.
in writing. - this is a report full of contradictions. on the one hand it uses language that praises the elderly, but on the other hand it presents substantive measures that in practice call into question the rights of the elderly and workers in general. examples of this include:- the encouragement of private pension systems, thus giving priority to the financial sector, forgetting the serious consequences that these practices have already had, especially in the us, which left millions of pensioners with nothing, forcing the state to intervene;- the encouragement of state intervention to increase part-time work and labour flexibility, ignoring the consequences of these practices in the devaluation of work, low wages, job insecurity and the increase in workers with incomes below the poverty line;- the encouragement of increasing the age to obtain the right to retire. for all these reasons, we voted against the report, although we acknowledge some positive aspects, but these are called into question by the neoliberal policies which it advocates.
in writing. − demographic challenges and solidarity between generations are the keys to a better future. we must therefore combat very strongly all the factors which cause low geographical growth, namely: the lack of services, the low levels of assistance, the slow and difficult integration into the labour market, the long periods of precarious or temporary employment and the insufficient support for young couples are among the reasons which lead young people to protect the foundation of a family household and procreation. on the other hand, with the average life expectancy increasing, the number of elderly people is increasing, with the resulting consequences. solidarity between generations must be strengthened if we are to have a fairer and more balanced society.

in writing. − solidarity is one of the values governing the european union, so it is essential that it is embodied in terms of equity between generations. member states face a set of demographic and social challenges that require the establishment of intergenerational solidarity. the positive increase in life expectancy and the decline in the birth rate will have perverse consequences on european social systems if concrete measures are not achieved. in view of the current situation, parliament believes that a dialogue aimed at intergenerational relations is necessary. the report covers such cross-cutting sectors as education and employment for the elderly and young, health and social benefits policies, family and birth policies, and the development of social systems, culminating in migration policies to address the effects of an ageing society. i hope that the initiatives in the report will be implemented and that justice and intergenerational dialogue will become a reality in the european union.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the introduction of exotic species is one of the main elements of disruption of ecosystems and one of the main causes of loss of biodiversity worldwide. as the commission itself acknowledges, a significant part of the introduction of exotic species into europe's coastal and inland waters is due to aquaculture and stocking practices. the amendment proposed by the commission to the regulation on the use of exotic and locally absent species in aquaculture is based on the results of a research project involving several european institutions, the impasse project, a concerted action on the environmental impacts of exotic species in aquaculture. this project proposes a more detailed and demanding operational definition of a closed aquaculture facility than the current one. according to this definition and the project conclusions, the degree of risk associated with exotic species can be reduced considerably, even to an acceptable level, if the possibilities of escape of target and non-target organisms during transport are eliminated and if clear protocols are defined in the reception facilities. in view of the results of this project, the commission proposes to relieve operators of unnecessary administrative formalities by exempting introductions and translocations to closed aquaculture installations from the permit procedure. it should be stressed that while the risk assessment process is based on scientific and technical analysis, the decision on the acceptability of the risk is a political decision. we therefore believe that the facilitation of the introduction of exotic species into aquaculture should be matched by the strictest possible definition of the requirements to be met by closed aquaculture installations, in accordance with the results of the impasse project. the need for supervision of installations should also be established in order to ensure that all technical requirements proposed by experts are effectively taken into account and respected during the operation of the installations. the same applies to the care to be taken when transporting target and non-target species to and from the installation. these were the main concerns which guided the drafting of the report and the amendments proposed to the commission's original proposal. allow me to add one additional consideration: the sustainable development of aquaculture requires strong support for scientific research and technological development in the area of native species farming, allowing for diversification of production and food supply and an increase in its quality, while also ensuring greater environmental safety. the present legislative initiative should therefore be accompanied by a strong stimulus in this area. the potential of aquaculture must be exploited, but its limitations must also be overcome in an environmentally sustainable way. among other things, it will be important to reorient the research framework programme to allow adequate coverage of this important area of research. i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs, with whom we have been able to do a useful job, and the commission and council services, the spanish presidency and now also the belgian presidency, for the work we have done over these months.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, with regard to the gallagher report and, in particular, the multiannual management plan for the carp stock, it is essential to defend the amendment proposed by the ppe, and which was made by mrs patrão neves in particular, in view of the three objectives of the green paper and the reform of the common fisheries policy: the environmental objective, which is perfectly respected in the report, and the economic and social objectives, both economic profitability and decent living for the professionals. in this line, it is very important that we make a distinction: when we talk about western carp it is important to distinguish between zone viii c, the surrounding area of the cantabrian coast which is mainly geared to small-scale fishing and supports a large number of stocks in portugal, spain and france in particular, and the northernmost zone, namely the industrial fishing zone, which is therefore mainly designed for economic profitability. that is why an amendment to this report is necessary, so that it is not only in line with the fundamental objectives of the green paper on the common fisheries policy or the reform of the common fisheries policy, but also with the recommendations that the council has made in the 2011 tac regulation, in which the carp in ices zone viii c is mainly considered for small-scale fishing, while the northern part of this western zone is mainly for industrial fishing. only by taking this approach, which takes account of the specific nature and the vocation of each area of western carp living, can the objectives of the common fisheries policy be truly protected.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i would like to thank you for your comments on my report and i would like to use this time to make a few comments on the multiannual plan for carp and the amendment i tabled on behalf of the gue/ngl to mr gallagher's report. the aim of this amendment, which the rapporteur's amendment no 7 does not fully address, is to clarify the specificities of the different fleets and to make it clear that these specificities and the final destination of the fish must be taken into account when setting the tacs. small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing has specific features distinct from industrial fishing of an economic and social nature, but not only. when it comes to setting fishing effort limits, fisheries that aim at the public supply of fish to populations for fresh consumption should not be treated in the same way as industrial fisheries, which aim at the processing of fish. as regards the different fleets and the technical question that has been raised, i also disagree with the rapporteur's position. we are indeed talking about the same stock, the same source, but it is a source which, as has been mentioned, evolves in different fishing areas: coastal and artisanal fisheries operate preferentially in one fishing zone, industrial fisheries in another. we are therefore talking about well-defined areas and it seems to us compatible, indeed necessary, for the rational management of the stock that the tacs be defined in accordance with each of these different fishing zones. this is because, as has also been pointed out here, the rational management of stocks must take account of the natural environmental and biological aspects, but also the economic and social aspects. so we should not treat in the same way what is actually different.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner dalli, the patient must have the right to know as much as possible about his illness and the medicines available to treat it. but how do you tell information from advertising? where and how can we get objective and unbiased information? there are different interpretations of the existing texts, so they must be harmonized, strengthening the sovereignty of the citizen. information must be reliable, validated by the authorities, independent, accessible and targeted at a general, non-specialist audience. the aim is to create a more informed and responsible citizenship of the end-user. the deadline for tacit approval by the european agency should be extended from 60 to 120 days. the requirement to state reasons for rejection reinforces the contradictory and balances the final result. the emea has a key role as the privileged source of objective information. i would like to end by congratulating the rapporteur, mr fjellner, on his work and congratulate him on having accepted almost all the proposals i put forward in the committee on the internal market as rapporteur for the opinion.
