in writing. the report endorses the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to help ireland cope with the disaster caused by the rains and floods in 2009. in recent years, eu member states have been hit by a considerable number of disasters. during the first six years of the eusf's existence, the commission received 62 requests for financial support from 21 different countries. of these, about a third fall into the category of "large-scale disasters". a large proportion of these requests received no support at all. other disasters have not led to calls for the mobilisation of the fund, although their impact on the affected populations, the environment and the economy has been considerable and in many cases lasting. it is necessary to adapt the rules for mobilising this fund, allowing for a more flexible and timely mobilisation, covering a wider range of disasters with significant impacts and reducing the time between disaster and the funds becoming available. but it is also important to say that, first of all, a consistent commitment to disaster prevention is required, by putting into practice the recommendations which this parliament has recently adopted.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is designed to help workers who have had their company relocated and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to ireland, which submitted an application for assistance from the egf following the heavy rains that caused the floods in november 2009. the floods caused severe damage to the agricultural sector, residential and business buildings, the road network and other infrastructure.
in writing. − this proposal for the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund (esf) expresses the need to provide assistance to ireland following the floods of november 2009, which caused enormous damage to the agricultural and business sectors, to infrastructure, in particular roads and water supply, and to residential areas. in this context, and recalling the disaster that struck the island of madeira in february 2010 and the effects of the storm xynthia in europe, i welcome the commission's proposal to provide aid to ireland totalling eur 13 022 500, based on the criterion of 'extraordinary regional disaster'. this criterion is used where it is demonstrated that the damage has affected a large part of the population of the region and that it has a serious and lasting impact on the living conditions and economic stability of the region concerned. however, i would reiterate the need to review the current esf regime in order to make it more rapid and effective in mitigating the indelible consequences of natural disasters.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by the netherlands in relation to 821 redundancies in 70 enterprises in division 18 (printing and reproduction of recorded media) of nace rev. 2 in the two contiguous nuts ii regions of nord brabant and zuid holland, i voted in favour of the resolution in order to agree with the european commission proposal and the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. i also agree with the request to the institutions involved in the process to make the necessary efforts to speed up the mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. − aid for workers made redundant as a result of restructuring and relocation should be dynamic and flexible so that it can be activated quickly and effectively. in the face of structural changes in international trade, it is important that the european economy is able to implement effectively the instruments to support the workers affected and to train them for their rapid reintegration into the labour market. in this respect, the financial assistance provided should be on an individual basis. it should also be stressed that such assistance does not replace liabilities normally borne by undertakings, nor is it intended for the financing and restructuring of undertakings. in view of the fact that the netherlands has submitted a request for assistance concerning 821 redundancies in 70 enterprises in division 18 (printing and reproduction of recorded media) of nace rev. 2 in the regions of north brabant and south holland, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - 821 redundancies in 70 printing companies in the noord brabant and zuid holland regions of the netherlands demonstrate how the global economic and financial crisis seems to have not spared sectors which at first sight would seem more immune from its effects and which point to the worrying decline in the number of printing and publishing in that country and, consequently, to the contraction of economic activity as a whole. the european commission considered this request concerning printing and reproduction companies to be satisfactory and was overwhelmingly supported in this understanding by the relevant parliamentary committee. i therefore believe that the conditions are right for me to support the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in this case. i hope that this temporary support will help to integrate the workers who have been made redundant into the labour market.
in writing. − in the face of the social impact of the global economic crisis, with particular effects on employment, the proper use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is of key importance in alleviating the suffering of many european citizens and families, contributing to their social reintegration and professional development, while also providing new qualified resources for the needs of businesses and the dynamisation of the economy. this is the context in which the intervention plan in the netherlands is situated, which concerns 821 redundancies in 70 enterprises operating in the regions of nord brabant and zuid holland. i therefore hope that the european institutions will step up their efforts to implement measures to speed up and improve the utilization rates of such an important resource as the egf, which at present has very low rates of mobilisation. this year, only 11% of the available €500 million has been requested.
in writing. - six more requests to mobilise the solidarity fund, corresponding to the closure of a further hundred firms in europe. in all, more than 3,000 workers have been thrown out of work. estimates of the number of people who could benefit from the fund at its inception have long since been far exceeded. more than the systematic use of this instrument, what is needed is a clear break with the neoliberal policies which are causing the visible economic and social disaster in the countries of the european union. the commission has already taken a number of measures to deal with the problem. each new request for the fund to be mobilised gives renewed urgency to the measures we have been advocating, namely the effective fight against unemployment, the stimulation of economic activity, the eradication of precariousness and the reduction of working hours without reduction of wages. measures also aimed at combating the relocation of firms. finally, as we have done on other occasions, we cannot but point out the injustice of a regulation which benefits the countries with the best incomes, in particular with higher wages and unemployment benefits.

in writing. − the application submitted by the netherlands for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of 821 redundancies in 70 enterprises in division 18 (printing and reproduction of recorded media) of nace rev. 2 in the two contiguous nuts ii regions of noord brabant and zuid holland fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in one or two regions adjacent to nuts ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i think that more time should be given to small distilleries in germany to adapt so that they can survive on the free market. i support the european commission's proposal to extend this period for a few more years to complete the process of abolishing the monopoly as well as the aid and allow for its final termination in 2017.
in writing. - like the rapporteur, i regret that the cap after 2013 has to inherit old situations such as this special provision under the single cmo regulation on aid granted under the german alcohol monopoly, but i understand the need for an extension of the deadline for the elimination of the monopoly, taking into account the economic needs of the german rural economy, especially in some of its federal states. the european rules, while they should be predictable and impartial, should also be able to provide the flexibility needed to meet the specific needs of european markets and citizens, in this case the owners of distilleries in germany.
in writing. - i agree with the commission's position since there is no evidence of any infringement of competition in the internal market. the council unanimously supports this proposal, which is important for the german rural economy. the commission proposal is accompanied by a timetable for reducing the quantities of alcohol produced under the monopoly until its total abolition on 1 january 2018. under article 182 (4) of the single wto regulation, and as an exception to the state aid rules, germany may grant state aid under the german alcohol monopoly to products marketed after processing by the monopoly, such as ethyl alcohol of agricultural origin. the total amount that is allowed to be granted as state aid is limited to eur 110 million per year, which goes mainly to farmers supplying the raw material and to distilleries using it. however, the budget used has been below this amount, having decreased since 2003. in addition, a large number of distilleries have already made efforts to prepare their entry into the free market by setting up cooperatives, investing in more energy-efficient equipment and increasingly marketing their alcohol directly.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report, although we do not agree with the commission or the rapporteur on the arguments they put forward to justify the extension of the aid. the prospect of both of these countries is that the few intervention measures which remain will be abolished altogether in the future, with agriculture subject to the 'free market'. they therefore merely consider that 'more time is needed to facilitate the adaptation process and to enable distilleries to survive on the free market'. contrary to the rapporteur's position, we believe that intervention in markets and regulatory instruments should be the rule and not the exception. only in this way will a decent income be guaranteed to farmers, especially small and mediumsized producers, thus guaranteeing the future of small and mediumsized farming, but also the right to produce and the right to food security and food sovereignty of each country. instead of an exception for germany and a specific production, other countries and other productions should be covered.
in writing. - the constant search for a functioning single market is incompatible with the existence of monopolies in any sector. in this particular case of the german alcohol monopoly there are some mitigating factors which allow it to still be a reality. however, as the report says, we must move towards the total abolition of agricultural distilleries from 2013 and of flat-rate distilleries from 2017.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because, in view of the needs of the german rural economy, i believe that it is justified to extend the initial period of validity of the exception provided for in article 182 (4) of the single wto regulation, so as to create all the conditions for small distilleries to prepare themselves adequately for entry into the free market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report authorising the addition of 718 pharmaceutical and chemical products to the existing list of 8619 products benefiting from duty-free importation into the eu with an expected implementation date of 1 january 2011 because i consider it important that the implementation of the exemption starts as early as next year, knowing that the us will make the implementation of the update conditional upon its entry into force on 1 january. i congratulate the rapporteur on the excellent report, in which he presents as essential the fourth revision (pharma iv) launched in 2009 to keep pace with the rapidly changing product environment in the pharmaceutical industry. as the lists were drawn up by industry and decided by consensus by the participants, i welcome the agreement reached by all member states who supported the previous revisions and who also supported product coverage in this fourth revision.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of goods and services. the revision of this list of products is required in order to keep pace with the rapidly changing pharmaceutical industry.
in writing. - knowing the importance of trade in pharmaceuticals not only for public health but also for the economy, i welcome the decision to add 718 new substances to the list of products eligible for duty exemption. the agreement is unanimously supported by the pharmaceutical industry because it removes duties on intermediate products which have to be paid, even in intra-company trade, facilitating international trade in these products and benefiting pharmaceutical companies, which may ultimately be reflected in the price of medicines sold to the public.
in writing. − this proposal invited the council and parliament to authorise the addition of 718 pharmaceutical and chemical products to the existing list of 8619 products benefiting from duty-free import into the eu. this is not a controversial issue, there is consensus among those concerned and support from the member states. the lists are drawn up by industry and decided by consensus by the participants. this addition of products is necessary to respond to the rapidly evolving product environment in the pharmaceutical industry. the target implementation date is 1 january 2011. the us has made the implementation of the update conditional upon its entry into force on 1 january. other participants are expected to follow suit, except japan, which announced an expected delay of 6 months in implementation.
in writing. - the trade in pharmaceutical products is an important part of world trade. therefore, the inclusion of 718 more products in the duty-free list is a good measure both from an economic and from a public health point of view. the decision to add these to the 8619 already on the list may also have an impact on the final price of medicines, which is beneficial for everyone.
in writing. - the addition of these 718 new substances to the existing list of 8619 products benefiting from duty-free import into the eu is agreed by the pharmaceutical industry and the other players in this review process and therefore deserves my support.

in writing. − the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and ukraine was signed in copenhagen on 4 july 2002 and entered into force on 11 february 2003. given the importance of the eu in the areas of science and technology, its capacity in these areas and the important role it can play alongside ukraine, i consider that the renewal of the agreement is in the interest of the union to continue to promote cooperation with ukraine in common priority scientific and technological areas that result in benefits for both parties. i hope that the renewed agreement will continue to prove beneficial to both parties.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution as it goes along with the resolution adopted on 25 february by the european parliament and the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy as regards the need for regional cooperation and sustainability outside european union waters. this resolution repeals the fisheries partnership agreement signed on 9 october 2006 for a period of three years and allows the continuation of fishing activities by community vessels, which is of particular interest to the european union, as it contributes to the viability of its tuna sector in the pacific ocean, while also allowing a sharp reduction in the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic, in accordance with the conservation and management measures adopted by the iattc (inter-american tropical tuna commission). it should also be noted that this agreement will provide a guaranteed income for the solomon islands, the amount of which will be used to support the implementation of its national fisheries policy, contributing to the principle of sustainability and good management of fisheries resources.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty gives the european parliament increased powers in fisheries partnership agreements, requiring parliament's prior approval. in this context, i voted in favour of the report on the 'fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the solomon islands', as i consider that it is in line with the aim of promoting responsible and sustainable fishing, serving the legitimate interests of both parties.
in writing. − the eu currently has 16 fisheries partnership agreements ('fpas') in force. through these, the community fleet has access to fishery resources that, for whatever reason, the partners cannot or do not wish to fish. at the moment, the intention is to renew the agreement with the solomon islands for another 3 years. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful organisms. this is particularly relevant when we note that under the previous version of the agreement portugal was fishing in the solomon islands eez with 4 surface longliners, which is no longer possible at this stage as no fishing opportunities for longliners have been negotiated, although a clause is included allowing the introduction of new fishing opportunities if necessary.
in writing. − the 2002 reform of the common fisheries policy introduced the concept of partnership with the aim of supporting the development of the national fisheries sector in the partner countries. from 2004 onwards, the agreements will be referred to as 'fisheries partnership agreements'. the treaty of lisbon gave the european parliament increased powers in the field of fisheries partnership agreements. article 218 (6) (a) of the treaty now requires parliament's prior consent for the conclusion of the agreement. in february 2004, the solomon islands and the european community signed a fisheries partnership agreement for a period of three years, which entered into force on 9 october 2006. i agree that this agreement should be repealed and replaced by a new version which is part of a set of three agreements in the western and central pacific region, including the partnership agreement with kiribati and the federated states of micronesia. in the agreements with african and pacific countries, part of the eu financial contribution is intended to support national fisheries policies based on the principle of sustainability.
in writing. − the conclusion of bilateral fisheries agreements between the eu and third countries ensures that eu fleets have access to relevant fisheries resources, both in quantitative and qualitative terms, while ensuring that financial resources are channelled to third countries, which often play a major role in the overall budgetary resources available for the pursuit of various sectoral policies, not just fisheries policy. that is also the case with this agreement. the vote in favour of the report does not remove the serious reservations we have about the way in which this agreement has been implemented to date, some of which have been expressed by the rapporteur. we refer, among other things, to the fact that the joint committee never met during the period of the agreement, that the terms for implementing responsible fishing practices in the solomon islands eez were not defined, and the lack of clarity on the control of the catches made. these failures seriously jeopardise the achievement of the objectives of the agreement and cannot be repeated in the new period of validity. the commission has undertaken to do everything possible to ensure that this does not happen again. it is now necessary that you fulfill that commitment.
in writing. − the eu has several fisheries partnership agreements which give it access to various fishing zones in exchange for resources that are channelled into the economies of the countries with which the partnerships are signed. this is a way for the eu to help developing countries and at the same time provide quality fishing grounds for eu fishermen to develop their economic activity which is essential for the eu economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of this fisheries partnership agreement, as i consider that it serves the interests of both parties in the main, allowing the eu to access 4,000 tonnes of tuna per year, a significant amount for the community industry and market, and providing the solomon islands with significant financial resources, partly to support the implementation of its fisheries sector policy. i believe, however, that everything must be done to avoid the problems just identified in the report.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur's concern that the commission should examine not only the specific question of the standard rate and other vat rates, but also the broader question of a new vat strategy, including its scope and derogations. due to the increasing complexity of rates, the vat system is not keeping pace with the evolution of the internal market, which puts companies and especially smes at a disadvantage. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of consumers. i welcome the commission's intention to launch a green paper on the revision of the vat system with the aim of creating a more business-friendly environment and a simpler and more robust system for the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i agree with the european commission proposal and the amendments to it introduced by parliament. i agree with the european commission's proposal for the extension for five years of the current requirement for eu member states to have a minimum standard vat rate of 15%, based on article 113 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. as regards the amendments tabled by parliament, i think it is particularly relevant that the new vat strategy should aim to reduce the administrative burden, remove tax obstacles and improve the business environment, particularly for small and mediumsized enterprises and labour-intensive enterprises, while ensuring the robustness of the system against fraud.
in writing. the renewal of the extension of the minimum value of the standard vat rate to 15% in the member states proposed by the commission is based on legal certainty. i have no objection to this principle, which is why i voted in favour of the proposal. however, i cannot fail to stress the urgency of taking comprehensive measures in relation to this tax. these must be geared to the fiscal competitiveness of the european union and to the necessary protection of smes. it is becoming increasingly clear that fiscal policies are not neutral. the success story of vat cannot and must not be an obstacle to its adaptation to the new times.
in writing. - in this proposal, which is based on article 113 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the commission proposes to extend for five years the current requirement for member states to have a minimum standard vat rate of 15%, with no consequence as regards tax rates. the commission proposes that the extension should start on 1 january 2011 and run until 31 december 2010. the purpose of the extension is not only to provide businesses with the necessary legal certainty but also to allow a better assessment of the appropriate level of the standard rate of vat at european union level. the current vat system, with its increasing complexity, not only in terms of rates, is not keeping pace with the development of the internal market and puts european companies, particularly smes, at a disadvantage. furthermore, as the european parliament has pointed out, the vat system, as currently designed and implemented by the member states, has weaknesses that fraudsters exploit and which cost billions of euros in lost tax revenues.
in writing. the report takes account of the proposal for a council directive amending directive 112/2006 on the minimum standard rate of vat of 15% by extending the current deadline, which expired at the end of this year, for a further five years, as no agreement was reached on the definitive standardisation of vat rates. the rapporteur took the opportunity to make some suggestions to the council, notably on the new vat strategy, which he said should aim to remove tax obstacles and improve the business environment, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises and labour-intensive businesses, while ensuring the robustness of the system against fraud. it also stressed that the council should move forward with a definitive system by 31 december 2015 and that the commission should present legislative proposals by 2013 to replace the current transitional level. this is a subject which we will be following very closely, given the possible negative implications of the proposal which may emerge in 2013.
in writing. - we must not forget that the current vat system, with its increasing complexity, not only in terms of rates, is not keeping pace with the development of the internal market. this puts european companies, particularly smes, at a disadvantage. moreover, as the european parliament has pointed out in the past, the vat system, as currently designed and implemented by the member states, has weaknesses that fraudsters exploit and which cost billions of euros in lost tax revenues. the new vat strategy should therefore focus on reforming the vat rules in order to actively promote the objectives of the internal market. the new vat strategy should aim to reduce the administrative burden, remove tax obstacles and improve the business environment, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises and labour-intensive enterprises, while ensuring the robustness of the system against fraud.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of this report. however, i cannot help but note that the successive postponements of definitive vat regulation are symptomatic of the impasse in which the construction of the european union has fallen. even if the commission were to submit a proposal for a revision of the vat system in the near future, we are all aware that the disparity of interests between the various member states, as expressed in the council, will ultimately prevent a proposal for a reduction in the variability of rates. it is worth remembering that, although it is a regressive tax, vat has been the fiscal instrument of emergency in the service of the austerity policies imposed by the council and the commission. the pressure for so-called 'fiscal consolidation' in the member states is now a powerful obstacle to convergence of vat rates. if we remember that the hypothesis of a european 'vat' suggested by the commission as a budget revenue of the union was immediately rejected by several member states, then we have to admit that asking the commission for a 'new strategy on vat' does not seem to make much sense.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the commission's proposal to extend for five years the current requirement for member states to have a minimum standard vat rate of 15%. as regards the vat system, it should be recognized, in line with the rapporteur's assertions, that it must be subject to a comprehensive reform in order to actively promote the objectives of the internal market, contributing to the creation of a more favourable environment for enterprises, especially smes. i therefore fully welcome the commission's announced intention to launch a green paper on the revision of the vat system.
in writing. − in its proposal, the european commission provides for a five-year extension of the current requirement for eu member states to have a minimum standard vat rate of 15% until 15 december 2015. the idea is to keep the harmonized tax structure with two mandatory rates for vat and harmonization within a range of variation of 10%, i.e. 15% to 25%. the member states undertake not to increase this differential beyond the minimum rate they currently apply. i agree with the rapporteur that the current vat system, with its increasing complexity, is not keeping pace with the development of the internal market. i therefore hope that the european commission will in future examine not only this question of the standard rate of vat but also the general theme of the revision of the current system, including its scope and derogations, and will endeavour to draw up a new strategy in the context of this tax. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ecb's annual report because i believe that measures to keep inflation close to 2% while increasing liquidity in the market have prevented the collapse of many financial institutions, although i acknowledge that the relaunch of the ecb's measures has not been fully realised because liquidity from the ecb has not always flowed into the real economy. it should be remembered that the crisis was initially a financial crisis and then turned into an economic crisis. the ems, through their governments, and the ecb had to react to the most austere crisis since the 1930s. we are witnessing a contraction in gdp, a slowdown in economic activity and an increase in budget deficits, which have led to a reduction in tax revenues and generated an unsustainable public debt, making it difficult to reach levels comparable to those existing before the crisis. this is due to the lack of internal structural reforms within the eu, as is so clearly evident in events in greece and other euro area countries. i therefore believe it is important to tackle the fragility of the financial system at global level and to remove all the links to the crisis by improving the quality of risk management and the transparency of financial markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's resolution because i agree that the financial crisis in some eurozone countries is a serious problem and reveals a certain dysfunction in the eurozone and because i think that this shows the need for reform and for stronger coordination between the various economic policies. i also agree with the call for the unrestricted and more coherent application of the stability and growth pact and consider that the pact should be complemented by the development of an early warning system to detect possible inconsistencies, for example in the form of a 'european semester', not only to strengthen the surveillance and coordination of economic policy, in order to ensure fiscal consolidation, but also to address other macroeconomic imbalances and strengthen the implementation processes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the stability and growth pact to include specific objectives to cover the differences in the competitiveness of european economies in order to encourage job-creating growth.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the definition of a public authority. proposals to strengthen the stability and growth pact should take account of the differences in the competitiveness of european economies in order to encourage growth with a particular focus on job creation.
in writing. - the crisis we are experiencing is an opportunity to review and improve what has gone wrong. strengthening the stability and growth pact and monitoring its implementation are essential to avoid future imbalances within the euro area. the creation of a european systemic risk board (esrb) and the replacement of the supervisory committees by three new supervisory authorities are salutary steps towards better economic supervision. i agree with the rapporteur when he refers to the need for prudence in relation to financial market regulation initiatives. it goes in the direction we have been advocating, better regulation does not necessarily mean more regulation.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty gave the ecb the status of an eu institution, which increases the ep's responsibility as the indispensable institution through which the ecb is accountable to european citizens. the ecb's annual report 2009 focuses on the ecb's response to the crisis, the exit strategy and governance issues. the financial crisis which began about two years ago with the mortgage crisis in the us has quickly spread to the eu and has also become an economic crisis affecting the real economy. real gdp in the euro area contracted by 4,1% in 2009, the overall average government deficit ratio increased by around 6,3% and the government debt/gdp ratio increased from 69,4% in 2008 to 78,7% in 2009. the ecb was right to adjust the interest rates downwards to 1%, and to continue with the implementation of important and unprecedented unconventional credit support measures. this has prevented the collapse of many financial institutions. however, liquidity did not always flow into the real economy. the crisis has made clear the need for greater transparency and better risk management in financial markets, sound public finances and the urgency of restoring credibility.
in writing. - the serious economic crisis affecting the whole world has been felt most acutely within the eu. the ecb's response to the crisis was effective, although it sometimes failed to act with sufficient speed or assertiveness, particularly in the case of the policy of reducing interest rates, which was more radical and effective in the united kingdom and the federal reserve. it is necessary to learn from mistakes so that in the future the same ones do not happen again. the financial crisis in some euro area countries is thus a serious problem for the euro area as a whole and reflects a certain dysfunction of the euro area. this shows the need for reform and stronger coordination between economic policies in the euro area. this is a task which must be undertaken by all the member states of the euro area if the euro is to consolidate itself definitively and be able to emerge quickly from the pressure it is currently under.
in writing. - i vote against this report. it ignores, or at least underestimates, the recessionary effect of a policy of reducing public spending pursued simultaneously by most of the countries of the union, just when it was emerging from the great recession that began in 2008. accepting this report means voting in favour of abandoning the policy of concerted stimulus that was put in place in 2009. the dominant neoliberal ideology at the ecb, which makes inflation a lurking threat even when there is a large unused productive capacity, is making the eurozone hostage to financial markets. this ideology has returned to remind us that austerity is not enough, that nominal wage cuts and further deregulation of the labour market are needed. as the contraction in aggregate demand will undermine the budgetary execution of greece and ireland in 2011, the ecb will still tell us that the austerity policy was right, that its extent and intensity were insufficient. this report is a veritable intellectual fraud.
in writing. − the current economic and financial crisis has made clear the need for reforms in the eu that can lead to a strengthening of the supervision and coordination of economic policies in the euro area and to the restoration of confidence in european public finances. important steps are being taken in this direction, including the creation of a european risk committee, which will fill the current gap in the macro-prudential oversight of the financial system in the eu, but it is essential to move forward with proposals to strengthen the stability and growth pact in order to ensure fiscal consolidation, but also to address other macroeconomic imbalances and strengthen the enforcement processes. this report, which i voted in favour of, also draws attention to the fact that the austerity packages adopted by the governments of the member states must not compromise their ability to promote economic recovery, and that it is important to strike a balance between the process of consolidating public accounts and meeting the needs for investment in employment and sustainable development, by using measures and instruments which can give meaning but also a horizon to the sacrifices imposed on citizens.

in writing. − we live in a world where, while conventional attacks on the eu or any of its member states are becoming less likely, threats are becoming more widespread and global, whether it be international terrorism, cyberattacks on vital computer systems, the use of long-range missiles against european targets or piracy in international waters. it is therefore essential that the eu, as an organisation committed to peace-keeping, conflict prevention and post-conflict reconstruction and the strengthening of international security, has the capacity to be a global player in this context, capable of ensuring the security of its citizens within its territory. that is why i believe that the eu's committed cooperation in the united nations and, on the euro-atlantic axis, with nato, which this weekend adopted its new strategic concept which aims to strengthen the alliance's capacity to deal with unconventional threats and to strengthen ties with the european union, which means 'strengthening practical cooperation in operations across the whole range of crises, from coordinated planning to mutual support on the ground'.
in writing. − in accordance with the principles of the united nations charter, the eu has committed itself to defining and implementing common policies and actions to preserve peace, prevent conflict, consolidate post-conflict reconstruction and strengthen international security. through its civilian crisis management, the eu is already making a clear contribution to global security, reflecting its core values and principles. the establishment of the european external action service (eeas) should further contribute to the development of a truly comprehensive european approach to civil and military crisis management, conflict prevention and peacebuilding and equip the eu with the structures, manpower levels and financial resources to meet its global responsibilities. i would stress the need to speed up the financing of civilian missions and to simplify decision-making processes and the procedures for implementation. this requires the council to take swiftly the appropriate decisions to set up the launching fund provided for in article 41 teu, after consulting the european parliament.
