in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a long-term plan for the stock of cod in the bay of biscay and the fisheries exploiting that stock, because it should contribute to maintaining biomass stocks at levels which allow their sustainable exploitation, based on scientific advice.
in writing. − given the importance of the cod fishery in the bay of biscay, the damage caused by the closure of the fishery to the groups that depend on it (fishermen, nets, the canning industry, etc.) and the fact that the loss of revenue has not been covered by the compensatory aid granted by the member states, it is essential to define a long-term plan to recover the cod stock so that these resources can be used again by fishermen, without endangering the preservation of this species so important for the european fishing and canning industries. as regards the 10% reduction in fishing quotas and the calculation formulas for exploitation, i believe that such measures are excessive, forgetting the economic and social impact they may have on the industries and populations involved.
in writing. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to establish a long-term plan for the stock of hake in the bay of biscay and the fisheries exploiting that stock. the fishing for the cod in the bay of biscay has been closed since 2005 due to the poor state of the same stock. in order to raise the stock of hake in the bay of biscay to a level that allows its sustainable exploitation, it is necessary to provide for long-term management measures to ensure that the exploitation of that stock is compatible with sustainable exploitation, ensuring, as far as possible, the stability of the fishery while maintaining a low risk of discontinuation. i welcome the adoption in this report of a long-term management plan rather than annual ad hoc measures to define fishing opportunities in order to ensure the stability of the fisheries sector and to strengthen control and enforcement. i agree with the support for the regional administrations responsible for control, inspection and surveillance, since they are closer to reality and with the need to draw up and publish a report before the start of the fishing season.
in writing. − the worrying state of conservation of the stock of cod in the bay of biscay led to the closure of the fisheries in 2005. as a result of this closure - with inevitably disastrous economic and social consequences, which, in this and other cases, must be prevented and remedied as much as possible - the source of the biqueirão has been recovering, making it possible to restart its exploitation. we believe that decisions on closing fisheries, on reopening them and on the definition of the conditions for exploiting resources must always be based, first and foremost, on scientific knowledge and advice on the state of resources. it is therefore essential that this knowledge is as accurate and up-to-date as possible and that the funding needs for this purpose should be ensured, in particular through the financial instruments of the common fisheries policy. long-term plans are an important instrument for fisheries management, combining the essential conservation of fisheries resources at sustainable levels with the guarantee of medium-term prospects for exploiting those resources, which is essential to give economic and social stability to fishing and the local communities that depend on it.
in writing. − the suspension of the cod fishery in the bay of biscay, which has been in place since 2005, has caused great difficulties for the operators who make their living from this economic activity. five years after that suspension, the stock of this species in the bay of biscay has now recovered to acceptable levels and it is now possible to resume its capture, but on the basis of a long-term plan to keep the stock of the bivalve mollusk always above the risk of extinction so that this activity can once again increase this economic sector in that area.
in writing. − the cod fishery in the bay of biscay is of great socioeconomic interest and its closure in 2005 has caused serious damage to the groups that depend on it (fishermen, nets, canning industry, etc.). i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the establishment of a long-term plan will make it possible to respond to the need to rationalise the exploitation of this resource, ensuring the long-term sustainability of the fishery and at the same time mitigating the risk of the stock of the cod being broken up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider the measures presented by the commission to be necessary in relation to the control and surveillance of the catch zones of the species. this resolution is an attempt to fill the gap in information on the stock of carp by establishing a formula for vessels involved in carp fishing, taking into account an annual limit of permitted landings and harvesting in defined areas. the main parties in the sector affected by this plan are the owners, operators and crew of pelagic fishing vessels operating in the western carp distribution area, i.e. the north sea, the areas west of the british isles, the western channel, the waters west of brittany, the bay of biscay and the north and north-west of spain, with the main objective of ensuring the exploitation of living aquatic resources under economically, environmentally and socially sustainable conditions. it should also be noted that portugal has been able to safeguard its fishing interests by benefiting from its historical fishing rights in the areas referred to. i would stress the positive solution for small-scale coastal fishing, which is perfectly compatible with the conservation of resources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a 'long-term plan for the western stock of carp and the fisheries exploiting that stock' because it helps to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources in economic, environmental and social terms. this proposal, which is of interest to portugal, also takes account of the specific nature and objectives of the fleets involved, particularly the artisanal fleet, with a view to the public supply of high-quality fresh fish.
in writing. - defending fisheries and the economic and social interests (beyond food) involved is not the same as defending fishing without rules and limits. we know that fisheries resources are finite and that intensive fishing means that the stocks caught do not have time to reproduce in sufficient numbers. it is therefore important that plans for the maintenance and conservation of fish stocks are drawn up, seeking to reconcile the economic and social interests at stake with the preservation of species, which is essential for the long-term maintenance of fishing opportunities. with the amendments introduced and approved, this report defends the traditional carp fishing and, in particular, allows some 30 portuguese vessels to continue fishing in the cantabrian sea area, which is fundamental from the point of view of the national interest, as pointed out by maria do céu patrão neves, the epp shadow rapporteur for this report.
in writing. − this proposal is an attempt to fill the gap in information on the stock of carp by establishing a formula for vessels involved in carp fishing, taking into account an annual limit of permitted landings of carp harvested in defined areas. this formula is based on the most reliable scientific and biological indicators currently available for the development of the population unit. i welcome the introduction of respect for the activity of the artisanal fleets which have traditionally specialised in this type of fishing for their own consumption of fresh fish, so that no areas should be established too far from the coast. i would stress the important role of the european parliament in repealing and amending the commission's delegated acts in this area.
in writing. - multiannual plans are important instruments for fisheries management, allowing the combination of the essential conservation of fisheries resources at sustainable levels and the guarantee of medium-term prospects for exploiting these resources, which is essential to give economic and social stability to fishing and the local communities that depend on it. we therefore welcome the adoption of this report and the adoption of the amendment tabled by our group concerning the zonal distribution of the total allowable catches (tacs), which we consider to be a crucial point for an economically and socially fair approach to the management of spring waters. when it comes to setting limits on fishing effort, coastal and artisanal fisheries, aimed at the public supply of fish to the population for fresh consumption, should not be treated in the same way as industrial fisheries, which are aimed at industrial processing and export. the specific characteristics of fleets and the destination of fisheries are thus recognized as aspects to be taken into account in the definition of tacs, in the name of a management of fisheries resources which takes account of biological and environmental aspects, but also of economic and social aspects.
in writing. − the establishment of a long-term plan for the western stock of carp and the fisheries exploiting this stock is essential for the efficient and correct use of fishery resources. in this way, and in accordance with the rules, fish stocks are not depleted and sustainable exploitation of these resources is possible. the report also emphasizes the fact that portugal can maintain its previous catch levels, which is essential to maintain a healthy fishing industry, which has suffered many setbacks in recent times.
in writing. − multiannual plans are a key instrument to ensure that exploitation of fisheries resources is environmentally, economically and socially sustainable. i therefore supported this report on the proposal for a multiannual management plan for the western stock of carp, and i welcome the fact that the amendment tabled by mrs patrão neves has been adopted, which is essential to ensure the protection of small-scale fisheries and the interests of portugal involved here.
in writing. - in economic terms, the most important carp stock in community waters is the western carp. the european commission's proposal sets out a long-term plan for this stock and the fisheries exploiting it. it is desirable to ensure that living aquatic resources are exploited in an economically, environmentally and socially sustainable manner. this proposal may even serve as a model for future multiannual plans on the regulation of fishing opportunities in european union waters. i support the amendments tabled in the committee on fisheries to make the determination of the biological reference factors and the method of calculating total removal more flexible by setting maximum and minimum limits and by coordinating more closely with the legislation establishing a community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. i therefore vote in favour of this document.
in writing. - for the european union, and especially for a country like portugal, with a maritime and fishing vocation and a strong fishery and canning industry, it is essential to maintain fishing as a viable and sustainable economic activity. portugal needs fisheries and as such it needs the sea to maintain its capacity to give us fish and for species to maintain their reproductive capacity intact. i therefore agree with the rapporteur when he says that 'in order to effectively prevent by-catches and limit the discarding of excessive amounts of juvenile and undersized fish belonging to targeted and non-targeted species, it is absolutely essential that the fishing industry be encouraged to use the most selective fishing gear and not to fish in areas where there are large quantities of undersized fish and non-targeted species'.
in writing. − in order to avoid overfishing and limit the return of excessive amounts of juvenile and undersized fish, it is absolutely essential that the fishing industry is encouraged to use the most selective fishing gear and not to fish in areas where there are large amounts of undersized fish and non-target species. i do not think it is appropriate to impose a total ban on discards for sole and other members of its family, as this will have a negative impact on sole stocks. this ban may also have the perverse effect of being used as an argument to legalise large-scale fishing for undersized cod in the baltic. it should be noted that the baltic sea has been classified as a particularly sensitive maritime zone by the marine environment protection committee of the international maritime organization.
in writing. − fisheries must be a sustainable economic activity in the long term, and this can only be achieved through the prudent management of fisheries resources. the concerns raised by the rapporteur are therefore legitimate and take account of the need to protect species and preserve biodiversity. i hereby agree to the prohibitions and restrictions hereby approved.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to promote sustainable management of marine resources in line with the objectives of preserving the baltic stocks, which are among the most valuable and sensitive ecosystems in the world.
in writing. - i agree with the amendment proposals in general, considering that the introduction of exotic species is one of the main problems of disruption of ecosystems, and is, along with the destruction of habitats, one of the main causes of biodiversity loss worldwide, as recognised by the commission. i therefore support the proposals for the definition of compensatory measures for the introduction of exotic species, in the sense of a strict definition of the requirements to be met by closed aquaculture installations and the need to monitor the installations in order to ensure that the technical requirements proposed by the experts are met. aquaculture, especially at a time when a new european strategy in this area is being launched, needs strong support in scientific research and technological development in the area of native species farming, which allows for greater diversification. in these amendments i agree with the idea of ensuring the involvement of the european parliament in this area, so that the previous comitology provisions are brought into line with the tfeu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'use of exotic and locally absent species in aquaculture', as it will make it possible to strengthen the requirements to which closed aquaculture facilities and the transport of species should be subject in order to minimise the impacts on ecosystems and biodiversity.
in writing. − the european aquaculture sector comprises more than 16 500 companies, with an overall annual turnover of over eur 3.5 billion and directly and indirectly employing some 64 000 people. moreover, when fisheries resources are becoming scarce, aquaculture offers a wealth of opportunities for european industries. the facilitation of the introduction of exotic and locally absent species into aquaculture, which is now being proposed, should be matched by a strict definition of the requirements to be met by closed aquaculture installations, as well as the necessary monitoring of these installations, in order to ensure that all the technical requirements proposed by experts are effectively taken into account and respected.
in writing. − the amendment proposed by the commission to this regulation is based on the results of the impasse project - a concerted action on the environmental impacts of exotic species in aquaculture. this project proposes a more detailed and demanding operational definition of a closed aquaculture facility than the current one, according to which the degree of risk associated with exotic species can be greatly reduced, even to an acceptable level, if the possibilities of escape of target and non-target organisms during transport are eliminated and if clear protocols are defined in the receiving facilities. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to exempt introductions and transfers in closed aquaculture facilities from the requirement of a licence, thus relieving operators of this administrative formality.
in writing. - as regards the substance of the report, as we said in the debate, the facilitation of the process of introducing exotic species into aquaculture in closed facilities should be matched by a strict definition of the requirements to be met by these facilities (in accordance with up-to-date technical and scientific information). monitoring of installations before and during their operation should also be ensured. the sustainable development of aquaculture requires strong support for scientific research and technological development in the area of native species farming. these species should be given preference over exotic species, thus allowing for diversification of food production and supply and an increase in food quality, while also ensuring greater environmental safety. as regards the reporting procedure, i welcome the fact that the commission has incorporated the proposals adopted by the committee on fisheries into its proposal for a regulation, but i regret that it considered it essential to submit a new formal proposal, which led to a delay in the formalisation of the agreement at first reading.
in writing. − the introduction of exotic species is one of the main causes of biodiversity loss and disruption of ecosystems on the planet. the introduction of exotic species into aquaculture should therefore lead to a strict definition of the requirements to be met by closed aquaculture facilities and their supervision. the transport of target and non-target species should also be subject to strict rules and supervision. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report. i believe, however, that research and development in the cultivation of indigenous species should be strengthened, so as to reduce the risks associated with the introduction of exotic species and promote more sustainable production.
in writing. − the introduction of exotic species is one of the main elements of ecosystem disturbance, along with the destruction of natural habitats, and is one of the main causes of biodiversity loss worldwide. facilitating the introduction of exotic species into aquaculture should be matched by a strict definition of the rules to be followed by closed aquaculture facilities (according to the results of the impasse project) and by monitoring of the facilities to ensure that all technical requirements proposed by experts are effectively taken into account and respected. the sustainable development of european aquaculture requires strong support for scientific research and technological development in the area of native species farming, which allows for diversification of production and food supply and an increase in its quality, while also ensuring greater environmental safety.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, as the results of the impasse project have shown, 'the degree of risk associated with exotic species can be greatly reduced, even to an acceptable level, if the escape possibilities of target and non-target organisms during transport are eliminated and clear protocols are defined in the receiving facilities', it makes perfect sense to exempt the introduction of exotic species into closed aquaculture facilities from the requirement of a licence. the reduction of the administrative burden and costs of licence applications is an important incentive for the aquaculture sector and this exemption, provided that it is accompanied by a strict definition of the requirements to be met by closed aquaculture facilities and adequate monitoring of their compliance, does not compromise the indispensable protection of biodiversity and the environment.
in writing. − aquaculture of exotic and locally absent species has counter-effects on natural ecosystems, in particular the loss of biodiversity worldwide, which deserve to be safeguarded by the european union. the impasse project, a concerted action on the environmental impacts of exotic species in aquaculture, has demonstrated the need to prevent the escape of these species and biological material during transport. i welcome the european parliament's report for its emphasis on biosecurity and at the same time for its streamlining of the administrative procedures for permitting introduction and translocation into closed aquaculture installations. the clear and rigorous definition of closed aquaculture facility and a regularly updated list of all facilities by member state will produce a sustainable development of this sector. member states should carry out surveillance of the facilities themselves and of the means of transport of the species. i also support the emphasis on scientific research and technological development as a means of reducing the harmful effects of this sector on natural ecosystems. finally, i would stress the amendment of this regulation under the ordinary legislative procedure of codecision, provided for by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − in the absence of specific regulation on the granting of state aid to the coal industry, since the applicable regulation expires on 31 december 2010, it is necessary to lay down rules enabling some member states, forced to close their coal mines, to mitigate the social and economic impacts of such closure. due to the regional concentration of coal mines (germany, spain and romania), the social impact of the simultaneous closure of the mines could be significant. in terms of employment, some 100,000 jobs may be at stake for miners who may not find employment in other sectors as quickly as they should and who are at risk of becoming longterm unemployed. the proposal therefore aims to provide member states with a regulatory framework to enable them to deal more effectively with the possible negative effects of the closure of mines, which may occur as a result of the phasing out of subsidies, in particular their social and environmental effects, while minimising distortions of competition in the internal market.
in writing. − aid to the european coal industry is regulated by regulation (ec) no 1407/2002 of 23 july 2002, which expires on 31 december 2010. in the absence of a new legal framework allowing certain types of state aid to the coal industry, member states may grant aid only within the limits set by general state aid rules applicable to all sectors. compared with the coal regulation, the general state aid rules significantly reduce the possibilities of state aid to the coal industry. it is therefore likely that some member states will be forced to close their coal mines and deal with the resulting social and regional impacts of this decision. i understand that given the regional concentration of coal mines, the social impact of simultaneous closure of the mines could be significant. in view of the jobs in industries related to the coal industry, up to 100 000 jobs may be at stake. i therefore agree that the closure plan be extended to 31 december 2018 and that the production units be closed definitively if they do not become competitive by that date and provided that the eu's energy needs do not require their existence.
in writing. - this report takes a positive view of and amends the european commission's proposal to amend this regulation, which in turn already amended the period of validity of the possibility of granting state aid to the coal industry. if this change did not occur, the deadline would have been 31 december 2010. now the new proposal from the european commission proposes to extend the support until 2014. however, the european parliament has approved a proposal, which we also voted in favour of, extending support until 2018, which seeks to take account of the problem at both the social level (preventing dismissals of workers and their difficult integration into the labour market) and the environmental level, with the support it advocates for its resolution. the commitment to safeguarding the maintenance of coal industries which have become competitive in the process is also positive, but it stresses the need to safeguard environmental and public health issues. the need to rehabilitate former coalmining centres is also stressed, in particular: the removal of mining equipment, work to make the underground zone safe, cleaning up the area and the removal of waste water.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, while important environmental issues such as energy sources and climate change are at stake, economic issues such as the retention of non-competitive production units in the economy in a time of economic and social crisis are the social issues that must be defended. we cannot take any measures that will aggravate the crisis. the response to the crisis is investment and protection of people, which in this case means ensuring the conditions for the closure of these mines in a foreseeable period of time after the crisis has been resolved, defending jobs and fighting unemployment.
in writing. − the support provided in this report is key to helping to support potential unemployed in this industry. preparations must be made immediately for the vocational retraining of workers affected by the closure of mines and all possibilities for using regional, national and union funds for financing must be explored. the financing of environmental protection measures and of the costs of long-term mine closures should be continued beyond 2014. a premature cessation of subsidies to the coal industry by member states could cause enormous environmental and financial problems in the regions concerned and could prove even more costly than a gradual elimination of these subsidies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, while important environmental issues such as energy sources and climate change are at stake, economic issues such as the retention of non-competitive production units in the economy in a time of economic and social crisis are the social issues that must be defended. we cannot take any measures that will aggravate the crisis. the response to the crisis is investment and protection of people, which in this case means ensuring the conditions for the closure of these mines in a foreseeable period of time after the crisis has been resolved, defending jobs and fighting unemployment.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1472/2002 of 23 july 2002 on state aid to the coal industry expires on 31 december 2010, which would oblige some member states to close their coal mines by that date and to cope with the considerable social and regional impact of these simultaneous closures. the commission proposal was to provide the member states with a regulatory framework to allow them to extend the support granted until 31 december 2014, and parliament extended this deadline until 31 december 2008, thus ensuring that the conditions for solving this problem in a sustainable way in social and environmental terms were met.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the work of the acp-eu joint assembly in 2009 because i consider it essential that the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) continues to play the role of monitoring the negotiations of economic partnership agreements (epas) and fosters interaction between parliamentarians, with the aim of greater transparency for all processes. i believe it is important in this respect to strengthen the parliamentary dimension of cooperation work, recognising that the creation of the african union and the growing power of the acp-eu partnership agreement are bound to pose a challenge to acp-eu cooperation and, consequently, to the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly. given that in 2009 the commission and the acp countries made proposals for the second revision of the cotonou partnership agreement, it is important that the app keeps abreast of developments in order to ensure that it can survive and move forward as an institution. this cooperation between the european parliament and the jpa, which started in 2007, resulted in the creation last year of a full-fledged delegation for delegations with the jpa.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2009, as i consider that this assembly continues to constitute an important framework for an open, democratic and in-depth dialogue between the european union and the acp countries. with a view to a more efficient and democratic cooperation process, it is necessary to involve the parliaments of the acp countries more closely in the formulation and drafting of strategic cooperation plans and to involve them more actively in the negotiation of economic partnership agreements together with the european authorities.
in writing. - without calling into question the importance of the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2009 and its undeniable contribution to cooperation and development, i cannot but express my concern about the content of paragraph 6 of the eva jolie report, where we read: 'encourages the jpa to continue its work in this area and to explore additional and innovative sources of development finance, such as an international financial transaction tax.' i do not believe that international taxation of financial transactions is of great benefit to the acp states.
in writing. − the joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) met twice in 2009, when the commission and the acp countries made proposals for the second revision of the cotonou partnership agreement to be negotiated during 2010. in view of the regionalisation of the acp group brought about by the economic partnership agreements, it is important that the acp closely monitor developments to ensure that it can survive and move forward as an institution. i would stress the concern of the ppp with the repercussions of the current financial crisis, the adoption in luanda of a resolution on the impact of the financial crisis in the acp countries and the resolutions on the impact and the fight against the crisis in the acp states.
in writing. - the full fulfilment of the role of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in supporting north-south cooperation and in strengthening the parliamentary dimension of this cooperation, to which the rapporteur refers, requires the defence of certain fundamental features of this assembly. its wide representation is both its greatest asset and an essential requirement for the full exercise of its role. we must therefore reject any attempt to reduce this representativeness on the pretext of cost containment, by defending the pluralist character of the assembly, without which some of its principles would be seriously distorted and some of its basic objectives compromised. we must also ensure that all means are available to ensure that all parliamentarians, both from the eu and, in particular, from the acp countries, participate effectively and widely. that is why we have repeatedly noted with concern that the necessary conditions for such participation have not been ensured, particularly as regards interpretation services. official languages of eu and acp countries are often omitted, as has been the case on more than one occasion with portuguese. this is a serious flaw that needs to be corrected.
in writing. − the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly met twice in 2009, at which important decisions were adopted on a range of issues, including the food and financial crisis, the situation in somalia, climate change and the situation in madagascar. they also brought together several working groups to discuss a number of relevant topics, including: training for better governance, urban construction and re-housing projects, disabled people, rural tourism and minority rights in the czech republic. it is this diversity and the discussion of issues of importance to both sides that make these periodic meetings important in trying to find solutions to the problems facing the less-favoured regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2009, in this context highlighting the role of the acp, which has succeeded in establishing itself as a key player in north-south cooperation, contributing to the deepening of an open and democratic dialogue between the eu and the acp countries.
in writing. - i approve of this report, emphasising article 67 on the different legal systems and practices and access to justice, aspects for which mutual recognition should contribute to a better understanding of the different legal systems and practices. i believe that enormous progress has already been made in the area of civil justice in the eu and that this ambitious plan for a more strategic and less fragmented approach to civil law must reflect the real needs of citizens and businesses and take account of the difficulties of legislating in a shared area of competence, with harmonisation being a possibility in the face of overlap. the different legal approaches and constitutional traditions of the different member states should therefore be kept alive, but at the same time an eu-wide approach should be devised in this area, so as to better address the problems at the global level, while also mentioning the need to ensure the functionality of the measures already put in place and to consolidate the progress already made, so as to move forward consistently towards a correct and functional implementation of the stockholm programme.
in writing. - i am pleased to note the enormous progress made in the field of civil justice since the union was given competence in the field of justice and home affairs and the ejn was set up. i also congratulate the commission on the very ambitious plan it has proposed, which makes it possible to respond to a significant number of the demands that have been made by the european parliament. it is essential to adopt a more strategic and less fragmented approach, based on the real needs of citizens and businesses when exercising their rights and freedoms in the single market. the stockholm action plan should reflect these needs (in terms of mobility, right to employment, equal opportunities, business needs, etc.) while promoting legal certainty and access to swift and effective justice. we cannot ignore the difficulties of legislating in a shared area of competence, where harmonisation is rarely an option and overlap is to be avoided. the differences in legal approaches and constitutional traditions between the various legal systems can serve as a source of inspiration for a european judicial culture, but should not constitute an obstacle to the further development of european law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates specific mechanisms that promote legal certainty and access to swift and effective justice. in the context of the stockholm action plan, it is necessary to ensure that the exchange of good practice between judicial systems pays particular attention to the needs of individual citizens and businesses, facilitating mobility within the eu area, the right to employment and equal opportunities.
in writing. − the areas of civil, commercial, family and private international law are some of the most sensitive areas of law applicable in each member state. i therefore believe that any change to them should be treated with particular caution, bearing in mind, first of all, the principle of subsidiarity. respect for the different legal systems, the consensus around them created in each of the respective political communities and their legitimate options must always be borne in mind by the european legislator who cannot and must not hide the fact that he is dealing with peoples and nations with stable, established and deeply rooted legal orders. i therefore recommend that the projects and initiatives proposed be adapted and proportionate to the actual needs of the people and that they be carefully assessed. i am also aware that there are legal relationships which, by their very nature, are more likely to call for the application of the laws of more than one country. i recognize the goodness of much of what is advocated and which is intended to contribute to the exchange of best practice and to the realisation of a true ems.
in writing. − the stockholm programme adopted by the european council in december 2009 sets out the priorities for the development of the european area of freedom, security and justice over the next five years. union law facilitates mobility and enables citizens to exercise their rights of free movement, while strengthening trust in the european judicial area. the commission's action plan for the implementation of the stockholm programme envisages making use of the tools available following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon to help facilitate everyday life and business exchanges between citizens of the european union, reconciling the needs of citizens and the single market with the diversity of legal traditions between member states. i support this report by stressing that some areas should be given priority, such as civil aspects and mutual recognition of documents.
in writing. − the own-initiative report covers a wide range of complex issues, drawing on the civil law, commercial law, family law and private international law aspects of the stockholm programme action plan. that is why the rapporteur's suggestions are also met with a mixed response. in some cases, we find them positive, particularly when they refer to the need to encourage debate on problems relating to maritime, commercial and family law. but in portugal there is still an unresolved question of the specialisation of magistrates in those areas. in the family courts, the very nature of the issues involved requires that, as a condition for the appointment of judges to those courts, they have specific training. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade mark is protected. here too, in portugal, delays are very great and it is recognised that many of the magistrates have difficulty in deciding on very specific matters.
in writing. − the areas of civil law, commercial law, family law and private international law are among the most sensitive areas of law applicable in the various member states. i abstained on this report because i consider it essential that the principle of subsidiarity should always be present in these matters, particularly in those relating to family law and when dealing with issues such as mutual recognition of marriage and family law.
in writing. − the stockholm programme adopted in december 2009 sets out the priorities for the development of the european area of freedom, security and justice over the next five years, highlighting the important results already achieved and hoping that the measures proposed will help to meet the real needs of citizens and businesses by facilitating their mobility and the exercise of their rights and freedoms in the single market, without compromising the requirements arising from the principle of subsidiarity and respect for the diversity of the legal approaches and traditional constitutions of the various member states.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow millions of portuguese workers will go on strike. and they 're going on strike with a very simple message: it is not the working people, it is not the pensioners, it is not the young people, it is not the unemployed who have to pay for the crisis for which they are not responsible. we cannot understand the current impasse over the european budget without looking at the context in which it is situated, which is the context of the social tragedy, the austerity policies that are being imposed on our countries. the austerity policies are not only unfair, they are a colossal economic mistake which promises to bring the european union back into recession, which promises a horizon of unemployment and which, above all, promises to accentuate the divergence between surplus and deficit countries. in this context, we must be very clear about this budgetary debate. for us, there is no currency without a consistent budget and, let us be practical, the budget for 2011 that we are discussing is not just modest, it is a mediocre budget, it is a budget that does not respond to the crisis, it is part of the crisis. that is why it is important that it does not happen again in 2012, in 2013 or after 2014. this is the question we are discussing, the question of the future: whether we want a europe held hostage by governments or whether we want a europe that continues to be trapped by the interests of the financial system. the european left is indeed interested in discussing own resources. we do not want new taxes on european citizens, but we certainly want to discuss how to make financial capital pay what it has not paid, pay what it owes. because that is the message that our citizens, the workers and the unemployed, demand from this house and from the european union. either we want a european project that is low-key and without any ambition, or else it is clear that we cannot be satisfied with the scenario that is being proposed to us by the united kingdom and a group of governments: "do more with less money because this is the europe we have to offer you".
mr president, in the negotiations with the council on the 2011 budget, the european parliament did everything possible to reach an agreement. the only requirement is that the commitments made by the council, such as the eu 2020 strategy and the need for its funding, and the lisbon treaty are respected. in fact, the european parliament must be involved, voting, giving opinions and being consulted, under the treaty, on the new interinstitutional agreement in the next multiannual financial framework and on the definition of new own resources. logical demands, simple demands, demands in the interests of the citizens, in the interests of preventing risks and institutional conflicts, demands which should be shared and defended by the council. as regards the interinstitutional agreement, it is obvious that flexibility for the current multiannual financial framework is a condition for the commitments made by the european institutions and, in particular, by the council to be respected. the european union 2020 strategy, the iter programme, the european external action service and financial supervisory bodies are some examples that need funding. the council must incorporate the treaty of lisbon, both in terms of the new powers that the european union is assuming and which are reflected in the budget, and in terms of the strengthening of the european parliament's powers, particularly in the budgetary area, which also strengthens the democratic legitimacy of the institutions of the european union. in this way we have a more democratic governance with the use of the community method instead of intergovernmentalisation. i hope that some national egos will not undermine and hinder the project of peace and solidarity and european progress.

member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all answer your written question on the simplification of the cap, a subject which is important, as i have said many times since i have been a commissioner, and which we will take into account in future regulations. i should like to begin with the first part of your question: what has the commission already done to make life easier for farmers? i think that if we look at what has been done in recent years, the answer is simple: it has already done a lot to simplify, it has already put in place many measures to simplify the lives of farmers. in march 2009, the commission presented the communication: 'a simplified cap for europe - a win-win for all'. this communication highlights the activities carried out in recent years and gives some indication of the reduction in administrative burdens thus achieved. i do not want to repeat every element of this communication, but i would like to give you some examples. firstly, the adoption in 2007 of the council regulation on the common organisation of the markets in agricultural products has significantly reduced the bureaucracy of the framework for the application of european legislation on the common agricultural policy. because of its technical nature, the purpose of this common organization of the single market was not to change basic policy but to harmonize provisions, thus making the cap rules simpler to administer and lighter, more accessible and less burdensome to apply. simplification was also one of the main reasons behind the commission's health check proposals. the regulation adopted in 2009 simplifies the provisions of the single payment scheme and thus improves the effectiveness of the 2003 cap reform. in addition, to illustrate the progress made in the agricultural sector, i would also like to refer to the action programme for the reduction of administrative burdens in the european union. in the context of this programme, several evaluations were carried out. the results of these evaluations show that administrative burdens in the agricultural sector have been reduced by 36%, well above the overall programme target of 25%. last year, my predecessor presented a first response from the commission services to the list of 39 simplification suggestions that had been put forward by 13 member states in april 2009. some of these 39 suggestions were implemented in late 2009/early 2010. another part is in the 'simplification' package which has just been adopted by the commission in relation to direct payments and rural development, and regulations have been tabled in the council and parliament. as regards the second pillar, the commission has launched a study on the administrative burden on beneficiaries of rural development programmes. this study focused on two categories of measures: agro-environment and farm modernisation. the results of this study will be used in our reflections on the cap after 2013. in conclusion on this first point, i would also like to inform you that the programme, which includes a stay on a farm for officials of the directorate-general for agriculture and rural development, is continuing. this programme, also known as the harvest experience, helps us to get in touch with the reality of the field and to use this experience in the decisions we prepare. on the second part of your question - how the commission will take parliament's suggestions into account in its work on the cap after 2013 - i can assure you that i am also concerned about these issues and that we will take into account all the analyses we have already made with a view to simplification, but also the proposals we are going to make, which do not go in the direction of more bureaucracy but in the direction of more assurance for the taxpayer as to the proper use of money. i am open to any technical suggestions you may have on this point as well. at the beginning of december i will be meeting your colleagues on the committee on budgetary control, who will also ask me what the commission is doing to ensure that public money is well spent. the commission, in this case, can only apply regulations which have been adopted by the council, often with the opinion of parliament. it is not the commission that adds administrative tasks. the commission is merely applying council regulations which already exist. i can assure you that in future we will not make proposals which complicate matters but which will, on the contrary, make the common agricultural policy more credible in terms of content. as far as farmers are concerned, their main role is, as i have already said, that of agricultural production; it is also because of this activity that part of the cap money is allocated to this policy. as regards what we are going to do for the period after 2013, i would like to inform you that, in parallel with the preparation of the legislative package for the cap after 2013, i have decided to set up a high-level group at technical level between the commission and the member states to ensure that this legislative package does not create more bureaucracy, but on the contrary simplifies where possible. as george lyon said, often the bureaucracy that the farmer finds in the field is not just what the commission does. you know that the management is shared with the member states and we often have applications which differ from one member state to another, precisely because we have a national administration. it is not the commission's job to simplify. i told you, the commission has already simplified. simplification is also needed at member state level. in reply to mr george lyon's question on scotland, the commission is also simply respecting the regulations which say that for farmers who do not respect the cross-compliance standards, penalties must apply not only in scotland but in northern ireland and throughout europe. once again, this is a rule which, if we do not respect it, discredits us as far as the commitments that farmers make to respect european legislation are concerned, since cross-compliance is not a standard added by the commission, by a member state or by another, but stems from european legislation which is translated into these regulations. governments will receive more details by early december, when the commission presents the results of its audits.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the simplification of the cap is a proposal which we have all been advocating for years. but it is still a long way from being fully achieved despite the efforts which, it must be acknowledged, the commission has been making. i would like to make it very clear, however, that for the socialist and democratic group, simplification cannot be understood as any kind of openness to facilitation or the absence of rigour in terms of control or monitoring of public aid. no pretext can be invoked to circumvent this elementary requirement of transparency. we now have an excellent opportunity to achieve this with the start of the new discussion on the cap post-2013. but there will be no significant progress in terms of simplification without a simplification of the architecture of the common agricultural policy itself. that is what the socialist and democratic group has been saying. last april we published a document in which we advocated a rearrangement of the two pillars and we are pleased to note that the commission has taken up some of our suggestions in this regard. i do not understand how it is possible for unrelated production support, which is subject to similar criteria of an essentially environmental nature, such as direct payments, agri-environmental measures or compensatory payments to less-favoured regions, to have different bureaucratic treatment and controls and not be included in a single unified system. i also find it very difficult to understand that many of those who talk most about simplification are precisely those who are most resistant to changing the current architecture of the common agricultural policy. i therefore look forward to the commissioner's work in the immediate future and the implementation of the guidelines he has just presented to us, and i take this opportunity to express my hope that all those who want genuine simplification will demonstrate this by action in the discussion we are now starting on the future of the common agricultural policy.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, madam president, when this parliament voted in may on the resolution on simplifying the cap, we pointed out that this simplification could not result in less support for farmers, nor in the dismantling of the instruments for managing the markets. i remember that the resolution we adopted itself also warned against this. six months after the resolution was adopted, there are still serious concerns, which are being exacerbated by the commission's recent communication. the traditional measures of market management, such as public intervention and others, must not and cannot be dismantled under the pretext of alleged rationalization and simplification, otherwise the process of destroying small and mediumsized farming in many countries will continue and intensify. there is certainly a lot to be done in the field of simplifying the cap, a lot of positive and even necessary things. i am referring, among other possible examples, to the need to change penalties, particularly where they concern non-compliance which is not the responsibility of the producer, to simplification of application procedures, to changes in the level of animal identification, among many others. but in addition to simplification which benefits all farmers, and in particular small and mediumsized producers, the cap also needs a fundamental change which strengthens the instruments of intervention, ensuring fair prices for production, which recovers the instruments of regulation of production, such as quotas and production rights, which guarantees each country, and since we are talking about simplification, something as simple as the right to produce, the right to food security and sovereignty, and which enshrines the principles of modelling and capping aid by overcoming the current imbalances between producing countries and production. the commission's insistence on subjecting agriculture and food production to the market and to farmers, the precariousness of incomes, the increasing volatility of prices, the worsening of food dependence in many countries and regions. a simplification which serves the interests of farmers, especially small and mediumsized farmers, and which allows them to continue their production, yes. we are not going to accept simplification which destroys production and the producers, and we will continue to fight against it as we have done so far.

the problems affecting european beekeeping are unfortunately more serious and more profound than some cyclical crises which recurrently affect other seemingly more important sectors. the problem of beekeeping is first and foremost an environmental problem, with consequences that can be catastrophic if we are not able to give it an adequate response in a timely manner. two figures from the fao, quoted in the draft resolution and referred to by mrs lulling, are illuminating: 84% of plant species and 76% of food production depend on pollination. but agriculture is also an important economic activity in rural areas, with great potential for growth, since european production is far from meeting our needs. no livestock activity (and i put livestock in commas, of course) is so closely linked to nature and sustainability and plays such an important and irreplaceable ecological role as beekeeping. so these are more than enough reasons why we should not spare any effort or resources to investigate the main causes of the alarming and progressive mortality of bees and to support health programmes. this debate should also be a reflection on finding imaginative and effective ways of including support for this particular landless livestock in the support mechanisms of the new cap, at the very moment when the area unit is envisaged as the basic criterion for the granting of new aid. i would therefore like the commission to tell us what immediate answers it has to this problem and whether it intends to fit this activity into the new architecture of the common agricultural policy which we are about to start discussing.
commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the mortality of bees is increasing and the number of beekeepers is decreasing, a problematic situation for agriculture, for biodiversity, as has been said here, given the enormous implications for food production and for plant species which depend on their pollination. the life span of a worker bee is very short (about six weeks) and very sensitive to changes in the external environment. honey production has therefore also been affected, not only by the increasingly uncertain duration and stability of the seasons, but also by the increase in external aggressions that may result from the use of pesticides, mites or other sources, and on which a higher level of research could contribute to better applied responses and a more appropriate reinforcement of measures in favour of biodiversity and the reduction of the effects of climate instability. the commissioner, the current programmes must undoubtedly be strengthened in the framework of the new cap so that we can also get more effective responses here.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2001/83/ec as regards information to the general public on medicinal products subject to prescription. this directive establishes a community code on medicinal products for human use and contributes to guaranteeing the right of patients to reliable, accessible, independent and validated information on available medicinal products by the competent authorities.
in writing. − directive 2001/83/ec establishing a community code relating to medicinal products for human use provides for a harmonised framework for the advertising of medicinal products at community level, the application of which remains a responsibility of the member states. this legislation prohibits advertising to the general public of prescription medicines. however, the provisions on information on medicinal products are not regulated, which only provides that information on certain supply activities is exempt from the advertising provisions. thus, community legislation does not prevent member states from establishing their own approaches to the provision of information on medicinal products, provided that the above-mentioned rules on advertising are respected. i agree with the rapporteur's proposal to exclude the possibility of pharmaceutical companies making information available in newspapers, magazines and similar publications or on television and radio.
in writing. the proposal for a directive amends the previous directive on the provision of information to the general public on medicinal products subject to prescription. in general, the responsibility for informing the public is concentrated on the pharmaceutical companies, ensuring that the information cannot be used for advertising. the commission is also given the role of monitoring and deciding, by means of delegated acts, on the definition of what constitutes information and what constitutes advertising. we believe that this approach centralizes too many information functions at the level of the pharmaceutical companies and the commission, functions which should be carried out in a sovereign, coordinated and certified manner by the specific national authorities, in order to improve the information provided to patients and the public and to defend their rights.
