in writing. − given the importance of adherence to the treatment regimen and the correct administration of medicines for the success of a treatment, it is essential that the public (patients) have access to quality, true, up-to-date, non-misleading and non-promotional information in accordance with the summary of product characteristics (spc). the person best placed to provide current and accurate information for each medicinal product is its marketing authorisation holder ('mah'). parliament has decided to put the emphasis on the interests of patients and to protect them. i could not agree more with this approach, although i do not think it requires us to restrict the possibilities offered by the commission's proposal for the pharmaceutical industry to disseminate information on a 'push' basis. it was a balanced proposal that took into account the interests of all parties, involved health professionals and protected the public from advertising msrm, which remained, well, prohibited. i believe that with the text now adopted, little will actually change in the reality of patients' access to information, which i consider to be a lost opportunity.
in writing. − access to quality information on prescription medicines will help to achieve better health outcomes for patients, as the better informed they are, the better they can understand decisions about their treatment. the aim of this proposal cannot therefore be limited to harmonizing european legislation, but must also promote health by improving knowledge in the field of health. the pharmaceutical industry has an important role to play in promoting health literacy, but this role needs to be clearly defined and the participation of the sector strictly regulated in order to prevent commercial logic from leading to an excessive consumption of medicines. it is also necessary to avoid misleading advertising and to try to better inform the consumer (patient), who has access to a variety of information without control via the internet, and not the same for reliable information provided by pharmaceutical laboratories.
in writing. - the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 726/2004 on the provision of information to the general public on medicinal products for human use subject to prescription introduces new rules on transparency and effectiveness of information, placing the emphasis on the interests of patients by protecting them, which was the reason for my vote in favour. to highlight the establishment of a european medicines agency and the clear contributions to ensuring the right of patients to reliable, accessible, independent and validated information by the competent authorities on available medicines.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards information to the general public on medicinal products for human use subject to prescription, regulation (ec) no 726/2004 laying down community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use and establishing a european medicines agency, as i believe it is essential to ensure that patients have access to reliable and independent information on medicinal products subject to prescription available on the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (recast), because i believe that the agreement reached with the council is consistent with the objective of contributing to the protection of human health and the environment by simplifying and making existing legislation more coherent.
in writing. - according to the commission, 9.3 million tonnes of electrical and electronic equipment (eee) are sold annually in the eu alone, the majority of which are large household appliances and computer and telecommunications equipment. due to market growth and innovation cycles, waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) is considered to be the fastest growing waste line. weee is estimated to grow to 12.3 million tonnes in 2020. the aim of the recast of the directive on the restriction of the use of certain dangerous substances (rusp) is to extend its scope and strengthen its preventive part so that, in accordance with article 174 (2) of the treaty, the correction of environmental damage is to be done as a matter of priority at source. however, this directive focuses mainly on large distributors, ignoring the budgetary impact it may have on eee-producing smes, and does not present solutions in the wake of both the com (2008) 0809 proposal and the report on biointelligence, which states that smes producing medical, control and monitoring equipment may face problems under this new regime.
in writing. − the present recast of the restriction on the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (rohs) is necessary, according to the commission, because of uncertainties about the scope, lack of clarity on the legal provisions and disparities in the member states as regards the conformity of the products concerned. i received several calls before the vote to reject the inclusion of pvc in the list of substances identified for priority review in annex iii of the rohs directive. i would point out that i disagree with this inclusion in that an indiscriminate listing of a number of suspect products, in which pvc has been included, is meaningless. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. however, in the case of pvc, a first assessment under the reach regulation concludes that it is of low hazard and is therefore not a priority substance for inclusion in annex iii. i voted in favour of this report because during the negotiations before the vote in plenary this listing was withdrawn. the commission should now carry out a reassessment three years after the entry into force of this legislation.
in writing. − the volume of sales of electrical and electronic equipment in the eu and the inevitable increase in waste from such equipment lead to the need to replace some of the hazardous substances that constitute them, in order to minimise their impact on the environment and also to ensure the protection of consumers and public health. we recognize this need and value the search for solutions that meet it. we therefore voted in favour of this report. in the course of the discussion process that has taken place in recent months, the council has reached agreement with parliament, after negotiations on some of the most controversial and worrying issues. we welcome the fact that the final text proposal excludes polvinyl chloride - pvc from the scope of the directive, which makes it possible to safeguard production in some industrial sectors, particularly in portugal, which could be seriously harmed if it were included, as has been proposed.
in writing. − the use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment is a major problem for public health, the environment and waste management. these risks are increased by poor recycling and recovery operations in developing countries and, above all, by illegal export for landfill in poorer countries. with this draft legislation, all the materials concerned will be included in the scope of this directive. in future, all materials should therefore comply with the provisions of the directive if an environmental assessment deems it necessary. the directive contributes to the establishment of clear rules in the member states concerning the placing on the market and reuse of these substances. this directive will bring a significant improvement to the present situation, and i have therefore voted in favour of it. i do, however, believe that some dangerous substances which have been left out of the directive should be included in the next three years, after a review and impact assessment.
in writing. - the increasing use of electrical and electronic equipment, together with the enormous technological development of the latter, leads to an increasingly shorter life cycle, and poses serious problems with regard to the use of dangerous substances in such equipment, such as difficulties in managing the increasing number of waste. the purpose of this directive on the restriction of the use of certain dangerous substances (rusp) is therefore to extend its scope and to strengthen its preventive element, so that, in accordance with article 174 (2) of the treaty, the correction of environmental damage is to be carried out as a matter of priority at source. this reformulation is essential for the successful reduction of hazardous substances in this type of equipment.
in writing. - my vote in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (recast) is due to the improvements introduced in the framework of the agreement with the council, which have contributed to major improvements in the protection of public health, the environment and waste management. the simplification and greater coherence of the new legislation should be emphasised. in the context of a large increase in sales of electrical and electronic equipment in the eu, it was imperative to reorganise and restrict the use of hazardous materials. with this legislation we are helping to prevent the waste we produce from electrical and electronic equipment such as mobile phones, computers and refrigerators from harming the environment and human health through the introduction of chemicals into the environment, either through landfills or by the release of toxic gases in incineration.
in writing. − the commission believes that for reasons of clarity and legal certainty, the current directive on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment, adopted in 2003, should be recast. the first step in this reformulation is to extend the scope of the directive in order to contribute to the protection of human health and the environmentally sound recovery and disposal of waste electrical and electronic equipment. in this respect, it is important to stress the need to take due account of the potential impact of the proposed solutions on smes.
in writing. − it will make it possible to strengthen international cooperation in the fight against counterfeiting by creating a tool for effective protection of ipr. it should not create new rights but ensure respect for existing rights through repressive measures and the creation of a comprehensive international framework for assistance to parties. it is a difficult agreement, with conflicting interests and which allows for controversial interpretations as to its effects. it is essential that ipr be protected, but on the other hand it is essential to strike a balance that ensures that freedom of expression and innovation is not threatened, or that limitations are created to the exercise of the civil and fundamental freedoms of individuals. counterfeiting is a very serious problem, posing enormous risks to european industry, the economy and innovation. i hope that this agreement will be a step in the right direction and that in the next negotiations it will be possible to resolve ambiguities and omissions which still exist in the text, such as the reference to false geographical indications. i commend the commission for its efforts to increase the degree of transparency of the negotiations and i hope that it will maintain this position by keeping parliament fully informed of the progress of the negotiations.
in writing. - i agree with the motion for a resolution on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta), which was adopted after many months of debate and after an effort to find a compromise solution between the various political groups, which unfortunately was not achieved. in the interests of sound functioning markets, the protection of the single market, the competitiveness of european businesses in a global economy and the creation and maintenance of jobs in the eu, it is important that the eu should make the fight against counterfeiting in all its forms a priority of its internal and international policy. aware that acta does not provide a solution to a complex and multi-dimensional problem such as counterfeiting; however, as stated in point 3, i believe that acta is a valid tool to make existing rules more effective, thereby benefiting eu exports and protecting rights holders when operating in the global market, where many holders of industrial and intellectual property rights are currently victims of systematic and widespread infringement of copyright, trademarks, patents, designs and geographical indications.
in writing. - i abstained on the resolution on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement because i considered that the text, although containing important considerations, was excessively critical of the agreement under consideration. i believe that, overall, acta is favourable to the eu's economic interests and balanced in the combination of the protection of intellectual property rights and the safeguarding of fundamental rights.
in writing. - following strong parliamentary pressure, the degree of transparency of the acta negotiations has increased substantially and, since the new zealand round of negotiations, parliament has been fully informed. the negotiated text reflects the main concerns expressed by parliament, in particular on issues such as respect for fundamental rights, privacy and data protection, respect for the importance of a free internet, the usefulness of safeguarding the role of service providers and the need to safeguard access to medicines. the fight against counterfeiting is a priority and international cooperation is essential to achieve this objective. with the accession of new emerging and developing countries to the agreement promoting a general protection of intellectual property rights acta could achieve the desired multilateralism.
in writing. − the negotiated agreement is an important step in the fight against counterfeiting and is a key element of the eu's political strategy to ensure fairness, a level playing field for european producers, the preservation of jobs for citizens and respect for the rule of law. the fight against counterfeiting must be a priority of the domestic and international political strategy and international cooperation is essential to achieve this objective. acta is a tool that makes existing rules more effective, thus benefiting eu exports and protecting rights holders when they operate in the global market. i stress the importance for european businesses and employment in the eu of protecting geographical indications and welcome the efforts made by the commission to include protection of geographical indications in the framework of acta. finally, i would stress the importance of the commission confirming that the implementation of acta will have no impact on fundamental rights and data protection, nor on the eu's current efforts to harmonise measures to enforce intellectual property rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion because it represents an important step in the fight against counterfeiting without calling into question issues such as the circulation of generic medicines and guaranteeing fundamental rights such as the right to privacy and data protection.
in writing. − the launch of the draft anti-counterfeiting trade agreement on 2 october 2010 following the tokyo round of negotiations is very important. however, it is also necessary that the commission communicates to parliament and the public the final text of the acta agreement after the technical aspects negotiation meeting held in sydney from 30 november to 3 december 2010. the fight against counterfeiting is a major priority of the domestic and international political strategy and international cooperation is essential to achieve this objective. we are fully aware that the negotiated agreement will not solve the complex and multi-dimensional problem of counterfeiting, but it is a step in the right direction to end this serious problem which is responsible for serious damage to the eu economy and to the gdp of the member states.
in writing. - i abstained from voting on the joint resolution tabled by the socialist and democratic, liberal, green and united left groups on acta (anti-counterfeiting trade agreement) because i consider its text to be too critical and that it should be more balanced. the text presented gives a clear indication that our final position will be against the adoption of the agreement. i believe that the agreement is overall in the union's economic interests, especially as we want to base our economy on innovation and r & d ('smart growth'). that is why, in my view, stronger protection of industrial property rights, including patents, is essential for european competitiveness. i also believe that the initial concerns about generic medicines, the protection of the right of access to the internet and the protection of geographical indications (denominations of origin) have been satisfactorily overcome in the final negotiations. we cannot ignore the progress that has been made. of course, not everything is satisfactory, but an international agreement must be judged globally.
in writing. - i am convinced that this motion represents an important step in the fight against counterfeiting while maintaining the necessary balance between conflicting values. freedom of expression and innovation are not compromised and fundamental rights such as the right to privacy and data protection are guaranteed. there are conflicting interests which make it difficult to reach consensus, but an agreement is, at its core, a meeting of common wills, which has been achieved here with some success. the commission's position on the transparency of these negotiations, keeping the ep informed, is welcome and i hope that in the next negotiations the ambiguities and omissions still being raised by all parties will be resolved. i believe that the agreement reached will strengthen international cooperation in the fight against counterfeiting, create a tool for effective protection of intellectual property rights and guarantee fundamental rights. it is also essential to ensure respect for existing rights through repressive measures and the establishment of a comprehensive international framework for assistance to the parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion because it represents an important step in the fight against counterfeiting without calling into question issues such as the circulation of generic medicines and guaranteeing fundamental rights such as the right to privacy and data protection.
in writing. − the fight against counterfeiting, which is a worldwide phenomenon, requires a multilateral approach based on enhanced cooperation between the major global players. in this respect, although i am aware that the negotiated agreement will not solve the complex problem of counterfeiting, i am convinced that it is a step in the right direction.
mr president, commissioner, i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on her excellent work on this report. the energy sector is the main engine of economic growth. since 2008, europe has had a strategy for energy and climate change. implementing this strategy is essential, but the treaty of lisbon allows us to go further, paving the way for the creation of a true energy community in europe. we need to deepen the internal energy market, build and interconnect networks, ensure energy security and solidarity and put the consumer at the centre of our concerns. there is an urgent need to increase funding and develop means and programmes to encourage energy efficiency. scientific research and technology play a key role in achieving these objectives. in this connection, i welcome the launch of several european industrial initiatives under the european strategic plan for energy technologies and call on the commission to implement the remaining measures of this plan. the 8th framework programme should also give priority to research and development of innovative technologies in the field of energy. it is therefore essential that there is adequate funding to support clean and sustainable technologies. only in this way will we be able to maintain the competitiveness of our industry, promote economic growth and create jobs.
in writing. i consider this new energy strategy to be imperative to achieving a competitive, sustainable and secure strategy. at a time when europe is increasingly dependent on imported energy, i believe it is essential that it continues to play its leading role in energy issues by focusing on innovation and technology. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common organisation of the market in raw materials and the common organisation of the market in natural gas is a welcome step towards the creation of a single market in the energy sector. i come from an ultraperipheral region which already has an energy autonomy of some 27% and which is projected to reach 75% by 2012. the azores have more ambitious specific targets than the eu, with results already recognised at european level, notably in geothermal energy, through an ambitious energy policy of partnerships between the region and the best national and international research centres. the union should look at these examples and increase its support in the field of research, innovation and development of its projects.
this report seeks to contribute to a new energy action plan under the europe 2020 strategy. in principle, a new plan can be a major initiative, provided that the errors and shortcomings of the previous ones are taken on board. it is no use insisting on the approach and proposals that have left us short of what we wanted. the following are some of the strategic shortcomings of european energy policy which should be taken into account: energy policy has been positioned as an appendage to environmental policy, the ultimate aim of which is to open up new fields for financial speculation by making greenhouse gas emission allowances profitable. but the energy problem calls for a specific approach based on improving specific indicators such as energy intensity or the energy deficit. in the energy sector too, it is assumed that by implementing the functioning of markets, where private investors operate, everything will be solved as if by magic. three successive packages of legislation have gone, public resources have been alienated and we have no competitive markets, no investment in infrastructure, no more affordable energy for consumers. a failure in the whole line of announced objectives. the argument that biofuels only have environmental advantages and would bring major agricultural and industrial development to european countries has been debunked.
mr president, i will repeat some of what has been said here. it was said that cancún is expected to be a significant intermediate step in the fight against climate change, just as it was also said that we cannot go any further or be any more ambitious than we were in copenhagen and accept what we had as a result of the copenhagen summit. we know that it was not enough, and therefore if there has been no change in the scientific evidence and the data we have, what seems to me to be a change in political will, a lack of courage, and we are afraid to go to cancun. i think that giving up cannot be an option in what is one of the most serious crises of the present time. i would also like to say that we have an opportunity to test ourselves in cancun, to test ourselves in several of the things that have already been mentioned here, but also to test ourselves in our capacity for redistribution and our capacity to support the poorest countries and the most disadvantaged populations. i believe that responding to the environmental crisis is also responding to the economic and social crisis we are experiencing today in a way that is solidarity-based and fair. this is being realistic.
the international context of this conference is not favourable: the global economic crisis, political and administrative uncertainty in the united states, the impasse in the negotiations between the united states and china. so expectations are low, but nevertheless, cop 16 should be seen as an opportunity to restore confidence in the multilateral process on climate change and consolidate the copenhagen accord. at least that, and even for that it takes determination and political leadership during the negotiations, and ambition in the decision. progress is needed particularly in areas affecting developing countries: financing, technology transfer, training. but progress is also expected on mitigation, in particular on setting ambitious and binding emission reduction targets and on the transfer of processes, including monitoring, reporting and verification. regardless of the outcome of the international negotiations, the european union must pursue the objective of reducing co2 emissions by more than 20% in order to create green jobs and economic growth. in short, the cancún outcome should contribute to the definition of the post-2012 horizon with a view to reaching a legally binding international agreement in 2011 and meeting the global target of limiting the temperature increase to two degrees.
the success of the cancun climate conference is fundamental to the credibility of the negotiating process within the united nations. it is therefore important that concrete commitments and realistic targets are set. it is essential to reach agreement on such matters as forest protection policy, technology transfer to developing countries and financing. in the event of no global agreement, there should still be an openness on the part of europe to consider a second commitment period to the kyoto protocol, but with conditions, notably on the environmental integrity of the protocol, the redesign of the clean development mechanism and the commitments of the world's major emitters such as china and the united states.
the european union bears its own responsibility for the failure of copenhagen and the lack of progress in the international negotiations. it is not enough to claim to be ambitious, setting targets above those of some other developed countries, even if they are below those recommended by the ipcc, when they do not take care of the means. more than the goals that have been the focus of the discussion, the means to achieve those goals matter and this is a central issue. the european union insists on a market approach, on market instruments which have so far revealed two things: inefficiency and perversity. we have a new treat for financial speculators: it is not just food, it is not just the sovereign debt of states, it is also the atmosphere itself, the air we breathe, which is serving up some new multi-billion dollar scheme for the generation of fictitious financial assets. commissioner, it is in the irrationality of this economic and social system that we find the causes of climate change. it is in breaking with this system that we find the solution.
in writing. for the climate summit in cancun starting next monday, i am in favour of a binding agreement with an international sanctions regime. clearly, this agreement only makes sense if it links the world's largest emitters: the united states, china and india. the eu has been a leader in the fight against climate change, and it should be encouraged to strengthen that leadership, but without forgetting the tremendous efforts our industries are already making to meet mandatory emission reductions in the european space. it is noted that the eu contributes 15% to global emissions, estimated to fall to 10% in 2030, while the us, china and india contribute half of the global emissions with a tendency to increase. i cannot therefore agree that the eu should limit itself to 30% of co2 emissions instead of the 20% target, if this is not properly accompanied by other countries, in particular the united states. this does not mean that the eu's ambition should be diminished. on the contrary, i believe that even if others do not follow, we must continue to invest in scientific research, in technological innovation in decarbonised energy, in energy efficiency and in the creation of green jobs in order to increase our competitiveness.
madam president, at the upcoming eu-africa summit in libya, eu leaders will face meles zenawi, the prime minister of ethiopia. ethiopia is not only the second most populous country in africa and the headquarters of the african union, it is also the partner – in terms of the cotonou agreement – which has prevented the delivery of the eu election report in addis ababa in 2005, and more recently in 2010, in order to avoid exposing the irregularities and the manipulation of the elections. what good is the talk of democracy, human rights and good governance, which the eu is going to have with african interlocutors, if meles zenawi, the dictator of ethiopia, is the interlocutor for africa?
the africa-eu strategic partnership established in 2007 at the lisbon summit allowed the two continents to define common strategic interests and objectives, which went beyond the traditional eu development policy. the objectives set were put into practice by the adoption of the 'africa-eu joint strategy' and the 2008-2010 action plan which identifies eight priority areas: • peace and security • democratic governance and human rights • trade, regional integration and infrastructure • millennium development goals • energy • climate change • migration, mobility and employment • science, information society and space. the 3rd africa-eu summit to be held in tripoli, libya, will focus on 'growth, investment and job creation' with the aim of outlining common long-term guidelines in these areas, while safeguarding the priorities set out in the eu 2020 strategy. i believe that this is an opportunity for portuguese economic operators to strengthen their business network in the african market, but it is important to safeguard the issues of insecurity and the high levels of crime transmitted by the portuguese community, in particular the madeiran community living in south africa. it is therefore necessary to strengthen and develop concrete and concerted cooperation, while adapting it to the new challenges in international relations.
the events in western sahara in recent weeks have not been an isolated episode. they are part of a long history of three and a half decades of repression, of violence, of oppression of a people. a history of constant attempts by morocco to block the negotiations on the realization of the inalienable right of the saharawi people to self-determination. this is therefore the occasion to condemn once again the brutal repression by the moroccan authorities in the occupied territories against all those who resist colonization and fight for the legitimate right of their people to self-determination. it is also an opportunity to denounce the real humanitarian tragedy being inflicted on the saharawi people, who are forced to live outside their homeland in refugee camps, and to call for urgently increased international humanitarian aid. we are also demanding compliance with international law and un resolutions, with the necessary holding of a referendum. the european union and its member states have a heavy responsibility in all this, which they cannot ignore or else they will become accomplices, morocco being a country which enjoys a special status as a result of the various agreements it has with the european union.
the brutal attack on the sahrawi peaceful protest camp has dealt a stab at the un-brokered talks. it reminded me of east timor in its darkest days: un talks and attacks on the population to thwart them. spain could be advocating the former colony it abandoned, as portugal was for the self-determination of east timor, but it is not, so as not to compromise business and other interests in morocco. it's been reported today that madrid and the un have been notified of the attack. from negligence to complicity, it's a chick. france has special responsibilities in encouraging morocco to continue the occupation. and the european union: the high representative didn't speak until weeks after the attack, with a minimalist statement that was irrelevant. in this resolution, parliament speaks out for the european union: it calls for an independent international inquiry into the events and the identification of the dead, missing and arrested; it calls for unrestricted access for the international press, humanitarian organisations and observers; it calls for the un to monitor human rights in western sahara and calls for the immediate release of all saharawis detained in morocco and the occupied territory of western sahara.

in writing. - we are currently experiencing an institutional impasse on the 2011 budget, with some states blocking the commission's proposal in the council. i hope that this impasse will be overcome as soon as possible, since the budget must respect the commitments and responsibilities of the european union under the lisbon treaty.
in writing. the european parliament wants the lisbon treaty to be respected and institutional peace to prevail in the eu. the ep must be involved, by voting or giving an opinion, under the treaty, in the new interinstitutional agreement, the next mff, and the definition of new own resources. as regards the interinstitutional agreement, it is obvious that flexibility for the current mff is a condition for the commitments made by the european institutions, and in particular by the council, to be respected. eu 2020, the iter programme, the eeas - external external action service -, financial supervisory bodies, are some examples that need funding. the council must incorporate the lisbon treaty both in terms of the new powers that the eu is assuming, which are reflected in the budget, and in terms of the strengthening of the ep's powers, particularly in the budgetary area, which also strengthens the democratic legitimacy of the eu institutions. we have thus a more democratic governance with the use of the community method instead of intergovernmentalism. the ep calls for the minimum that is desirable in view of the budgetary constraints of the member states.

in writing. − the inclusion of the human rights clause or the application of social and environmental standards in trade negotiations should be a principle to be safeguarded by the eu. i therefore support the eu's aim of lobbying within international organisations (including the wto and the ilo) or advocating the creation of a new environmental organisation to promote fair trade. if europe has to respect strict social and environmental standards, the same level of standards must be required of its partners, but this is possible if we take account of the progress made in the free trade agreements. however, a clear regulatory framework within the io is needed, which can be achieved by enhancing the dialogue within the io, in particular on the mandatory application of these standards in trade agreements and the necessary monitoring mechanisms and incentive practices, as well as the strengthening of arbitration panels. gsp instruments, which allow the union to grant trade preferences unilaterally, could be an opportunity to identify more accurately the beneficiaries taking into account their level of development and the monitoring of the commitments made.
in writing. - i believe that social and environmental standards are not incompatible with the commercial interests of the european union and its partners. strengthen cooperation between international organisations in the framework of a global climate agreement, including on carbon mechanisms complementary to the community's emissions trading system, while ensuring that existing gaps are closed. i support the eu should also lead efforts towards the use of bilateral free trade, so as to include not only human rights terms but also sustainable development issues.
in writing. − i recognise the complexity of the discussion on the inclusion of human rights and social and environmental clauses in trade agreements and am mindful of the imbalance between international trade rules and other rules of international law. i believe that the european union has a decisive role to play in the search for a new model of global governance and, in this respect, it must promote the coherence of the policies developed by the international institutions. i believe that the european union must be able to strike a balance between a restrictive and a liberal approach to trade, and a compromise between defending its commercial interests and demanding respect for the values on which it is based. it is therefore necessary to foster dialogue and partnerships of cooperation with international institutions, in particular the world trade organisation and the international labour organisation. i would also point out that the treaty of lisbon has introduced changes in the area of trade policy which are in line with some of the proposals made in this report. i therefore vote in favour of most of the measures contained in this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'human rights, social and environmental standards in international trade agreements', because trade policy must be consistent with the eu's objectives and must contribute to safeguarding its social model and environmental policy. as such, it is of the utmost importance that the eu ensures that certain social and environmental standards are applied in international trade agreements.
in writing. - the question of whether we should trade with those who do not have the same standards of respect for human rights is an old one in international relations and threatens to become eternal. i believe, with the utmost realism, that the union must strive to ensure greater acceptance of standards deemed appropriate and seek to link the countries with which it negotiates to the global effort to respect those rights. i believe that the union cannot fail to recognize the importance and centrality of this issue in the economic and diplomatic field when it comes to establishing lasting trade channels. however, as is well known, we are not always in a position to impose these standards or to make such demands. while these are often formally respected, it is also true that the union is aware of partners who regularly fail to comply with them. the main energy suppliers in europe are: that said, i would reiterate the importance of continuing to fight for human rights and making them a condition for the establishment of sound trade relations.
in writing. − the inclusion of the human rights clause or the application of social and environmental standards in trade negotiations are complex issues that divide the international community. on the one hand, the nordic countries denounce the social and environmental dumping practiced by the emerging countries, which distorts competition in trade; on the other hand, the countries of the south are suspicious that the countries of the north intend to impede their economic development and resort, by applying these rules, to a form of disguised protectionism. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that trade policy must function as an instrument in the service of the overall objectives of the european union and it is therefore important that trade is not seen as an end in itself but as a tool for promoting european trade interests and also fair trade, capable of generalising the inclusion and effective implementation of social and environmental standards with all the eu's trading partners.
in writing. − eu countries and all their economic actors are scrupulously committed to respecting human rights and social and environmental standards, and it is only natural that their trading partners should be required to do the same in the wto, if world trade is to become fairer and more equitable. we are aware that sometimes these obligations are not easy to fulfil, particularly in the so-called emerging countries. however, the eu must continue to make an effort to make this happen, and it is therefore up to the eu and the european parliament to make every effort to defend respect for human life, that fair work is equal anywhere in the world and for everyone, and that the meaning of environmental and social rights (trade union rights, the fight against child labour, etc.) has a universal aspect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on human rights and social and environmental standards in international trade agreements, as i agree with the inclusion of human rights clauses or the application of social and environmental standards in trade negotiations. the tension between the countries of the north, which denounce social and environmental dumping by the emerging countries, and the countries of the south, which suspect that the countries of the north intend to impede their economic development and resort, by applying these rules, to a form of disguised protectionism, is a reality. however, this conflict of interest cannot block a positive, but also legally binding, approach by the eu in its negotiations, with the inclusion of provisions on sustainable development, in particular in bilateral agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that the european union, which plays a crucial role in the search for a new world economic governance, should seek to promote the coherence of the policies implemented by the various international institutions. there is now a growing imbalance between the specific rules of international trade and the other international rules. as frontline actors, we have an obligation to find new avenues of reflection, in particular by seeking to establish genuine coordination between international bodies.
in writing. the role of the european administration is vast and complex. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to ensure citizens' trust in the european institutions through an efficient administration where procedures are transparent and access to infrastructure is facilitated. i welcome the positive results in terms of reducing complaints and improving their handling at european level.
in writing. − the ombudsman's work is essential and contributes to greater transparency, bringing the union closer to citizens, while strengthening the trust that citizens place in the institutions' ability to enforce their rights. although there was a slight decrease in the number of complaints (9%) in 2009 compared to 2008, of the 335 open investigations, some 318 were completed and closed. it is quite positive that 56% of cases were closed because they were settled or subject to an amicable agreement. these results demonstrate the constructive cooperation between the ombudsman and the union institutions and bodies, which in most cases see these complaints as the ideal opportunity to remedy any mistakes made and to cooperate with the ombudsman for the benefit of citizens. i would stress the importance of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which included the right to good administration among the fundamental rights inherent in union citizenship and introduced two substantial changes: the fact that the ombudsman is now elected, reinforcing his democratic legitimacy; and the fact that his mandate has been extended to the area of the common foreign and security policy.
in writing. − the ombudsman registered a total of 3 098 complaints in 2009, compared with 3 406 in 2008, a decrease of 9%. the complaints were addressed to: the european commission (56%), the administration of the european parliament (11%), the european personnel selection office (epso) (9%), the council (4%) and the court of justice (3%). the main complaint was about maladministration and lack of transparency, including the refusal to provide information, which is so crucial to ensuring the security and confidence of citizens in the union. the need to work towards better administration and greater transparency in the institutions was thus demonstrated, and this can be achieved by a joint effort between the ombudsman and the institutions, in particular through a continuous exchange of good practice.
in writing. − the role of the european ombudsman is very important, as it helps to bring citizens closer to the european institutions. the ombudsman registered a total of 3 098 complaints in 2009, compared with 3 406 in 2008, a decrease of 9% compared with 2008, and 335 complaint-based inquiries were opened and 230 complaints were declared inadmissible. the majority of inquiries opened by the ombudsman in 2009 were against the european commission (56%). the complaints also concerned the administration of the european parliament (11%), the european personnel selection office (epso) (9%), the council (4%) and the court of justice (3%). twenty-three other eu institutions and bodies were also the subject of 59 investigations (17%). the figures in the report clearly demonstrate the efficiency of this body and its importance in the transparency of relations between the european institutions and citizens.
in writing. − the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2009 reveals a high level of activity by the body. the new legal framework reflecting the changes to the statute of the epp and the entry into force of the tfeu adding the cfsp and the activities of the european council to the ombudsman's mandate did not affect the pace of work. the average time taken to deal with complaints has gone from 13 months to 9 months. to stress the clear willingness of the community institutions and bodies to see complaints to the epo as an opportunity to redress mistakes and to cooperate with the ombudsman for the benefit of citizens. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the 2009 annual report and sets out guidelines for the future, including the following: the call to the ombudsman to ensure compliance with the charter of fundamental rights, which has been legally binding since lisbon; the call to the commission to draw up a european administrative law common to all the union's bodies, institutions and agencies; and the warning to the ombudsman to follow the new process for the selection of staff for the european institutions through epso.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, stressing the key role played by the european ombudsman in ensuring respect for citizens' rights in the eu and in promoting a culture of service to the citizen in the institutions, based on best practice in good administration.
in writing. − the ombudsman's special report follows the commission's refusal to disclose to an environmental protection ngo three letters (part of a set of 18) sent by porsche ag to commissioner günter verheugen concerning the exchange of information between the commission and car manufacturers on a possible approach to be taken on carbon dioxide emissions from vehicles. following the ombudsman's request to the commission for a reasoned opinion on the non-disclosure of the documents, the commission extended its reply for six times (15 months), thus violating the principles of good faith and cooperation, undermining interinstitutional dialogue and the public image of the union. it is the responsibility of the european parliament, as the sole elected body of the union, to safeguard and protect the independence of the european ombudsman in the performance of his duties towards european citizens and to monitor the implementation of his recommendation to the european commission.
in writing. - article 228 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union gives the european ombudsman the power to receive complaints from any citizen of the union concerning maladministration in the activities of the union institutions or bodies. these complaints by eu citizens are an important source of information on possible breaches of union law. article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights states that 'every person has the right to have his or her affairs handled impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time by the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union'. in the context of the consultations provided for in article 4 (4) of regulation 1049/2001, the commission shall set a deadline for the author of a document to reply and shall exercise this power in such a way as to respect its own deadlines. furthermore, the commission cannot delay or obstruct inquiries by the ombudsman in cases relating to questions of access to documents, and must respond to the ombudsman without delay in order to fulfil the duty of sincere cooperation as provided for in the treaty.
in writing. − the role of the european ombudsman is well defined and consists of investigating complaints against the institutions and bodies of the european union (eu). such powers lead to greater transparency in the relations of citizens, businesses, associations or other bodies with a registered office in the union with the european institutions. the complaint lodged by the ngo concerned in this report relates to access to documentation held by the commission. the ombudsman gave the commission three months to submit a detailed opinion, and it did so only after 15 months. by this behaviour the commission has failed to fulfil its obligation to cooperate with the ombudsman in a frank and good faith manner during the inquiry, damaging not only the interinstitutional dialogue but also the public image of the european union. i consider the european parliament, as the sole elected body of the union, responsible for protecting the independence of the european ombudsman in the performance of his duties towards european citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the special report of the european ombudsman to the european parliament following the draft recommendation submitted to the european commission concerning complaint 676/2008/rt concerning the serious delay in the european commission's response to the ombudsman's services. i share the ombudsman's concerns and criticisms as excessive delays in responding to the ombudsman in any proceedings are a breach of the duty of sincere cooperation as laid down in the treaty. the commission's response to the ombudsman's request for information was not received. the ombudsman's reply was not received.
in writing. − this special report by the ombudsman followed a complaint lodged following the commission's refusal to disclose three letters sent by porsche ag to commissioner günter verheugen, and the commission subsequently extended the deadline for issuing a detailed opinion on the ombudsman's draft recommendation six times. it's important that situations like this don't happen again. the eu institutions have a duty to cooperate with each other in good faith in their relations and the fulfilment of this obligation is essential to safeguard the trust of citizens in european institutional actors.
in writing. - it is regrettable that several member states underestimate the importance of correct and timely application of eu legislation. poor and late transposition and inadequate implementation and enforcement create legal uncertainty and prevent citizens and businesses from reaping the benefits of the internal market. in 2008, 55% of the transpositions required were late, in many cases by two years or more. although the figures show an improvement of 15% in that year, we must bear in mind that there was also a 40% reduction in the volume of transpositions to be made. it is unacceptable that in may 2009 there were some 22 directives with transposition deadlines that had expired more than two years ago, and whose transposition had not yet been completed by one to five member states. to ensure more correct, effective and timely application of eu law and to detect early possible implementation problems, it is essential to strengthen cooperation between the eu institutions and national authorities, as well as between member states' administrations.
in writing. − as the european union is a legal construct, based on treaties and legislative acts, it is essential that these are correctly and uniformly applied in the 27 member states. however, we know that the member states often fail to apply or transpose the rules of community law in a timely manner or that they apply or transpose them in a weak or incomplete way. as the imco commission points out, 'poor and late transposition and inadequate implementation and enforcement of the rules create legal uncertainty and prevent citizens and businesses from fully enjoying the benefits of the internal market'. it is therefore essential that member states do not underestimate the value of the correct and timely application of eu law and that the commission keeps parliament duly informed on the state of implementation of eu law.
in writing. − poor and late transposition and inadequate implementation and enforcement of the rules create legal uncertainty and prevent citizens and businesses from fully enjoying the benefits of the internal market. it is therefore important that there is closer and more permanent cooperation between the eu institutions and national authorities, as well as between member states' administrations, in order to ensure the correct, effective and timely application of eu law. to this end, it is important that the european parliament and national parliaments use the new framework for cooperation established by the lisbon treaty and conduct annual reviews of the implementation process in a specific area of the single market. i would like to stress the paragraph in this report which calls for the commission to provide detailed data on all types of infringement and for all such data to be made freely available to parliament in order to enable it to play its role of monitoring. the compilation and classification of these data should be consistent with previous annual reports in order to help parliament to make relevant assessments of the progress made by the commission.
in writing. − annual reports on monitoring the application of european union law are essential to gauge how eu law is being applied by the member states. in 2008, 55% of the transpositions required were late, in many cases by two years or more. although the figures show an improvement of 15% in that year, we must bear in mind that there was also a 40% reduction in the volume of transpositions to be made. we can therefore conclude that there is still a long way to go before the rules deriving from community law are properly and timely transposed into the member states. only if this is achieved will it be possible for citizens and businesses to enjoy the full benefits of the internal market.
in writing. − the 26th annual report on monitoring the application of european union law (2008) aims to highlight the problems in the application and transposition of eu law. this is a document which, if properly drafted and with a comprehensive systematic framework, could be a mechanism for monitoring and speeding up the process of developing eu law. the absence of new methodologies and the lack of information in this report have led to criticism from the ep, which i support in voting in favour of this report. i cannot, however, fail to stress that delays in the correct application and transposition of eu law, in addition to creating a lack of confidence in the european institutions, affect us all as european citizens and have associated costs, making it impossible to enjoy the rights created by diplomas, generating legal uncertainty and preventing citizens from fully benefiting from the internal market. i therefore share the desire to ensure that the commission continues to provide detailed data on all types of infringement and that all such data are freely available to parliament, allowing it to play its role of monitoring the commission's compliance with its duty as guardian of the treaties.
in writing. − i believe that an assessment should be made of the added value that eu pilot brings to the infringement case management process. the availability of relevant data obviously depends on this. i would also like to stress, in line with what is said in the report, that national courts play a decisive role in the application of european union law. it is therefore necessary to support the union's efforts to improve and coordinate the judicial training of national judges and of the legal profession in general.
in writing. − broadcasting services are one of the most important sources of information available to citizens in the eu member states. as such, they are a major factor in influencing people's values and opinions. a balanced european system plays a key role in promoting democracy, social cohesion, integration and freedom of expression, with particular emphasis on preserving and promoting media pluralism, media literacy, cultural and linguistic diversity and respect for european standards on freedom of the press. the commission should adapt copyright to the new digital age, allowing broadcasting services to continue to provide a wide range of quality european content, and consider specific ways to facilitate the re-use of archive content and put in place extended collective licensing schemes and simple one-stop systems for clearing rights.
in writing. − access to information and participation of citizens in public debate are essential in a democratic european society. it is essential that there is an independent and competitive audiovisual and print media sector. in the current context of the audiovisual sector in the eu, it is in the general interest to safeguard the so-called dual system, ensuring a true balance between public service broadcasters and private broadcasters. only in this way can we ensure that there is a fairly diverse programme and contribute to pluralism, cultural and linguistic diversity, editorial competition in the media and freedom of expression. it is essential that there is a strong, viable public service broadcasting system, free from political pressure or lack of editorial independence and with the necessary financial support, although care should always be taken not to jeopardise the existence of fair competition with private operators. it is the eu's role to try to bring together the different stakeholders in the media sector with the aim of maintaining the existence of a healthy and viable industry. i believe that the implementation of the monitoring mechanism for media pluralism can play an essential role.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the media, public and private, must be free from political and economic pressure to carry out their duties. the dual european system can play a key role in promoting democracy and freedom of expression, and in preserving and promoting media pluralism, cultural and linguistic diversity.
in writing. − the importance of ensuring the pluralism of broadcasting services derives from the central role they play in our society, both in terms of information and pluralism and in promoting rights, freedoms and guarantees, thus contributing unequivocally to a more informed and participatory society. it is therefore essential to ensure that these services have financial and editorial independence, avoiding their politicization or their subordination to economic interests. recently in portugal, there have been several allegations of possible government interference in the news landscape, including the replacement of the director of a daily newspaper and the information director of a radio station, and the abrupt closure of a television news channel and the replacement of the general director of this private channel. in addition, there were several episodes of the removal of critical columnists and an alleged plan for a company in which the state holds a golden share to acquire a stake in a media company that owns a private channel. in this respect, it is essential to promote a two-tier system in the union which guarantees independence at all levels and ensures freedom of expression in both public and private broadcasting services, since the latter are not free from political interference.
in writing. - the eu audiovisual landscape is characterised by a 'double system'. the coexistence of public and commercial broadcasters has ensured a very diverse programme. it contributes to pluralism, cultural and linguistic diversity, editorial competition (in terms of quality and diversity of content) in the media and freedom of expression. i stress the need for member states to tackle the digital divide between urban and rural areas and to ensure that, through digitalisation, all individuals in all regions enjoy equitable access to public service broadcasting, as well as to offer attractive and quality content to attract young people accessing the media.
in writing. - we have seen a little bit of interference by the political powers in broadcasting services, whether public or private, all over the eu. in portugal there have been several strange situations recently with tv news broadcasters being suspended, tv station heads and managers being replaced for no apparent plausible reason, seemingly on political mandate. of course, the public sector is more subject to this type of pressure, but the private sector is not immune to it, as its revenues often depend on the sale of advertising space to the state sector. citizens have the right to a broadcasting service, whether public or private, which is independent and free in its approach to all content. i am therefore convinced that the dual european system will play a key role in promoting democracy and freedom of expression, as well as in preserving and promoting media pluralism and cultural and linguistic diversity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on public service broadcasting in the digital age: the future of the dual system, considering that the role of public service broadcasting in a multimedia society must take account of the concentration and pluralism of the media in the european union, media literacy in the digital world, the diversity of content and the guarantee of the independence of the public service broadcasting as a mission in the information society. indeed, the dual broadcasting system, in which public and private media perform their respective functions free from political and economic pressures, is important for access to information of the highest quality and for the promotion of democracy itself. public and private broadcasting services have a crucial role to play in european audiovisual production, cultural diversity and identity, information, pluralism, social cohesion, the promotion of fundamental freedoms and the functioning of democracy. i support the recommendations made, stressing the encouragement of the exchange of best practice between member states and the intensification of cooperation between national media regulators in the european platform of regulatory authorities (epra).
in writing. - i consider it very important that the european union brings together the different actors and stakeholders in the media sector with the aim of moving towards the formation of a healthy and economically viable industry. the rapid transformation of the media, in particular digital media, will require new solutions and will necessarily lead to the definition of a 'new media ecology'.
in writing. − women, peace and security are areas to which the utmost attention should be given. the 10th anniversary of un security council resolution 1325 is an opportunity to make progress in these areas, as are all the ongoing european policy reviews, in particular on human rights and the fight against violence against women, the use of children in armed conflict and the fight against all forms of discrimination. in addition, another aspect which i think is relevant to this report is the fact that it calls for the promotion of women's participation in reconciliation, peacebuilding and conflict prevention activities, which reinforced my positive vote for the adoption of the report.
in writing. - we are now celebrating the 10th anniversary of this first un resolution on the specific and disproportionate impact of armed conflict situations on women. i hope that the eu can take this opportunity to give a strong political signal and to step up efforts to implement it, either through political guidelines or through increased financial resources. i also hope that the current review of the eu's human rights policy will lead to the development of a coherent human rights strategy and to an assessment of the eu's guidelines on violence against women and girls and the situation of children in situations of armed conflict, with the aim of combating all forms of violence and discrimination. i believe that the establishment of the european external action service can contribute to a better implementation of these resolutions, while at the same time it should highlight the role of the eu in this area. i congratulate the 10 member states, including portugal, which have already adopted a national action plan for the implementation of this resolution and i hope that all the others will follow suit as soon as possible.
in writing. when we think of armed conflict and the more traditional war scenarios, we imagine men as their first victims. it turns out that, unfortunately, all over the world, where there are armed conflicts and threats to peace, women and children are often the first and most important victims, albeit silent. women face many threats, whether in the context of war and conflict, whether in the context of the practice of barbaric customs that violate their rights, or in the context of poverty and social exclusion. it is therefore important that europe does not forget the women who suffer daily violations of their most basic rights, such as life and physical integrity, the women who are sentenced to death by stoning, the women who are denied access to education, the women who are forced to flee and live as refugees in order to enjoy the freedom that the bill of rights gives us all and the women who are discriminated against solely on the basis of their gender. in the end, may europe not forget and turn its back on all the women who are still denied the guarantee of a future of freedom and hope.
in writing. - violence against women in conflict zones is often an extension of gender discrimination which unfortunately already exists in peacetime. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to allocate financial and human resources to the participation of women and the integration of gender issues in the field of foreign and security policy. i stress the need to establish appropriate public complaint procedures in the context of csdp missions to facilitate, in particular, the reporting of sexual and gender-based violence and invite the hr/vp to include detailed information on women, peace and security in the semi-annual evaluation of csdp missions.
in writing. - we voted against this resolution because we believe that it is not enough to have a gender perspective in civil and military missions. it is not because more women are assigned to military missions of intervention in wars and occupations, such as in iraq or afghanistan, that the problems of discrimination against women are solved or that wars become more just. reality shows us that this is not so. we believe that military interventions do not help to protect women's rights, but rather increase the violations of these rights. only conflict prevention and the application of civil measures in conflict situations are capable of fulfilling the promise of resolution 1325. we therefore regret that our amendments were not adopted.
in writing. − although we are celebrating the 10th anniversary of un security council resolution 1325 on women, peace and security, much remains to be done in this area, particularly with regard to violence against women, eu guidelines on the use of children in armed conflict and the fight against all forms of discrimination against them. it is time for us all to join forces to make this plan come true.
in writing. − ten years have passed since the adoption of un security council (unsc) resolutions 1325 (2000) and 1820 (2008) on women, peace and security, and unsc resolution 1888 (2009) on sexual violence against women and children in situations of armed conflict. these resolutions emphasise the responsibility of all states to end impunity and to prosecute those responsible for crimes against humanity and war crimes, including those relating to acts of sexual and other violence against women and girls. ten years have passed since the adoption of these resolutions, and as stated in the resolution which i voted in favour of, there is still a long way to go. the international day for the elimination of violence against women, which was celebrated on 25 november, the date of the vote on this resolution, is not just another day, but a warning to a reality that persists. these issues must be addressed at the highest level and remain on the political agenda until this scourge, which knows no race, creed or age, is eradicated.
in writing. - i hope that the 10th anniversary of security council resolution 1325 will mark the beginning of a reinvigorated agenda for the implementation of commitments on women, peace and security.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the mortality of bees is increasing and the number of beekeepers is decreasing. this is a problematic situation for agriculture and biodiversity, as 76% of food production and 84% of plant species depend on pollination. i am in favour of a higher level of research, which will help to achieve better responses and a more correct reinforcement of measures to promote biodiversity and reduce the effects of climate instability, because the life of a worker bee is very short and very sensitive to changes in the external environment. so honey production has also been affected, not only by the duration and stability of the increasingly uncertain seasons, but also by the increase in external aggression that may result from the use of pesticides, mites or other. the current programmes must therefore be strengthened in the framework of the new cap, so that we can also achieve a more effective level of response at this level.
in writing. − bees play an important role in the ecological balance and their extinction has serious consequences for the food chain. this report aims to reinforce the necessary promotion and improvement of the beekeeping sector, in particular in terms of statistical data for honey production forecasts, the improvement and harmonisation of monitoring and research programmes, clarity in the definition of provisions on the labelling of honey origin, the drawing up of beekeeping programmes and related legislation, and the development of innovative and effective treatments against varroa mites.
in writing. - 40% of the european honey market is currently dependent on imports, which leads to enormous price volatility and puts beekeepers across the eu, including portuguese beekeepers, at a competitive disadvantage compared to honey from third countries. in portugal, according to official statistics, there are 17,291 beekeepers, with 38,203 apiaries and 562,557 colonies. production in 2009 was 6,654 tonnes of honey and 235 tonnes of wax, representing 1,9% of eu honey production (351 thousand tonnes). the action of bees and beekeeping is fundamental to the maintenance of ecosystems, the ecological balance of flora and the preservation of biodiversity, and economically it is an activity that makes perfect sense for europe to protect and encourage, so as to become less dependent on imports.
in writing. − bees are indispensable for the pollination of crops, for the maintenance of the ecological balance and as a preservation element of biodiversity. it is therefore regrettable that the number of colonies is decreasing, a phenomenon for which we need scientific data to enable us to understand the mechanisms that contribute to the spread of this species and to develop mechanisms for its preservation. i think it is essential to focus on european honey, which is gradually being replaced by other honey of lower quality and which does not meet the criteria for production in the eu.
in writing. - the eu is heavily dependent on imports in this beekeeping sector, as about 40% of the honey we consume is imported. given the strategic role of the beekeeping sector in society, taking into account the public and environmental service provided by beekeepers, and given that this activity is a valuable example of 'green employment' (improvement and maintenance of biodiversity, ecological balance and conservation of flora) and a model of sustainable production in rural areas, it is in the interest of all to support the sector so that it can grow sustainably and we become less and less dependent on third countries. in my country too, this sector must be nurtured so that the benefits of its activity are visible both in economic and environmental terms and so that honey production increases, as it currently amounts to only 1.9% of eu production.
in writing. - i welcome the resolution adopted by a large majority at the strasbourg plenary session on 25 november, which includes important contributions from azorean beekeepers transmitted in the course of direct consultation conducted by me. however, the text of the final resolution falls short of my initial expectations, as some of the issues of fundamental importance to producers, such as the issue of quality standards and labelling for imported honey, should have been more thoroughly dealt with. this was not the case, probably because of a lack of sensitivity to some of the important problems in the sector, which led, for example, to the fact that local labelling was not included in the final text of the resolution. the resolution nevertheless deals with important issues for azorean and also national beekeeping in general, following the work carried out in the sector, such as honey imported from third countries, which has serious quality problems and is currently insufficiently labelled; the need to continue to ensure diversified agriculture to ensure pollination; and, finally, the importance of common approval and research within the community.
in writing. − the beekeeping sector plays a strategic role in society, providing a valuable example of 'green employment' (improving and maintaining biodiversity, ecological balance and conservation of flora) and a model of sustainable production in rural areas. this sector faces numerous challenges and problems at european level, including marketing, price volatility, promotion of beekeeping among young people, declining numbers of bee colonies and increasing bee mortality, and it therefore makes sense to strengthen support for this sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on a new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020 because i consider this new energy strategy imperative to achieve a competitive, sustainable and secure strategy. at a time when europe is increasingly dependent on imported energy, i believe it is essential that europe continues to play its leading role in energy issues by investing in innovation and technology. i believe that for the energy strategy to be more sustainable, we must continue to focus on renewable energy by introducing greater competition in the sector, so that we can achieve an effective internal energy market which will lead to cost reductions and increased competitiveness of the economy, and also generate wealth and employment, which are important for the balance of trade. i come from an ultraperipheral region which already has an energy autonomy of some 27% and which is projected to reach 75% by 2012. the azores have more ambitious specific targets than the eu, with results already recognised at european level, notably in geothermal energy, through an ambitious energy policy of partnerships between the region and the best national and international research centres.
in writing. - the energy sector is a key driver of economic growth. since 2008, europe has had a strategy for energy and climate change. it is essential to implement this strategy. however, the lisbon treaty allows us to go further, paving the way for the creation of a true energy community in europe. we need to deepen the internal energy market, build and interconnect energy networks and ensure energy security and solidarity and put the consumer at the centre of our concerns. there is an urgent need to increase funding and develop more means and programmes to encourage energy efficiency. scientific research and technology play a key role in achieving these objectives. in this connection, i welcome the launch of the various european industrial initiatives under the european strategic plan for energy technologies and call on the commission to implement the remaining measures of this plan. the 8th framework programme should give priority to research and development of innovative technologies in the field of energy. it is therefore essential that there is adequate funding to support clean and sustainable technologies. only in this way will we be able to maintain the competitiveness of our industry, promote economic growth and create jobs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'a new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020' because i believe that a new strategic direction for the energy sector is needed to meet the objectives of article 194 of the treaty, the 20-20-20 targets set in the energy and climate package, and the long-term target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80% to 95% by 2050.
in writing. − the commission has set three objectives for european energy policy: (i) to move towards a low-carbon energy system; (ii) to ensure security of energy supply; and (iii) to ensure that the union's competitiveness is strengthened and that energy is supplied to all consumers at affordable prices. i agree with these three objectives in general, but i think there is a fourth and perhaps more important challenge missing here: the reduction of energy dependence, particularly as regards fossil fuels. in addition, the target of reducing carbon emissions will have to be viewed very carefully in order to minimise the risks of carbon leakage and loss of competitiveness for european industries.
