in writing. − the commission document 'towards a new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020' is an excellent contribution to an overall eu policy for the energy sector under the eu 2020 strategy. the lisbon treaty provides a solid legal basis for the development of energy initiatives based on sustainability, security of supply, network interconnection and solidarity. we can have a new strategy for the energy sector to meet the objectives of article 194 of the treaty and the 20-20-20 targets set in the climate package. new actions to be taken in the energy sector should aim at moving towards a low-carbon energy system, where the security of energy supply for all is ensured, while ensuring the competitiveness of the union and the supply of energy to all consumers at affordable prices. the objectives of the lisbon treaty of a single energy market, security of supply, energy efficiency, energy saving, the development of new and renewable forms of energy and the promotion of energy networks must be met. this strategy should be implemented in a spirit of solidarity and responsibility so that no member state is left behind or isolated.
in writing. the european energy strategy advocated in this report - and advocated by the commission in its various communications on the subject - is closely linked to the definition of a community policy described in the lisbon treaty: 'completion of the internal energy market'. the rapporteur calls for the drawing up of 'plans for the creation of a european energy community', insisting on the application and transposition by the member states of the current internal market directives, while accepting 'as a last resort the possibility of re-introducing the main provisions of the current internal market directives in the form of regulations in order to ensure their direct and full application throughout the single market'. as we have said, we are totally opposed to this proposal as the energy solution for europe and have therefore voted against the report. this is a strategic sector for the economy and the functioning of a state, which must be sovereign in defining its energy policies. in addition, the increasing reliance on imports of primary resources and the consumer price of energy combined with the divestment of energy infrastructure have already revealed the failure of this private market strategy. only the public sector can ensure that everyone has access to energy, that it is managed effectively and efficiently, and that we are less dependent on fossil fuels.
in writing. − the energy strategy for europe 2011-2020 sets out broad guidelines aimed at strengthening the newly defined internal energy market. this report strengthens the areas of competition and market instruments, but is not ambitious on renewable energy or reducing energy consumption. the commission has also taken the initiative of proposing a new regulation on the protection of the environment. finally, it links european energy security to close cooperation with nato. for these and other reasons i voted against.
in writing. the three objectives outlined by the commission for european energy policy are very clear and ambitious, namely: moving towards a low-carbon energy system, ensuring security of energy supply and ensuring the enhancement of the union's competitiveness and the supply of energy to all consumers at affordable prices. to achieve them , a very strong financial and human effort is required .
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on a new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020 (2010/2108 (ini)) because, following the rapporteur's lead, i consider that the lisbon treaty, by including a specific chapter on energy, now provides a sound legal basis for the development of energy initiatives based on sustainability, security of supply, network interconnection and solidarity. this requires a strong leadership from the commission, together with a convincing demonstration of the will and clear support of the member states, to confront the problem of late or poor implementation of energy legislation and the lack of comprehensive energy strategies. in this sense, the document 'towards a new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020' is a first step towards a comprehensive european union policy for the energy sector under the eu 2020 strategy. the strategy proposed for the union highlights the following: ensuring support for modern integrated networks, ensuring security of energy supply, promoting energy research, development and innovation and placing consumers and citizens at the centre of eu energy policy.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty sets out a set of clear energy policy objectives: ensuring the functioning of the internal energy market, security of supply, energy efficiency and the promotion of energy networks and renewable energy sources. the eu therefore needs to adopt a new energy strategy to achieve these objectives and the 20-20-20 targets set in the climate package.
in writing. - an energy strategy for europe is essential to implement the new policy under the lisbon treaty. there is now a solid legal basis for developing energy initiatives based on sustainability, security of supply and network interconnection and solidarity. the objectives of a structured plan, as presented to the european parliament, should be the completion of a single energy market and the security and efficiency of energy supply. it is a fact that the energy sector in europe faces many current and future challenges. the european union is increasingly dependent on imported energy and its production at home requires high investment, at a time when it is still facing the consequences of an economic crisis. i would like to stress the importance of exploiting the potential of renewable energy in the european union better and of putting eu consumers and citizens at the centre of european energy policy. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union should actively contribute to making the cancun climate change conference a promising and transparent one, particularly as regards financing for adaptation, forestry, resource efficiency, technology transfer, surveillance, reporting and verification. the european union should therefore also facilitate the building of strong political engagement with third countries through the development of policies that create effective mechanisms for international cooperation on climate change, both within and outside the united nations framework convention on climate change. the historical responsibility of developed countries for the irreversibility of climate change and their obligation to assist developing and least developed countries in their adaptation to climate change should also be emphasised, including through the provision of financial support to national adaptation action programmes, which are important instruments for climate change adaptation that promote ownership.
in writing. − the success of the cancun climate conference is fundamental to the credibility of the negotiating process within the united nations. it is therefore important that concrete commitments and realistic targets are set. it is essential to reach agreement on such issues as policies for the protection of forests, the transfer of technology to developing countries and financing. in the event of no global agreement, there should still be an openness on the part of europe to consider a second commitment period to the kyoto protocol, imposing conditions, notably on the environmental integrity of the protocol, the redesign of the clean development mechanism and the commitments of the world's major emitters such as china and the united states.
in writing. - i vote in favour of most of the measures and proposals contained in this report. following the unambitious outcome of the copenhagen conference, there is a need to restore confidence in international climate change negotiations. it is up to the european union to take up its leadership role in the climate change negotiations and to actively contribute to more constructive, transparent and bold compromise solutions coming out of cancún. i also believe that the european union should aim to step up its action in the field of climate diplomacy by seeking solid commitments with third countries in the design of policies that create effective instruments and mechanisms for international cooperation on environmental protection and climate change. in this attempt to achieve more ambitious and bold results, i also believe that, at the final stage of the cop16 negotiations, the chief negotiator on behalf of the european union should be given some flexibility so that he is able to react to the developments in the negotiations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the cancún climate conference because i believe that the european parliament must send a clear message that it is necessary for world leaders to show political determination and leadership during the negotiations in order to make progress towards the convention and the kyoto protocol.
in writing. − regardless of the debate on the origin of climate change, the role of human action in its verification and the power of human action to reverse it, it is now clear that the issue has very serious implications in the most varied areas of human life and threatens to provoke various imbalances on a global scale. it cannot therefore be left unattended with concern and rigor. climate change has caused, among other things, worrying sea level rise, forced migration, the struggle for access to waterways and the most fertile land, and has, as in the case of sudan, pitted nomadic herders against sedentary farmers. the european union must actively participate in this global effort and do its utmost to follow up the problem and to find lasting solutions which, ideally, can reconcile scientific and technological progress and the development of populations with environmental quality and respect for nature. the cancun conference is an excellent moment to pursue this objective, to set more ambitious targets and to achieve a more solid and comprehensive collective commitment to tackling the problem.
in writing. - for the cancun climate summit i advocate a binding agreement which includes an international sanctioning regime. clearly, this agreement only makes sense if it links the world's largest emitters: the united states, china and india. the eu has been a leader in the fight against climate change, and it should be encouraged to strengthen that leadership, but without forgetting the tremendous efforts our industries are already making to meet mandatory emission reductions in the european space. it is noted that the eu contributes 15% to global emissions, estimated to fall to 10% in 2030, while the us, china and india contribute half of the global emissions with a tendency to increase. i cannot therefore agree that the eu should limit itself to 30% of co2 emissions instead of the 20% target if this is not properly accompanied by other countries, in particular the united states. this does not mean that the eu's ambition should be diminished. on the contrary, i believe that even if others do not follow, we must continue to invest in scientific research, in technological innovation in decarbonised energy, in energy efficiency and in the creation of green jobs, in order to increase our competitiveness.
in writing. - this resolution repeats some of the shortcomings, weaknesses and mistakes of the position adopted by parliament at the copenhagen summit (cop15), failing to recognise the causes of its resounding failure. the discussion remains overly focused on the reduction targets, to the detriment of the means to achieve them, which discredits the whole discussion. it insists on a market approach when market instruments have already revealed their inefficiency and perversity. it falls short of what would be necessary in discussing the distortions introduced by the so-called flexibility mechanisms and the need for their abolition or reformulation. there is a clear misunderstanding of the deep meaning and significance of the principle of "common but differentiated responsibility" when historically large emitters (such as the us, the world's largest per capita emitter, which resists making serious reduction commitments) and emerging economies such as china or india (with per capita emissions 10 and 4 times lower than the us respectively) are put on an equal footing. as regards the financing of adaptation and mitigation in developing countries, serious constraints on these countries, such as the colossal and unfair external debt of the least developed countries, continue to be ignored. despite some positive points, the general content of the resolution does not merit our support.
in writing. - once again, expectations are high for the cancún climate conference. the countries with the greatest responsibility in this area have to continue to work on reducing greenhouse gas emissions. this is a problem that requires a short-term solution and is of concern to the whole world. the eu must be able to show its leadership in the fight against climate change. and all countries, from the united states to the so-called emerging countries, including china, which is a major polluter, must also shoulder all the responsibilities in a struggle which leaves less and less room for new opportunities. the sustaining future of mankind is increasingly at stake in a process that, if nothing is done in due time, may reach the point of no return.
in writing. - cop16 is crucial for all of us in europe and for citizens of the world in general. we need a responsible and ambitious policy at this level from all political actors. the european union has a key role to play and should lead the way in ambition in the context of climate change. in this context i voted against the european parliament's resolution because i consider that the objectives set are not very ambitious. in fact, i cannot accept a target higher than 1.5 degrees in a future global post-2012 international agreement in south africa, given the latest developments in science. as regards emission reduction commitments, the increase should also be kept below 1,5 °c, with global greenhouse gas emissions needing to peak by 2015 at the latest and to decrease by at least 50% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels and then continue to decrease. these are not mere percentages, but targets scientifically studied as possible and necessary to create a decisive turning point in the path we have taken towards the destruction of significant parts of the biodiversity of our planet.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union must show its strong commitment and determination in the context of the global effort to find solutions to mitigate climate change and its impacts.
in writing. - i support the united nations inquiry into the question of western sahara and support the position that morocco should allow free access to this particular region for journalists, independent observers and humanitarian organisations. i am aware that morocco is a strategic partner and ally of the european union in the fight against radical islamic fundamentalism. however, i do not accept the attitude of the moroccan authorities towards the violent and serious incidents they provoked in the gadaym izik camp in western sahara on 8 november, which resulted in the death of an as yet unknown number of people. i am glad to be a member of an institution like the european parliament, which has as one of its basic principles the protection and promotion of human rights. i therefore assume that it is necessary to call on the un bodies to propose the creation of a human rights monitoring mechanism in western sahara. i commend the efforts of the secretary-general of the united nations and his personal envoy to find a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution which will allow the people of western sahara to exercise self-determination.
in writing. - the situation in western sahara has been dragging on for more than thirty years with no apparent solution. it is one of a number of cases, along with the israeli-palestinian conflict and the cyprus conflict, which are difficult to resolve and have been going on for some time. despite some welcome initiatives to open up channels of dialogue, it is now clear that the parties to the conflict have not yet been able to take concrete steps towards a negotiated solution to the conflict. the recent news of the incidents in the gadaym izik camp has raised grave concerns about the moroccan authorities' respect for the human rights of the people of western sahara and has given rise to a worrying escalation of this conflict. i hope that this problem can be put to an end once and for all and that a political and administrative solution to the conflict can be found which reconciles the interests of the parties to the dispute.
in writing. - we welcome the european parliament's strong condemnation of the violent incidents in the gadaym izik camp in western sahara on 8 november, which resulted in the death of an as yet unknown number of people. we hope that the commission and the council will demand the measures proposed here, insisting on the need to call on un bodies to propose the creation of a human rights monitoring mechanism in western sahara and to demand compliance with the resolutions already adopted, including the self-determination of the people of western sahara. as the resolution says, "the united nations would be the most appropriate body to carry out an independent international inquiry to clarify the events, deaths and disappearances". it also deplored the attacks on freedom of the press and information suffered by many european journalists and urged the kingdom of morocco to allow free access and free movement in western sahara for the press, independent observers and humanitarian organisations. finally, we stress the importance of approving increased funding for the provision of the necessary humanitarian aid to the sarawi refugees living in the tindouf region, estimated at between 90 000 and 165 000, with a view to helping them to meet their basic needs for food, water, housing and medical care and to improve their living conditions.
in writing. the situation in western sahara is very worrying and the european parliament must give a clear signal of its condemnation of what is happening there. it is therefore necessary to put an end to the violence on both sides and to embark on a transparent and good faith dialogue to put an end to a conflict which has already caused too many deaths and which continues to cause a large number of displaced persons and refugees. the eu must continue to make an effort to provide humanitarian aid to these refugees so that they have a minimum of survival conditions.
in writing. - i have supported this resolution because i consider the fight for human rights to be fundamental. in western sahara, there were cases of police violence against citizens who, without resorting to violence, were protesting in a camp outside the city - el aaiun - against the social, political and economic situation and their living conditions. police forces used tear gas and batons against the protesters to evacuate the camp. more than a political issue with a neighbouring state, we are facing a violation of human rights which we must all condemn without exception, and i therefore vote in favour of this resolution and join my voice with that of my colleagues in urging all parties to remain calm and to refrain from all acts of violence.
in writing. - i am critical of the local elections in ukraine on 31 october and would like freedom of the press to be respected. i condemn the last-minute change to the electoral law before 31 october and the fact that opposition parties were not allowed to present candidates in the constituencies. i agree with the european parliament that we must not tolerate restrictions on democratic norms and that we must preserve freedom of expression. i agree with the european parliament in condemning the kiev government for its failure to act on this sensitive issue.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution because the relations between the european union and ukraine, one of the union's main partners in its eastern neighbourhood, are very important for the stability, security and prosperity of the whole of europe. aware of their shared responsibilities in promoting stability, the european union and ukraine have been intensifying negotiations and seeking new cooperation partnerships that go beyond mere economic cooperation, also integrating the areas of the rule of law and respect for human rights, where there is still so much to be done in ukraine, as evidenced by the backsliding in the recent electoral process. i would also stress the fundamental importance of ukraine's european integration process for the implementation of the necessary economic, social and political reforms. i therefore consider the conclusion of the association agreement to be particularly important for the effective implementation of the eu-ukraine association agenda.
in writing. −despite the initial gestures of president yanukovych and the successive statements by the ukrainian authorities about ukraine's willingness to join the european union and adopt european standards of good governance and respect for the human rights and civil liberties of its citizens, caution must be exercised. in fact, too often news reports are published of the retreat of freedom of expression and association, as well as of political influence in the media and the judiciary and the action of their security services. i believe that a ukraine that is true to the promises of its political leaders could begin a path towards accession, the first step of which should be the institutionalisation of a free state based on the rule of law.
in writing. - i consider ukraine a crucial strategic partner of the eu, and therefore cannot but express my concern about the excessive powers granted to the security services to intimidate ngos operating in that country to control the ukrainian media. it is also important to allow ukrainian opposition parties to participate in the elections without restrictions or discrimination. i believe that only to the extent that ukraine takes account of the recommendations in this resolution can we maintain our support for ukraine's prospects of european integration in order to secure the strategic partnership with this country.
in writing. − the recent elections in ukraine and, in the light of the statements of the osce/odhir observation mission, which considered that international standards were largely met, are a sign that this country continues to move positively towards future integration into the eu area. it is important, however, that ukrainian politicians and authorities work to ensure that political and economic stabilisation is a reality in the near future. this requires the implementation of the necessary constitutional reforms, the consolidation of the rule of law, the establishment of a social market economy and renewed efforts to combat corruption and improve the business and investment climate.
in writing. − the new political context and institutional framework in ukraine and the willingness of the newly elected president of ukraine, viktor yanukovych, and the ukrainian parliament (verkhovna rada) to confirm ukraine's determination to join the eu are another step towards opening an accession process. in accordance with article 49 teu, ukraine may apply for eu membership, like any european state which respects the principles of liberty, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law. the resolution which i voted for sets out proposals which will be communicated to the ukrainian authorities. there is still a long way to go towards institutional stability that recognises the full participation of all political actors leading to a healthy alternation of power. i hope that the strong historical, cultural and economic ties which the eu has with ukraine will be consolidated and allow the ukrainian people to join the union in due course. in this context, i stress the importance of strengthening cooperation on youth and student exchanges and the development of scholarship programmes which will enable ukrainians to become familiar with the eu and its member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union must take the lead in the fight against climate change by strengthening its economic competitiveness through energy saving and renewable economies, two sectors which can improve its energy security and which have a strong potential in terms of industrial development, innovation, spatial planning and job creation. however, to fulfil this role and benefit from competitiveness, the european union will have to change its trade policies, whether bilateral, regional or multilateral, as trade in goods and services is responsible for around 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions. it should encourage the necessary disruptions in production and consumption patterns and investment strategies. it should also be active in relation to emissions from international transport and climate-friendly technologies. despite the way ahead for the union in this area, important contributions have already been made, in particular with regard to illegal timber imports, biofuels and aviation emissions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'international trade policy in the context of the climate change imperatives', because, given that trade in goods and services is responsible for some 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions, measures are needed at the level of the common trade policy to curb global warming.
in writing. − after the impasse of the copenhagen climate change conference, it is important that the european union continues along the lines it has followed so far, towards a serious commitment to sustainable development, seeking to reduce its carbon emissions without jeopardising european industries. but europe's commitment to reducing emissions must not lose sight of economic efficiency and must not jeopardise the economic sustainability of states currently experiencing an unprecedented economic crisis. we cannot allow the increasing transfer of technology to developing countries as a means of dealing with carbon leakage and we cannot allow policies to reduce co2 emissions to doom european industry.
in writing. the un climate summit in copenhagen resulted in a disappointing agreement that is not enough to limit global warming to below 2°c. moreover, the copenhagen accord is neither global nor binding. the eu is far from being primarily responsible for this fiasco. the eu has, on the contrary, been a leader in the fight against climate change and should be encouraged to strengthen that leadership, not forgetting the tremendous efforts our industries are already making to meet the mandatory emission reductions in the european space. it is noted that the eu contributes 15% to global emissions, estimated to fall to 10% in 2030, while the us, china and india contribute half of the global emissions with a tendency to increase. in the context of the eu's international trade policy on climate change, even if others do not follow, our aim should be to focus on scientific research, technological innovation in decarbonised energy, energy efficiency and the creation of green jobs in order to increase our competitiveness.
in writing. − implementing many of the measures proposed in this report would not make a positive contribution to combating climate change. on the contrary, supporting the lisbon treaty and 'free trade', applying palliative controls on the environmental degradation that trade liberalization is generating, will only worsen the environmental degradation that increasingly threatens the planet and everyone who lives on it. the question is whether we accept the continued unrestrained exploitation of natural resources and of workers and peoples to serve a dominant capitalist system in permanent crisis. for our part, we do not accept it and therefore oppose: the continuing insistence on control of emissions through 'emission trading', which has shown that instead of reducing emissions it increases them; greater 'opening of markets' and the division of labour at world level, so that eu capital can lay its hands on the resources of the third world countries, lowering costs and increasing profits; a green capitalism which combines 'climate protection and trade liberalisation' and 'exchanges of environmental goods and services'.
in writing. - trade in goods and services is responsible for about 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions. in many member states, consumption-related emissions are higher than production-related emissions. the european union must fight these 'traded' emissions. that is the only way to start fighting climate change effectively. for example, the eu cannot finance the fight against deforestation while at the same time encouraging it through the import of forest products and biofuels. the eu must transform its modes of production and consumption and not simply outsource its emissions. the eu should orient its trade policies towards discriminating products on the basis of their climate impact and thus contribute to the necessary disruptions in production and consumption patterns and investment strategies. the climate policies of our social partners cannot be compromised to increase european market shares. the eu must take an active stance on international transport emissions and ensure access to climate-friendly technologies from developing countries. as the report points in this direction, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the balance between international trade policy and the imperatives of climate change is not easy to achieve, but an effort must be made to significantly reduce the levels of greenhouse gas emissions for which international trade is responsible. however, this cannot be done at the expense of the loss of competitiveness of european industries, especially in a context of severe economic crisis and rising unemployment. we must find environmentally friendly policies that simultaneously boost the economy and reduce alarming levels of unemployment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ep resolution on international trade policies in the context of the climate change imperatives, as i am reviewing the european council's ambitious targets for reducing european greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels, which is necessary if the union is to regain international leadership in climate terms, and which will certainly lead to an incentive for other countries to make more ambitious commitments as well. i stress the importance of achieving a binding international agreement on climate protection and strongly support the launching of a public debate on the creation of a world environmental organisation. i also believe it is essential to strengthen the positive interaction between trade and climate protection, to make international trade prices fairer and to avoid carbon leakage, to encourage product differentiation in line with their effects on the climate, to ensure that trade liberalisation does not jeopardise ambitious climate policies, to fully integrate transport into the climate trade issue, to strengthen the instruments for trade-climate compatibility and the eu's trade-climate coherence from the perspective of developing countries.
in writing. − globalisation and the financial and social crisis have reinforced the need for stronger rules in the world economy, as international trade is currently only in the interests of a few economic players, who have taken advantage of trade liberalisation to outsource part of their production and diversify their supply chain from countries with low production costs and a smaller regulatory framework. i therefore accept the principles proposed in this report to conduct trade in a way that is consistent with the union's objectives and, in particular, with its external policy, which can be achieved by implementing corporate social and environmental responsibility in trade so that they no longer continue to breach the principles of social responsibility, as this is a form of social dumping which must be regulated, by endorsing the proposals in this report, in particular as regards the mechanisms for judicial cooperation between the eu and partner countries to prosecute multinational companies for serious breaches of the environment and fundamental rights and by adopting a new initiative by the commission.
in writing. − within economic globalisation and international trade there has been an increase in competitive pressure between nations which has sometimes led to serious abuses of human rights and the environment. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it particularly relevant in ensuring the development of more sustainable policies which take social and environmental issues into account, in particular by promoting corporate social responsibility. it is essential that the activities of european companies investing and operating elsewhere are in line with european values and internationally agreed standards. in particular, this report proposes that future trade agreements negotiated by the european union contain a chapter on sustainable development which includes a clause on 'corporate social responsibility', which i consider crucial.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates the need for a new regulatory approach to international trade. these more effective and well-implemented standards should contribute to the development of more sustainable policies that genuinely take into account social and environmental concerns and not just the profit-at-all-costs of companies.
in writing. − the principles governing csr are fully recognised at international level and focus on the expectation of responsible behaviour on the part of companies, which presupposes respect for the legislation in force, in particular in the field of taxation, employment, industrial relations, human rights, the environment, consumer rights and their involvement in the fight against corruption. i therefore welcome the fact that the eu is now incorporating a chapter on sustainable development with csr clauses in future trade agreements.
in writing. − the promotion of corporate social responsibility is an objective supported by the european union. the union shall ensure that the external policies it pursues contribute effectively to the sustainable development and social development of those countries. it should also ensure that the activities of european companies, wherever they invest and operate, are in line with european values and internationally agreed standards. according to article 207 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the eu's common commercial policy is to be conducted 'in accordance with the principles and objectives of the union's external action', and according to article 3 it is to contribute, inter alia, to 'the sustainable development of the planet, solidarity and mutual respect among peoples, free and fair trade, the eradication of poverty and the protection of human rights, in particular those of the child, as well as the strict observance and development of international law, including respect for the principles of the united nations charter'.
in writing. − the principles governing existing legislation, particularly in the fields of taxation, employment, industrial relations, human rights, the environment, consumer rights and their involvement in the fight against corruption, must be adopted by all companies operating in international trade. it is therefore very important that in future such clauses should be included in the trade agreements to be negotiated.
in writing. the european parliament resolution on corporate social responsibility in international trade agreements is intended to be a wake-up call and a step forward towards a new social model based on ethics and responsibility in the business world. the failure of the welfare state model as we know it requires the creation of new realities and corporate social responsibility can be the engine of a new paradigm of evolution. in fact, global challenges have been exacerbated by the financial crisis and its social consequences. the principles governing corporate social responsibility are fully recognised at international level, both within the oecd and the ilo and within the united nations. the promotion of corporate social responsibility is an objective of the european union to which i subscribe. in this connection, i also stress my support for the establishment, within the wto, of a trade and decent work committee, where issues such as labour standards, particularly as regards the employment of children, and the social responsibility of enterprises in connection with international trade can be discussed.
in writing. - horizontal agreements between undertakings, which are permitted under the legal provisions, are forms of business collaboration often essential to give rise to significant economic advantages which ultimately benefit the market and consumers. they are normally cooperative activities which do not involve any coordination of the parties' competitive behaviour on the market and therefore have no effect on competition, but which promote gains which would not otherwise be possible. they are therefore exempted from the application of article 101 (1) tfeu. this is particularly relevant for the specialisation agreements and for the research and development agreements provided for in regulations (ec) no 2659/2000 and (ec) no 2658/2000, which the commission now proposes to review. at a time when europe needs to invest in r & d and must focus on innovation, it is essential that the legal conditions are created for the creation of the necessary synergies between companies operating in the market, in compliance with competition laws.
in writing. − according to articles 101 (1) and (3), 103 (1) and 105 (3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, horizontal forms of collaboration between undertakings are permitted provided that such agreements contribute to improving the production or distribution of products or to promoting technical or economic progress and that there are benefits for consumers. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that, given the significant legislative changes since the adoption of the regulations and the horizontal guidelines and the subsequent experience that the commission has gained with the application of these rules, it is necessary to codify a new set of rules issued by the commission which takes into account the case law of the european court of justice in this area.
in writing. − the review of the rules applicable to horizontal cooperation agreements between companies is very important to increase business collaboration, particularly at the level of r&d, thus helping to create synergies for further development in all areas of cooperation. we must, however, be careful that this type of cooperation is not designed to disregard the rules of sound competition.

in writing. - we naturally voted in favour of this report which proposes the mobilisation of the solidarity fund to cover the enormous damage caused on the island of madeira following the storm that hit the region in february 2010. we would like to make a few points, however. the fund's rules state that 'in situations of major disasters, the community must show solidarity with the population of the affected regions by providing financial assistance to help them to return to normal living conditions in the affected areas.' it also states that this instrument should enable 'actions to be taken quickly and effectively and to contribute rapidly to the mobilisation of the emergency services to meet the immediate needs of the population and to contribute to the short-term reconstruction of the main damaged infrastructure'. the rules and procedures for mobilising the fund have already shown in practice that this principle of rapid aid to the affected populations has not been observed. in this case, it is not until ten months after the disaster that parliament votes to mobilise the fund. we have therefore advocated, and we reiterate here, the need to adapt the rules for mobilising this fund, allowing for more flexible and timely mobilisation, reducing the time between the catastrophe and the availability of funds.
in writing. − the eu is a solidarity space and the eu solidarity fund is part of it . these are essential for helping areas affected by natural disasters, such as the floods in madeira (portugal) and the storm xynthia in france. having verified that both applications fulfil the eligibility criteria of regulation (ec) no 2012/2002, the commission has proposed to mobilise the solidarity fund to the amount of eur 31 255 790 for portugal (floods in madeira) and eur 35 635 750 for france (storm xynthia), making a total amount of eur 66 891 540 to be deducted from the ceiling of eur 1000 million in commitment and payment appropriations. i would, however, like to point out the delay in mobilising this kind of support. the process needs to be made less bureaucratic and more rapid in order to respond in time to future disaster situations.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report by agreeing that, in the framework of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, the european union solidarity fund be mobilised in the amount of eur 66.891.540 in commitment and payment appropriations to meet the request made by:- portugal to mobilise the fund in response to a disaster caused by landslides and floods on the island of madeira.- france to mobilise the fund in relation to a disaster caused by the storm xynthia.
in writing. - i welcome this proposal for an amending budget, which makes it possible to mobilise the european solidarity fund (esf) for a total amount of eur 66.891.540 in commitment and payment appropriations, of which eur 31.255.790 is intended to meet the request for assistance submitted by portugal following the heavy damage caused by the storm that hit the autonomous region of madeira in february 2010.
in writing. − the purpose of this european parliament document is to approve the council's position on draft amending budget no 9/2010 with a view to making the necessary amendments to mobilise the solidarity fund. the commission considered the disasters in madeira and france to be major and extraordinary disasters respectively, and both requests for the mobilisation of the fund by the respective national authorities were accepted. the european commission may present draft amending budgets in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances, in accordance with the financial regulation. in this context, the commission proposed the mobilisation of the solidarity fund in the amount of eur 31 255 790 for portugal and eur 35 635 750 for france, for a total of eur 66 891 540. today, in the name of european solidarity, we are approving a reallocation of the payment appropriations corresponding to this amount from budget line 06041403: energy projects for the recovery of the economy european offshore wind network system, with a view to repairing infrastructure and rebuilding areas affected by disasters. i welcome the measure taken, but i regret the delay in the whole procedure for mobilising the fund in view of the scale of the tragedy that has struck my home region, the autonomous region of madeira.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by slovenia in respect of 2 554 redundancies in the clothing manufacturing company mura, european fashion design, i voted in favour of the resolution in order to accept the european commission's proposal, as amended by parliament. i also agree that the commission proposal, in its explanatory statement, should include clear and detailed information on the application, analysing the eligibility criteria and explaining the reasons for its approval, in line with parliament's requests.
in writing. − aid for workers made redundant as a result of restructuring and relocation should be dynamic and flexible so that it can be activated quickly and effectively. in the face of structural changes in international trade, it is important that the european economy is able to implement instruments to support the workers affected promptly and to train them for their rapid reintegration into the labour market. in this respect, the financial assistance provided should be on an individual basis. it should also be stressed that such assistance does not replace liabilities normally borne by undertakings, nor is it intended for the financing and restructuring of undertakings. considering that slovenia has submitted a request for assistance concerning 2 554 redundancies in the mura group, european fashion design, which operates in the textile and clothing manufacturing sector, pomurje region (nuts iii region), and also bearing in mind that 7% of the employed population in the pomurje region was working in the mura group and that this region is already below the slovenian average income, i vote overall in favour of this report, i.e. the mobilisation of the egf in favour of slovenia.
in writing. - i think that the frequency with which we have in recent months in this parliament approved the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), which was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade, is very significant in the crisis europe is going through. the egf is not the solution to this problem, but it is a significant and important aid. in the present case, the aid is intended to deal with the consequences of 2554 redundancies at mura, european fashion design, a clothing manufacturing company in slovenia, which has been particularly affected by changes in international trade and has been the victim of cheap textile imports.
in writing. − in the face of the social impact of the global economic crisis, with particular effects on employment, the proper use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is of key importance in alleviating the suffering of many european citizens and families, contributing to their social reintegration and professional development, while also providing new qualified resources for the needs of businesses and the dynamisation of the economy. this is the context in which the intervention plan for slovenia is situated, which concerns 2 554 redundancies at mura, european fashion design, a company active in the clothing sector. i therefore hope that the european institutions will step up their efforts to implement measures to speed up and improve the utilization rates of such an important resource as the egf, which at present has very low rates of mobilisation. this year, only 11% of the available €500 million has been requested.
in writing. - each month there is a new round of calls for the globalisation adjustment fund. this time there are eight more requests from four member states: slovenia, germany, poland and spain. several hundred more companies are closing their doors, in a variety of industries, from the automotive to the textile to the retail trade. in total, more than 6,500 workers (6,592) are thrown into unemployment. almost ten thousand, if we add to that those who were here a month ago were also considered. at the time of this approval, we cannot but reiterate here that a break with the neoliberal policies that are causing the visible economic and social disaster in the eu countries is necessary. the palliatives for disaster are necessary, but the causes must be tackled. the proposal we made during the debate on the 2011 budget to create a european programme for employment and sustainable development, allocating 1% of eu gdp, to be complemented by funds from the member states, with a view to real convergence, promoting the potential of each country, the sustainable use of its resources, and focusing on production and the creation of jobs with rights, is now becoming more urgent.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be granted to slovenia, which has submitted a request for assistance in respect of 2 554 redundancies at mura, european fashion design, a company active in the clothing manufacturing sector.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by slovenia in respect of 2 554 redundancies in the clothing manufacturing company mura, european fashion design, i voted in favour of the resolution in order to accept the european commission's proposal, as amended by parliament. i also agree that:- the egf should support the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market on an individual basis, reiterating that egf assistance does not replace actions which are the responsibility of enterprises by virtue of national legislation or collective agreements, nor does it finance the restructuring of enterprises or sectors; - the functioning and added value of the egf are assessed in the context of the overall evaluation of the programmes and various other instruments established by the iia of 17 may 2006; i welcome the european commission's proposal to establish an alternative source of payment appropriations to unused esf resources, following the european parliament's frequent calls for the egf to be set up as a separate specific instrument with its own objectives and deadlines, and therefore the need to identify appropriate budget lines for carrying out transfers.
in writing. − the application submitted by slovenia for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of the 2554 redundancies in the clothing manufacturing company mura, european fashion design, in the period from 21 october 2009 to 20 february 2010, fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a company in a member state in a four-month period'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.

in writing. - today we are approving the mobilisation of a package of aid totalling eur 1 422 850 from the egf for spain, a country which has been severely affected by the world economic crisis and, in particular, which has seen unemployment rise above the european average. in this case, the aid concerns 528 redundancies in 66 enterprises in division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) of nace rev. 2. i hope that the spanish economy will be able to give an adequate response to the crisis, and the mobilisation of this aid is only part of that response.
in writing. − in the face of the social impact of the global economic crisis, with particular effects on employment, the proper use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is of key importance in alleviating the suffering of many european citizens and families, contributing to their social reintegration and professional development, while also providing new qualified resources for the needs of businesses and the dynamisation of the economy. this is the context in which the intervention plan for spain is situated, concerning 66 enterprises in division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) of nace rev. 2 in the comunidad valenciana region at nuts ii level. i therefore hope that the european institutions will step up their efforts to implement measures to speed up and improve the utilization rates of such an important resource as the egf, which at present has very low rates of mobilisation. this year, only 11% of the available €500 million has been requested.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to spain, which submitted a request for assistance in respect of 300 redundancies in 66 enterprises in division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) of nace rev. 2 in the nuts ii region of comunidad valenciana.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by spain in relation to 300 redundancies in 66 enterprises in division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) of nace rev. 2 in the nuts ii region of the comunidad valenciana, i voted in favour of the resolution in order to agree with the european commission proposal, as amended by the european parliament. i also agree that:- the egf should support the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market on an individual basis, reiterating that egf assistance does not replace actions which are the responsibility of enterprises by virtue of national legislation or collective agreements, nor does it finance the restructuring of enterprises or sectors; - the functioning and added value of the egf are assessed in the context of the overall evaluation of the programmes and various other instruments established by the iia of 17 may 2006; i welcome the european commission's proposal to establish an alternative source of payment appropriations to unused esf resources, following the european parliament's frequent calls for the egf to be set up as a separate specific instrument with its own objectives and deadlines, and therefore the need to identify appropriate budget lines for carrying out transfers.
in writing. − the application submitted by spain for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of 300 cases out of a total of 528 redundancies in 66 enterprises in division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) of nace rev. 2 in the nuts ii region of the valencian community fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in one or two regions adjacent to nuts ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.
