in writing. − given that this is a proposal dating back to 2003, which aims to include refugees in long-term resident status after five years of continuous legal status, it is regrettable that this inclusion proposal has not been taken into account at this stage. with the amendment proposals made by the european parliament in april 2008, which provide, among other measures, for the calculation of five years of residence after the procedures for obtaining residence status, and the lack of unanimity in the council, this new proposal will directly benefit beneficiaries of international protection who have resided in the eu territory for more than five years and who do not yet have resident status.
in writing. − this initiative followed the 2007 proposal for a directive on the extension of long-term resident status to refugees and persons under subsidiary protection, which never achieved the unanimity in the council that was needed before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it aims to provide beneficiaries of international protection who have been legally resident in a member state for at least five years with legal certainty as to their right of residence in a member state and to confer on them rights comparable to those of eu nationals. the compromise reached is of the utmost importance not only because it allows a high level of protection and legal certainty for refugees in the eu, which will also ensure better integration, but also because they will finally no longer be discriminated against against against against all other third country nationals. it is also an important political signal, as the adoption of this first initiative of the set of 6 pieces of legislation is not only a first step, but also reflects the constructive approach that guides the three institutions in establishing a common asylum system by 2012.
in writing. − this proposal aims to extend the scope of council directive 2003/109/ec on the status of third-country nationals who are long-term residents and beneficiaries of international protection who have been legally resident for more than five years in the territory of a member state. this measure, by treating beneficiaries of international protection equally in all member states, puts an end to the inequalities which have existed between states and will allow them to reside in a state other than the one in which they have been recognised, which was not the case until now. these measures are important precisely because we are building a common area of security and freedom in europe, where those who are recognised as entitled to international protection should enjoy equivalent rights in the various member states.
in writing. − the adoption of this report is intended to extend the scope of council directive 2003/109/ec on the status of third-country nationals who are long-term residents and beneficiaries of international protection who have been legally resident for more than five years in a member state. it will now be possible to treat beneficiaries of international protection equally in all member states, who will be able to reside in a state other than the one in which they have been recognised, which was not the case until now. the importance of these measures is directly linked to the aim of creating a common area of security and freedom in europe, where those who are recognised as entitled to international protection should enjoy equivalent rights in all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree to extend the scope of directive 2003/109/ec to beneficiaries of international protection who are already legally residing in the territory of a member state for a period of five years, by granting them long-term resident status. i would like to emphasize the policy of inclusion which this proposal entails. long-term resident status creates the opportunity to integrate these individuals, including through language training, which should be provided by the member state to long-term residents. in the same vein, i support the rapporteur's proposal to encourage member states to develop training programmes on the structural laws and fundamental values of the member state of residence, as well as on the general principles of democracy, human rights and individual rights and duties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that, in order to ensure equal treatment for all third-country nationals and to promote economic and social cohesion in the european union, it is fully justified to extend long-term resident status to beneficiaries of international protection who have been legally resident in the territory of a member state for five years.
in writing. - the european union's action must be centred on the principles of good governance and respect for human rights and democracy. in its relations with the south caucasus region in particular, the eu should accompany the region in its economic and trade development, security, stability, prosperity and conflict resolution. the agreement on the facilitation of the issuance of visas in the case of georgia will contribute to the eu's enlarged neighbourhood policy by facilitating cooperation and the movement of persons between the two contracting parties. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − this agreement is undoubtedly a significant step forward in eu-georgia relations. following the strengthening of bilateral cooperation with the eu and the accession of this country to the council of europe and the european convention on human rights, this agreement represents a further step towards improving the administration of justice and increasing the level of respect for freedoms in this country. it is hoped that this agreement will provide an incentive for georgia to undertake the necessary reforms in the areas of freedom, security and justice. at the same time it should facilitate travel and personal contacts between the citizens of the two contracting parties, which is a key condition for ensuring the development of economic, humanitarian, cultural and other relations. i hope that the necessary information campaigns will also be carried out in georgia to inform its citizens of the entry into force of this visa facilitation scheme and of the new possibilities they will be able to benefit from.
in writing. - the growing rapprochement of georgia with the european union, as expressed by several recent acts, is to be welcomed. the visa facilitation agreement is another important step towards their european integration. the free movement of persons is one of the most important rights that the union gives to its citizens and therefore i welcome cooperation between the union and georgia. the fight against illegal immigration and the incentives for reform in the area of security, freedom and justice can bear fruit if there is a spirit of commitment on both sides.
in writing. - the efforts to bring georgia closer to the european union are well known, as evidenced by a number of recent acts. this agreement on the simplification of the issuance of visas is thus another important step towards its european integration. the free movement of persons is one of the most important rights that the union gives to its citizens and that is why this cooperation between the union and georgia is very important. it is, however, essential to continue the fight against illegal immigration and to maintain the incentives for reforms in the area of security, freedom and justice in georgia.
in writing. − the process of deepening relations between the european union and the countries of the south caucasus, including georgia, is vital for a sound, coherent and effective neighbourhood policy. the conclusion of an agreement on visa facilitation has made a full contribution to this objective. the proposal for a decision on the conclusion of the agreement includes standard elements of the european union visa facilitation agreements, setting out the time limits for the visa decision, the fees and exemptions, the required documentation, as well as a joint declaration on cooperation and travel documents. i support the proposal to include a european union declaration on simplification for family members, responding to specific requests from georgia, in order to facilitate the mobility of a large number of persons who have family ties with georgian citizens legally residing in the territories of the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement because i consider that it, together with the agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation, constitutes very significant progress in eu-georgia relations, marking an important step on the path to european integration and providing an incentive for georgia to pursue the necessary reforms in the areas of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on the establishment of an eu rapid response capacity to the various large-scale disasters (natural or man-made) outside the european union in recent years because i consider it important to increase the effectiveness of the eu's disaster response capacity. a comprehensive and integrated eu response with a preventive action plan is increasingly needed. the catastrophe in haiti has shown the need for profound reforms by the european union in its rapid and efficient response to emergencies and disasters. i believe that a rapid and effective response will also require greater political will on the part of the various parties involved. it is also necessary to restructure competences to allow for greater coherence and coordination of the european union's response to disasters, and i consider it essential to put into practice some of the concrete proposals contained in the barnier report of 2006 on the creation of a european civil protection force.
in writing. - in view of the increasing frequency and intensity of disasters with serious human, economic, social and environmental consequences, the european parliament's recommendation on the establishment of a rapid eu response to disasters is of particular importance, and i voted in favour of it as it sets out the key aspects to be taken into account. among these, it stresses that cooperation between member states can provide operational and financial added value, and recognises that there should be an integrated approach to disaster management which also includes prevention, preparedness, disaster management and post-disaster reconstruction. i also think it is important to improve the coordination and efficiency of the european response, in particular through a european civil protection force.
in writing. - the recent natural disasters that have struck the world highlight the urgent need for rapid and effective response mechanisms to mitigate the adverse social, economic and cultural effects on the affected regions. following on from previous ep resolutions, of which i would like to highlight the most recent ones on the earthquake in haiti and on the prevention of natural and man-made disasters, this house is once again dealing with this matter. i generally support mrs zanicchi's report and i would stress at once that the future of the eu's disaster response capacity must be based on instruments available at european and international level, avoiding duplication, optimising resources and allowing the european civil protection force to build on the existing community civil protection mechanism. i welcome the fact that, following the tragedy in haiti, there has been greater effort and political will to strengthen the coherence and coordination between the civil protection and humanitarian aid dimensions, and the work done by the parties involved to achieve this. i regret, however, that the previous proposals of the european parliament have not yet been fully implemented, in particular those concerning the barnier report.
in writing. − responding quickly to natural disasters and catastrophes is essential as it is in the first hours after they have occurred that most people can be saved. in addition, in recent years we have seen a proliferation of natural and man-made disasters, which require a high degree of technical rigour and coordination of the different means of responding to disasters. the creation of a community civil protection mechanism is a first step, but, like the rapporteur, i believe that more needs to be done in this field. coordination, cooperation for a rapid and effective response to disasters by the european union can be successful, as was the case with the earthquake in haiti last january. and it needs to be.
in writing. - the occurrence of catastrophes can and should be prevented. factors such as intensive land use, disorderly urban growth, rural neglect and desertification, among others, are causing an increase in vulnerability to the occurrence of disasters. the promotion of a balanced use of land and economic and social development in harmony with nature is thus a key element in disaster prevention. this is where the eu's efforts should be intensified, following up the recommendations made in a recent report by this parliament and reinforcing this dimension in its cooperation policy. as regards the response to catastrophes which cannot be avoided, there is of course also room for strengthening cooperation, mutual assistance and coordination between the different member states and with third countries. the best ways and means of achieving this should be the result of a debate involving the different national civil protection authorities and others, with respect for the sovereignty of each state. this should be the path the report points to, not the 'immediate constitution of an eu civil protection force' or the use of military means in responding to humanitarian aid situations, which the report admits can operate outside the aegis and coordination of the un.
in writing. − the creation of a rapid response capacity to natural disasters and catastrophes is essential because it is in the first hours after they have occurred that the most people can be saved. on the other hand, we have unfortunately seen the multiplication of both natural and man-made disasters, which require a great deal of rapid intervention capacity. the creation of a community civil protection mechanism is thus very important but there is still much to be done in this area.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in fact, the analysis of the lessons learned in haiti clearly shows the need for further reforms of the eu's disaster response capacity, as i had already stated in my opinion on a community approach to the prevention of natural and man-made disasters. a rapid and effective response in emergency situations is essential to ensure eu solidarity with either one of its member states or third countries, and requires strong political will from the different decision-making bodies. the efforts made to strengthen coherence and coordination between civil protection and the various dimensions of humanitarian aid are acknowledged. however, concrete steps must be taken towards the creation of a european civil protection force, as my opinion on a community approach to the prevention of natural and man-made disasters also states. i agree with the rapporteur. it is time to make further progress in this area, in particular by putting into practice the concrete proposals of the barnier 2006 report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree that it is essential to make efforts and implement measures to strengthen the eu's disaster response capacity by promoting its efficiency, coordination and visibility.
in writing. − the record of natural and man-made disasters has been increasing not only in number but also in intensity and extent, and consequently in their human, socioeconomic and environmental effects. this is forcing the european union to rethink its response strategy in terms of prevention, management and assistance, in order to make it more concerted and operational. i welcome the adoption of this report, which is based on the recent disaster in haiti and calls for the creation of a european union civil protection force capable of creating synergies between the member states and the european institutions in order to prevent and assist third countries, in particular developing countries, when they are struck by a disaster. this humanitarian initiative is a representative of the european union's solidarity in its external dimension. however, i think it is extremely important that this initiative should also be designed to coordinate and manage disasters within the european union. i am reminded of the catastrophe which devastated the island of madeira last february, and i therefore consider it essential to set up this civil protection force together with the optimisation of existing resources.
in writing. − since the implementation of the markets in financial instruments directive (mfid), european financial markets have undergone unprecedented changes both as a result of the directive and as a result of external factors linked to the crisis, and the desired effects of regulation have not been achieved. the application of fdm has led to a fragmentation of markets which has encouraged the exponential emergence of high-frequency trading strategies. the market has adapted to the use of unregulated trading platforms (dark pools) to trade large orders in private order-crossing networks set up by intermediary brokers and to the use of the derogations provided for in the directive for such operations (opaque transactions), which were previously carried out through regulated markets. rules should be applied to these technological developments to ensure their effective regulation and transparency, in order to avoid the creation of systemic risks that jeopardise the overall functioning of markets.
in writing. - the european parliament continues to approve reports on partial aspects of financial regulation, without ever going to the bottom of the matter. of course, it is better to have some regulation of financial transactions carried out in private brokers and/or financial companies. but that's not the point. the report merely advocates greater regulation of trading venues, citing the need for 'increased transparency and security in financial instrument markets' and 'equal treatment' between multilateral trading venues and regulated markets. the essential question here is the persistence of the same system of speculation, touching only the form of that speculation and not the most important part, that is, its content. we, for our part, continue to advocate the end of the derivatives market and tax havens and effective control by political power over financial power, and not the other way around. until that happens, the rest is just make-up operations.
in writing. − with the recent implementation of the markets in financial instruments directive (mfid), european financial markets have undergone major changes, both as a result of the directive and other factors related to the crisis, and the desired effects of the mfid approval have not been achieved. the market has adapted to the use of unregulated trading platforms (dark pools) to trade large orders in private order-crossing networks set up by intermediary brokers and to the use of the derogations provided for in the directive for such operations, which were previously carried out through regulated markets. it is therefore essential to start applying rules to these technological developments to ensure that they are effectively regulated and transparent, so that in the future we do not create systemic risks that again jeopardise the overall functioning of the markets.
in writing. - supporting the call on the commission to strengthen market infrastructures for all trading platforms and clearing systems so that they can cope with future risks through greater transparency, resilience and regulatory oversight of all aggregated transactions, i voted in favour of parliament's resolution to approve:- multilateral trading platforms to be subject to the same level of supervision and thus regulated in a comparable manner;- investment firms, which provide portfolio management services and operate in the context of portfolio management, to benefit from the best execution conditions by investment firms; - the commission assesses the effects of the establishment of a minimum order size for all opaque transactions;- firms implementing high frequency trading strategies are regulated to ensure that they have reliable control mechanisms and standards with permanent regulatory reviews of the algorithms they use.
in writing. − i agree that the commission should assess the effects of setting a minimum order size for all opaque transactions and whether its strict enforcement could be ensured in order to maintain an adequate trading flow on platforms operating in a transparent manner in favour of price formation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential that the eu be prepared for the ncd risks which give a new dimension to terrorist attacks, accidents and natural disasters, since they know no borders and are likely to cause numerous victims. the eu's response to this danger should not be limited to post-emergency intervention programmes but should be pre-programmed at the stage of handling these materials, their storage, access limitation and control. i think it is essential that the response to an incident be accompanied by extensive cooperation between different authorities in a member state (civil protection, military, police, etc.) as well as between the national authorities of different member states and european bodies, i.e. i think a coordinated and comprehensive approach is essential. the commission presented the eu's action plan on cbrn in june 2009 for a period of three years (2010-2012), with the following components: prevention, detection, preparedness and response. in this connection, i consider it essential to recognise the importance of each of these aspects in ensuring that risk assessment studies, reactions and control measures are carried out correctly.
in writing. - it is essential that we adopt an effective action plan to deal with the existing and ongoing risk of chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear disasters on eu territory. whether accidental or intentional, they represent a serious threat with the potential to have devastating and far-reaching effects on the safety, well-being and health of european citizens, the environment, cultural heritage and basic infrastructure. fortunately, the number of incidents, including terrorist acts, related to qbrn matters has been quite low. this action plan demonstrates the need for a global and cross-border approach, as the effects of a brn disaster know no borders and should focus on the various aspects of prevention, detection, preparedness and response. it should thus ensure effective interaction of national and eu initiatives to address nbrq risks and prepare the response and mitigation capacity. like the rapporteur, ana gomes, i have no doubt that we need to adopt an eu action plan, but i regret that the commission has not been more ambitious, because the proposed action plan shows a lack of strength and coherence in some areas.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism, and for the eu to take action to combat terrorism, including by providing the necessary financial support to the eu's efforts to combat terrorism. we are increasingly dealing with diffuse and unconventional threats and as such europe needs to have an appropriate strategy for their prevention, detection and protection in order to be able to guarantee the safety and health of europeans. that is the direction the commission should take and that is what i hope.
in writing. - chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (cbrn) risks give a new dimension to terrorist attacks, accidents, natural disasters and pandemics, as they know no borders and are likely to cause numerous casualties. the eu cbrn action plan was presented by the commission in june 2009 and amended by the council in november. the plan will be implemented over the next three years (2010-2012) and has four main components: prevention, detection, preparedness and response. but the amendments introduced by the council do away with the action plan and make the measures envisaged less binding, as well as the monitoring and control of their implementation. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which seeks to give the commission a stronger regulatory role, as i believe that only in this way will it be possible to fill the gaps in the efforts made by the various member states in this field.
in writing. - if there were a real concern for the security of the npt, there would be no insistence on the maintenance of a very powerful nuclear arsenal of some eu countries, which could be used in military attacks, nor would there be any permission to maintain the stationing of us nuclear weapons in several european countries - an action which goes against one of the three pillars of the npt which it euphemistically claims to defend. the report makes no reference to decisions such as the recent decision by the united kingdom to sell nuclear technology to india, a non-signatory to the non-proliferation treaty, or the decision by france and germany to cooperate in maintaining their nuclear arsenals, citing a hypocritical 'cost rationalization'. nor is there any mention of the support of the major eu and nato powers for the project of installing anti-missile systems in europe and of nato's decision to remain a 'nuclear alliance'. in a period of intensifying crisis of capitalism, what this report shows is that it is not declarations of intent that count but concrete actions. and these demonstrate that militarism continues to assert itself as a resource for capitalist economic globalization.
in writing. - i think the eu should be prepared to deal with any attack or accident that could jeopardise the safety and health of its citizens. therefore, the qbrn action plan is necessary for the prevention or response to any type of threat or accident registered in the eu territory the current threats are diverse, hence the complexity of this matter, which now has its own mechanism to deal with the most diverse situations. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on enhancing chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (cbrn) safety in the european union, an action plan for the chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear safety of the european union in line with the epp group's argument, stressing the need for an eu-wide approach to prevent and detect attacks and/or accidents, as the threat of cbrn attacks is 'global', and the focus on enhancing chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear safety is necessary in the prevention of terrorist attacks. i also welcome the commitment made by the two largest political groups to relax the requirement for the entire chemical industry to substitute high-risk materials regardless of the associated risks.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and consider it of great importance at a time of economic and financial crisis, when it is necessary to ensure the harmonious development of all regions within the eu. i agree with the general purpose of a tripartite agreement between the eu, the member states and the regions, whereby modernization, interconnected infrastructure and support for investment plans and development projects according to the specific characteristics of each region are essential. i also believe that continued investment in infrastructure is essential in many european regions, particularly in the south and east. in view of the different levels of decentralisation of european regions, a balance must be found for a horizontal approach between different levels of government and between all areas of activity. efforts to modernise and reform the administrative structures of the regions, in addition to high-quality technical assistance from the commission, are essential to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of eu investments. simplification of procedures and the allocation of structural funds and the cohesion fund accessible to all stakeholders is essential, ensuring on the one hand the participation of all actors in society and on the other hand a better implementation on the ground of eu programmes, instruments and policies.
in writing. − the decentralisation of member states' powers is based on the sharing of responsibility between the different levels of government. the powers of regional and local authorities in implementing community policies are thus being strengthened. i agree with the adoption of this resolution as it focuses on the specificity of local and regional challenges, drawing attention to the need to consider integrated approaches which take account of the special characteristics of regions, such as geographical and natural disadvantages, depopulation and the special characteristics of the outermost regions, but which also look at the different administrative arrangements existing in the various member states. these approaches should also allow for the coordination of the interests of the different actors involved in order to facilitate governance at various levels. the resolution also draws attention to the complexity of procedures and control of funding applications, which distances potential beneficiaries from cohesion policy, and to the obligation to consult the public as a way of legitimising the decision-making process. at the same time, i agree that the strengthening of power at regional and local level must be accompanied by a reaffirmation of the commission's supervisory role and by strong coordination between cohesion policy and structural policy.
in writing. − the cohesion fund represents more than one third of the total eu budget and its ultimate objective is to reduce disparities in the levels of development of the various regions by directing resources in particular towards growth and employment. however, in recent days the financial times has been publishing an investigation into the fate of the cohesion fund and the scenario described is very worrying: the use of the fund for purposes totally different from those for which it was intended. i therefore believe it is essential to strengthen the commission's control procedures for the use and allocation of the cohesion funds by strengthening the mechanisms for good governance.
in writing. - we agree that criteria of effectiveness, efficiency, rigor and transparency must be guaranteed 'at all stages of the programming and implementation of the structural funds'. we acknowledge that the 'ongoing simplification of the financial regulation and the structural funds' may be indispensable in removing some of the barriers currently existing to access to the funds, particularly by less developed regions. as regards the principle of co-financing, while recognising the importance of the national authorities taking responsibility for the implementation of cohesion policy, we believe that in the face of the deep crisis we are experiencing, which particularly affects some member states and their regions, the rules on co-financing should be made more flexible, allowing for a higher rate of absorption of the resources allocated to cohesion, in particular by lowering the co-financing rate to 10% for all the structural funds. some aspects of the report continue to arouse our disagreement and opposition. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are not left behind in the process of economic and monetary union. the same applies to the uncritical attachment to the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy, a strategy guided by liberalization, privatisation and labour flexibility, a path that is clearly contrary to the objectives of cohesion.
in writing. - given that the regions have clear geographical and natural disadvantages, such as depopulation, among others, i consider this measure to be essential to make cohesion policy more effective. it is essential that there is greater rigour in the allocation of cohesion funds, so that asymmetries between eu states and regions are reduced. this will result in a process with greater transparency, less bureaucracy, more equity in the distribution of funds and consequently less disparity in the level of competitiveness. hence my vote.
in writing. − the principle of subnational subsidiarity, introduced by the treaty of lisbon, gives substance to the ambition to involve the regions in the european decision-making process. the increase in contacts with the european commission implies the principles of good governance in regional policy and the adoption of other assistance and control procedures. this report, which i voted for, deals with the powers and role of regional and local authorities in the process of implementing cohesion policies. regional authorities can now participate more directly and more actively in the decision-making process, whether in designing and implementing policies or in establishing themselves as genuine partners in achieving the community's objectives. i welcome this important step for governance, which responds to the european parliament's repeated calls for increased participation of subnational entities in the design and implementation of european policies.
in writing. - i believe that governance in the field of regional policy needs to be improved in order to make the management of the structural funds and cohesion policy not only more effective but also more balanced. i agree with the rapporteur when she calls for the commission to have a more forward-looking policy for results, focusing above all on the quality of assistance and the development of strategic projects. i also believe that the european networks for the exchange of good practice should strengthen their initiatives and thus help to ensure that these procedures are effectively applied.
in writing. - good governance of european regional policy is essential to its success. governance at several levels needs to be implemented in order to enhance the participation of all entities in the legislative process. in this respect, it is essential to increase the involvement of regional and local authorities in the pre-legislative phase and also in the implementation phase of policies. i would like to stress that the lisbon treaty recognises subnational subsidiarity, not only in the context of regional policy, but also in a horizontal way, that is, in all european policies. i believe that greater and better involvement of the various decision-making levels will help to achieve the objective of territorial cohesion, based on an integrated approach. however, a bottom-up approach must be pursued, as it is the local and regional level entities that best understand the characteristics and problems of the regions. the europe 2020 territorial compact for regional and local authorities could contribute to enhancing their contribution to the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the principles of partnership and co-financing will help to increase the accountability of the entities and the european commission should be given a stronger supervisory role, in particular through an improved control and audit system.

in writing. - this proposal for a directive on the european protection order aims to prevent crime and takes account of the fact that, although member states provide protection for victims and that it no longer has any effect beyond national borders, a european-wide early warning and prevention mechanism is needed. taking into account the recommendations launched by the stockholm programme and the procedures resulting from the implementation of the lisbon treaty, which allows for reports to be provided on a cross-cutting basis, as well as the first council proposal for a european directive on protection for victims of 5 january 2010, i agree with a broad approach to include victims of various types of crime, with the amendments providing for arrangements for revoking the protection order, ensuring continuity of legal protection, limiting the grounds for refusal of the protection order, setting a deadline for the execution of the order and clarifying the position of victims when moving from one member state to another.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this draft directive on the 'european protection decision' which aims to protect victims of crime throughout the european union. the aim of this initiative is to introduce a mechanism of judicial and police cooperation between member states so that victims of crime who benefit from a protection measure in one member state do not have to start the whole judicial procedure for obtaining protection measures again, and so that they are also protected if they decide to reside or remain in another eu country. the european protection decision will be issued at the request of the protected person and should be addressed not only to women victims of domestic violence, who are the vast majority, but also to any victims, such as victims of trafficking in human beings, female genital mutilation, forced marriage, honour killings, incest, gender-based violence, witnesses, victims of terrorism and organised crime.
in writing. - i support this resolution because i consider it essential to enable victims of violence to benefit from crime prevention and protection measures throughout the european union, i.e. that this protection is not restricted to one member state but that it allows them to reside or remain in other countries of the european union. this measure should apply to victims of trafficking in human beings, female genital mutilation, forced marriage, honour killings, incest, gender-based violence, witnesses, victims of terrorism and victims of organised crime. in this respect, it will be necessary to overcome the fact that the judicial systems of the member states are different.
in writing. - this proposal for a directive aims to address a gap in the current legislation on victims, which does not address the issue of crime prevention and the need for a rapidly and effectively functioning alert and prevention mechanism for the defence of victims throughout europe. the creation of a european protection order should thus become an important instrument for the protection of victims of any form of violence across the borders of the member states in order to avoid victims having to start the whole judicial procedure for obtaining protection measures over again when moving to another member state. while we have been passing legislation on the civil and procedural rights of suspects in the eu, we cannot forget the civil and procedural rights of victims, who are undoubtedly the most vulnerable and most unprotected. the adoption of this directive is an important step for the benefit of victims, but i hope that the commission can go further and present as soon as possible a comprehensive and more complete legislative package on victims.

in writing. − this directive is based on the application of protection measures to support persons against criminal acts, whenever the life of a person or his physical, psychological or sexual integrity is endangered. protection measures exist in all eu member states, but they cease to have effect when someone crosses the country's borders. the 'european protection decision' aims to ensure that protection afforded to a person in one member state is maintained and continued in any other member state to which the person moves or has moved. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. but the text still needs to be confirmed by a qualified majority of member states in the council. although much of the protection measures are aimed at women victims of domestic violence, the new rules should cover any victims: this directive applies to protection measures aimed at protecting all victims, not just victims of gender-based violence, taking into account the specificities of each type of crime committed, the adopted report states.
in writing. − it is the most basic principle of justice that a victim of crime who enjoys a protection measure in one member state should also be protected if he or she decides to reside or remain in another eu country. it is with this in mind that we have adopted these new rules today. any victim, not just victims of domestic violence, should be able to benefit from the european protection order. protection measures exist in all eu member states, but they cease to have effect when someone crosses the country's borders. the 'european protection order' aims to ensure that the protection afforded to a person in one member state is maintained and continued in any other member state to which the person moves or has moved, irrespective of the crime of which he or she has been the victim.
in writing. − this report is in line with the already adopted stockholm action plan, the european union's initiative to maintain and develop an area of freedom, security and justice. apart from the problems with the legal basis of these amendments, i decided to vote in favour of them because i consider the measures to protect victims or potential victims of crime to be very positive. the possibility of extending the scope of a judicial protection order from one member state (the issuing state) to the member state where the protected person intends to move (the executing state) is a significant step forward in the effective creation of an area of freedom, security and justice in the european union, an ideal which i share.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this directive because i regard it as a key element in extending the fight against trafficking in human beings. the eu response at this level now considers exploitation of prostitution or other forms of sexual exploitation, labour exploitation such as forced labour and begging, organ harvesting, cases of illegal adoption, forced marriage, drug trafficking, or even exploitation of a person for petty theft or theft. i believe that this document strengthens the prevention of crime, in particular by means of criminal offences, sanctions and confiscation of property or permanent closure of establishments used for the practice of crime in the case of traffickers in human beings. on the other hand, i believe that there is also greater support and assistance for victims, such as adequate housing, legal advice and material, psychological and medical assistance.
in writing. − human trafficking is the modern form of slavery and the second most lucrative activity for organised crime worldwide. this directive is the first legal instrument adopted in this area, with the new possibilities opened up by the treaty of lisbon, and it creates a common approach to the fight against trafficking in human beings and the protection of its victims, filling a serious gap in the legal framework we had. a balanced compromise was reached, creating an instrument capable of dealing more effectively with this type of crime, creating more stringent measures and increasing the level of penalties with prison sentences of 5 to 10 years and confiscation of proceeds of crime. it also reinforces the prevention and protection of victims, with special attention to children and other groups at risk. i also support the proposal to create a coordinator for the fight against trafficking in human beings in the eu, although we must avoid any overlapping of functions with other existing bodies, such as europol.
in writing. - human trafficking is today, for the victims, an inhuman and modern form of slavery and, for those responsible - criminal organisations operating in the areas of prostitution and sexual exploitation, illegal adoption, forced labour, illegal immigration and illegal organ trade - a highly profitable activity. since several european countries are the 'destination' of these networks, the initiative to create a common regime for preventing and combating trafficking in human beings at european level, which is in line with the motion for a resolution of this parliament voted on 10 february 2010, is to be welcomed.
in writing. − trafficking in human beings is a serious violation of human rights and represents a significant source of revenue for organised crime. the importance of this form of modern slavery is impressive, but its true extent is unknown. the lisbon treaty has strengthened the european union's action in the field of judicial and police cooperation in criminal matters, including the fight against trafficking in human beings. the european parliament, by becoming a co-legislator in this area, will have an important role to play here. i welcome the approval of the measures adopted in this report on the need to collect information on the number of people trafficked, on the sex, age and nationality of the victims, as well as on the way the trafficking is processed, the type of services to which the victims have been referred, the number of traffickers arrested, prosecuted and convicted, and on the national referral mechanisms to the national asylum authorities.
in writing. - we know that it is not enough to adopt legal instruments to combat trafficking in human beings and to protect victims, although the fight to eradicate trafficking in human beings must be seen as a priority in the fight for respect for human rights. it takes political will to put them into practice. but, above all in this area, it is also essential to act in the area of prevention, which requires other economic and social policies and implies an end to capitalist exploitation and neoliberal policies. we need to create the conditions to lift people out of poverty by promoting policies of fair redistribution of wealth, ensuring access to essential public services, promoting the creation of more jobs with rights and with wages that allow people to live with dignity. the vote on this document is therefore only one step in a long and hard struggle which must continue to put an end to trafficking in human beings.
in writing. - recent estimates by the international labour organisation have revealed that at least 2.45 million people worldwide are in forced labour as a result of trafficking in human beings. this is a phenomenon that has been evolving in recent years and is also present in european countries. the commission is therefore of the opinion that this is a scourge which must be vigorously combated in the eu, without neglecting its support and protection of the victims. hence my vote.
in writing. − a policy to prevent and combat trafficking in human beings is essential within the european union. i share the aim of creating tougher rules in this area, creating a hostile environment for traffickers, greater protection for victims and more rigorous prevention. i also agree with the european parliament's proposal to set up an anti-trafficking coordinator. i also welcome the proposed sanctions, in particular the prison sentence of up to 10 years and the possibility of 'confiscating the assets' of the criminal, as well as the council's proposal to urge the member states to transfer the confiscated assets to the assistance and protection of victims, including compensation for them.

in writing. - the efforts to bring georgia closer to the european union are well known, as evidenced by a number of recent acts. this agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation is essential to stimulate relations between georgia, its neighbours and the european union, as well as to the difficult fight against illegal immigration. it is, however, essential that the incentives for reforms in the area of security, freedom and justice in georgia are maintained.
in writing. − the process of deepening relations between the european union and the countries of the south caucasus, including georgia, is vital for a sound, coherent and effective neighbourhood policy. i support the agreement between the european union and georgia on the readmission of persons without residence permit. i would like to highlight the following positive measures: the readmission obligations laid down in the agreement are developed in a fully reciprocal manner, covering nationals themselves as well as third-country nationals and stateless persons. the obligation to readmit own nationals also includes former nationals who have renounced, lost or been deprived of their nationality without having acquired the nationality of another state. the readmission obligation in relation to nationals also covers family members (spouses and minor or unmarried children), irrespective of their nationality, who do not have a right of residence in the requesting state. the so-called 'fast track' procedure is agreed for persons intercepted in the 'border region', i.e. within an area extending up to 5 kilometres from seaports, including customs zones and international airports of the member states or georgia.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the principles set out in this report, reinforcing the idea that the european union can only be globally competitive if it mobilizes the convergence of its regions and its member states. i agree that despite progress, regional disparities need to be reduced to strengthen the internal market and strategy 2020, which can only have tangible results if the starting point of all regions is taken into account. while i agree that many regions still need investment in infrastructure and accessibility, i also stress the importance of investment in research and innovation, and the involvement of all levels of government and private actors is key to this in order to improve the absorption and application of funds. the commission's clear concept of partnership is needed to implement this idea and community support for the competitiveness of smes needs to be reviewed and consolidated.
in writing. − the union's cohesion policy has proved essential in reducing the development gaps between the various european regions. horizontal and vertical coordination between the different levels of governance is necessary to achieve common development standards and economic, social and territorial cohesion. support for research, innovation and education is a key measure to ensure an inclusive labour market, which should be accompanied by policies at regional level. the active role of regional and local authorities is crucial to ensure greater economic competitiveness in the global market.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty establishes as one of its founding values the promotion of economic, social and territorial cohesion in the eu and solidarity between member states (article 3 tfeu). the main objective of cohesion policy is to promote balanced development among the 271 different regions of the eu by reducing the disparity between the levels of development of these regions. particular attention shall be paid to the least favoured regions, as well as to rural areas, areas affected by industrial transition, regions with severe and permanent natural or demographic constraints and island, cross-border and mountain regions. in this respect, i have advocated the need to align cohesion policy with the eu 2020 strategic objectives and to promote transparency in the allocation of funds. in my view, all information on the approval and implementation of cohesion policy fund projects by nuts should be made available in real time, in as much detail as possible (e.g. implementation by nuts 3 should be presented where this designation exists), on a website accessible to the general public. this is what i am advocating in my opinion attached to the cohesion policy report on the implementation of the 2007-13 programmes.
in writing. - the reality of the european union today is the most vivid and complete refutation of the report's assertion that cohesion policy has effectively responded to the socioeconomic difficulties generated by the crisis. another idea runs through the report: the association of cohesion policy with the so-called 'eu 2020 strategy'. it is well known that the eu 2020 strategy, which is the successor to the old lisbon strategy, follows the same political line of liberalisation, privatisation and the relaxation of labour laws. these guidelines, which have been pursued, do not contribute to cohesion but, on the contrary, lead to an increase in disparities between countries and regions and within each country. the redistributive function of the community budget - essential to the implementation of the principle of cohesion - is seriously compromised by its meagreness. in addition, the report ignores the costs to the eu's most vulnerable economies of integration into the single market, economic and monetary union and the liberalisation and deregulation of international trade. the development of production in each country and region, the sustainable use of resources and the preservation of the environment are strategic drivers for the economic development of each country, as are the creation of jobs with rights, the strengthening of the public service network and the social functions of the state.
in writing. − it is through a strong cohesion policy that the union has been able to reduce the development gaps between the various european regions. it is essential to continue to ensure coordination between all levels of governance in order to achieve the eu's development objectives and economic, social and territorial cohesion. support for research, innovation and education is a key measure to ensure a labour market for all. everyone must play their part in ensuring greater economic competitiveness on the global market.
in writing. - this report is the result of the initiative of the epp group in the course of the debate on the future of cohesion and regional policy. the strengthening of territorial, social and economic cohesion in the european union is one of the necessary guidelines to be adopted as a contribution to global competitiveness. i fully agree with the fundamental aim of this report to highlight the role that cohesion policy plays in reducing economic, social and territorial disparities, creating new jobs, increasing growth and building infrastructure. territorial and social cohesion must be at the heart of the architecture of a new policy aimed at ensuring sustainable growth and increased competitiveness on a global scale.
in writing. − the european union's cohesion policy is crucial to enabling regions to meet the challenges of the new global context. by supporting development, by enhancing local and regional specificities and by ensuring that the living standards of the citizens of the union are brought closer together, we are consolidating the european project. however, alongside policies and measures at regional level, there is a need to strengthen support for research, development and innovation, as well as the development of education and skills needed by citizens to ensure an inclusive labour market.
in writing. - economic, social and territorial cohesion is a necessary but not sufficient condition for ensuring global competitiveness. european cohesion policy aims to reduce regional disparities, taking into account the impact of global challenges such as climate change, demographic change, energy and biodiversity protection issues, as well as the new challenges arising from the economic and financial crisis. i therefore support the text proposed by the rapporteur, my colleague in the committee on regional development, and reiterate the idea that cohesion and competitiveness are not contradictory or incompatible, but have elements of complementarity. competitiveness within the european union can only be achieved through sustainable economic growth, and cohesion policy therefore contributes to the successful achievement of the eu 2020 objectives and to responding to societal and economic challenges. the regional dimension must not be forgotten, but rather be given greater weight, either by involving regional and local authorities more closely or by enhancing the role of urban and rural areas, because only by promoting regional competitiveness can we achieve strong global competitiveness.

in writing. − aid for workers made redundant as a result of restructuring and relocation should be dynamic and flexible so that it can be activated quickly and effectively. in the face of structural changes in international trade, it is important that the european economy is able to implement instruments to support the workers affected promptly and to train them for their rapid reintegration into the labour market. in this respect, the financial assistance provided should be on an individual basis. it should also be stressed that such assistance does not replace liabilities normally borne by undertakings, nor is it intended for the financing and restructuring of undertakings. given that the netherlands has submitted a request for assistance concerning 613 redundancies in two enterprises in division 46 (wholesale trade other than motor vehicles and motorcycles) of nace rev. 2 in the region of north holland, i vote in favour of this report as a whole, i.e. in favour of mobilising the egf for the netherlands.
in writing. - the financial and economic crisis we are experiencing, together with the constant changes in the labour market caused by changes in the structure of international trade, has resulted in numerous victims of unemployment, which is often long-lasting. the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to respond to these situations. in this case, we are talking specifically about the mobilisation of just over two and a half million euros for the netherlands to support 613 redundancies in two trading and retail companies between 1 may 2009 and 31 january 2010. since the commission, after examining this application, has found it to be suitable and to meet the requirements laid down and recommends that the application be approved, i have voted in favour.
in writing. − in the face of the social impact of the global economic crisis, with particular effects on employment, the proper use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is of key importance in alleviating the suffering of many european citizens and families, contributing to their social reintegration and professional development, while also providing new qualified resources for the needs of businesses and the dynamisation of the economy. this is the context in which the dutch intervention plan concerns 613 redundancies in two enterprises operating in nace rev. 2 division 46 (wholesale trade other than in motor vehicles) in the nuts ii region of north holland in the netherlands. i therefore hope that the european institutions will step up their efforts to implement measures to speed up and improve the utilization rates of such an important resource as the egf, which at present has very low rates of mobilisation. this year, only 11% of the available €500 million has been requested.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to the netherlands, which has applied to mobilise the egf, in respect of 613 redundancies in two enterprises operating in nace rev. 2 division 46 (wholesale trade other than in motor vehicles) in the nuts ii region of north holland, the netherlands.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by the netherlands in relation to 613 redundancies in two enterprises operating in nace rev. 2 division 46 (wholesale trade other than of motor vehicles and motorcycles) in the nuts ii region of north holland in the netherlands, i voted in favour of the resolution in order to agree with the european commission proposal, as amended by the european parliament. i also agree that:- the egf should support the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market on an individual basis, reiterating that egf assistance does not replace actions which are the responsibility of enterprises by virtue of national legislation or collective agreements, nor does it finance the restructuring of enterprises or sectors; - the functioning and added value of the egf are assessed in the context of the overall evaluation of the programmes and various other instruments established by the iia of 17 may 2006; i welcome the european commission's proposal to establish an alternative source of payment appropriations to unused esf resources, following the european parliament's frequent calls for the egf to be set up as a separate specific instrument with its own objectives and deadlines, and therefore the need to identify appropriate budget lines for carrying out transfers.
in writing. − the application submitted by the netherlands for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of 613 redundancies in two enterprises in division 46 (wholesale trade other than motor vehicles and motorcycles) of nace rev. 2 in the nuts ii region of north holland fulfils all the legally defined eligibility criteria. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in one or two regions adjacent to nuts ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.
in writing. − the present proposal does not seek to harmonise substantive law applicable to divorce and legal separation, but rather to establish harmonised rules for the settlement of international jurisdictional disputes. this means that we are working within the framework of private international law and not within the substantive framework of family law, where each state will continue to have its own laws. it is therefore important to recall that, for example, the proposed regulation, by adding article 7a, does not oblige a state to recognise as marriage - even if only to ensure its dissolution - an act which is not regarded as such by its national law (which would be contrary to the principle of subsidiarity). this cannot, however, limit the rights of persons whose unions are not recognised in a state, a compromise solution having to be found. having made these reservations, i cannot but consider it an important step towards the construction of an area of freedom and justice, in which the free movement of persons is effective, to give greater legal certainty to the resolution of conflicts of international jurisdiction in the field of family law, in particular in the field of dissolution of marriage and legal separation of persons.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report which should allow couples from different member states, or residing in a country other than their own, the possibility of choosing the law that should apply to their divorce. in 2007, one million divorces were recorded in the eu, 13% of which involved couples with partners of different nationalities. in these cases, european citizens are confronted with problems of the legal order applicable to their separation. i would stress that portugal is part of the process of enhanced cooperation which has enabled progress to be made on this matter, which was blocked in the council. i would stress the need, as stated in this report, not to oblige a member state to recognise as a marriage - even if only for the purpose of its dissolution - an act which is not regarded as such by the legislation of that state and which would also be contrary to the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. − the new regulation will allow international couples (couples with different nationalities, couples living in different countries or couples living together in a country other than their country of origin) to choose the national law applicable to their divorce, provided that one of the spouses has a connection to that country (e.g. habitual residence or nationality). the new rules also clarify the law applicable in the event of a disagreement between the spouses. the new regulation will allow, for example, a portuguese-spanish couple living in belgium to choose whether the law applicable to their divorce will be portuguese, spanish or belgian law.
in writing. - portugal is participating, together with 13 other eu countries (spain, italy, hungary, luxembourg, austria, romania, slovenia, bulgaria, france, germany, belgium, latvia and malta) in the first trial of enhanced cooperation in the history of the eu. this enhanced cooperation shall be developed in the area of the law applicable to divorce and legal separation of persons and property. i voted in favour of this report on the regulation laying down clear rules on the procedure for international couples (with spouses of different nationalities) to apply for divorce or legal separation of persons and property in their countries of origin or residence. this is a widely agreed theme which will make life easier for some europeans. at the same time, it is also a symbolic moment in which a situation of enhanced cooperation between eu member states is beginning. these provisions are intended to enhance legal certainty and predictability in matters of divorce and legal separation of persons and property. the agreement provides only for the harmonization of situations of conflict and not for the harmonization of the substantive national rules.
in writing. − the development of an area of freedom, security and justice in which the free movement of persons is ensured is one of the primary objectives of the european union. i therefore welcome this proposal, which introduces greater legal certainty in determining the law applicable to divorces and separations of national marriages, and i hope that other member states will join in this effort to achieve the compatibility of national conflict-of-law rules in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the global financial crisis, to which the credit rating agencies have contributed in part, has shown the need to introduce a framework for the supervision of credit rating agencies. i agree with this report, which calls for the establishment at european level of a system for the registration and supervision of credit rating agencies issuing ratings used in the eu, and which also provides for the conditions for the use in the eu of ratings issued by third country agencies. the agreement reached on the european supervisory architecture, which will enter into force on 1 january 2011, now makes it possible to effectively implement the supervision of these agencies. it is essential that, from its inception, esma should be able to exercise its powers to ensure sound supervision of credit rating agencies active in the eu as well as those from third countries whose ratings are authorised in the eu, in full coordination with national authorities. i also welcome the fact that the usa has also decided to adopt stricter supervisory rules in this area, which have been taken into account by the commission in preparing further international harmonization.
in writing. − the need for this amendment arises from the need to adapt regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 to the new european supervisory architecture and the introduction of a new mechanism for centralising the operations of credit rating agencies. to this end, the european supervisory authority (european securities and markets authority - esma) will be given specific supervisory, investigative and sanctioning powers. it is now necessary to ensure that esma is able to exercise its powers and to ensure sound supervision of credit rating agencies active in the european union as well as of third-country credit rating agencies whose ratings are authorised in the european union.
in writing. − this amendment is necessary to allow the adaptation of regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 to the new european supervisory architecture and to introduce a new mechanism for centralising the operations of credit rating agencies. the european supervisory authority (european securities and markets authority - esma) will thus be given powers of its own for supervision, investigation and the application of sanctions. it is essential that esma is able to exercise its powers and ensure sound supervision of credit rating agencies active in the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament's resolution to agree that:- the registration and ongoing supervision of credit rating agencies in the union should be the sole responsibility of the european supervisory authority (esa), in particular the european securities and markets authority (esma), which should have exclusive competence to conclude cooperation agreements on the exchange of information with the competent authorities of third countries;- the esma should be responsible for the registration and ongoing supervision of credit rating agencies and have the right to request, by simple request or decision, all information it needs from credit rating agencies, persons involved in credit rating activities, entities subject to credit rating and related third parties, third parties to whom credit rating agencies have subcontracted operational functions and persons who are otherwise closely and substantially related or connected to credit rating agencies or credit rating activities; - the registration of a credit rating agency granted by a competent authority is valid throughout the union after the transfer of the supervisory powers of the competent authorities to esma.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's resolution because i agree that transparency of information provided by the issuer of a rated financial instrument to the designated credit rating agency can potentially represent a major added value for the functioning of the market and the protection of investors.
in writing. - i agree with the need to simplify the acquis communautaire and to update directives that no longer make sense and make them relevant to today. the directives in question are outdated and do not contribute to better regulation. the commission considered that there was no need to harmonise metrology legislation as it considered that there was sufficient cooperation between member states and that the current situation of common recognition of rules based on international parameters in the different member states was satisfactory. however, it must be borne in mind that a lack of regulation in this area would be harmful and that we cannot contribute to legal uncertainty.
in writing. the report in question concerns the choice to be made as regards eight directives relating to metrology in six sectors, with a view to simplifying the acquis of european law in this field: cold water meters for non-clean water (directive 75/33/eec); alcoholometers and alcohol-metering tables (directives 76/765/eec and 76/766/eec); weights of average and above-average precision respectively (directives 71/317/eec and 74/148/eec); manometers for motor vehicle tyres (directive 86/217/eec); measurement of the mass of cereals (directive 71/347/eec); calibration of vessel tanks (directive 71/349/eec). in considering the different options for these eight directives - total repeal, conditional repeal and no action - the commission concludes that there is no single option that stands out. but for the sake of better regulation, the commission is in favour of the total repeal of all the directives, that is, it is in favour of new regulation in the field of measuring instruments. i support this choice by the commission on the basis of a principle of legislative excellence, but i believe that member states should be given sufficient time to consider the possible consequences in the context of a broader review of the basic legal instrument in this field, namely the measuring instruments directive (directive 2004/22/ec).
in writing. − a simple and updated acquis communautaire is one of the eu's objectives. there is no point in maintaining certain completely outdated standards. as regards metrology, it is understood that no harmonisation is necessary as the legislation in force is a common recognition of the rules based on the international parameters of the different member states. we must not, however, leave a regulatory vacuum in this area, so that there is no legal uncertainty.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. the commission advocated the complete repeal of all eight metrology directives, while the rapporteur's position is more balanced by giving member states more time to investigate whether repealing the directives will lead to legal uncertainty that would necessitate european harmonisation of metrology rules. a transitional period is therefore established to examine the possible consequences of the repeal of the directives and to examine the need to revise the basic directive in this area (directive 2004/22/ec).
in writing. - i agree with the general aim of better regulating the issue of metrology. however, i think that greater consideration is advisable, since hasty standardization could cause more disruption and legal uncertainty than it would bring benefits.
