in writing. − the citizens' initiative, adopted today, is another step towards establishing a europe for and by the people, increasing democracy, transparency and bringing europe closer to citizens and to an active, engaged and participatory civil society. european citizens will now be able to ask the european commission to propose legislation on a given subject, provided that a minimum number of signatories from at least one fifth of the member states is guaranteed. however, i cannot help but express some perplexity at the exclusion of legal persons and organisations as 'organisers' (article 2 (3)), thinking in particular of ngos and also of political parties, founding organisations of representative democracy, and at the terminology chosen - 'citizens' committee' - to identify the set of organisers. i cannot help feeling a certain oddity at the attempt to set the minimum age of signatories at 16, when the right to vote and stand as a candidate in most member states comes at the age of 18. that should be the heading proposed by the commission (article 3 (7) and (2) of the proposal).
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report on the european citizens' initiative introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which aims to give citizens the same powers of political initiative as the council of ministers and the european parliament. each initiative will have 12 months to collect one million signatures, which must come from at least one quarter of the member states (currently seven). the minimum number of signatories per country varies between 74,250 in germany and 3,750 in malta. in the case of portugal, the minimum number of signatories required to support an initiative is 16.500. the validity of statements of support shall be determined by the member states. in portugal, the number of the identity card, passport or national identity card should be included. signatories must be eu citizens and of the age required to vote in european elections (18 in portugal). the commission will then examine the initiative and decide within three months whether to submit european legislation on the matter. the community executive will have to 'indicate the measures it intends to take and the reasons which justify or do not justify them'. this justification shall be made public.
in writing. - this is clearly a demagogic initiative, propaganda by the european union, which serves only to try to hide the impoverishment of democracy that is being experienced and to make people forget that european officials prevented the referendum on the same lisbon treaty that provides for the so-called citizens' initiative. moreover, the treaty on european union itself sets out the limits of such a citizens' initiative by stating in article 11 that one million signatures from a significant number of member states are required, and then adding that they can only invite the european commission to submit an appropriate proposal on matters on which those citizens consider a legal act of the union to be necessary for the implementation of the treaties. in other words, after all the work of collecting signatures and meeting the requirements laid down in the proposal for a regulation, there is no guarantee that citizens will have their requests taken into account. the report adopted by the ep slightly improves the european commission's proposal, but it must respect the provisions of the treaty, which in fact limits the scope of the citizens' initiative. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - with this important initiative by the european parliament, one million european citizens will be able to ask the european commission to come forward with legislation on a particular subject. the rules implementing the citizens' initiative, which was approved by the european parliament today, stipulate that signatories must come from at least seven member states. in the case of portugal, at least 16,500 signatures will be needed to support an initiative. the treaty of lisbon created a 'right of initiative for citizens' under which one million citizens can ask the commission to submit certain legislative proposals. the regulation adopted today in plenary establishes the conditions for the presentation of future citizens' initiatives.
in writing. − naturally supporting the citizens' initiative regulation, i disagree, however, with the possibility of these initiatives being subscribed to by members of the european parliament (or national members) and of their being financed by political parties or public bodies. i think that both solutions run counter to the spirit of the new mechanism, which is to give ordinary citizens and civil society a means of intervening in the political life of the union. i also disagree with the commission's power to adopt certain technical specifications necessary for the implementation of the law by means of an executive act. acts of general scope entrusted to the commission for the implementation of legislative acts should not be considered as executive acts, under the control of the member states, but as delegated acts, under the direct control of the legislator. it is also pointless, after the treaty of lisbon, to continue to apply the regulatory procedure of traditional comitology, since these are obviously matters which are now covered by the legislative procedure or the procedure for delegated acts. those provisions are therefore contrary to the treaty of lisbon. apart from these specific objections, i think that overall this is an excellent law that does justice to the political and constitutional importance of this new mechanism of participatory democracy in the eu.
in writing. - i am very pleased to vote in favour of this report on the citizens' initiative, one of the major innovations of the lisbon treaty. this new legal instrument could be a way of promoting the exercise of european citizenship. in fact, giving a million citizens the opportunity to propose to the european commission that it legislate on a particular subject is a very positive step towards bringing europe closer to its citizens. i commend the work of the rapporteurs who have sought to simplify the citizens' initiative and to remove any bureaucratic burden so as to make it as accessible as possible. i agree with most of the demands made by the european parliament, in particular that the admissibility of an initiative should be checked at the time of its submission and not after 300,000 signatures have been collected, which could meet the expectations of the citizens who have signed it. i welcome the reduction in the minimum number of member states involved in the initial signature of the initiative. the original proposal was for signatories from at least one third of the member states and the european parliament and the council agreed to signatories from one quarter of the member states.

in writing. − the european citizens' initiative (eci) is a public participation instrument that aims to address the democratic deficit and, as such, to reduce the distance that european citizens feel towards the european institutions. the institutionalisation of this initiative, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon, gives european citizens the possibility of indirectly inviting the european commission to propose certain legislative measures, provided that they fall within its competence. this report by the european parliament sets out the criteria for the exercise of this right of initiative, in order to make it simpler, more accessible, faster, more transparent and uniform across all the member states. the creation of a genuine european public space will be possible thanks to this initiative, which promotes civil dialogue and the involvement of civil society. i believe that all initiatives aimed at reducing the distance between citizens and the european project should be emphasised, implemented and fully exercised.

in writing. − the challenges facing african countries are immense in the context of a serious crisis in the world economy. the crisis presented as financial finally exposes the limits of economic growth as understood by capitalism, namely in the availability of fertile land for the production of food and other biological raw materials, geological reserves for the extraction of mineral raw materials and energy to power industries. this accelerates the race to africa, a continent immensely rich in natural resources. dominating markets and natural resources is the goal. it is in this context that the eu's policy towards africa should be understood: blackmailing for the signing of the so-called economic partnership agreements; promoting the secession of south sudan; supporting and financing the african peace and security architecture, seeking to put its armies to repress its peoples, to serve the interests of the eu and its economic and financial groups. these are just a few examples. for all these reasons, this resolution is about neo-colonialism. it is necessary to break the shackles that keep the countries of this region in subjection to interests alien to their peoples, by establishing genuine cooperation, helping them to consolidate their independence and sovereignty with a view to their development and economic and social progress.
in writing. - it has been three years since the last africa-eu summit, which was the beginning of a dialogue between europe and the african continent. this partnership is fundamental to development and progress and an important effort by both sides to deepen relations. the partnerships should not be limited to community aid. trade relations, economic partnerships and exchanges of experience in the fields of research, innovation and education should also be established, thus deepening future relations.
in writing. - relations between the european union and africa are admittedly fundamental. i therefore welcome the adoption of the strategic action plan 2010-2013 and the partnerships established. i would highlight the peace and security agenda, the eu's efforts to provide predictable and sustainable funding for african peace support operations, and the need to build local capacity, resilience and resolve to protect civilians in armed conflict. i cannot fail to emphasize the efforts of cooperation on issues of common interest such as democratic governance and human rights, trade, regional integration and infrastructure and the millennium goals. in the latter area, the commitment of the european union countries to renew their commitment to allocate 0.7% of their gross national income to official development assistance by 2015 should be highlighted. this effort is crucial to meet the millennium development goals, notably with regard to specific policies on maternal, newborn and child health, gender, education, agricultural policy, sustainable development, access to water and sanitation.
in writing. the third africa-eu summit in the libyan capital of tripoli has reinforced the level of cooperation between the two continents. on the subject of growth, investment and job creation, the summit stressed the need to create economic growth capable of generating employment and, at the same time, sustainable social development. the africa-eu strategy will be implemented in accordance with the action plan adopted for the period 2010-13, which focuses on the eight priority areas already established at the lisbon summit in 2007. concrete measures on private enterprise, economic integration and social issues, security and peace on the african continent, respect for human rights and the achievement of the millennium development goals were included in the tripoli final declaration. i would first of all like to welcome this partnership between the two continents, which has demonstrated the added value for both partners and the importance of continuing to promote regional and global integration on the african continent. however, i believe it is appropriate for the european parliament to play a more active role in this partnership and for a financing plan to be drawn up for the effective implementation of the 2010-13 action plan.
in writing. − the importance of protecting and promoting human rights and fundamental freedoms is at the heart of democratic values and of the european union itself. i agree that local and regional authorities can play a key role in implementing these values by proposing a bottom-up approach. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon should be seen as a strengthening of the multi-level system of protection of fundamental rights, including the charter. it is necessary to reflect on the developments in the protection of these rights since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, recalling that the charter has the same legal value as the treaties and must be incorporated into eu primary law. the new horizontal obligations created by the lisbon treaty are welcomed and their effectiveness requires better coordination of efforts between the institutions. the creation of the new 'justice, fundamental rights and citizenship' portfolio within the commission is recalled and further action by the commissioner is expected in this new context. tangible results are expected from the new commission communication: strategy for an effective implementation of the charter of fundamental rights by the eu.
in writing. − the effective protection of fundamental rights and respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality and the rule of law should be an overarching objective of all european policies and an essential condition for the consolidation of the european area of freedom, security and justice. the year 2009-2010 was of particular importance in this context, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which made the charter of fundamental rights legally binding, thereby translating fundamental values into concrete rights directly enforceable by european and national courts. it is necessary to ensure that all new legislative proposals are in conformity with the charter and, in the same vein, to verify existing instruments. it is important to strengthen cooperation and coherence between the different bodies responsible, at european and national level, for monitoring and implementing this new general framework established by the lisbon treaty, in order to ensure its effective implementation. i also hope that the commission will complete the process of eu accession to the echr as soon as possible, which will provide an additional mechanism for respect for human rights. i am glad that citizens and the protection of their rights have finally been placed at the heart of the european architecture.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on fundamental rights in the european union (2009) - effective implementation after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, because i consider it necessary to promote a culture of fundamental rights in the european union and the member states. the protection of fundamental rights must be an objective of all european policies, including foreign policy, in order to promote peace, human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. − the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon marks a new paradigm in the field of fundamental rights in the union by making the charter of fundamental rights legally binding. it is our duty to position the union as a community that protects fundamental rights, both internally and externally. there are still too many attacks on freedom of expression, as i have warned on several occasions, such as the recent cases in saudi arabia and azerbaijan. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to respond to the threat posed by terrorism. the challenge now is to answer these questions and to adopt the measures and strategies needed to solve these problems.
in writing. − the entry into force of the lisbon treaty created a new situation in the eu in the field of human rights by making the charter of fundamental rights legally binding and by giving the union legal personality, which enables it to accede to international treaties. the effective protection and promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms are the foundation of democracy and the rule of law in the european union and an essential condition for the consolidation of the european area of freedom, security and justice, which requires action at various levels (international, european, national, regional and local). in this context, the important role that regional and local authorities can play in the practical implementation and promotion of these rights should be highlighted. i also welcome the invitation to the commission to designate 2013 as the 'european year of citizenship' in order to boost the debate on european citizenship and to inform european citizens about their rights, in particular the new rights arising from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has brought more responsibilities to the eu in terms of creating a culture of defence of fundamental rights in the eu and the member states. it is essential that the eu promotes the defence of fundamental rights not only at home but also throughout the world, where today we are unfortunately still witnessing major attacks on these rights. only in this way can peace, human rights and fundamental freedoms be promoted.
in writing. − this report emphasises the obligations arising from the lisbon treaty to combat social exclusion and discrimination and to promote social justice and protection, equality between men and women, solidarity between generations and the protection of the rights of the child. the emphasis on these points, together with the explicit reference to persons belonging to minorities, another fundamental value of the european union, motivates my vote in favour. i support the european parliament's position that the commission should conclude the negotiations and technical consultations so that the european union can accede to the european convention on human rights without further delay.
in writing. - advertising is a key instrument for a functioning market and for competition and ultimately for consumers, as it ensures a more informed choice when properly regulated. however, new technologies in the advertising sector open up a whole new area for the development of new unfair promotional practices, which justifies an evolution of the unfair commercial practices directive. for advertising to fulfil its essential functions in a free and competitive market, it must be well regulated and commercial practices which subvert the market must be duly punished. this is particularly important in the forms of online advertising (via the internet and telephone), which reach the public often unsolicited and raise important issues relating, inter alia, to unfair practices and the misuse of personal data. that is why i consider this an excellent initiative which deserves my support.
in writing. − this report focuses on unfair commercial practices in advertising as defined in the unfair commercial practices directive (ucpd), focusing on the issues inherent in the development of new advertising practices and technologies. the report does not address business-to-business ('b2b') relationships covered by, inter alia, directive 2006/114/ec. unfair practices in advertising take many forms: invasion of public space and the public sphere and targeting of particularly vulnerable people such as children. since young people and children are the most exposed to advertising on the internet, i support the need to develop an integrated european policy to combat the misuse of the internet and the media. to this end, i propose the creation of a new compulsory area specifically devoted to learning about the risks associated with the use of the internet and the media, particularly unfair advertising practices, for first-year students, and a compulsory subject in the final year of a degree or training for primary school teachers and early childhood educators to prepare children for the safe and responsible use of the internet and the media, as well as continuing training for education professionals in this area.
in writing. - unfair commercial practices in advertising must be combated. we are increasingly faced with a serious phenomenon of family indebtedness, and everything in our power must be done to prevent this problem from becoming even worse. advertising can and should be an important tool for society, serving as a source of income, stimulating competitiveness, healthy competition and also promoting creativity. we all know that there are vulnerable people, such as children, who are the prime target of these advertising campaigns. i therefore agree that this matter should be given special attention so that we can build a more economically and socially sustainable society. hence my vote
in writing. - the impact of advertising on consumer behaviour is a reality that should not be overlooked and that this report does not escape. this report, which i voted for, deals with unfair commercial practices in advertising as defined in the unfair commercial practices directive, focusing on the problems inherent in the development of new advertising practices and technologies. advertising is a useful tool both for the internal market and for consumers. however, a number of abuses need to be tackled, including unfair practices, the invasion of public and private space (e.g. unsolicited e-mails), the over-focus on vulnerable people and the potential for distortion of the internal market (purchasing goods or services that consumers would not normally buy). the evaluation of these deviations should be the basis for the analysis of the legislation in force and any proposals for its revision and improvement. i agree with the rapporteur that we should intensify european cooperation in combating unfair advertising practices, by extending both its scope and its frequency.
in writing. − i agree with the general objectives of this action plan, that better information flow at local level should be ensured or that one-stop shops should be set up, that in view of the reduced use of erdf resources for energy efficiency measures, member states and regions should make energy efficiency a horizontal approach to their development, as it is a cost-effective means of promoting economic competitiveness, creating jobs and reducing fuel shortages. i also agree that the commission should consult local and regional representatives in order to define guidelines for energy development and provide financial support for local and regional projects through innovative programmes using existing energy resources and the structural funds. in this context of possible actions, it is proposed to create greater incentives for regions which have so far played an above-average role in energy efficiency, by promoting their energy independence and, on the other hand, to promote the sharing of good practices between these regions and those with little development in this area.
in writing. − energy efficiency is crucial to increasing security of supply, air quality, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and increasing the competitiveness of our society. energy efficiency means doing "more" with "less" resources. this report proposes an ambitious vision for energy efficiency through, for example, the introduction of individual targets and positive incentives. important elements are introduced in the area of modernisation of energy infrastructures such as smart grids, energy efficiency in buildings and transport, use of ict and development of scientific research in the field of energy. this report stresses the need to double funding for scientific research, technological development and demonstration in the field of energy. in the area of financing, the report also encourages the use of the structural funds for energy efficiency and that this should be a priority in the eu budget after 2013. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr bendtsen, on the excellent work he has done and the balance he has struck, and i would ask everyone to support this important report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the energy efficiency action plan because it contains important proposals for the environment and the economy, in particular the presentation of european legislation introducing binding targets for the reduction of energy consumption.
in writing. − in 2008, europe committed itself to achieving a 20% reduction in energy consumption by 2020 at the latest and to ensuring that 20% of its energy consumption comes from renewable sources. this is a key goal to help europe meet its co2 emissions reduction target and to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels, but it must remain the same, a goal to which the various states voluntarily adhere. for this to happen, rather than imposing a binding limit, it will be more important for member states to agree on solutions that allow for greater energy efficiency and less energy waste, without jeopardising development and without this representing an excessive cost for european industries and producers, especially at a time of economic crisis such as the one we are going through.
in writing. − this report deals with energy efficiency policy in the eu. i am in favour of binding targets. the commission green paper (2005/0265 final) on energy efficiency estimates that about one million new jobs could potentially be created, directly and indirectly, in europe. according to this communication, the beneficiaries of energy efficiency measures are especially smes and it is added that an average household could save on average €1,000 per year with energy efficiency measures. mandatory energy efficiency measures are also crucial to reduce the energy deficit resulting from oil and gas imports from the gulf and russia. we already have binding targets to increase the share of renewable energy in the european union by 20%. without binding energy efficiency measures and with the current framework we could only achieve half of the potential. it is also a matter of legal certainty and an important signal for directing new investment. for the eu and portugal, i see more gains than losses in this binding objective. moreover, if the objectives of eu 2020 are not more than intentions, this strategy will be useless.
in writing. − there have been many promises to increase energy efficiency, but the european union is at risk of not meeting its own targets of 20% by 2020. the latest figures suggest an actual average of only 9%, despite the contribution that increased energy efficiency can make to reducing emissions and energy consumption and dependence. the report contains a wide range of issues which conveniently cover the whole wide field of energy efficiency, although it points to paths which are unlikely to achieve the objectives it seeks to achieve. but there are aspects on which we disagree, such as the association of energy efficiency with the so-called europe 2020 strategy, which envisages the completion of the internal energy market, the promotion of market instruments, the european emissions trading system (covering part of the profits in energy efficiency), and forgetting the need to defend a strong public energy sector that each state must promote. while agreeing that community funds are needed to achieve the objectives, there are still some doubts as to the practical feasibility of using up to 15% of the erdf or using the eafrd for energy efficiency, since it should be up to the member states to define their needs and priorities for the distribution of these funds.
in writing. − an action plan for european energy policy must address the following aspects: moving towards a low-carbon energy system, ensuring security of energy supply and ensuring the enhancement of the union's competitiveness and the supply of energy to all consumers at affordable prices. to achieve them requires a very strong financial and human effort.
in writing. − the rapporteur, a member of the epp group, for the review of the energy efficiency action plan proposes a balanced approach to achieving the 20% energy saving target set by the european council in 2007. the pragmatic way of implementing an energy efficiency policy, proposed by the rapporteur, through individual targets and without the imposition of legally binding objectives, seemed to me the most appropriate way, in the present economic and political context, to achieve this objective. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. in the report, which i am voting in favour of, i highlight the various actions at community and member state level to promote energy efficiency: the implementation of existing legislation in this field, energy-efficient urban development, the construction of energy-efficient buildings and the financing of these and other measures through the creation of national energy efficiency funds. it should be noted that this report by the european parliament is an important contribution to the ongoing review of the energy efficiency action plan by the european commission.
madam high representative, how do you feel when you see governments like the french or the portuguese divert demonstrations when chinese dignitaries visit their capitals so that they are not seen by chinese dignitaries visiting these countries? wasn't the idea to have a high representative so that europe could speak with one voice about human rights abroad, for example in china? don't you think that's a little much to speak of in more than one voice? curious, why do you always sit on the council's side? what is the philosophy or constitutional theory behind this choice? a third question: i would like our european diplomats to make human rights a daily priority, but not the second, third or fourth priority, but the first. what will you do to get some of our diplomats to think of human rights as a full-time job every day? would it not be good to have, as several colleagues have already suggested, a permanent board devoted to this?
richard holbrooke, to whom i also pay my deepest respects, said just before he died: the war in afghanistan must be stopped. in fact, this country is crucial to our european and global security and that is why, as the pino arlacchi report goes on to say, we need to correct the colossal mistakes made by investing in afghanisation and putting the human security of the afghan people first, which implies a responsibility to protect on the part of the foreign forces present. let us not be fooled: a state of law and democratic institutions cannot be built by warlords, corrupt and discredited in the eyes of the people. ending the war in afghanistan also depends on the democratically elected government controlling the military power in neighbouring pakistan, a nuclear power outside the npt. if they do not continue the policy of ostriching over these fundamental political issues, the europeans in the european union and nato can help stop the war in afghanistan, and also the descent into hell in pakistan.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the nato summit was held in lisbon and so let me say a few words about what happened in my country in connection with this summit. at that time, the portuguese authorities prohibited european citizens from entering the country for one reason only: they were carrying with them texts critical of the alliance. in those days, the least we can say is that an arbitrary regime, a genuine thought police, was in force in portugal. a regime so special that it led the portuguese government to buy riot control equipment worth five million euros and that did not even arrive in time for the summit. and these are the priorities of a government facing a huge social crisis. in the europe we dream of, freedom of expression is a fundamental value. the europe we dream of will not bow down to military organizations that write their history in blood. the nato summit has legitimized their military intervention all over the planet. the european union has also been subordinated to american military strategy and interests. thirdly, the militarization of access to energy sources has been consolidated. finally, the military defence of the development model which creates environmental imbalances and disturbs the social crisis has been instituted. i would therefore like to say to you, madam president, that i believe that with this summit we have lost democracy, we have lost freedom and we have lost so that some can gain from war.
as stated in the conclusions of the nato summit held in lisbon, nato confirms itself as a military alliance, a nuclear military alliance determined to intervene rapidly and massively anywhere in the world, at any time and under any pretext, claiming to have the only robust set of political and military capabilities, capable of dealing with all kinds of crises: before, during and after conflicts. in a disturbing global threat, nato states that it is affected by and can affect political and security developments beyond its borders and that it will therefore actively engage to improve international security through partnerships with relevant countries and other international organizations. it is a statement which reveals two objectives: on the one hand, to assert itself as a sort of emanating centre from which relations of dependence radiate which enable its forces to be present, to exert pressure and to intervene throughout the globe. and on the other hand, to go further down the path of interventionism and the fusion between international security and the internal security of states, thus aiming at the destruction of international law, in a direct affront to the role of the united nations organization in addressing international security issues. the united states, led by a power, is also seeking to strengthen its european pillar, the european union, which is considered a unique and essential partner of nato, and therefore nato leaving lisbon is bigger, more powerful, more dangerous and more covert, but the threat is great and the response of the portuguese people was also great with the parade of more than thirty thousand people in the streets of lisbon, fighting against this organization, demanding its dissolution, which is considered essential for the defence of peace.
the nato strategic council, adopted in lisbon, is not new in its doctrine of nuclear deterrence, it is old. the alliance has decided to retain nuclear weapons as a last-ditch deterrent. ironically, it thus contradicts president obama's calls for a world free of nuclear weapons and the disarmament promised at the last npt review conference. the alliance should lead by example, but that won't stop nuclear proliferation, tragically it will encourage it. and in times of financial crisis, it diverts needed resources to other threats we face. what good are nuclear bombs against terrorism without a sender or an address, against piracy in the indian ocean, against organized crime, cyberattacks or chemical and biological attacks? the council of the european union this week warned of the need to step up efforts against nuclear proliferation. madam high representative, what are your plans to play this card in nato where 21 of the 28 allies are also members of the european union? and what do you have to say to the two nuclear powers who are members of the european union and who have been the most resistant to attempts to change the nato strategic council on this existential question for all mankind?
in writing. the nato summit in lisbon put an end to the strategic concept of security that had been in force since the cold war. the enshrinement of this new security strategy represents a shift from the traditional defence of the atlantic alliance member countries to a global security concept for the 21st century. the challenges highlighted in the new strategic security concept involve close collaboration with the various international institutions, both governmental and non-governmental, and the strengthening of partnerships, in particular with russia. in addition to the establishment of political vectors, operational issues concerning nato's own capabilities and structure have been adapted to new global threats. the adoption of a transitional plan for the nato mission in afghanistan, with the aim of the afghan authorities taking the lead in matters of national security, should also be underlined. i consider this new strategic vision, which sets out the guidelines for the international relations of the member states, to be of the utmost importance.
this legislative initiative on the control of the commission's 'executive acts' is required by the treaty of lisbon, which places this matter within the legislative competence of the european parliament. this is undeniably a positive overall result, given the current situation. but there are a number of aspects which fall short of full implementation of the lisbon treaty. among the negative aspects, two stand out. firstly, there is no deadline for the mandatory adaptation of the many existing situations to the new regime and the treaty of lisbon. i therefore signed an amendment introducing such a clause. secondly, and most importantly, the derogations provided for in the trade defence instruments (in particular anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures and safeguard measures) are unacceptable, as they will give member states more intrusive control over the commission, making it more difficult to apply those measures and allowing them to be politicised. these measures are essential to protect european companies from competition from imports benefiting from such unlawful advantages. there is no constitutional or political basis for this discriminatory treatment of trade defence measures, which undermines the commission's (and the union's) ability to defend european industry against unfair external competition in the european internal market itself.
mr president, commissioner, this is not new, we have heard it in the debate on other reports in this parliament, we have heard it again here today: the current conception of culture in the european union is an eminently instrumental one. this has various expressions, whether in the context of so-called cultural diplomacy, which sees culture as an instrument of its foreign policy, or in the context of what is now proposed here, the creation of a heritage label of the european union, in the words of the rapporteur, to strengthen citizens' belief in the european union and its leaders and to reduce the distance between the european union and its citizens. the rapporteur has realised in good time that there are other more effective ways of achieving this, and there is much to be said about this. i am surprised to see that no single brand can erase the many marks that the policies that the eu has been developing, its economic governance and, finally, the plans for genuine social terrorism that it has set in motion with the connivance of national governments, are leaving on the citizens and peoples of europe. it is also worth taking into account the effect of policies such as the common agricultural policy or the common fisheries policy, among others, on the destruction of important cultural landmarks of the european peoples, living elements of their historical and cultural heritage. think about the de-structuring, in the course of just one generation, of coastal communities or of secular rural communities, but farther. this initiative, which is predominantly symbolic, is based on the development of a fallacy, the existence of a unique european identity and culture, and on values such as freedom, democracy, tolerance and solidarity. it does so by entering a particularly sensitive area, that of cultural heritage and, in this way, the field of history, a reason for serious concern about the feeding of disturbing processes of rewriting history, which we have seen in recent times. culture, like other historical phenomena, is not made up of any homogeneous common identity, but is rather the expression of antagonisms, conflicts and contexts of cultural domination. we also question the meaning of the designation of the european union's heritage as a trademark, which is based on the mere location of the heritage elements in question. the european union's heritage or heritage in the european union, knowing, as we do, that european heritage is indebted to many cultures and could be claimed equally by the islamic world, by mediterranean cultures or by the cultures of the peoples subject to european colonialism. i would conclude, mr president, by saying that, with a few exceptions, the amendments proposed by the rapporteur generally improve the commission's original text, but in this case the specific objectives of this report are far less relevant than the misconceptions behind it.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, like our president paolo de castro, i too had the opportunity, as minister of agriculture 12 years ago, to take part in the decision which adopted the legislation we are discussing here today. it was a very long and very difficult debate because we had two conflicting values on the table: creating conditions for animal welfare and ensuring the competitiveness of the sector. the solution was to give priority to animal welfare and to allow the sector a sufficiently long period to adapt. although the new rules will not come into force for another year, the data available on farms which have not yet adapted are cause for concern, as the commissioner has confirmed. we cannot allow companies that have invested and made great efforts to be in a position to comply with the legislation to be penalized or subject to unfair competition. i am grateful for the information the commissioner has given us, but we would like to know more about the actual situation in each member state and what specific measures, in addition to those mentioned by the commissioner, the commission intends to take to ensure that companies in the sector can generally comply with this legislation by 1 january 2012, and whether there is in fact a framework of sanctions that is at least uniform across the various member states. that is the spirit of the resolution we are discussing here today, and which i am sure will have the broad support of this parliament. my group will, however, vote against the total or partial deletion of paragraphs f, 8, 9 and 14, which contain expressions and objectives which we consider to be of doubtful compatibility with community law and which, if retained, would undermine the credibility of the resolution.
mr president, commissioner, on the subject under discussion today, let me begin by reiterating what i believe: firstly, that the directives are indeed to be complied with and so is the 1999 directive; secondly, that concerns for animal welfare are a european union flag to be kept. that said, it is important to stress that the adaptation of companies in this sector to the directive is quite onerous: 30% per chicken in portugal. and there is no specific support from the rural development programme for this purpose. with the sector decapitalised, limited bank credit and widespread crisis it is imperative and urgent to recognise that these exceptional circumstances have delayed the adaptation of many companies and it is therefore important to allow extra time for those and only those who have already started the required adaptation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the commission's proposal to extend the original concept of the european heritage label from an intergovernmental action to a formal eu action, so as to contribute to a stronger european identity, because i believe that the intention of this label should be proposed not only with the aim of promoting the internal cohesion of the european union, but also as a sign of european unity and values across borders. the brand should be valued and put into practice after effective demonstration of results within the eu.
in writing. - one of the great riches of the european union is its cultural diversity, which is perfectly reflected in the diverse nature of its cultural, artistic, architectural and linguistic heritage. it is this diversity, combined with a rich history and a great respect for heritage and its preservation, that makes europe a unique place. but even though we all share a very rich and comparatively small space, the truth is that there is often not the closeness and interest that we could find, which is why this initiative can lead to greater closeness between european citizens and to greater knowledge of the european heritage and the common values that we all share, making europe a true union in diversity.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. but there are also some negative aspects. the amendments proposed by the rapporteur do not touch on the central aspect of promoting multilingualism, and do not correct the serious flaw in the original proposal. indeed, the real and effective promotion of multilingualism is not achieved by using several eu languages, but by using the various eu languages. but more important than the specific aims of the report are the misconceptions behind this idea. the european heritage label (or eu heritage label) is based on the development of the fallacy of the existence of a unique european identity and culture, based on values such as freedom, democracy, etc. there is no such thing as a single european cultural heritage. the whole of european cultural history, like its history in general, is not only built up of diversity and admirable creative energy and progress, but also of violent antagonistic confrontation, of intolerance, of multiple lines and contexts of cultural domination. the domain of heritage is particularly sensitive because it is closely associated with that of history, a reason for serious concern about the feeding of disturbing processes of rewriting history, which we have witnessed in recent times.
in writing. - i warmly welcome the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council to establish a european heritage label. the aim of forming a european identity and promoting the union's interests is fundamental to peace and social cohesion. the proposed measure to promote european heritage through a transnational website is inviting for young europeans, and can appeal to the best knowledge of the continent's history, to familiarity with the multinational heritage and the common cultural heritage, and to knowledge of the people and ideas that led to the construction of the european union itself. it is a high symbolic and educational value event which will present european history and culture as a whole. i support the intention expressed in the report to ensure effective involvement of the european parliament and the council in the selection of the venues and content presented in order to ensure a high degree of transparency and democratic character of the initiative.

in writing. − cooperation with switzerland in the field of education is an important step in relations between the european union and switzerland. the two programmes in question support lifelong learning and the integration of young people in the construction of europe through tolerance and solidarity among young europeans. the agreement between the commission and switzerland is appropriate, given that swiss participants in these programmes apply on an equal footing with all other young europeans and that switzerland is committed to complying with european rules and their monitoring and to providing financial assistance for both programmes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation establishing the terms and conditions for the participation of the swiss confederation in the 'youth in action' programme and in the action programme in the field of lifelong learning (2007-2013), as i considered that the agreement negotiated by the commission with the swiss authorities was quite positive, extending the benefits of the programmes to switzerland and safeguarding the interests, including financial interests, of the european union.
in writing. − the role of the european union in defending human rights is a fundamental task which the institutions must not abdicate and which must remain a priority diplomatic task. annex i to this report is the best proof of this, since it gives an account of all the situations in which human rights have been violated and in which europe has denounced or in which we have not waived a word of condemnation, from afghanistan to somalia, from russia to iran. we did not close our eyes or bury our heads in the sand, even when it came to strategic partners, because the defence of freedom and human rights cannot be subordinated to specific interests. in my view, this must remain the union's position: to be bold and to fight for human rights and democracy.
in writing. - this report is part of a recurrent exercise of pure hypocrisy by this majority, dominated by the right and social democracy, which sees itself as an ambassador for the defence of human rights. this is an exercise which is unmasking itself by the obvious contradictions it contains, namely in the instrumentalisation of a supposed defence of human rights to promote interference in countries where its interests are at stake, whitening and supporting its allies, particularly the usa. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the european union's role in the world. there is the continuing occupation of afghanistan by nato forces and the successive killings of civilians under the pretext of the fight against terrorism. there is support for the continuation of israel's apartheid policy against the palestinian people and support for morocco's continuation of the occupation of western sahara. there is support for the continuation of the criminal us blockade of cuba, condemned by the united nations general assembly 18 times in a row. these policies, like the majorities who promote them, smell like breath. the time is coming when people will know how to reject them.
in writing. − this report on the annual report on human rights in the world (2009) and the european union's policy on the matter provides an exhaustive overview of human rights violations on a global scale. it is worth recalling here the european parliament's unwavering determination and its longstanding efforts to defend human rights and democracy in the world through the implementation of a firm and effective policy of defending human rights in the eu. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty opens up a historic opportunity to address the remaining gaps in eu policy on human rights and democracy. in this context, i support the rapporteur's call for the european external action service to fully comply with the objective and spirit of the lisbon treaty, namely to ensure that respect for and promotion of human rights are at the heart of the various areas of intervention in the union's external policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the new strategy for afghanistan. i believe that international aid should be channelled directly to the afghan authorities, eliminating the intermediaries. as regards the peace process, the eu's role should give the karzai government sufficient leeway in choosing partners for dialogue, insisting on the following conditions: banning al qaeda, eliminating the crops of the nightingale and a willingness to establish basic respect for fundamental human rights. as regards the vocational training of police forces, i agree with the objectives of not focusing solely on increasing the number of police and military personnel, but mainly on the training, organisation and relations of police forces with the parallel judicial institutions.
in writing. - nine years after the start of the military intervention in afghanistan, this is possibly the greatest challenge facing europe and its allies in terms of external intervention and global security. the truth is that in the last decade, despite the strong (and uninterrupted) international presence in afghanistan, security in the territory has deteriorated. the support and training of terrorists has continued and, moreover, the main socioeconomic indicators are unsatisfactory. the main objective of the international community and europe at this time must therefore be to enable the formation of a strong and stable government, and that is why the peace process must continue to be supported in accordance with the three essential commitments listed in the report: (i) afghanistan's commitment to banish al-qaeda from the country; (ii) the elimination of poppy crops and the fight against drug trafficking; (iii) the will to establish basic respect for fundamental rights. in this context, and in accordance with our international commitments under nato, the military presence in afghanistan must be progressively reduced, while maintaining international support for the maintenance of peace and security, with a view to post-intervention stabilisation.
in writing. − following the council meeting, at a joint session of the foreign and defence ministers, which discussed how to move forward with the implementation of the action plan for afghanistan and pakistan and which presented the first half-yearly implementation report, this report on a new strategy for afghanistan has been drawn up. i am in favour of a strategy aimed at protecting the population and rebuilding areas where security is guaranteed, and of all political solutions in which all parties are called to negotiate. i welcome the objective of gradually transferring security responsibilities to afghan forces by 2014. i fully support parliament's call on the commission to ensure full transparency in the financial assistance provided to the afghan government, international organisations and local ngos. only a transparent process can preserve the coherence of aid and the ultimate goal of success in afghanistan's reconstruction and development.
in writing. − the new rules introduced by the treaty of lisbon as regards implementing acts have given rise to this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. this is a sensitive issue, particularly in relation to agriculture and fisheries. under the current comitology system, the cap is the policy covering the vast majority of comitology acts. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the current provisions on comitology will have to be replaced by delegated and implementing acts in accordance with articles 290 and 291 tfeu. the problem of adapting existing legislation to the provisions of the lisbon treaty is of the greatest importance, especially for policies (such as agricultural and fisheries policy) which were not adopted under the codecision procedure. only the test of the new legislation, which has been amended substantially by the european parliament and the council, can indicate whether the course taken is conducive to the effectiveness and implementation of european policies.
in writing. - we voted against this resolution because we disagree with the positions being taken on the financial problems facing the member states, without taking account of their causes and without presenting substantive measures that would lead to a full resolution. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european monetary system is fully operational, and that the european central bank is fully operational. since the european union does not want to take any of these measures, it is opting for positions which only mitigate the existing problem, but which maintain a high dependence on financial markets and the richest countries. the resolution also calls for sanctions to be imposed on member states which do not comply with the rules laid down, in particular by the stability pact, which will tend to aggravate the overall situation of the countries with the weakest economies. the interests of the great powers, such as germany, are therefore predominant, and the solidarity so much praised is still lacking.
in writing. the political situation in côte d'ivoire is deplorable at all levels. it is worrying to note that the sovereign will of the electorate is not respected and that the presidential candidate who, according to the independent electoral commission of côte d'ivoire (cei), won the elections has been prevented from taking office by the constitutional court. there were reports of serious attacks on freedom during the second round of elections, including a climate of tension and violence that caused several deaths and injuries. the political situation in côte d'ivoire is unsustainable, the attitude of the constitutional court is unacceptable and mr gbagbo's bad defeat is contrary to democracy and the principles of the rule of law.
in writing. - the serious political and institutional crisis in côte d'ivoire following the second round of the presidential elections on 28 november 2010 is the reason for this resolution. the election process, which was monitored by the un and the european union, was generally satisfactory. however, the results presented by the independent electoral commission of côte d'ivoire, which announced ouattara's victory, were refuted by the country's constitutional council which reversed the result, claiming that fraud occurred in some areas and declaring laurent gbagbo, the current president, the winner. the only source of democratic legitimacy is universal suffrage, the results of which have been certified by the un, and in this resolution, which i vote in favour of, parliament calls on mr gbagbo to resign and hand over power to alassane ouattara, and strongly condemns the acts of intimidation directed against eu observers. the resolution also calls on the eu to take action against those who obstruct the peace and national reconciliation process and supports the eu's decision to impose sanctions on laurent gbagbo.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, advocating some flexibility for those who have already started this adaptation but, because of the current crisis, have not yet been able to complete it. from 1 january 2012, the use of unimproved cages for rearing laying hens shall be prohibited and this shall set out minimum standards for the protection of laying hens. it is therefore important to know whether the commission can indicate the progress made by the member states in preparing for the ban on the rearing of laying hens in conventional battery farms from 1 january 2012, what measures it will take against member states whose producers do not comply and also what measures it will take to avoid possible unfair competition from third countries on the community egg market after 1 january 2012.
in writing. − the issue raised here is fundamental, not only from the point of view of animal welfare and hygiene, but especially with regard to the need to ensure the applicability and effectiveness of directive 1999/74/ec, avoiding potential distortions of competition. it has already been demonstrated in other situations concerning animal transport that the non-application and non-compliance of certain producers and distributors with community rules creates unfair competition and market distortions. it is therefore urgent that the union should demonstrate its ability to enforce its directives throughout the union so that, while respecting the same rules, the market can operate more efficiently and without distortion.
the situation of eritrean refugees in the sinai desert is very serious, as has been described by several colleagues. obviously we must be tough in the way we deal with the human traffickers who are currently holding these refugees hostage and demanding very high ransoms from them, but we must also, at the same time, be equally protective of the refugees, because we cannot just want to be tough on the traffickers and then completely forget about the victims, and we must also recognise the reasons why they are in the sinai desert, when before their migratory route was through libya, and the agreements between italy and libya and between the european union and libya, so often presented here by the commission as good news, mean that people who come from what has been described, correctly, as a concentration camp like north korea in africa have nowhere to run. action is therefore required, not only from egypt, which is clearly doing far less than it should, but also from the european union itself. i would ask the european commission to send a delegation to egypt immediately to find out what is happening there, and we also ask all our institutions to take action, because eritreans are a clear case of resettlement, a policy which we have with the european refugee fund, and they cannot return to eritrea, they cannot stay in a transit country, the only lasting solution for them is resettlement, and you know, ladies and gentlemen, why is the resettlement package not moving forward? it is not moving forward because parliament has already done its half of the co-decision in the resettlement case in may and because of the famous delegated acts controversy the council refuses to do its part. if the resettlement package had been adopted at this stage, we would have had an urgent procedure which parliament inserted in that report of which i am the rapporteur, it was approved here by 500 votes and the european commission could have started an urgent procedure to resettle these refugees. since the council is not doing its part of what we should call a codecision process, those people are in the sinai desert for who knows how long. this co-decision process has consequences for real lives of real people and it was time for the council to get on with its half of the homework.
mr president, egypt is not just turning a blind eye to the horrific treatment and exploitation of african refugees, particularly from somalia and eritrea, who are trying to escape their countries to israel through the sinai. egypt is deporting them, despite them obviously qualifying as refugees and asylum seekers from countries, one with a terrible conflict with terrorism, with no law and order, and the other, eritrea, being one of the most oppressive, most tyrannical countries in the world. egyptian authorities are in fact practicing a take-to-kill policy and 85 migrants have already died in sinai since 2007, according to a human rights watch report. we call on the egyptian authorities to fulfil their obligations with regard to human rights and migrants and refugees in particular and to cooperate with the unhcr and we call on the european authorities to do the same and to fully support what mr rui tavares has said on this matter regarding the possibility of resettlement.
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission shares the concerns of the european parliament. the reports received speak of several hundred refugees, from eritrea, ethiopia, sudan and somalia, apparently being held hostage in sinai by traffickers requesting hard payment for their release. since the first notification, we have been following the case, establishing the facts, assessing the situation and taking appropriate action. the european union delegation in cairo has close contacts with local civil-society organisations and liaises with the united nations high commissioner for refugees’ regional representation in cairo. they are very much following the case. in coordination with the embassies of the eu member states, the egyptian ministry of foreign affairs has been approached. the eu has expressed our concerns, as well as our strong belief that the egyptian authorities should take appropriate measures to liberate these people and grant them appropriate protection. there are reports of ongoing investigations to find the group of refugees, and we hope that things will be clearer in the next few days. this case is not the only cause of concern. migrants and refugees in egypt still suffer from many protection gaps. the most serious incidents are reported in the sinai. many migrants intending to cross to israel via the sinai border are subject to abuse and mistreatment. we have raised this issue several times with our egyptian counterparts in the framework of the regular subcommittee meetings discussing either migration issues or political affairs, including human rights. the latest occasion when the point was raised was at the meeting of the eu-egypt association committee on 14 december in cairo. the eu has regularly invited egyptian authorities to improve the quality of the assistance and protection offered to asylum seekers and refugees, and has offered financial and technical assistance in this endeavour. the eu has also invited the egyptian authorities to ensure that the principle of non-refoulement is observed for all migrants in need of international protection, including eritreans. the eu has asked that the unhcr be given full authorisation to implement its mandate throughout the entire territory of egypt, including in the sinai region. there have been some positive developments that should be stressed. in the spring of this year, egypt adopted new legislation criminalising human trafficking and also protecting its victims. another welcome development was the adoption of a transplant act, which criminalises organ trafficking. we hope that the egyptian administration will now take effective measures to ensure efficient implementation of this legal framework, and we have offered our cooperation in this field. we will continue to support the work of the unhcr and civil-society organisations to ensure better living conditions, as well as proper legal protection, for migrants and refugees living in the country. we will continue to follow with care the case of the hostage refugees in sinai and we will pursue our contacts with the egyptian authorities in this regard. i truly hope for an early solution to this case and i regret the reported loss of eight lives so far.
